# Siva Purana. Chapter 7

## Section 11 - Vāyavīya-saṃhitā (1)

## Chapter 1 - Origin of the sacred lore

## \|\| 11.1.1 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*namaśśivāya somāya sagaṇāya sasūnave \|*  
*pradhānapuruṣeśāya sargasthityaṃtahetave \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: Most of the verses of this chapter are identical on form and content with those of the last chapter in the Vidyeśvara-saṃhitā.

Vyāsa said:—

1\. Obeisance to Śiva accompanied by Umā, Gaṇas and his sons, the lord of Prakṛti and Puruṣa and the cause of creation, sustenance and annihilation.

## \|\| 11.1.2-3 \|\|

*śaktirapratimā yasya hyaiśvaryaṃ cāpi sarvagam \|*  
*svāmitvaṃ ca vibhutvaṃ ca svabhāvaṃ saṃpracakṣate \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tamajaṃ viśvakarmāṇaṃ śāśvataṃ śivamavyayam \|*  
*mahādevaṃ mahātmānaṃ vrajāmi śaraṇaṃ śivam \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. I seek refuge in Śiva, whose power is unequalled, whoso glory spreads everywhere, whose lordship and potency are said to be natural, who is unborn, who is the creator of the universe, eternal, auspicious and the unchanging great Ātman.

## \|\| 11.1.4-5 \|\|

*dharmakṣetre mahātīrthe gaṃgākāliṃdisaṃgame \|*  
*prayāge naimiṣāraṇye brahmalokasya vartmani \|\| 4 \|\|*

*munayaśśaṃsitātmānaḥ satyavrataparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*mahaujaso mahābhāgā mahāsatraṃ vitenire \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Noble sages engaged in truthful rites, highly fortunate and dignified performed a great sacrifice in the Naimiṣa\[1\] forest, a virtuous spot and a holy centre of many sacrifices at the confluence\[2\] of the Gaṅgā and Kālindī, a pathway that leads to Brahmaloka.

## \|\| 11.1.6-9 \|\|

*tatra satraṃ samākarṇya teṣāmakliṣṭakarmaṇām \|*  
*sākṣātsatyavatīsūnorvedavyāsasya dhīmataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*śiṣyo mahātmā medhāvī triṣu lokeṣu viśrutaḥ \|*  
*pañcāvayavayuktasya vākyasya guṇadoṣavit \|\| 7 \|\|*

*uttarottaravaktā ca bruvato 'pi bṛhaspateḥ \|*  
*madhuraḥ śravaṇānāṃ ca manojñapadaparvaṇām \|\| 8 \|\|*

*kathānāṃ nipuṇo vaktā kālavinnayavitkaviḥ \|*  
*ājagāma sa taṃ deśaṃ sūtaḥ paurāṇikottamaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

6-9. On hearing that the sages of good rites wore performing the sacrifice, Sūta the most excellent of Paurāṇikas came to that place, Sūta who was a noble disciple of the intelligent Veda Vyāsa the son of Satyavatī, who was very intelligent and famous in the world, who knew the faults and merits of syllogistic statements. He could satisfy even the queries of Bṛhaspati. He was an expert in narrating the stories of charming anecdotes. He knew the proper time for everything and the policy to bo adopted. He was a poet.

## \|\| 11.1.10 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā sūtamāyāṃtaṃ munayo hṛṣṭamānasāḥ \|*  
*tasmai sāma ca pūjāṃ ca yathāvatpratyapādayan \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. On seeing Sūta come, the sages were delighted in their minds. They received him and worshipped him suitably.

## \|\| 11.1.11 \|\|

*pratigṛhya satāṃ pūjāṃ munibhiḥ pratipāditām \|*  
*uddiṣṭamānasaṃ bheje niyukto yuktamātmanaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Accepting their welcome and worship he took the proper seat offered by them.

## \|\| 11.1.12 \|\|

*tatastatsaṃgamādeva munīnāṃ bhāvitātmanām \|*  
*sotkaṃṭhamabhavaccitaṃ śrotuṃ paurāṇikīṃ kathām \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. By their contact with him the sages of pious souls became eager and impatient to hear the Purāṇic lore.

## \|\| 11.1.13 \|\|

*tadā tamanukūlābhirvāgbhiḥ pūjya 1 maharṣayaḥ \|*  
*atīvābhimukhaṃ kṛtvā vacanaṃ cedamabruvan \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Worshipping him with words of praise the sages sat in front of him and spoke.

## \|\| 11.1.14 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*romaharṣaṇa sarvajña bhavānno bhāgyagauravāt \|*  
*saṃprāptodya mahābhāga śaivarāja mahāmate \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O omniscient Romaharṣaṇa, the principal devotees of Śiva of great fortune and keen intellect, it is due to the weightiness of our good luck that you have come here now.

## \|\| 11.1.15-17 \|\|

*purāṇavidyāmakhilāṃ vyāsātpratyakṣamīyivān \|*  
*tasmādāścaryabhūtānāṃ kathānāṃ tvaṃ hi bhājanam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*ratnānāmurusārāṇāṃ ratnākara ivārṇavaḥ \|*  
*yacca bhūtaṃ yacca bhavyaṃ yaccānyadvastu vartate \|\| 16 \|\|*

*na tavāviditaṃ kiñcittriṣu lokeṣu vidyate \|*  
*tvamadṛṣṭavaśādasmaddarśanārthamihāgataḥ \|*  
*akurvankimapi śreyo na vṛthā gantumarhasi \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-17. You have directly acquired the Purāṇic lore from Vyāsa, Hence you are a repository of wonderful tales, even as the ocean of precious gems. There is nothing in the three worlds past, present or future, which is not known to you. Fortunately you have come here to visit us. It does not behove you to go in vain without conferring blessing on us.

## \|\| 11.1.18 \|\|

*tasmācchrāvyataraṃ puṇyaṃ satkathājñānasaṃhitam \|*  
*vedāṃtasārasarvasvaṃ purāṇaṃ śrāvayāśu naḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Please narrate to us the holy Purāṇa the storehouse of good stories and the essence of the Vedānta.

## \|\| 11.1.19 \|\|

*evamabhyarthitassūto munibhirvedavādibhiḥ \|*  
*ślakṣṇāṃ ca nyāyasaṃyuktāṃ pratyuvāca śubhāṃ giram \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Thus requested by the sages, the habitual reciters of the Vedic texts, Sūta spoke auspicious words full of sweet and rational meaning.

## \|\| 11.1.20 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*pūjito 'nugṛhītaśca bhavadbhiriti coditaḥ \|*

*kasmātsamyaṅna vibrūyāṃ purāṇamṛṣipūjitam \|*  
*abhivaṃdya mahādevaṃ devīṃ skaṃdaṃ vināyakam \|\| 20 \|\|*

Sūta said:—

20\. I have been honoured, blessed and urged by you all. Why shall I not then expound clearly the Purāṇa, held in esteem by the sages.

## \|\| 11.1.21-22 \|\|

*naṃdinaṃ ca tathā vyāsaṃ sākṣātsatyavatīsutam \|*  
*vakṣyāmi paramaṃ puṇyaṃ purāṇaṃ vedasaṃmitam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*śivajñānārṇavaṃ sākṣādbhaktimuktiphalapradam \|*  
*śabdārthanyāyasaṃyuktai rāgamārthairvibhūṣitam \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. After saluting Śiva, Pārvatī, Skanda, Gaṇeśa, Nandin and Vyāsa the son of Satyavatī, I shall narrate the extremely meritorious Purāṇa which is on a par with the Vedas, which being an ocean of Śaivitc knowledge directly yields worldly pleasures and salvation.

## \|\| 11.1.23 \|\|

*śvetakalpaprasaṃgena vāyunā kathitaṃ purā \|*  
*vidyāsthānāni sarvāṇi purāṇānukramaṃ tathā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. It is embellished with the topics of the Āgamas full of rational meaning. In the context of the Śveta Kalpa it was narrated by Vāyu formerly.

## \|\| 11.1.24 \|\|

*tatpurāṇasya cotpattiṃ bruvato me nibodhata \|*  
*aṃgāni vedāścatvāro mīmāṃsānyāyavistaraḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Understand well even as I narrate the various sacred lores, the due order of the Purāṇas and their origin.

## \|\| 11.1.25 \|\|

*purāṇaṃ dharmaśāstraṃ ca vidyāścetāścaturdaśa \|*  
*āyurvedo dhanurvedo gāṃdharvaścetyanukramāt \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The sacred lore consists of fourteen texts viz., the six Aṅgas, the four Vedas, Mīmāṃsā, Nyāya, Purāṇas and the Dharma Śāstras.

## \|\| 11.1.26 \|\|

*arthaśāstraṃ paraṃ tasmādvidyā hyaṣṭādaśa smṛtāḥ \|*  
*aṣṭādaśānāṃ vidyānāmetāsāṃ bhinnavartmanām \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. There are eighteen secular Vidyās—Āyurveda Dhanurveda, Gāndharvaveda etc. ending with Arthaśāstra.

## \|\| 11.1.27 \|\|

*ādikartā kavissākṣācchūlapāṇiriti śrutiḥ \|*  
*sa hi sarvajagannāthaḥ sisṛkṣurakhilaṃ jagat \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Śruti mentions that the original exponent and poet of the eighteen Vidyās, each having its own individual path, is the trident-bearing lord himself.

## \|\| 11.1.28 \|\|

*brahmāṇaṃ vidadhe sākṣātputramagre sanātanam \|*  
*tasmai prathamaputrāya brahmaṇe viśvayonaye \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Indeed he is the lord of the universe. At the outset, with the desire of creating the universe, he created Brahmā, as his son.

## \|\| 11.1.29 \|\|

*vidyāścemā dadau pūrvaṃ viśvasṛṣṭyarthamīśvaraḥ \|*  
*pālanāya hariṃ devaṃ rakṣāśaktiṃ dadau tataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. To his eldest son Brahmā, the cause of the universe, Śiva gave these lores in the beginning in order to facilitate the creation of the universe.

## \|\| 11.1.30 \|\|

*madhyamaṃ tanayaṃ viṣṇuṃ pātāraṃ brahmaṇo 'pi hi \|*  
*labdhavidyena vidhinā prajāsṛṣṭiṃ vitanvatā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. He created Viṣṇu for the protection, of even Brahmā himself and endowed him with the power of protection.

## \|\| 11.1.31 \|\|

*prathamaṃ sarvaśāstrāṇāṃ purāṇaṃ brahmaṇā smṛtam \|*  
*anaṃtaraṃ tu vaktrebhyo vedāstasya vinirgatāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Purāṇa, the first among the Śāstras, was learnt by Brahmā who had acquired the lore and began the creation of the subjects.

## \|\| 11.1.32 \|\|

*pravṛttissarvaśāstrāṇāṃ tanmukhādabhavattataḥ \|*  
*yadāsya vistaraṃ śaktā nādhigaṃtuṃ prajā bhuvi \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The Vedas came out of his mouths. The Śāstras too had their origin from him.

## \|\| 11.1.33-34 \|\|

*tadā vidyāsamāsārthaṃ viśveśvaraniyogataḥ \|*  
*dvāparāṃteṣu viśvātmā viṣṇurviśvaṃbharaḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*vyāsanāmnā caratyasminnavatīrya mahītale \|*  
*evaṃ vyastāśca vedāśca dvāparedvāpare dvijāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. When the people could not follow the big sacred texts, at the instance of Viśveśvara, lord Viṣṇu the sustainer and the soul of the universe incarnated on the earth at the end of Dvāpara Yuga, in order to abridge them. He walked about the earth in the name of Vyāsa.

## \|\| 11.1.35 \|\|

*nirmitāni purāṇāni anyāni ca tataḥ param \|*  
*sa punardvāpare cāsminkṛṣṇadvaipāyanākhyayā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. O Brahmins, in every Dvāpara Yuga the Vedas are classified by him. The Purāṇas and other texts are written by him.

## \|\| 11.1.36 \|\|

*araṇyāmiva havyāśī satyavatyāmajāyata \|*  
*saṃkṣipya sa punarvedāṃścaturdhā kṛtavānmuniḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. In this Dvāpara age he was born of Satyavatī in the name of Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana as fire from Araṇi.

## \|\| 11.1.37 \|\|

*vyastavedatayā loke vedavyāsa iti śrutaḥ \|*  
*purāṇānāñca saṃkṣiptaṃ caturlakṣapramāṇataḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. He abridged and classified the Vedas into four groups. He is known as Vedavyāsa.

## \|\| 11.1.38 \|\|

*adyāpi devaloke tacchatakoṭipravistaram \|*  
*yo vidyāccaturo vedān sāṃgopaṇiṣadāndvijaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Purāṇas extending to a hundred crore Ślokas were condensed by him into four hundred thousand Ślokas. Even now in the Devaloka they have the original number.

## \|\| 11.1.39 \|\|

*na cetpurāṇaṃ saṃvidyānnaiva sa syādvicakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*itihāsapurāṇābhyāṃ vedaṃ samupabṛṃhayet \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Even if a brahmin knows the four Vedas with their Aṅgas and the Upaniṣads he is not an expert if he does not know the Purāṇas.

## \|\| 11.1.40 \|\|

*bibhetyalpaśrutādvedo māmayaṃ pratariṣyati \|*  
*sargaśca pratisargaśca vaṃśo manvaṃtarāṇi ca \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The knowledge of the Vedas shall he enlarged by Itihāsa and the Purāṇas. The Vedas are afraid of a man of deficient knowledge thinking “This man will deceive me”.

## \|\| 11.1.41 \|\|

*vaṃśānucaritaṃ caiva purāṇaṃ pañcalakṣaṇam \|*  
*daśadhā cāṣṭadhā caitatpurāṇamupadiśyate \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Purāṇas have five characteristics—creation, subsidiary creation, genealogy, manvantaras and the chronological account of kings, these are described in every Purāṇa.

## \|\| 11.1.42 \|\|

*bṛhatsūkṣmaprabhedena munibhistattvavittamaiḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṃ pādmaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ ca śaivaṃ bhāgavataṃ tathā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The sages reckon ten Purāṇas and eight big Purāṇas.

## \|\| 11.1.43 \|\|

*bhaviṣyaṃ nāradīyaṃ ca mārkaṃḍeyamataḥ param \|*  
*āgneyaṃ brahmavaivartaṃ laiṃgaṃ vārāhameva ca \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Brāhma, Pādma, Vaiṣṇava, Śaiva, Bhāgavata, Bhaviṣya. Nāradīya and Mārkaṇḍeya are the eight big Purāṇas.

## \|\| 11.1.44-45 \|\|

*skāndaṃ ca vāmanaṃ caiva kaurmyaṃ mātsyaṃ ca gāruḍam \|*  
*brahmāṃḍaṃ ceti puṇyo 'yaṃ purāṇānāmanukramaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*tatra śaivaṃ turīyaṃ yacchārvaṃ sarvārthasādhakam \|*  
*graṃtho lakṣapramāṇaṃ tadvyastaṃ dvādaśasaṃhitam \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. Āgneya, Brahmavaivarta, Liṅga, Vārāha, Skānda, Vāmana, Kūrma, Matsya, Garuḍa and Brahmāṇḍa are the ten small Purāṇas. These are the eighteen Purāṇas in order. Śivapurāṇa, the fourth in the list belongs to Śiva and is conducive to the achievement of all objects.

## \|\| 11.1.46 \|\|

*nirmitaṃ tacchivenaiva tatra dharmaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ \|*  
*taduktenaiva dharmeṇa śaivāstraivarṇikā narāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. It contains a hundred thousand verses. It is divided into twelve Saṃhitās. It is created by Śiva. All sacred rites are mentioned therein.

## \|\| 11.1.47 \|\|

*tasmādvimukutimanvicchañcchivameva samāśrayet \|*  
*tamāśrityaiva devānāmapi muktirna cānyathā \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Men are classified under three castes in accordance with their duties. Hence he who wishes for liberation shall resort to Śiva alone.

## \|\| 11.1.48 \|\|

*no sanskrit verse \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Even the gods can attain liberation by resorting to him alone and not otherwise.

## \|\| 11.1.49 \|\|

*yadidaṃ śaivamākhyātaṃ purāṇaṃ vedasaṃmitam \|*  
*tasya bhedānsamāsena bruvato me nibodhata \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. What I mentioned as the Śivapurāṇa on a par with the Vedas, know its creations as I briefly explain.

## \|\| 11.1.50-56 \|\|

*vidyeśvaraṃ tathā raudraṃ vaināyakamanuttamam \|*  
*aumaṃ mātṛpurāṇaṃ ca rudraikādaśakaṃ tathā \|\| 50 \|\|*

*kailāsaṃ śatarudraṃ ca śatarudrākhyameva ca \|*  
*sahasrakoṭirudrākhyaṃ vāyavīyaṃ tataḥparam \|\| 51 \|\|*

*dharmasaṃjñaṃ purāṇaṃ cetyevaṃ dvādaśa saṃhitāḥ \|*  
*vidyeśaṃ daśasāhasramuditaṃ graṃthasaṃkhyayā \|\| 52 \|\|*

*raudraṃ vaināyakaṃ caumaṃ mātṛkākhyaṃ tataḥ param \|*  
*pratyekamaṣṭasāhasraṃ trayodaśasahasrakam \|\| 53 \|\|*

*raudrakādaśakākhyaṃ yatkailāsaṃ ṣaṭsahasrakam \|*  
*śatarudraṃ trisāhasraṃ koṭirudraṃ tataḥ param \|\| 54 \|\|*

*sahasrairnavabhiryuktaṃ sarvārthajñānasaṃyutam \|*  
*sahasrakoṭirudrākhyamekādaśasahasrakam \|\| 55 \|\|*

*catussahasrasaṃkhyeyaṃ vāyavīyamanuttamam \|*  
*dharmasaṃjñaṃ purāṇaṃ yattaddvādaśasahasrakam \|\| 56 \|\|*

50-56. There are twelve Saṃhitās: Vidyeśvara, Rudra, Vaināyaka, Auma, Mātṛ, Rudraikādaśaka, Kailāsa, Śatarudra, Koṭirudra, Sahasrakoṭirudra, Vāyavīya and Dharmapurāṇa. Vidyeśvara contains ten thousand verses. There are eight thousand verses in each of the four—Raudra, Vaināyaka, Auma and Mātṛpurāṇa. Rudraikādaśa contains thirteen thousand verses; Kailāsa six thousand; Śatarudra three thousand; Koṭirudra nine thousand; Sahasrakoṭirudra eleven thousand; Vāyavīya four thousand and Dharma contains twelve thousand verses.

## \|\| 11.1.57 \|\|

*tadevaṃ lakṣamuddiṣṭaṃ śaivaṃ śākhāvibhedataḥ \|*  
*purāṇaṃ vedasāraṃ tadbhuktimuktiphalapradam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Thus Śivapurāṇa contains a hundred thousand verses. This Purāṇa, the essence of the Vedas, yields worldly pleasures and salvation.

## \|\| 11.1.58 \|\|

*vyāsena tattu saṃkṣiptaṃ caturviṃśatsahasrakam \|*  
*śaivantatra purāṇaṃ vai caturthaṃ saptasaṃhitam \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Śiva Purāṇa the fourth one was abridged into seven Saṃhitās with twenty four thousand verses.

## \|\| 11.1.59-60 \|\|

*vidyeśvarākhyā tatrādyā dvitīyā rudrasaṃhitā \|*  
*tṛtīyā śatarudrākhyā koṭirudrā caturthikā \|\| 59 \|\|*

*pañcamī kathitā comā ṣaṣṭhī kailāsasaṃhitā \|*  
*saptamī vāyavīyākhyā saptaivaṃ saṃhitā iha \|\| 60 \|\|*

59-60. The first Saṃhitā is Vidyeśvara; the second Rudrasaṃhitā; the third Śatarudra. Koṭirudra is the fourth. Umāsaṃhitā is the fifth; the sixth is Kailāsa. The seventh is Vāyavīya. These are only seven compendiums.

## \|\| 11.1.61-64 \|\|

*vidyeśvaraṃ dvisāhasraṃ raudraṃ pañcaśatāyutam \|*  
*triṃśattathā dvisāhasraṃ sārdhaikaśatamīritam \|\| 61 \|\|*

*śatarudrantathā koṭirudraṃ vyomayugādhikam \|*  
*dvisāhasraṃ ca dviśataṃ tathomaṃ bhūsahasrakam \|\| 62 \|\|*

*catvāriṃśatsāṣṭaśataṃ kailāsaṃ bhūsahasrakam \|*  
*catvāriṃśacca dviśataṃ vāyavīyamataḥ param \|\| 63 \|\|*

*catussāhasrasaṃkhyākamevaṃ saṃkhyāvibhedataḥ \|*  
*śrutamparamapuṇyantu purāṇaṃ śivasaṃjñakam \|\| 64 \|\|*

61-64. Vidyeśvara contains two thousand verses, Rudra ten thousand five hundred; Śatarudra two thousand one hundred and eighty; Koṭirudra two thousand two hundred and forty; Umā one thousand eight hundred and forty; Kailāsa one thousand two hundred and forty and the Vāyavīya four thousand verses. Thus is the holy text of Śivapurāṇa.

## \|\| 11.1.65 \|\|

*catuḥsāhasrakaṃ yattu vāyavīyamudīritam \|*  
*tadidaṃ vartayiṣyāmi bhāgadvayasamanvitam \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. I shall now begin the Vāyavīya containing four thousand verses and consisting of two parts.

## \|\| 11.1.66 \|\|

*nāvedaviduṣe vācyamidaṃ śāstramanuttamam \|*  
*na caivāśraddhadhānāya nāpurāṇavide tathā \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. This excellent Śāstra shall not be mentioned to one who is not conversant with the Vedas nor to one who has no faith nor to one who does not know the Purāṇas.

## \|\| 11.1.67 \|\|

*parīkṣitāya śiṣyāya dhārmikāyānasūyave \|*  
*pradeyaṃ śivabhaktāya śivadharmānusāriṇe \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. It shall be given to a tested virtuous disciple uncontaminated by malice. He shall be a devotee of Śiva and a follower of the Śaiva cult.

## \|\| 11.1.68 \|\|

*purāṇasaṃhitā yasya prasādānmayi vartate \|*  
*namo bhagavate tasmai vyāsāyāmitatejase \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Obeisance to the holy sage Vyāsa of brilliant splendour whose grace has endowed me with the Purāṇic lore.

## Chapter 2 - The problem of the sages

## \|\| 11.2.1-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*purā kālena mahatā kalpetīte punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*asminnupasthite kalpe pravṛtte sṛṣṭhikarmaṇi \|\| 1 \|\|*

*pratiṣṭhitāyāṃ vārtāyāṃ prabuddhāsu prajāsu ca \|*  
*munīnāṃ ṣaṭkulīyānāṃ bruvatāmitaretaram \|\| 2 \|\|*

*idaṃ paramidaṃ neti vivādassumahānabhūt \|*  
*parasya durnirūpatvānna jātastatra niścayaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:—

1-3. When a long time had elapsed, many kalpas had come and gone, the present kalpa had started, the activity of creation had begun, and the customs among the enlightened subjects had become established, a dispute arose among the sages of six clans. One said “This is the greatest being.” Another said, “It is not.” Because the greatest being could not be reviewed or defined no conclusion was arrived at.

## \|\| 11.2.4 \|\|

*te 'bhijagmurvidhātāraṃ draṣṭuṃ brahmāṇamavyayam \|*  
*yatrāste bhagavān brahmā stūyamānassurāsuraiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. In order to see the eternal creator they went where the lord was staying eulogised by gods and Asuras.

## \|\| 11.2.5-6 \|\|

*meruśṛṃge śubhe ramye devadānavasaṃkule \|*  
*siddhacāraṇasaṃvāde yakṣagaṃdharvasevite \|\| 5 \|\|*

*vihaṃgasaṃghasaṃghuṣṭe maṇividrumabhūṣite \|*  
*nikuṃjakaṃdaradarīgṛhānirjharaśobhite \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. It was on the auspicious and charming peak of Meru, where there were plenty of gods and Asuras where Siddhas and Cāraṇas thronged, where Yakṣas and Gandharvas frequented, where flocks of birds chirped and crow, which was embellished by jewels and corals and which shone due to streams and rivulets, caves and crevices, bushes and hedges.

## \|\| 11.2.7-8 \|\|

*tatra brahmavanaṃ nāma nānāmṛgasamākulam \|*  
*daśayojanavistīrṇaṃ śatayojanamāyatam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*surasāmalapānīyapūrṇaramyasarovaram \|*  
*mattabhramarasaṃchannaramyapuṣpitapādapam \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. There was a forest Brahmavana which abounded in different species of deer. It was ten Yojanas wide and hundred Yojanas long. There were beautiful lakes full of sweet and clean water. It had plenty of trees in full bloom where swarms of bees hummed and hovered.

## \|\| 11.2.9 \|\|

*taruṇādityasaṃkāśaṃ tatra cāru mahatpuram \|*  
*durdharṣabaladṛptānāṃ daityadānavarakṣasām \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. This was a great city as beautiful and brilliant as the midday sun. It could not be attacked by the haughty Daityas, Dānavas and Rākṣasas.

## \|\| 11.2.10 \|\|

*taptajāṃbūnadamayaṃ prāṃśuprākāratoraṇam \|*  
*nirvyūhavalabhīkūṭapratolīśatamaṃḍitam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. It had lofty ramparts and portals made of molten gold. It was embellished by hundreds of main streets, turrets and wooden ceilings.

## \|\| 11.2.11 \|\|

*mahārhamaṇicitrābhirlelihānamivāṃbaram \|*  
*mahābhavanakoṭībhiranekābhiralaṃkṛtam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. It appeared to lick the sky with crores of huge mansions set with precious gems of variegated colours. It was decorated with many such mansions.

## \|\| 11.2.12-13 \|\|

*tasminnivasati brahmā sabhyaiḥ sārdhaṃ prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*tatra gatvā mahātmānaṃ sākṣāllokapitāmaham \|\| 12 \|\|*

*daddaśurmunayo devā devarṣigaṇasevitam \|*  
*śuddhacāmīkaraprakhyaṃ sarvābharaṇabhūṣitam \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. Lord Brahmā resides there along with his councillors. Going there the sages saw the lord, the noble Ātman served by the groups of gods and sages. He was shining like pure gold. Ho was bedecked in all ornaments.

## \|\| 11.2.14 \|\|

*prasannavadanaṃ saumyaṃ padmapatrāyatekṣaṇam \|*  
*divyakāṃtisamāyuktaṃ divyagaṃdhānulepanam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. He was gentle with delightful face. His eyes were as large as the petals of a lotus. He was endowed with a divine lustre. He had smeared divine unguents and scents.

## \|\| 11.2.15 \|\|

*divyaśuklāṃbaradharaṃ divyamālāvibhūṣitam \|*  
*surāsurendrayogīṃdravaṃdyamānapadāṃbujam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. He was clad in brilliant white garments. He was bedecked in divine garlands. His lotus-like feet were saluted by the gods, Asuras and leading yogins.

## \|\| 11.2.16 \|\|

*sarvalakṣaṇayuktāṃgyā labdhacāmarahastayā \|*  
*bhrājamānaṃ sarasvatyā prabhayeva divākaram \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Accompanied by Sarasvatī whose body had all auspicious marks who held the chowries in her hands, he shone as the sun with his dazzling light.

## \|\| 11.2.17 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā munayassarve prasannavadanekṣaṇāḥ \|*  
*śirasyaṃjalimādhāya tuṣṭuvussurapuṃgavam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. On seeing him the sages were delighted and their eyes and faces shone. With palms joined in reverence and held over their heads they eulogised the leading god.

## \|\| 11.2.18 \|\|

*munaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*namastrimūrtaye tubhyaṃ sargasthityaṃtahetave \|*  
*puruṣāya purāṇāya brahmaṇe paramātmane \|\| 18 \|\|*

The sages said:—

18\. Obeisance to you in the form of Trinity, the cause of creation, sustenance and annihilation, the ancient Puruṣa, Brahmā the great Ātman.

## \|\| 11.2.19 \|\|

*namaḥ pradhānadehāya pradhānakṣobhakāriṇe \|*  
*trayoviṃśatibhedena vikṛtāyāvikāriṇe \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Obeisance to the deity who has Prakṛti for his body, who is the cause of quickening Pradhāna, who though transformed into twenty-three principles is yet free from aberration.

## \|\| 11.2.20 \|\|

*namo brahmāṇḍadehāya brahmāṃḍodaravartine \|*  
*tatra saṃsiddhakāryāya saṃsiddhakaraṇāya ca \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Obeisance to the deity who has universe for his body, who is stationed within the belly of the universe, who has accomplished his task and whose body is perfectly accomplished.

## \|\| 11.2.21 \|\|

*namostu sarvalokāya sarvalokavidhāyine \|*  
*sarvātmadehasaṃyoga viyogavidhihetave \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Obeisance to the deity identical with the world, the creator, the sustainer and the annihilator of the world.

## \|\| 11.2.22 \|\|

*tvayaiva nikhilaṃ sṛṣṭaṃ saṃhṛtaṃ pālitaṃ jagat \|*  
*tathāpi māyayā nātha na vidmastvāṃ pitāmaha \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O Brahmā, it is by you alone that the entire universe is created, sustained and annihilated. Still, due to illusion, O lord, we do not know you.

## \|\| 11.2.23 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ brahmā mahābhāgairmaharṣibhirabhiṣṭutaḥ \|*  
*prāha gaṃbhīrayā vācā munīn prahlādayanniva \|\| 23 \|\|*

Sūta said:—

23\. Thus eulogised by the fortunate sages, Brahmā spoke to the sages in a majestic tone delighting them.

## \|\| 11.2.24 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ṛṣayo he mahābhāgā mahāsattvā mahaujasaḥ \|*  
*kimarthaṃ sahitāssarve yūyamatra samāgatāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

24\. O blessed sages of great splendour and strength, why have you come here all together?

## \|\| 11.2.25 \|\|

*tamevaṃvādinaṃ devaṃ brahmāṇaṃ brahmavittamāḥ \|*  
*vāgbhirvinayagarbhābhissarve prāṃjalayo 'bruvan \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The sages foremost of those who know Brahman spoke with palms joined in reverence, with words couched in humility to lord Brahmā who spoke thus.

## \|\| 11.2.26 \|\|

*munaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*bhagavannaṃdhakāreṇa mahatā vayamāvṛtāḥ \|*  
*khinnā vivadamānāśca na paśyāmo 'tra yatparam \|\| 26 \|\|*

The sages said:—

26\. O lord, we have been encompassed in deep darkness. We are distressed. Unable to understand the greatest being we are arguing among ourselves.

## \|\| 11.2.27 \|\|

*tvaṃ hi sarvajagaddhātā sarvakāraṇakāraṇam \|*  
*tvayā hyaviditaṃ nātha neha kiṃcana vidyate \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Indeed you are the creator of the universe. You are the cause of all causes. O lord, there is nothing here not known to you.

## \|\| 11.2.28 \|\|

*kaḥ pumān sarvasattvebhyaḥ purāṇaḥ puruṣaḥ paraḥ \|*  
*viśuddhaḥ paripūrṇaśca śāśvataḥ parameśvaraḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Who is that being more ancient than all living beings? Who is the greatest Puruṣa? Who is the purest, perfect, and eternal Being?

## \|\| 11.2.29 \|\|

*kenaiva citrakṛtyena prathamaṃ sṛjyate jagat \|*  
*tattvaṃ vada mahāprājña svasaṃdehāpanuttaye \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Who by indulging in wonderful activities has created the universe? O intelligent lord, please mention it and quell our doubts.

## \|\| 11.2.30-31 \|\|

*evaṃ pṛṣṭastadā brahmā vismayasmeravīkṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*devānāṃ dānavānāṃ ca munīnāmapi sannidhau \|\| 30 \|\|*

*utthāya suciraṃ dhyātvā rudra ityuddharan girim \|*  
*ānaṃdaklinnasarvāṃgaḥ kṛtāṃjalirabhāṣata \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. Thus questioned, Brahmā, with smiling eyes, stood up and meditated for long in the presence of the gods, Dānavas and sages. Uttering the words “Rudra” he joined his palms in reverence, with a blissful sensation moistening his body and spoke.

## Chapter 3 - The Naimiṣa episode

## \|\| 11.3.1-4 \|\|

*brahamovāca \|*  
*yato vāco nivartaṃte aprāpya manasā saha \|*  
*ānaṃdaṃ yasya vai vidvānna bibheti kutaścana \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yasmātsarvamidaṃ brahmaviṣṇurudrendrapūrvakam \|*  
*saha bhūtendriyaiḥ sarvaiḥ prathamaṃ saṃprasūyate \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kāraṇānāṃ ca yo dhātā dhyātā paramakāraṇam \|*  
*na saṃprasūyate 'nyasmātkutaścana kadācana \|\| 3 \|\|*

*sarvaiśvaryeṇa saṃpanno nāmnā sarveśvaraḥ svayam \|*  
*sarvairmumukṣubhirdhyeyaśśaṃbhurākāśamadhyagaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

1-4. Śiva stationed in the middle of the ether shall be meditated upon by those desirous of salvation; Śiva from whom the words recede not approaching him along with the mind; knowing and realising whose bliss-form one has no fear from anywhere; from whom every thing inclusive of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Indra, the elements, the sense-organs, is born at first, who is the creator, meditator and ultimate cause of all causes; who is not born from anything else at any time; who is endowed with glory and prosperity and who is known as Sarveśvara.

## \|\| 11.3.5 \|\|

*yo 'gre māṃ vidadhe putraṃ jñānaṃ ca prahiṇoti me \|*  
*tatprasādānmayālabdhaṃ prājāpatyamidaṃ padam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. It was he who created me at the outset as his son and gave me perfect knowledge. It was due to his grace that the lordship of the people was attained by me.

## \|\| 11.3.6 \|\|

*īśo vṛkṣa iva stabdho ya eko divi tiṣṭhati \|*  
*yenedamakhilaṃ pūrṇaṃ puruṣeṇa mahātmanā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He is the lord who stands in heaven like the lofty stump of a tree; and by whom, by the Puruṣa, the great Ātman, all this is filled up.

## \|\| 11.3.7 \|\|

*eko bahūnāṃ jaṃtūnāṃ niṣkriyāṇāṃ ca sakriyaḥ \|*  
*ya eko bahudhā bījaṃ karoti sa maheśvaraḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. He is active among the inactive creatures; he who being single himself creates many is Maheśvara.

## \|\| 11.3.8 \|\|

*jīvairebhirimāṃllokānsarvānīśo ya īśate \|*  
*ya eko bhāgavānrudro na dvitīyo 'sti kaścana \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He rules over all the worlds through the Jīvas. He is the only lord Rudra. There is none second to him.

## \|\| 11.3.9 \|\|

*sadā janānāṃ hṛdaye saṃniviṣṭo 'pi yaḥ paraiḥ \|*  
*alakṣyo lakṣayanviśvamadhitiṣṭhati sarvadā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Though he has entered and is ever present in the hearts of the people he is invisible to others; he occupies and views at the universe always.

## \|\| 11.3.10 \|\|

*yastu kālātpramuktāni kāraṇānyakhilānyapi \|*  
*anantaśaktirevaiko bhagavānadhitiṣṭhati \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. He is the sole lord of infinite Śakti who presides over all causes and is released from Time—Death.

## \|\| 11.3.11 \|\|

*na yasya divaso rātrirna samāno na cādhikaḥ \|*  
*svabhāvikī parāśaktirnityā jñānakriye api \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He has neither day nor night; neither equals nor superiors. The great knowledge and activity is innate in him.

## \|\| 11.3.12 \|\|

*yadidaṃ kṣaramavyaktaṃ yadapyamṛtamakṣaram \|*  
*tāvubhāvakṣarātmānāveko devaḥ svayaṃ haraḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. That which is perishable and unmanifest, that which is imperishable and immortal—both these have the imperishable as their Ātman. The sole lord is Śiva himself.

## \|\| 11.3.13 \|\|

*īśate tadabhidhyānādyojanāsattvabhāvanaḥ \|*  
*bhūyo hyasya paśorante viśvamāyā nivartate \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. By concentrating on him, the person of Sāttvaic feelings becomes the lord himself. At the end the universal illusion recedes from him.

## \|\| 11.3.14 \|\|

*yasminna bhāsate vidyunna sūryo na ca candramāḥ \|*  
*yasya bhāsā vibhātīdamityeṣā śāśvatī śrutiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The eternal Śruti says “In whom neither the lightning flashes nor the sun blazes nor the moon sheds light and by whose brilliance this universe comes in the limelight.”

## \|\| 11.3.15 \|\|

*eko devo mahādevo vijñeyastu maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*na tasya paramaṃ kiṃcitpadaṃ samadhigamyate \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. That lord Śiva shall be realised. There is no other region greater than his worthy of attainment.

## \|\| 11.3.16 \|\|

*ayamādiranādyantassvabhāvādeva nirmalaḥ \|*  
*svatantraḥ paripūrṇaśca svecchādhīnaścarācaraḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Hr is the cause. He has no beginning, no end. He is naturally purr, independent and perfect. The mobile and immobile beings are subservient to his will.

## \|\| 11.3.17 \|\|

*aprākṛtavapuḥ śrīmāṃllakṣyalakṣaṇavarjitaḥ \|*  
*ayaṃ mukto mocakaśca hyakālaḥ kālacodakaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. His body is not the creation of Prakṛti. He is glorious, devoid of examples and definitions. He is both the liberated and liberator. He is not influenced by Time. He is the activiser of time.

## \|\| 11.3.18 \|\|

*sarvoparikṛtāvāsassarvāvāsaśca sarvavit \|*  
*ṣaḍvidhādhvamayasyāsya sarvasya jagataḥ patiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He has taken up residence above all. He is the repository of all. He is the knower of all. He is the lord of the universe comprising the sixfold path.

## \|\| 11.3.19 \|\|

*uttarottarabhūtānāmuttaraśca niruttaraḥ \|*  
*anantānantasandohamakaraṃdamadhuvrataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. He is the Being above all beings, one above the other. There is no being above him. He is the bee imbibing the honey of endless bliss.

## \|\| 11.3.20 \|\|

*akhaṃḍajagadaṃḍānāṃ piṃḍīkaraṇapaṃḍitaḥ \|*  
*audāryavīryagāṃbhīryamādhuryamakarālayaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. He is an expert in solidifying the unsevered cosmic

eggs. He is the ocean of benevolence, prowess, majesty and sweetness.

## \|\| 11.3.21 \|\|

*naivāsya sadṛśaṃ vastu nādhikaṃ cāpi kiṃcana \|*  
*atulaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ rājarājaśca tiṣṭhati \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. There is no object equal to him or excelling him. He stands as the unparalleled Emperor of all living beings.

## \|\| 11.3.22 \|\|

*anena citrakṛtyena prathamaṃ sṛjyate jagat \|*  
*aṃtakāle punaścedaṃ tasminpralayameṣyate \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The universe is created by him indulging in wonderful activities. At the time of dissolution this gets dissolved in him.

## \|\| 11.3.23 \|\|

*asya bhūtāni vaśyāni ayaṃ sarvaniyojakaḥ \|*  
*ayaṃ tu parayā bhaktyā dṛśyate nānyathā kvacit \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The living beings are under his control. He is the employer of all. He is seen by great devotion and not otherwise.

## \|\| 11.3.24 \|\|

*vratāni sarvadānāni tapāṃsi niyamāstathā \|*  
*kathitāni purā sadbhirbhāvārthaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Sacred rites, charitable gifts, penances and observances, these are advocated by people for the purification of emotions. There is no doubt in this.

## \|\| 11.3.25 \|\|

*hariścāhaṃ ca rudraśca tathānye ca surāsurāḥ \|*  
*tapobhirugrairadyāpi tasya darśanakāṃkṣiṇaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Viṣṇu, I, Rudra, gods and Asuras are desirous of seeing him even today by performing great penances.

## \|\| 11.3.26 \|\|

*adṛśyaḥ patitairmūḍhairdurjanairapi kutsitaiḥ \|*  
*bhaktairantarbahiścāpi pūjyaḥ saṃbhāṣya eva ca \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. He is invisible to fallen wicked men, the despicable and the stupid. He is worshipped within and without by devotees and can be spoken to.

## \|\| 11.3.27-28 \|\|

*tadidaṃ trividhaṃ rūpaṃ sthūlaṃ sūkṣmaṃ tataḥ param \|*  
*asmadādyamarairdṛśyaṃ sthūlaṃ sūkṣmaṃ tu yogibhiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*tataḥ paraṃ tu yannityaṃ jñānamānaṃdamavyayam \|*  
*tanniṣṭhaistatparairbhaktairdṛśyaṃ tadvratamāśritaiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. Forms in the universe are threefold—the gross, subtle and that which is beyond. The gross is seen by us, the gods and others. The subtle is seen by the Yogins. That which is beyond the two, is eternal, knowledge, bliss and the unchanging can be seen by those who dwell in it, are devoted to it and are engaged in the rites concerning it.

## \|\| 11.3.29 \|\|

*bahunātra kimuktena guhyādguhyataraṃ param \|*  
*śive bhaktirna sandehastayā yukto vimucyate \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Of what avail is much talk? Devotion to Śiva is the secret of secrets. He who is endowed with it becomes liberated. There is no doubt in this.

## \|\| 11.3.30 \|\|

*prasādādeva sā bhaktiḥ prasādo bhaktisaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*yathā cāṃkurato bījaṃ bījato vā yathāṃkuraḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Devotion is the result of grace and grace is the result of devotion just as the sprout comes out of the seed and produces the seed.

## \|\| 11.3.31 \|\|

*prasādapūrvikā eva paśossarvatra siddhayaḥ \|*  
*sa eva sādhanairante sarvairapi ca sādhyate \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The achievements of the individual are due to the grace of God. Lord alone is achieved in the end through all the means.

## \|\| 11.3.32 \|\|

*prasādasādhanaṃ dharmassa ca vedena darśitaḥ \|*  
*tadabhyāsavaśātsāmyaṃ pūrvayoḥ puṇyapāpayoḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Virtue and holy rites constitute the means for the attainment of grace. That is indicated by the Vedas. By practising Dharma the sins and merits are levelled to equality.

## \|\| 11.3.33 \|\|

*sāmyātprasādasaṃparko dharmasyātiśayastataḥ \|*  
*dharmātiśayamāsādya paśoḥ pāpaparikṣayaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Contact with grace yields excellence of Dharma. After attaining this excellence the sins of the individual decline.

## \|\| 11.3.34 \|\|

*evaṃ prakṣīṇapāpasya bahubhirjanmabhiḥ kramāt \|*  
*sāṃbe sarveśvare bhaktirjñānapūrvā prajāyate \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. When his sins decline through succession of births the devotion to Sarveśvara and Ambā is generated along with knowledge.

## \|\| 11.3.35 \|\|

*bhāvānuguṇamīśasya prasādo vyatiricyate \|*  
*prasādātkarmasaṃtyāgaḥ phalato na svarūpataḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The grace of the lord varies in accordance with the purity of emotions. Due to grace, eschewment of rites results. Here the eschewment is of the fruits of rites and not the rites themselves.

## \|\| 11.3.36 \|\|

*tasmātkarmaphalatyāgācchivadharmānvayaḥ śubhaḥ \|*  
*sa ca gurvanapekṣaśca tadapekṣa iti dvidhā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. As a result of the abandonment of the desire for the fruits of holy rites, the auspicious Śaivite virtues are attained. This is twofold: that dependent on the preceptor and that which is not.

## \|\| 11.3.37 \|\|

*tatrānapekṣātsāpekṣo mukhyaḥ śataguṇādhikaḥ \|*  
*śivadharmānvayasyāsya śivajñānasamanvayaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. That which is dependent on the preceptor is more important and hundred times more efficacious since in the Śaivite creed there is an association of Śaivite knowledge.

## \|\| 11.3.38 \|\|

*jñanānvayavaśātpuṃsaḥ saṃsāre doṣadarśanam \|*  
*tato viṣayavairāgyaṃ vairāgyādbhāvasādhanam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. In view of the knowledge the man sees the defects in the worldly existence (saṃsāra). Thereafter arises non-attachment to the sensual objects and thence Bhāva is attained.

## \|\| 11.3.39 \|\|

*bhāvasiddhyupapannasya dhyāne niṣṭhā na karmaṇi \|*  
*jñānadhyānābhiyuktasya puṃso yogaḥ pravartate \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. When Bhāva is attained the man becomes more inclined towards meditation than towards rituals. A man endowed with knowledge and meditation becomes engaged in Yoga.

## \|\| 11.3.40 \|\|

*yogena tu parā bhaktiḥ prasādastadanaṃtaram \|*  
*prasādānmucyate jaṃturmuktaḥ śivasamo bhavet \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Through Yoga arises the great, devotion and then grace of God. By means of the grace the creature is liberated and becomes equal to Śiva.

## \|\| 11.3.41 \|\|

*anugrahaprakārasya kramo 'yamavivakṣitaḥ \|*  
*yādṛśī yogyatā puṃsastasya tādṛganugrahaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The different modes of blessings may not be in the order mentioned. The blessing is based on the ability of the man.

## \|\| 11.3.42 \|\|

*garbhastho mucyate kaścijjāyamānastathāparaḥ \|*  
*bālo vā taruṇo vātha vṛddho vā mucyate paraḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Some soul is liberated even while in the womb; another even while being born; a third whether he be a boy or a youth or an old man.

## \|\| 11.3.43 \|\|

*tiryagyonigataḥ kaścinmucyate nārako 'paraḥ \|*  
*aparastu padaṃ prāpto mucyate svapadakṣaye \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. A soul born as a lower species, a soul undergoing torture in hell, a soul achieving a heavenly region may be liberated when the tenure is over.

## \|\| 11.3.44 \|\|

*kaścitkṣīṇapado bhūtvā punarāvartya mucyate \|*  
*kaścidadhvagatastasmin sthitvāsthitvā vimucyate \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Some soul may return after the enjoyment of heavenly region and then liberated. Still another soul may be liberated on its way.

## \|\| 11.3.45 \|\|

*tasmānnaikaprakāreṇa narāṇāṃ muktiriṣyate \|*  
*jñānabhāvānurūpeṇa prasādenaiva nirvṛtiḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Hence there is no stipulated mode or order in the attainment of liberation. The supreme bliss is in accordance

with the knowledge and emotion and attained by the grace of the lord.

## \|\| 11.3.46-48 \|\|

*tasmādasya prasādārthaṃ vāṅmanodoṣavarjitāḥ \|*  
*dhyāyaṃtaśśivamevaikaṃ sadāratanayāgnayaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*tanniṣṭhāstatparāssarve tadyuktāstadupāśrayāḥ \|*  
*sarvakriyāḥ prakurvāṇāstameva manasāgatāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*dīrghasūtrasamārabdhaṃ divyavarṣasahasrakam \|*  
*satrāṃte maṃtrayogena vāyustatra gamiṣyati \|\| 48 \|\|*

46-48. Hence, in order to win his grace you shall avoid verbal and mental defects; meditate on Śiva alone along with your wives, sons and others; abide by him; be attached to him. You shall associate with him, resort to him, do holy rites with your minds fixed in him, continue a long sacrifice for a thousand divine years. At the end of the sacrifice due to the efficacy of the mantras Vāyu will come there.

## \|\| 11.3.49-50 \|\|

*sa eva bhavataḥ śreyaḥ sopāyaṃ kathayiṣyati \|*  
*tato vārāṇasī puṇyā purī paramaśobhanā \|\| 49 \|\|*

*gaṃtavyā yatra viśveśo devyā saha pinākadhṛk \|*  
*sadā viharati śrīmān bhaktānugrahakāraṇāt \|\| 50 \|\|*

49-50. He will tell you what is good for you along with the means. Then you shall go to the holy and auspicious city of Vārāṇasī where the glorious trident-bearing lord sports about with the goddess for blessing his devotees.

## \|\| 11.3.51 \|\|

*tatrāścaryaṃ mahaddṛṣṭvā matsamīpaṃ gamiṣyatha \|*  
*tato vaḥ kathayiṣyāmi mokṣopāya dvijottamāḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. O excellent brahmins, after seeing the great wonder therein you come to me again. Then I shall tell you the means of salvation.

## \|\| 11.3.52 \|\|

*yenaikajanmanā muktiryuṣmatkaratale sthitā \|*  
*anekajanmasaṃsārabaṃdhanirmokṣakāriṇī \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Thereby in a single birth, salvation comes within your reach, salvation which sets you free from the bondage of births and transmigrations.

## \|\| 11.3.53 \|\|

*etanmanomayaṃ cakraṃ mayā sṛṣṭaṃ visṛjyate \|*  
*yatrāsya śīryate nemiḥ sa deśastapasaśśubhaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Now I am releasing this mentally created wheel. The place where its rim gets shattered is auspicious for your penance.

## \|\| 11.3.54 \|\|

*ityuktvā sūryasaṃkāśaṃ cakraṃ dṛṣṭvā manomayam \|*  
*praṇipatya mahādevaṃ visasarja pitāmahaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. After saying this Brahmā created a mental wheel as bright as the sun. After bowing to lord Śiva he released it.

## \|\| 11.3.55 \|\|

*te 'pi hṛṣṭatarā viprāḥ praṇamya jagatāṃ prabhum \|*  
*prayayustasya cakrasya yatra nemiraśīryata \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Those delighted brahmins bowed to the lord and pursued the wheel to the place where its rim got shattered.

## \|\| 11.3.56 \|\|

*cakraṃ tadapi saṃkṣiptaṃ ślakṣṇaṃ cāruśilātale \|*  
*vimalasvādupānīye nijapāta vane kvacit \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The wheel thus hurled fell on a smooth charming rock in a certain forest where the water was sweet and clear.

## \|\| 11.3.57 \|\|

*tadvanaṃ tena vikhyātaṃ naimiṣaṃ munipūjitam \|*  
*anekayakṣagaṃdharvavidyādharasamākulam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. That forest became famous as Naimiṣa. It is worshipped by the sages. It abounds in Yakṣas, Gandharvas, and Vidyādharas.

## \|\| 11.3.58-59 \|\|

*aṣṭādaśa samudrasya dvīpānaśnanpurūravāḥ \|*  
*vilāsavaśamurvaśyā yāto daivena coditaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*akrameṇa haranmohādyajñavāṭaṃ hiraṇmayam \|*  
*munibhiryatra saṃkruddhaiḥ kuśavajrairnipātitaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

58-59. Indulging in sexual dalliance with Urvaśī, Purūravas was moving about in the eighteen islands in the ocean. Urged by fate he came to this place and foolishly spoiled the golden sacrificial altar here. The infuriated sages hurled Kuśa grass at him which Had the power of thunderbolt and felled him to the ground.

## \|\| 11.3.60 \|\|

*viśvaṃ sisṛkṣamāṇā vai yatra viśvasṛjaḥ purā \|*  
*satramārebhire divyaṃ brahmajñā gārhapatyagāḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Formerly the Viśvasṛja Brahmeśa householders desirous of creating the universe began a divine sacrifice here.

## \|\| 11.3.61 \|\|

*ṛṣibhiryatra vidvadbhiḥ śabdārthanyāyakovidaiḥ \|*  
*śaktiprajñākriyāyogairvidhirāsīdanuṣṭhitaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. There had been many scholarly sages here experts in words, meanings and logical arguments. They performed rites by their power of intellect and yogic practice.

## \|\| 11.3.62 \|\|

*yatra vedavido nityaṃ vedavādabahiṣkṛtān \|*  
*vādajalpabalairghnaṃti vacobhirativādinaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Here persons well-versed in the Vedas refute those who are excluded from Vedic path by their power of arguments. They speak eloquently.

## \|\| 11.3.63 \|\|

*sphaṭikamayamahībhṛtpādajābhyaśśilābhyaḥ prasaradamṛtakalpassvacchapānīyaramyam \|*  
*atirasaphalavṛkṣaprāyamavyālasattvaṃ tapasa ucitamāsīnnaimiṣaṃ tanmunīnām \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. This Naimiṣa forest was the fitting place for the penance of the sages. It was beautiful with nectarine clear water flowing from the bottom rocks of the crystalline mountain. It abounded in fruit-bearing trees and was free from beasts of prey.

## Chapter 4 - The advent of Vāyu

## \|\| 11.4.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tasmindeśe mahābhāgā munayaśśaṃsitavratāḥ \|*  
*arcayaṃto mahādevaṃ satramārebhire tadā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sūta said:—

1\. The fortunate sages of devout rites worshipped lord Śiva and began their sacrifice there.

## \|\| 11.4.2 \|\|

*tacca satraṃ pravavṛte sarvāścaryaṃ maharṣiṇām \|*  
*viśvaṃ sisṛkṣamāṇānāṃ purā viśvasṛjāmiva \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The sacrifice of the sages functioned evoking wonder in everyone like that of the Viśvasṛjas formerly who were desirous of creating the universe.

## \|\| 11.4.3 \|\|

*atha kāle gate satre samāpte bhūridakṣiṇe \|*  
*pitāmahaniyogena vāyustatrāgamatsvayam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. After sometime when the Satra had concluded with the distribution of manifold gifts Vāyu himself came there at the instance of Brahmā.

## \|\| 11.4.4-7 \|\|

*śiṣyassvayaṃbhuvo devassarvapratyakṣadṛgvaśī \|*  
*ājñāyāṃ maruto yasya saṃsthitāssaptasaptakāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*prerayañchaśvadaṃgāni prāṇādyābhiḥ svavṛttibhiḥ \|*  
*sarvabhūtaśarīrāṇāṃ kurute yaśca dhāraṇam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*aṇimādibhiraṣṭābhiraiśvaryaiśca samanvitaḥ \|*  
*tiryakkālādibhirmedhyairbhuvanāni bibharti yaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*ākāśayonirdviguṇaḥ sparśaśabdasamanvayāt \|*  
*tejasāṃ prakṛtiśceti yamāhustattvaciṃtakāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

4-7. Vāyu the disciple of Brahmā, the self-controlled lord who perceives everything directly; in whose bidding stay the forty-nine Maruts always; who sustains the bodies of all living beings urging them perpetually by his own functionaries Prāṇa and others; who is endowed with the eightfold glories; who supports the worlds with his holy hands; who is born of Ākāśa; who possesses the two qualities of touch and sound and whom the philosophers call the material cause of fiery principle.

## \|\| 11.4.8 \|\|

*tamāśramagataṃ dṛṣṭvā munayo dīrghasatriṇaḥ \|*  
*pitāmahavacaḥ smṛtvā praharṣamatulaṃ yayuḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. On seeing him at the hermitage the sages who were busy in a long Satra remembered the words of Brahmā and felt unequalled pleasure.

## \|\| 11.4.9 \|\|

*abhyutthāya tatassarve praṇamyāṃbarasaṃbhavam \|*  
*cāmīkaramayaṃ tasmai viṣṭaraṃ samakalpayan \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Standing up they welcomed and bowed to him. They offered him a golden seat.

## \|\| 11.4.10 \|\|

*sopi tatra samāsīno munibhissamyagarcitaḥ \|*  
*pratinaṃdya ca tān sarvān papraccha kuśalaṃ tataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. He seated himself there and was worshipped by the sages. Congratulating them he enquired after their health.

## \|\| 11.4.11 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*atra vaḥ kuśalaṃ viprāḥ kaccidvṛtte mahākratau \|*  
*kaccidyajñahano daityā na bādheransuradviṣaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

11\. O brahmins, hope you are all quite well, now that this great sacrifice has concluded. Hope that the Asuras, the enemies of the gods, the destroyers of sacrifices do not harass you.

## \|\| 11.4.12-13 \|\|

*prāyaścittaṃ duriṣṭaṃ vā na kaccitsamajāyata \|*  
*stotraśastragṛhairdevān pitḥn pitryaiśca karmabhiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*kaccidabhyarcya yuṣmābhirvidhirāsītsvanuṣṭhitaḥ \|*  
*nivṛtte ca mahāsatre paścātkiṃ vaścikīrṣitam \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. Hope that imprecations and expiatory rites do not take place. Hope that the rites are duly performed by you after worshipping the gods, with Stotra and Śastra hymns and the ancestors with the rites due to them. What do you propose to do afterwards, now that the great Satra has been concluded?

## \|\| 11.4.14 \|\|

*ityuktā munayaḥ sarve vāyunā śivabhāvinā \|*  
*prahṛṣṭamanasaḥ pūtāḥ pratyūcurvinayānvitāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. When addressed thus by Vāyu, the meditator on Śiva, the sages were delighted in their minds. They considered themselves sanctified. They replied thus humbly.

## \|\| 11.4.15 \|\|

*munaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*adya naḥ kuśalaṃ sarvamadya sādhu bhavettapaḥ \|*  
*asmacchreyobhivṛddhyarthaṃ bhavānatrāgato yataḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Today we have attained bliss; our penances are rendered fruitful since you have come for the increase of our welfare.

## \|\| 11.4.16 \|\|

*śṛṇu cedaṃ purāvṛttaṃ tamasākrāṃtamānasaiḥ \|*  
*upāsitaḥ purāsmābhirvijñānārthaṃ prajāpatiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Listen to an old anecdote. Formerly we meditated on Prajāpati when we were overwhelmed by darkness. We wanted to acquire perfect knowledge.

## \|\| 11.4.17 \|\|

*sopyasmānanugṛhyāha śaraṇyaśśaraṇāgatān \|*  
*sarvasmādadhiko rudro viprāḥ paramakāraṇam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The lord Brahmā worthy of being sought refuge in, blessed us as we sought refuge in him and said, “O brahmins, Lord Rudra is superior to all. He is the ultimate cause.

## \|\| 11.4.18 \|\|

*tamapratarkyaṃ yāthātmyaṃ bhaktimāneva paśyati \|*  
*bhaktiścāsya prasādena prasādādeva nirvṛtiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Only the devotee sees the lord whose real nature cannot be reflected upon or argued over. Devotion is acquired through grace and through grace is bliss attained.

## \|\| 11.4.19 \|\|

*tasmādasya prasādārthaṃ naimiṣe satrayogataḥ \|*  
*yajadhvaṃ dīrghasatreṇa rudraṃ paramakāraṇam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Hence, in order to propitiate him perform the Satra. Worship him who is the ultimate cause, perform Satra in Naimiṣa extending over a long period.

## \|\| 11.4.20 \|\|

*tatprasādena satrāṃte vāyustatrāgamiṣyati \|*  
*tanmukhājjñānalābho vastatra śreyo bhaviṣyati \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. At the end of the Satra, by means of his grace Vāyu will come there. You will acquire perfect knowledge from his mouth and attain welfare.

## \|\| 11.4.21 \|\|

*ityādiśya vayaṃ sarve preṣitā parameṣṭhinā \|*  
*asmindeśe mahābhāga tavāgamanakāṃkṣiṇaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Commanding thus Brahmā sent us all to this place. O fortunate one, we were eagerly awaiting your arrival.

## \|\| 11.4.22 \|\|

*dīrghasatraṃ samāsīnā divyavarṣasahasrakam \|*  
*atastavāgamādanyatprārthyaṃ no nāsti kiṃcana \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. We sat and performed the Satra for a thousand divine years. We had nothing to wish for except your advent.

## \|\| 11.4.23 \|\|

*ityākarṇya purāvṛttamṛṣīṇāṃ dīrghasatriṇām \|*  
*vāyuḥ prītamanā bhūtvā tatrāsīnmunisaṃvṛtaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. On hearing thus this story of the sages who had performed the satra for a long time Vāyu was delighted in his mind and stayed there surrounded by the sages.

## \|\| 11.4.24 \|\|

*tatastairmunibhiḥ pṛṣṭasteṣāṃ bhāvavivṛddhaye \|*  
*sargādi śārvamaiśvaryaṃ samāsāda vadadvibhuḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. On being implored by the sages, the lord succinctly narrated the glory of Śiva beginning with creation in order to enhance their piety.

## Chapter 5 - The Principles of Śiva cult

## \|\| 11.5.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*tatra pūrvaṃ mahābhāgā naimiṣāraṇyavāsinaḥ \|*  
*praṇipatya yathānyāyaṃ papracchuḥ pavanaṃ prabhum \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sūta said:—

1\. There at the outset the fortunate residents of the Naimiṣa bowed duly to lord Vāyu and asked him.

## \|\| 11.5.2 \|\|

*naimiṣīyā ūcuḥ \|*  
*bhavān kathamanuprāpto jñānamīśvaragocaram \|*  
*kathaṃ ca śivabhāvaste brahmaṇo 'vyaktajanmanaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

The sages said:—

2\. How did you, sir, acquire the knowledge of Śiva? Wherefore is your devotion to Śiva, the Brahman whose birth is unmanifest.

## \|\| 11.5.3 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*ekonaviṃśatiḥ kalpo vijñeyaḥ śvetalohitaḥ \|*  
*tasminkalpe caturvaktrassraṣṭukāmo 'tapattapaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

3\. The twenty-first kalpa shall be known as Śvetalohita. In that kalpa the four-faced lord, desirous of creative activity performed a penance.

## \|\| 11.5.4-5 \|\|

*tapasā tena tīvreṇa tuṣṭastasya pitā svayam \|*  
*divyaṃ kaumāramāsthāya rūpaṃ rūpavatāṃ varaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*śveto nāma munirbhūtvā divyāṃ vācamudīrayan \|*  
*darśanaṃ pradadau tasmai devadevo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Delighted by his austere penance his father lord Śiva, foremost among the handsome assumed the divine form of a bechelor \[bachelor?\]. He became a sage Śveta and uttering divine.words appeared in front of him.

G. On seeing his father, Brahmā bowed to him and secured perfect knowledge along with Gāyatrī.

## \|\| 11.5.7 \|\|

*tatassa labdhavijñāno viśvakarmā caturmukhaḥ \|*  
*asṛjatsarvabhūtāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Having acquired knowledge, the four-faced lord created all living beings—the mobile and immobile.

## \|\| 11.5.8 \|\|

*yataśśrutvāmṛtaṃ labdhaṃ brahmaṇā parameśvarāt \|*  
*tatastadvadanādeva mayā labdhaṃ tapobalāt \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. That immortal knowledge was acquired by me through the power of penance from that face through which it was acquired by Brahmā.

## \|\| 11.5.9 \|\|

*munaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kiṃ tajjñānaṃ tvayā labdhaṃ tathyāttathyaṃtaraṃ śubham \|*  
*yatra kṛtvā parāṃ niṣṭhāṃ puruṣassukhamṛcchati \|\| 9 \|\|*

The sages said:—

9\. What is that knowledge attained by you—the knowledge that is auspicious, more truthful than the most truthful, abiding by which a man attains happiness.

## \|\| 11.5.10 \|\|

*vayuruvāca \|*  
*paśupāśapatijñānaṃ yallabdhaṃ tu mayā purā \|*  
*tatra niṣṭhā parā kāryā puruṣeṇa sukhārthinā \|\| 10 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

10\. Great and steady devotion shall be applied by a man who wishes for happiness, for the perfect knowledge of the individual soul, illusion and the lord who releases from the bondage.

## \|\| 11.5.11-12 \|\|

*ajñānaprabhavaṃ duḥkhaṃ jñānenaiva nivartate \|*  
*jñānaṃ vastuparicchedo vastu ca dvividhaṃ smṛtam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*ajaḍaṃ ca jaḍaṃ caiva niyaṃtṛ ca tayorapi \|*  
*paśuḥ pāśaḥ patiśceti kathyate tattrayaṃ kramāt \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Misery arises from ignorance. It is removed by knowledge that is a correct and precise comprehension of objects. Object is twofold: sentient and non-sentient. There is a controller of the two. The three are called Paśu, Pāśa and Pati.

## \|\| 11.5.13 \|\|

*akṣaraṃ ca kṣaraṃ caiva kṣarākṣaraparaṃ tathā \|*  
*tadetattritayaṃ bhūmnā kathyate tattvavedibhiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. On many occasions knowers of reality call the three by Akṣara, Kṣara and Kṣarākṣarapara.

## \|\| 11.5.14 \|\|

*akṣaraṃ paśurityuktaḥ kṣaraṃ pāśa udāhṛtaḥ \|*  
*kṣarākṣaraparaṃ yattatpatirityabhidhīyate \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The Paśu is called Akṣara. The Pāśa is called Kṣara. Pati is called Kṣarākṣarapara.

## \|\| 11.5.15 \|\|

*munaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kiṃ tadakṣaramityuktaṃ kiṃ ca kṣaramudāhṛtam \|*  
*tayośca paramaṃ kiṃ vā tadetadbrūhi māruta \|\| 15 \|\|*

The sages said:—

15\. O Māruta, please mention What is Kṣara? What is Akṣara? What is that which is greater and beyond these two?

## \|\| 11.5.16 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*prakṛtiḥ kṣaramityuktaṃ puruṣo 'kṣara ucyate \|*  
*tāvimau prerayatyanyassa parā parameśvaraḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

16\. Prakṛti is Kṣara. Puruṣa is Akṣara. The one who urges these two is the greatest Parameśvara.

## \|\| 11.5.17 \|\|

*munaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kaiṣā prakṛtirityuktā ka eṣa puruṣo mataḥ \|*  
*anayoḥ kena sambandhaḥ koyaṃ preraka īśvaraḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

The sages said:—

17\. What is this Prakṛti? Who is Puruṣa? What is the relationship between the two? Who is this instigator Īśvara?

## \|\| 11.5.18 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*māyā prakṛtiruddiṣṭā puruṣo māyayā vṛtaḥ \|*  
*saṃbandho mūlakarmabhyāṃ śivaḥ preraka īśvaraḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

18\. Māyā is the Prakṛti. Puruṣa is enveloped by Māyā. The relationship is through the root and Karman. Lord Śiva is the instigator.

## \|\| 11.5.19 \|\|

*munaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*keyaṃ māyā samā khyātā kiṃrūpo māyayā vṛtaḥ \|*  
*mūlaṃ kīdṛkkuto vāsya kiṃ śivatvaṃ kutaśśivaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

The sages said:—

19\. What is this Māyā that is mentioned? Of what form is he who is enveloped by Māyā? Of what nature is the root? Whence is it? What is Śivahood? Whence is Śiva?

## \|\| 11.5.20 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*māyā māheśvarī śaktiścidrūpo māyayā vṛtaḥ \|*  
*malaścicchādako naijo viśuddhiśśivatā svataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

20\. Māyā is the Śakti of Maheśvara. The form of Cit is enveloped by Māyā. The dirt is that which covers the Cit. Śivatva is his own innate purity.

## \|\| 11.5.21 \|\|

*munaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*āvṛṇoti kathaṃ māyā vyāpinaṃ kena hetunā \|*  
*kimarthaṃ cāvṛtiḥ puṃsaḥ kena vā vinivartate \|\| 21 \|\|*

The sages said:—

21\. How does the Māyā cover up the pervading one? What for? Why is this covering up of the Puruṣa? By what is it made to recede?

## \|\| 11.5.22 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*āvṛtirvyapino 'pi syādvyāpi yasmātkalādyapi \|*  
*hetuḥ karmaiva bhogārthaṃ nivarteta malakṣayāt \|\| 22 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

22\. Even a pervasive can he covered just as Kalā etc. that are pervasive. The cause is Karman alone. The purpose is enjoyment. It recedes when dirt is quelled.

## \|\| 11.5.23-24 \|\|

*munaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kalādi kathyate kiṃ tatkarma vā kimudāhṛtam \|*  
*tatkimādi kimantaṃ vā kiṃ phalaṃ vā kimāśrayam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*kasya bhogena kiṃ bhogyaṃ kiṃ vā tadbhogasādhanam \|*  
*malakṣayasya ko hetuḥ kīdṛkkṣīṇamalaḥ pumān \|\| 24 \|\|*

The sages said:—

23-24. What are these Kalā etc.? What is Karman? What its beginning and what its end? What the fruit? What the support? Whose enjoyment? What is enjoyed What is the means of enjoyment, the cause of the diminution of dirt? Of what nature is the Puruṣa devoid of dirt?

## \|\| 11.5.25-28 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*kalā vidyā ca rāgaśca kālo niyatireva ca \|*  
*kalādayassamākhyātā yo bhoktā puruṣo bhavet \|\| 25 \|\|*

*puṇyapāpātmakaṃ karma sukhaduḥkhaphalaṃ tu yat \|*  
*anādimalabhogāntamajñānātmasamāśrayam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*bhogaḥ karmavināśāya bhogamavyaktamucyate \|*  
*bāhyāṃtaḥkaraṇadvāraṃ śarīraṃ bhogasādhanam \|\| 27 \|\|*

*bhāvātiśayalabdhena prasādena malakṣayaḥ \|*  
*kṣīṇe cātmamale tasmin pumāñcchivasamo bhavet \|\| 28 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

25-28. Kalā, Vidyā, Rāga, Kāla and Niyati, these are certain entities Tlir enjoyer is Puruṣa, Karman is merit and sin. The fruits are happiness and misery. The beginningless dirt\[?\] till the enjoyment rests in the ignorant soul. Enjoyment is for quelling Karman. The unmanifest is what is enjoyed. The means of enjoyment is the body with external and the internal senses as doors. Dirt is quelled by grace acquired by piety. When the dirt is quelled the Puruṣa becomes equal to Śiva.

## \|\| 11.5.29 \|\|

*munaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kalādipañcatattvānāṃ kiṃ karma pṛthagucyate \|*  
*bhokteti puruṣaśceti yenātmā vyapadiśyate \|\| 29 \|\|*

The sages said:—

29\. What are the several functions of the five principles Kalā etc.? Why is Atman called the enjoyer and Puruṣa?

## \|\| 11.5.30 \|\|

*kimātmakaṃ tadavyaktaṃ kenākāreṇa bhujyate \|*  
*kiṃ tasya śaraṇaṃ bhuktau śarīraṃ ca kimucyate \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Of what nature is that unmanifest? In what form is it enjoyed? What is its instrument in the act of enjoyment? What is it called body?

## \|\| 11.5.31 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*dikkriyāvyaṃjakā vidyā kālo rāgaḥ pravartakaḥ \|*  
*kālo 'vacchedakastatra niyatistu niyāmikā \|\| 31 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

31\. Vidyā (learning) that reveals the place and activity, time and passion these are the inducing agents. Time is the conditioning factor there; destiny is the controlling factor.

## \|\| 11.5.32 \|\|

*avyaktaṃ kāraṇaṃ yattattriguṇaṃ prabhavāpyayam \|*  
*pradhānaṃ prakṛtiśceti yadāhustattvaciṃtakāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The unmanifest is the cause. It consists of three Guṇas. It is the source of origin and the place of merger. It is called Pradhāna and Prakṛti by philosophers.

## \|\| 11.5.33 \|\|

*kalātastadabhivyaktamanabhivyaktalakṣaṇam \|*  
*sukhaduḥkhavimohātmā bhujyate guṇavāṃstridhā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Characteristically unmanifest it becomes manifest through Kalās. It is of the form and content of happiness, misery and delusion while being enjoyed. It has the three Guṇas.

## \|\| 11.5.34 \|\|

*sattvaṃ rajastama iti guṇāḥ prakṛtisaṃbhavāḥ \|*  
*prakṛtau sūkṣmarūpeṇa tile tailamiva sthitāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The Guṇas Sattva, Rajas and Tamas, originate from Prakṛti. Like oil in the gingelly seed they are present in the latest form in Prakṛti.

## \|\| 11.5.35-36 \|\|

*sukhaṃ ca sukhahetuśca samāsātsāttvikaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*rājasaṃ tadviparyāsātstaṃbhamohau tu tāmasau \|\| 35 \|\|*

*sāttvikyūrdhvagatiḥ proktā tāmasī syādadhogatiḥ \|*  
*madhyamā tu gatiryā sā rājasī paripaṭhyate \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. Happiness and its cause constitute briefly the Sātttvaic trait. The Rājasaic trait is its opposite. Stunned state and delusion are Tāmasic traits. The Sāttvaic movement is upward progress; the Tāmasic one is downfall; the middle course is cited as Rājasaic.

## \|\| 11.5.37-38 \|\|

*tanmātrāpañcakaṃ caiva bhūtapañcakameva ca \|*  
*jñāneṃdriyāṇi pañcaikyaṃ pañca karmendriyāṇi ca \|\| 37 \|\|*

*pradhānabuddhyahaṃkāramanāṃsi ca catuṣṭayam \|*  
*samāsādevamavyaktaṃ savikāramudāhṛtam \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. Briefly the unmanifest with its ramifications is as follows:—five subtle and primary dements, five gross elements, five sense-organs of activity and the set of four, viz. Pradhāna, intellect, ego and mind.

## \|\| 11.5.39 \|\|

*tatkāraṇadaśāpannamavyaktamiti kathyate \|*  
*vyaktaṃ kāryadaśāpannaṃ śarīrādighaṭādivat \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. When it is in the state of a cause, it is unmanifest; when it is in the state of an effect such as the body, pot etc, it is manifest.

## \|\| 11.5.40 \|\|

*yathā ghaṭādikaṃ kāryaṃ mṛdādernātibhidyate \|*  
*śarīrādi tathā vyaktamavyaktānnātibhidyate \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Just as the pot is not materially different from clay, so the manifest, body etc. is not materially different from the unmanifest.

## \|\| 11.5.41 \|\|

*tasmādavyaktamevaikyakāraṇaṃ karaṇāni ca \|*  
*śarīraṃ ca tadādhāraṃ tadbhogyaṃ cāpi netarat \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Hence the unmanifest alone is the cause of the composite viz. organs, body but their support, the object or enjoyment is unmanifest.

## \|\| 11.5.42 \|\|

*munaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*buddhīndriyaśarīrebhyo vyatirekasya kasyacit \|*  
*ātmaśabdābhidheyasya vastuto 'pi kutaḥ sthitiḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

The sages said:—

42\. How can Ātman which is separate from the sense-organs and the body exist?

## \|\| 11.5.43 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*buddhīndriyaśarīrebhyo vyatireko vibhordhruvam \|*  
*astyeva kaścidātmeti hetustatra sudurgamaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

43\. The separateness of all-pervading lord from the intellect, sense-organs and the body is definite. There is something called Ātman. A reason thereof is difficult to understand.

## \|\| 11.5.44 \|\|

*buddhīndriyaśarīrāṇāṃ nātmatā sadbhiriṣyate \|*  
*smṛteraniyatajñānādayāvaddehavedanāt \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The intellect, the sense-organs and the bodies are not the Ātman due to indefinite knowledge and non-eternality.

## \|\| 11.5.45 \|\|

*ataḥ smartānubhūtānāmaśeṣajñeyagocaraḥ \|*  
*antaryāmīti vedeṣu vedāṃteṣu ca gīyate \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Hence the one who has the cognition of experienced objects and comprehends the entire knowables, is sung about in the Vedas and Upaniṣads as the immanent soul.

## \|\| 11.5.46 \|\|

*sarvaṃ tatra sa sarvatra vyāpya tiṣṭhati śāśvataḥ \|*  
*tathāpi kvāpi kenāpi vyaktameṣa na dṛśyate \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. It is eternal. It incorporates and pervades everything. It stands everywhere. Still it is not perceived by any one clearly anywhere.

## \|\| 11.5.47 \|\|

*naivāyaṃ cakṣuṣā grāhyo nāparairindriyairapi \|*  
*manasaiva pradīptena mahānātmāvasīyate 1 \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. This Atman cannot be perceived by the eye nor by any other sense-organ. The great Ātman is comprehended only by the enlightened mind.

## \|\| 11.5.48 \|\|

*na ca strī na pumāneṣa naiva cāpi napuṃsakaḥ \|*  
*naivordhvaṃ nāpi tiryaknādhastānna kutaścana \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. It is neither woman nor man nor an eunuch. It is neither above nor below nor in the sides. It is nowhere.

## \|\| 11.5.49 \|\|

*aśarīraṃ śarīreṣu caleṣu sthāṇumavyayam \|*  
*sadā paśyati taṃ dhīro naraḥ pratyavamarśanāt \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. It remains unembodied in the unsteady bodies. It is stable and steady like a stump. It is unchanging. Only the sober, self-possessed and bold can perceive it by means of reflection.

## \|\| 11.5.50 \|\|

*kimatra bahunoktena puruṣo dehataḥ pṛthak \|*  
*apṛthagye tu paśyaṃti hyasamyakteṣu darśanam \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Of what avail is much talk? The Puruṣa is separate from the body. Unwarranted is the vision of those who do not see it separate.

## \|\| 11.5.51 \|\|

*yaccharīramidaṃ proktaṃ puruṣasya tataḥ param \|*  
*aśuddhamavaśaṃ duḥkhamadhruvaṃ na ca vidyate \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. There is nothing more impure, uncontrolled, miserable and uncertain than the body of the Puruṣa.

## \|\| 11.5.52 \|\|

*vipadāṃ vījabhūtena puruṣastena saṃyutaḥ \|*  
*sukhī duḥkhī ca mūḍhaśca bhavati svena karmaṇā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. The Puruṣa becomes happy, miserable or deluded on becoming associated with the body—the seed of all adversities caused by his own activities.

## \|\| 11.5.53 \|\|

*adbhirāplavitaṃ kṣetraṃ janayatyaṃkuraṃ yathā \|*  
*ājñānātplāvitaṃ karma dehaṃ janayate tathā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. As the field flooded with water generates sprouts so also the action flooded with ignorance generates the man.

## \|\| 11.5.54 \|\|

*atyaṃtamasukhāvāsāssmṛtāścaikāṃtamṛtyavaḥ \|*  
*anāgatā atītāśca tanavo 'sya sahasraśaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Thousands in number are his bodies both of the past and the future. These are mortals, abodes of excessive distress.

## \|\| 11.5.55 \|\|

*āgatyāgatya śīrṇeṣu śarīreṣu śarīriṇaḥ \|*  
*atyaṃtavasatiḥ kvāpi na kenāpi ca labhyate \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. A perpetual stay in the bodies that successively come to the embodied soul and get shattered, is never attained by any one.

## \|\| 11.5.56 \|\|

*chāditaśca viyuktaśca śarīraireṣu lakṣyate \|*  
*caṃdrabiṃbavadākāśe taralairabhrasaṃcayaiḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Covered by and separated from these bodies this soul resembles the disc of the moon in the sky that is covered by and separated from the passing clouds.

## \|\| 11.5.57 \|\|

*anekadehabhedena bhinnā vṛttirihātmanaḥ \|*  
*aṣṭāpadaparikṣepe hyakṣamudreva lakṣyate \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. The different activities of the soul in the different bodies resemble the motion of the die in the different squares in the chess-board.

## \|\| 11.5.58 \|\|

*naivāsya bhavitā kaścinnāsau bhavati kasyacit \|*  
*pathi saṃgama evāyaṃ dāraiḥ putraiśca baṃdhubhiḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. None belongs to him. He does not belong to anyone. The contact with wives, sons and kinsmen is but a chance meeting on the way.

## \|\| 11.5.59 \|\|

*yathā kāṣṭhaṃ ca kāṣṭhaṃ ca sameyātāṃ mahodadhau \|*  
*sametya ca vyapeyātāṃ tadvadbhūtasamāgamaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. The mutual contact of living beings is like that of a piece of log with another log in the great ocean. The two meet together and get separated.

## \|\| 11.5.60 \|\|

*sa paśyati śarīraṃ taccharīraṃ tanna paśyati \|*  
*tau paśyati paraḥ kaścittāvubhau taṃ na paśyataḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. He sees the body but the body does not see him. A certain other being, the great Ātman secs both but both of them do not see him.

## \|\| 11.5.61 \|\|

*brahmādyāḥ sthāvarāṃtaśca paśavaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|*  
*paśūnāmeva sarveṣāṃ proktametannidarśanam \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. All living beings beginning with Brahmā and ending with the immobile are termed Paśus. Examples cited relate to these Paśus.

## \|\| 11.5.62 \|\|

*sa eṣa badhyate pāśaiḥ sukhaduḥkhāśanaḥ paśuḥ \|*  
*līlāsādhanabhūto ya īśvarasyeti sūrayaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. These Paśus are bound with Pāśa (noose) and are fed upon joy and misery as their fodder. The wise say that these are but instruments of games and sports of lord Śiva.

## \|\| 11.5.63 \|\|

*ajño jaṃturanīśo 'yamātmanassukhaduḥkhayoḥ \|*  
*īśvaraprerito gacchetsvargaṃ vā śvabhrameva vā \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. The ignorant creature cannot effect and prevent his happiness and misery. Induced by the lord he goes up to the heaven or falls into the deep ditch.

## \|\| 11.5.64 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇyānilavaco munayaḥ prītamānasāḥ \|*  
*procuḥ praṇamya taṃ vāyuṃ śaivāgamavicakṣaṇam \|\| 64 \|\|*

Śūta said:—

64\. On hearing these words of Vāyu, the sages were delighted in their minds. After bowing to him who was expert in the Śaivitc Āgama they spoke:—

## Chapter 6 - The Principles of Śiva cult (2)

## \|\| 11.6.1 \|\|

*munaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*yo 'yaṃ paśuriti prokto yaśca pāśa udāhṛtaḥ \|*  
*abhyāṃ vilakṣaṇaḥ kaścitkoyamasti tayoḥ patiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

The sages said:—

1\. You have explained what is Paśu and what is Pāśa. Now mention what is their lord different in characteristics from the two?

## \|\| 11.6.2 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*asti kaścidaparyaṃtaramaṇīyaguṇāśrayaḥ \|*  
*patirviśvasya nirmātā paśupāśavimocanaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

2\. There is a certain releaser of Paśu from Pāśa. He is Pati, the creator of the universe. He is the abode of endless charming attributes.

## \|\| 11.6.3 \|\|

*abhāve tasya viśvasya sṛṣṭireṣā kathaṃ bhavet \|*  
*acetanatvādajñānādanayoḥ paśupāśayoḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. In his absence how could the universe have been created, since Pāśa is insentient and the Paśu is ignorant?

## \|\| 11.6.4 \|\|

*pradhānaparamāṇvādi yāvatkiṃcidacetanam \|*  
*tatkartṛkaṃ svayaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ buddhimatkāraṇaṃ vinā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Without an intelligent cause nothing has ever been seen anywhere created by Pradhāna, Paramāṇu or any such insentient being.

## \|\| 11.6.5 \|\|

*jagacca kartṛsāpekṣaṃ kāryaṃ sāvayavaṃ yataḥ \|*  
*tasmātkāryasya kartṛtvaṃ patyurna paśupāśayoḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Since the universe is an effect possessing parts it is dependent on a creator. And creativity can be only in Pati and not in Paśu or Pāśa.

## \|\| 11.6.6 \|\|

*paśorapi ca kartṛtvaṃ patyuḥ preraṇapūrvakam \|*  
*ayathākaraṇajñānamaṃdhasya gamanaṃ yathā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Creativity of Paśu without the knowledge of creation like the going of a blind man is due to the inducement of his lord.

## \|\| 11.6.7 \|\|

*ātmānaṃ ca pṛthaṅmatvā preritāraṃ tataḥ pṛthak \|*  
*asau juṣṭastatastena hyamṛtatvāya kalpate \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Realising distinction between him and himself and being gratified after resorting to him Paśu can attain immortality.

## \|\| 11.6.8 \|\|

*paśoḥ pāśasya patyuśca tattvato 'sti padaṃ param \|*  
*brahmavittadviditvaiva yonimukto bhaviṣyati \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The sphere of Pati is really greater than and beyond that of Paśu and Pāśa. The knower of Brahman becomes free from births by knowing him alone.

## \|\| 11.6.9 \|\|

*saṃyuktametaddvitayaṃ kṣaramakṣarameva ca \|*  
*vyaktāvyaktaṃ bibhartīśo viśvaṃ viśvavimocakaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Lord the redeemer of the universe sustains the universe of Kṣara and Akṣara, the two in unison, the manifest and the unmanifest.

## \|\| 11.6.10 \|\|

*bhoktā bhogyaṃ prerayitā maṃtavyaṃ trividhaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*nātaḥ paraṃ vijānadbhirveditavyaṃ hi kiṃcanaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The enjoyer, the enjoyed and the instigator—the three alone shall be distinguished. There is nothing else to be known by the seekers of knowledge.

## \|\| 11.6.11-12 \|\|

*tileṣu vā yathā tailaṃ dadhni vā sarpirarpitam \|*  
*yathāpaḥ srotasi vyāptā yathāraṇyāṃ hutāśanaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*evameva mahātmānamātmanyātmavilakṣaṇam \|*  
*satyena tapasā caiva nityayukto 'nupaśyati \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. The man endowed with truth and penance sets in his Ātman the great Ātman like the oil in the gingelly seed or the ghee in the curd or water in the current or the fire in the Araṇi.

## \|\| 11.6.13 \|\|

*ya eko jālavānīśa īśānībhissvaśaktibhiḥ \|*  
*sarvāṃllokānimān kṛtvā eka eva sa īśate 1 \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. He is the lord born alone. Associated with Īśānīs, his Śaktis he creates the worlds and rules over them.

## \|\| 11.6.14 \|\|

*eka eva tadā rudro na dvitīyo 'sti kaścana \|*  
*saṃsṛjya viśvabhuvanaṃ goptā te saṃcukoca yaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. He is always alone. There is none second to him. After creating the worlds he protects them and withdraws them.

## \|\| 11.6.15 \|\|

*viśvataścakṣurevāyamutāyaṃ viśvatomukhaḥ \|*  
*tathaiva viśvatobāhuviśvataḥ pādasaṃyutaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. He has eyes, faces and feet all round.

## \|\| 11.6.16 \|\|

*dyāvābhūmī ca janayan deva eko maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*sa eva sarvadevānāṃ prabhavaścodbhavastathā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The sole lord and creator of the heaven and earth is Maheśvara. He is the origin and the place of merger of all the gods.

## \|\| 11.6.17 \|\|

*hiraṇyagarbhaṃ devānāṃ prathamaṃ janayedayam \|*  
*viśvasmādadhiko rudro maharṣiriti hi śrutiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The Śruti says that Rudra the great sage is superior to all; he creates Hiraṇyagarbha the first among the deities.

## \|\| 11.6.18 \|\|

*vedāhametaṃ puruṣaṃ mahāṃtamamṛtaṃ dhruvam \|*  
*ādityavarṇaṃ tamasaḥ parastātsaṃsthitaṃ prabhum \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. I know this great Puruṣa, the undying, steady, having the colour of the sun, the lord stationed beyond darkness.

## \|\| 11.6.19 \|\|

*asmānnāsti paraṃ kiṃcidaparaṃ paramātmanaḥ \|*  
*nāṇīyo 'sti na ca jyāyastena pūrṇamidaṃ jagat \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. There is nothing greater, subtler and grosser than this. The universe is filled by him.

## \|\| 11.6.20 \|\|

*sarvānanaśirogrīvaḥ sarvabhūtaguhāśayaḥ \|*  
*sarvavyāpī ca bhagavāṃstasmātsarvagataśśivaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. He has all faces, heads and necks. He lies in the cavity of the heart of all. He is all-pervading and present everywhere.

## \|\| 11.6.21 \|\|

*sarvataḥ pāṇipādo 'yaṃ sarvato 'kṣiśiromukhaḥ \|*  
*sarvataḥ śrutimāṃlloke sarvamāvṛtya tiṣṭhati \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. He has hands, feet, eyes, heads, ears and faces all around. He stands enveloping everything in the world.

## \|\| 11.6.22 \|\|

*sarvendriyaguṇābhāsassarvendriyavivarjitaḥ \|*  
*sarvasya prabhurīśānaḥ sarvasya śaraṇaṃ suhṛt \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. He has all apparent attributes but is devoid of the sense-organs. The lord is the friend and refuge of all.

## \|\| 11.6.23 \|\|

*acakṣurapi yaḥ paśyatyakarṇo 'pi śṛṇoti yaḥ \|*  
*sarvaṃ vetti na vettāsya tamāhuḥ puruṣaṃ param \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. They call him the great Puruṣa—who sees without eyes, hears without ears and comprehends all and whom no one knows.

## \|\| 11.6.24 \|\|

*aṇoraṇīyānmahato mahīyānayamavyayaḥ \|*  
*guhāyāṃ nihitaścāpi jaṃtorasya maheśvaraḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. He is subtler than the atom, greater than the greatest. He is the unchanging. He lies in the cavity of the heart of this Paśu.

## \|\| 11.6.25 \|\|

*tamakratuṃ kratuprāyaṃ mahimātiśayānvitam \|*  
*dhātuḥ prasādādīśānaṃ vītaśokaḥ prapaśyati \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. By the grace of the creator, one devoid of sorrows perceives him who is endowed with the excellence of greatness and who docs not possess intelligence but is intelligence itself.

## \|\| 11.6.26 \|\|

*vedāhamenamajaraṃ purāṇaṃ sarvagaṃ vibhum \|*  
*nirodhaṃ janmano yasya vadaṃti brahmavādinaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. I know the unaging ancient omnipresent lord whose birth is denied by those who can expound the knowledge of the Brahman.

## \|\| 11.6.27 \|\|

*eko 'pi trīnimāṃllokān bahudhā śaktiyogataḥ \|*  
*vidadhāti vicetyaṃte 1 viśvamādau maheśvaraḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. After annihilating in the end, the lord creates the universe again from the beginning in association with his manifold Śaktis.

## \|\| 11.6.28-29 \|\|

*viśvadhātrītyajākhyā ca śaivī citrā kṛtiḥ parā \|*  
*tāmajāṃ lohitāṃ śuklāṃ kṛṣṇāmekāṃ tvajaḥ prajām \|\| 28 \|\|*

*janitrīmanuśete 'nyojuṣamāṇassvarūpiṇīm \|*  
*tāmevājāmajo 'nyastu bhaktabhogā jahāti ca \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. The Māyā of Śiva is the unborn mother of the universe and has variegated colours and shapes. It is white, red and black. She, the unborn, gives birth to man. He, the unborn, resorts to it and gets involved in distress Another Aja, the liberated soul, eschews her after she has been enjoyed.

## \|\| 11.6.30 \|\|

*dvau suparṇau ca sayujau samānaṃ vṛkṣamāsthitau \|*  
*eko 'tti pippalaṃ svādu paro 'naśnan prapaśyati \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Two birds resort to the same tree. One eats the sweet fruit, the other simply watches without eating.

## \|\| 11.6.31-32 \|\|

*vṛkṣesmin puruṣo magno guhyamānaśca śocati \|*  
*juṣṭamanyaṃ yadā paśyedīśaṃ paramakāraṇam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tadāsya mahimānaṃ ca vītaśokassukhī bhavet \|*  
*chaṃdāṃsi yajñāḥ ṛtavo yadbhūtaṃ bhavyameva ca \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. Sitting on this tree the deluded Puruṣa bewails. When he sees the lord, the ultimate cause, and realises his greatness he is freed from sorrow and becomes happy.

## \|\| 11.6.33 \|\|

*māyī viśvaṃ sṛjatyasminniviṣṭo māyayā paraḥ \|*  
*māyāṃ tu prakṛtiṃ vidyānmāyinaṃ tu maheśvaram \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The great Ātman, the Māyin entering this, creates the universe by his Māyā. Māyā shall be known as Prakṛti and Maheśvara as Māyin.

## \|\| 11.6.34-35 \|\|

*tasyāstvavayavaireva vyāptaṃ sarvamidaṃ jagat \|*  
*sūkṣmātisūkṣmamīśānaṃ kalalasyāpi madhyataḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*sraṣṭāramapi viśvasya veṣṭitāraṃ ca tasya tu \|*  
*śivameveśvaraṃ jñātvā śāṃtimatyaṃtamṛcchati \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. The universe is permeated by his parts. The Puruṣa attains perpetual peace and calmness on realising lord Śiva the creator and enveloper of the universe and the subtler of the subtlest, from his very inception in the foetus.

## \|\| 11.6.36 \|\|

*sa eva kālo goptā ca viśvasyādhipatiḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*taṃ viśvādhipatiṃ jñātvā mṛtyupāśātpramucyate \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. He alone is Kāla, the protector, the lord of universe. On realising him one is released from the noose of death.

## \|\| 11.6.37 \|\|

*ghṛtātparaṃ maṃḍamiva sūkṣmaṃ jñātvā sthitaṃ prabhum \|*  
*sarvabhūteṣu gūḍhaṃ ca sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. On realising the lord pervading all living beings like the subtle cream over the ghee, one is freed from sins.

## \|\| 11.6.38 \|\|

*eṣa eva paro devo viśvakarmā maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*hṛdaye saṃniviṣṭaṃ taṃ jñātvaivāmṛtamaśnute \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. He alone is the great god Śivā, the creator of the universe. Only on realising him one attains immortality.

## \|\| 11.6.39 \|\|

*yadā samastaṃ na divā na rātrirna sadapyasat \|*  
*kevalaśśiva evaiko yataḥ prajñā purātanī \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. When everything was neither existent nor non-existent, when it was neither day nor night, Śiva alone existed from whom the ancient wisdom emanated.

## \|\| 11.6.40 \|\|

*nainamūrdhvaṃ na tiryakca na madhyaṃ paryajigrahat \|*  
*na tasya pratimā cāsti yasya nāma mahadyaśaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. None can grasp his top, sides or middle. There is nolhing resembling him. His is the great fame.

## \|\| 11.6.41 \|\|

*ajātamimamevaike buddhā janmani bhīravaḥ \|*  
*rudrasyāsya prapadyaṃte rakṣārthaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ sukham \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Those who are frightened of rebirths meditate on the unborn. For the sake of succour they resort lo the front face of Rudra.

## \|\| 11.6.42 \|\|

*dve akṣare brahmapare tvanaṃte samudāhṛte \|*  
*vidyāvidye samākhyāte nihite yatra gūḍhavat \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The two Vidyā and Avidyā lie hidden in the imperishable, infinite great Brahman.

## \|\| 11.6.43 \|\|

*kṣaraṃ tvavidyā hyamṛtaṃ vidyeti parigīyate \|*  
*te ubhe īśate yastu so 'nyaḥ khalu maheśvaraḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Avidyā is perishable while Vidyā is imperishable. He who rules over the two is lord Śiva. He is other than the two.

## \|\| 11.6.44 \|\|

*ekaikaṃ bahudhā jālaṃ vikurvannekavacca yaḥ \|*  
*sarvādhipatyaṃ kurute sṛṣṭvā sarvān pratāpavān \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. It is he who spreads his net in various ways, creates all and rules all. He possesses such exploits.

## \|\| 11.6.45 \|\|

*diśa ūrdhvamadhastiryakbhāsayan bhrājate svayam \|*  
*yo niḥsvabhāvādapyeko vareṇyastvadhitiṣṭhati \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. He illuminates the quarters above, below and to the sides, shining himself. He is innately alone, foremost of all who presides over all.

## \|\| 11.6.46 \|\|

*svabhāvavācakān sarvān vācyāṃśca pariṇāmayan \|*  
*guṇāṃśca bhogyabhoktṛtve tadviśvamadhitiṣṭhati \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Transforming the attributes, the expressions of nature and expressed ones into what is enjoyed and the one that enjoys, he occupies the universe.

## \|\| 11.6.47 \|\|

*te vai guhyopaṇiṣadi gūḍhaṃ brahma parātparam \|*  
*brahmayoniṃ jagatpūrvaṃ vidurdevā maharṣayaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. The gods and the sages know him as hidden in the secret Upaniṣad, who is Brahman, greater than the greatest, the progenitor of Brahmā and the cause of the universe.

## \|\| 11.6.48 \|\|

*bhāvagrāhyamanīhākhyaṃ bhāvābhāvakaraṃ śivam \|*  
*kalāsargakaraṃ devaṃ ye viduste jahustanum \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Those who knew the lord eschewed their bodies. The lord can be realised only through piety. He is wishless, the cause of positive and negative substances and the creator of Kalās.

## \|\| 11.6.49 \|\|

*svabhāvameke manyaṃte kālameke vimohitāḥ \|*  
*devasya mahimā hyeṣa yenedaṃ bhrāmyate jagat \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. It is the greatness of the lord whereby this universe revolves but the deluded people call it a natural occurrence or the power of time.

## \|\| 11.6.50 \|\|

*yenedamāvṛtaṃ nityaṃ kālakālātmanā yataḥ \|*  
*teneritamidaṃ karma bhūtaiḥ saha vivartate \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. It is by him in the form of the annihilator of death that these are enveloped perpetually, the activities urged' by him transform into worldly existence along with the elements.

## \|\| 11.6.51-53 \|\|

*tatkarma bhūyaśaḥ kṛtvā vinivṛtya ca bhūyaśaḥ \|*
