*tattvasya saha tattvena yogaṃ cāpi sametya vai \|\| 51 \|\|*

*aṣṭābhiśca tribhiścaivaṃ dvābhyāṃ caikena vā punaḥ \|*  
*kālenātmaguṇaiścāpi kṛtsnameva jagatsvayam \|\| 52 \|\|*

*guṇairārabhya karmāṇi svabhāvādīni yojayet \|*  
*teṣāmabhāve nāśaḥ syātkṛtasyāpi ca karmaṇaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

51-53. The individual indulges in activities more and more and returns to the earth. He gets entangled in the tattvas. By means of the fourteen attributes of the Ātman he pursues worldly activities. When these activities cease even the results are quelled.

## \|\| 11.6.54 \|\|

*karmakṣaye punaścānyattato yāti sa tattvataḥ \|*  
*sa evādissvayaṃ yoganimittaṃ bhoktṛbhogayoḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. When these are quelled he goes to another world. This is the cause of union of the two—the enjoyer and the enjoyed.

## \|\| 11.6.55 \|\|

*parastrikālādakalassa eva parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*sarvavittriguṇādhīśo brahmasākṣātparātparaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Lord alone is beyond the three times. He is attributeless, the knower of all, the lord of the three attributes. He is brahman itself greater than the greatest.

## \|\| 11.6.56 \|\|

*taṃ viśvarūpamabhavaṃ bhavamīḍyaṃ prajāpatim \|*  
*devadevaṃ jagatpūjyaṃ svacittasthamupāsmahe \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. We worship and meditate upon th lord of manifold forms, the unborn, lord of people, object of worship and meditation by the entire universe. He is stationed in our minds.

## \|\| 11.6.57 \|\|

*kālādibhiḥ paro yasmātprapañcaḥ parivartate \|*  
*dharmāvahaṃ pāpanudaṃ bhogeśaṃ viśvadhāma ca \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. He is beyond Kāla. From him the whole cosmos originates. He is the repository of the universe and effects virtue and quells sins. He is the lord of enjoyment.

## \|\| 11.6.58 \|\|

*tamīśvarāṇāṃ paramaṃ maheśvaraṃ taṃ devatānāṃ paramaṃ ca daivatam \|*  
*patiṃ patīnāṃ paramaṃ parastādvidāma devaṃ bhuvaneśvareśvaram \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. We know him as the greatest of lords, the greatest of deities, the lord of the worlds.

## \|\| 11.6.59 \|\|

*na tasya vidyeta kāryaṃ kāraṇaṃ ca na vidyate \|*  
*na tatsamo 'dhikaścāpi kvacijjagati dṛśyate \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. He has neither cause nor effect. Nowhere in the universe there is anyone equal or superior to him.

## \|\| 11.6.60 \|\|

*parāsya vividhā śaktiḥ śrutau svābhāvikī śrutā \|*  
*jñānaṃ balaṃ kriyā caiva yābhyo viśvamidaṃ kṛtam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. It is mentioned in the Vedas that his threefold power is great, manifold and innate, comprising knowledge, strength and activity. It is by these activities that the universe is created.

## \|\| 11.6.61 \|\|

*tasyāsti patiḥ kaścinnaiva liṃgaṃ na ceśitā \|*  
*kāraṇaṃ kāraṇānāṃ ca sa teṣāmadhipādhipaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. He has no lord, no sex and no ruler. He is the cause of causes and the lord of lords.

## \|\| 11.6.62 \|\|

*na cāsya janitā kaścinna ca janma kutaścana \|*  
*na janmahetavastadvanmalamāyādisaṃjñakāḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. He has no progenitor nor does he take birth from anywhere. He has no causes of birth such as Dirt, Māyā etc.

## \|\| 11.6.63 \|\|

*sa ekassarvabhūteṣu gūḍho vyāptaśca viśvataḥ \|*  
*sarvabhūtāṃtarātmā ca dharmādhyakṣassa kathyate \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. He is the solitary lord hidden in all living beings. Spread all round he is the innate soul of all living beings. He is mentioned as the presiding deity of all sacred rites.

## \|\| 11.6.64 \|\|

*sarvabhūtādhivāsaśca sākṣī cetā ca nirguṇaḥ \|*  
*eko vaśī niṣkriyāṇāṃ bahūnāṃ vivaśātmanām \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. He is the abode of all living beings, the cosmic witness, the provoker of thoughts, devoid of attributes and the sole lord with self-control, devoid of activities and helpless.

## \|\| 11.6.65 \|\|

*nityānāmapyasau nityaścetanānāṃ ca cetanaḥ \|*  
*eko bahūnāṃ cākāmaḥ kāmānīśaḥ prayacchati \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. He is the most permanent among the permanent. He is the most sentient among the sentient.

## \|\| 11.6.66 \|\|

*sāṃkhyayogādhigamyaṃ yatkāraṇaṃ jagatāṃ patim \|*  
*jñātvā devaṃ paśuḥ pāśaissarvaireva vimucyate \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. On realising the lord of the universe, comprehensible through Sāṅkhya and Yoga, the cause of the universe the person gets released from all illusions.

## \|\| 11.6.67 \|\|

*viśvakṛdviśvavitsvātmayonijñaḥ kālakṛdguṇī \|*  
*pradhānaḥ kṣetrajñapatirguṇeśaḥ pāśamocakaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. He is the creator and the knower of the universe. He is the knower of his source, and the creator of time. He possesses attributes. He is the lord of Prakṛti and the individual soul; he presides over the Guṇas; he is the releaser of illusion.

## \|\| 11.6.68-69 \|\|

*brahmāṇaṃ vidadhe pūrvaṃ vedāṃścopādiśatsvayam \|*  
*yo devastamahaṃ buddhvā svātmabuddhiprasādataḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

*mumukṣurasmātsaṃsārātprapadye śaraṇaṃ śivam \|*  
*niṣphalaṃ niṣkriyaṃ śāṃtaṃ niravadyaṃ niraṃjanam \|\| 69 \|\|*

68-69. Alter realising the lord who at the outset created Brahma and taught him the Vedas, through the clarity of my intellect, I shall be desirous of salvation from this worldly existence. I take refuge in Śiva who is devoid of attributes and activities, who is quiescent, the undespicable and the unsullied.

## \|\| 11.6.70-71 \|\|

*amṛtasya paraṃ setuṃ dagdheṃdhanamivānilam \|*  
*yadā carmavadākāśaṃ veṣṭayiṣyaṃti mānavāḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*tadā śivamavijñāya duḥkhasyāṃto bhaviṣyati \|*  
*tapaḥprabhāvāddevasya prasādācca maharṣayaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

70-71. After realising the great bridge that takes to immortality I shall be quiescent like the fire that has consumed fuel. When men wear the ether as they wear a hide they will realise the end of miseries before they have realised Śiva.

## \|\| 11.6.72-73 \|\|

*atyāśramocitajñānaṃ pavitraṃ pāpanāśanam \|*  
*vedāṃte paramaṃ guhyaṃ purākalpapracoditam \|\| 72 \|\|*

*brahmaṇo vadanāllabdhaṃ mayedaṃ bhāgyagauravāt \|*  
*nāpraśāṃtāya dātavyametajjñānamanuttamam \|\| 73 \|\|*

72-73. O sages, due to the power of penance, the grace of the lord and the result of my good fortune I secured the holy knowledge straight from the mouth of Brahmā, the knowledge that quells sins, lies hidden in the Upaniṣads and was enunciated in a previous Kalpa.

## \|\| 11.6.74 \|\|

*na putrāyāśuvṛttāya nāśiṣyāya ca sarvathā \|*  
*yasya deve parābhaktiryathā deve tathā gurau \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. This excellent knowledge shall not be delivered to one who is not quiet, nor to a son who is not well behaved nor to one who is not one’s own disciple.

## \|\| 11.6.75 \|\|

*tasyaite kathitāhyarthāḥ prakāśaṃte mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*ataśca saṃkṣepamidaṃ śṛṇudhvaṃ śivaḥ parastātprakṛteśca puṃsaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. These facts reveal to him who is of noble soul, who has great devotion to the lord and to the preceptor in the form of Śiva.

## \|\| 11.6.76 \|\|

*sa sargakāle ca karoti sarvaṃ saṃhārakāle punarādadāti \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Hence listen to the gist. Śiva is greater than Prakṛti and Puruṣa and beyond it. At the time of creation he creates the universe and at the time of dissolution he withdraws everything.

## Chapter 7 - The glory of Time (kāla)

## \|\| 11.7.1 \|\|

*munaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kālādutpadyate sarvaṃ kāladeva vipadyate \|*  
*na kālanirapekṣaṃ hi kvacitkiṃcana vidyate \|\| 1 \|\|*

The sages said:—

1\. Every thing originates from Kāla and is annihilated through Kāla. There is nothing independent of Kāla anywhere.

## \|\| 11.7.2 \|\|

*yadāsyāṃtargataṃ viśvaṃ śaśvatsaṃsāramaṇḍalam \|*  
*sargasaṃhṛtimudrābhyāṃ cakravatparivartate \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The whole universe caught in its mouth whirls like a wheel through the activities of creation and annihilation.

## \|\| 11.7.3 \|\|

*brahmā hariśca rudraśca tathānye ca surāsurāḥ \|*  
*yatkṛtāṃ niyatiṃ prāpya prabhavo nātivartitum \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. By his control, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, gods and Asuras cannot transgress the laws of propriety.

## \|\| 11.7.4 \|\|

*bhūtabhavyabhaviṣyādyairvibhajya jarayan prajāḥ \|*  
*atiprabhuriti svairaṃ vartate 'tibhayaṃkaraḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. It classifies itself in the factors of past, present and future and makes people grow old. Thus freely lording over all it is extremely terrible.

## \|\| 11.7.5 \|\|

*ka eṣa bhagavān kālaḥ kasya vā vaśavartyayam \|*  
*ka evāsya vaśe na syātkathayaitadvicakṣaṇa \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O skilful one, please tell us. Who is this lord Kāla? Under whose control is he? Who does not come under his control?

## \|\| 11.7.6 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*kālakāṣṭhānimeṣādikalākalitavigraham \|*  
*kālātmeti samākhyātaṃ tejo māheśvaraṃ param \|\| 6 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

6\. It is the great splendour of lord Śiva named Kālātman. Kalā, Kāṣṭḥā, Nimeṣa are the forms it embodies.

## \|\| 11.7.7 \|\|

*yadalaṃghyamaśeṣasya sthāvarasya carasya ca \|*  
*niyogarūpamīśasya balaṃ viśvaniyāmakam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. It is the power of the lord that controls the universe in the form of directives which are untransgressable to the universe consisting of the mobile and immobile beings.

## \|\| 11.7.8 \|\|

*tasyāṃśāṃśamayī muktiḥ kālātmani mahātmani \|*  
*tato niṣkramya saṃkrāṃtā visṛṣṭāgrerivāyasī \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The Energy in the form of Kāla consists of its various parts. It comes out of it and permeates it like the piece of steel that sheds sparks of fire.

## \|\| 11.7.9 \|\|

*tasmātkālavaśe viśvaṃ na sa viśvavaśe sthitaḥ \|*  
*śivasya tu vaśe kālo na kālasya vaśe śivaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The universe is under the control of Kāla. Kāla is not under the control of the universe. Kāla is under the control of Śiva. Śiva is not subject to its control.

## \|\| 11.7.10 \|\|

*yato 'pratihataṃ śārvaṃ tejaḥ kāle pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*mahatī tena kālasya maryādā hi duratyayā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Since the unobstructed splendour of Śiva is firmly fixed in Kāla the limit of Kāla is extensive and is untransgeressable.

## \|\| 11.7.11 \|\|

*kālaṃ prajñāviśeṣeṇa ko 'tivartitumarhati \|*  
*kālena tu kṛtaṃ karma na kaścidativartate \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Who can go beyond Kāla with the help of intellect? None can go beyond Karman perpetrated by Kāla.

## \|\| 11.7.12 \|\|

*ekacchatrāṃ mahīṃ kṛtsnāṃ ye parākramya śāsati \|*  
*te 'pi naivātivartaṃte kālavelāmivābdhayaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Even those who attack the earth and rule it under a single umbrella cannot step beyond Kāla like the oceans that do not overflow the shore.

## \|\| 11.7.13 \|\|

*ye nigṛhyeṃdriyagrāmaṃ jayaṃti sakalaṃ jagat \|*  
*na jayaṃtyapi te kālaṃ kālo jayati tānapi \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Even those who restrain their sense-organs and conquer the universe cannot conquer Kāla. Kāla overwhelms them.

## \|\| 11.7.14 \|\|

*āyurvedavido vaidyāstvanuṣṭhitarasāyanāḥ \|*  
*na mṛtyumativartaṃte kālo hi duratikramaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Physicians well-versed in medicines regularly taking in elixirs and aphrodisiacs do not thwart death. Indeed Kāla is untransgressable.

## \|\| 11.7.15 \|\|

*śriyā rūpeṇa śīlena balena ca kulena ca \|*  
*anyacciṃtayate jaṃtuḥ kālo 'nyatkurute balāt \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The individual soul proposes something on the basis of its glory, beauty, conduct, strength and pedigree but Kāla disposes it.

## \|\| 11.7.16 \|\|

*apriyaiśca priyaiścaiva hyaciṃtitagamāgamaiḥ \|*  
*saṃyojayati bhūtāni viyojayati ceśvaraḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. By means of pleasing, displeasing and unexpected contacts, Kāla unites and separates the living beings.

## \|\| 11.7.17 \|\|

*yadaiva duḥkhitaḥ kaścittadaiva sukhitaḥ paraḥ \|*  
*durvijñeyasvabhāvasya kālāsyāho vicitratā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. At the same time when some one is miserable another is very happy. Wonderful indeed is the unscrutable nature of Kāla.

## \|\| 11.7.18 \|\|

*yo yuvā sa bhavedvṛddho yo balīyānsa durbalaḥ \|*  
*yaḥ śrīmānso 'pi niḥśrīkaḥ kālaścitragatirdvijā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. A young man changes into a feeble aged man. A powerful man becomes weak. A rich man becomes deprived of prosperity. O brahmins, the ways of Kāla are wonderful.

## \|\| 11.7.19 \|\|

*nābhijātyaṃ na vai śīlaṃ na balaṃ na ca naipuṇam \|*  
*bhavetkāryāya paryāptaṃ kālaśca hyanirodhakaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Neither nobility of birth, nor good conduct nor strength nor skill is of any avail. Kāla is unthwartable.

## \|\| 11.7.20 \|\|

*ye sanāthāśca dātāro gītavādyairupasthitāḥ \|*  
*ye cānāthāḥ parānnādāḥ kālasteṣu samakriyaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Kāla is impartial in its activity over those who are well guarded donors attended upon by songs and musical instruments as well as those who are helpless, living on doles.

## \|\| 11.7.21 \|\|

*phalaṃtyakāle na rasāyanāni samyakprayuktānyapi cauṣadhāni \|*  
*tānyeva kālena samāhṛtāni siddhiṃ prayāṃtyāśu sukhaṃ diśaṃti \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Even elixirs, panaceas and well administered medicines do not have any effect if the time is not opportune. Those very things brought into use at the proper time are efficacious and yield happiness.

## \|\| 11.7.22 \|\|

*nākālato 'yaṃ mriyate jāyate vā nākālataḥ puṣṭimagryāmupaiti \|*  
*nākālataḥ sukhitaṃ duḥkhitaṃ vā nākālikaṃ vastu samasti kiṃcit \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. No one dies or is born before time. No one flourishes well before the proper time. No one is happy or miserable before the time for it arrives. There is no object which is untimely.

## \|\| 11.7.23 \|\|

*kālena śītaḥ prativāti vātaḥkālena vṛṣṭirjaladānupaiti \|*  
*kālena coṣmā praśamaṃ prayāti kālena sarvaṃ saphalatvameti \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. At the proper time the cool wind blows, the rain falls; the heat subsides and every thing grows.

## \|\| 11.7.24 \|\|

*kālaśca sarvasya bhavasya hetuḥ kālena sasyāni bhavaṃti nityam \|*  
*kālena sasyāni layaṃ prayāṃti kālena saṃjīvati jīvalokaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Kāla is the cause of all births. Plants grow and perish at the proper time. The living world too comes into life.

## \|\| 11.7.25 \|\|

*itthaṃ kālātmanastattvaṃ yo vijānāti tattvataḥ \|*  
*kālātmānamatikramya kālātītaṃ sa paśyati \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. He who thus correctly understands the principle of Kāla goes beyond it and sees that which is beyond Kāla.

## \|\| 11.7.26 \|\|

*na yasya kālo na ca baṃdhamuktī na yaḥ pumānna prakṛtirna viśvam \|*  
*vicitrarūpāya śivāya tasmai namaḥparasmai parameśvarāya \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Obeisance to the great. Obeisance to Śiva of wonderful form who has no Kāla to influence him, no bondage and liberation and is identical neither with Puruṣa nor Prakṛti nor the universe.

## Chapter 8 - The span of life of the trinity

## \|\| 11.8.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kena mānena kālesminnāyussaṃkhyā prakalpyate \|*  
*saṃkhyārūpasya kālasya kaḥ punaḥ paramo 'vadhiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

The sages said:—

1\. By what unit is the duration of life calculated in Kāla? What is the upper limit of Kāla in the form of number?

## \|\| 11.8.2 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*āyuṣo 'tra nimeṣākhyamādyamānaṃ pracakṣate \|*  
*saṃkhyārūpasya kālasya śāṃttvatītakalāvadhi \|\| 2 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

2\. The basic unit of life is Nimeṣa. The upper limit is Śāntyatīta.

## \|\| 11.8.3 \|\|

*akṣipakṣmaparikṣepo nimeṣaḥ parikalpitaḥ \|*  
*tādṛśānāṃ nimeṣāṇāṃ kāṣṭhā daśa ca pañca ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The time taken for the winking of an eye is Nimeṣa. Fifteen such Nimeṣas constitute one Kāṣṭhā.

## \|\| 11.8.4 \|\|

*kāṣṭhāṃstriṃśatkalā nāma kalāṃstriṃśanmuhūrtakaḥ \|*  
*muhūrtānāmapi triṃśadahorātraṃ pracakṣate \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Thirty such Kāsthās make one Kalā. Thirty Kalās make one Muhūrta. Thirty Muhūrtas make one day.

## \|\| 11.8.5-6 \|\|

*triṃśatsaṃkhyairahorātrairmāsaḥ pakṣadvayātmakaḥ \|*  
*jñeyaṃ pitryamahorātraṃ māsaḥ kṛṣṇasitātmakaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*no sanskrit verse \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. Thirty days constitute one month of two fortnights. A month constituting the bright and dark halves is one day of the manes.

## \|\| 11.8.7-8 \|\|

*māsaistairayanaṃ ṣaḍbhirvarṣaṃ dve cāyanaṃ matam \|*  
*laukikenaiva mānena abdo yo mānuṣaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*etaddivyamahorātramiti śāstrasya niścayaḥ \|*  
*dakṣiṇaṃ cāyanaṃ rātristathodagayanaṃ dinam \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. Six Māsas constitute one Ayana. Two Ayanas make a year. One human year constitutes one day and night for the celestials, Uttarāyana being the day and Dakṣiṇāyana the night.

## \|\| 11.8.9 \|\|

*māsastriṃśadahorātrairdivyo mānuṣavatsmṛtaḥ \|*  
*saṃvatsaro 'pi devānāṃ māsairdvādaśabhistathā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The divine month like the human month constitutes thirty days. The year of the gods constitutes twelve months.

## \|\| 11.8.10 \|\|

*trīṇi varṣaśatānyeva ṣaṣṭivarṣayutānyapi \|*  
*divyassaṃvatsaro jñeyo mānuṣeṇa prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Three hundred and sixty human years make one divine year.

## \|\| 11.8.11 \|\|

*divyenaiva pramāṇena yugasaṃkhyā pravartate \|*  
*catvāri bhārate varṣe yugāni kavayo viduḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The calculation of yugas is based on the divine unit of time. The wise understand that there are four Yugas in the land of Bhārata.

## \|\| 11.8.12 \|\|

*pūrvaṃ kṛtayugaṃ nāma tatastretā vidhīyate \|*  
*dvāparaṃ ca kaliścaiva yugānyetāni kṛtsnaśaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The first Yuga is Kṛta, then comes Tretā. Dvāpara and Kali are the other Yugas. These are the four Yugas.

## \|\| 11.8.13 \|\|

*catvāri tu sahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ tatkṛtaṃ yugam \|*  
*tasya tāvacchatīsaṃdhyā saṃdhyāṃśaśca tathāvidhaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Four thousand years constitute the Kṛtayuga. The period of four hundred years constitutes the intervening junction and a hundred year period constitutes Sandhyāṃśa (a subdivision of the junction).

## \|\| 11.8.14 \|\|

*itareṣu sasaṃdhyeṣu sasaṃdhyāṃśeṣu ca triṣu \|*  
*ekāpāyena vartaṃte sahasrāṇi śatāni ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. In the three other yugas, their Sandhyās and Sandhyāṃśas the thousands and the hundreds become reduced by one.

## \|\| 11.8.15 \|\|

*etaddvādaśasāhasraṃ sādhikaṃ ca caturyugam \|*  
*caturyugasahasraṃ yatsaṃkalpa iti kathyate \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Thus the twelve thousand years and the surplus period constitute a Caturyuga. A thousand Caturyugas constitute a Kalpa.

## \|\| 11.8.16 \|\|

*caturyugaikasaptatyā manoraṃtaramucyate \|*  
*kalpe caturdaśaikasminmanūnāṃ parivṛttayaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Seventyone Caturyugas constitute a Manvantara. In a Kalpa there are fourteen such Manvantaras.

## \|\| 11.8.17 \|\|

*etena kramayogena kalpamanvaṃtarāṇi ca \|*  
*saprajāni vyatītāni śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. In this order, hundreds and thousands of such Kalpas and Manvantaras have passed by this time.

## \|\| 11.8.18 \|\|

*ajñeyatvācca sarveṣāmasaṃkhyeyatayā punaḥ \|*  
*śakyo naivānupūrvyādvai teṣāṃ vaktuṃ suvistaraḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. They are innumerable and hard to be known precisely. It is impossible to mention them in detail in the precise order.

## \|\| 11.8.19 \|\|

*kalpo nāma divā prokto brahmaṇo 'vyaktajanmanaḥ \|*  
*kalpānāṃ vai sahasraṃ ca brāhmaṃ varṣamihocyate \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. A Kalpa constitutes a day of Brahmā of unmanifest origin. A thousand Kalpas make a year of Brahmā.

## \|\| 11.8.20 \|\|

*varṣāṇāmaṣṭasāhasraṃ yacca tadbrahmaṇo yugam \|*  
*savanaṃ yugasāhasraṃ brahmaṇaḥ padmajanmanaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Eight thousand Brahmā years make one Brahmā Yuga. A thousand Brahmā Yugas make one Savana of Brahmā.

## \|\| 11.8.21 \|\|

*savanānāṃ sahasraṃ ca triguṇaṃ trivṛtaṃ tathā \|*  
*kalpyate sakalaḥ kālo brahmaṇaḥ parameṣṭhinaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Three thousand and three Savanas make the life time of Brahmā.

## \|\| 11.8.22-23 \|\|

*tasya vai divase yāṃti caturdaśa puraṃdarāḥ \|*  
*śatāni māse catvāri viṃśatyā sahitāni ca \|\| 22 \|\|*

*abde pañca sahasrāṇi catvāriṃśadyutāni ca \|*  
*catvāriṃśatsahasrāṇi pañca lakṣāṇi cāyuṣi \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. A day of Brahma’s life constitutes the life of fourteen Indras, a month of his life constitutes a four hundred and twenty Indras; a year of his life five thousand and forty Indras; his whole life five hundred and forty thousand Indras.

## \|\| 11.8.24-25 \|\|

*brahmā viṣṇordine caiko viṣṇū rudradine tathā \|*  
*īśvarasya dine rudrassadākhyasya tatheśvaraḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*sākṣācchivasya tatsaṃkhyastathā so 'pi sadāśivaḥ \|*  
*catvāriṃśatsahasrāṇi pañcalakṣāṇi cāyuṣi \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. A day of Viṣṇu is the life-time of Brahmā. A day of Rudra is equal to the life-time of Viṣṇu. A day of Śiva is equal to the life-period of one Rudra. A day of Sadāśiva is the life-period of Śiva. A day of Sākṣāt Śivā is the life-period of Sadāśiva. The life-time of the latter is equal to the life-period of five hundred and forty thousand previous deities.

## \|\| 11.8.26 \|\|

*tasminsākṣācchivenaiṣa kālātmā sampravartate \| yattatsṛṣṭessamākhyātaṃ kālāntaramiha dvijāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. This Kāla functions as directed by Sākṣātśiva. O Brahmins, this is the period of time of creation as mentioned by me.

## \|\| 11.8.27 \|\|

*tasminsākṣācchivenaiṣa kālātmā sampravartate \|*  
*yattatsṛṣṭessamākhyātaṃ kālāntaramiha dvijāḥ \|*  
*etatkālāntaraṃ jñeyamaharvai pārameśvaram \|*  
*rātriśca tāvatī jñeyā parameśasya kṛtsnaśaḥ \|*  
*ahastasya tu yā sṛṣṭī rātriśca pralayaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. This Kālāntara shall be known as a day of Parameśvara. Parameśvara’s night shall be known to extend so long.

## \|\| 11.8.28 \|\|

*aharna vidyate tasya na rātririti dhārayet \|*  
*eṣopacāraḥ kriyate lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. His day is the period of creation. His night is the period of dissolution. But understand that he has neither day nor night as we conceive them.

## \|\| 11.8.29-31 \|\|

*prajāḥ prajānāṃ patayo mūrtayaśca surāsurāḥ \|*  
*indriyāṇīndriyārthāśca mahābhūtāni pañca ca \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tanmātrāṇyatha bhūtādirbuddhiśca saha daivataḥ \|*  
*ahastiṣṭhaṃti sarvāṇi pārameśasya dhīmataḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*aharaṃte pralīyante rātryante viśvasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*yo viśvātmā karmakālasvabhāvādyarthe śaktiryasya nollaṃghanīyā \|\| 31 \|\|*

29-31. The dissolution is effected for the benefit of the world. The subjects, the Prajāpatis, the three deities, gods, Asuras, the sense-organs, the sensual objects, the five great elements, the subtle and gross elements, the cosmic Intellect, the deities, all these abide during the day of the self-possessed Parameśvara. They get dissolved at the end of the day. At the end of the night again begins the origin of the universe.

## \|\| 11.8.32 \|\|

*yasyaivājñādhīnametatsamastaṃ namastasmai mahate śaṃkarāya \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Obeisance to the great Śiva, the soul of the universe, whose energy in respect of activity, time and innate nature is untransgressable and under whose command the whole universe functions.

## Chapter 9 - The creation and sustenance

## \|\| 11.9.1 \|\|

*munaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ jagadidaṃ kṛtsnaṃ vidhāya ca nidhāya ca \|*  
*ājñayā paramāṃ krīḍāṃ karoti parameśvaraḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

The sages said:—

1\. How does lord Śiva perform his great sport commanding all, creating the universe and placing it in position?

## \|\| 11.9.2 \|\|

*kiṃ tatprathamasaṃbhūtaṃ kenedamakhilaṃ tatam \|*  
*kenā vā punarevedaṃ grasyate pṛthukukṣiṇā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. What is it that came into being at the outset? By what are all these pervaded? By which being of huge belly is this swallowed?

## \|\| 11.9.3 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*śaktiḥ prathamasambhūtā śāṃtyatītapadottarā \|*  
*tato māyā tato 'vyaktaṃ śivācchaktimataḥ prabhoḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

3\. Śakti came into being at the outset; with Śāntyatītapadā following. From Śiva in association with Śakti Māyā came into being and then the unmanifest from it.

## \|\| 11.9.4 \|\|

*śāntyatītapadaṃ śaktestataḥ śāntipadakramāt \|*  
*tato vidyāpadaṃ tasmātpratiṣṭhāpadasaṃbhavaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Śāntyatītapada originated from Śakti and from it Śāntipada; then the Vidyāpada; from it the Pratiṣṭhāpada came into being.

## \|\| 11.9.5 \|\|

*nivṛttipadamutpannaṃ pratiṣṭhāpadataḥ kramāt \|*  
*evamuktā samāsena sṛṣṭirīśvaracoditā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Nivṛttipada originated from Pratiṣṭhāpada. Thus has been briefly described the creation induced by the lord.

## \|\| 11.9.6 \|\|

*ānulomyāttathaiteṣāṃ pratilomyena saṃhṛtiḥ \|*  
*asmātpañcapadoddiṣṭātparassraṣṭā samiṣyate \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The creation of these is in the inverse order; the annihilation is in the reverse order. There is a creator apart from and greater than what is indicated by these five Padas.

## \|\| 11.9.7 \|\|

*kalābhiḥ pañcabhirvyāptaṃ tasmādviśvamidaṃ jagat \|*  
*avyaktaṃ kāraṇaṃ yattadātmanā samanuṣṭhitam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Hence the entire universe is pervaded by the five Kalās. Avyakta is the cause there but activitised by the Ātman.

## \|\| 11.9.8-10 \|\|

*mahadādiviśeṣāṃtaṃ sṛjatītyapi saṃmatam \|*  
*kiṃ tu tatrāpi kartṛtvaṃ nāvyaktasya na cātmanaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*acetanatvātprakṛterajñatvātpuruṣasya ca \|*  
*pradhānaparamāṇvādi yāvatkiñcidacetanam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tatkartṛkaṃ svayaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ buddhimatkāraṇaṃ vinā \|*  
*jagacca kartṛsāpekṣaṃ kāryaṃ sāvayavaṃ yataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

8-10. It is agreed that everything begins with intellect and ends with Viśeṣa but the makership is neither of the Avyakta nor of the Puruṣa since Prakṛti is insentient and Puruṣa ignorant. Without an intelligent cause nothing is created by the insentient beings—Pradhāna, Paramāṇu etc. But the universe is dependent on a maker since it is an effect composed of parts.

## \|\| 11.9.11-12 \|\|

*tasmācchaktassvatantro yaḥ sarvaśaktiśca sarvavit \|*  
*anādinidhanaścāyaṃ mahadaiśvaryasaṃyutaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*sa eva jagataḥ kartā mahādevo maheśvarāḥ \|*  
*pātā hartā ca sarvasya tataḥ pṛthagananvayaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Hence the creator must be powerful, independent, omnipotent and omniscient with no beginning, no end and endowed with lordly qualities. He is the maker of the universe, Mahādeva, Maheśvara, the protector and annihilator of everything. He is separate from it.

## \|\| 11.9.13 \|\|

*pariṇāmaḥ pradhānasya pravṛttiḥ puruṣasya ca \|*  
*sarvaṃ satyavratasyaiva śāsanena pravartate \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The transformation of Pradhāna and the activities of the Puruṣa function at the bidding of the lord of truthful vow.

## \|\| 11.9.14 \|\|

*itīyaṃ śāśvatī niṣṭhā satāṃ manasi vartate \|*  
*na cainaṃ pakṣamāśritya vartate svalpacetanaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. It is in the minds of the noble that this firm and permanent conviction finds a place. A being of meagre consciousness does not' resort to this side.

## \|\| 11.9.15-17 \|\|

*yāvadādisamāraṃbho yāvadyaḥ pralayo mahān \|*  
*tāvadapyeti sakalaṃ brahmaṇaḥ śāradāṃ śatam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*paramityāyuṣo nāma brahmaṇo 'vyaktajanmanaḥ \|*  
*tatparākhyaṃ tadardhaṃ ca parārdhamabhidhīyate \|\| 16 \|\|*

*parārdhadvayakālāṃte pralaye samupasthite \|*  
*avyaktamātmanaḥ kāryamādāyātmani tiṣṭhati \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-17. Hundred Brahmā years constitute the span of Brahmā born of unmanifest It is termed Para. Its half is Parārdha. At the advent of Dissolution the Avyakta withdraws to itself all its effects and abides in Ātman.

## \|\| 11.9.18 \|\|

*ātmanyavasthite 'vyakte vikāre pratisaṃhṛte \|*  
*sādharmyeṇādhitiṣṭhete pradhānapuruṣāvubhau \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. When the Avyakta abides in Ātman, when the effects have been withdrawn, Pradhana and Puruṣa stand on an equal footing.

## \|\| 11.9.19 \|\|

*tamaḥ sattvaguṇāvetau samatvena vyavasthitau \|*  
*anudriktāvanantau tāvotaprotau parasparam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The two have the Guṇas of Tamas and Sattva, remaining on a par with each other. The two without the Guṇas being predominant are mutually interwoven.

## \|\| 11.9.20 \|\|

*guṇasāmye tadā tasminnavibhāge tamodaye \|*  
*śāṃtavātaikanīre ca na prājñāyata kiṃcana \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. In the equal and undivided state of Guṇas in the rise of darkness, when the wind was in full\[?\] and the water was calm, there was nothing to be seen.

## \|\| 11.9.21-22 \|\|

*aprajñāte jagatyasminneka eva maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*upāsya rajanīṃ kṛtsnāṃ parāṃ māheśvarīṃ tataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*prabhātāyāṃ tu śarvaryāṃ pradhānapuruṣāvubhau \|*  
*praviśya kṣobhayāmāsa māyāyogānmaheśvaraḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. When the universe was unmanifest the lord meditated upon the great Śakti throughout the night. When it dawned the lord in contact with Māya entered Pradhāna and Puruṣa and set them to motion.

## \|\| 11.9.23 \|\|

*tataḥ punaraśeṣāṇāṃ bhūtānāṃ prabhavāpyayāt \|*  
*avyaktādabhavatsṛṣṭirājñayā parameṣṭhinaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Then at the bidding of Brahmā, the creation evolved out of the unmanifest that is the source of origin and the spot of merger for all living creatures.

## \|\| 11.9.24 \|\|

*viśvottarottaravicitramanorathasya yasyaikaśaktiśakale sakalassamāptaḥ \|*  
*ātmānamadhvapatimadhvavido vadaṃti tasmai namaḥ sakalalokavilakṣaṇāya \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Obeisance to him who is different from the worlds, in a fraction of whose Śakti everything terminates, whose will is ever variegated and wonderful far above that of the universe and whom those who know the path call the lord of the path—the Ātman.

## Chapter 10 - The description of creation (sṛṣṭi) (1)

## \|\| 11.10.1 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*puruṣādhiṣṭhitātpūrvamavyaktādīśvarājñayā \|*  
*buddhyādayo viśeṣāṃtā vikārāścābhavan kramāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

1\. At the outset, at the bidding of Īśvara the secondary elements beginning with the cosmic intellect and ending with Viśeṣa came into being from the Avyakta presided over by Puruṣa.

## \|\| 11.10.2 \|\|

*tatastebhyo vikārebhyo rudro viṣṇuḥ pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*kāraṇatvena sarveṣāṃ trayo devāḥ prajajñire \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Then from these, the three deities Rudra, Viṣṇu and Brahmā were born as the cause of all.

## \|\| 11.10.3-4 \|\|

*sarvato bhuvanavyāptiśaktimavyāhatāṃ kvacit \|*  
*jñānamapratimaṃ śaśvadaiśvaryaṃ cāṇimādikam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*sṛṣṭisthitilayākhyeṣu karmasu triṣu hetutām \|*  
*prabhutvena sahaiteṣāṃ prasīdati maheśvaraḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. Maheśvara bestows on these the power to pervade all the worlds unobstructed anywhere, unequalled perfect wisdom, the perpetual Siddhis of Aṇimā etc; and the state of being the cause of activities of creation (sṛṣṭi), sustenance and dissolution.

## \|\| 11.10.5 \|\|

*kalpāntare punasteṣāmaspardhā buddhimohinām \|*  
*sargarakṣālayācāraṃ pratyekaṃ pradadau ca saḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. In another Kalpa he conferred on each the activities of creation, sustenance and dissolution in order that they may not have any mutual rivalry due to delusion of intellect.

## \|\| 11.10.6 \|\|

*ete parasparotpannā dhārayanti parasparam \|*  
*paraspareṇa vardhaṃte parasparamanuvratāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. These three are born from one another, sustain one another, flourish one another, respect and follow one another.

## \|\| 11.10.7 \|\|

*kvacidbrahmā kvacidviṣṇuḥ kvacidrudraḥ praśasyate \|*  
*nānena teṣāmādhikyamaiśvaryaṃ cātiricyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Somewhere Brahmā, somewhere Viṣṇu and somewhere Rudra are praised. However their glory docs not diminish.

## \|\| 11.10.8 \|\|

*mūrkhā niṃdaṃti tānvāgbhiḥ saṃraṃbhābhiniveśinaḥ \|*  
*yātudhānā bhavaṃtyeva piśācāśca na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Only impetuous fools censure them. Undoubtedly they become demons and ghosts.

## \|\| 11.10.9 \|\|

*devo guṇatrayātītaścaturvyūho maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*sakalassakalādhāraśakterutpattikāraṇam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Lord Śiva who is beyond the three Guṇas, who is divided into four units, who is all-in-all and the support of all is the cause of creation.

## \|\| 11.10.10 \|\|

*soyamātmā trayasyāsya prakṛteḥ puruṣasya ca \|*  
*līlākṛtajagatsṛṣṭirīśvaratve vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The Atman who has created the universe sportively remains as the lord of three deities as well as of Prakṛti and Puruṣa.

## \|\| 11.10.11 \|\|

*yassarvasmātparo nityo niṣkalaḥ parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*sa eva ca tadādhārastadātmā tadadhiṣṭhitaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He alone is their support, he who is greater than all, who is supreme, eternal, devoid of attributes and is their Ātman and their presiding deity.

## \|\| 11.10.12 \|\|

*tasmānmaheśvaraścaiva prakṛtiḥ puruṣastathā \|*  
*sadāśivabhavo viṣṇurbrahmā sarvaśivātmakam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Hence he alone is Prakṛti, Puruṣa, Sadāśiva, Bhava, Viṣṇu and Brahmā. Everything is identical with Śiva.

## \|\| 11.10.13 \|\|

*pradhānātprathamaṃ jajñe vṛddhiḥ khyātirmatirmahān \|*  
*mahattattvasya saṃkṣobhādahaṃkārastridhā 'bhavat \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. In the beginning were born the cosmic intellect, the great principle. When it was agitated the ego was born. The ego was split into three.

## \|\| 11.10.14 \|\|

*ahaṃkāraśca bhūtāni tanmātrānīṃdriyāṇi ca \|*  
*vaikārikādahaṃkārātsattvodriktāttu sāttvikaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The ego split into the gross and subtle elements and the sense-organs. When the ego had the Sattva predominant the Sāttvika creation took place.

## \|\| 11.10.15-16 \|\|

*vaikārikaḥ sa sargastu yugapatsaṃpravartate \|*  
*buddhīndriyāṇi pañcaiva pañcakarmeṃdriyāṇi ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

*ekādaśaṃ manastatra svaguṇenobhayātmakam \|*  
*tamoyuktādahaṃkārādbhūtatanmātrasaṃbhavaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. The secondary creation took place simultaneously. The five sense-organs, the five organs of activity and the eleventh the mind, originated. The mind is both an organ of knowledge and of activity. When the ego becomes associated with Tamas, the Bhūtatanmātras are born.

## \|\| 11.10.17 \|\|

*bhūtānāmādibhūtatvādbhūtādiḥ kathyate tu saḥ \|*  
*bhūtādeśśabdamātraṃ syāttatra cākāśasaṃbhavaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17' Since it is the cause of Bhūtas it is called Bhūtādi. From this is born the Śabdatanmātra, from this the ether.

## \|\| 11.10.18 \|\|

*ākāśātsparśa utpannaḥ sparśādvāyusamudbhavaḥ \|*  
*vāyo rūpaṃ tatastejastejaso rasasaṃbhavaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. From the ether the Sparśatanmātra, from it Vāyu, from Vāyu the Rūpatanmātra, from this the Tejas, from Tejas the Rasatanmātra is born.

## \|\| 11.10.19 \|\|

*rasādāpassamutpannāstebhyo gandhasamudbhavaḥ \|*  
*gandhācca pṛthivī jātā bhūtebhyonyaccarācaram \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. From Rasa the water; from this the Gandha Tanmātra is born, from this the Pṛthivī, from these elements the mobile and immobile beings are created.

## \|\| 11.10.20 \|\|

*puruṣādhiṣṭhitatvācca avyaktānugraheṇa ca \|*  
*mahadādiviśeṣāntā hyaṇḍamutpādayanti te \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Since they are presided over by Puruṣa and blessed by Avyakta the principles beginning with Mahat and ending with Viśeṣa generate the cosmic egg.

## \|\| 11.10.21 \|\|

*tatra kāryaṃ ca karaṇaṃ saṃsiddhaṃ brahmaṇo yadā \|*  
*tadaṃḍe supravṛddho 'bhūtkṣetrajño brahmasaṃjñitaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. When thus the activities of Brahmā are fulfilled Brahmā becomes flourished in that Egg.

## \|\| 11.10.22 \|\|

*sa vai śarīrī prathamaḥ sa vai puruṣa ucyate \|*  
*ādikartā sa bhūtānāṃ brahmāgre samavartata \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. He is the first embodied soul, called Puruṣa. He is the first creator of living beings. Brahmā thus existed in the beginning.

## \|\| 11.10.23 \|\|

*tasyeśvarasya pratimā jñānavairāgyalakṣaṇā \|*  
*dharmaiśvaryakarī buddhirbrāhmī yajñe 'bhimāninaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. From him was born the intellect, the cause of virtue and prosperity, with the characteristics of wisdom and detachment.

## \|\| 11.10.24-25 \|\|

*avyaktājjāyate tasya manasā yadyadīpsitam \|*  
*vaśī vikṛtvāttraiguṇyātsāpekṣatvātsvabhāvataḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*tridhā vibhajya cātmānaṃ trailokye saṃpravartate \|*  
*sṛjate grasate caiva vīkṣate ca tribhissvayam \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. Whatever is wished for by the mind is born of Avyakta. He functions in the three worlds, dividing himself into three because he has all in his control, possesses all the attributes and is dependent on Avyakta. In these three forms he creates, supports and annihilates.

## \|\| 11.10.26 \|\|

*caturmukhastu brahmatve kālatve cāṃtakassmṛtaḥ \|*  
*sahasramūrdhā puruṣastisrovasthāssvayaṃbhuvaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. He is four-faced as creator; as destroyer he is Kāla and as Puruṣa he has thousand heads. The self-born has thus three states.

## \|\| 11.10.27 \|\|

*sattvaṃ rajaśca brahmā ca kālatve ca tamo rajaḥ \|*  
*viṣṇutve kevalaṃ sattvaṃ guṇavṛddhistridhā vibhau \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. As Brahmā he has Sattva and Rajas, as Kāla Tamas and Rajas, as Viṣṇu he has Sattva alone. Thus the increase of Guṇas in the lord is threefold.

## \|\| 11.10.28 \|\|

*brahmatve sṛjate lokān kālatve saṃkṣipatyapi \|*  
*puruṣatve 'tyudāsīnaḥ karma ca trividhaṃ vibhoḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. As Brahmā he creates the worlds, as Kāla he condenses; as Puruṣa he sustains; he is indifferent. Thus the activity of the lord is threefold.

## \|\| 11.10.29 \|\|

*evaṃ tridhā vibhinnatvādbrahmā triguṇa ucyate \|*  
*caturdhā pravibhaktatvāccāturvyūhaḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Since he is divided into three he is called Triguṇa. Since he has split himself into four he is glorified as Caturvyūha.

## \|\| 11.10.30 \|\|

*āditvādādidevo 'sāvajātatvādajaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*pāti yasmātprajāḥ sarvāḥ prajāpatiriti smṛtaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Since he is the beginning he is called Ādideva; since he is unborn he is called Aja; since he protects the subjects he is called Prajāpati.

## \|\| 11.10.31 \|\|

*hiraṇmayastu yo merustasyolbaṃ sumahātmanaḥ \|*  
*garbhodakaṃ samudrāśca jarāyuścā'pi parvatāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The golden Meru is the foetus of that great Ātman; the oceans constitute the water of the womb and the mountains constitute the outer skin of the womb.

## \|\| 11.10.32 \|\|

*tasminnaṃḍe tvime lokā aṃtarviśvamidaṃ jagat \|*  
*caṃdrādityau sanakṣatrau sagrahau saha vāyunā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. All these worlds in this universe, the moon, sun, stars, planets and Vāyu are in this cosmic egg.

## \|\| 11.10.33 \|\|

*adbhirdaśaguṇābhistu bāhyatoṇḍaṃ samāvṛtam \|*  
*āpo daśaguṇenaiva tejasā bahirāvṛtāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The egg is enveloped with waters ten times bigger than it. The waters are enveloped by Tejas ten times bigger.

## \|\| 11.10.34 \|\|

*tejo daśaguṇenaiva vāyunā bahirāvṛtam \|*  
*ākāśenāvṛto vāyuḥ khaṃ ca bhūtādināvṛtam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The Tejas is enveloped by Vāyu ten times bigger. Vāyu is enveloped by Ākāśa and Ākāśa is enveloped by Bhūtādi.

## \|\| 11.10.35 \|\|

*bhūtādirmahatā tadvadavyaktenāvṛto mahān \|*  
*etairāvaraṇairaṇḍaṃ saptabhirbahirāvṛtam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The Bhūtādi is enveloped by the Mahat. The Mahat is enveloped by Avyakta. Thus the egg is enveloped by even coverings.

## \|\| 11.10.36 \|\|

*etadāvṛttya cānyonyamaṣṭau prakṛtayaḥ sthitāḥ \|*  
*sṛṣṭipālanavidhvaṃsakarmakartryo dvijottamāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O excellent brahmins, eight Prakṛtis, the causes of creation, sustenance and destruction are stationed covering each of these.

## \|\| 11.10.37 \|\|

*evaṃ parasparotpannā dhārayaṃti parasparam \|*  
*ādhārādheyabhāvena vikārāstu vikāriṣu \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Thus born of one another, the effects and their causes sustain one another supporting and being supported.

## \|\| 11.10.38 \|\|

*kūrmoṃgāni yathā pūrvaṃ prasārya viniyacchati \|*  
*vikārāṃśca tathā 'vyaktaṃ sṛṣṭvā bhūyo niyacchati \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Just as the tortoise spreads its limbs first and then withdraws them, so the Avyakta creates the beings and then withdraws them.

## \|\| 11.10.39 \|\|

*avyaktaprabhavaṃ sarvamānulomyena jāyate \|*  
*prāpte pralayakāle tu pratilomyenulīyate \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Everything originating from Avyakta is born in this order. When the time of dissolution arrives it gets dissolved in the reverse order.

## \|\| 11.10.40 \|\|

*guṇāḥ kālavaśādeva bhavaṃti viṣamāḥ samāḥ \|*  
*guṇasāmye layo jñeyo vaiṣamye sṛṣṭirucyate \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The Guṇas become equal and unequal due to Kāla. Dissolution takes place when there is equilibrium of the Guṇas. When this is upset, creation takes place.

## \|\| 11.10.41 \|\|

*tadidaṃ brahmaṇo yoniretadaṃḍaṃ ghanaṃ mahat \|*  
*brahmaṇaḥ kṣetramuddiṣṭaṃ brahmā kṣetrajña ucyate \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Thus this egg, large and thick, is the source of origin of Brahmā. It is called Brahmā’s sphere; Brahmā is the lord of this.

## \|\| 11.10.42 \|\|

*itīdṛśānāmaṇḍānāṃ koṭyo jñeyāḥ sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*sarvagatvātpradhānasya tiryagūrdhvamadhaḥ sthitāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. There are thousands and crores of such eggs stationed at the sides, above and below since Pradhāna is present everywhere.

## \|\| 11.10.43 \|\|

*tatra tatra caturvaktrā brahmāṇo harayo bhavāḥ \|*  
*sṛṣṭā pradhānena tathā labdhvā śaṃbhostu sannidhim \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. In the different places there are four-faced Brahmas, Viṣṇus and Rudras created by Pradhāna with the presence of Śiva.

## \|\| 11.10.44 \|\|

*maheśvaraḥ parovyaktādaṃḍamavyaktasaṃbhavam \|*  
*aṇḍājjajñe vibhurbrahmā lokāstena kṛtāstvime \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The lord is beyond the manifest. The egg is born of the unmanifest. From that egg is born lord Brahmā and the worlds are created by him.

## \|\| 11.10.45 \|\|

*abuddhipūrvaḥ kathito mayaiṣa pradhānasargaḥ prathamaḥ pravṛtaḥ \|*  
*ātyaṃtikaśca pralayontakāle līlākṛtaḥ kevalamīśvarasya \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The primary creation of Pradhāna is without the intervention of the cosmic intellect. The ultimate dissolution is effected sportively by the lord alone at the end.

## \|\| 11.10.46 \|\|

*yattatsmṛtaṃ kāraṇamaprameyaṃ brahmā pradhānaṃ prakṛteḥ prasūtiḥ \|*  
*anādimadhyāntamanantavīryaṃ śuklaṃ suraktaṃ puruṣeṇa yuktam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. What is called as the unmanifest cause is Pradhāna. Brahmā is the progeny of Prakṛti. The Pradhāna has neither beginning nor middle nor end. Its prowess is infinite. It is white and deep red. It is associated with Puruṣa.

## \|\| 11.10.47 \|\|

*utpādakatvādrajasotirekāllokasya saṃtānavivṛddhihetūn \|*  
*aṣṭau vikārānapi cādikāle sṛṣṭvā samaśnāti tathāṃtakāle \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. When the Rajas predominates it becomes generative. It creates the eight secondary tattvas in the beginning, which cause flourishing of the worlds. In the end it devours them.

## \|\| 11.10.48 \|\|

*prakṛtyavasthāpitakāraṇānāṃ yā ca sthitiryā ca punaḥ pravṛttiḥ \|*  
*tatsarvamaprākṛtavaibhavasya saṃkalpamātreṇa maheśvarasya \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The stability and the subsequent operation of the causes projected by Prakṛti take place by the thought of supreme lord whose prowess is not effected by Prakṛti.

## Chapter 11 - The description of creation (sṛṣṭi) (2)

## \|\| 11.11.1 \|\|

*munaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*manvaṃtarāṇi sarvāṇi kalpabhedāṃśca sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*teṣvevāṃtarasargaṃ ca pratisargaṃ ca no vada \|\| 1 \|\|*

The sages said:—

1\. Please narrate the Manvantaras, the Kalpas, the subsidiary creations and the re-creation after dissolution.

## \|\| 11.11.2 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*kālasaṃkhyāvivṛttasya parārdho brahmaṇassmṛtaḥ \|*  
*tāvāṃścaivāsya kālonyastasyāṃte pratisṛjyate \|\| 2 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

2\. The tenure of Brahmā who comes and goes according to the calculation of time is first a Parārdha and another Parārdha thereafter. At the end of the latter the re-creation takes place.

## \|\| 11.11.3 \|\|

*divase divase tasya brahmaṇaḥ pūrvajanmanaḥ \|*  
*caturdaśamahābhāgā manūnāṃ parivṛttayaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. In each day in the life of Brahmā, the fourteen Manus come and go.

## \|\| 11.11.4 \|\|

*anāditvādanaṃtatvādajñeyatvācca kṛtsnaśaḥ \|*  
*manvaṃtarāṇi kalpāśca na śakyā vacanātpṛthak \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The Manvantaras and Kalpas have no beginning or

end. Being unknowable they cannot be narrated separately.

## \|\| 11.11.5 \|\|

*ukteṣvapi ca sarveṣu śṛṇvatāṃ vo vaco mama \|*  
*kimihāsti phalaṃ tasmānna pṛthakvaktumutsahe \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Even if they be knowable, of what avail is it to

you to know them. Hence I do not attempt to narrate them separately.

## \|\| 11.11.6 \|\|

*ya eva khalu kalpeṣu kalpaḥ saṃprati vartate \|*  
*tatra saṃkṣipya vartaṃte sṛṣṭayaḥ pratisṛṣṭayaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Among these Kalpas, I describe the creation and re-creation of this Kalpa.

## \|\| 11.11.7 \|\|

*yastvayaṃ vartate kalpo vārāho nāma nāmataḥ \|*  
*asminnapi dvijaśreṣṭhā manavastu caturdaśa \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The current Kalpa is named Vārāha. O excellent brahmins, in this Kalpa the Manus are fourteen in number.

## \|\| 11.11.8 \|\|

*svāyaṃbhuvādayassapta sapta sāvarṇikādayaḥ \|*  
*teṣu vaivasvato nāma saptamo vartate manuḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Among the Manus, Svāyambhuva and others constitute the first seven Manus, Sāvarṇika and others constitute the next seven. Among them Vaivasvata Manu is the seventh.

## \|\| 11.11.9 \|\|

*manvaṃtareṣu sarveṣu sargasaṃhāravṛttayaḥ \|*  
*prāyaḥ samābhavaṃtīti tarkaḥ kāryo vijānatā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. It shall be known that in all the Manvantaras, the creation, sustenance and annihilation are more or less of the same nature.

## \|\| 11.11.10-13 \|\|

*pūrvakalpe parāvṛtte pravṛtte kālamārute \|*  
*samunmūlitamūleṣu vṛkṣeṣu ca vaneṣu ca \|\| 10 \|\|*

*jagaṃti tṛṇavaktrīṇi deve dahati pāvake \|*  
*vṛṣṭyā bhuvi niṣiktāyāṃ viveleṣvarṇaveṣu ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

*dikṣu sarvāsu magnāsu vāripūre mahīyasi \|*  
*tadadbhiścaṭulākṣepaistaraṃgabhujamaṇḍalaiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*prārabdhacaṇḍanṛtyeṣu tataḥ pralayavāriṣu \|*  
*brahmā nārāyaṇo bhūtvā suṣvāpa salile sukham \|\| 13 \|\|*

10-13. When the previous Kalpa had ceased, the storm had hurst, the forest and trees had been uprooted, the fire-god had consumed the worlds like dry grass, the earth had been drenched, oceans had overflowed their shores, the quarters had been sunk in deep sheet of water and the waters of dissolution had started their fierce devil dances with the waves for their arms showing movements of gestures by means of the water, Brahmā assumed the form of Viṣṇu, slept soundly in that vast expanse of water.

## \|\| 11.11.14 \|\|

*imaṃ codāharanmaṃtraṃ ślokaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ prati \|*  
*taṃ śṛṇudhvaṃ muniśreṣṭhāstadarthaṃ cākṣarāśrayam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. One shall cite this mantra, a Śloka, regarding Nārāyaṇa. O excellent sages, listen to the mantra as well as the actual meaning of the words.

## \|\| 11.11.15 \|\|

*āpo nārā iti proktā āpo vai narasūnavaḥ \|*  
*ayanaṃ tasya tā yasmāttena nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Waters are called ‘Nārāḥ’. Waters are sons of Nara. He is called Nārāyaṇa because waters constitute his abode.

## \|\| 11.11.16-17 \|\|

*śivayogamayīṃ nidrāṃ kurvantaṃ tridaśeśvaram \|*  
*baddhāṃjali puṭāssiddhā janalokanivāsinaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*stotraiḥ prabodhayāmāsuḥ prabhātasamaye surāḥ \|*  
*yathā sṛṣṭyādisamaye īśvaraṃ śrutayaḥ purā \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. With their palms joined in reverence the Siddha residents of Janaloka and the gods awakened the lord of gods who was in Yogic slumber, with hymns, in the morning as the Śrutis had done formerly at the beginning of creation.

## \|\| 11.11.18 \|\|

*tataḥ prabuddha utthāya śayanāttoyamadhyagāt \|*  
*udaikṣata diśaḥ sarvā yoganidrālasekṣaṇaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The lord woke up, got up from his bed and came to the water. He looked all round at the quarters with the Yogic slumber still lingering in the eyes idly.

## \|\| 11.11.19 \|\|

*nāpaśyatsa tadā kiṃcitsvātmano vyatireki yat \|*  
*savismaya ivāsīnaḥ parāṃ ciṃtāmupāgamat \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. He did not see anything except himself He sat up like a wonderstruck person and began to ponder deeply.

## \|\| 11.11.20 \|\|

*kva sā bhagavatī yā tu manojñā mahatī mahī \|*  
*nānāvidhamahāśailanadīnagarakānanā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. “Where is that charming goddess the great Earth, with her lofty mountains, rivers, cities and forests.”

## \|\| 11.11.21 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃciṃtayanbrahmā bubudhe naiva bhūsthitim \|*  
*tadā sasmāra pitaraṃ bhagavaṃtaṃ trilocanam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Thinking thus Brahmā could not locate the earth. Then he thought of his father, the three-eyed lord.

## \|\| 11.11.22 \|\|

*smaraṇāddevadevasya bhavasyāmitatejasaḥ \|*  
*jñātavānsalile magnāṃ dharaṇīṃ dharaṇīpatiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. By meditating on the lord of gods, of immeasurable splendour, Brahmā understood that the earth had sunk under water.

## \|\| 11.11.23 \|\|

*tato bhūmessamuddhāraṃ kartukāmaḥ prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*jalakrīḍocitaṃ divyaṃ vārāhaṃ rūpamasmarat \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Then Brahmā desirous of lifting up the Earth, thought of the divine Boar supporting about and diving into the waters.

## \|\| 11.11.24-29 \|\|

*mahāparvatavarṣmāṇaṃ mahājaladaniḥsvanam \|*  
*nīlameghapratīkāśaṃ dīptaśabdaṃ bhayānakam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*pīnavṛttaghanaskaṃdhapīnonnatakaṭītaṭam \|*  
*hrasvavṛttorujaṃghāgraṃ sutīkṣṇapuramaṇḍalam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*padmarāgamaṇiprakhyaṃ vṛttabhīṣaṇalocanam \|*  
*vṛttadīrghamahāgātraṃ stabdhakarṇasthalojjvalam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*udīrṇocchvāsaniśvāsaghūrṇitapralayārṇavam \|*  
*visphuratsusaṭācchannakapolaskaṃdhabaṃdhuram \|\| 27 \|\|*

*maṇibhirbhūṣaṇaiścitrairmahāratnaiḥpariṣkṛtam \|*  
*virājamānaṃ vidyudbhirmeghasaṃghamivonnatam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*āsthāya vipulaṃ rūpaṃ vārāhamamitaṃ vidhiḥ \|*  
*pṛthivyuddharaṇārthāya praviveśa rasātalam \|\| 29 \|\|*

24-29. He then assumed the form of a Boar and entered the nether worlds in order to lift up the Earth. His body was like a huge mountain. His snorting sound was like thunder. He had the lustre of a blue cloud. He was terrible with his snorting sound. His shoulders were thick, heavy and rounded. His buttocks were plump and raised. The tips of his calves were short and rounded. The hoots were sharp. His eyes were round and terrible having the brilliance of rubies. The huge body was oval-shaped. The stiff cars shone brilliantly. Inhaling and exhaling his breath he stirred up the waters of dissolution. The shining manes covered his beautiful checks and shoulders. He was embellished in gemset jewels of various sorts. He shone like clustering clouds with lightning.

## \|\| 11.11.30 \|\|

*sa tadā śuśubhe 'tīva sūkaro girisaṃnibhaḥ \|*  
*liṃgākṛtermaheśasya pādamūlaṃ gato yathā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Then the boar that resembled a mountain shone well as if he had reached the foot of the lord.

## \|\| 11.11.31 \|\|

*tatassa salile magnāṃ pṛthivīṃ pṛthivīṃdharaḥ \|*  
*uddhṛtyāliṃgya daṃṣṭrābhyāmunmamajja rasātalāt \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Then he lifted the Earth sunk under water and held it on his curved fangs. He rose up from the nether worlds.

## \|\| 11.11.32 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā munayassiddhā janalokanivāsinaḥ \|*  
*mumudurnanṛturmūrdhni tasya puṣpairavākiran \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. On seeing him, the Siddhas, sages and other human beings rejoiced and danced. They scattered flowers on his head.

## \|\| 11.11.33 \|\|

*vapurmahāvarāhasya śuśubhe puṣpasaṃvṛtam \|*  
*patadbhiriva khadyotaiḥ prāśuraṃjanaparvataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The body of the Boar covered up with flowers shone like the mountain of collyrium with glow-worms falling on it.

## \|\| 11.11.34 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃsthānamānīya varāho mahatīṃ mahīm \|*  
*svameva rūpamāsthāya sthāpayāmāsa vai vibhuḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The Boar brought the earth to its own place. It then assumed his natural form and fixed it there.

## \|\| 11.11.35 \|\|

*pṛthivīṃ ca samīkṛtya pṛthivyāṃ sthāpayangirīn \|*  
*bhūrādyāṃścaturo lokān kalpayāmāsa pūrvavat \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. He levelled the earth, fixed the mountains and set up the four worlds on the earth as before.

## \|\| 11.11.36 \|\|

*iti saha mahatīṃ mahīṃ mahīdhraiḥ pralayamahājaladheradhaḥsthamadhyāt \|*  
*upari ca viniveśya viśvakarmā caramacaraṃ ca jagatsasarja bhūyaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Thus after lifting the earth along with the mountains from the midst of the vast sea of dissolution the lord created the universe—the mobile and immobile beings.

## Chapter 12 - The description of creation (sṛṣṭi) (3)

## \|\| 11.12.1 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*sargaṃ ciṃtayatastasya tadā vai buddhipūrvakam \|*  
*pradhyānakāle mohastu prādurbhūtastamomayaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

1\. At the time of meditation while he was pondering intelligently, delusion in the form of darkness appeared before him.

## \|\| 11.12.2 \|\|

*tamomoho mahāmohastāmisraścāndhasaṃjñitaḥ \|*  
*avidyā pañcamī caiṣā prādurbhūtā mahātmanaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Darkness, delusion, great delusion, blinding darkness and ignorance; the five appeared before the noble lord.

## \|\| 11.12.3 \|\|

*pañcadhā 'vasthitaḥ sargo dhyāyatastvabhimāninaḥ \|*  
*sarvatastamasātīva bījakumbhavadāvṛtaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. While he was meditating, the creation was ramified into five, enveloped all round by darkness as in a seed vessel(?)

## \|\| 11.12.4 \|\|

*bahirantaścāprakāśaḥ stabdho niḥsaṃjña eva ca \|*  
*tasmātteṣāṃ vṛtā buddhirmukhāni karaṇāni ca \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Both within and without it was devoid of light benumed and unconscious. It had no intellect, faces and sense-organs.

## \|\| 11.12.5-6 \|\|

*tasmātte saṃvṛtātmāno nagā mukhyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā'sādhakaṃ brahmā prathamaṃ sargamīdṛśam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*aprasannamanā bhūtvā dvitīyaṃ so 'bhyamanyata \|*  
*tasyābhidhāyataḥ sargaṃ tiryaksroto 'bhyavartata \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. Hence this creation became stationary consisting of trees and mountains. On seeing that this creation did not multiply Brahmā was dissatisfied. He began conceiving and meditating a second time. While he meditated, the lower animals came into being.

## \|\| 11.12.7 \|\|

*antaḥprakāśāstiryaṃca āvṛtāśca bahiḥ punaḥ \|*  
*paśvātmānastato jātā utpathagrāhiṇaśca te \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. These animals had light within but not without.

They had the form of animals and went a wrong path.

## \|\| 11.12.8 \|\|

*tamapyasādhakaṃ jñātvā sargamanyamamanyata \|*  
*tadordhvasrotaso vṛtto devasargastu sāttvikaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. When this creation too proved ineffective the creation of the gods of the Sāttvika type took place.

## \|\| 11.12.9 \|\|

*te sukhaprītibahulā bahirantaśca nāvṛtāḥ \|*  
*prakāśā bahirantaścasvabhāvādeva saṃjñitāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Men had plenty of pleasure, were not concealed but had light within and light without. They had innate consciousness too.

## \|\| 11.12.10 \|\|

*tato 'bhidhyāyatovyaktādarvāksrotastu sādhakaḥ \|*  
*manuṣyanāmā sañjātaḥ sargo duḥkhasamutkaṭaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Again he meditated and from the unmanifest evolved the human creation which had a downward trend. Though effective it was full of misery.

## \|\| 11.12.11-13 \|\|

*prakāśābahirantaste tamodriktā rajo 'dhikāḥ \|*  
*pañcamonugrahaḥ sargaścaturdhā saṃvyavasthitaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*viparyayeṇa śaktyā ca tuṣṭyāsiddhyā tathaiva ca \|*  
*te 'parigrāhiṇaḥ sarve saṃvibhāgaratāḥ punaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*khādanāścāpyaśīlāśca bhūtādyāḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|*  
*prathamo mahataḥ sargo brahmaṇaḥ parameṣṭhinaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. The human beings had light within and light without. They had Tamas and Rajas in abundance. The fifth creation appeared in four forms in respect of Viparyaya, Śakti Tuṣṭi and Siddhi. These had no possessions, being of different species, prone to eating and drinking, were known as Bhūtas etc.

## \|\| 11.12.14 \|\|

*tanmātrāṇāṃ dvitīyastu bhūtasargaḥ sa ucyate \|*  
*vaikārikastṛtīyastu sarga aindriyakaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The first creation of Brahmā is that of Mahat; the second is that of subtle elements and is called Bhūtasarga; the third is known as organic.

## \|\| 11.12.15 \|\|

*ityeṣa prakṛteḥ sargaḥ sambhṛto 'buddhipūrvakaḥ \|*  
*mukhyasargaścaturthastu mukhyā vai sthāvarāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The primary creation took place without the intervention of intellect. The fourth was the creation or immobile beings.

## \|\| 11.12.16-17 \|\|

*tiryaksrotastu yaḥ proktastiryagyoniḥ sa pañcamaḥ \|*  
*tadūrdhvasrotasaḥ ṣaṣṭho devasargastu sa smṛtaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*tato 'rvāksrotasāṃ sargaḥ saptamaḥ sa tu mānuṣaḥ \|*  
*aṣṭamo 'nugrahaḥ sargaḥ kaumāro navamaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. The fifth was the creation of animal kingdom; the sixth of gods; the seventh of human beings. The eighth is called Anugraha and the ninth Kumāra.

## \|\| 11.12.18 \|\|

*prākṛtāśca trayaḥ pūrve sargāste 'buddhipūrvakāḥ \|*  
*buddhipūrvaṃ pravartante mukhyādyāḥ pañca vaikṛtāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The first three creations are primary. They work without intelligence. The five secondary creations function intelligently.

## \|\| 11.12.19-20 \|\|

*agre sasarja vai brahmā mānasānātmanaḥ samān \|*  
*sanandaṃ sanakañcaiva vidvāṃsañca sanātanam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*ṛbhuṃ sanatkumārañca pūrvameva prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*sarve te yogino jñeyā vītarāgā vimatsarāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Brahmā had in the beginning created four sons: Sanaka, Sananda, Sanātana and Sanatkumāra. These are known as yogins free from passion and jealousy.

## \|\| 11.12.21-22 \|\|

*īśvarāsaktamanaso na cakruḥ sṛṣṭaye matim \|*  
*teṣu sṛṣṭyanapekṣeṣu gateṣu sanakādiṣu \|\| 21 \|\|*

*sraṣṭukāmaḥ punarbrahmā tatāpa paramaṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*tasyaivaṃ tapyamānasya na kiṃcitsamavartata \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. They were not interested in the activity of creation because their minds were drawn towards the lord. When Sanaka and others disinterested in creation had left the world, Brahmā, desirous of creation, performed penance. Though he performed penance nothing happened.

## \|\| 11.12.23 \|\|

*tato dīrgheṇa kālena duḥkhātkrodho vyajāyata \|*  
*krodhāviṣṭasya netrābhyāṃ prāpatannaśrubindavaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. When a long time elapsed he was distressed and his distress turned into anger. From the eyes of the infuriated Brahmā drops of tears fell.

## \|\| 11.12.24 \|\|

*tatastebhyo 'śrubindubhyo bhūtāḥ pretāstadābhavan \|*  
*sarvāṃstānaśrujāndṛṣṭvā brahmātmānamaniṃdata \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. From these goblins and ghosts emerged. On seeing these born of tears Brahmā censured himself.

## \|\| 11.12.25 \|\|

*tasya tīvrā 'bhavanmūrchā krodhāmarṣasamudbhavā \|*  
*mūrchitastu jahau prāṇānkrodhāviṣṭaḥ prajāpatiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. As a result of anger and annoyance he fell into swoon. Then the enraged Brahmā cast off his breath.

## \|\| 11.12.26 \|\|

*tataḥ prāṇeśvaro rudro bhagavānnīlalohitaḥ \|*  
*prasādamatulaṃ kartuṃ prādurāsītprabhormukhāt \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Then Rudra, the lord of vital breaths, appeared through the mouth of Brahmā in order to confer unequalled favour.

## \|\| 11.12.27 \|\|

*daśadhā caikadhā cakre svātmānaṃ prabhurīśvaraḥ \|*  
*te tenoktā mahātmāno daśadhā caikadhā kṛtāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Lord Rudra divided himself into eleven Ātmans. When these appeared they were addressed by him.

## \|\| 11.12.28-29 \|\|

*yūyaṃ sṛṣṭā mayā vatsā lokānugrahakāraṇāt \|*  
*tasmātsarvasya lokasya sthāpanāya hitāya ca \|\| 28 \|\|*

*prajāsantānahetośca prayatadhvamatandritāḥ \|*  
*evamuktāśca rurudurdudruvuśca samantataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. O dear, you have been created by me for blessing the worlds. Hence endeavour assiduously for the establishment and benefit of the world and for its progeny. Thus spoken to, they cried and ran all round.

## \|\| 11.12.30 \|\|

*rodanāddrāvaṇāccaiva te rudrā nāmataḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*ye rudrāste khalu prāṇā ye prāṇāste mahātmakāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. In view of their crying and flight they are called Rudras. Rudras are vital breaths and vital breaths are Rudras.

## \|\| 11.12.31 \|\|

*tato mṛtasya devasya brahmaṇaḥ parameṣṭhinaḥ \|*  
*ghṛṇī dadau punaḥ prāṇānbrahmaputro maheśvaraḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Then Rudra, the merciful son of Brahmā, bestowed vital breaths on Brahmā.

## \|\| 11.12.32 \|\|

*prahṛṣṭavadano rudraḥ prāṇapratyāgamādvibhoḥ \|*  
*abhyabhāṣata viśveśo brahmāṇaṃ paramaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Rudra was delighted at the return of Brahmā to life. He spoke to Brahmā.

## \|\| 11.12.33 \|\|

*mābhairmābhairmahābhāga viriṃca jagatāṃ guro \|*  
*mayā te prāṇitāḥ prāṇāḥ sukhamuttiṣṭha suvrata \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. O Brahmā, preceptor of the worlds, do not be afraid. Your vital breaths have been resuscitated by me. O one of good rites, get up comfortably.

## \|\| 11.12.34-35 \|\|

*svapnānubhūtamiva tacchrutvā vākyaṃ manoharam \|*  
*haraṃ nirīkṣya śanakairnetraiḥ phullāmbujaprabhaiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*tathā pratyāgataprāṇaḥ snigdhagambhīrayā girā \|*  
*uvāca vacanaṃ brahmā tamuddiśya kṛtāñjaliḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. On hearing these words as if heard in dreams Brahmā glanced at Rudra, his eyes shedding lustre of lotuses, when the vital breath returned to him. With palms joined in reverence he spoke in pleasing but majestic tone.

## \|\| 11.12.36 \|\|

*tvaṃ hi darśanamātreṇa cānandayasi me manaḥ \|*  
*ko bhavān viśvamūrtyā vā sthita ekādaśātmakaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. “Indeed by your very vision you delight my mind. Who are you, sir, standing in cosmic form dividing yourself into eleven forms?”

## \|\| 11.12.37 \|\|

*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā vyājahāra maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*spṛśan kārābhyāṃ brahmāṇaṃ susukhābhyāṃ sureśvaraḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. On hearing his words, Śiva lord of the gods touched Brahmā with his pleasing hands and spoke.

## \|\| 11.12.38 \|\|

*māṃ viddhi paramātmānaṃ tava putratvamāgatam \|*  
*ete caikādaśa rudrāstvāṃ surakṣitumāgatāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Know me as the great Ātman, born as your son. The eleven Rudras have come to protect you well.

## \|\| 11.12.39 \|\|

*tasmāttīvrāmimāmmūrchāṃ vidhūya madanugrahāt \|*  
*prabuddhasva yathāpūrvaṃ prajā vai sraṣṭumarhasi \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Hence shake off this lethargy through my blessing. Be wakeful. It behoves you to create beings as before.

## \|\| 11.12.40 \|\|

*evaṃ bhagavatā prokto brahmā prītamanā hyabhūt \|*  
*nānāṣṭakena viśvātmā tuṣṭāva parameśvaram \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. When the lord spoke thus, Brahtnā was pleased. He eulogised Rudra with the eight names.

## \|\| 11.12.41-43 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*namaste bhagavan rudra bhāskarāmitatejase \|\| 41 \|\|*

*namo bhavāya devāya rasāyāmbumayātmane \|*  
*śarvāya kṣitirūpāya nandīsurabhaye namaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*īśāya vasave tubhyaṃ namassparśamayātmane \|*  
*paśūnāṃ pataye caiva pāvakāyātitejase \|*  
*bhīmāya vyomarūpāya śabdamātrāya te namaḥ \|*  
*ugrāyograsvarūpāya yajamānātmane namaḥ \|*  
*mahādevāya somāya namostvamṛtamūrtaye \|\| 43 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

41-43. (i) Obeisance O lord Rudra, with the splendour of the sun; to lord Bhava the taste, of the form of water; to Śarva of the form of the earth, Nandin the bull; to Īśa, Vasu in the form of touch, to the lord of Paśus, to the fire-god of great brilliance, to Bhīma in the form of ether, the sound, the subtle element, to Ugra of terrible features in the form of the sacrificer, to Mahādeva with Umā and the moon. Obeisance to the lord of eight forms.

## \|\| 11.12.44 \|\|

*evaṃ stutvā mahādevaṃ brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*prārthayāmāsa viśveśaṃ girā praṇatipūrvayā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. After eulogising Mahādeva, Brahmā, the grand-father of the worlds requested the lord after due homage.

## \|\| 11.12.45 \|\|

*bhagavan bhūtabhavyeśa mama putra maheśvara \|*  
*sṛṣṭihetostvamutpanno mamāṃge 'naṃganāśanaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. O lord of the past and the future, O Rudra, my son, it was for the creation that you the destroyer of the cupid were born out of my limbs.

## \|\| 11.12.46 \|\|

*tasmānmahati kāryesmin vyāpṛtasya jagatprabho \|*  
*sahāyaṃ kuru sarvatra sraṣṭumarhasi sa prajāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Hence, O lord of the universe, help me in this task. It behoves you to create beings everywhere.

## \|\| 11.12.47 \|\|

*tenaiṣāṃ pāvito devo rudrastripuramardanaḥ \|*  
*bāḍhamityeva tāṃ vāṇīṃ pratijagrāha śaṃkaraḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Thus requested by him Rudra, the suppressor of the Tripuras, consented to his proposal.

## \|\| 11.12.48 \|\|

*tatassa bhagavān brahmā hṛṣṭaṃ tamabhinaṃdya ca \|*  
*sraṣṭuṃ tenābhyanujñātastathānyāścāsṛjatprajāḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Then Brahmā congratulated him. Permitted by him Brahmā created people.

## \|\| 11.12.49 \|\|

*marīcibhṛgvaṃgirasaḥ pulastyaṃ pulahaṃ kratum \|*  
*dakṣamatriṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ ca so 'sṛjanmanasaiva ca \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. He mentally created Marīci, Bhṛgu, Aṅgiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Dakṣa, Atri and Vasiṣṭha. He created Dharma and Saṃkalpa too.

## \|\| 11.12.50 \|\|

*purastādasṛjadbrahmā dharmaṃ saṃkalpameva ca \|*  
*ityete brahmaṇaḥ putrā dvādaśādau prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*saha rudreṇa saṃbhūtāḥ purāṇā gṛhamedhinaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. These are the twelve sons of Brahmā including Rudra. They are the ancient householders.

## \|\| 11.12.51 \|\|

*teṣāṃ dvādaśa vaṃśāḥ syurdivyā devagaṇānvitāḥ \|*  
*prajāvantaḥ kriyāvanto maharṣibhiralaṃkṛtāḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Their families are twelve including the gods. Endowed with progeny and holy rites they are embellished by the sages.

## \|\| 11.12.52-53 \|\|

*atha devāsurapitḥnmanuṣyāṃśca catuṣṭayam \|*  
*saha rudreṇa sisṛkṣuraṃbhasyetāni vai vidhiḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*sa sṛṣṭyarthaṃ samādhāya brahmātmānamayūyujat \|*  
*mukhādajanayaddevān pitḥṃścaivopapakṣataḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. Then he created the four—the gods, Asuras, Pitṛs and the human beings. Desirous of creating these, Brahmā set himself to the task of creation along with Rudra. He created the gods from his face and the pitṛs from the sides.

## \|\| 11.12.54 \|\|

*jaghanādasurān sarvān prajanādapi mānuṣān \|*  
*avaskare kṣudhāviṣṭā rākṣasāstasya jajñire \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. From his loins he created the Asuras; from the organ of generation the human beings. The Rākṣasas overwhelmed by hunger were born of his privities.

## \|\| 11.12.55 \|\|

*putrāstamorajaḥprāyā balinaste niśācarāḥ \|*  
*sarpā yakṣāstathā bhūtā gaṃdharvāḥ saṃprajajñire \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Strong night-prowlers with Tamas and Rajas prominent were born as his sons. The serpents, Yakṣas, Bhūtas and Gandharvas were born.

## \|\| 11.12.56 \|\|

*vayāṃsi pakṣataḥ sṛṣṭāḥ pakṣiṇo vakṣaso 'sṛjat \|*  
*mukhatojāṃstathā pārśvāduragāṃśca vinirmame \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The crows were created from the sides, birds from his chest, goats from the face and serpents from the sides.

## \|\| 11.12.57 \|\|

*padbhyāṃ cāśvānsamātaṃgān śarabhān gavayānmṛgān \|*  
*uṣṭrānaśvatarāṃścaiva nyaṃkūnanyāśca jātayaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. From his feet were born the horses, elephants, Śarabhas, wild oxen, deer, camels, mules, stags and other animals.

## \|\| 11.12.58-62 \|\|

*auṣadhyaḥ phalamūlāni romabhyastasya jajñire \|*  
*gāyatrīṃ ca ṛcaṃ caiva trivṛtsāma rathaṃtaram \|\| 58 \|\|*

*agniṣṭomaṃ ca yajñānāṃ nirmame prathamānmukhāt \|*  
*yajūṃṣi traiṣṭubhaṃ chaṃdaḥstomaṃ pañcadaśaṃ tathā \|\| 59 \|\|*

*bṛhatsāma tathokthaṃ ca dakṣiṇādasṛjanmukhāt \|*  
*sāmāni jagatīchaṃdaḥ stomaṃ saptadaśaṃ tathā \|\| 60 \|\|*

*vairūpyamatirātraṃ ca paścimādasṛjanmukhāt \|*  
*ekaviṃśamatharvāṇamāptoryāmāṇameva ca \|\| 61 \|\|*

*anuṣṭubhaṃ sa vairājamuttarādasṛjanmukhāt \|*  
*uccāvacāni bhūtāni gātrebhyastasya jajñire \|\| 62 \|\|*

58-62. Medicinal herbs, fruits and roots were born of his hairs. From his eastern face he created Gāyatrī, Ṛks, Trivṛtsāma, Rathantara, Agniṣṭoma and other sacrifices. From his southern face he created Yajus Traiṣṭubha Chandas, the fifteen Stomas, Bṛhatsāma and Uktha. From his western face he created Sāman, Jagati Chandas, the seventeen Stomas, Vairūpya and Atirātra mantras. From his northern face he created the Atharva Veda, the twenty-one Āptorvāman, Anuṣṭubh Chandas and the Vairāja. High and low animals and living beings were born of his different limbs.

## \|\| 11.12.63 \|\|

*yakṣāḥ piśācā gaṃdharvāstathaivāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ \|*  
*narakinnararakṣāṃsi vayaḥpaśumṛgoragāḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Yakṣas, Piśācas, Gandharvas, Apsaras, human beings, Kinnaras, Rākṣasas, birds, deer and other animals, serpents etc. were born.

## \|\| 11.12.64 \|\|

*avyayaṃ caiva yadidaṃ sthāṇusthāvarajaṃgamam \|*  
*teṣāṃ vai yāni karmāṇi prāksṛṣṭāni prapedire \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. The mobile and immobile beings which were perishable and imperishable attained their activities.

## \|\| 11.12.65 \|\|

*tānyeva te prapadyaṃte sṛjyamānāḥ punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*hiṃsrāhiṃsre mṛdukrūre dharmādharmāvṛtānṛte \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Created again and again the beings retain their previous nature, violent or non-violent, soft or ruthless, virtuous or evil, true or false.

## \|\| 11.12.66-70 \|\|

*tadbhāvitāḥ prapadyaṃte tasmāttattasya rocate \|*  
*mahābhūteṣu nānātvamiṃdriyārtheṣu muktiṣu \|\| 66 \|\|*

*viniyogaṃ ca bhūtānāṃ dhātaiva vyadadhatsvayam \|*  
*nāma rūpaṃ ca bhūtānāṃ prākṛtānāṃ prapañcanam \|\| 67 \|\|*

*vedaśabdebhya evādau nirmame 'sau pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*ārṣāṇi caiva nāmāni yāśca vedeṣu vṛttayaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

*śarvaryaṃte prasūtānāṃ tānyevaibhyo dadāvajaḥ \|*  
*yathartāvṛtuliṃgāni nānārūpāṇi paryaye \|\| 69 \|\|*

*dṛśyaṃte tāni tānyeva tathā bhāvā yugādiṣu \|*  
*ityeṣa karaṇodbhūto lokasargassvayaṃbhuvaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

66-70. They attain birth with the impressions of their previous traits. The creator himself has assigned the variety and diversity to the elements, the sensual objects etc. He himself has assigned them names and forms through the Vedic texts. He has bestowed thç names of the sages and the functions prescribed in the Vedas on those who were born at the close of the night. When a new season arrives its nature appears itself. So also when the new yuga arrives its nature appears along with it. Thus creation manifests itself through the limbs of Brahmā.

## \|\| 11.12.71-73 \|\|

*mahadādyoviśeṣāṃto vikāraḥ prakṛteḥ svayam \|*  
*caṃdrasūryaprabhājuṣṭo grahanakṣatramaṃḍitaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*nadībhiśca samudraiśca parvataiśca sa maṃḍitaḥ \|*  
*paraiśca vividhairamyaissphītairjanapadaistathā \|\| 72 \|\|*

*tasmin brahmavane 'vyakto brahmā carati sarvavit \|*  
*avyaktabījaprabhava īśvarānugrahe sthitaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

71-73. Beginning with intellect and ending with Viśeṣa this secondary creation is derived from Prakṛti itself. There in the Brahmavana which has the light of the moon and the sun, which is embellished by planets, stars, rivers, oceans, mountains and abounds in beautiful cities and countries the unmanifest Brahmā, having his source in the seed of Avyakta and blessed with the benign favour of the lord, the knower of alḥ moves about.

## \|\| 11.12.74-75 \|\|

*buddhiskaṃdhamahāśākha indriyāṃtarakoṭaraḥ \|*  
*mahābhūtapramāṇaśca viśeṣāmalapallavaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*dharmādharmasupuṣpāḍhyaḥ sukhaduḥkhaphalodayaḥ \|*  
*ājīvyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ brahmavṛkṣaḥ sanātanaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

74-75. The eternal tree in the form of Brahmā shall be resorted to by all. The cosmic intellect is its main stem as well as its branch; the sense-organs its inner hollows; the great elements characterize its size; the Viśeṣa is its tender sprout; Dharma and Adharma its good flowers; happiness and misery its fruits.

## \|\| 11.12.76 \|\|

*dyāṃ mūrdhānaṃ tasya viprā vadaṃti khaṃ vai nābhiṃ caṃdrasūryau ca netre \|*  
*diśaḥ śrotre caraṇau ca kṣitiṃ ca so 'cintyātmā sarvabhūtapraṇetā \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Wise men say that the heaven is his head; the sky his navel; the sun and the moon his eyes; the quarters his cars and the earth his feet. That unponderable soul is the maker of all living beings.

## \|\| 11.12.77 \|\|

*vaktrāttasya brahmaṇāssaṃprasūtāstadvakṣasaḥ kṣatriyāḥ pūrvabhāgāt \|*  
*vaiśyā urubhyāṃ tasya padbhyāṃ ca śūdrāḥ sarve varṇā gātrataḥ saṃprasūtāḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Brahmins are born of his mouth: the Kṣatriyas of his chest, the Vaiśyas of his thighs; the Śūdras of his feet. All the castes are born of his

## Chapter 13 - The creation of Brahmā and Viṣṇu

## \|\| 11.13.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*bhavatā kathitā sṛṣṭirbhavasya paramātmanaḥ \|*  
*caturmukhamukhāttasya saṃśayo naḥ prajāyate \|\| 1 \|\|*

The sages said:—

1\. Sir, you have narrated the creation of the great Ātman through the mouth of the four-faced lord. There we have a doubt.

## \|\| 11.13.2-6 \|\|

*devaśreṣṭho virūpākṣo dīptaśśūladharo haraḥ \|*  
*kālātmā bhagavān rudraḥ kapardī nīlalohitaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*sabrahmakamimaṃ lokaṃ saviṣṇumapi pāvakam \|*  
*yaḥ saṃharati saṃkruddho yugāṃte samupasthite \|\| 3 \|\|*

*yasya brahmā ca viṣṇuśca praṇāmaṃ kuruto bhayāt \|*  
*lokasaṃkocakasyāsya yasya tau vaśavartinau \|\| 4 \|\|*

*yo 'yaṃ devaḥ svakādaṃgādbrahmaviṣṇū purāsṛjat \|*  
*sa eva hi tayornityaṃ yogakṣemakaraḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*sa kathaṃ bhagavān rudra ādidevaḥ purātanaḥ \|*  
*putratvamagamacchaṃbhurbrahmaṇo 'vyaktajanmanaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

2-6. The Odd-eyed Śiva is the foremost among the gods. The trident-bearing Śiva is brilliant. Lord Rudra the Kālātman is Kapardin and Nīlalohita. When the end of the yuga arrives he becomes infuriated and annihilates this universe including Brahmā, Viṣṇu and the fire-god. He makes the worlds shrink. Brahmā and Viṣṇu are under his control. They make obeisance to him out of fright. He is the lord who formerly created Brahmā and Viṣṇu from his limbs. He alone is the cause of acquisition and retention. He is the primordial and ancient god. How did such a lord become the son of Brahmā who is born of Avyakta?

## \|\| 11.13.7 \|\|

*prajāpatiśca viṣṇuśca rudrasyaitau parasparam \|*  
*sṛṣṭau parasparasyāṃgāditi prāgapi śuśruma \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. We have also heard that Brahmā and Viṣṇu were born of Rudra and created Rudra. Thus they mutually created each other.

## \|\| 11.13.8 \|\|

*kathaṃ punaraśeṣāṇāṃ bhūtānāṃ hetubhūtayoḥ \|*  
*guṇapradhānabhāvena prādurbhāvaḥ parasparāt \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. How could the two, progenitors of the living beings, come out of each other thereby possessing both prominence or otherwise?

## \|\| 11.13.9 \|\|

*nāpṛṣṭaṃ bhavatā kiṃcinnāśrutaṃ ca kathaṃcana \|*  
*bhagavacchiṣyabhūtena bhavatā sakalaṃ smṛtam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. There is nothing unseen or unheard by you. Every thing is remembered by you who had been the disciple of the lord himself.

## \|\| 11.13.10 \|\|

*tattvaṃ vada yathā brahmā munīnāmavadadvibhuḥ \|*  
*vayaṃ śraddhālavastāta śrotumīśvarasadyaśaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Please narrate how Brahmā became the lord of all sages. O dear, we are faithful and eager to hear the great glory of the lord.

## \|\| 11.13.11 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*sthāne pṛṣṭamidaṃ viprā bhavadbhiḥ praśnakovidaiḥ \|*  
*idameva purā pṛṣṭo mama prāha pitāmahaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

11\. O Brahmins, this question has been well put by you, experts in the art of queries. I had put the same query to Brahmā who replied suitably.

## \|\| 11.13.12 \|\|

*tadahaṃ sampravakṣyāmi yathā rudrasamudbhavaḥ \|*  
*yathā ca punarutpattirbrahmaviṣṇvoḥ parasparam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. I shall narrate how Rudra was born and how Brahmā and Viṣṇu were born from each other.

## \|\| 11.13.13-15 \|\|

*trayaste kāraṇātmāno jatāssākṣānmaheśvarāt \|*  
*carācarasya viśvasya sargasthityaṃtahetavaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*paramaiśvaryasaṃyuktāḥ parameśvarabhāvitāḥ \|*  
*tacchaktyādhiṣṭhitā nityaṃ tatkāryakaraṇakṣamāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*pitrā niyamitāḥ pūrvaṃ trayopi triṣu karmasu \|*  
*brahmā sarge haristrāṇe rudraḥ saṃharaṇe tathā \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. The three are the Ātmans as causes born of Maheśvara; they are the causes of creation, sustenance and annihilation of the universe consisting of the mobile and immobile beings. Endowed with great qualities they are sanctified by the great lord. Presided over by his Śakti they can always perform their activities. Brahmā can create; Viṣṇu can protect; Rudra can annihilate.

## \|\| 11.13.16-21 \|\|

*tathāpyanyonyamātsaryādanyonyātiśayāśinaḥ \|*  
*tapasā toṣayitvā svaṃ pitaraṃ parameśvaram \|\| 16 \|\|*

*labdhvā sarvātmanā tasya prasādātparameṣṭhinaḥ \|*  
*brahmanārāyaṇau pūrvaṃ rudraḥ kalpāntare 'sṛjat \|\| 17 \|\|*

*kalpāntare punarbrahmā rudraviṣṇū jaganmayaḥ \|*  
*viṣṇuśca bhagavānrudraṃ brahmāṇamasṛjatpunaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*nārāyaṇaṃ punarbrahmā brahmāṇamasṛjatpunaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ kalpeṣu kalpeṣu brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*paraspareṇa jāyaṃte parasparahitaiṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*tattatkalpāntavṛttāntamadhikṛtya maharṣibhiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*prabhāvaḥ kathyate teṣāṃ parasparasamudbhavāt \|*  
*śṛṇu teṣāṃ kathāṃ citrāṃ puṇyāṃ pāpapramocinīm \|\| 21 \|\|*

16-21. But they rivalled with one another. Desirous of excelling one another they propitiated their father, the supreme lord by means of penance. Attaining all round favour of the lord at the outset in a former Kalpa, Rudra created Brahmā and Viṣṇu. In another Kalpa, Brahma created Rudra and Viṣṇu. In another Kalpa Viṣṇu created Rudra and Brahmā. Thus in different Kalpas, Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Rudra desiring mutual benefit are born of one another. Based on the events in their respective Kalpas, their process in being the cause of origin of one another is extolled by the sages. Now listen to their holy and wonderful story that releases from sins.

## \|\| 11.13.22-26 \|\|

*kalpe tatpuruṣe vṛttāṃ brahmaṇaḥ parameṣṭhinaḥ \|*  
*purā nārāyaṇo nāma kalpe vai meghavāhane \|\| 22 \|\|*

*divyaṃ varṣasahasraṃ tu megho bhūtvāvahaddharām \|*  
*tasya bhāvaṃ samālakṣya viṣṇorviśvajagadguruḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*sarvassarvātmabhāvena pradadau śaktimavyayām \|*  
*śaktiṃ labdhvā tu sarvātmā śivātsarveśvarāttadā \|\| 24 \|\|*

*sasarja bhagāvan viṣṇurviśvaṃ viśvasṛjā saha \|*  
*viṣṇostadvaibhavaṃ dṛṣṭvā sṛṣṭastena pitāmahaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*īrṣyayā parayā grastaḥ prahasannidamabravīt \|*  
*gaccha viṣṇo mayā jñātaṃ tava sargasya kāraṇam \|\| 26 \|\|*

22-26. Listen also to what happened to Brahmā in his Kalpa. In the Kalpa, Meghavāhana, Viṣṇu became a cloud and showered the earth for a thousand divine years. Seeing this, Śiva gave imperishable Śakti to Viṣṇu. Obtaining the Śakti from Śiva Viṣṇu created the universe along with Brahmā. On seeing that glory of Viṣṇu, Brahmā created by him was seized by jealousy and said derisively. Go you, O Viṣṇu. The cause of your origin is known to me. Rudra is superior to both of us. There is no doubt in this.

## \|\| 11.13.27 \|\|

*āvayoradhikaścāsti sa rudro nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*tasya devādhidevasya prasādātparameṣṭhinaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. It is due to the grace of that lord that you, the sustained have become a creator today.

## \|\| 11.13.28 \|\|

*sraṣṭā tvaṃ bhagavānādyaḥ pālakaḥ paramārthataḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ ca tapasārādhya rudraṃ tridaśanāyakam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. I too shall propitiate Rudra, the leader of gods, by means of penance and shall create the entire universe along with you. There is no doubt in this.

## \|\| 11.13.29 \|\|

*tvayā saha jagatsarvaṃ srakṣyāmyatra na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ viṣṇumupālabhya bhagavānabjasambhavaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Slighting Viṣṇu thus, Brahmā attained Śiva by means of penance and submitted to him thus.

## \|\| 11.13.30 \|\|

*evaṃ vijñāpayāmāsa tapasā prāpya śaṃkaram \|*  
*bhagavan devadeveśa viśveśvara maheśvara \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. O lord of the gods, O lord of the universe, Viṣṇu is born of your left and I am born of your right side.

## \|\| 11.13.31 \|\|

*tava vāmāṃgajo viṣṇurdakṣiṇāṃgabhavo hyaham \|*  
*mayā saha jagatsarvaṃ tathāpyasṛjadacyutaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Still Viṣṇu created the universe along with me. Due to rivalry he was taunted by me depending on the strength of your support.

## \|\| 11.13.32 \|\|

*sa matsarādupālabdhastvadāśrayabalānmayā \|*  
*madbhāvānnādhikasteti bhāvastvayi maheśvare \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. “O Viṣṇu, your piety towards the lord is not more than that of mine” (I told him) because our origin from you is on the same footing.

## \|\| 11.13.33 \|\|

*tvatta eva samutpattirāvayossadṛśī yataḥ \|*  
*tasya bhaktyā yathāpūrvaṃ prasādaṃ kṛtavānasi \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. O Śiva, it behoves you to give all that to me also in the manner you bestowed on him before due to his devotion.

## \|\| 11.13.34 \|\|

*tathā mamāpi tatsarvaṃ dātumarhasi śaṃkara \|*  
*iti vijñāpitastena bhagavān bhaganetrahā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Thus implored by him the merciful lord Śiva gave all to him as justifiable.

## \|\| 11.13.35 \|\|

*nyāyena vai dadau sarvaṃ tasyāpi sa ghṛṇānidhiḥ \|*  
*labdhvaivamīśvarādeva brahmā sarvātmatāṃ kṣaṇāt \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Thus obtaining the state of being the Atman of all in a trice, from Śiva, Brahmā hastened to and saw Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 11.13.36-41 \|\|

*tvaramāṇotha saṃgamya dadarśa puruṣottamam \|*  
*kṣīrārṇavālaye śubhre vimāne sūryasaṃnibhe \|\| 36 \|\|*

*hemaratnānvite divye manasā tena nirmite \|*  
*anaṃtabhogaśayyāyāṃ śayānaṃ paṃkajekṣaṇam \|\| 37 \|\|*

*caturbhujamudārāṃgaṃ sarvābharaṇabhūṣitam \|*  
*śaṃkhacakradharaṃ saumyaṃ candrabiṃbasamānanam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*śrīvatsavakṣasaṃ devaṃ prasannamadhurasmitam \|*  
*dharāmṛdukarāṃbhojasparśaraktapadāṃbujam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*kṣīrārṇavāmṛtamiva śayānaṃ yoganidrayā \|*  
*tamasā kālarudrākhyaṃ rajasā kanakāṃḍajam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*sattvena sarvagaṃ viṣṇuṃ nirguṇatve maheśvaram \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā puruṣaṃ brahmā pragalbhamidamabravīt \|\| 41 \|\|*
