36-41. He saw Viṣṇu lying on Śeṣa\[1\] in his abode in the milk-ocean. A white canopy resembling the sun was spread. It was created by him mentally. It was set with gold and gems. Lord Viṣṇu had eyes resembling lotus. He had splendid body with four arms. He was bedecked in ornaments. He was holding conch and discus. His face shone like the disc of the moon. The scar Śrīvatsa marked his chest. He was smiling sweetly. His lotus-like feet attained red hue due to the contact of the lotus-like Lakṣmī. In Yogic slumber he appeared lying in the nectarine milky ocean. By the Guṇa of Tamas he was Kālarudra; by that of Rajas he was Brahmā; by that of Sattva he was Viṣṇu. In Nirguṇa state he was lord Śiva. On seeing him Brahmā spoke seriously—“O Viṣṇu, I am going to devour you as you did me formerly.”

## \|\| 11.13.42 \|\|

*grasāmi tvāmahaṃ viṣṇo tvamātmānaṃ yathā purā \|*  
*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā pratibuddhya pitāmaham \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. On hearing this Viṣṇu woke up, saw Brahmā and smiled slightly.

## \|\| 11.13.43 \|\|

*udaikṣata mahābāhussmitamīṣaccakāra ca \|*  
*tasminnavasare viṣṇurgrastastena mahātmanā \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. In the meantime Viṣṇu was devoured by Brahmā and immediately created through the middle of the eyebrows.

## \|\| 11.13.44-47 \|\|

*sṛṣṭaśca brahmaṇā sadyo bhruvormadhyādayatnataḥ \|*  
*tasminnavasare sākṣādbhagavānindubhūṣaṇaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*śaktiṃ tayorapi draṣṭumarūpo rūpamāsthitaḥ \|*  
*prasādamatulaṃ kartuṃ purā dattavarastayoḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*āgacchattatra yatremau brahmanārāyaṇau sthitau \|*  
*atha tuṣṭuvaturdevaṃ prītau bhītau ca kautukāt \|\| 46 \|\|*

*praṇematuśca bahuśo bahumānena dūrataḥ \|*  
*bhavopi bhagavānetāvanugṛhya pinākadhṛk \|\| 47 \|\|*

44-47. In the meantime the moon-crested lord came to the place to test their Śakti. Though devoid of form he assumed a form in order to bless them as he had previously done. Both of them were delighted and frightened and so eulogised the lord and bowed to him with respect from a distance. The trident-bearing lord blessed them and vanished even as they watched him with respect.

## Chapter 14 - The manifestation of Rudras

## \|\| 11.14.2 \|\|

*kalpekalpe prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā brahmā brahmāṃḍasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*avṛddhihetorbhūtānāṃ mumoha bhṛśaduḥkhitaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

I. I shall expain the reasons for the manifestation of Rudra in every Kalpa whereby the broken series of Brahmā’s creation is resumed.

2\. After creating the subjects in every Kalpa, Brahmā born of the cosmic egg felt excessively distressed. He was deluded.

## \|\| 11.14.3-4 \|\|

*tasya duḥkhapraśāṃtyarthaṃ prajānāṃ ca vivṛddhaye \|*  
*tattatkalpeṣu kālātmā rudro rudragaṇādhipaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*nirdiṣṭaḥ pamameśena maheśo nīlalohitaḥ \|*  
*putro bhūtvānugṛhṇāti brahmāṇaṃ brahmaṇonujaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. In order to pacify his misery and to multiply his subjects, in the various Kalpas, Rudra, Brahma’s younger brother, becomes the son of Brahmā and blesses him.

## \|\| 11.14.5 \|\|

*sa eva bhagavānīśastejorāśiranāmayaḥ \|*  
*anādinidhanodhātā bhūtasaṃkocako vibhuḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Ho alone is lord Īśa, a mass of splendour, free from ailment, devoid of beginning and end, the creator and the lord making all living beings shrink.

## \|\| 11.14.6 \|\|

*paramaiśvaryasaṃyuktaḥ parameśvarabhāvitaḥ \|*  
*tacchaktyādhiṣṭhitaśśaśvattaccihnairapi cihnitaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Endowed with lordly qualities, he is purified by Parameśvara. He is presided over by his Śakti and marked by his symbols.

## \|\| 11.14.7 \|\|

*tannāmanāmā tadrūpastatkāryakaraṇakṣamaḥ \|*  
*tattulyavyavahāraśca tadājñāparipālakaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. He has the same name, the same form; he can perform his task; he has same function as he maintains and abides by his commands.

## \|\| 11.14.8 \|\|

*sahasrādityasaṃkāśaścandrāvayavabhūṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*bhujaṃgahārakeyūravalayo muṃjamekhalaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He resembles a thousand suns, he is bedecked in crescent moon. Serpents constitute his necklaces, shoulderlets and bangles.

## \|\| 11.14.9 \|\|

*jalaṃdharaviriṃcendrakapālaśakalojjvalaḥ \|*  
*gaṅgātuṃgataraṃgārdhapiṃgalānanamūrdhajaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. He is brilliant holding the skulls of asura Jalandhara, Brahmā, and Indra, his tawny hair, moustache and beard are drenched in the surging waves of Gaṅgā.

## \|\| 11.14.10 \|\|

*bhagnadaṃṣṭrāṃkurākrāntaprāntakāntadharādharaḥ \|*  
*savyaśravaṇapārśvāṃtamaṃḍalīkṛtakuṇḍalaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. His lips shine with the tips being hit by the sharp-pointed curved fangs; his ear-rings make a halo around his left ear.

## \|\| 11.14.11 \|\|

*mahāvṛṣabhaniryāṇo mahājaladaniḥsvanaḥ \|*  
*mahānalasamaprakhyo mahābalaparākramaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He is seated on a great bull; his voice sounds like thunder. He is lustrous like fire, his strength and exploits are great.

## \|\| 11.14.12 \|\|

*evaṃ ghoramahārūpo brahmaputrīṃ maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*vijñānaṃ brahmaṇe dattvā sarge sahakaroti ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. He whose features are hideous in this manner and who is born as the son of Brahmā bestows wisdom on him and co-operates with him in the activity of creation.

## \|\| 11.14.13 \|\|

*tasmādrudraprasādena pratikalpaṃ prajāpateḥ \|*  
*pravāharūpato nityā prajāsṛṣṭiḥ pravartate \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. It is due to his grace that the creation in every Kalpa functions as a perpetual series.

## \|\| 11.14.14 \|\|

*kadācitprārthitaḥ sraṣṭuṃ brahmaṇā nīlalohitaḥ \|*  
*svātmanā sadṛśān sarvān sasarja manasā vibhuḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Once, when requested by Brahmā to create, he mentally created all beings exactly like himself.

## \|\| 11.14.15 \|\|

*kapardino nirātaṃkānnīlagrīvāṃstrilocanān \|*  
*jarāmaraṇanirmuktān dīptaśūlavarāyudhān \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. All of them had matted hair; they were free from fear and distress, had blue necks and three eyes, were free from decaying age and death; they had shining tridents as their excellent weapons.

## \|\| 11.14.16 \|\|

*taistu saṃcchāditaṃ sarvaṃ caturdaśavidhaṃ jagat \|*  
*tāndṛṣṭā vividhānrudrān rudramāha pitāmahaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The fourteen worlds of the universe were filled up by them. On seeing these various Rudras, Brahmā spoke to Śiva.

## \|\| 11.14.17 \|\|

*namaste devadeveśa māsrākṣīrīdṛśīḥ prajāḥ \|*  
*anyāḥ sṛja tvaṃ bhadraṃ te prajā mṛtyusamanvitāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. “Obeisance to you, O lord of gods, do not create such subjects. Welfare to you. Create other subjects that may be endowed with death.”

## \|\| 11.14.18 \|\|

*ityuktaḥ prahasanprāha brahmāṇaṃ parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*nāsti me tādṛśassargassṛja tvamaśubhāḥ prajāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. When told thus, the lord replied to Brahmā, “Such a creation is not my task. You alone create inauspicious beings.

## \|\| 11.14.19 \|\|

*ye tvime manasā sṛṣṭā mahātmāno mahābalāḥ \|*  
*cariṣyaṃti mayā sārdhaṃ sarva eva hi yājñikāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The noble beings of great strength created by me mentally will walk about in my company. They will regulate the sacrifices.”

## \|\| 11.14.20 \|\|

*ityuktvā viśvakarmāṇaṃ viśvabhūteśvaro haraḥ \|*  
*saha rudraiḥ prajāsargānnivṛttātmā vyatiṣṭhata \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. After saying thus to the creator, Śiva the lord of living beings desisted from creation and remained in the company of Rudras.

## \|\| 11.14.21 \|\|

*tataḥ prabhṛti devo 'sau na prasūte prajāḥ śubhāḥ \|*  
*ūrdhvaretāḥ sthitaḥ sthāṇuryāvadābhūtasaṃplavam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. From that time onwards the lord does not procreate auspicious beings. He stands in Yogic trance till the dissolution of the universe.

## Chapter 15 - Song of Prayer addressed to Śiva and Śivā

## \|\| 11.15.1 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*yadā punaḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭā na vyavardhanta vedhasaḥ \|*  
*tadā maithunajāṃ sṛṣṭiṃ brahmā kartumamanyata \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

1\. When the creation of Brahmā did not multiply Brahmā thought of creation by the process of sexual intercourse.

## \|\| 11.15.2 \|\|

*na nirgataṃ purā yasmānnārīṇāṃ kulamīśvarāt \|*  
*tena maithunajāṃ sṛṣṭiṃ na śaśāka pitāmahaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Since the race of women had not emanated from the lord formerly, Brahmā could not produce creation through sexual intercourse.

## \|\| 11.15.3 \|\|

*tatassa vidadhe buddhimarthaniścayagāminīm \|*  
*prajānameva vṛddhyarthaṃ praṣṭavyaḥ parameśvara \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Then he finally resolved that the lord should be asked in respect of multiplying the subjects.

## \|\| 11.15.4 \|\|

*prasādena vinā tasya na vardherannimāḥ prajāḥ \|*  
*evaṃ saṃcintya viśvātmā tapaḥ kartuṃ pracakrame \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Thinking that without his grace the subjects will not increase, Brahmā began to perform penance.

## \|\| 11.15.5-7 \|\|

*tadādyā paramā śaktiranaṃtā lokabhāvinī \|*  
*ādyā sūkṣmatarā śuddhā bhāvagamyā manoharā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*nirguṇā niṣprapañcā ca niṣkalā nirupaplavā \|*  
*niraṃtaratarā nityā nityamīśvarapārśvagā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tayā paramayā śaktyā bhagavaṃtaṃ triyambakam \|*  
*saṃcintya hṛdaye brahmā tatāpa paramaṃ tapaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

5-7. His primordial eternal Śakti is subtle, pure, pleasant and intelligible only through piety; it is devoid of attributes, unsullied, unramified unruffled, perpetual and it ever remains with Īśvara. Thus Brahmā pondered over the lord and his great Śakti and performed penance.

## \|\| 11.15.8 \|\|

*tīvreṇa tapasā tasya yuktasya parameṣṭhinaḥ \|*  
*acireṇaiva kālena pitā saṃpratutoṣa ha \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Ere long the lord was pleased with Brahmā who was endowed with severe penance.

## \|\| 11.15.9 \|\|

*tataḥ kenacidaṃśena mūrtimāviśya kāmapi \|*  
*ardhanārīśvaro bhūtvā yayau devassvayaṃ haraḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Becoming half-female after introducing certain parts into a certain image, the lord himself came there.

## \|\| 11.15.10-15 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā paramaṃ devaṃ tamasaḥ paramavyayam \|*  
*advitīyamanirdeśyamadṛśyamakṛtātmabhiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*sarvalokavidhātāraṃ sarvalokeśvareśvaram \|*  
*sarvalokavidhāyinyā śaktyā paramayā yutam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*apratarkyamanābhāsamameyamajaraṃ dhruvam \|*  
*acalaṃ nirguṇaṃ śāṃtamanaṃtamahimāspadam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*sarvagaṃ sarvadaṃ sarvasadasadvyaktivarjitam \|*  
*sarvopamānanirmuktaṃ śaraṇyaṃ śāśvataṃ śivam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*praṇamya daṃḍavadbrahmā samutthāya kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|*  
*śraddhāvinayasaṃpannaiḥ śrāvyaiḥ saṃskarasaṃyutaiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*yathārthayuktasarvārthairvedārthaparibṛṃhitaiḥ \|*  
*tuṣṭāva devaṃ devīṃ ca sūktaiḥ sūkṣmārthagocaraiḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

10-15. On seeing the lord, Brahmā eulogised him as well as the goddess, with hymns full of subtle meaning—the lord who is beyond darkness, is eternal, without a second, incomprehensible, invisible to the libertine, the creator, overlord, endowed with the creative power, who is beyond arguments, has no fallacious appearance, is immeasurable, unaging, stable, unmoving, devoid of attributes, quiescent, possessed of infinity, omnipresent, bestower of boons, devoid of difference between the Existent and the non-Existent, incomparable, worthy of being sought refuge and permanent. He prostrated before him and then stood up with palms joined with reverence. He eulogised him with faith and humility by means of hymns of subtle, sweet, refined and pious meanings that explained the Vedic texts.

## \|\| 11.15.16 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*jaya deva mahādeva jayeśvara maheśvara \|*  
*jaya sarvaguṇa śreṣṭha jaya sarvasurādhipa \|\| 16 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

16\. O lord, be victorious. O Īśvara, O Maheśvara, splendid with attributes, be victorious.

## \|\| 11.15.17 \|\|

*jaya prakṛti kalyāṇi jaya prakṛtināyike \|*  
*jaya prakṛtidūre tvaṃ jaya prakṛtisundari \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O auspicious goddess, O heroine of Prakṛti and the one beyond Prakṛti and naturally beautiful, be victorious.

## \|\| 11.15.18 \|\|

*jayāmoghamahāmāya jayāmogha manoratha \|*  
*jayāmoghamahālīla jayāmoghamahābala \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O lord of fruitful Māyā, of fruitful will, of great sports and of fruitful strength, be victorious.

## \|\| 11.15.19 \|\|

*jaya viśvajaganmātarjaya viśvajaganmaye \|*  
*jaya viśvajagaddhātri jaya viśvajagatsakhi \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O mother of the universe, O goddess identical with the universe, O creator and companion of the universe, be victorious.

## \|\| 11.15.20 \|\|

*jaya śāśvatikaiśvarye jaya śāśvatikālaya \|*  
*jaya śāśvatikākāra jaya śāśvatikānuga \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Be victorious, O lord of eternal prosperity and permanent abode. Be victorious, O lord of eternal form. Be victorious, O lord of permanent devotees.

## \|\| 11.15.21 \|\|

*jayātmatrayanirmātri jayātmatrayapālini \|*  
*jayātmatrayasaṃhartri jayātmatrayanāyike \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Be victorious O creatress, protectress, annihilatress and the heroine of the three Ātmans.

## \|\| 11.15.22 \|\|

*jayāvalokanāyattajagatkāraṇabṛṃhaṇa \|*  
*jayopekṣākaṭākṣotthahutabhugbhuktabhautika \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Be victorious, O lord ready to survey, enlarge the universe. Be victorious, O lord from whose terrible glance rises the fire that consumes all the worlds.

## \|\| 11.15.23 \|\|

*jaya devādyavijñeye svātmasūkṣmadṛśojjvale \|*  
*jaya sthūlātmaśaktyeśejaya vyāptacarācare \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Be victorious, O goddess incomprehensible to the gods and others, O goddess that shinest brilliantly with your subtle vision. Be victorious,'O goddess the part of the gross Śakti of the Ātman. Be victorious, O goddess pervading the mobile and immobile beings.

## \|\| 11.15.24 \|\|

*jaya nāmaikavinyastaviśvatattvasamuccaya \|*  
*jayāsuraśironiṣṭhaśreṣṭhānugakadaṃbaka \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Be victorious. O lord merging various principles of the universe into one. Be victorious, O lord the groups of whose followers have stepped on the heads of Asùras.

## \|\| 11.15.25 \|\|

*jayopāśritasaṃrakṣāsaṃvidhānapaṭīyasi \|*  
*jayonmūlitasaṃsāraviṣavṛkṣāṃkurodgame \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Be victorious, O goddess affording protection to those who resort to you. Be victorious, O goddess who uproot the spirits of the poisonous tree of worldly existence.

## \|\| 11.15.26 \|\|

*jaya prādeśikaiśvaryavīryaśauryavijṛṃbhaṇa \|*  
*jaya viśvabahirbhūta nirastaparavaibhava \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Be victorious, O lord enhancing prosperity, prowess and heroism. Be victorious, O lord, stationed beyond the universe, O lord who hast quelled the might of the enemies.

## \|\| 11.15.27 \|\|

*jaya praṇītapañcārthaprayogaparamāmṛta \|*  
*jaya pañcārthavijñānasudhāstotrasvarūpiṇi \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Be victorious, O immortal lord who hast laid the rite of “five objects.” Be victorious, O goddess having the form of the hymn with the knowledge of the “five objects.”

## \|\| 11.15.28 \|\|

*jayati ghorasaṃsāramahārogabhiṣagvara \|*  
*jayānādimalājñānatamaḥpaṭalacaṃdrike \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Be victorious, O lord, the physician par excellence for the great suffering of the terrible worldly existence. Be victorious, O goddess the moon-light for the layers of darkness of ignorance, the primordial dirt.

## \|\| 11.15.29 \|\|

*jaya tripurakālāgne jaya tripurabhairavi \|*  
*jaya triguṇanirmukte jaya triguṇamardini \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Be victorious, O black fire that consumed the Tripuras. Be victorious, O goddess Tripurabhairavī. Be victorious, O lord devoid of three attributes. Be victorious P goddess, the possessor of three attributes.

## \|\| 11.15.30 \|\|

*jaya prathamasarvajña jaya sarvaprabodhika \|*  
*jaya pracuradivyāṃga jaya prārthitadāyini \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Be victorious, O omniscient one. Be victorious, O goddess enlightening every one. Be victorious O lord having prolific divine limbs. Be victorious, O goddess bestowing all desires.

## \|\| 11.15.31 \|\|

*kva deva te paraṃ dhāma kva ca tucchaṃ ca no vacaḥ \|*  
*tathāpi bhagavan bhaktyā pralapaṃtaṃ kṣamasva mām \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O lord, where is your great splendour and where the worthless words of ours. Still O lord, forgive me that babble but with devotion.

## \|\| 11.15.32 \|\|

*vijñāpyaivaṃvidhaiḥ sūktairviśvakarmā caturmukhaḥ \|*  
*namaścakāra rudrāya radrāṇyai ca muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. After eulogising with these and similar hymns the four-faced lord, the creator of the universe bowed again and again to Rudra and Rudrāṇī.

## \|\| 11.15.33 \|\|

*idaṃ stotravaraṃ puṇyaṃ brahmaṇā samudīritam \|*  
*ardhanārīśvaraṃ nāma śivayorharṣavardhanam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. This holy and excellent hymn “Ardhanārīśvara Stotra” uttered by Brahma enhances the delight of Śiva and Śivā.

## \|\| 11.15.34 \|\|

*ya idaṃ kīrtayedbhaktyā yasya kasyāpi śikṣayā \|*  
*sa tatphalamavāpnoti śivayoḥ prītikāraṇāt \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. He who recites this with devotion or teaches to anyone whatsoever reaps the fruit thereof as a result of the pleasure of Śiva and Śivā.

## \|\| 11.15.35 \|\|

*sakalabhuvanabhūtabhāvanābhyāṃ jananavināśavihīnavigrahābhyām \|*  
*naravarayuvatīvapurdharābhyāṃ satatamahaṃ praṇatosmi śaṃkarābhyām \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. I bow to Śiva and Śivā the sanctifiers of living beings in the entire universe; the couple whose bodies are devoid of birth and death and who have taken the bodies of an excellent man and a youthful maiden.

## Chapter 16 - The manifestation of divine Śakti

## \|\| 11.16.1-3 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*atha devo mahādevo mahājaladanādayā \|*  
*vācā madhuragaṃbhīraśivadaślakṣṇavarṇayā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*arthasaṃpannapadayā rājalakṣaṇayuktayā \|*  
*aśeṣaviṣayāraṃbharakṣāvimaladakṣayā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*manoharatarodāramadhurasmitapūrvayā \|*  
*saṃbabhāṣe susaṃpīto viśvakarmāṇamīśvaraḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

1-3. Then the delighted god Śiva spoke to Brahmā with a benign and sweet smile. His voice sounded like thunder. All the letters were sweet, majestic, soft, clear, full and rich in meanings. They had royal qualities being pure and efficient in the protection of all subjects.

## \|\| 11.16.4 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*vatsa vatsa mahābhāga mama putra pitāmaha \|*  
*jñātameva mayā sarvaṃ tava vākyasya gauravam \|\| 4 \|\|*

Lord Śiva said:—

4\. Dear child, O fortunate one, the gravity of your statements has been understood by me.

## \|\| 11.16.5 \|\|

*prajānāmeva bṛddhyarthaṃ tapastaptaṃ tvayādhunā \|*  
*tapasā 'nena tuṣṭosmi dadāmi ca tavepsitam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. It is for the increase in the number of the subjects that this penance has been performed by you. I am delighted with your penance. I shall grant you what you desire.

## \|\| 11.16.6 \|\|

*ityuktvā paramodāraṃ svabhāvamadhuraṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*sasarja vapuṣo bhāgāddevīṃ devavaro haraḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. After this sweet and liberal speech the excellent lord created the goddess from a part of his body.

## \|\| 11.16.7 \|\|

*yāmāhurbrahmavidvāṃso devīṃ divyaguṇānvitām \|*  
*parasya paramāṃ śaktiṃ bhavasya paramātmanaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. It is the goddess whom scholars of the Vedas call

the greatest Śakti endowed with the divine qualities of Śiva the great soul.

## \|\| 11.16.8 \|\|

*yasyāṃ na khalu vidyaṃte janma mṛtyujarādayaḥ \|*  
*yā bhavānī bhavasyāṃgātsamāvirabhavatkila \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. It was the goddess in whom there is neither birth, nor death nor old age nor other similar things. It was the goddess who manifested herself from the body of Śiva.

## \|\| 11.16.9 \|\|

*yasyā vāco nivartante manasā ceṃdriyaiḥ saha \|*  
*sā bharturvapuṣo bhāgājjāteva samadṛśyata \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. She from whom words recede along with the mind and the sense-organs, appeared to be born of a part of the body of her husband.

## \|\| 11.16.10 \|\|

*yā sā jagadidaṃ kṛtsnaṃ mahimnā vyāpya tiṣṭhati \|*  
*śarīriṇīva sa devī vicitraṃ samalakṣyata \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The goddess who pervades everything through her greatness was seen like a wonderfully embodied being.

## \|\| 11.16.11 \|\|

*sarvaṃ jagadidaṃ caiṣā saṃmohayati māyayā \|*  
*īśvarātsaiva jātābhūdajātā paramārthataḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. It is she who fascinates the entire universe with her Māyā. Really she is unborn but she appeared to be born of Śiva.

## \|\| 11.16.12 \|\|

*na yasyā paramo bhāvaḥ surāṇāmapi gocaraḥ \|*  
*viśvāmareśvarī caiva vibhaktā bharturaṃgataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Her great form is not visible even to the gods. Such a great goddess of all the gods was divided in the body of her lord.

## \|\| 11.16.13-14 \|\|

*tāṃ dṛṣṭvā parameśānīṃ sarvalokamaheśvarīm \|*  
*sarvajñāṃ sarvagāṃ sūkṣmāṃ sadasadvyaktivarjitām \|\| 13 \|\|*

*paramāṃ nikhilaṃ bhāsā bhāsayantīmidaṃ jagat \|*  
*praṇipatya mahādevīṃ prārthayāmāsa vai virāṭ \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. On seeing the great omniscient, omnipresent subtle goddess, devoid of the difference between Sat and Asat, the goddess who illuminates the universe with her brilliance, Brahmā bowed and prayed.

## \|\| 11.16.15 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*devi devena sṛṣṭo 'hamādau sarvajaganmayi \|*  
*prajāsarge niyuktaśca sṛjāmi sakalaṃ jagat \|\| 15 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

15\. O Goddess in the beginning I was created by the lord and employed in the activity of the creation. I create the universe.

## \|\| 11.16.16 \|\|

*manasā nirmitāḥ sarve devi devādayo mayā \|*  
*na vṛddhimupagacchanti sṛjyamānāḥ punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O Goddess, the gods and others are mentally created by me. Though they are created again and again they do not increase in number.

## \|\| 11.16.17 \|\|

*mithunaprabhavāmeva kṛtvā sṛṣṭimataḥ param \|*  
*saṃvardhayitumicchāmi sarvā eva mama prajāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Hereafter I wish to increase the number through copulation.

## \|\| 11.16.18 \|\|

*na nirgataṃ purā tvatto nārīṇāṃ kulamavyayam \|*  
*tena nārīkulaṃ sraṣṭuṃ śaktirmama na vidyate \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The race of women has not emerged from you. Hence I cannot create an everlasting race of women.

## \|\| 11.16.19-22 \|\|

*sarvāsāmeva śaktīnāṃ tvattaḥ khalu samudbhavaḥ \|*  
*tasmātsarvatra sarveṣāṃ sarvaśaktipradāyinīm \|\| 19 \|\|*

*tvāmeva varadāṃ māyāṃ prārthayāmi sureśvarīm \|*  
*carācaravivṛddhyarthamaṃśenaikena sarvage \|\| 20 \|\|*

*dakṣasya mama putrasya putrī bhava bhavārdini \|*  
*evaṃ sā yācitā devī brahmaṇā brahmayoninā \|\| 21 \|\|*

*śaktimekāṃ bhruvormadhyātsasarjātmasamaprabhām \|*  
*tāmāha prahasanprekṣya devadevavaro haraḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

19-22. Śaktis originate from you. Hence I worship you alone who bestow Śaktis upon everyone everywhere, who grant boons and who are Māyā and the goddess of the gods. O omnipresent goddess for the increase of the mobile and immobile beings, please be born with a part of yours, as the daughter of Dakṣa my son. Thus requested by Brahmā the goddess created a Śakti equal in splendour to herself from the middle of her eyebrows. Lord Śiva looked at her laughingly and spoke.

## \|\| 11.16.23-25 \|\|

*brahmāṇaṃ tapasārādhya kuru tasya yathepsitam \|*  
*tāmājñāṃ parameśasya śirasā pratigṛhya sā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*brahmaṇo vacanāddevī dakṣasya duhitābhavat \|*  
*dattvaivamatulāṃ śaktiṃ brahmaṇe brahmarūpiṇīm \|\| 24 \|\|*

*viveśa dehaṃ devasya devaścāṃtaradhīyata \|*  
*tadā prabhṛti loke 'smin striyāṃ bhogaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

23-25. “After propitiating Brahmā with penance you shall carry out what he desires”. The Śakti obeyed the lord. At the instance of Brahmā she became the daughter of Dakṣa. After giving the incomparable Śakti in the form of Brahman to Brahmā, the goddess re-entered the body of the lord. The lord vanished. Since that time the enjoyment of sexual pleasures in women was established.

## \|\| 11.16.26 \|\|

*prajāsṛṣṭiśca vipreṃdrā maithunena pravartate \|*  
*brahmāpi prāpa sānandaṃ santoṣaṃ munipuṃgavāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. O leading brahmins, procreation functions through copulation. O leading sages, Brahmā too was satisfied.

## \|\| 11.16.27 \|\|

*etadvassarvamākhyātaṃ devyāḥ śaktisamudbhavam \|*  
*puṇyavṛddhikaraṃ śrāvyaṃ bhūtasargānupaṃgataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Thus the manifestation of Śakti has been narrated to you. It enhances merit. It shall be narrated with the story of creation.

## \|\| 11.16.28 \|\|

*ya idaṃ kīrtayennityaṃ devyāḥ śaktisamudbhavam \|*  
*puṇyaṃ sarvamavāpnoti putrāṃśca labhate śubhān \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. He who recites this every day attains merits and obtains worthy sons.

## Chapter 17 - The Narrative of Creation

## \|\| 11.17.1-2 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*evaṃ labdhvā parāṃ śaktimīśvarādeva śāśvatīm \|*  
*maithunaprabhavāṃ sṛṣṭiṃ kartṛkāmaḥ prajāpatiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*svayamapyadbhuto nārī cārdhena puruṣo 'bhavat \|*  
*yārdhena nārī sā tasmācchatarūpā vyajāyata \|\| 2 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

1-2. Securing the great and eternal Śakti from the lord and desiring to initiate the process of procreation by copulation, Brahmā became a wondrous man in one half and a woman in one half. From the woman-half was born Śatarūpā.

## \|\| 11.17.3 \|\|

*virājamasṛjadbrahmā so 'rdhana puruṣo 'bhavat \|*  
*sa vai svāyaṃbhuvaḥ pūrvaṃ puruṣo manurucyate \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The man-half created Virāja, called Svāyambhuva Manu, the first creation.

## \|\| 11.17.4 \|\|

*sā devī śatarūpā tu tapaḥ kṛtvā suduścaram \|*  
*bhartāraṃ dīptayaśasaṃ manumevānvapadyata \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Performing a difficult penance the gentle Śatarūpā got the Manu of bright fame as her husband.

## \|\| 11.17.5 \|\|

*tasmāttu śatarūpā sā putradvayamasūyata \|*  
*priyavratottānapādau putrau putravatāṃ varau \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Śatarūpā bore him two sons, Priyavrata and Uttānapāda.

## \|\| 11.17.6 \|\|

*kanye dve ca mahābhāge yābhyāṃ jātāstvimāḥ prajāḥ \|*  
*ākūtirekā vijñeyā prasūtiraparā smṛtā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. She bore two daughters of great fortune from whom emanates all creation. They were Ākūti and Prasūti.

## \|\| 11.17.7 \|\|

*svāyaṃbhuvaḥ prasūtiṃ ca dadau dakṣāya tāṃ prabhuḥ \|*  
*ruceḥ prajāpatiścaiva cākūtiṃ samapādayat \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Lord Manu gave Prasūti to Dakṣa. Brahmā gave Ākūti to Ruci.

## \|\| 11.17.8 \|\|

*ākūtyāṃ mithunaṃ jajñe mānasasya ruceḥ śubham \|*  
*yajñaśca dakṣiṇā caiva yābhyāṃ saṃvartitaṃ jagat \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The mental son Ruci begot of Ākūti a son Yajña and a daughter Dakṣiṇā. The two make the universe whirl.

## \|\| 11.17.9 \|\|

*svāyaṃbhuvasutāyāṃ tu prasūtyāṃ lokamātaraḥ \|*  
*catasro viṃśatiḥ kanyā dakṣastvajanayatprabhuḥ \| \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Lord Dakṣa begot of Prasūti, the daughter of Svāyambhuva, twenty-four daughters called the mothers of the world.

## \|\| 11.17.10-16 \|\|

*śraddhā lakṣmīrdhṛtiḥ puṣṭistuṣṭirmedhā kriyā tathā \|*  
*buddhirlajjā vapuḥ śāṃtissiddhiḥ kīrtistrayodaśī \|\| 10 \|\|*

*patnyarthaṃ pratijagrāha dharmo dākṣāyaṇīḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*tābhyaḥ śiṣṭā yavīyasya ekādaśa sulocanāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*khyātiḥ satyarthasaṃbhūtiḥ smṛtiḥ prītiḥ kṣamā tathā \|*  
*sannatiścānasūyā ca ūrjā svāhā svadhā tathā \|\| 12 \|\|*

*bhṛguśśarvo marīciśca aṃgirāḥ pulahaḥ kratuḥ \|*  
*pulastyo 'trirviśiṣṭhaśca pāvakaḥ pitarastathā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*khyātyādyā jagṛhuḥ kanyāmunayo munisattamāḥ \|*  
*kāmādyāstu yaśoṃtā ye te trayodaśa sūnavaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*dharmasya jajñire tāstu śraddhādyāssusukhottarāḥ \|*  
*duḥkhottarāśca hiṃsāyāmadharmasya ca saṃtatau \|\| 15 \|\|*

*nikṛtyādaya utpannāḥputrāśca dharmalakṣaṇāḥ \|*  
*naiṣāṃ bhāryāśca putrā vā sarve tvaniyamāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

10-16. Lord Dharma took thirteen of his daughters as his wives. They were Śraddhā, Lakṣmī, Dhṛti, Puṣṭi, Tuṣṭi, Medhā, Kriyā, Buddhi, Lajjā, Vapu, Śānti, Siddhi and Kīrti the thirteenth. The other eleven were Khyāti, Satī, Asambhūti, Smṛti, Prīti, Kṣamā, Sannati, Anasūyā, Ūrjā, Svāhā and Svadhā. O sages, the sages Bhṛgu, Śarva, Marīci, Aṅgiras, Pulaha, Kratu, Pulastya, Atri, Vasiṣṭha, Pāvaka and the Pitṛs married them. Thirteen sons beginning with Kama and ending with Yaśas were begotten by Dharma of Śraddhā and others happy and conducive to happiness. Nikṛti and others were begotten of Hiṃsā by Adharma. They bore the traits of Adharma and were conducive to unhappiness. They had no wives or sons. They practised no virtue.

## \|\| 11.17.17-21 \|\|

*sa eṣa tāmasassargo jajñe dharmaniyāmakaḥ \|*  
*yā sā dakṣasya duhitā rudrasya dayitā satī \|\| 17 \|\|*

*bhartṛnindāprasaṃgena tyaktvā dākṣāyiṇīṃ tanum \|*  
*dakṣaṃ ca dakṣabhāryāṃ ca viniṃdya saha bandhubhiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*sā menāyāmāvirabhūtputrī himavato gireḥ \|*  
*rudrastu tāṃ satīṃ dṛṣṭvā rudrāṃstvātmasamaprabhān \|\| 19 \|\|*

*yathāsṛjadasaṃkhyātāṃstathā kathitameva ca \|*  
*bhṛgoḥ khyātyāṃ samutpannā lakṣmīrnārāyaṇapriyā \|\| 20 \|\|*

*devau dhātṛvidhātārau manvaṃtaravidhāriṇau \|*  
*tayorvai putrapautrādyāśśataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

17-21. The Tāmasa creation was controlled by Dharma. Dakṣa’s daughter Satī, wife of Rudra cast off her body as daughter of Dakṣa in the context of the insult offered to her husband. She rebuked Dakṣa and Dakṣa’s wife and their kinsmen. She was born as the daughter of Menā and Himavat. On seeing Satī how Rudra created many Rudras with lustres similar to his, has already been narrated. Bhṛgu begot of Khyāti the daughter Lakṣmī who became the wife of Viṣṇu. He begot two sons Dhātṛ and Vidhātṛ who became the founders of Manvantara. Their progeny is numerous, in hundreds and thousands.

## \|\| 11.17.22 \|\|

*svāyaṃbhuve 'ṃtare nītāḥ sarve te bhārgavā matāḥ \|*  
*marīcerapi saṃbhūtiḥ paurṇamāsamasūyata \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The descendants of Bhṛgu lived in the Svāyambhuva Manvantara. Sambhūti, son of Marīci, gave birth to a son Paurṇamāsa.

## \|\| 11.17.23 \|\|

*kanyācatuṣṭayaṃ caiva mahīyāṃsastadanvayāḥ \|*  
*yeṣāṃ vaṃśe samutpanno bahuputrasya kaśyapaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. He had four daughters and descendants large in number. In that family was born Kaśyapa who had many sons.

## \|\| 11.17.24-25 \|\|

*smṛtiścāṃgirasaḥ patnī janayāmāsa vai sutau \|*  
*āgnīdhraṃ śarabhañcaiva tathā kanyācatuṣṭayam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*tadīyāḥ putrapautrāśca yetītāste sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*prītyāṃ pulastyabhāryāyāṃ dantognirabhavatsutaḥ \|*  
*pūrvajanmani yogastyassmṛtaḥ svāyaṃbhuve 'ṃtare \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. Smṛti, wife of Aṅgiras, bore two sons Āgnīdhra and Śarabha and four daughters. Their progeny continued in thousands. Dantogni was born as the son of Prīti the wife of Pulastya. He was Agastya in the previous birth in the Svāyambhuva Manvantara.

## \|\| 11.17.26-27 \|\|

*tatsaṃtatīyā bahavaḥ paulastyā iti viśrutāḥ \|*  
*kṣamā tu suṣuve putrānpulahasya prajāpateḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*kardamaśca suriścaiva sahiṣṇuśceti te trayaḥ \|*  
*tretāgnivarcasassarve yeṣāṃ vaṃśaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. His descendants famous as Paulastyas were many. Kṣamā bore sons to Pulaha the Prajāpati. The three known as Kardama, Āsuri and Sahiṣṇu had the splendour of the sacrificial fires. Their race is well established.

## \|\| 11.17.28 \|\|

*kratoḥ kratusamānbhāryā sannatissuṣuve sutān \|*  
*naiṣāṃ bhāryāśca putrāśca sarve te hyūrdhvaretasaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Sannati, wife of Kratu, bore him sons who were equal to Kratu. They did not marry and hence were issueless.

## \|\| 11.17.29 \|\|

*ṣaṣṭistāni sahasrāṇi vālakhilyā iti smṛtāḥ \|*  
*anūroragrato yāṃti parivārya divākaram \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. They were sixty thousand in number and known as Vālakhilyas. They surround the sun and go ahead of his charioteer.

## \|\| 11.17.30 \|\|

*atrerbhāryānusūyā ca pañcātreyānasūyata \|*  
*kanyakāṃ ca śrutiṃ nāma mātā śaṃkhapadasya ca \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Atri’s wife Anasūya bore five sons the Ātreyas and a daughter Śruti, the mother of Śaṅkhapada.

## \|\| 11.17.31 \|\|

*satyanetraśca havyaśca āpomūrtiśśanaiścaraḥ \|*  
*somaśca pañcamastvete pañcātreyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The glorified five Ātreyas are Satyanetra, Havya, Āpomūrti, Śanaiścara and Soma.

## \|\| 11.17.32 \|\|

*teṣāṃ putrāśca pautrāśca hyātreyāṇāṃ mahātmanām \|*  
*svāyaṃbhuve 'ṃtare 'tītāḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The sons and grandsons of the noble Ātreyas are in hundreds and thousands. They lived in the Svāyambhuva Manvantara.

## \|\| 11.17.33-34 \|\|

*ūrjāyāṃ tu vasiṣṭhasya putrā vai sapta jajñire \|*  
*jyāyasī ca svasā teṣāṃ puṃḍarīkā sumadhyamā \|\| 33 \|\|*

*rajo gātrordhvabāhū ca savanaścānayaśca yaḥ \|*  
*sutapāśśukra ityete sapta saptarṣayaḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. Seven sons were born to Vasiṣṭha in Ūrjā and a daughter Puṇḍarīkā. They were Rajas, Gātra, Ūrdhvabāhu, Savana, Anaya, Sutapas and Śukra.

## \|\| 11.17.35 \|\|

*gotrāṇi nāmabhisteṣāṃ vāsiṣṭhānāṃ mahātmanām \|*  
*svāyaṃbhuve 'ṃtare 'tītānyarbudāni śatāni ca \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Their descendants with the names of Vasiṣṭha were in hundreds and hundred millions all in Svāyambhuva Manvantara.

## \|\| 11.17.36 \|\|

*ityeṣa ṛṣisargastu sānubaṃdhaḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*samāsādvistarādvaktumaśakyo 'yamiti dvijāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. This is the creation of the sages. It is impossible to mention this in detail.

## \|\| 11.17.37 \|\|

*yo 'sau rudrātmako bahnibrahmaṇo mānasassutaḥ \|*  
*svāhā tasya priyā lebhe putrāṃstrīnamitaujasaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Svāhā, wife of the fire-god the mental son of Brahma in the form of Rudra, bore three sons of unmeasured splendour.

## \|\| 11.17.38 \|\|

*pāvakaḥ pavamānaśca śucirityeṣa te trayaḥ \|*  
*nirmaṃthyaḥ pavamānassyādvaidyutaḥ pāvakassmṛtaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. They are Pāvaka, Pavamāna and Śuci. Pavamāna is the fire kindled by attrition. Pāvaka is the fire produced by lightning.

## \|\| 11.17.39-40 \|\|

*sūrye tapati yaścāsau śuciḥ saura udāhṛtaḥ \|*  
*havyavāhaḥ kavyavāhaḥ saharakṣā iti trayaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*trayāṇāṃ kramaśaḥ putrā devapitṛsurāśca te \|*  
*eteṣāṃ putrapautrāśca catvāriṃśannavaiva te \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. The solar fire is called Śuci. Their sons in order are:—Havyavāha, Kavyavāha and Saharakṣas. They are the deities, manes and gods. Their sons and grandsons are forty-nine.

## \|\| 11.17.41 \|\|

*kāmyanaimittikājasrakarmasu triṣu saṃsthitāḥ \|*  
*sarve tapasvino jñeyāḥ sarve vratabhṛtastathā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. They are propitiated in the three rites Kāmya, Naimittika and Nitya. They shall be known as saintly observing holy rites.

## \|\| 11.17.42-43 \|\|

*sarve rudrātmakaścaiva sarve rudraparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*tasmādagnimukhe yattaddhutaṃ syādeva kenacit \|\| 42 \|\|*

*tatsarvaṃ rudramuddiśya dattaṃ syānnātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*ityevaṃ niścayognīnāmanukrāṃto yathātatham \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. These are in the form of Rudra and devoted to him. Whatever is offered in fire by whomsoever it may be is the offering to Rudra. This is the decision in regard to the fires stated in order.

## \|\| 11.17.44-47 \|\|

*nātivistarato viprāḥ pitṝnvakṣyāmyataḥ param \|*  
*yasmātṣaḍṛtavasteṣāṃ sthānaṃ sthānābhimāninām \|\| 44 \|\|*

*ṛtavaḥ pitarastasmādityeṣā vaidikī śrutiḥ \|*  
*yuṣmādṛtuṣu sarve hi jāyaṃte sthāsnujaṃgamā \|\| 45 \|\|*

*tasmādete pitara ārtavā iti ca śrutam \|*  
*evaṃ pitṝṇāmeteṣāmṛtukālābhimāninām \|\| 46 \|\|*

*ātmaiśvaryā mahātmānastiṣṭhaṃtīhābbhrasaṃgamāt \|*  
*āgniṣvāttā barhiṣadaḥ pitaro dvividhāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

44-47. O Brahmins, I shall describe the manes now but not in detail. The manes preside over the seasons. Hence the Vedas declare “The seasons are the Pitṛs”. The mobile and immobile beings are created in the seasons. Hence it is mentioned in the Śruti, “The things produced in the seasons are the Pitṛs.” Noble persons derive prosperity from the Pitṛs who preside over the seasons. They stand in contact with the clouds. The Pitṛs are of two types: Agniṣvāttas and Barhiṣads.

## \|\| 11.17.48-49 \|\|

*ayajvānaśca yajvānaḥ kramātte mṛhamedhinaḥ \|*  
*svadhāsūta pitṛbhyaśca dve kanye lokaviśrute \|\| 48 \|\|*

*menāṃ ca dharaṇīṃ caiva yābhyāṃ viśvamidaṃ dhṛtam \|*  
*agniṣvāttasutā menā dharaṇī barhiṣatsutā \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. Householders are also of two types: Non-sacrificers, and Sacrificers. Svadhā bore the Pitṛs two daughters: Menā and Dharaṇī who uphold the universe. Menā was the daughter of Agniṣvāttas and Dharaṇī the daughter of Barhiṣads.

## \|\| 11.17.50 \|\|

*menā himavataḥ patnī mainākaṃ krauṃcameva ca \|*  
*gaurīṃ gaṃgāṃ ca suṣuve bhavāṃgāśleṣapāvanīm \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Menā, wife of Himavat, gave birth to Maināka, Krauñca, Gaṅgā and Gaurī sanctified by the embrace of Śiva’s body.

## \|\| 11.17.51 \|\|

*merostu dharaṇī patnī divyauṣadhisamanvitam \|*  
*maṃdaraṃ suṣuve putraṃ citrisundarakandharam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Dharaṇī, wife of Meru, gave birth to Mandara abounding in divine herbs and beautiful peaks of variegated forms.

## \|\| 11.17.52 \|\|

*sa eva maṃdaraḥ śrīmānmeruputrastapobalāt \|*  
*sākṣācchrīkaṃṭhanāthasya śivasyāvasathaṃ gataḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Mandara the glorious son of Meru became the abode of Śiva due to the strength of penance.

## \|\| 11.17.53 \|\|

*sāsūtā dharaṇī bhūyastriṃśatkanyāśca viśrutāḥ \|*  
*velāṃ ca niyatiṃ caiva tṛtīyāmapi cāyatim \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Dharaṇī gave birth to three famous daughters Velā, Niyati and Āyati.

## \|\| 11.17.54 \|\|

*āyatirniyatiścaiva patnyau dve bhṛguputrayoḥ \|*  
*svāyaṃbhuve 'ṃtare pūrvaṃ kathitaste tadanvayaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Āyati and Niyati became the wives of the sons of Bhṛgu. I have mentioned to you about their race in Svāyambhuva Manvantara.

## \|\| 11.17.55 \|\|

*suṣuve sāgarādvelā kanyāmekāmaniṃditām \|*  
*savarṇāṃ nāma sāmudrīṃ patnīṃ prācīnabarhiṣaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Velā bore Sāgara the holy daughter Savarṇā who became the wife of Prācīnabarhiṣ.

## \|\| 11.17.56 \|\|

*sāmudrī suṣuve putrāndaśa prācīnabarhiṣaḥ \|*  
*sarve prācetasā nāma dhanurvedasya pāragāḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Sāmudrī bore Prācīnabarhiṣ ten sons who were called Prācetasas. They were the masters of the science of archery.

## \|\| 11.17.57 \|\|

*yeṣāṃ svāyaṃbhuve dakṣaḥ putratvamagamatpurā \|*  
*triyambakasya śāpena cākṣuṣasyāṃtare manoḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Dakṣa in Svāyambhuva Manvantara became the son of the Prācetasas in the Cākṣuṣa Manvantara due to the curse of Siva.

## \|\| 11.17.58-59 \|\|

*ityete brahmaputrāṇāṃ dharmādīnāmmahātmanām \|*  
*nātisaṃkṣepato viprā nāti vistarataḥ kramāt \|\| 58 \|\|*

*varṇitā vai mayā vaṃśā divyā devagaṇānvitāḥ \|*  
*kriyāvaṃtaḥ prajāvaṃto mahardhibhiralaṃkṛtāḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

58-59. Thus the divine families, attended upon by the devas, of the noble-souled sons of Brahmā, Dharma and others, have been described by me, O Brahmins. They observed holy rites. They had progenies and were embellished by great prosperity.

## \|\| 11.17.60 \|\|

*prajānāṃ saṃniveśo 'yaṃ prajāpatisamudbhavaḥ \|*  
*na hi śakyaḥ prasaṃkhyātuṃ varṣakoṭiśatairapi \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. This creation born of the Prajāpatis cannot be enumerated even in hundreds of crores of years.

## \|\| 11.17.61 \|\|

*rājñāmapi ca yo vaṃśo dvidhā so 'pi pravartate \|*  
*sūryavaṃśassomavaṃśa iti puṇyatamaḥ kṣitau \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Holy royal families function in two different lines viz. the solar and the lunar.

## \|\| 11.17.62 \|\|

*ikṣvākurambarīṣaśca yayātirnāhuṣādayaḥ \|*  
*puṇyaślokāḥ śrutā ye 'tra te pi tadvaṃśasaṃbhavāḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Ikṣvāku, Ambarīṣa, Yayāti, Nahuṣa and others belong to those families well known and reputed.

## \|\| 11.17.63 \|\|

*anye ca rājaṛṣayo nānāvīryasamanvitā \|*  
*kiṃ taiḥ phalamanutkrāṃtairuktapūrvaiḥ purātanaiḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. There are several other saintly kings of different exploits. Of what avail is their detailed enuneration?

## \|\| 11.17.64 \|\|

*kiṃ ceśvarakathā vṛttā yatra tatrānyakīrtanam \|*  
*na sadbhiḥ saṃmataṃ matvā notsahe bahubhāṣitum \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Moreover, in the context of the story of lord Śiva, the eulogy of royal families is not approved of by good men. Thus I do not attempt to speak much.

## \|\| 11.17.65 \|\|

*prasaṃgādīśvarasyaiva prabhāvadyotanādapi \|*  
*sargādayo 'pi kathitā ityatra tatpravistaraiḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Being relevant so far as it implies the greatness of lord Śiva, I have mentioned creation. Enough of those details too.

## Chapter 18 - The abandonment of the body by Satī

## \|\| 11.18.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*devī dakṣasya tanayā tyaktvā dākṣāyaṇī tanum \|*  
*kathaṃ himavataḥ putrī menāyāmabhavatpurā \|\| 1 \|\|*

The sages said:—

1\. How did the goddess, daughter of Dakṣa become the daughter of Himavat and Menā after abandoning the body born of Dakṣa?

## \|\| 11.18.2 \|\|

*kathaṃ ca nindito rudro dakṣeṇa ca mahātmanā \|*  
*nimittamapi kiṃ tatra yena syānniṃdito bhavaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. How was Rudra censured by Dakṣa the noble soul? What could be the cause whereby Śiva was censured?

## \|\| 11.18.3 \|\|

*utpannaśca kathaṃ dakṣo abhiśāpādbhavasya tu \|*  
*cākṣuṣasyāṃtare pūrvaṃ manoḥ prabrūhi māruta \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O wind-god, formerly in the Cākṣuṣa Manvantara how was Dakṣa born due to the curse of Śiva? Please narrate.

## \|\| 11.18.4 \|\|

*vāyuruvāva \|*  
*śṛṇvaṃtu kathayiṣyāmi dakṣasya laghucetasaḥ \|*  
*vṛttaṃ pāpātpramādācca viśvāmaravidūṣaṇam \|\| 4 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

4\. Please listen. I shall narrate the activity of the mean Dakṣa resulting in his insult to all gods due to his sinful blunder.

## \|\| 11.18.5 \|\|

*purā surāsurāḥ sarve siddhāśca paramarṣayaḥ \|*  
*kadāciddraṣṭumīśānaṃ himavacchikharaṃ yayuḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Once formerly, all the gods, Asuras, Siddhas and the sages went to the summit of Himavat in order to see the lord.

## \|\| 11.18.6 \|\|

*tadā devaśca devī ca divyāsanagatāvubhau \|*  
*darśanaṃ dadatusteṣāṃ devādīnāṃ dvijottamāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O Brahmins, the lord and the goddess were seated on a divine scat as they granted interview to the gods and others.

## \|\| 11.18.7 \|\|

*tadānīmeva dakṣo 'pi gatastatra sahāmaraiḥ \|*  
*jāmātaraṃ haraṃ draṣṭuṃ draṣṭuṃ cātmasutāṃ satīm \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. At the same time Dakṣa too had accompanied the gods in order to see Śiva his son-in-law and the goddess his own daughter.

## \|\| 11.18.8 \|\|

*tadātmagauravāddevo devyā dakṣe samāgate \|*  
*devādibhyo viśeṣeṇa na kadācidabhūtsmṛtiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. In view of their dignity, the lord and the Goddess did not give any special preferential treatment to Dakṣa.

## \|\| 11.18.9 \|\|

*tasya tasyāḥ paraṃ bhāvamajñātuścāpi kevalam \|*  
*putrītyevaṃ vimūḍhasya tasyāṃ vairamajāyata \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. But deluded that he was, Dakṣa did not realise the greatness of the lord and the goddess. Thinking her to be his daughter he began to nurse a grudge and hatred against her.

## \|\| 11.18.10 \|\|

*tatastenaiva vaireṇa vidhinā ca pracoditaḥ \|*  
*nājuvāha bhavaṃ dakṣo dīkṣitastāmapi dviṣan \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Due to this enmity and further incited by Brahmā, Dakṣa after initiation did not invite them in the sacrifice.

## \|\| 11.18.11 \|\|

*anyāñ1 āmātarassarvānāhūya sa yathākramam \|*  
*śataśaḥ puṣkalāmarcāñcakāra ca pṛthakpṛthak \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He invited the other sons-in-law and honoured them severally.

## \|\| 11.18.12 \|\|

*tathā tānsaṃgatāñchrutvā nāradasya mukhāttadā \|*  
*yayau rudrāya rudrāṇī vijñāpya bhavanaṃ pituḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. On hearing from Nārada that they had assembled there, Satī went to her father’s abode after informing Rudra.

## \|\| 11.18.13-19 \|\|

*atha saṃnihitaṃ divyaṃ vimānaṃ viśvatomukham \|*  
*lakṣaṇāḍhyaṃ sukhārohamatimātramanoharam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*taptajāṃbūnadaprakhyaṃ citraratnapariṣkṛtam \|*  
*muktāmayavitānāgnyaṃ sragdāmasamalaṃkṛtam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*taptakaṃcananirvyūhaṃ ratnastaṃbhaśatāvṛtam \|*  
*vajrakalpitasopānaṃ vidrumastaṃbhatoraṇam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*puṣpapaṭṭaparistīrṇaṃ citraratnamahāsanam \|*  
*vajrajālakiracchidramacchidramaṇikuṭṭimam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*maṇidaṃḍamanojñena mahāvṛṣabhalakṣmaṇā \|*  
*alaṃkṛtapurobhāgamabbhraśubbhreṇa ketunā \|\| 17 \|\|*

*ratnakaṃcukaguptāṃgaiścitravetrakapāṇibhiḥ \|*  
*adhiṣṭhitamahādvāramapradhṛṣyairguṇeśvaraiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*mṛdaṃgatālagītādiveṇuvīṇāviśāradaiḥ \|*  
*vidagdhaveṣabhāṣaiśca bahubhiḥ strījanairvṛtam \|\| 19 \|\|*

13-19. She stepped into the aeroplane along with her dear friends. It was a divine plane with doors on all sides; had good conditions; could be easily mounted. It was very charming. It shed golden lustre. It was studded with jewels of various sorts and had a canopy covered with pearls. It was decorated with stringed flower garlands. It had been wrought in molten gold; hundreds of bejewelled pillars supported it all round. The adamantine steps were neatly built. The columns and festoons were decorated with corals. The chief seat therein was studded with gems and covered with a silken cloth with flower-designs. Through every aperture rays of diamonds were diffused; a good gemset platform without dents shone. A flagstaff as pure as cloud decorated its front with the sign of the great Bull. It was studded with jewels. The main door was guarded by invincible Gaṇeśvaras wearing jewel-studded bodices and wielding canes in their hands. Many women, experts in playing on Mṛdaṅgas, flutes, Vīṇās and in music were seated there richly dressed and bedecked in ornaments.

## \|\| 11.18.20-21 \|\|

*āruroha mahādevī saha priyasakhījanaiḥ \|*  
*cāmāravyañjanaṃ tasyā vajradaṃḍamanohare \|\| 20 \|\|*

*gṛhītvā rudrakanye dve vivījaturubhe śubhe \|*  
*tadācāmarayormadhye devyā vadanamābabhau \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. Two Rudra virgins held the auspicious chowries and fans beautiful in their handles set with diamonds, and fanned the goddess. In the middle of the chowries the face of the goddess shone like a lotus in the midst of two fighting swans.

## \|\| 11.18.22-23 \|\|

*anyonyaṃ yudhyatormadhye haṃsayoriva paṃkajam \|*  
*chatraṃ śaśinibhaṃ tasyāścūḍopari sumālinī \|\| 22 \|\|*

*dhṛtamuktāparikṣiptaṃ babhāra premanirbharā \|*  
*tacchatramujjvalaṃ devyā ruruce vadanopari \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. Sumālinī held over her head a pearl-stringed umbrella as white as the moon. The splendid umbrella shone above the face of the goddess as the moon's disc above the vessel of nectar.

## \|\| 11.18.24-25 \|\|

*uparyamṛtabhāṃḍasya maṃḍalaṃ śaśino yathā \|*  
*atha cāgre samāsīnā susmitāsyā śubhāvatī \|\| 24 \|\|*

*akṣadyūtavinodena ramayāmāsa vai satīm \|*  
*suyaśāḥ pāduke devyāśśubhe ratnapariṣkṛte \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. Śubhāvatī of sweet smiling face sat in front of Satī and delighted her by playing at the game of dice. Suyaśas held the auspicious sandals of the goddess, studded with gems, in the middle of her breasts and served the goddess.

## \|\| 11.18.26-27 \|\|

*stanayoraṃtare kṛtvā tadā devīmasevataḥ \|*  
*anyā kāṃcanacārvaṃgī dīptaṃ jagrāha darpaṇam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*aparā tālavṛntaṃ ca parā tāṃbūlapeṭikām \|*  
*kācitkrīḍāśukaṃ cāru kare 'kuruta bhāminī \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. Another lady held the glistening mirror. Another held the fan. Another held the betelbox. Another held the charming parrot.

## \|\| 11.18.28 \|\|

*kācittu sumanojñāni puṣpāṇi surabhīṇi ca \|*  
*kācidābharaṇādhāraṃ babhāra kamalekṣaṇā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. A certain lady held charming fragrant flowers. Another lotus-eyed lady held the repository of ornaments.

## \|\| 11.18.29-30 \|\|

*kācicca punarālepaṃ suprasūtaṃ śubhāṃjanam \|*  
*anyāśca sadṛśāstāstā yathāsvamucitakriyāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*āvṛttyā tāṃ mahādevīmasevaṃta samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*atīva śuśubhe tāsāmaṃtare parameśvarī \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. A certain lady held the unguent, good flowers and the auspicious collyrium. Other ladies did their respective duties. They sat around serving her. In their midst the goddess shone like the moon in the Autumn in the midst of a galaxy of stars.

## \|\| 11.18.31-32 \|\|

*tārāpariṣado madhye caṃdralekheva śāradī \|*  
*tataḥ śaṃkhasamutthasya nādasya samanaṃtaram \|\| 31 \|\|*

*prāsthāniko mahānādaḥ paṭahaḥ samatāḍyata \|*  
*tato madhuravādyāni saha tālodyataissvanaiḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. Then after the blowing of the conch the great wardrum was sounded indicating the time of departure. Then hundreds of bugles and sweet-toned instruments sounded without being beaten (obstructed) along with the sounds of clapping the hands.

## \|\| 11.18.33-34 \|\|

*anāhatāni sanneduḥ kāhalānāṃ śatāni ca \|*  
*sāyudhānāṃ gaṇeśānāṃ maheśasamatejasām \|\| 33 \|\|*

*sahasrāṇi śatānyaṣṭau tadānīṃ purato yayuḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ madhye vṛṣārūḍho gajārūḍho yathā guruḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. Then eight hundred groups of the thousand strong armed Gaṇeśas equal in brilliance to lord Śiva went ahead. In their midst, the glorious chief of Gaṇas, honoured by the moon and Nandīśvara sat on the Bull like Bṛhaspati on an elephant.

## \|\| 11.18.35-37 \|\|

*jagāma gaṇapaḥ śrīmān somanaṃdīśvarārcitaḥ \|*  
*devaduṃdubhayo nedurdivi divyasukhā ghanāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*nanṛturmunayassarve mumuduḥ siddhayoginaḥ \|*  
*sasṛjuḥ puṣpavṛṣṭiṃ ca vitānopari vāridāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*tadā devagaṇaiścānyaiḥ pathi sarvatra saṃgatā \|*  
*kṣaṇādiva piturgehaṃ praviveśa maheśvarī \|\| 37 \|\|*

35-37. The divine drums were sounded in heaven. Clouds were divinely pleasing. The sages danced. Siddhas and Yogins rejoiced. Everywhere on the way the clouds in association with the gods and others made showers of flowers above the canopy. The goddess entered her father’s house as if in a moment.

## \|\| 11.18.38 \|\|

*tāṃ dṛṣṭvā kupito dakṣaścātmanaḥ kṣayakāraṇāt \|*  
*tasyā yavīyasībhyo 'pi cakre pūjāma satkṛtām \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. On seeing her Dakṣa became infuriated which subsequently became the cause of his destruction. He worshipped her younger sisters too in an insulting manner(?)

## \|\| 11.18.39 \|\|

*tadā śaśimukhī devī pitaraṃ sadasi sthitam \|*  
*aṃbikā yuktamavyagramuvācākṛpaṇaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Then the goddess spoke to her father in the midst of the assembly, relevantly unexcitedly and undemeaningly.

## \|\| 11.18.40 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*brahmādayaḥ piśācāṃtā yasyājñāvaśavartinaḥ \|*  
*sa devassāṃprataṃ tāta vidhinā nārcitaḥ kila \|\| 40 \|\|*

The goddess said:—

40\. O father, the lord at whose bidding everyone from Brahmā to the Piśācas becomes subservient has not been duly worshipped.

## \|\| 11.18.41 \|\|

*tadāstāṃ mama jyāyasyāḥ putryāḥ pūjāṃ kimīdṛśīm \|*  
*asatkṛtāmavajñāya kṛtavānasi garhitam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Let that alone. Why did you slight me your eldest daughter in a despicable manner?

## \|\| 11.18.42 \|\|

*evamukto 'bravīdenāṃ dakṣaḥ krodhādamarṣitaḥ \|*  
*tvattaḥ śreṣṭhā viśiṣṭāśca pūjyā bālāḥ sutā mama \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Thus addressed, the infuriated Dakṣa replied angrily “The younger daughters are better than you. They deserve my special reverence.

## \|\| 11.18.43 \|\|

*tāsāṃ tu ye ca bhartāraste me bahumatā mudā \|*  
*gunaiścāpyadhikāssarvairbhartuste tryaṃbakādapi \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Their husbands evoke my respect and joy, for they are superior to your husband lord Śiva.

## \|\| 11.18.44 \|\|

*stabdhātmā tāmasaśśarvastvamimaṃ samupāśritā \|*  
*tena tvāmavamanye 'haṃ pratikūlo hi me bhavaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. He is stiff-souled and you have resorted to him. So I dishonour you. He is antagonistic to me.”

## \|\| 11.18.45 \|\|

*tathoktā pitaraṃ dakṣaṃ kruddhā devī tamabravīt \|*  
*śṛṇvatāmeva sarveṣāṃ ye yajñasadasi sthitāḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Thus insulted the infuriated goddess spoke to her father within the hearing of all present there.

## \|\| 11.18.46 \|\|

*akasmānmama bhartāramajātāśeṣadūṣaṇam \|*  
*vācā dūṣayase dakṣa sākṣāllokamaheśvaram \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. O Dakṣa, you insult my husband the lord of the world, whose insult no one has hitherto made.

## \|\| 11.18.47 \|\|

*vidyācauro gurudrohī vedeśvaravidūṣakaḥ \|*  
*ta ete bahupāpmānassarve daṃḍyā iti śrutiḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. The Śruti says that these are great sinners—viz. a stealer of learning, a traitor to the preceptor and an insulter of the Vedas and of the god. They deserve to be punished.

## \|\| 11.18.48 \|\|

*tasmādatyutkaṭasyāsya pāpasya sadṛśo bhṛśam \|*  
*sahasā dāruṇo daṃḍastava daivādbhaviṣyati \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Therefore a terrible punishment befitting the great sin shall be meted out to you by divine intercession.

## \|\| 11.18.49 \|\|

*tvayā na pūjito yasmāddevadevastriyaṃbakaḥ \|*  
*tasmāttava kulaṃ duṣṭaṃ naṣṭamityavadhāraya \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Since the lord of gods has not been worshipped by you, know that your family is defiled and ruined.

## \|\| 11.18.50 \|\|

*ityuktvā pitaraṃ ruṣṭā satī saṃtyaktasādhvasā \|*  
*tadīyāṃ ca tanuṃ tyaktvā himavaṃtaṃ yayau girim \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. After saying thus to her father Satī abandoned her body and without fear went to mountain Himavat.

## \|\| 11.18.51 \|\|

*sa parvataparaḥ śrīmāṃllabdhapuṇyaphalodayaḥ \|*  
*tadarthameva kṛtavān suciraṃ duścaraṃ tapaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The glorious leader of mountains attained the fruit of his merits. It was for her that he had performed penance for a long time.

## \|\| 11.18.52 \|\|

*tasmāttamanugṛhṇāti bhūdhareśvaramīśvarī \|*  
*svecchayā pitaraṃ cakre svātmano yogamāyayā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. The goddess blessed the lord of mountains. Through her Yogic Māyā and at her own will, she made him her father.

## \|\| 11.18.53 \|\|

*yadā gatā satī dakṣaṃ viniṃdya bhayavihvalā \|*  
*tadā tirohitā maṃtrā vihataśca tato 'dhvaraḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. When Satī rebuked Dakṣa and went away, the frightened and agitated Mantras too vanished. The sacrifice became hindered.

## \|\| 11.18.54 \|\|

*tadupaśrutya gamanaṃ devyāstripurumardanaḥ \|*  
*dakṣāya ca ṛṣibhyaśca cukopa ca śaśāpa tān \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. On hearing about the departure of the goddess, Śiva was angry with Dakṣa and the sages and cursed them.

## \|\| 11.18.55-57 \|\|

*yasmādavamatā dakṣamatkṛte 'nāgasā satī \|*  
*pūjitāścetarāḥ sarvāḥ svasutā bhartṛbhiḥ saha \|\| 55 \|\|*

*vaivasvate 'ṃtare tasmāttava jāmātarastvamī \|*  
*utpatsyaṃte samaṃ sarve brahmayajñeṣvayonijāḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*bhavitā mānuṣo rājā cākṣuṣasya tvamanvaye \|*  
*prācīnabarhiṣaḥ pautraḥ putraścāpi pracetasaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

55-57. O Dakṣa, since for my sake the sinless Satī had been dishonoured and the other daughters worshipped along with their husbands, these sons-in-law of yours will be born but not of a womb in the sacrifices of Brahmā in the Vaivasvata Manvantara. In the Cākṣuṣa Manvantara you will become a king as the grandson of Prācinabarhiṣ and the son of Pracetas.

## \|\| 11.18.58 \|\|

*ahaṃ tatrāpi te vighnamācariṣyāmi durmate \|*  
*dharmārthakāmayukteṣu karmasvapi punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. O wicked one, there also I shall put up obstacles before you in all activities regarding virtue, wealth and love.

## \|\| 11.18.59 \|\|

*tenaivaṃ vyāhṛto dakṣo rudreṇāmitatejasā \|*  
*svāyaṃbhuvīṃ tanuṃ tyaktvā papāta bhuvi duḥkhitaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Thus addressed by Rudra of unmeasured splendour, Dakṣa abandoned the body and fell on the ground.

## \|\| 11.18.60 \|\|

*tataḥ prācetaso dakṣo jajñe vai cākṣuṣe 'ntare \|*  
*prācīnabarhiṣaḥ pautraḥ putraścaiva pracetasām \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Then in the Cākṣusa Manvantara Dakṣa was born as the grandson of Prācinabarhiṣ and the son of Pracetas.

## \|\| 11.18.61 \|\|

*bhṛgvādayo 'pi jātā vai manorvaivasvatasya tu \|*  
*aṃtare brahmaṇo yajñe vāruṇīṃ bibhratastanum \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Bhṛgu and others were born in the Vaivasvata Manvantara in the sacrifice of Brahmā bearing the bodies of Varuṇa.

## \|\| 11.18.62 \|\|

*tadā dakṣasya dharmārthaṃ yajñe tasya durātmanaḥ \|*  
*maheśaḥ kṛtavānvighnaṃ manā vavasvate sati \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Then in the Vaivasvata Manvantara in the virtuous sacrifice of the wicked Dakṣa the lord created obstacles.

## Chapter 19 - The origin of Vīrabhadra

## \|\| 11.19.2-4 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*viśvasya jagato māturapi devyāstapobalāt \|*  
*pitṛbhāvamupāgamya mudite himavadgirau \|\| 2 \|\|*

*deve 'pi tatkṛtodvāhe himavacchikharālaye \|*  
*saṃkīḍati tayā sārdhaṃ kāle bahutare gate \|\| 3 \|\|*

*vaivasvate 'ṃtare prāpte dakṣaḥ prācetasaḥ svayam \|*  
*aśvamedhena yajñena yakṣyamāṇo 'nvapadyata \|\| 4 \|\|*

The sages said:—

I. How did the lord create obstacles before the wicked Dakṣa who performed a sacrifice for virtue’s sake? We wish to know this.

Vāyu said:—

2-4. When Himavat was delighted by becoming the father of the mother of the universe by the strength of his penance, when Śiva married her and sported with her in his abode on the peak of Himavat when a long time elapsed, in the Vaivasvata Manvantara Dakṣa as the son of Pracetas wanted to perform a horse-sacrifice.

## \|\| 11.19.5 \|\|

*tato himavataḥ pṛṣṭhe dakṣo vai yajñamāharat \|*  
*gaṃgādvāre śubhe deśe ṛṣisiddhaniṣevite \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. On the top of Himavat in an auspicious spot at the source of Gaṅgā, frequented by the sages and the Siddhas Dakṣa began his sacrifice.

## \|\| 11.19.6 \|\|

*tasya tasminmakhedevāḥ sarve śakra purogamāḥ \|*  
*gamanāya samāgamya buddhimāpedire tadā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. All the gods Indra and others gathered there and thought of going to attend the sacrifice.

## \|\| 11.19.7-8 \|\|

*ādityā vasavo rudrāssādhyāssaha marudgaṇaiḥ \|*  
*ūṣmapāḥ somapāścaiva ājyapā dhūmapāstathā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*aśvinau pitaraścaiva tathā cānye maharṣayaḥ \|*  
*viṣṇunā sahitāḥ sarve svāgatā yajñabhāginaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. The Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras, Sādhyas, Maruts, Ūṣmapās, Somapās, Ājyapās, Dhūmapās, Aśvins, Pitṛs, and the other sages came there along with Viṣṇu to take part in the sacrifice.

## \|\| 11.19.9 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā devakulaṃ sarvamīśvareṇa vināgatam \|*  
*dadhīco manyunāviṣṭo dakṣamevamabhāṣata \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. On seeing all the gods assembled there without Śiva, Dadhīca became angry. He spoke to Dakṣa thus.

## \|\| 11.19.10 \|\|

*dadhīca uvāca \|*  
*aprapūjye caiva pūjā pūjyānāṃ cāpya pūjane \|*  
*naraḥ pāpamavāpnoti mahadvai nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

Dadhīca said:—

10\. Indeed that man incurs great sin who does not worship those who deserve worship and worships those who do not befit it.

## \|\| 11.19.11 \|\|

*asatāṃ saṃmatiryatra satāmavamatistathā \|*  
*daṃḍo devakṛtastatra sadyaḥ patati dāruṇaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Lord’s terrible punishment falls where the wicked are honoured and the good are dishonoured.

## \|\| 11.19.12 \|\|

*evamuktvā tu viprarṣiḥ punardakṣamabhāṣata \|*  
*pūjyaṃ tu paśubhartāraṃ kasmānnārcayase prabhum \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. After saying this the sage spoke again to Dakṣa, “Why don’t you worship the lord deserving worship, the lord of souls?”

## \|\| 11.19.13 \|\|

*dakṣa uvāca \|*  
*saṃti me bahavo rudrāḥ śūlahastāḥ kapardinaḥ \|*  
*ekādaśāvasthitā ye nānyaṃ vedmi maheśvaram \|\| 13 \|\|*

Dakṣa said:—

13\. I see eleven Rudras armed with tridents and having matted hair. I do not know anyone else as the lord.

## \|\| 11.19.14 \|\|

*dadhīca uvāca \|*  
*kimebhiramarairanyaiḥ pūjitairadhvare phalam \|*  
*rājā cedadhvarasyāsya na rudraḥ pūjyate tvayā \|\| 14 \|\|*

Dadhīca said:—

14\. What avails worshipping the gods in the sacrifice if the king of sacrifice, Rudra, is not worshipped by you?

## \|\| 11.19.15 \|\|

*brahmaviṣṇumaheśānāṃ sraṣṭā yaḥ prabhuravyayaḥ \|*  
*brahmādayaḥ piśācāṃtā yasya kaiṃkaryavādinaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. He is unchanging, the creator of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Rudra, to whom all from Brahmā to Piśācas, say “What shall we do?”

## \|\| 11.19.16 \|\|

*prakṛtīnāṃ paraścaiva puruṣasya ca yaḥ paraḥ \|*  
*ciṃtyate yogavidvadbhi ṛṣibhistattvadarśibhiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. He is beyond all Prakṛtis and Puruṣa. He is meditated upon by Yogic scholars, sages and the seers of truthful principles.

## \|\| 11.19.17 \|\|

*akṣaraṃ paramaṃ brahma hyasacca sadasacca yat \|*  
*anādimadhyanidhanamapratarkyaṃ sanātanam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. He is the imperishable great Brahman, the Sat-Asat and Asat; devoid of beginning, middle and end, incomprehensible and eternal.

## \|\| 11.19.18 \|\|

*yaḥ sraṣṭā caiva saṃhartā bhartā caiva maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*tasmādanyaṃ na paśyāmi śaṃkarātmānamadhvare \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He is the creator, sustainer, and annihilator. I do not see any one else in the form of Śiva in the sacrifice.

## \|\| 11.19.19 \|\|

*dakṣa uvāca \|*  
*etanmakheśasya suvarṇapātre haviḥ samastaṃ vidhimaṃtrapūtam \|*  
*viṣṇornayāmyapratimasya bhāgaṃ prabhorvibhajyāvahanīyamadya \|\| 19 \|\|*

Dakṣa said:—

19\. I offer this Caru in the golden vessel, sanctified by mantras, after assigning the share to Viṣṇu the lord of sacrifice.

## \|\| 11.19.20 \|\|

*dadhīca uvāca \|*  
*yasmānnārādhito rudrassarvadeveśvareśvaraḥ \|*  
*tasmāddakṣa tavāśeṣo yajño 'yaṃ na bhaviṣyati \|\| 20 \|\|*

Dadhīca said:—

20\. “O Dakṣa, since Rudra the lord of the chief of the gods is not propitiated your sacrifice will not be efficacious.”

## \|\| 11.19.21 \|\|

*ityuktvā vacanaṃ kruddho dadhīco munisattamaḥ \|*  
*nirgamya ca tato deśājjagāma svakamāśramam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. After saying this, the infuriated sage Dadhīca left for his hermitage.

## \|\| 11.19.22 \|\|

*nirgate 'pi munau tasmindevā dakṣaṃ na tatyajuḥ \|*  
*avaśyamanubhāvitvādanarthasya tu bhāvinaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Even when the sage walked out, the gods did not leave Dakṣa in view of the inevitability of the disaster that was to take place.

## \|\| 11.19.23 \|\|

*etasminneva kāle tu jñātvaitatsarvamīśvarāt \|*  
*dagdhuṃ dakṣādhvaraṃ viprā devī devamacodayat \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O brahmins, in the meantime knowing about all this from Śiva the goddess urged the lord to destroy the sacrifice of Dakṣa.

## \|\| 11.19.24 \|\|

*devyā saṃcodito devo dakṣādhvarajighāṃsayā \|*  
*sasarja sahasā vīraṃ vīrabhadraṃ gaṇeśvaram \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Urged by the goddess the lord created the heroic Vīrabhadra the chief of Ganas, intending to destroy the sacrifice.

## \|\| 11.19.25-33 \|\|

*sahasravadanaṃ devaṃ sahasrakamalekṣaṇam \|*  
*sahasramudgaradharaṃ sahasraśarapāṇikam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*śūlaṭaṃkagadāhastaṃ dīptakārmukadhāriṇam \|*  
*cakravajradharaṃ ghoraṃ caṃdrārdhakṛtaśekharam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*kuliśodyotitakaraṃ taḍijjvalitamūrdhajam \|*  
*daṃṣṭrākarālaṃ bibhrāṇaṃ mahāvaktraṃ mahodaram \|\| 27 \|\|*

*vidyujjihvaṃ pralaṃboṣṭhaṃ meghasāgaraniḥsvanam \|*  
*vasānaṃ carma vaiyāghraṃ mahadrudhiranisravam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*gaṇḍadvitayasaṃsṛṣṭamaṇḍalīkṛtakuṇḍalam \|*  
*varāmaraśiromālāvalīkalitaśekharam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*raṇannūpurakeyūramahākanakabhūṣitam \|*  
*ratnasaṃcayasaṃdīptaṃ tārahārāvṛtorasam \|\| 30 \|\|*

*mahāśarabhaśārdūlasiṃhaiḥ sadṛśavikramam \|*  
*praśastamattamātaṃgasamānagamanālasam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*śaṃkhacāmarakuṃdendumṛṇālasadṛśaprabham \|*  
*satuṣāramivādrīndraṃ sākṣājjaṃgamatāṃ gatam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*jvālāmālāparikṣiptaṃ dīptamauktikabhūṣaṇam \|*  
*tejasā caiva dīvyaṃtaṃ yugāṃta iva pāvakam \|\| 33 \|\|*

25-33. He had a thousand faces, a thousand lotus-like eyes. He was holding a thousand iron clubs, thousands of arrows, spear, axe, mace, bow, discus and the thunderbolt. He looked fierce and terrible. The crescent moon adorned his crest; the thunderbolt illuminated his hands. His hair shone like lightning. He had a huge mouth terrible with the curved fangs and a huge belly. His tongue was like lightnings His lips hung down. His voice sounded like the cloud and the ocean. He wore the tiger’s hide dripping with blood. He ear-rings formed circles close to his cheeks. He had adorned his crest with the garlands from the heads of leading gods. He was bedecked in golden shoulderlets and jingling anklets. He was shining with heaps of gems. His chest was covered by necklaces. He was equal in exploit to the great fabulous animal Śarabha, tigers and lions. His gait was gentle and majestic as that of a stately elephant in rut. His lustre was white like conch, chowrie, Kunda flower, moon and the lotus-stalk. He was like the snow-capped lord of mountains who had become mobile. Flames surrounded him. Wearing pearl ornaments he shone brilliantly as the fire at the dissolution of the world.

## \|\| 11.19.34 \|\|

*sa jānubhyāṃ mahīṃ gatvā praṇataḥ prāṃjalistataḥ \|*  
*pārśvato devadevasya paryatiṣṭhadgaṇeśvaraḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. That chief of Gaṇas knelt and bowed. With palms joined in reverence he stood beside the lord of gods.

## \|\| 11.19.35 \|\|

*manyunā cāsṛjadbhadrāṃ bhadrakālīṃ maheśvarīm \|*  
*ātmanaḥ karmasākṣitve tena gaṃtuṃ sahaiva tu \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. With his anger he created Bhadrā the goddess Kālī as a witness of his activities and his companion.

## \|\| 11.19.36 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvāvasthitaṃ vīrabhadraṃ kālāgnisannibham \|*  
*bhadrayā sahitaṃ prāha bhadramastviti śaṃkaraḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. On seeing Vīrabhadra standing like deadly fire in the company of Bhadrā, Śiva said “Welfare be to you.”

## \|\| 11.19.37 \|\|

*sa ca vijñāpayāmāsa saha devyā maheśvaram \|*  
*ājñāpaya mahādeva kiṃ kāryaṃ karavāṇyaham \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. He submitted to the lord in the company of the goddess. “Please command what task shall I carry out?”

## \|\| 11.19.38 \|\|

*tatastripurahā prāha haimavatyāḥ priyecchayā \|*  
*vīrabhadraṃ mahābāhuṃ vācā vipulanādayā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Then with a desire to please Pārvatī, Śiva spoke to the huge-armcd Vīrabhadra in raised sound.

## \|\| 11.19.39 \|\|

*devadeva uvāca \|*  
*prācetasasya dakṣasya yajñaṃ sadyo vināśaya \|*  
*bhadrakālyā sahāsi tvametatkṛtyaṃ gaṇeśvara \|\| 39 \|\|*

The lord of gods said:—

39\. O chief of Gaṇas, accompanied by Bhadrakālī, destroy the sacrifice of Dakṣa the son of Pracetas.

## \|\| 11.19.40 \|\|

*ahamapyanayā sārdhaṃ raibhyāśramasapīpataḥ \|*  
*sthitvā vīkṣe gaṇeśāna vikramaṃ tava duḥsaham \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. O chief of Gaṇas, I shall witness your exploit staying near Raibhya’s hermitage along with the goddess.

## \|\| 11.19.41-42 \|\|

*vṛkṣā kanakhale ye tu gaṃgādvārasamīpagāḥ \|*  
*suvarṇaśṛṃgasya girermerumaṃdarasaṃnibhāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*tasminpradeśe dakṣasya yujñaḥ saṃprati vartate \|*  
*sahasā tasya yajñasya vighātaṃ kuru mā ciram \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. In the place Kanakhala\[3\] there are huge trees near Gaṅgādvāra\[4\] resembling the mountain with the golden peaks like Meru\[5\] and Mandara. Dakṣa is holding sacrifice there. Immediately create obstacles in that sacrifice too. Do not delay.

## \|\| 11.19.43-44 \|\|

*ityukte sati devena devī himagirīndrajā \|*  
*bhadraṃ bhadraṃ ca saṃprekṣya vatsaṃ dhenurivaurasam \|\| 43 \|\|*

*āliṃgya ca samāghrāya mūrdhni ṣaḍvadanaṃ yathā \|*  
*sasmitā vacanaṃ prāha madhuraṃ madhuraṃ svayam \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. When this was mentioned by the lord, the goddess, daughter of Hímavat looked at Vīrabhadra and Bhadrakālī as docs a cow at her calf. Embracing him and sniffing at his head as at the head of Subrahmaṇya she smiled and spoke in sweet voice.

## \|\| 11.19.45 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*vatsa bhadra mahābhāga mahābalaparākrama \|*  
*matpriyārthaṃ tvamutpanno mama manyuṃ pramārjaka \|\| 45 \|\|*

The goddess said:—

45\. O dear Bhadra, O blessed one, of great strength and exploit, you are born to carry out the task that pleases me. Wipe off my anger and sorrow.

## \|\| 11.19.46 \|\|

*yajñeśvaramanāhūya yajñakarmarato 'bhavat \|*  
*dakṣaṃ vaireṇa taṃ tasmādbhiṃdhi yajñaṃ gaṇeśvara \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. In view of his enmity Dakṣa is performing sacrifice without inviting the lord of sacrifice. O chief of Gaṇas, split that sacrifice.

## \|\| 11.19.47 \|\|

*yajñalakṣmīmalakṣmīṃ tvaṃ bhadra kṛtvā mamājñayā \|*  
*yajamānaṃ ca taṃ hatvā vatsa hiṃsaya bhadrayā \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. At my bidding O dear, inflict violence in the company of Bhadrā. Kill the sacrificer. Let the holy sacrifice be turned into non-sacrifice.

## \|\| 11.19.48 \|\|

*aśeṣāmiva tāmājñāṃ śivayościtrakṛtyayoḥ \|*  
*mūrdhni kṛtvā namaskṛtya bhadro gaṃtuṃ pracakrame \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. At the behest of Śiva and Śivā of wonderful activities, with bent head, as if it was their blessing, Bhadra bowed to them and left.

## \|\| 11.19.49-50 \|\|

*athaiṣa bhagavānkruddhaḥ pretāvāsakṛtālayaḥ \|*  
*vīrabhadro mahādevo devyā manyupramārjakaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*sasarja romakūpebhyo romajākhyāngaṇeśvarān \|*  
*dakṣiṇādbhujadeśāttu śatakoṭigaviśvarān \|\| 50 \|\|*

49-50. The infuriated lord Vīrabhadra, fond of cremation ground, created from his skin-pores chiefs of Gaṇas, and from his right hand hundred crores others.

## \|\| 11.19.51 \|\|

*pādāttathorudeśācca pṛṣṭhātpārśvānmukhādgalāt \|*  
*guhyādgulphācchiromadhyātkaṃṭhādāsyāttathodarāt \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. He also created these from his feet, thighs, back, sides, mouth, throat, privities, heels, middle of the head, neck, face and belly.

## \|\| 11.19.52 \|\|

*tadā gaṇeśvarairbhadrairbhadratulyaparākramaiḥ \|*  
*saṃchāditamabhūtsarvaṃ sākāśavivaraṃ jagat \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Then the universe with all its open spaces and crevices was covered with the chiefs of gaṇas equal in exploit to Bhadra.

## \|\| 11.19.53 \|\|

*sarve sahasrahastāste sahasrāyudhapāṇayaḥ \|*  
*rudrasyānucarāssarve sarve rudrasamaprabhāḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. These had thousand hands holding thousands of weapons and had the lustre of Rudra.

## \|\| 11.19.54 \|\|

*śūlaśaktigadāhastāṣṭaṃkopalaśilādharāḥ \|*  
*kālāgnirudrasadṛśāstrinetrāśca jaṭādharāḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. They had spears, tridents and maces, axes, stones and rocks. They resembled deadly fire and Rudra. They had three eyes and matted hair.

## \|\| 11.19.55 \|\|

*nipeturbhṛśamākāśe śataśassiṃhavāhanāḥ \|*  
*vineduśca mahānādāñjaladā iva bhadrajāḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. They flew in hundreds and seated on lions roared loudly like clouds.

## \|\| 11.19.56 \|\|

*tairbhadrairbhagavānmadrastathā parivṛto babhau \|*  
*kālānalaśatairyukto yathāṃte kālabhairavaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Lord Bhadra surrounded by the Bhadras shone like Kālabhairava surrounded by hundreds of deadly fires at the time of dissolution.

## \|\| 11.19.57 \|\|

*teṣāṃ madhye samāruhya vṛṣeṃdraṃ vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|*  
*jagāma bhagavānbhadraśśubhamabhraṃ yathā bhavaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. In their midst, mounted on a lordly bull and with a bull-emblem, lord Bhadra went ahead like Śiva seated on Nandin.

## \|\| 11.19.58 \|\|

*tasminvṛṣabhamārūḍhe bhadre tu bhasitaprabhaḥ \|*  
*babhāra mauktikaṃ chatraṃ gṛhītasitacāmaraḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. When Bhadra was seated on the bull, Bhasitaprabha held the pearl umbrella and the white chowries.

## \|\| 11.19.59 \|\|

*sa tadā śuśubhe pārśve bhadrasya bhasitaprabhaḥ \|*  
*bhagavāniva śailendraḥ pārśve viśvajagadguroḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Bhasita shone by the side of Bhadra like the lord of mountains by the side of Śiva.

## \|\| 11.19.60 \|\|

*so 'pi tena babhau bhadraḥ śvetacāmarapāṇinā \|*  
*bālasomena saumyena yathā śūlavarāyudhaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Bhadra too shone in his company as he held the white chowries like the lord with the trident weapon and the crescent moon.

## \|\| 11.19.61 \|\|

*dadhmau śaṃkhaṃ sitaṃ bhadraṃ bhadrasya purataḥ śubham \|*  
*bhānukaṃpo mahātejā hemaratnairalaṃkṛtaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Bhānukampa of great splendour bedecked in gold and jewels blew on the auspicious white conch Bhadra in front of Bhadra.

## \|\| 11.19.62 \|\|

*devaduṃdubhayo nedurdivyasaṃkulaniḥsvanāḥ \|*  
*vavṛṣuśśataśo mūrdhni puṣpavarṣaṃ balāhakāḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. The divine drums were sounded with divine tumultuous tone. The clouds in hundreds made showers of flowers on his head.

## \|\| 11.19.63 \|\|

*phullānāṃ madhugarbhāṇāṃ puṣpāṇāṃ gaṃdhabaṃdhavaḥ \|*  
*mārgānukūlasaṃvāhā vabuśca pathi mārutāḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Winds taking up the fragrance of full blown flowers pregnant with honey blew favourbly on their way.

## \|\| 11.19.64 \|\|

*tato gaṇeśvarāḥ sarve mattā yuddhabaloddhatāḥ \|*  
*nanṛturmumudur1 edurjahasurjagadurjaguḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Then the elated chiefs proud of their strength danced, rejoiced, cried, laughed, spoke and sang.

## \|\| 11.19.65 \|\|

*tadā bhadragaṇāṃtaḥstho babhau bhadraḥ sa bhadrayā \|*  
*yathā rudragaṇāṃtaḥ sthastryambakoṃbikayā saha \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Then Bhadra stationed in the midst of the Bhadragaṇas in the company of Bhadrā shone like Śiva in the midst of Rudragaṇas in the company of Pārvatī.

## \|\| 11.19.66 \|\|

*tatkṣaṇādeva dakṣasya yajñavāṭaṃ raṇmayam \|*  
*praviveśa mahābāhurvīrabhadro mahānugaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. In a moment the strong Vīrabhadra with his followers entered the golden gate of the sacrificial altar.

## \|\| 11.19.67 \|\|

*tatastu dakṣapratipāditasya kratupradhānasya gaṇapradhānaḥ \|*  
*prayogabhūmiṃ praviveśa bhadro rudro yathāṃte bhuvanaṃ didhakṣuḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Then the chief of Gaṇas Bhadra entered like Rudra desirous of burning the worlds at the time of dissolution.

## Chapter 20 - The destruction of Dakṣa’s sacrifice (1)

## \|\| 11.20.1 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*tato viṣṇupradhānānāṃ surāṇāmamitaujasām \|*  
*dadarśa ca mahatsatraṃ citradhvajaparicchadam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

1\. Then he saw the great Satra of the gods of great splendour the chief of whom was Viṣṇu. The satra had all the paraphernalia—the flags of various colours etc.

## \|\| 11.20.2 \|\|

*sudarbhaṛtusaṃstīrṇaṃ susamiddhahutāśanam \|*  
*kāṃcanairyajñabhāṃḍaiśca bhrājiṣṇubhiralaṃkṛtam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Good grass was scattered in straight lines. The sacrificial fire was well-kindled. It was embellished with glittering sacrificial vessels of gold.

## \|\| 11.20.3 \|\|

*ṛṣibhiryajñapaṭubhiryathāvatkarmakartṛbhiḥ \|*  
*vidhinā vedadṛṣṭena svanuṣṭhitabahukramam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The rites were performed neatly in accordance with the rules found in the Vedas by the sages who were experts in sacrifices and who performed the rites properly.

## \|\| 11.20.4 \|\|

*devāṃganāsahasrāḍhyamapsarogaṇasevitam \|*  
*veṇuvīṇāravairjuṣṭaṃ vedaghoṣaiśca bṛṃhitam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Thousands of celestial damsels were there. The Satra was attended by the Apsaras. The sweet sound of flutes and lutes spread and was enhanced by the sound of Vedic hymns.

## \|\| 11.20.5 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā dakṣādhvare vīro vīrabhadraḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*siṃhanādaṃ tadā cakre gaṃbhīro jalado yathā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. On seeing all this, the heroic Vīrabhadra of great exploits roared like a lion or a majestic rumbling cloud.

## \|\| 11.20.6 \|\|

*tataḥ kilakilāśabda ākāśaṃ pūrayanniva \|*  
*gaṇeśvaraiḥ kṛto jajñe mahānnyakkṛtasāgaraḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Then a hurrah of joy, filling the sky and superseding the sound of the ocean was produced by the lords of gaṇas.

## \|\| 11.20.7 \|\|

*tena śabdena mahatāḥ grastā sarvedivaukasaḥ \|*  
*dudruvuḥ parito bhītāḥ srastavastravibhūṣaṇāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Overwhelmed by the great sound the frightened heaven-dwellers ran helter-skelter dropping their garments and ornaments.

## \|\| 11.20.8 \|\|

*kiṃsvidbhagno mahāmeruḥ kiṃsvitsaṃdīryate mahī \|*  
*kimidaṃ kimidaṃ veti jajalpustridaśā bhṛśam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. “Has the great Meru been burst? Is the earth pierced through? What is this?” the gods, began to scream and shout.

## \|\| 11.20.9 \|\|

*mṛgendrāṇāṃ yathā nādaṃ gajeṃdrā gahane vane \|*  
*śrutvā tathāvidhaṃ kecittatyajurjīvitaṃ bhayāt \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Some abandoned their lives due to fear like lordly elephants in a thick forest on hearing the roar of the lion.

## \|\| 11.20.10 \|\|

*parvatāśca vyaśīryaṃta cakampe ca vasuṃdharā \|*  
*marutaśca vyaghūrṇaṃta cukṣubhe makarālayaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Mountains crumbled. The earth quaked. Winds rolled and reeled. The ocean was agitated.

## \|\| 11.20.11 \|\|

*agnayo naiva dīpyaṃte na ca dīpyati bhāskaraḥ \|*  
*grahāśca na prakāśaṃte nakṣatrāṇi ca tārakāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Fires did not blaze. The sun did not shine. Neither the planets nor the stars nor the other luminary bodies shone.

## \|\| 11.20.12 \|\|

*etasminneva kāle tu yajñavāṭaṃ tadujjvalam \|*  
*saṃprāpa bhagavānbhadro bhadraiśca saha bhadrayā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. In the meantime lord Bhadra in the company of Bhadras and the goddess Bhadrā reached the brilliant sacrificial altar.

## \|\| 11.20.13 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā bhītabhīto 'pi dakṣo dṛḍha iva sthitaḥ \|*  
*kruddhavadvacanaṃ prāha ko bhavān kimihecchasi \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. On seeing him, Dakṣa stood steady and firm though he was frightened. He spoke angrily “Who are you? What do you wish?”

## \|\| 11.20.14-15 \|\|

*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā dakṣasya ca durātmanaḥ \|*  
*vīrabhadro mahātejā meghasaṃbhīranissvanaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*smayanniva tamālokya dakṣaṃ devāśca ṛtvijaḥ \|*  
*arthagarbhamasaṃbhrāntamavocaducitaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. On hearing the words of the wicked Dakṣa, Vīrabhadra of great splendour and of majestically rumbling sound like the cloud smilingly looked at Dakṣa, the gods and the Ṛtviks. He spoke the relevent words full of meaning without the least excitement.

## \|\| 11.20.16 \|\|

*vīrabhadra uvāca \|*  
*vayaṃ hyanucarāḥ sarve śarvasyāmitatejasaḥ \|*  
*bhāgābhilipsayā prāptā bhāgo nassaṃpradīyatām \|\| 16 \|\|*

Vīrabhadra said:—

16\. We are the followers of lord Śiva of great splendour. We have come for our share. May that be given to us.

## \|\| 11.20.17 \|\|

*atha cedadhvare 'smākaṃ na bhāgaḥ parikalpitaḥ \|*  
*kathyatāṃ kāraṇaṃ tatra yudhyatāṃ vā mayāmaraiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. If the share has not been allotted to us in the sacrifice let the reason be mentioned or let the gods fight with me.

## \|\| 11.20.18 \|\|

*ityuktāste gaṇeṃdreṇa devā dakṣapurogamāḥ \|*  
*ūcurmantrāḥ pramāṇaṃ no na vayaṃ prabhavastviti \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. When they were told thus by the chief of Gaṇas the gods headed by Dakṣa said—“The mantras are our authorities. We are not the lords.”

## \|\| 11.20.19 \|\|

*mantrā ūcussurā yūyaṃ mohopahatacetasaḥ \|*  
*yena prathamabhāgārhaṃ na yajadhvaṃ maheśvaram \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The Mantras said—“O gods, your minds are oppressed by Tamas. Hence you do not deserve the first share. Worship lord Śiva.”

## \|\| 11.20.20 \|\|

*maṃtroktā api te devāḥ sarve saṃmūḍhacetasaḥ \|*  
*bhadrāya na dadurbhāgaṃ tatprahāṇamabhīpsavaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Though advised by the Mantras the gods with deluded minds did not offer the share to Bhadra. They desired to drop him out.

## \|\| 11.20.21 \|\|

*yadā tathyaṃ ca pathyaṃ ca svavākyaṃ tadvṛthā 'bhavat \|*  
*tadā tato yayurmaṃdā brahmalokaṃ sanātanam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. When their truthful and wholesome words went in vain the Mantras turned away from that place and went to the eternal Brahmaloka.

## \|\| 11.20.22-23 \|\|

*athovāca gaṇādhyakṣo devānviṣṇupurogamān \|*  
*mantrāḥ pramāṇaṃ na kṛtā yuṣmābhirbalagarvitaiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*yasmādasminmakhe devairitthaṃ vayamasatkṛtāḥ \|*  
*tasmādvo jīvitaissārdhamapaneṣyāmi garvitam \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. Then the chief of Gaṇas spoke to the gods headed by Viṣṇu, “You have not accepted the mantras being proud of your strength. Since we have been dishonoured by the gods thus in this sacrifice, I will drive out your arrogance along with your lives.”

## \|\| 11.20.24 \|\|

*ityuktvā bhagavān kruddho vyadahannetravahninā \|*  
*yakṣavāṭaṃ mahākūṭaṃ yathātisraḥ puro haraḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. After saying thus the infuriated lord burnt the sacrificial altar with the fire of his eyes as Śiva had burnt the three Puras.

## \|\| 11.20.25-26 \|\|

*tato gaṇeśvarāssarve parvatodagravigrahāḥ \|*  
*yūpānutpāṭya hotḥṇāṃ kaṃṭheṣvābadhya rajjubhiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*yajñapātrāṇi citrāṇi bhittvā saṃcūrṇya vāriṇi \|*  
*gṛhītvā caiva yajñāṃgaṃ gaṃgāsrotasi cikṣipuḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. Then the lords of gaṇas of mountain-like huge bodies uprooted the sacrificial posts and tied them to the necks of the Hotṛ priests by means of ropes. They broke and powdered the sacrificial vessels of various shapes and sizes dissolved them in water anḍ hurled all the appendages of the sacrifice in the currents of the Gaṅgā river.

## \|\| 11.20.27-28 \|\|

*tatra divyānnapānānāṃ rāśayaḥ parvatopamāḥ \|*  
*kṣīranadyo 'mṛtasrāvāḥ susnigdhadadhikardamāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*uccāvacāni māṃsāni bhakṣyāṇi surabhīṇi ca \|*  
*rasavanti ca pānāni lehyacoṣyāṇi tāni vai \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. There were heaps of foodstuffs and beverages; milk flowed like rivers exuding nectar; curds formed smooth slimy slush. Sweet smelling meat and foodstuffs lay in heaps high and low. There were juicy beverages, and foodstuffs to be lapped up. The heroes ate, chewed and scattered them.

## \|\| 11.20.29-30 \|\|

*vīrāstadbhujate vaktrairviluṃpaṃti kṣipaṃti ca \|*  
*vajraiścakrairmahāśūlaiśśaktibhiḥ pāśapaṭṭiśaiḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*musalairasibhiṣṭaṃkairbhidhipālaiḥ paraśvadhaiḥ \|*  
*uddhatāṃstridaśānsarvāṃllokapālapurassarān \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. The heroic Bhadras born of Vīrabhadra’s body hit and split the haughty gods including the guardians oi the quarters by means of discus, thunderbolts, spears, Śaktis, nooses, iron clubs, iron rods, swords, axes, Bhindipalas and huge battle-axes

## \|\| 11.20.31-32 \|\|

*bibhidurbalino vīrā vīrabhadrāṃgasaṃbhavāḥ \|*
