*chiṃdhi bhiṃdhi kṣipa kṣipraṃ māryatāṃ dāryatāmiti \|\| 31 \|\|*

*harasva praharasveti pāṭayotpāṭayeti ca \|*  
*saṃraṃbhaprabhavāḥ krūrāśśabdāḥ śravaṇaśaṃkavaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. “Chop off and split” “Hurl quickly” “Let him be killed” “Take away and strike” “Peel and tear off” such ruthless words full of excitement, usual in wars and jarring to the ears arose from the lords of Gaṇas.

## \|\| 11.20.33-36 \|\|

*yatratatra gaṇeśānāṃ jajñire samarocitāḥ \|*  
*vivṛttanayanāḥ keciddaṣṭadaṃṣṭroṣṭhatālavaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*āśramasthānsamākṛṣya mārayanti tapodhanāt \|*  
*sruvānapaharantaśca kṣipantogniṃ jaleṣu ca \|\| 34 \|\|*

*kalaśānapi bhindaṃtaśchiṃdaṃto maṇivedikāḥ \|*  
*gāyaṃtaśca nadantaśca hasantaśca muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*raktāsavaṃ pibantaśca nanṛturgaṇapuṃgavāḥ \|*  
*nirmathya seṃdrānamarān gaṇendrānvṛṣendranāgendramṛgendrasārāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

33-36. Some rolled their eyes, gnashed their fanglike teeth and bit their lips and palates. They pulled out the sages in the hermitages and killed them. They took away sacrificial ladles and spoons and hurled them into fire and water. They broke domes, gemset platforms. They sang, shouted and laughed again and again drinking blood-like wine. The leading Gaṇas danced.

## \|\| 11.20.37 \|\|

*cakrurbahūnyapratimabhāvāḥ saharṣaromāṇi viceṣṭitāni \|*  
*nandaṃti kecitpraharanti keciddhāvanti kecitpralapanti kecit \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Pounding up the gods including Indra, the leading Gaṇas, strong like lordly bulls, elephants and lions, of unrivalled glory, perpetrated hair-raising deeds of destruction.

## \|\| 11.20.38 \|\|

*nṛtyanti kecidvihasanti kecidvalganti kecitpramathā balena \|*  
*kecijjighṛkṣaṃti ghanānsa toyānkecidgrahītuṃ ravimutpataṃti \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The Pramathas rejoiced, struck, ran, prattled, danced, laughed and jumped about.

## \|\| 11.20.39 \|\|

*kecitprasartuṃ pavanena sārdhamicchaṃti bhīmāḥ pramathā viyatsthāḥ \|*  
*ākṣipya kecicca varāyudhāni mahā bhujaṃgāniva vainateyāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Some of them evinced a desire to seize the watery clouds, some jumped up to seize the sun; others wished to blow along with the wind.

## \|\| 11.20.40 \|\|

*bhramaṃti devānapi vidravaṃtaḥ khamaṃḍale parvatakūṭakalpāḥ \|*  
*utpāṭya cotpāṭyagṛhāṇi kecitsajālavātāyanavedikāni \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Some wielded weapons and rushed through the sky like peaks of mountains; tossed the gods like the Garuḍa tossing huge pythons.

## \|\| 11.20.41 \|\|

*vikṣipya vikṣipya jalasya madhye kālāṃbudābhāḥ pramathā nineduḥ \|*  
*udvartitadvārakapāṭakuḍyaṃ vidhvastaśālāvalabhīgavākṣam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Some looking like the black clouds uprooted the houses, windows, daises, hurled them into water and roared.

## \|\| 11.20.42 \|\|

*aho batābhajyata yajñavāṭamanāthavadvākyamivāyathārtham \|*  
*hā nātha tāteti pituḥ suteti bhratarmamāmbeti ca mātuleti \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The doors, door-frames and walls of the sacrificial mansion were upset; the windows, ceiling frames, the halls were destroyed utterly. The complete edifice of sacrifice crumbled helplessly like a statement without foundation.

## \|\| 11.20.43 \|\|

*utpāṭyamāneṣu gṛheṣu nāryo hyānāthaśabdānbahuśaḥ pracakruḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. While houses were being dismantled, the women shrieked and cried helplessly “O husband” “O Child” “O father” “O brother” “O mother” “O uncle.”

## Chapter 21 - The destruction of Dakṣa’s sacrifice (2): The punishment of the gods

## \|\| 11.21.1 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*tatastridaśamukhyāste viṣṇuśakrapurogamāḥ \|*  
*sarve bhayaparitrastādudruvurbhayavihvalāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

1\. The chiefs of gods headed by Viṣṇu and Indra were terribly afraid. They fled in excessive fright.

## \|\| 11.21.2 \|\|

*nijairadūṣitairaṃgairdṛṣṭvā devānupadrutān \|*  
*daṃḍyānadaṃḍitānmatvā cukopa gaṇapuṃgavaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Seeing that the gods had fled uninjured and thinking that those who deserved to be punished remained unpunished the leading Gaṇa became angry.

## \|\| 11.21.3-4 \|\|

*tatastriśūlamādāya śarvaśaktinibarhaṇam \|*  
*ūrdhvadṛṣṭirmahābāhurmukhājjvālāḥ samutsṛjan \|\| 3 \|\|*

*amarānapi dudrāva dviradāniva kesarī \|*  
*tānabhidravatastasya gamanaṃ sumanoharam \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. He took up the all-destroying trident and looked up. He vomitted flames from his mouth, chased the gods as the lion chases the elephants. His gait as he pursued them resembled that of an elephant in its rut.

## \|\| 11.21.5-7 \|\|

*vārāṇasyeva mattasya jagāma prekṣaṇīyatām \|*  
*tatastatkṣobhayāmāsa mahatsurabalaṃ balī \|\| 5 \|\|*

*mahāsarovaraṃ yadvanmatto vāraṇayūthapaḥ \|*  
*vikurvanbahudhāvarṇānnīlapāṃḍuralohitān \|\| 6 \|\|*

*vibhradvyāghrājinaṃ vāso hemapravaratārakam \|*  
*chindanbhindannuda 1 lindandārayanpramathannapi \|\| 7 \|\|*

5-7. Then he agitated the army of the gods as the lord of elephants in rut stirs up a lake, shedding different hues blue, grey and red. He wore a tiger’s skin as his cloth which was inlaid with excellent gold and pearls. Cutting, piercing, moistening, tearing and pounding, Bhadra moved among the hosts of the gods like fire consuming dry grass.

## \|\| 11.21.8-9 \|\|

*vyacaraddevasaṃgheṣu bhadro 'gniriva kakṣagaḥ \|*  
*tatra tatra mahāvegāccaraṃtaṃ śūladhāriṇam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tamekaṃ tridaśāḥ sarve sahasramiva menire \|*  
*bhadrakālī ca saṃkruddhā yuddhavṛddhamadoddhatā \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. As he walked about speedily armed with a spear all alone, the gods thought him to be numbering a thousand. The infuriated Bhadrakālī excited by the fight pierced through the gods in the war holding spears shedding flames.

## \|\| 11.21.10-11 \|\|

*muktajvālena śūlena nirbibheda raṇe surān \|*  
*sa tayā ruruce bhadro rudrakopasamudbhavaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*prabhayeva yugāṃtāgniścalayā dhūmadhūmrayā \|*  
*bhadrakālī tadāyuddhe vidrutatridaśābabhau \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Bhadra born of Rudra’s anger shone in her company as the fire at the time of dissolution with a lustre pale and smoky due to smoke. Pursuing the gods in the course of war, Bhadrakālī shone as the flame of fire at the end of the Kalpa that burns the universe.

## \|\| 11.21.12-15 \|\|

*kalpe śeṣānalajvālādagdhāviśvajagadyathā \|*  
*tadā savājinaṃ sūryaṃ rudrānrudragaṇāgraṇīḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*bhadro mūrdhni jaghānāśu vāmapādena līlayā \|*  
*asibhiḥ pāvakaṃ bhadraḥ paṭṭiśaistu yamaṃ yamī \|\| 13 \|\|*

*rudrāndṛḍhena śūlena mudgarairvaruṇaṃ dṛḍhaiḥ \|*  
*parighairnirṛtiṃ vāyuṃ ṭaṃkaiṣṭaṃkadharaḥ svayam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*nirbibheda raṇe vīro līlayaiva gaṇeśvaraḥ \|*  
*sarvāndevagaṇānsadyo munīñchaṃbhorvirodhinaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

12-15. Bhadra the leader of Rudragaṇas angrily kicked the sun and his horse on the head sportively with his left leg. The heroic Gaṇeśvara, Bhadra with self-control hit Pāvaka with his swords, Yama with iron-clubs, Rudras with his spear and Varuṇa with iron clubs. Holding the axe he hit Vāyu with it and Nirṛti with big clubs. The war was a sportive game for him. He attacked the gods and the sages antagonistic to Śiva.

## \|\| 11.21.16 \|\|

*tato devaḥ sarasvatyā nāsikāgraṃ suśobhanam \|*  
*ciccheda karajāgreṇa devamātustathaiva ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Then the lord cut off the tip of the nose of Sarasvatī as well as of the mother of the gods with the tip of his nail.

## \|\| 11.21.17 \|\|

*ciccheda ca kuṭhāreṇa bāhudaṃḍaṃ vibhāvasoḥ \|*  
*agrato dvyaṃgulāṃ jihvāṃ māturdevyā lulāva ca \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. With a dagger he chopped off an arm of Vibhāvasu, and the tongue up to two inches from the tip, of the mother of the gods.

## \|\| 11.21.18 \|\|

*svāhādevyāstathā devo dakṣiṇaṃ nāsikāpuṭam \|*  
*cakarta karajāgreṇa vāmaṃ ca stanacūcukam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The lord nipped off the right nostril and the nipple of the left breast of Svāhā with his nail-end.

## \|\| 11.21.19 \|\|

*bhagasya vipule netre śatapatrasamaprabhe \|*  
*prasahyotpāṭayāmāsa bhadraḥ paramavegavān \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The impetuous Bhadra uprooted the eyes of Bhaga large and lustrous like the lotus.

## \|\| 11.21.20 \|\|

*pūṣṇo daśanarekhāṃ ca dīptāṃ muktāvalīmiva \|*  
*jaghāna dhanuṣaḥ koṭyā sa tenāspaṣṭavāgabhūt \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. With the end of his bow he hit Puṣan’s pearl like row of teeth. Thereafter Puṣan could not utter words clearly.

## \|\| 11.21.21 \|\|

*tataścaṃdramasaṃ devaḥ pādāṃguṣṭhena līlayā \|*  
*kṣaṇaṃ kṛmivadākramya gharṣayāmāsa bhūtale \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Then the lord stamped the moon with his toe, as though he was only a worm and ground him on the ground.

## \|\| 11.21.22 \|\|

*śiraściccheda dakṣasya bhadraḥ paramakopataḥ \|*  
*krośaṃtyāmeva vairiṇyāṃ bhadrakālyai dadau ca tat \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The infuriated Bhadra cut off the head of Dakṣa and handed it over to Bhadrakālī even as Vīriṇi, wife of Dakṣa was lamenting.

## \|\| 11.21.23 \|\|

*tatprahṛṣṭā samādāya śirastālaphalopamam \|*  
*sā devī kaṃḍukakrīḍāṃ cakāra samarāṃgaṇe \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Taking up the head resembling the fruit of a palmyra the goddess played with it like a ball in the battlefield.

## \|\| 11.21.24 \|\|

*tato dakṣasya yajñastrī kuśīlā bhartṛbhiryathā \|*  
*pādābhyāṃ caiva hastābhyāṃ hanyate sma gaṇeśvaraiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Then the sacrifice itself was hit and smashed with feet and hands like fallen women hit by their husbands.

## \|\| 11.21.25-26 \|\|

*ariṣṭanemine somaṃ dharmaṃ caiva prajāpatim \|*  
*bahuputraṃ cāṃgirasaṃ kṛśāśvaṃ kaśyapaṃ tathā \|\| 25 \|\|*

*gale pragṛhya balino gaṇapāḥ siṃhavikramāḥ \|*  
*bhartsayaṃto bhṛśaṃ vāgbhirnirjaghnurmūrdhni muṣṭibhiḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. Catching hold of by the neck, Ariṣṭanemi, Soma, Dharma, Prajāpati Aṅgiras, father of many sons, Kṛśāśva and Kaśyapa, the powerful chiefs of Gaṇas of leonine exploits rebuked and hit them on the heads with fists.

## \|\| 11.21.27 \|\|

*dharṣitā bhūtavetālairdārāssutaparigrahāḥ \|*  
*yathā kaliyuge jārairbalena kulayoṣitaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Just as in Kaliyuga women of noble families are molested and defiled by paramours forcibly so also the women and the daughters-in-law were molested by Bhūtas and Vetālas.

## \|\| 11.21.28-30 \|\|

*tacca vidhvastakalaśaṃ bhagnayūpaṃ gatotsavam \|*  
*pradīpitamahāśālaṃ prabhinnadvāratoraṇam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*utpāṭitasurānīkaṃ hanyamānaṃ tapodhanam \|*  
*praśāntabrahmanirghoṣaṃ prakṣīṇajanasaṃcayam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*krandamānāturastrīkaṃ hatāśeṣaparicchadam \|*  
*śūnyāraṇyanibhaṃ jajñe yajñavāṭaṃ tadārditam \|\| 30 \|\|*

28-30. Thus the sacrificial spot appeared like a desolate forest. The domes were smashed. The posts were broken. The festivities ended. The hall was burnt. The portals and festoons had crumbled. The army of the gods was uprooted. The sages were killed. The Vedic chant had subsided. The population had dwindled. The distressed women shrieked. The appendages were spoiled.

## \|\| 11.21.31 \|\|

*śūlavegaprarugṇāśca bhinnabāhūruvakṣasaḥ \|*  
*vinikṛttottamāṃgāśca petururvyāṃ surottamāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The excellent gods fell on the ground with their arms, thighs and chests pierced, with the heads cut off with the trident.

## \|\| 11.21.32 \|\|

*hateṣu teṣu deveṣu patiteṣuḥ sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*praviveśa gaṇeśānaḥ kṣaṇādāhavanīyakam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. When thousands of gods were killed and their bodies lay sprawled on the ground, the chief of Ganas entered the place of sacrificial fires.

## \|\| 11.21.33 \|\|

*praviṣṭamatha taṃ dṛṣṭvā bhadraṃ kālāgnisaṃnibham \|*  
*dudrāva maraṇādbhīto yajño mṛgavapurdharaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. On seeing that Bhadra resembling the deadly fire had come the sacrifice was afraid of death and fled assuming the form of a deer.

## \|\| 11.21.34 \|\|

*sa visphārya mahaccāpaṃ dṛḍhajyāghoṣaṇabhīṣaṇam \|*  
*bhadrastamabhidudrāva vikṣipanneva sāyakān \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Bhadra pursued him drawing his great bow, terrible due to the twanging sound of the firm bow-siring, and discharging the arrows.

## \|\| 11.21.35 \|\|

*ākarṇapūrṇamākṛṣṭaṃ dhanurambudasaṃnibham \|*  
*nādayāmāsa ca jyāṃ dyāṃ khaṃ ca bhūmiṃ ca sarvaśaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. He sounded the bow by drawing the string to the ears like the thundering cloud. The bowstring, heaven, sky and earth reverberated.

## \|\| 11.21.36-37 \|\|

*tamupaśritya sannādaṃ hato 'smītyeva vihvalam \|*  
*śaraṇārdhena vakreṇa sa vīro 'dhvarapūruṣam \|\| 36 \|\|*

*mahābhayaskhalatpādaṃ vepantaṃ vigatatviṣam \|*  
*mṛgarūpeṇa dhāvantaṃ viśiraskaṃ tadākarot \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. The sacrifice was terrified on hearing the sound, “O I am doomed”, he thought. He was trembling with the legs shaking. His lustre disappeared. He ran in the form of a deer. The heroic Bhadra. with a half curved arrow, decapitated him.

## \|\| 11.21.38 \|\|

*tamīdṛśamavajñātaṃ dṛṣṭvā vai sūryasaṃbhavam \|*  
*viṣṇuḥ paramasaṃkruddho yuddhāyābhavadudyataḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. On seeing the sacrifice thus insulted, Viṣṇu was infuriated and got ready for a fight.

## \|\| 11.21.39-41 \|\|

*tamuvāha mahāvegātskandhena natasaṃdhinā \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ vayasāṃ rājā garuḍaḥ pannagāśanaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*devāśca hataśiṣṭā ye devarājapurogamāḥ \|*  
*pracakrustasya sāhāyyaṃ prāṇāṃstyaktumivodyatāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*viṣṇunā sahitāndevānmṛgendraḥ kroṣṭukāniva \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā jahāsa bhūtendro mṛgendra iva vivyathaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

39-41. Garuḍa the devourer of serpents and the king of birds bore him speedily over his shoulders. The god Indra and others who had escaped helped him as if ready to abandon their lives. Seeing them along with Viṣṇu like the lion viewing the jackals the lord of Bhūtas laughed. He looked like a lion without distress.

## Chapter 22 - The destruction of Dakṣa’s sacrifice (3)

## \|\| 11.22.1 \|\|

*tasminnavasare vyomni samāvirabhavadrathaḥ \|*  
*sahasrasūryasaṃkāśaścārucīravṛṣadhvajaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

1\. At that time a chariot resembling a thousand suns and with the emblem of a bull on the banner cloth appeared in the sky.

## \|\| 11.22.2 \|\|

*aśvaratnadvayodāro rathacakracatuṣṭayaḥ \|*  
*sañcitānekadivyāstraśastraratnapariṣkṛtaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The splendid chariot had two horses and four wheels. Several divine weapons and missiles had been kept ready therein. It was embellished with jewels.

## \|\| 11.22.3 \|\|

*tasyāpi rathavaryasya syātsa eva hi sārathiḥ \|*  
*yathā ca traipure yuddhe pūrvaṃ śārvarathe sthitaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. It was driven by the same charioteer who drove Śiva’s chariot in the latter’s war with the Tripuras.

## \|\| 11.22.4 \|\|

*sa taṃ rathavaraṃ brahmā śāsanādeva śūlinaḥ \|*  
*haressamīpamānīya kṛtāñjalirabhāṣata \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. At the bidding of Śiva, Brahmā brought the excellent chariot to Vīrabhadra and spoke with palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 11.22.5 \|\|

*bhagavanbhadra bhadrāṃga bhagavānindubhūṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*ājñāpayati vīrastvāṃ rathamāroḍhumavyayaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. “O lord Vīrabhadra the eternal moon-crested lord commands you to mount the chariot.

## \|\| 11.22.6 \|\|

*rebhyāśramasamīpasthastryaṃbako 'ṃbikayā saha \|*  
*sampaśyate mahābāho dussahaṃ te parākramam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O great-armed one, Śiva, stationed near the hermitage of Raibhya along with Śivā, is witnessing your unbearable exploit.

## \|\| 11.22.7 \|\|

*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā sa vīro gaṇakuñjaraḥ \|*  
*āruroha rathaṃ divyamanugṛhya pitāmaham \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. On hearing his words and Blessing Brahmā, the heroic leading Gaṇa mounted the divine chariot.

## \|\| 11.22.8 \|\|

*tathā rathavare tasminsthite brahmaṇi sārathau \|*  
*bhadrasya vavṛdhe lakṣmī rudrasyeva puradviṣaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. In the excellent chariot where Brahmā sat as the charioteer the splendour of Bhadra increased like that of Rudra, the enemy of the Tripuras.

## \|\| 11.22.9 \|\|

*tataḥ śaṃkhavaraṃ dīptaṃ pūrṇacaṃdrasamaprabham \|*  
*pradadhmau vadane kṛtvā bhānukaṃpo mahābalaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Then keeping an excellent conch shining like the full moon, in his mouth, the powerful Bhānukampa blew on it.

## \|\| 11.22.10 \|\|

*tasya śaṃkhasya taṃ nādaṃ bhinnasārasasannibham \|*  
*śrutvā bhayena devānāṃ jajvāla jaṭharānalaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. At the sound of the conch resembling that of the swan, the fire in the belly of the gods blazed with fear.

## \|\| 11.22.11 \|\|

*yakṣavidyādharāhīndraiḥ siddhairyuddhadidṛkṣubhiḥ \|*  
*kṣaṇena nibaḍībhūtāḥ sākāśavivarā diśāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. In an instant the quarters including open spaces and crevices were filled up and thronged with leading Yakṣas Vidyādharas, serpents and Siddhas who desired to witness the battle.

## \|\| 11.22.12 \|\|

*tataḥ śārṅgeṇa cāpāṅkātsa nārāyaṇanīradaḥ \|*  
*mahatā bāṇavarṣeṇa tutoda gaṇagovṛṣam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Then Nārāyaṇa as the cloud inflicted pain on the Gaṇas as the cattle, through a great shower of arrows from his bow.

## \|\| 11.22.13 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā viṣṇumāyāṃtaṃ śatadhā bāṇavarṣiṇam \|*  
*sa cādade dhanurjaitraṃ bhadro bāṇasahasramuk \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. On seeing Viṣṇu coming and discharging arrows Bhadra took up his bow and showered thousands of arrows.

## \|\| 11.22.14 \|\|

*samādāya ca taddivyaṃ dhanussamarabhairavam \|*  
*śanairvisphārayāmāsa meruṃ dhanuriveśvaraḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. He took up the divine bow and slowly drew it like Śiva who drew the bow Meru.

## \|\| 11.22.15 \|\|

*tasya visphāryamāṇasya dhanuṣo 'bhūnmahāsvanaḥ \|*  
*tena svanena mahatā pṛthivīṃ samakaṃpayat \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. As the bow was drawn a loud report was produced shaking the earth.

## \|\| 11.22.16 \|\|

*tataḥ śaravaraṃ ghoraṃ dīptamāśīviṣopamam \|*  
*jagrāha gaṇapaḥ śrīmānsvayamugraparākramaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Then the chief of Gaṇas, of fierce valour and glory took an excellent arrow blazing like a serpent.

## \|\| 11.22.17 \|\|

*bāṇoddhāre bhujo hyasya tūṇīvadanasaṃgataḥ \|*  
*pratyadṛśyata valmīkaṃ vivekṣuriva pannagaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. His hand in contact with the opening of the quiver for taking up the arrows appeared like a serpent wishing to enter an anthill.

## \|\| 11.22.18 \|\|

*samuddhṛtaḥ kare tasya tatkṣaṇaṃ ruruce śareḥ \|*  
*mahābhujaṃgasaṃdaṣṭo yathā bālabhujaṅgamaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The arrow lifted and held in the hand shone like the young one of a serpent held within the mouth of a great serpent.

## \|\| 11.22.19 \|\|

*śareṇa ghanatīvreṇa bhadro rudraparākramaḥ \|*  
*vivyādha kupito gāḍhaṃ lalāṭe viṣṇumavyayam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. With his stout and sharp arrow, the infuriated Bhadra who resembled Rudra, hit the unchanging Viṣṇu on his forehead.

## \|\| 11.22.20 \|\|

*lalāṭe 'bhihito viṣṇuḥ pūrvamevāvamānitaḥ \|*  
*cukopa gaṇapeṃdrāya mṛgeṃdrāyeva govṛṣaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Viṣṇu thus insulted and hit on the forehead became angry with the chief of Gaṇas like a cow or bull becoming angry with the lion.

## \|\| 11.22.21 \|\|

*tatastvaśanikalpena krūrāsyena maheṣuṇā \|*  
*vivyādha gaṇarājasya bhuje bhujagasannibhe \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Then he hit the serpent like arm of the chief of Gaṇas, with a cruel, pointed great arrow resembling the thunderbolt.

## \|\| 11.22.22 \|\|

*so 'pi tasya bhuje bhūyaḥ sūryāyutasamaprabham \|*  
*visasarja śaraṃ vegādvīrabhadro mahābalaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The powerful Vīrabhadra too, with a great velocity discharged an arrow brilliant like ten thousand suns again at his arm.

## \|\| 11.22.23 \|\|

*sa ca viṣṇuḥ punarbhadraṃ bhadro viṣṇuṃ tathā punaḥ \|*  
*sa ca taṃ sa ca taṃ viprāśśaraistāvanujaghnatuḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Viṣṇu hit Bhadra. Bhadra hit Viṣṇu. O brahmins both of them hit each other.

## \|\| 11.22.24 \|\|

*tayoḥ parasparaṃ vegāccharānāśu vimuṃcatoḥ \|*  
*dvayossamabhavadyuddhaṃ tumulaṃ romaharṣaṇam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The tumultuous hair-raising fight between the two discharging the arrows on each other in quick succession then ensued.

## \|\| 11.22.25 \|\|

*taddṛṣṭvā tumulaṃ yuddhaṃ tayoreva parasparam \|*  
*hāhākāro mahānāsīdākāśe khecareritaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. On seeing their mutual noisy battle the sounds of “Hā-Hā” raised by the aerial wanderers rose in the sky.

## \|\| 11.22.26 \|\|

*tatastvanalatuṃḍena śareṇādityavarcasā \|*  
*vivyādha sudṛḍhaṃ bhadro viṣṇormahati vakṣasi \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Then Bhadra hit in the broad chest of Viṣṇu with an arrow that shone like the sun and the tip of which blazed like fire.

## \|\| 11.22.27 \|\|

*sa tu tīvraprapātena śareṇa dṛḍhamāhataḥ \|*  
*mahatīṃ rujamāsādya nipapāta vimohitaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Acutely hit by the arrow that fell sharply, Viṣṇu suffered great pain and fell into swoon.

## \|\| 11.22.28 \|\|

*punaḥ kṣaṇādivotthāya labdhasaṃjñastadā hariḥ \|*  
*sarvāṇyapi ca divyāstrāṇyathainaṃ pratyavāsṛjat \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. He regained consciousness instantaneously and got up. He discharged his weapons against Bhadra.

## \|\| 11.22.29 \|\|

*sa ca viṣṇurdhanurmuktānsarvāñcharvacamūpatiḥ \|*  
*sahasā vārayāmāsa ghoraiḥ pratiśaraiḥ śarān \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The chief of the army of Śiva stopped all the missiles discharged from Viṣṇu’s bow by means of terrible anti-missiles.

## \|\| 11.22.30 \|\|

*tato viṣṇussvanāmāṃkaṃ bāṇamavyāhataṃ kvacit \|*  
*sasarja krodharaktā kṣastamuddiśya gaṇeśvaram \|*  
*taṃ bāṇaṃ bāṇavaryeṇa bhadro bhadrāhvayeṇa tu \|*  
*aprāptameva bhagavāñciccheda śatadhā pathi \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Then Viṣṇu with eyes reddened by anger discharged an arrow in which his name had been engraved and which had never been obstructed anywhere, against the Gaṇa chief. Showering arrows, lord Bhadra split the arrow into pieces on the way before it reached him.

## \|\| 11.22.31-33 \|\|

*athaikeneṣuṇā śārṅgaṃ dvābhyāṃ pakṣau garutmataḥ \|*  
*nimeṣādeva ciccheda tadadbhutamivābhavat \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tato yogabalādviṣṇurdehāddevānsudāruṇān \|*  
*śaṃkhacakragadāhastān visasarja sahasraśaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*sarvāṃstānkṣaṇamātreṇa traipurāniva śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*nirdadāha mahābāhurnetrasṛṣṭena vahninā \|\| 33 \|\|*

31-33. Then within an instant he split the bow with a single arrow and the wings of Garuḍa with the two arrows. This was a wonderful feat. Then by his Yogic powers Viṣṇu let loose from his body thousands of terrific gods holding conch, discus and the club. Bat the mighty Bhadra burnt all of them instantaneously by means of the fire of his eyes like Śiva who burnt the Tripuras.

## \|\| 11.22.34-36 \|\|

*tataḥ kruddhataro viṣṇuścakramudyamya satvaraḥ \|*  
*tasminvīro samutsraṣṭuṃ tadānīmudyato 'bhavat \|\| 34 \|\|*

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā cakramudyamya purataḥ samupasthitam \|*  
*smayanniva gaṇeśāno vyaṣṭaṃbhayadayatnataḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*staṃbhitāṃgastu taccakraṃ ghoramapratimaṃ kvacit \|*  
*icchannapi samutsraṣṭuṃ na viṣṇurabhavatkṣamaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

34-36. Thus infuriated Viṣṇu raised his discus in a hurry and attempted to hurl it on the hero. On seeing him in front with the discus lifted up, the chief of the Gaṇas smiled and without any strain made his hand stiff and benumbed. With his limbs turned numb, Viṣṇu became incapable though he was desirous of hurling the unequalled and terrible discus.

## \|\| 11.22.37-39 \|\|

*śvasannivaikamuddhṛtya bāhuṃ cakrasamanvitam \|*  
*atiṣṭhadalaso bhūtvā pāṣāṇa iva niścalaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*viśarīro yathājīvo viśṛṅgo vā yathā vṛṣaḥ \|*  
*vidaṃṣṭraśca yathā siṃhastathā viṣṇuravasthitaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā durdaśāpannaṃ viṣṇumiṃdrādayaḥ surāḥ \|*  
*samunnaddhā gaṇendreṇa mṛgeṃdreṇeva govṛṣāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

37-39. Gasping for breath with a hand holding the discus he stood idly, immobile like a stone, like the soul without a body, like a bull without a horn or like a lion without its fangs. So stood Viṣṇu. On seeing Viṣṇu in a miserable plight the infuriated Indra and other gods took up their weapons. They hastened to fight with the chief of Gaṇas like cows or bulls attempting to fight with a lion.

## \|\| 11.22.40-41 \|\|

*pragṛhītāyudhā yauddhuṃkruddhāḥ samupatasthire \|*  
*tāndṛṣṭvā samare bhadraḥkṣudrāniva harirmṛgān \|\| 40 \|\|*

*sākṣādrudratanurvīro varavīragaṇāvṛtaḥ \|*  
*aṭṭahāsena ghoreṇa vyaṣṭaṃ bhayadaniṃditaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. On glancing at them as a lion glances at the deer, Bhadra of Rudra’s body, the hero surrounded by excellent heroes, benumbed them with a boisterous laugh.

## \|\| 11.22.42 \|\|

*tathā śatamakhasyāpi savajro dakṣiṇaḥ karaḥ \|*  
*sisṛkṣoreva udvajraścitrīkṛta ivābhavat \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The right hand of Indra who desired to release the thunderbolt it held remained steady as painted in a picture.

## \|\| 11.22.43 \|\|

*anyeṣāmapi sarveṣāṃ saraktā api bāhavaḥ \|*  
*alasānāmivāraṃbhāstādṛśāḥ pratiyāṃtyuta \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. The hands of others too became fixed, as the activities of idle men at the start remain unprogressive.

## \|\| 11.22.44 \|\|

*evaṃ bhagavatā tena vyāhatāśeṣavaibhavāt \|*  
*amarāḥ samare tasya purataḥ sthātumakṣamāḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Thus the gods with their efficacy thwarted in the battle were rendered incapable of standing in front of him.

## \|\| 11.22.45 \|\|

*stabdhairavayavaireva dudruvurbhayavihvalāḥ \|*  
*sthitiṃ ca cakrire yuddhe vīratejobhayākulāḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Frightened by the splendour of Vīrabhadra they could not stay further in the battle. In that fierce battle they fled even with their benumbed limbs.

## \|\| 11.22.46 \|\|

*vidrutāṃstridaśānvīrānvīrabhadro mahābhujaḥ \|*  
*vivyādha niśitairbāṇairmagho varṣairivācalān \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The mighty Vīrabhadra hit the fleeing warriors, with sharp arrows like the cloud hitting the mountains with sharp showers.

## \|\| 11.22.47 \|\|

*bahavastasya vīrasya bāhavaḥ parighopamāḥ \|*  
*śastraiścakāśire dīptaiḥ sāgnijvālā ivoragāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. The multitudinous arms of Vīrabhadra, resembling iron clubs, shone with their various shining weapons like serpents with fiery flames.

## \|\| 11.22.48 \|\|

*astraśastrāṇyanekānisavīro visṛjanbabhau \|*  
*visṛjansarvabhūtāni yathādau viśvasaṃbhavaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The hero discharging weapons and missiles shone like Brahma discharging (creating) all living beings.

## \|\| 11.22.49 \|\|

*yathā raśmibhirādityaḥ pracchādayati medinīm \|*  
*tathā vīraḥ kṣaṇādeva śaraiḥ prācchādayaddiśaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Just as the sun covers the earth by his rays so the hero enveloped the quarters by means of his arrows.

## \|\| 11.22.50 \|\|

*khamaṃḍale gaṇendrasya śarāḥ kanakabhūṣitāḥ \|*  
*utpataṃtastaḍidrūpairupamānapadaṃ yayuḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The arrows of the Gaṇa chieftains embellished with gold and flying in the firmament like lightning became the standard of comparison.

## \|\| 11.22.51 \|\|

*mahāṃtaste suragaṇānmaṃḍūkānivaḍuṃḍubhāḥ \|*  
*prāṇairviyojayāmāsuḥ papuśca rudhirāsavam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The great arrows took away the lives of the gods even as the water snakes squeeze the lives out of the frogs. They drank their blood as though that were wine.

## \|\| 11.22.52 \|\|

*nikṛttabāhavaḥ kecitkecillūnavarānanāḥ \|*  
*pārśve vidāritāḥ kecinnipeturamarā bhuvi \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. The hands of some had been cut off. The faces of some had been split. Some gods fell on the ground with their sides lacerated and bruised.

## \|\| 11.22.53-54 \|\|

*viśikhonmathitairgātrairbahubhiśchinnasandhibhiḥ \|*  
*vivṛttanayanāḥ kecinnipeturbhūtale mṛtāḥ \|*  
*gāṃ praveṣṭumivecchaṃtaḥ khaṃ gaṃtumiva lipsavaḥ \|*  
*alabdhātmanirodhānāṃ vyalīyaṃtaḥ parasparam \|\| 53 \|\|*

*bhūmau kecitpraviviśuḥ parvatānāṃ guhāḥ pare \|*  
*apare jagmurākāśaṃ pare ca viviśurjalam \|\| 54 \|\|*

53-54. With their limbs shattered by the arrows, joints

severed and eyes dislocated they fell dead on the ground. Some desired to enter the earth and some wished to go up to the sky. Being unobstructed they merged into one another. Some entered the earth. Others entered the caves of mountains. Others went up to the sky. Still others entered the water.

## \|\| 11.22.55-56 \|\|

*tathā saṃchinnasarvāṃgaissa vīrastridaśairbabhau \|*  
*parigrastaprajāvargo bhagavāniva bhairavaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*dagdhatripurasaṃvyūhastripurāriryathābhavat \|*  
*evaṃ devabalaṃ sarvaṃ dīnaṃ bībhatsadarśanam \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. With the gods with their limbs cut off, the hero shone like Bhairava who had seized people and like Śiva who had burnt the three cities.

## \|\| 11.22.57 \|\|

*gaṇeśvarasamutpannaṃ kṛpaṇaṃ vapurādade \|*  
*tadā tridaśavīrāṇāmasṛksalilavāhinī \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Thus the entire army of the gods was dejected and looked hideous. They had their bodies mutilated by the Gaṇeśvara.

## \|\| 11.22.58 \|\|

*prāvartata nadī ghorā prāṇināṃ bhayaśaṃsinī \|*  
*rudhireṇa pariklinnā yajñabhūmistadā babhau \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Then a terrible stream of flood from the bodies of the warriors began to flow striking terror in the living beings.

## \|\| 11.22.59 \|\|

*raktārdravasanā śyāmā hataśuṃbheva kaiśikī \|*  
*tasminmahati saṃvṛtte samare bhṛśadāruṇe \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. The ground of the sacrificial rites drenched with the blood shone like the goddess Kauśikī who had killed Śumbha with her garments wet with the blood.

## \|\| 11.22.60 \|\|

*bhayeneva paritrastā pracacāla vasundharā \|*  
*mahormikalilāvartaścukṣubhe ca mahodadhiḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60 When the extremely terrible battle had concluded the earth quaked as though frightened terribly.

## \|\| 11.22.61 \|\|

*petuścolkā mahotpātāḥ śākhāśca mumucurdrumāḥ \|*  
*aprasannā diśaḥ sarvāḥ pavanaścāśivo vavau \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. The ocean was agitated with the surging waves, foams and whirlpools. Meteors fell portending great evil. Trees shed down their branches.

## \|\| 11.22.62-64 \|\|

*aho vidhiviparyāsastvaśvamedhoyamadhvaraḥ \|*  
*yajamānassvayaṃ dakṣau brahmaputraprajāpatiḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*dharmādayassadasyāśca rakṣitā garuḍadhvajaḥ \|*  
*bhāgāṃśca pratigṛhṇaṃti sākṣādiṃdrādayaḥ surāḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*tathāpi yajamānasya yajñasya ca sahartvijaḥ \|*  
*sadya eva śiraśchedassādhu saṃpadyate phalam \|\| 64 \|\|*

62-64. The quarters looked gloomy. Inauspicious wind blew. Ah, the adverse working of the fate. This is a horse-sacrifice. The sacrifìcer is Dakṣa himself. Dharma and others are the councillors. The Garuḍa-bannered deity is the patron. Indra and other gods take their shares directly. Still the sacrificer, the sacrifice and the priests are beheaded immediately.

## \|\| 11.22.65 \|\|

*tasmānnāvedanirdiṣṭaṃ na ceśvarabahiṣkṛtam \|*  
*nāsatparigṛhītaṃ ca karma kuryātkadācana \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Hence no such action shall be performed that is not indicated in the Vedas, and that which excludes Śiva and is taken up by the wicked.

## \|\| 11.22.66 \|\|

*kṛtvāpi sumahatpuṇyamiṣṭvā yajñaśatairapi \|*  
*na tatphalamavāpnoti bhaktihīno maheśvare \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. A person devoid of devotion to Śiva docs not attain the fruit of any rite even though he may perform holy rites and sacrifices.

## \|\| 11.22.67 \|\|

*kṛtvāpi sumahatpāpaṃ bhaktyā yajati yaśśivam \|*  
*mucyate pātakaiḥ sarvairnātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Even after committing great sin, if any one worships Śiva with devotion he is liberated from the sin. No hesitation need be made in this respect.

## \|\| 11.22.68 \|\|

*bahunātra kimuktena vṛthā dānaṃ vṛthā tapaḥ \|*  
*vṛthā yajño vṛthā homaḥ śivanindāratasya tu \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Of what avail is much talk? If any one censures Śiva, the charitable gifts he makes, the penance, the sacrifice, the homa, everything goes in vain.

## \|\| 11.22.69 \|\|

*tataḥ sanārāyaṇakāssarudrāḥ salokapālāssamare suraughāḥ \|*  
*gaṇeṃdracāpacyutabāṇaviddhāḥ pradudruvurgāḍharujābhibhūtāḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Then the gods including Viṣṇu and the guardians of the quarters pierced by the arrows discharged from the bow of the chief of Gaṇas and overwhelmed by great pain fled from the battle.

## \|\| 11.22.70 \|\|

*celuḥ kvacitkecana śīrṇakeśāḥ seduḥ kvacitkecana dīrghagātrāḥ \|*  
*petuḥ kvacitkecana bhinnavaktrā neśuḥ kvacitkecana devavīrāḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. The warriors of the gods with their hair dishevelled moved about. Some sat exhausted with their huge bodies. Some fell with their faces cut and some perished.

## \|\| 11.22.71 \|\|

*kecicca tatra tridaśā vipannā visrastavastrābharaṇāstraśastrāḥ \|*  
*nipeturudbhāsitadīnamudrā madaṃ ca darpaṃ ca balaṃ ca hitvā \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Some fell in adversity with their garments, ornaments, weapons and missiles scattered. Eschewing their pride, arrogance and strength they fell evincing signs of dejection.

## \|\| 11.22.72 \|\|

*sasmutpathaprasthitamapradhṛṣyo vikṣipya dakṣādhvaramakṣatāstraiḥ \|*  
*babhau gaṇeśassa gaṇeśvarāṇāṃ madhye sthitaḥ siṃha ivarṣabhāṇām \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Destroying Dakṣa’s sacrifice, performed in the wrong way, by means of weapons the invincible lord of Gaṇas shone amidst the leading Gaṇas like the lion in the midst of bulls.

## Chapter 23 - The destruction of Dakṣa’s sacrifice (4): Śiva’s Fury

## \|\| 11.23.1 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*iti sañchinnabhinnāṃgā devā viṣṇupurogamāḥ \|*  
*kṣaṇātkaṣṭāṃ daśāmetya tresuḥ stokāvaśeṣitā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

1\. Thus the gods headed by Viṣṇu with their bodies split and mutilated attained a miserable plight and trembled. Only a few of them scrvived.

## \|\| 11.23.2-3 \|\|

*trastāṃstānsamare vīrān devānanyāṃśca vai gaṇāḥ \|*  
*pramathāḥ paramakruddhā vīrabhadrapraṇoditāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*pragṛhya ca tathā doṣaṃ nigaḍairāyasairdṛḍhaiḥ \|*  
*babandhuḥ pāṇipādeṣu kaṃdhareṣūdareṣu ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. The excessively infuriated Pramathas and Gaṇas urged by Vīrabhadra seized the warriors frightened of the battle tying their hands, feet, shoulders and bellies by means of strong iron fetters.

## \|\| 11.23.4 \|\|

*tasminnavasare brahmā bhadramadrīndrajānutam \|*  
*sārathyāllabdhavātsalyaḥ prārthayan praṇato 'bravīt \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. In the meantime Brahmā who had secured his favour due to his charioteership, implored Bhadra, the devotee of the daughter of Himavat.

## \|\| 11.23.5 \|\|

*alaṃ krodhena bhagavannaṣṭāścaite divaukasaḥ \|*  
*prasīda kṣamyatāṃ sarvaṃ romajaissaha suvrata \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. “O lord, enough of this fury. The gods are ruined. Please forgive their faults. O you of auspicious rites.”

## \|\| 11.23.6 \|\|

*evaṃ vijñāpitastena brahmaṇā parameṣṭhinā \|*  
*śamaṃ jagāma saṃprīto gaṇapastasya gauravāt \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Implored thus by Brahmā the delighted chief of Gaṇas became calm.

## \|\| 11.23.7 \|\|

*devāśca labdhāvasarā devadevasya maṃtriṇaḥ \|*  
*dhārayanto 'ñjalīnmūrdhni tuṣṭuvurvividhaiḥ stavaiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Getting the opportunity through Brahmā the gods joined their palms in reverence above their heads and eulogised him by various hymns.

## \|\| 11.23.8 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*namaḥ śivāya śāntāya yajñahantre triśūline \|*  
*rudrabhadrāya rudrāṇāṃ pataye rudrabhūtaye \|\| 8 \|\|*

The gods said:—

8\. Obeisance to Śiva the quiescent. Obeisance to the trident-bearing destroyer of sacrifice. Obeisance to Bhadra, the lord of Rudras, the wealth and prosperity of Rudras.

## \|\| 11.23.9 \|\|

*kālāgnirudrarūpāya kālakāmāṃgahāriṇe \|*  
*devatānāṃ śirohantre dakṣasya ca durātmanaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Obeisance to Rudra the deity of deadly fire; to the slayer of death and Kama; the remover of the heads of the gods and of the wicked-souled Dakṣa.

## \|\| 11.23.10 \|\|

*saṃsargādasya pāpasya dakṣasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ \|*  
*śāsitāḥ samare vīra tvayā vayamaninditā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. O hero, incensurable though we are we have been chastised by you in the war due to our association with this sinner Dakṣa.

## \|\| 11.23.11 \|\|

*dagdhāścāmī vayaṃ sarve tvatto bhītāśca bho prabho \|*  
*tvameva gatirasmākaṃ trāhi naśśaraṇāgatān \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. We have been burnt. O lord, we are afraid of you. You alone are our goal. Save us who have sought refuge in you.

## \|\| 11.23.12 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*tuṣṭastvevaṃ stuto devān visṛjya nigaḍātprabhuḥ \|*  
*ānayaddevadevasya samīpamamarāniha \|\| 12 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

12\. Thus eulogised the lord was satisfied. He set gods free from fetters. He took them to the presence of lord Śiva.

## \|\| 11.23.13 \|\|

*devopi tatra bhagavānantarikṣe sthitaḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*sagaṇaḥ sarvagaḥ śarvassarvalokamaheśvaraḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Śiva, the omnipresent lord of the worlds, was standing in the firmament along with the Gaṇas.

## \|\| 11.23.14 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā parameśānaṃ devā viṣṇupurogamāḥ \|*  
*prītā api ca bhītāśca namaścakrurmaheśvaram \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. On seeing him the gods headed by Viṣṇu were pleased and awe-struck. They bowed to him.

## \|\| 11.23.15 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā tānamarānbhītānpraṇatārtiharo haraḥ \|*  
*idamāha mahādevaḥ prahasan prekṣya pārvatīm \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Seeing them frightened, Śiva the destroyer of the distress of his devotees said laughingly after glancing at Pārvatī.

## \|\| 11.23.16 \|\|

*mahādeva uvāca \|*  
*mābhaiṣṭa tridaśāssarve yūyaṃ vai māmikāḥ prajāḥ \|*  
*anugrahārthameveha dhṛto daṃḍaḥ kṛpālunā \|\| 16 \|\|*

Lord Śiva said:—

16\. O gods, do not be afraid. You are my own subjects. It is only to bless you that the punishment has been meted out to you by the merciful lord.

## \|\| 11.23.17 \|\|

*bhavatāṃ nirjarāṇāṃ hi kṣānto 'smābhirvyatikramaḥ \|*  
*kruddheṣvasmāsu yuṣmākaṃ na sthitirna ca jīvitam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The transgression of you the gods has been forgiven by us. When we are infuriated you have neither sustenance nor life.

## \|\| 11.23.18 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*ityuktāstridaśāssarve śarveṇāmitatejasā \|*  
*sadyo vigatasandehā nanṛturvibudhā mudā \|\| 18 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

18\. Thus spoken to by Śiva of unmeasured splendour the gods immediately had their doubts cleared. The gods danced joyously.

## \|\| 11.23.19 \|\|

*prasannamanaso bhūtvānandavihvalamānasāḥ \|*  
*stutimārebhire kartuṃ śaṃkarasya divaukasaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Becoming delighted and excited in their minds with bliss, the gods began to eulogise Śiva.

## \|\| 11.23.20 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*tvameva devākhilalokakartā pātā ca hartā parameśvaro 'si \|*  
*kaviṣṇurudrākhyasvarūpabhedai rajastamassattvadhṛtātmamūrte \|\| 20 \|\|*

The gods said:—

20\. O lord assuming the forms of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Rudra through Rajas, Tamas and Sattva you are the creator, protector and the annihilator of the worlds.

## \|\| 11.23.21 \|\|

*sarvamūrte namaste 'stu viśvabhāvana pāvana \|*  
*amūrte bhaktahetorhi gṛhītākṛtisaukhyada \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O omniformed, O conceiver of the universe, O sanctifier. O formless, O bestower of happiness you take up forms only for the sake of devotees.

## \|\| 11.23.22 \|\|

*caṃdro 'gado hi deveśa kṛpātastava śaṃkara \|*  
*nimajjanānmṛtaḥ prāpa sukhaṃ mihirajājaliḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O Śiva, O lord of gods, it is due to your favour that the moon became free from ailment when dead she plunged into Yamuna and regained life and happiness.

## \|\| 11.23.23 \|\|

*sīmantinī hatadhavā tava pūjanataḥ prabho \|*  
*saubhāgyamatulaṃ prāpa somavāravratātsutān \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Sīmantinī whose husband had died, O lord, attained unequalled marital bliss by worshipping you. By performing the holy rites on Mondays she bore sons.

## \|\| 11.23.24 \|\|

*śrīkarāya dadau devaḥ svīyaṃ padamanuttamam \|*  
*sudarśanamarakṣastvaṃ nṛpamaṃḍalabhītitaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The lord gave excellent region to Śrīkara. You protected Sudarśana from the fear of danger from the hosts of kings.

## \|\| 11.23.25 \|\|

*meduraṃ tārayāmāsa sadāraṃ ca ghṛṇānidhiḥ \|*  
*śāradāṃ vidhavāṃ cakre sadhavāṃ kriyayā bhavān \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The storehouse of mercy enabled Medina to cross the ocean of worldly existence. By your miraculous activity you enlivened the husband of Śāradā.

## \|\| 11.23.26 \|\|

*bhadrāyuṣo vipattiṃ ca vicchidya tvamadāḥ sukham \|*  
*sauminī bhavabandhādvai muktā 'bhūttava sevanāt \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Destroying the calamity of Bhadrāyus you conferred happiness on him. By serving you Sauminī became free from worldly bondage.

## \|\| 11.23.27 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*tvaṃ śaṃbho kaharīśāśca rajassattvatamoguṇaiḥ \|*  
*kartā pātā tathā hartā janānugrahakāṃkṣayā \|\| 27 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:—

27\. O Śiva you are Brahma, Viṣṇu and Śiva by means of the Guṇas Rajas, Sattva and Tamas. With the desire to bless the people you became the creator, sustainer and the annihilator.

## \|\| 11.23.28 \|\|

*sarvagarvāpahārī ca sarvatejovilāsakaḥ \|*  
*sarvavidyādigūḍhaśca sarvānugrahakārakaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. You are the destroyer of the arrogance and the brilliance of everyone. You are the hidden secret of all lores, the cause of blessings for all.

## \|\| 11.23.29 \|\|

*tvattaḥ sarvaṃ ca tvaṃ sarvaṃ tvayi sarvaṃ girīśvara \|*  
*trāhi trāhi punastrāhi kṛpāṃ kuru mamopari \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O lord, everything originates from you. You are all. Everything is in you. Save us again Please be merciful on me.

## \|\| 11.23.30 \|\|

*athāsminnantare brahmā praṇipatya kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|*  
*evaṃ tvavasaraṃ prāpya vyajñāpayata śūline \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. In the meantime, getting the opportunity Brahmā bowed to him with palms joined in reverence and informed the trident-bearing lord.

## \|\| 11.23.31 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*jaya deva mahādeva praṇatārtivibhaṃjana \|*  
*īdṛśeṣvaparādheṣu ko 'nyastvattaḥ prasīdati \|\| 31 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

31\. O lord, be victorious. O destroyer of the distress of your devotees, who else other than you becomes pleased when offences are of this nature?

## \|\| 11.23.32 \|\|

*labdhamāno bhaviṣyaṃti ye purā nihitā mṛdhe \|*  
*pratyāpattirna kasya syātprasanne parameśvare \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Those who are killed in battle will regain their souls. When the lord is delighted who will not revive?

## \|\| 11.23.33 \|\|

*yadidaṃ devadevānāṃ kṛtamantuṣu dūṣaṇam \|*  
*tadidaṃ bhūṣaṇaṃ manyeta aṃgīkāragauravāt \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The fault in the offences committed by the gods, O lord, is actually a blessing because of the weightiness of your acceptance. I consider so.

## \|\| 11.23.34-35 \|\|

*iti vijñāpyamānastu brahmaṇā parameṣṭhinā \|*  
*vilokya vadanaṃ devyā devadevassmayanniva \|\| 34 \|\|*

*putrabhūtasya vātsalyādbrahmaṇaḥ padmajanmanaḥ \|*  
*devādīnāṃ yathāpūrvamaṃgāni pradadau prabhuḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. When Brahmā implored thus, the lord smiled and glanced at the face of the goddess. As a result of his affection to Brahmā who was like a son unto him, the lord revived the gods to life.

## \|\| 11.23.36 \|\|

*prathamādyaiśca yā devyo daṃḍitā devamātaraḥ \|*  
*tāsāmapi yathāpūrvāṇyaṃgāni giriśo dadau \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. He restored the goddesses—mothers of the gods who had been punished by the Pramathas and others.

## \|\| 11.23.37 \|\|

*dakṣasya bhagavāneva svayaṃ brahmā pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*tatpāpānuguṇaṃ cakre jaracchāgamukhaṃ mukham \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Lord Brahma made the face of Dakṣa look like the the face of an old goat as a befitting punishment for his sins.

## \|\| 11.23.38 \|\|

*so 'pi saṃjñāṃ tato labdhvā sa dṛṣṭvā jīvitaḥ sudhī \|*  
*bhītaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ śaṃbhuṃ tuṣṭāva pralapanbahu \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. He was resuscitated and endowed with good intellect. On seeing Śiva he was afraid. With palms joined in reverence he eulogised Śiva.

## \|\| 11.23.39 \|\|

*dakṣa uvāca \|*  
*jaya deva jagannātha lokānugrahakāraka \|*  
*kṛpāṃ kuru maheśānāparādhaṃ me kṣamasva ha \|\| 39 \|\|*

Dakṣa said:—

39\. O lord of the universe, O cause of the blessing for the worlds, O lord, be merciful. Forgive my guilt.

## \|\| 11.23.40 \|\|

*kartā bhartā ca hartā ca tvameva jagatāṃ prabho \|*  
*mayā jñātaṃ viśeṣeṇa viṣṇvādisakaleśvaraḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. You are the creator, protector and the annihilator of the worlds. This has been known by me particularly. You are the lord of Viṣṇu and all others.

## \|\| 11.23.41 \|\|

*tvayaiva vitataṃ sarvaṃ vyāptaṃ sṛṣṭaṃ na nāśitam \|*  
*na hi tvadadhikāḥ kecidīśāste 'cyutakādayaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Everything is spread and pervaded by you alone, created and destroyed by you alone. Viṣṇu and other lords are not superior to you.

## \|\| 11.23.42 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*taṃ tathā vyākulaṃ bhītaṃ pralapaṃtaṃ kṛtāgasam \|*  
*smayannivāvadatprekṣya mā bhairiti 1 ghṛṇānidhiḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

42\. The lord, the storehouse of mercy glanced at the guilty one who was emotionally distressed and smilingly said “Do not fear”.

## \|\| 11.23.43 \|\|

*tathoktvā brahmaṇastasya pituḥ priyacikīrṣayā \|*  
*gāṇapatyaṃ dadau tasmai dakṣāyākṣayamīśvaraḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Saying so and with a desire to please his father Brahmā, the lord bestowed on Dakṣa the imperishable chieftancy of the Gaṇas.

## \|\| 11.23.44 \|\|

*tato brahmādayo devā abhivaṃdya kṛta 2 ṃjaliḥ \|*  
*tuṣṭuvuḥ praśrayā vācā śaṃkaraṃ girijādhipam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Then Brahma and other gods saluted the lord with palms joined in reverence. In words of humility they eulogised the lord.

## \|\| 11.23.45 \|\|

*brahmādaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*jaya śaṃkara deveśa dīnānātha mahāprabho \|*  
*kṛpāṃ kuru maheśānāparādhaṃ no kṣamasva vai \|\| 45 \|\|*

Brahmā and others said:—

45\. O Śiva, O lord of the gods of the distressed and the helpless, O great lord, be merciful, forgive our guilt.

## \|\| 11.23.46 \|\|

*makhapāla makhādhīśa makhavidhvaṃsakāraka \|*  
*kṛpāṃ kuru maśānāparādhaṃ naḥ kṣamasva vai \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. O protector of sacrifices, O lord of sacrifices, O destroyer of sacrifices, O Maheśāna, forgive our guilt.

## \|\| 11.23.47 \|\|

*devadeva pareśāna bhaktaprāṇaprapoṣaka \|*  
*duṣṭadaṇḍaprada svāminkṛpāṃ kuru namo 'stu te \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. O lord of the gods, O great lord, O nourisher of the vital breath of your devotees, O lord, bestower of punishment on the wicked, be merciful. Obeisance be to you.

## \|\| 11.23.48 \|\|

*tvaṃ prabho garvahartā vai duṣṭānāṃ tvāmajānatām \|*  
*rakṣako hi viśeṣeṇa satāṃ tvatsaktacetasām \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. O lord, you remove the arrogance of the wicked who do not know you. You are the protector of the good whose minds are devoted to you.

## \|\| 11.23.49 \|\|

*adbhutaṃ caritaṃ te hi niścitaṃ kṛpayā tava \|*  
*sarvāparādhaḥ kṣaṃtavyo vibhavo dīnavatsalāḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Certainly due to your kindness your conduct is wonderful. O lord, forgive us for our fault. Lords are favourably disposed towards the distressed.

## \|\| 11.23.50 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*iti stuto mahādevo brahmādyairamaraiḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*sa bhaktavatsalassvāmī tutoṣa karuṇodadhiḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

50\. Thus eulogised by Brahmā and other gods lord Śiva, the ocean of mercy, favourably disposed towards the devotees was pleased.

## \|\| 11.23.51 \|\|

*cakārānugrahaṃ teṣāṃ brahmādīnāṃ divaukasām \|*  
*dadau narāṃśca suprītyā śaṃkaro dīnavatsalaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Śiva favourably disposed to the distressed blessed Brahmā and other gods and delightedly granted them boons.

## \|\| 11.23.52 \|\|

*sa ca tatastridaśāñcharaṇāgatān paramakāruṇikaḥ parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*anugatasmitalakṣaṇayā girā śamitasarvabhayaḥ samabhāṣata \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Then the merciful lord who made their fear subside addressed the gods who had sought refuge in him, with words characterised by smile.

## \|\| 11.23.53 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*yadidamāga ihācaritaṃ surairvidhiniyogavaśādiva yantritaiḥ \|*  
*śaraṇameva gatānavalokya vastadakhilaṃ kila vismṛtameva naḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

53\. On seeing you all seeking refuge in me your entire guilt and sin committed as if urged by fate, has been excused by us.

## \|\| 11.23.54 \|\|

*tadiha yūyamapi prakṛtaṃ manasyavigaṇayya vimardamapatrapāḥ \|*  
*hariviriṃcisurendramukhāssukhaṃ vrajata devapuraṃ prati saṃprati \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. O gods headed by Viṣṇu, Brahmā and Indra return happily to Devapura unmindful of the present suppression and without the sense of shame in your minds.

## \|\| 11.23.55 \|\|

*iti surānabhidhāya sureśvaro nikṛtadakṣakṛtakraturakratuḥ \|*  
*sagirijānucarassaparicchadaḥ sthita ivāmbaratontaradhāddharaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Saying this to the gods lord Śiva the destroyer of the sacrifice performed by Dakṣa, along with Śivā, his attendants and followers disappeared even as he stood in the firmament.

## \|\| 11.23.56 \|\|

*atha surā api te vigatavyathāḥ kathitabhadrasubhadraparākramāḥ \|*  
*sapadi khena sukhena yathāsukhaṃ yayuranekamukhāḥ maghavanmukhāḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The gods too returned through the aerial path, free from worries. Discussing about the heroic exploits of Bhadra, Indra and others went in different directions.

## Chapter 24 - Śiva’s sports on the Mandara mountain

## \|\| 11.24.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*antardhānagato devyā saha sānucaro haraḥ \|*  
*kva yātaḥ kutra vāsaḥ kiṃ kṛtvā virarāma ha \|\| 1 \|\|*

The sages said:—

1\. Where did Śiva who vanished along with the goddess and his attendants go? Where did he stay? What did he do and not do?

## \|\| 11.24.2 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*mahīdharavaraḥ śrīmānmaṃdaraścitrakaṃdaraḥ \|*  
*dayito devadevasya nivāsastapaso 'bhavat \|\| 2 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

2\. The excellent mountain Mandara with different caves became the pleasing spot of penance for lord Śiva.

## \|\| 11.24.3 \|\|

*tapo mahatkṛtaṃ tena voḍhuṃ svaśirasā śivau \|*  
*cireṇa labdhaṃ tatpādapaṃkajasparśajaṃ sukham \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. He had performed a great penance for the previlege to support Śiva and Śivā on his head. After a long time he felt the pleasure of contact with their lotus like feet.

## \|\| 11.24.4 \|\|

*tasya śailasya saundaryaṃ sahasravadanairapi \|*  
*na śakyaṃ vistarādvaktuṃ varṣakoṭiśatairapi \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The beauty of the mountain cannot be mentioned in detail by persons with thousand faces even in hundreds of crores of years.

## \|\| 11.24.5 \|\|

*śakyamapyasya saundaryaṃ na varṇayitumutsahe \|*  
*parvatāntarasaundaryaṃ sādhāraṇavidhāraṇāt \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Even if it is possible to describe I do not attempt to describe its beauty lest it should stand comparison with the other beautiful mountains.

## \|\| 11.24.6 \|\|

*idantu śakyate vaktumasminparvatasundare \|*  
*ṛddhyā kayāpi saundaryamīśvarāvāsayogyatā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. This is possible to mention that it has the beauty of being qualified to be the residence of the lord through some supernatural magnificence.

## \|\| 11.24.7 \|\|

*ata eva hi devena devyāḥ priyacikīrṣayā \|*  
*atīva ramaṇīyoyaṃ girirantaḥpurīkṛtaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. That was why the lord made this mountain as his harem with a desire to do what was pleasing to the goddess.

## \|\| 11.24.8 \|\|

*mekhalābhūmayastasya vimalopalapādapāḥ \|*  
*śivayornityasānnidhyānnyakkurvaṃtyakhilaṃjagat \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The slopes of the mountain abounding in rocks and trees humiliate the universe due to the perpetual presence of Śiva and Śivā.

## \|\| 11.24.9-10 \|\|

*pitṛbhyāṃ jagato nityaṃ snānapānopayogataḥ \|*  
*avāptapuṇyasaṃskāraḥ prasaradbhiritastataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*laghuśītalasaṃsparśairacchācchairnirjharāmbubhiḥ \|*  
*adhirājyena cādrīṇāmadrīreṣo 'bhiṣicyate \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. The mountain renders help to the parents of the worlds with light and clean waters of the streams cool to the touch for bath as well as drinking. Due to these merits he is coronated as the king of mountains with the very waters spreading here and there.

## \|\| 11.24.11 \|\|

*niśāsu śikharaprāntarvartinā sa śiloccayaḥ \|*  
*caṃdreṇācala sāmrājyacchatreṇeva virājate \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. During the nights when the moon remains at the outskirts of its peaks the mountain shines with the imperial umbrella in the form of the moon.

## \|\| 11.24.12 \|\|

*sa śailaścaṃcalībhūtairbālaiścāmarayoṣitām \|*  
*sarvaparvatasāmrājyacāmarairiva vījyate \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. When the tresses of the womenfolk of the gods shake, he appears as being fanned by the chowries signifying his Emperorship.

## \|\| 11.24.13 \|\|

*prātarabhyudite bhānau bhūdharo ratnabhūṣitaḥ \|*  
*darpaṇe dehasaubhāgyaṃ draṣṭukāma iva sthitaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. In the morning when the sun rises, the mountain embellished with jewels and gems appears to be eager for observing the beauty of his body in a mirror.

## \|\| 11.24.14-15 \|\|

*kūjadvihaṃgavācālairvātoddhṛtalatābhujaiḥ \|*  
*vimuktapuṣpaiḥ satataṃ vyālambimṛdupallavaiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*latāpratānajaṭilaistarubhistapasairiva \|*  
*jayāśiṣā sahābhyarcya niṣevyata ivādrirāṭ \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. This king of mountains appears to be honoured with benedictions of victory by the trees that seem to be sages with the twining growths of creepers for the matted hair; through the chirping of vociferous birds, by extending their arms in the form of creepers shaken by the breeze and shedding flowers and tender sprouts.

## \|\| 11.24.16-19 \|\|

*adhomukhairūrdhvamukhaiśśṛṃgaistiryaṅmukhaistathā \|*  
*prapatanniva pātāle bhūpṛṣṭhādutpatanniva \|\| 16 \|\|*

*parītaḥ sarvato dikṣu bhramanniva vihāyasi \|*  
*paśyanniva jagatsarvaṃ nṛtyanniva nirantaram \|\| 17 \|\|*

*guhāmukhaiḥ pratidinaṃ vyāttāsyo vipulodaraiḥ \|*  
*ajīrṇalāvaṇyatayā jṛṃbhamāṇa ivācalaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*grasanniva jagatsarvaṃ pibanniva payonidhim \|*  
*vamanniva tamontasthaṃ mādyanniva khamambudaiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

16-19. With the various peaks some facing down, some shooting up and some projecting sideways he appears to jump into the nether worlds, jump up from the ground, fly through the sky in all directions. Through the vast caves he appears to have kept his mouth gaping. He appears to see the universe and dance continuously. His beauty never fades nor wears out. He appears to stretch himself to devour the universe, to drink the ocean; to vomit the darkness within and to cover up the sky with clouds.

## \|\| 11.24.20 \|\|

*nivāsa bhūmayastāstā darpaṇapratimodarāḥ \|*  
*tiraskṛtātapāssnigdhāśramacchāyāmahīruhāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The different abodes have mirror-like surface. The tall shady trees in the hermitages set the blazing sunshine at nought.

## \|\| 11.24.21 \|\|

*saritsarastaḍāgādisaṃparkaśiśirānilāḥ \|*  
*tatra tatra niṣaṇṇābhyāṃ śivābhyāṃ saphalīkṛtāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The breezes made cool by their contact with the rivers, tanks and lakes are rendered fruitful by Śiva and Śivā who roam here and there and enjoy them.

## \|\| 11.24.22 \|\|

*tamimaṃ sarvataḥ śreṣṭhaṃ smṛtvā sāmbastriyambakaḥ \|*  
*raibhyāśramasamīpasthaścāntardhānaṃ gato yayau \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. It was to this excellent mountain that Śiva accompanied by Śivā while staying in the hermitage of Raibhya was attracted and proceeded.

## \|\| 11.24.23 \|\|

*tatrodyānamanuprāpya devyā saha maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*rarāma ramaṇīyāsu devyāntaḥpurabhūmiṣu \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Reaching the garden there along with the goddess, lord Śiva sported about in the divine harem grounds.

## \|\| 11.24.24 \|\|

*tathā gateṣu kāleṣu pravṛddhāsu prajāsu ca \|*  
*daityau śuṃbhaniśuṃbhākhyau bhrātarau saṃbabhūvatuḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. As time elapsed and population increased, two demons were born. They were two brothers Śumbha and Niśumbha.

## \|\| 11.24.25 \|\|

*tābhyāṃ tapo balāddattaṃ brahmaṇā parameṣṭinā \|*  
*avadhyatvaṃ jagatyasminpuruṣairakhilairapi \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. As a result of the power of their penance Brahmā granted them the boon that they would not be killed by any man in the universe.

## \|\| 11.24.26-27 \|\|

*ayonijā tu yā kanyā hyaṃbikāṃśasamudbhavā \|*  
*ajātapuṃsparśaratiravilaṃghyaparākramā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tayā tu nau vadhaḥ saṃkhye tasyāṃ kāmābhibhūtayoḥ \|*  
*iti cābhyarthito brahmā tābhyāmprāha tathāstviti \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. Brahmā was requested by them thus—“Our death may take place in a battle with the lady with whom we fall passionately in love. She shall be a virgin born of Śiva’s part, not from any womb. She should not have experienced the sexual contact with any man. Her exploit shall be unthwartable.” Brahmā had consented to their request.

## \|\| 11.24.28 \|\|

*tataḥ prabhṛti śakrādīnvijitya samare surān \|*  
*niḥsvādhyāyavaṣaṭkāraṃ jagaccakraturakramāt \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Ever since, the two demons wrought havoc in the universe. They defeated Indra and other gods in war. They abolished the study of the Vedas and offering to the gods.

## \|\| 11.24.29-30 \|\|

*tayorvadhāya deveśaṃ brahmābhyarthitavānpunaḥ \|*  
*viniṃdyāpi rahasyaṃ vāṃ krodhayitvā yathā tathā \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tadvarṇakośajāṃ śaktimakāmāṃ kanyakātmikām \|*  
*niśumbhaśuṃbhayorhaṃtrīṃ surebhyo dātumarhasi \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. Then Brahmā requested Śiva, the lord of the gods for killing them—“It behoves you to bestow on the gods the goddess who will kill Śumbha and Niśumbha. She shall be the Śakti born of the sheath of Śiva’s colour. She shall be in the form of a virgin devoid of passion. By rebuking her secretly or by infuriating her this shall be arranged.

## \|\| 11.24.31-32 \|\|

*evamabhyarthito dhātrā bhagavānnīlalohitaḥ \|*  
*kālītyāha rahasyaṃ vāṃ nindayanniva sasmitaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tataḥ kruddhā tadā devī suvarṇā varṇakāraṇāt \|*  
*smayantī cāha bhartāramasamādheyayā girā \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. Thus requested by Brahmā, the lord Nīlalohita called Kālī in secret outwardly rebuking her while smiling within. The goddess Kālī was angry by her allusion to the colour. Derisively and forcibly she spoke to her husband thus.

## \|\| 11.24.33 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*īdṛśo mama varṇesminna ratirbhavato 'sti cet \|*  
*evāvantaṃ ciraṃ kālaṃ kathameṣā niyamyate \|\| 33 \|\|*

The goddess said:—

33\. “If my lord has no pleasure in my complexion how is it that I have been held up here so long.

## \|\| 11.24.34 \|\|

*aratyā vartamāno 'pi kathaṃ ca ramase mayā \|*  
*na hyaśakyaṃ jagatyasminnīśvarasya jagatprabhoḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. If you are displeased with me why do you spoil with me? There is nothing in this universe which is unachievable for my lord, the lord of the universe.

## \|\| 11.24.35 \|\|

*svātmārāmasya bhavato ratirna sukhasādhanam \|*  
*iti hetoḥ smaro yasmātprasabhaṃ bhasmasātkṛtaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. To my lord taking delight in the soul, happiness is not derivable from sexual indulgence; for the very reason Kāma was reduced to ashes.

## \|\| 11.24.36 \|\|

*yā ca nābhimatā bharturapi sarvāṃgasundarī \|*  
*sā vṛthaiva hi jāyeta sarvairapi guṇāntaraiḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The life of the lady most beautiful in limbs is in vain though she may possess all other qualities if her husband is not delighted with her.

## \|\| 11.24.37 \|\|

*bharturbhogaikaśeṣo hi sarga evaiṣa yoṣitām \|*  
*tathāsatyanyathābhūtā nārī kutropayujyate \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The creation of women rests solely in the enjoyment of her husband. That being the case, where can a woman who is contrary to that be used?

## \|\| 11.24.38 \|\|

*tasmādvarṇamimaṃ tyaktvā tvayā rahasi ninditam \|*  
*varṇāntaraṃ bhajiṣye vā na bhajiṣyāmi vā svayam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Hence, eschewing this colour censured by you in secret I shall attain another colour or I shall cease to exist myself.”

## \|\| 11.24.39 \|\|

*ityuktvotthāya śayanāddevī sācaṣṭa gadgadam \|*  
*yayāce 'numatiṃ bhartustapase kṛtaniścayā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. After saying this she stood up from the bed. Bent upon penance she requested for the permission of her lord in words choked with emotion.

## \|\| 11.24.40 \|\|

*tathā praṇayabhaṃgena bhīto bhūtapatiḥ svayam \|*  
*pādayoḥ praṇamanneva bhavānīṃ pratyabhāṣata \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Then lord Śiva, afraid of a rupture in love, replied to her falling at her feet.

## \|\| 11.24.41 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*ajānatī ca krīḍoktiṃ priye kiṃ kupitāsi me \|*  
*ratiḥ kuto vā jāyeta tvattaścedaratirmama \|\| 41 \|\|*

Lord Śiva said:—

41\. “O beloved, why are you angry with me, not knowing that this was only a jocular remark of mine. If I am not delighted with you, where else can I seek delight?

## \|\| 11.24.42 \|\|

*mātā tvamasya jagataḥ pitāhamadhipastathā \|*  
*kathaṃ tadutpapadyeta tvatto nābhiratirmama \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. If I am not delighted with you how can it be proper since you are mother of this universe and I am its father and lord?

## \|\| 11.24.43 \|\|

*āvayorabhikāmo 'pi kimasau kāmakāritaḥ \|*  
*yataḥ kāmasamutpattiḥ prāgeva jagadudbhavaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Is our mutual love generated by Kāma? Even before the birth of Kāma the universe existed.

## \|\| 11.24.44 \|\|

*pṛthagjanānāṃ rataye kāmātmā kalpito mayā \|*  
*tataḥ kathamupālabdhaḥ kāmadāhādahaṃ tvayā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The deity Kāma was formulated by me for the sexual pleasure of men and women. Then why did you taunt me for having burnt Kāma?

## \|\| 11.24.45 \|\|

*māṃ vai tridaśasāmānyaṃ manyamāno manobhavaḥ \|*  
*manākparibhavaṃ kurvanmayā vai bhasmasātkṛtaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The mind-born Kāma considered me on a par with the gods. While he attempted to tease me I reduced him to ashes.

## \|\| 11.24.46 \|\|

*vihāropyāvayorasya jagatastrāṇakāraṇāt \|*  
*tatastadarthaṃ tvayyadya krīḍoktiṃ kṛtavāhanam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Even our sport and pastime is meant for the universe. For that very purpose I have made this jocular remark.

## \|\| 11.24.47 \|\|

*sa cāyamacirādarthastavaivāviṣkariṣyate \|*  
*krodhasya janakaṃ vākyaṃ hṛdi kṛtvedamabravīt \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. That purpose ere long will be revealed to you.” On hearing this the goddess, remembered the remark that caused her annoyance and said.

## \|\| 11.24.48 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*śrutapūrvaṃ hi bhagavaṃstava cāṭu vaco mayā \|*  
*yenaivamatidhīrāhamapi prāgabhivaṃcitā \|\| 48 \|\|*

The goddess said:—

48\. O lord, your jocular remarks I have heard before whereby I have been deceived though I am very bold.

## \|\| 11.24.49 \|\|

*prāṇānapyapriyā bharturnārī yā na parityajet \|*  
*kulāṃganā śubhā sadbhiḥ kutsitaiva hi gamyate \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Even an auspicious lady of a noble family who does not abandon her life incurs the displeasure of her husband and is held despicable by good men.

## \|\| 11.24.50 \|\|

*bhūyasī ca tavāprītiragauramiti me vapuḥ \|*  
*krīḍoktirapi kālīti ghaṭate kathamanyathā \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Your displeasure is very great because I am not fair. How is the remark “Kālī” relevant otherwise though it be a jocular remark?

## \|\| 11.24.51 \|\|

*sadbhirvigarhitaṃ tasmāttava kārṣṇyamasaṃmatam \|*  
*anutsṛjya tapoyogātsthātumeveha notsahe \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Dark complexion is hated by good men. You too disapprove of it. Without wiping it off by dint of penance I am not inclined to stay here.

## \|\| 11.24.52 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*sa yadyevaṃvidhatāpaste tapasā kiṃ prayojanam \|*  
*mamecchayā svecchayā vā varṇāntaravatī bhava \|\| 52 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

52\. If your distress is such, of what avail is penance? You can assume any other colour at my will or at your choice.

## \|\| 11.24.53 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*necchāmi bhavato varṇaṃ svayaṃ vā kartumanyathā \|*  
*brahmāṇaṃ tapasārādhya kṣipraṃ gaurī bhavāmyaham \|\| 53 \|\|*

The goddess said:—

53\. I do not wish to have any other colour either at your will or at my choice. I shall propitiate Brahmā by penance and become Gaurī.

## \|\| 11.24.54 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca \|*  
*matprasādātpurā brahmā brahmatvaṃ prāptavānpurā \|*  
*tamāhūya mahādevi tapasā kiṃ kariṣyasi \|\| 54 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

54\. O goddess, Brahmā attained his status formerly by my grace. What will you do by invoking him through your penance?

## \|\| 11.24.55-56 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*tvatto labdhapadā eva sarve brahmādayaḥ surāḥ \|*  
*tathāpyārādhya tapasā brahmāṇaṃ tvanniyogataḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*purā kila satī nāmnā dakṣasya duhitā 'bhavam \|*  
*jagatāṃ patimevaṃ tvāṃ patiṃ prāptavatī tathā \|\| 56 \|\|*

The goddess said:—

55-56. True that Brahmā and other gods acquired their status only from you. Still at your bidding I propitiated Brahmā formerly and in the name of Satī I became Dakṣa’s daughter and attained you, the lord of the worlds, as my husband.

## \|\| 11.24.57 \|\|

*evamadyāpi tapasā toṣayitvā dvijaṃ vidhim \|*  
*gaurī bhavitumicchāmi ko doṣaḥ kathyatāmiha \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. So now also by propitiating him by penance I wish to become Gaurī. What is the harm therein?

## \|\| 11.24.58 \|\|

*evamukto mahādevyā vāmadevaḥ smayanniva \|*  
*na tāṃ nirbaṃdhayāmāsa devakāryacikīrṣayā \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Thus replied to by the goddess, Śiva did not insist on his point as he desired to carry out the task of the gods.

## Chapter 25 - The goddess (devī) attains fair complexion

## \|\| 11.25.1 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*tataḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya patimambā pativratā \|*  
*niyamya ca viyogārtiṃ jagāma himavadgirim \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

1\. Then circumambulating the lord and restraining the pangs of separation she went to the mountain Himavat.

## \|\| 11.25.2 \|\|

*tapaḥkṛtavatī pūrvaṃ deśe yasminsakhījanaiḥ \|*  
*tameva deśamavṛnottapase praṇayātpunaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Out of love she selected the same spot for her penance where she had formerly performed the same along with her friends.

## \|\| 11.25.3-7 \|\|

*tataḥ svapitaraṃ dṛṣṭvā mātaraṃ ca tayorgṛhe \|*  
*praṇamya vṛttaṃ vijñāpya tābhyāṃ cānumatā satī \|\| 3 \|\|*

*punastapovanaṃ gatvā bhūṣaṇāni visṛjya ca \|*  
*snātvā tapasvino veṣaṃ kṛtvā paramapāvanam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*saṃkalpya ca mahātīvraṃ tapaḥ paramaduścaram \|*  
*sadā manasi sandhāya bhartuścaraṇapaṃkajam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tameva kṣaṇike liṃge dhyātvā bāhyavidhānataḥ \|*  
*trisandhyamabhyarcayantī vanyaiḥ puṣpaiḥ phalādibhiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*sa eva brahmaṇo mūrtimāsthāya tapasaḥ phalam \|*  
*pradāsyati mametyevaṃ nityaṃ kṛtvā 'karottapaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

3-7. She visited her parents at their house and bowed to them. Informing them of her intention and securing their permission she went to the penance-grove and discarded her ornaments. She took her bath and assumed the holy dress and features of ascetics. She performed the very difficult penance. She meditated upon the lotus-like feet of her lord. She conceived the same in Śiva’s external phallic emblem in accordance with the injunctions. In the three junctions of time every day she worshipped the same with the flowers and fruits of the forest. Thinking thus—“He alone, after assuming the form of Brahmā, will grant me the fruit of this penance”, she conducted the penance.

## \|\| 11.25.8 \|\|

*tathā tapaścarantīṃ tāṃ kāle bahutithe gate \|*  
*dṛṣṭaḥ kaścinmahāvyāghro duṣṭabhāvādupāgamat \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. After some time had elapsed, seeing her performing the penance a huge tiger approached her with wicked intention.

## \|\| 11.25.9 \|\|

*tathaivopagatasyāpi tasyātīvadurātmanaḥ \|*  
*gātraṃ citrārpitamiva stabdhaṃ tasyāssakāśataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The body of that animal of wicked soul became stiff and benumbed when he approached her.

## \|\| 11.25.10 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvāpi tathā vyāghraṃ duṣṭabhāvādupāgatam \|*  
*na pṛthagjanavaddevī svabhāvena vivicyate \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Even after seeing the tiger that approached her with wicked intention the goddess (devī) did not turn away from her pious thoughts like ordinary people.

## \|\| 11.25.11-12 \|\|

*sa tu viṣṭabdhasarvāṃgo bubhukṣāparipīḍitaḥ \|*  
*mamāmiṣaṃ tato nānyaditi matvā nirantaram \|\| 11 \|\|*

*nirīkṣyamāṇaḥ satataṃ devīmeva tadā 'niśam \|*  
*atiṣṭhadagratastasyā upāsanamivācarat \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. The animal with his body stunned and overwhelmed with hunger, stood there in front of her glancing perpetually at the goddess and thought, “My prey is nothing else.” Virtually this became his cherished goal.

## \|\| 11.25.13 \|\|

*devyāśca hṛdaye nityaṃ mamaivāyamupāsakaḥ \|*  
*trātā ca duṣṭasattvebhya iti pravavṛte kṛpā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Mercy was generated in the heart of the goddess who thought, “He is the perpetual performer of contemplation on me and my protector from the wicked animals.”

## \|\| 11.25.14 \|\|

*tasyā eva kṛpā yogātsadyonaṣṭamalatrayaḥ \|*  
*babhūva sahasā vyāghro devīṃ ca bubudhe tadā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. By this feeling of mercy the threefold dirt of the tiger perished and he realised the goddess.

## \|\| 11.25.15 \|\|

*nyavartata bubhukṣā ca tasyāṃgastambhanaṃ tathā \|*  
*daurātmyaṃ janmasiddhaṃ ca tṛptiśca samajāyata \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. His hunger receded. The benumbed stiffness subsided. His congenital wickedness disappeared. Contentment set in.

## \|\| 11.25.16 \|\|

*tadā paramabhāvena jñātvā kārtārthyamātmanaḥ \|*  
*sadyopāsaka evaiṣa siṣeve parameśvarīm \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Realising his contentment with great piety he waited upon the goddess as a sudden devotee.

## \|\| 11.25.17 \|\|

*duṣṭānāmapi sattvānāṃ tathānyeṣāndurātmanām \|*  
*sa eva drāvako bhūtvā vicacāra tapovane \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. He roamed about the penance-grove as a router of wicked animals and wicked souls.

## \|\| 11.25.18 \|\|

*tapaśca vavṛdhe devyāstīvraṃ tīvratarātmakam \|*  
*devāśca daityanirbandhādbrahmāṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The penance of the goddess increased and became gradually acute. Meanwhile the gods sought refuge in Brahma due to the pressure of the Daityas.

## \|\| 11.25.19 \|\|

*cakrurnivedanaṃ devāḥ svaduḥkhasyāripīḍanāt \|*  
*yathā ca dadatuḥ śumbhaniśumbhau varasammadāt \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The gods submitted to him how Śumbha and Niśumbha inflicted pain on them due to their strength derived from the boons.

## \|\| 11.25.20-21 \|\|

*so 'pi śrutvā vidhirduḥkhaṃ surāṇāṃ kṛpayānvitaḥ \|*  
*āsīddaityavadhāyaiva smṛtvā hetvāśrayāṃ kathām \|\| 20 \|\|*

*sāmaraḥ prārthito brahmā yayau devyāstapovanam \|*  
*saṃsmaranmanasā devaduḥkhamokṣaṃ svayatnataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. On hearing the distress of the gods Brahma grew merciful. He knew how Daityas could be destroyed. On being requested he went to the penance-grove of the goddess along with the gods reflecting in his mind that the liberation of the gods from misery could be achieved through his effort.

## \|\| 11.25.22-23 \|\|

*dadarśa ca suraśreṣṭhaḥ śreṣṭhe tapasi niṣṭhitām \|*  
*pratiṣṭhāmiva viśvasya bhavānīṃ parameśvarīm \|\| 22 \|\|*

*nanāma cāsya jagato mātaraṃ svasya vai hareḥ \|*  
*rudrasya ca piturbhāryāmāryāmadrīśvarātmajām \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. Brahmā saw the goddess, the mother of this universe, the mother of Trinity, the daughter of the lord of mountains, the foundation of the universe, firmly engaged in penance. On seeing her he was delighted.

## \|\| 11.25.24 \|\|

*brahmāṇamāgataṃ dṛṣṭvā devī devagaṇaiḥ saha \|*  
*arghyaṃ tadarhaṃ dattvā 'smai svāgatādyairupācarat \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. On seeing that Brahmā had come along with the gods, the goddess offered him Arghya and received him with words of welcome.

## \|\| 11.25.25 \|\|

*tāṃ ca pratyupacāroktiṃ puraskṛtyābhinaṃdya ca \|*  
*papraccha tapaso hetumajānanniva padmajaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Replying suitably and congratulating her the lotus-born Brahmā asked her the purpose of her penance as though he did not know.

## \|\| 11.25.26 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*tīvreṇa tapasānena devyā kimiha sādhyate \|*  
*tapaḥphalānāṃ sarveṣāṃ tvadadhīnā hi siddhayaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

26\. What is being striven for, O goddess, by means of this penance? The benefits of penances are under your control.

## \|\| 11.25.27 \|\|

*yaścaiva jagatāṃ bhartā tameva parameśvaram \|*  
*bhartāramātmanā prāpya prāptañca tapasaḥ phalam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The fruit of the penance has been obtained by you in having obtained lord Śiva as your husband, who alone is the lord of all worlds.

## \|\| 11.25.28 \|\|

*athavā sarvamevaitatkrīḍāvilasitaṃ tava \|*  
*idantu citraṃ devasya virahaṃ sahase katham \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Or all this is only a form of your divine sport. But this is surprising how you can bear separation from the lord.

## \|\| 11.25.29 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*sargādau bhavato devādutpattiḥ śrūyate yadā \|*  
*tadā prajānāṃ prathamastvaṃ me prathamajaḥ sutaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

The Goddess (devī) said:—

29\. When at the beginning of creation as mentioned in the Vedas you are born of lord Śiva you are the first of my creation, my first-born son.

## \|\| 11.25.30 \|\|

*yadā punaḥ prajāvṛddhyai lalāṭādbhavato bhavaḥ \|*  
*utpanno 'bhūttadā tvaṃ me guruḥ śvaśurabhāvataḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. When for multiplying the subjects, Śiva was born of your forehead you became my father-in-law and so elder to me.

## \|\| 11.25.31 \|\|

*yadā bhavadgirīndraste putro mama pitā svayam \|*  
*tadā pitāmahastvaṃ me jāto lokapitāmaha \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. When the lord of mountains, my father became your son you became my grandfather, O grandfather of the worlds!

## \|\| 11.25.32 \|\|

*tadīdṛśasya bhavato lokayātrāvidhāyinaḥ \|*  
*vṛttavantaḥpure bhartā kathayiṣye kathaṃ punaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. How can I inform you, the arranger of worldly existence what happened at the harem with my husband?

## \|\| 11.25.33 \|\|

*kimatra bahunā dehe yaścāyaṃ mama kālimā \|*  
*tyaktvā sattvavidhānena gaurī bhavitumutsahe \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Of what avail is this talk? I wish to get rid of my dark complexion through legitimate remedies and obtain white colour.

## \|\| 11.25.34 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*etāvatā kimarthena tīvraṃ devi tapaḥ kṛtam \|*  
*svecchaiva kimaparyāptā krīḍeyaṃ hi tavedṛśī \|\| 34 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

34\. O goddess, why did you perform a severe penance for this purpose? Was not your wish alone sufficient for that? Indeed this is only your sport

## \|\| 11.25.35 \|\|

*krīḍā 'pi ca jaganmātastava lokahitāya vai \|*  
*ato mameṣṭamanayā phalaṃ kimapi sādhyatām \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. O mother of the universe, your play too benefits the worlds. Hence some benefit pleasing to me may be sought through it.

## \|\| 11.25.36 \|\|

*niśuṃbhaśuṃbhanāmānau daityau dattavarau mayā \|*  
*dṛptau devānprabādhete tvatto labdhastayorvadhaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Two Daityas, Śumbha and Niśumbha to whom I had granted boons have turned arrogant. They are harassing the gods. Their destruction is only through you.

## \|\| 11.25.37 \|\|

*alaṃ vilaṃbanenātra tvaṃ kṣaṇena sthirā bhava \|*  
*śaktirvisṛjyamānā 'dya tayormṛtyurbhaviṣyati \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Do not delay. For a short while be steady. The Śakti that is to be released now shall be their death.

## \|\| 11.25.38 \|\|

*brāhmaṇābhyarthitā caiva devī girivarātmajā \|*  
*tvakkośaṃ sahasotsṛjya gaurī sā samajāyata \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Thus requested by Brahmā, the goddess, daughter of the mountain, cast off her outer skin and became white.

## \|\| 11.25.39 \|\|

*sā tvakkośātmanotsṛṣṭā kauśikī nāma nāmataḥ \|*  
*kālī kālāmbudaprakhyā kanyakā samapadyata \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The outer sheath thus cast off became Kauśikī who is known as Kālī, the virgin with the lustre of’ the black cloud.

## \|\| 11.25.40 \|\|

*sā tu māyātmikā śaktiryoganidrā ca vaiṣṇavī \|*  
*śaṃkhacakratriśūlādisāyudhāṣṭamahābhujā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. She is the Śakti in the form of Māyā, the Yogic slumber of Viṣṇu. She held the weapons, conch, discus, trident in her eight great arms.

## \|\| 11.25.41 \|\|

*saumyā ghorā ca miśrā ca trinetrā candraśekharā \|*  
*ajātapuṃsparśaratiradhṛṣyā cātisundarī \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. She had three traits: gentle, terrible and a mixture of the two. She had three eyes. She was moon-crested. She had not experienced the sexual contact of any man. She was invincible and beautiful.

## \|\| 11.25.42 \|\|

*dattā ca brahmaṇe devyā śaktireṣā sanātanī \|*  
*niśuṃbhasya ca śuṃbhasya nihaṃtrī daityasiṃhayoḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. This eternal Śakti was given to Brahmā by the goddess (devī) as the would-be destroyer of Śumbha and Niśumbha, the leonine Daityas.

## \|\| 11.25.43 \|\|

*brahmaṇāpi prahṛṣṭena tasyai paramaśaktaye \|*  
*prabalaḥ kesarī datto vāhanatve samāgataḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. A very powerful lion that came there, was given to her as vehicle by the delighted Brahmā.

## \|\| 11.25.44 \|\|

*vindhye ca vasatiṃ tasyāḥ pūjāmāsavapūrvakaiḥ \|*  
*māṃsairmatsyairapūpaiśca nirvartyāsau samādiśat \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. He fixed her abode on the Vindhya mountain. He ordained her worship by the gift of meat, fish, pies and wine.

## \|\| 11.25.45-46 \|\|

*sā caiva saṃmatā śaktirbrahmaṇo viśvakarmaṇaḥ \|*  
*praṇamya mātaraṃ gaurīṃ brahmāṇaṃ cānupūrvaśaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*śaktibhiścāpi tulyābhiḥ svātmajābhiranekaśaḥ \|*  
*parītā prayayau vindhyaṃ daityendrau hantumudyatā \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. That Śakti, approved of by Brahmā, the creator of the universe, bowed to her mother Gaurī and Brahmā in due order. Surrounded by many Śaktis equal to her and born of her she proceeded to the Vindhya ready to slay the leading Daityas.

## \|\| 11.25.47-48 \|\|

*nihatau ca tayā tatra samare daityapuṃgavau \|*  
*tadbāṇaiḥ kāmabāṇaiśca cchinnabhinnāṃgamānasau \|\| 47 \|\|*

*tadyuddhavistaraścātra na kṛto 'nyatra varṇanāt \|*  
*ūhanīyaṃ parasmācca prastutaṃ varṇayāmi vaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. The leading Daityas were killed by her in battle, the Daityas whom the arrows of Kāma pierced in the minds and her own arrows split and pierced in the bodies. That battle is not described here as it has been described elsewhere. It can be guessed through other sources as well. I shall resume the present description.

## Chapter 26 - The attainment of higher status by the tiger (vyāghra)

## \|\| 11.26.1 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*utpādya kauśikīṃ gaurī brahmaṇe pratipādya tām \|*  
*tasya pratyupakārāya pitāmahamathābravīt \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

1\. After creating Kauśikī and handing her over to Brahmā, Gaurī spoke to Brahmā demanding the recompense.

## \|\| 11.26.2 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*dṛṣṭaḥ kimeṣa bhavatā śārdūlo madupāśrayaḥ \|*  
*anena duṣṭasattvebhyo rakṣitaṃ mattapovanam \|\| 2 \|\|*

The goddess said:—

2\. Is this tiger that has resorted to me seen by you? He has guarded my penance grove from wicked animals.

## \|\| 11.26.3 \|\|

*mayyarpitamanā eṣa bhajate māmananyadhīḥ \|*  
*asya saṃrakṣaṇādanyatpriyaṃ mama na vidyate \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Dedicating his mind to me he worships me without thinking of anything else. There is nothing more pleasing to me than his protection.

## \|\| 11.26.4 \|\|

*bhavitavyamanenāto mamāntaḥpuracāriṇā \|*  
*gaṇeśvarapadaṃ cāsmai prītyā dāsyati śaṃkaraḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He shall be appointed as an official in my harem. Out of pleasure Śiva will grant him the post of Ganeśvara.

## \|\| 11.26.5 \|\|

*enamagresaraṃ kṛtvā sakhībhirgantumutsahe \|*  
*pradīyatāmanujñā me prajānāṃ patinā 1 tvayā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. I wish to return with my friends keeping him ahead. I seek permission from you the lord of the subjects.

## \|\| 11.26.6 \|\|

*ityuktaḥ prahasanbrahmā devīmmugdhāmiva smayan \|*  
*tasya tīvraiḥ purāvṛttairdaurātmyaṃ samavarṇayat1 \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Thus addressed, Brahmā smiled and told the goddess describing the lion’s wicked antecedents as though the goddess was unaware.

## \|\| 11.26.7 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*paśau devi mṛgāḥ krūrāḥ kva ca te 'nugrahaḥ śubhaḥ \|*  
*āśīviṣamukhe sākṣādamṛtaṃ kiṃ niṣicyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

7\. O Goddess, animals are cruel. How can your blissful thought be directed to these? Why do you sprinkle nectar in the mouth of the serpent?

## \|\| 11.26.8 \|\|

*vyāghramātreṇa sanneṣa duṣṭaḥ ko 'pi niśācaraḥ \|*  
*anena bhakṣitā gāvo brāhmaṇāśca tapodhanāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. This is a certain night-prowling wicked demon in the garb of a tiger (vyāghra). Cows, Brahmins and saints have been devoured by him.

## \|\| 11.26.9 \|\|

*tarpayaṃstānyathākāmaṃ kāmarūpī caratyasau \|*  
*avaśyaṃ khalu bhoktavyaṃ phalaṃ pāpasya karmaṇaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. He is roaming about assuming forms as he pleases, pleasing and propitiating them. The fruit of a sinful action must of necessity be reaped by him.

## \|\| 11.26.10 \|\|

*ataḥ kiṃ kṛpayā kṛtyamīdṛśeṣu durātmasu \|*  
*anena devyāḥ kiṃ kṛtyaṃ prakṛtyā kaluṣātmanā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Why shall mercy be shown to wicked souls like this? What is the purpose served by one innately sinful?

## \|\| 11.26.11 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*yaduktaṃ bhavatā sarvaṃ tathyamastvayamīdṛśaḥ \|*  
*tathāpi māṃ prapanno 'bhūnna tyājyo māmupāśritaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

The goddess said:—

11\. What you have said is entirely true. Let him be like this. Still he has resorted to me. One who has sought refuge in me shall not be abandoned.

## \|\| 11.26.12 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*asya bhaktimavijñāya prāgvṛttaṃ te niveditam \|*  
*bhaktiścedasya kiṃ pāpairna te bhaktaḥ praṇaśyati \|\| 12 \|\|*

Brahmā said:—

12\. I narrated his antecedents without realising his devotion. If there be devotion, sins are not effective? Your devotee never perishes.

## \|\| 11.26.13 \|\|

*puṇyakarmāpi kiṃ kuryāttvadīyājñānapekṣayā \|*  
*ajā prajñā purāṇī ca tvameva parameśvarī \|\| 13 \|\|*
