13\. What can a man of virtuous rites achieve without depending on your behest? You alone are the unborn, intelligent, ancient goddess.

## \|\| 11.26.14 \|\|

*tvadadhīnā hi sarveṣāṃ baṃdhamokṣavyavasthitiḥ \|*  
*tvadṛte paramā śaktiḥ saṃsiddhiḥ kasya karmaṇā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Bondage and liberation depend on you. There is no greater Śakti than you. Without you rites cannot achieve results.

## \|\| 11.26.15 \|\|

*tvameva vividhā śaktiḥ bhavānāmatha vā svayam \|*  
*aśaktaḥ karmakaraṇe kartā vā kiṃ kariṣyati \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. You alone constitute Śakti of living beings. Himself incompetent to do anything what will a mere agent do?

## \|\| 11.26.16 \|\|

*viṣṇośca mama cānyeṣāṃ devadānavarakṣasām \|*  
*tattadaiśvaryasamprāptyai tavaivājñā hi kāraṇam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. It is only your behest that is the cause of acquisition of prosperity and glory by Viṣṇu, by me or by any of these—gods, Dānavas or Rākṣasas.

## \|\| 11.26.17 \|\|

*atītāḥ khalvasaṃkhyātā brahmāṇo harayo bhavāḥ \|*  
*anāgatāstvasaṃkhyātāstvadājñānuvidhāyinaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Innumerable Brahmās, Viṣṇus and Śivas have passed by. Such innumerable ones are yet to be born, these carry out your behests.

## \|\| 11.26.18 \|\|

*tvāmanārādhya deveśi puruṣārthacatuṣṭayam \|*  
*labdhuṃ na śakyamasmābhirapi sarvaiḥ surottamaiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O goddess of the gods without propitiating you the fourfold arms of life cannot be acquired by all of us.

## \|\| 11.26.19 \|\|

*vyatyāso 'pi bhavetsadyo brahmatvasthāvaratvayoḥ \|*  
*sukṛtaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ cāpi tvayeva sthāpitaṃ yataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Since merit and evil have been established by you the mobile and immobile may even be inter-changed.

## \|\| 11.26.20 \|\|

*tvaṃ hi sarvajagadbhartuśśivasya paramātmanaḥ \|*  
*anādimadhyanidhanā śaktirādyā sanātanī \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. You are the primordial and eternal Śakti of Śiva the great soul, the lord of the universe, the Śakti without beginning, middle or death.

## \|\| 11.26.21 \|\|

*samastalokayātrārthaṃ mūrtimāviśya kāmapi \|*  
*krīḍase 2 vividhairbhāvaiḥ kastvāṃ jānāti tattvataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. For the functioning of the universe you assume some form or other and play about in different aspects. Who knows you factually?

## \|\| 11.26.22 \|\|

*ato duṣkṛtakarmāpi vyāghro 'yaṃ tvadanugrahāt \|*  
*prāpnotu paramāṃ siddhimatra kaḥ pratibandhakaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Hence let this wicked tiger (vyāghra) too attain the great Siddhi by your blessings. Nothing can prevent it?”

## \|\| 11.26.23 \|\|

*ityātmanaḥ paraṃ bhāvaṃ smārayitvānurūpataḥ \|*  
*brahmaṇābhyarthitā gaurī tapaso 'pi nyavartata \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Thus requested by Brahmā after duly reminding her of her great aspect the goddess ceased from her penance.

## \|\| 11.26.24-29 \|\|

*tato devīmanujñāpya brahmaṇyantarhite sati \|*  
*devīṃ ca mātaraṃ dṛṣṭvā menāṃ himavatā saha \|\| 24 \|\|*

*praṇamyāśvāsya bahudhā pitarau virahāsahau \|*  
*tapaḥ praṇayino devī tapovanamahīruhān \|\| 25 \|\|*

*viprayogaśucevāgre puṣpabāṣpaṃ vimuṃcataḥ \|*  
*tattucchākhāsamārūḍhavihago dīritai rutaiḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*vyākulaṃ bahudhā dīnaṃ vilāpamiva kurvataḥ \|*  
*sakhībhyaḥ kathayaṃtyevaṃ sattvarā bhartṛdarśane \|\| 27 \|\|*

*puraskṛtya ca taṃ vyāghraṃ snehātputramivaurasam \|*  
*dehasya prabhayā caiva dīpayantī diśo daśa \|\| 28 \|\|*

*prayayau maṃdaraṃ gaurī yatra bhartā maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ jagatāṃ dhātā kartā pātā vināśakṛt \|\| 29 \|\|*

24-29. Then taking leave of the goddess Brahmā vanished. The goddess visited her parents Menā, Himavat. She bowed to them and alleviated the pangs of her parents due to her absence. The goddess then proceeded to Mandara talking to her friends about the trees in the penance-grove who had been her loving companions. “They are shedding tears due to their grief at separation, by their scattering flowers, they are crying in distress by the chirping sound of birds seated on their boughs.” The goddess was impatient to see her lord. She kept the tiger ahead thinking him as son born of herself, out of affection. With the brilliant lustre of her body she illuminated the quarters. Thus Gaurī reached Mandara where lord Śiva was staying—the lord who is the creator, protector and annihilator of the worlds.

## Chapter 27 - Gaurī’s embellishment

## \|\| 11.27.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā gauraṃ vapurdivyaṃ devī girivarātmajā \|*  
*kathaṃ dadarśa bhartāraṃ praviṣṭā manditaṃ satī \|\| 1 \|\|*

The sages said:—

1\. After assuming fair complexion how did the goddess, the daughter of the excellent mountain look at her husband on entering the mansion?

## \|\| 11.27.2 \|\|

*praveśasamaye tasyā bhavanadvāragocaraiḥ \|*  
*gaṇeśaiḥ kiṃ kṛtaṃ devastāndṛṣṭvā kintadā 'karot \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. What was done by the Gaṇeśas at the portals at her entry? What did the lord do?

## \|\| 11.27.3 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*pravaktumaṃjasā 'śakyaḥ tādṛśaḥ paramo rasaḥ \|*  
*yena praṇayagarbheṇa bhāvo bhāvavatāṃ hṛtaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

3\. It is impossible to narrate adequately such an exquisite sentiment couched in love whereby the imagination of all sentimental people has been captured.

## \|\| 11.27.4 \|\|

*dvāsthaissasaṃbhramaireva devo devyāgamotsukaḥ \|*  
*śaṃkamānā praviṣṭāntastañca sā samapaśyata \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. She was received by the doorkeepers in full flutter and agitation. The lord was eagerly awaiting her arrival. Entering within the mansion she hesitatingly glanced at the lord.

## \|\| 11.27.5 \|\|

*taistaiḥ praṇayabhāvaiśca bhavanāntaravartibhiḥ \|*  
*gaṇendrairvanditā vācā praṇanāma triyambakam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. She was welcomed by the inmates of the mansion with loving feelings. She was saluted by the Gaṇa chiefs with words of welcome. She bowed to lord Śiva.

## \|\| 11.27.6-8 \|\|

*praṇamya notthitā yāvattāvattāṃ parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*pragṛhya dorbhyāmāśliṣya paritaḥ parayā mudā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*svāṃke dhartuṃ pravṛtto 'pi sā paryaṃke nyaṣīdata \|*  
*paryaṃkato balāddevīṃ soṅkamāropya susmitām \|\| 7 \|\|*

*sasmito vivṛtairnetraistadvaktraṃ prapibanniva \|*  
*tayā saṃbhāṣaṇāyeśaḥ pūrvabhāṣitamabravīt \|\| 8 \|\|*

6-8. After bowing no sooner did she get up than the lord seized her with his hands, embraced her and joyously walked her round. Even when he attempted to make her sit on his lap she sat on the couch. Smilingly he seized her from the couch and made her sit on his lap. Smilingly gazing at her with his wide open eyes as if he would drink her in, the lord initiated the conversation with her by speaking himself first.

## \|\| 11.27.9 \|\|

*devadeva uvāca \|*  
*sā daśā ca vyatītā kiṃ tava sarvāṃgasundari \|*  
*yasyāmanunayopāyaḥ ko 'pi kopānna labhyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

The lord of the gods said:—

9\. O lady, exquisitely beautiful in every limb, has that condition of yours passed wherein no means of pacification is fruitful due to your anger?

## \|\| 11.27.10-11 \|\|

*svecchayāpi na kālīti nānyavarṇavatīti ca \|*  
*tvatsvabhāvāhṛtaṃ cittaṃ subhru ciṃtāvahaṃ mama \|\| 10 \|\|*

*vismṛtaḥ paramo bhāvaḥ kathaṃ svecchāṃgayogataḥ \|*  
*na sambhavanti ye tatra cittakāluṣyahetavaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. O lovely lady, I do not mind whether you are Kālī or of any other complexion. My mind is attracted by your innermost feeling. How did this concept escape your memory? Out of our will we have accepted physical bodies. Causes dirtying up the mind do not crop up there.

## \|\| 11.27.12 \|\|

*pṛthagjanavadanyonyaṃ vipriyasyāpi kāraṇam \|*  
*āvayorapi yadyasti nāstyevaitaccarācaram \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Should there be any cause for our mutual displeasure as in the case of ignorant fellows, the whole world consisting of the mobile and immobile beings would cease to exist.

## \|\| 11.27.13 \|\|

*ahamagniśironiṣṭhastvaṃ somaśirasi sthitā \|*  
*agnīṣomātmakaṃ viśvamāvābhyāṃ samadhiṣṭhitam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. I am stationed on the head of Agni. You are stationed on the head of Soma. This universe in the form of “Agnīṣoma” is presided over by us both.

## \|\| 11.27.14 \|\|

*jagaddhitāya caratoḥ svecchādhṛtaśarīrayoḥ \|*  
*āvayorviprayoge hi syānnirālambanaṃ jagat \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. We move about for the welfare of the universe. We have taken up physical bodies out of our free will. At our separation the universe is left without support.

## \|\| 11.27.15-16 \|\|

*asti hetvantaraṃ cātra śāstrayuktiviniścitam \|*  
*vāgarthamiva me vaitajjagatsthāvarajaṃgamam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tvaṃ hi vāgamṛtaṃ sākṣādahamarthāmṛtaṃ param \|*  
*dvayamapyamṛtaṃ kasmādviyuktamupapadyate \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. There is another reason based on Scriptural texts and independent arguments. The universe comprising the mobile and immobile beings is integrated as words to their meaning. You are the nectarine word. I am the nectarine meaning. How can the two nectars become disjointed?

## \|\| 11.27.17 \|\|

*vidyāpratyāyikā tvaṃ me vedyo 'haṃ pratyayāttava \|*  
*vidyāvedyātmanoreva viśleṣaḥ kathamāvayoḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. You are the lore that makes my conviction possible. I am the object of knowledge on the basis of your conviction. How can we separate in asmuch as we are in the forms of knowledge and object of knowledge?

## \|\| 11.27.18 \|\|

*na karmaṇā sṛjāmīdaṃ jagatpratisṛjāmi ca \|*  
*sarvasyājñaikalabhyatvādājñātvaṃ hi garīyasī \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. I am not creating and re-creating this universe merely by my activity since everything gets evolved through command or behest. You are the great command.

## \|\| 11.27.19 \|\|

*ājñaikasāramaiśvaryaṃ yasmātsvātaṃtryalakṣaṇam \|*  
*ājñayā viprayuktasya caiśvaryaṃ mama kīdṛśam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Lordship has behest as its core because it is the symbol of freedom. How can there be lordship in me if I am deprived of command?

## \|\| 11.27.20 \|\|

*na kadācidavasthānamāvayorviprayuktayoḥ \|*  
*devānāṃ kāryamuddiśya līloktiṃ kṛtavānaham \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. We can never stay apart from each other. It was for accomplishing the task of the gods that I made that joke.

## \|\| 11.27.21 \|\|

*tvayāpyaviditaṃ nāsti kathaṃ kupitavatyasi \|*  
*tatastrilokarakṣārthe kopo mayyapi te kṛtaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. It was not unknown to you that you got angry? It was for the protection of the worlds that you feigned anger towards me.

## \|\| 11.27.22-24 \|\|

*yadanarthāya bhūtānāṃ na tadasti khalu tvayi \|*  
*iti priyaṃvade sākṣādīśvare parameśvare \|\| 22 \|\|*

*śṛṃgārabhāvasārāṇāṃ janmabhūmirakṛtrimā \|*  
*svabhartrā lalitantathyamuktaṃ matvā smitottaram \|\| 23 \|\|*

*lajjayā na kimapyūce kauśikī varṇanātparam \|*  
*tadeva varṇayāmyadya śṛṇu devyāśca varṇanam \|\| 24 \|\|*

22-24. What is harmful to the living beings does not find room in you. When lord himself spoke thus the goddess, the natural source of love, smiled but did not reply to her husband. Out of bashfulness she did not say anything but gave an accorm? of Kauśikī.

## \|\| 11.27.25 \|\|

*devyuvāca \|*  
*kiṃ devena na sā dṛṣṭā yā sṛṣṭā kauśikī mayā \|*  
*tādṛśī kanyakā loke na bhūtā na bhaviṣyati \|\| 25 \|\|*

The goddess said:—

25\. Was not Kauśiki, created by me seen by my lord? Such a girl has never been before in the world nor will ever be.

## \|\| 11.27.26-27 \|\|

*tasyā vīryaṃ balaṃ vindhyanilayaṃ vijayaṃ tathā \|*  
*śuṃbhasya ca niśuṃbhasya māraṇe ca raṇe tayoḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*pratyakṣaphaladānaṃ ca lokāya bhajate sadā \|*  
*lokānāṃ rakṣaṇaṃ śaśvadbrahmā vijñāpayiṣyati \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. Brahma will tell you about her prowess, strength, residence on the Vindhya, her victory in the battle with Śumbha and Niśumbha, their death, her blessing to the devotees and her protection of the worlds.

## \|\| 11.27.28 \|\|

*iti saṃbhāṣamāṇāyā devyā evājñayā tadā \|*  
*vyāghraḥ sakhyā samānīya puro 'vasthāpitastadā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. At the behest of the goddess who spoke thus her friends brought the tiger in their presence.

## \|\| 11.27.29 \|\|

*taṃ prekṣyāha punardevī devānītamupāyatam \|*  
*vyāghraṃ paśya na cānena sadṛśo madupāsakaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. On seeing him the goddess spoke again—“O lord, see this tiger. There is no other devotee of mine like him.

## \|\| 11.27.30-32 \|\|

*anena duṣṭasaṃghebhyo rakṣitaṃ mattapovanam \|*  
*atīva mama bhaktaśca viśrabdhaśca svarakṣaṇāt \|\| 30 \|\|*

*svadeśaṃ ca parityajya prasādārthaṃ samāgataḥ \|*  
*yadi prītirabhūnmattaḥ parāṃ prītiṃ karoṣi me \|\| 31 \|\|*

*nityamantaḥpuradvāri niyogānnandinaḥ svayam \|*  
*rakṣibhissaha taccihnairvartatāmayamīśvara \|\| 32 \|\|*

30-32. My penance-grove was guarded by him from wicked hosts. He is greatly devoted to me. In view of his protecting me he is trustworthy. He has left his native place and come here for your favour. If you are pleased with him and if you love me, O god, let him stay at the door of the harem along with the other guards and under the charge of Nandin himself.”

## \|\| 11.27.33-34 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*madhuraṃ praṇayodarkaṃ śrutvā devyāḥ śubhaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*prīto 'smītyāha taṃ devassa cādṛśyata tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 33 \|\|*

*bibhradvetralatāṃ haimīṃ ratnacitraṃ ca kaṃcukam \|*  
*churikāmuragaprakhyāṃ gaṇeśo rakṣaveṣadhṛk \|\| 34 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

33-34. On hearing the auspicious, loving and sweet words of the goddess the lord said to him “I am pleased”. Immediately he was seen like Gaṇeśa wearing the dress and features of a watchman, holding the cane made of gold and a dagger of serpentine lustre and wearing a bodice set with various gems.

## \|\| 11.27.35 \|\|

*yasmātsomo mahādevo nandī cānena nanditaḥ \|*  
*somanandīti vikhyātastasmādeṣa samākhyayā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. He was named Somanandin because Soma means Śiva and this tiger pleased Soma as well as Nandin.

## \|\| 11.27.36 \|\|

*itthaṃ devyāḥ priyaṃ kṛtvā devaścardhendubhūṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*bhūṣayāmāsa tandivyairbhūṣaṇai ratnabhūṣitaiḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. After carrying out this task pleasing to the goddess the lord with the circular moon on his crest embellished him with divine ornaments set with gems.

## \|\| 11.27.37 \|\|

*tatassa gaurīṃ giriśo girīndrajāṃ sagauravāṃ sarvamanoharāṃ haraḥ \|*  
*paryaṃkamāropya varāṃgabhūṣaṇairvibhūṣayāmāsa śaśāṃkabhūṣaṇaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Then lord Śiva with the moon as his ornament made the majestic beautiful Gaurī the daughter of the lord of Himavat sit on the conch and embellished her with ornaments.

## Chapter 28 - The glory of Bhasma

## \|\| 11.28.1-2 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*devīṃ samādadhānena devenedaṃ kimīritam \|*  
*agniṣomātmakaṃ viśvaṃ vāgarthātmakamityapi \|\| 1 \|\|*

*ājñaikasāramaiśvaryamājñā tvamiti coditam \|*  
*tadidaṃ śrotumicchāmo yathāvadanupūrvaśaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

The sages said:—

1-2. We wish to hear these things in the proper order. What was it mentioned by the lord while pacifying the goddess? He had said that the universe is in the form of Agnīṣoma. He had said that it was in the form of words and their meanings. He also mentioned lordship has command as its core. You are that command.

## \|\| 11.28.3 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*agnirityucyate raudrī ghorā yā taijasī tanuḥ \|*  
*somaḥ śākto 'mṛtamayaḥ śakteḥ śāntikarī tanuḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

3\. The body of Rudra which is fiery and terrible is called fire. The moon pertains to Śakti. It is nectarine and is the body of Śakti that causes calmness.

## \|\| 11.28.4 \|\|

*amṛtaṃ yatpratiṣṭhā sā tejo vidyā kalā svayam \|*  
*bhūtasūkṣmeṣu sarveṣu ta eva rasatejasī \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. What is called Amṛta is Pratiṣṭhā. Tejas is Vidyā and Kalā itself. In all the subtle elements the two are predominant, viz, Rasa and Tejas.

## \|\| 11.28.5 \|\|

*dvividhā tejaso vṛttisūryātmā cānalātmikā \|*  
*tathaiva rasavṛttiśca somātmā ca jalātmikā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Tejas functions in two ways, in the form of the sun and of fire. Rasa too functions in the form of the moon and of water.

## \|\| 11.28.6 \|\|

*vidyudādimayantejo madhurādimayo rasaḥ \|*  
*tejorasavibhedaistu dhṛtametaccarācaram \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Tejas is lightning etc. Rasa is sweet etc. The universe of the mobile and immobile beings, is sustained by Tejas and Rasa.

## \|\| 11.28.7 \|\|

*agneramṛtaniṣpattiramṛtenāgniredhate \|*  
*ata eva hi vikrāntamagnīṣomaṃ jagaddhitam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Amṛta issues from Agni. Agni increases through Amṛta. The powerful Agnīṣoma is beneficent to the universe.

## \|\| 11.28.8 \|\|

*haviṣe sasyasampattirvṛṣṭiḥ sasyābhivṛddhaye \|*  
*vṛṣṭereva havistasmādagnīṣomadhṛtaṃ jagat \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The luxuriant growth of Vegetation is for the Havis. The rain contributes to the flourishing growth of vegetation. So Havis is the outcome of rain, the universe is sustained by Agnīṣoma.

## \|\| 11.28.9 \|\|

*agnirūrdhvaṃ jvalatyeṣa yāvatsaumyaṃ parāmṛtam \|*  
*yāvadagnyāspadaṃ saumyamamṛtaṃ ca sravatyadhaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The Agni blazes upwards as far as the great Amṛta of Soma. The Amṛta of Soma flows as far as the support of Agni.

## \|\| 11.28.10 \|\|

*ata eva hi kālāgniradhastācchaktirūrdhvataḥ \|*  
*yāvadādahanaṃ cordhvamadhaścāplāvanaṃ bhavet \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. That is why the Kālāgni stays below and the Śakti upwards. The upward blazing is till burning and the downward flow is till complete drenching.

## \|\| 11.28.11 \|\|

*ādhāraśaktyaiva dhṛtaḥ kālāgnirayamūrdhvagaḥ \|*  
*tathaiva nimnagaḥ somaśśivaśaktipadāspadaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The Kālāgni supported by Ādhāra Śakti proceeds upwards. Similarly Soma having its region in Śiva-Śakti flows downwards.

## \|\| 11.28.12 \|\|

*śivaścordhvamadhaśśaktirūrdhvaṃ śaktiradhaḥ śivaḥ \|*  
*taditthaṃ śivaśaktibhyānnāvyāptamiha kiñcana \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Śivā sustains Śakti from below and Śiva is Śaktidhara (upholder of Śakti) above. Thus there is nothing not pervaded by Śiva and Śakti.

## \|\| 11.28.13 \|\|

*asakṛccāgninā dagdhaṃ jagadyadbhasmasātkṛtam \|*  
*agnervīryamidaṃ cāhustadvīryaṃ bhasma yattataḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Frequently the world consumed by fire is reduced to ashes. They call it Agnivīrya because Bhasma constitutes the powerful part of the same.

## \|\| 11.28.14 \|\|

*yaścetthaṃ bhasmasadbhāvaṃ jñātvā snāti ca bhasmanā \|*  
*agnirityādibhirmantrairbaddhaḥ pāśātpramucyate \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. He who dusts himself with Bhasma repeating the mantra “Agniriti” etc., if bound becomes free from bondage.

## \|\| 11.28.15 \|\|

*agnervīryaṃ tu yadbhasma somenāplāvitampunaḥ \|*  
*ayogayuktyā prakṛteradhikārāya kalpate \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Bhasma which is Agnivīrya when drenched with Soma is conducive to the lordship of Prakṛti without having recourse to Yogic union.

## \|\| 11.28.16 \|\|

*yogayuktyā tu tadbhasma plāvyamānaṃ samantataḥ \|*  
*śāktenāmṛtavarṣeṇa cādhikārānnivartayet \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. But being drenched all round by having recourse to Yogic union the Bhasma may turn one back from lordship by the shower of Amṛta belonging to Śakti.

## \|\| 11.28.17 \|\|

*ato mṛtyuṃjayāyetthamamṛtaplāvanaṃ sadā \|*  
*śivaśaktyamṛtasparśe labdhaṃ yena kuto mṛtiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Hence for the conquest of death the drenching with Amṛta shall be perpetual. How and wherefore shall one die if the nectarine contact of Śiva and Śakti is acquired?

## \|\| 11.28.18 \|\|

*yo veda dahanaṃ guhyaṃ plāvanaṃ ca yathoditam \|*  
*agnīṣomapadaṃ hitvā na sa bhūyo 'bhijāyate \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He who knows the secret of burning and drenching as mentioned is never reborn after leaving the world, the region of Agnīṣoma.

## \|\| 11.28.19 \|\|

*śivāgninā tanuṃ dagdhvā śaktisaumyā mṛtena yaḥ \|*  
*plāvayedyogamārgeṇa so 'mṛtatvāya kalpate \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. He who burns his body with Śaivite fire and drenches it with the nectar of Śakti and Soma attains immortality.

## \|\| 11.28.20 \|\|

*hṛdi kṛtvemamarthaṃ vai devena samudāhṛtam \|*  
*agnīṣomātmakaṃ viśvaṃ jagadityanurūpataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. It was after keeping this in mind that the lord had said—“The universe is in the form of Agnīṣoma”.

## Chapter 29 - The analysis of Vāgartha (vāg-artha)

## \|\| 11.29.1 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*nivedayāmi jagato vāgarthātmyaṃ kṛtaṃ yathā \|*  
*ṣaḍadhvavedanaṃ samyaksamāsānna tu vistarāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

1\. I shall mention briefly how the universe in the form of “Vāg-Artha” can be known through the six pathways.

## \|\| 11.29.2 \|\|

*nāsti kaścidaśabdārtho nāpi śabdo nirarthakaḥ \|*  
*tato hi samaye śabdassarvassarvārthabodhakaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. There is nothing that is not the meaning of a word. There is no word without meaning. Therefore all words make all meanings known in their proper time.

## \|\| 11.29.3 \|\|

*prakṛteḥ pariṇāmo 'yaṃ dvidhā śabdārthabhāvanā \|*  
*tāmāhuḥ prākṛtīṃ mūrtiṃ śivayoḥ paramātmanoḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The two words and their meanings are the transformations of Prakṛti which is form of Śiva and Śivā.

## \|\| 11.29.4 \|\|

*śabdātmikā vibhūtiryā sā tridhā kathyate budhaiḥ \|*  
*sthūlā sūkṣmā parā ceti sthūlā yā śrutigocarā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The magnificence in the form of word is mentioned as threefold by scholars—gross, subtle and the great. The gross one is what we hear with our ears.

## \|\| 11.29.5-8 \|\|

*sūkṣmā cintāmayī proktā ciṃtayā rahitā parā \|*  
*yā śaktiḥ sā parā śaktiśśivatattvasamāśrayā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*jñānaśaktisamāyogādicchopodbalikā tathā \|*  
*sarvaśaktisamaṣṭyātmā śaktitattvasamākhyayā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*samastakāryajātasya mūlaprakṛtitāṃ gatā \|*  
*saiva kuṇḍalinī māyā śuddhādhvaparamā satī \|\| 7 \|\|*

*sā vibhāgasvarūpaiva ṣaḍadhvātmā vijṛṃbhate \|*  
*tatra śabdāstrayo 'dhvānastrayaścārthāḥ samīritāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

5-8. The subtle one is in the form of thought, the one beyond is devoid of thought. The Śakti based on the principle of Śiva is Parāśakti. In the name of “Śakti Tattva” it is the root cause of all effects. It is the composite unit (Samaṣṭi) of all Śaktis because it is in association with Jñāna Śakti and is supported by Icchāśakti. The same

is called Kuṇḍalinī Māyā and Śuddhādhvaparamā. This Śakti is ramified into six paths. The three paths pertain to words and the three pertain to their meanings.

## \|\| 11.29.9-10 \|\|

*sarveṣāmapi vai puṃsāṃ naijaśuddhyanurūpataḥ \|*  
*layabhogādhikārāssyussarvatattvavibhāgataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*kalābhistāni tattvāni vyāptānyeva yathātatham \|*  
*parasyāḥ prakṛterādau pañcadhā pariṇāmataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. The capacity for merging and enjoyment is possessed by all men in accordance with their purity based on the divisions of all Principles. The principles are pervaded by Kalās suitably as in the beginning the great Prakṛti is transformed into five. They are Kalā, Nivṛtti and others.

## \|\| 11.29.11-12 \|\|

*kalāśca tā nivṛttyādyāḥ paryāptā iti niścayaḥ \|*  
*maṃtrādhvā ca padādhvā ca varṇādhvā ceti śabdataḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*bhuvanādhvā ca tattvādhvā kalādhvā cārthataḥ kramāt \|*  
*atrānyonyaṃ ca sarveṣāṃ vyāpyavyāpakatocyate \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. The three paths based on words are: the path of mantras, the path of words, the path of letters. The three paths based on meanings are the path of universe, the path of principles, the path of Kalās. These are mutually pervaded and pervading.

## \|\| 11.29.13 \|\|

*maṃtrāḥ sarvaiḥ padairvyāptā vākyabhāvātpadāni ca \|*  
*varṇairvarṇasamūhaṃ hi padamāhurvipaścitaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The mantras are pervaded by the words constituting the statement. The words are pervaded by letters. Learned men call the group of letters a word.

## \|\| 11.29.14-17 \|\|

*varṇāstu bhuvanairvyāptāsteṣāṃ teṣūpalaṃbhanāt \|*  
*bhuvanānyapi tattvaughairutpattyāṃtarbahiṣkramāt \|\| 14 \|\|*

*vyāptāni kāraṇaistattvairārabdhatvādanekaśaḥ \|*  
*aṃtarādutthitānīha bhuvanāni tu kānicit \|\| 15 \|\|*

*paurāṇikāni cānyāni vijñeyāni śivāgame \|*  
*sāṃkhyayogaprasiddhāni tattvānyapi ca kānicit \|\| 16 \|\|*

*śivaśāstraprasiddhāni tatonyānyapi kṛtsnaśaḥ \|*  
*kalābhistāni tattvāni vyāptānyeva yathātatham \|\| 17 \|\|*

14-17. The letters are pervaded by the words because they are obtained there. The words are pervaded by the Tattvas because of their origin from within and without. They are effected by the Tattvas in various ways. Some of the words have cropped up from the middle, some from the Śaiva Āgamas. Some of Tattvas are those famous in the Sāṅkhya and Yoga systems of Philosophy. Others are famous in the sacred texts of Śiva. The Tattvas are duly pervaded by Kalās.

## \|\| 11.29.18 \|\|

*parasyāḥ prakṛterādau pañcadhā pariṇāmataḥ \|*  
*kalāśca tā nivṛttyādyā vyāptāḥ pañca yathottaram \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Since in the beginning the primordial Prakṛti is transformed into five Kalās, Nivṛtti and others pervaded by each other.

## \|\| 11.29.19 \|\|

*vyāpikātaḥ parā śaktiravibhaktā ṣaḍadhvanām \|*  
*paraprakṛtibhāvasya tatsattvācchivatattvataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The undivided Śakti pervades the six paths. She is pervaded by Śivatattva.

## \|\| 11.29.20 \|\|

*śaktyādi ca pṛthivyantaṃ śivatattvasamudbhavam \|*  
*vyāptamekena tenaiva mṛdā kuṃbhādikaṃ yathā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Everything from Śakti to Earth is born of Śivatattva and pervaded by it alone just as pot etc. are pervaded by clay.

## \|\| 11.29.21 \|\|

*śaivaṃ tatparamaṃ dhāma yatprāpyaṃ ṣaḍbhiradhvabhiḥ \|*  
*vyāpikā 'vyāpikā śaktiḥ pañcatattvaviśodhanāt \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The great abode of Śiva is attainable through six paths. The non-pervading Śakti becomes pervasive by the purification by five Tattvas.

## \|\| 11.29.22 \|\|

*nivṛttyā rudraparyantaṃ sthitiraṇḍasya śodhyate \|*  
*pratiṣṭhayā tadūrdhvaṃ tu yāvadavyaktagocaram \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The situation of the cosmic egg upto Rudra is purified by Nivṛtti. Above that upto the sphere of Avyakta It is purified by Pratiṣṭhā.

## \|\| 11.29.23 \|\|

*tadūrdhvaṃ vidyayā madhye yāvadviśveśvarāvadhi \|*  
*śāntyā tadūrdhvaṃ madhvānte viśuddhiḥ śāntyatītayā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Above that upto Viśveśvara it is purified by Vidyā in the middle. Above that it is purified by Śānti. At the end of the path the purification is through Śāntyatīta.

## \|\| 11.29.24 \|\|

*yāmāhuḥ paramaṃ vyoma paraprakṛtiyogataḥ \|*  
*etāni pañcatattvāni yairvyāptamakhilaṃ jagat \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. It is this they call the greatest firmament in view of the contact with Parāprakṛti. These are the five Tattvas whereby the entire universe is pervaded.

## \|\| 11.29.25-26 \|\|

*tatraiva sarvamevedaṃ draṣṭavyaṃ khalu sādhakaiḥ \|*  
*adhvavyāptimavijñāya śuddhiṃ yaḥ kartumicchati \|\| 25 \|\|*

*sa vipralambhakaḥ śuddhernālamprāpayituṃ phalam \|*  
*vṛthā pariśramastasya nirayāyaiva kevalam \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. All this could be seen only there by the aspirants. He who wishes to purify without realising the mode of pervasion of the paths is a deceiver of purity. He cannot achieve the fruit. His effort is wasted and leads him to hell.

## \|\| 11.29.27 \|\|

*śaktipātasamāyogādṛte tattvāni tattvataḥ \|*  
*tadvyāptistadvivṛddhiśca jñātumevaṃ na śakyate \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. It is not possible to know the Tattvas factually nor their pervasiveness nor increase without the union of Śakti and the individual soul.

## \|\| 11.29.28 \|\|

*śaktirājñā parā śaivī cidrūpā marameśvarī \|*  
*śivo 'dhitiṣṭhatyakhilaṃ yayā kāraṇabhūtayā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Śakti is the order of Śiva in the form of cit. With that as the cause Śiva presides over everything.

## \|\| 11.29.29 \|\|

*nātmano naiva māyaiṣā na vikāro vicārataḥ \|*  
*na baṃdho nāpi muktiśca baṃdhamuktividhāyinī \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. It is not of the nature of the Ātman nor of Māyā nor of secondary nature. It is neither bondage nor liberation but it causes bondage and liberation.

## \|\| 11.29.30 \|\|

*sarvaiśvaryaparākāṣṭā śivasya vyabhicāriṇī \|*  
*samānadharmiṇī tasya taistairbhāvairviśeṣataḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. She is the acme of Śiva’s lordship never swerving. By means of sensations she is of the same traits as he.

## \|\| 11.29.31 \|\|

*sa tayaiva gṛhī sāpi tenaiva gṛhiṇī sadā \|*  
*tayorapatyaṃ yatkāryaṃ paraprakṛtijaṃ jagat \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. With her alone he is a householder and with him alone she is a housewife always. As a result of their union the universe is the offspring.

## \|\| 11.29.32 \|\|

*sa kartā kāraṇaṃ seti tayorbhedo vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*eka eva śivaḥ sākṣāddvidhā 'sau samavasthitaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Their difference is specified in this that he is the maker and she is the cause. The single Śiva himself stands two-fold.

## \|\| 11.29.33-34 \|\|

*strīpuṃsabhāvena tayorbheda ityapi kecana \|*  
*apare tu parā śaktiḥ śivasya samavāyinī \|\| 33 \|\|*

*prabheva bhānościdrūpā bhinnaiveti vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*tasmācchivaḥ paro hetustasyājñā parameśvarī \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. Some declare that their difference consists in their genders: man and woman. Others say that she is undetachably associated with him as the light of the sun. But in the form of cit she is different. The arrangement is that Śiva is the great cause and his behest is the great goddess.

## \|\| 11.29.35-36 \|\|

*tayaiva preritā śaivī mūlaprakṛtiravyayā \|*  
*mahāmāyā ca māyā ca prakṛtistriguṇeti ca \|\| 35 \|\|*

*trividhā kāryavedhena sā prasūte ṣaḍadhvanaḥ \|*  
*sa vāgarthamayaścādhvā ṣaḍvidho nikhilaṃ jagat \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. Urged by his behest the original unchanging Prakṛti becomes threefold in accordance with the three types of effects. It is called Mahāmāyā, Māyā and Triguṇā Prakṛti. It produces the six paths in the form of words and their meanings. The entire universe is thus sixfold. The whole collection of scriptural text is only an extension of this.

## Chapter 30 - The principle of Śiva

## \|\| 11.30.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*caritāni vicitrāṇi gṛhyāṇi gahanāni ca \|*  
*durvijñeyāni devaiśca mohayaṃti manāṃsi naḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

The sages said:—

1\. The activities of deities of domestic nature are curious, dense and inscrutable, even to the gods. They delude our minds.

## \|\| 11.30.2 \|\|

*śivayostattvasambandhe na doṣa upalabhyate \|*  
*caritaiḥ prākṛto bhāvastayorapi vibhāvyate \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. In the union of the principles of Śiva and Śivā no defect is noticeable. However in their activities the Prākṛta feeling is rather prominent.

## \|\| 11.30.3 \|\|

*brahmādayo 'pi lokānāṃ sṛṣṭisthityantahetavaḥ \|*  
*nigrahānugrahau prāpya śivasya vaśavartinaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Brahmā and others the causes of creation, sustenance and annihilation attain restraint and blessing from Śiva and are subservient to him.

## \|\| 11.30.4 \|\|

*śivaḥ punarna kasyāpi nigrahānugrahāspadam \|*  
*ato 'nāyattamaiśvaryaṃ tasyaiveti viniścitam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Śiva is not subject to anyone’s Nigraha and Anugraha. Surely his lordship is not dependent on any one else.

## \|\| 11.30.5 \|\|

*yadyevamīdṛśaiśvaryaṃ tattu svātantryalakṣaṇam \|*  
*svabhāvasiddhaṃ caitasya mūrtimattāspadaṃ bhavet \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. If his lordship is like this, characterised by freedom, it can be either innate or subject to his embodied state.

## \|\| 11.30.6 \|\|

*na mūrtiśca svataṃtrasya ghaṭate mūlahetunā \|*  
*mūrterapi ca kāryatvāttatsiddhiḥ syādahaitukī \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. But a physical form docs not fit in with a free being for this basic reason. But the form is an effect of some cause. Lordship has no cause for its being.

## \|\| 11.30.7 \|\|

*sarvatra paramo bhāvo 'paramaścānya ucyate \|*  
*paramāparamau bhāvau kathamekatra saṃgatau \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Everywhere the greater and the lower Bhāvas are mentioned. How can these two be relevant in one place?

## \|\| 11.30.8 \|\|

*niṣphalo hi svabhāvo 'sya paramaḥ paramātmanaḥ \|*  
*sa eva sakalaḥ kasmātsvabhāvo hyaviparyayaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Indeed the great Ātman is devoid of attributes. How can he become possessed of attributes. Svabhāva is unrevertible.

## \|\| 11.30.9 \|\|

*svabhāvo viparītaścetsvataṃtraḥ svecchayā yadi \|*  
*na karoti kimīśāno nityānityaviparyayam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. If you say that his innate nature is reverted by his own wish he being free, why does not Īśāna make an interchange in permanent and non-permanent things?

## \|\| 11.30.10 \|\|

*mūrtātmā sakalaḥ kaścitsa cānyo niṣphalaḥ śivaḥ \|*  
*śivenādhiṣṭhitaśceti sarvatra laghu kathyate \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The wise have said that the embodied Ātman is Sakala; the unembodied Śiva is Niṣkala. The embodied Ātman is presided over by Śiva.

## \|\| 11.30.11 \|\|

*mūrtyātmaiva tadā mūrtiḥ śivasyāsya bhavediti \|*  
*tasya mūrtau mūrtimatoḥ pārataṃtryaṃ hi niścitam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. If it is contended that the embodied Ātman is the form of Śiva, the dependence of the embodied on the form becomes certain. How can we explain that?

## \|\| 11.30.12 \|\|

*anyathā nirapekṣeṇa mūrtiḥ svīkriyate katham \|*  
*mūrtisvīkaraṇaṃ tasmānmūrtau sādhyaphalepsayā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Otherwise how is the form adopted by the nondependant? The adoption of form is with a purpose to get the fruit of his desire.

## \|\| 11.30.13 \|\|

*na hi svecchāśarīratvaṃ svātaṃtryāyopapadyate \|*  
*svecchaiva tādṛśī puṃsāṃ yasmātkarmānusāriṇī \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The assuming of physical bodies out of wish is not consistent with freedom. Such a wish too follows the activities of men.

## \|\| 11.30.14 \|\|

*svīkartuṃ svecchayā dehaṃ hātuṃ ca prabhavantyuta \|*  
*brahmādayaḥ piśācāṃtāḥ kiṃ te karmātivartinaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Even beings including Brahmā and Piśācas can assume or cast off their bodies out of their wish. But don’t they come under the scope of Karmans?

## \|\| 11.30.15 \|\|

*icchayā dehanirmāṇamindrajālopamaṃ viduḥ \|*  
*aṇimādiguṇaiśvaryavaśīkārānatikramāt \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. They consider the assumption of bodies at one’s choice on a par with jugglery. It is not beyond the achievements derived from Aṇimā and other powers.

## \|\| 11.30.16 \|\|

*viśvarūpaṃ dadhadviṣṇurdadhīcena maharṣiṇā \|*  
*yudhyatā samupālabdhastadrūpaṃ dadhatā svayam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. While Viṣṇu who had assumed the cosmic form was fighting with Dadhīca the latter assumed the cosmic form of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 11.30.17 \|\|

*sarvasmādadhikasyāpi śivasya paramātmanaḥ \|*  
*śarīravattayānyātmasādharmyaṃ pratibhāti naḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Although Śiva is the great Ātman and superior to all, his similarity with other beings is observed by us because he has a body.

## \|\| 11.30.18 \|\|

*sarvānugrāhakaṃ prāhuśśivaṃ paramakāraṇam \|*  
*sa nirgṛhṇāti devānāṃ sarvānugrāhakaḥ katham \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. They say that Śiva the supreme cause blesses us all. He curbs and kills the gods. How can he be a blesser of all?

## \|\| 11.30.19 \|\|

*ciccheda bahuśo devo brahmaṇaḥ pañcamaṃ śiraḥ \|*  
*śivanindāṃ prakurvaṃtaṃ putreti kumaterhaṭhāt \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The lord cut off the fifth head of Brahmā who stubbornly and repeatedly censured Śiva calling him “O son.”

## \|\| 11.30.20 \|\|

*viṣṇorapi nṛsiṃhasya rabhasā śarabhākṛtiḥ \|*  
*bibheda padbhyāmākramya hṛdayaṃ nakharaiḥ kharaiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. In the form of a Śarabha he forcefully attacked Viṣṇu the man-lion. Pressing him with his feet he tore off his heart by his sharp claws.

## \|\| 11.30.21 \|\|

*devastrīṣu ca deveṣu dakṣasyādhvarakāraṇāt \|*  
*vīreṇa vīrabhadreṇa na hi kaścidadaṇḍitaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. With the sacrifice of Dakṣa for a pretext none among the gods or their womenfolk was spared from punishment by the heroic Vīrabhadra.

## \|\| 11.30.22 \|\|

*puratrayaṃ ca sastrīkaṃ sadaityaṃ saha bālakaiḥ \|*  
*kṣaṇenaikena devena netrāgneriṃdhanīkṛtam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The three cities along with the Daityas, their womenfolk and children were made the fuel for the fire from his eyes in an instant by him.

## \|\| 11.30.23 \|\|

*prajānāṃ ratihetuśca kāmo ratipatissvayam \|*  
*krośatāmeva devānāṃ huto netrahutāśane \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Kāma the husband of Rati, the cause of the sexual pleasure of the people was consigned to the fire from his eyes even as the gods were lamenting.

## \|\| 11.30.24 \|\|

*gāvaśca kaściddugdhaughaṃ sravantyo mūrdhni khecarāḥ \|*  
*saruṣā prekṣya devena tatkṣaṇe bhasmasātkṛtaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Angrily glancing at some cows walking along the sky and shedding milk over his head he reduced them to ashes immediately.

## \|\| 11.30.25 \|\|

*jalaṃdharāsuro dīrṇaścakrīkṛtya jalaṃ padā \|*  
*baddhvānaṃtena yo viṣṇuṃ cikṣepa śatayojanam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The demon Jalandhara who bound Viṣṇu and his Serpent and hurled them a hundred Yojanas, was pierced after evolving a discus by making a circle in water with the foot.

## \|\| 11.30.26 \|\|

*tameva jalasaṃdhāyī śūlenaiva jaghāna saḥ \|*  
*taccakraṃ tapasā labdhvā labdhavīryo harissadā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. He then killed him with his trident in the water (?). By performing penance Viṣṇu secured the discus and became powerful.

## \|\| 11.30.27 \|\|

*jighāṃsatāṃ surārīṇāṃ kulaṃ nirghṛṇacetasām \|*  
*triśūlenāndhakasyoraḥ śikhinaivopatāpitam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The family of cruel demons who desired to kill him was scorched in fire. The chest of Andhaka was pierced with the trident.

## \|\| 11.30.28-29 \|\|

*kaṇṭhātkālāṃganāṃ sṛṣṭvā dārako 'pi nipātitaḥ \|*  
*kauśikīṃ janayitvā tu gauryāstvakkośagocarām \|\| 28 \|\|*

*śuṃbhassaha niśuṃbhena prāpito maraṇaṃ raṇe \|*  
*śrutaṃ ca mahadākhyānaṃ skānde skandasamāśrayam \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. After creating a dark woman from his neck he killed Dāraka. After creating Kauśikī out of the outer skin of Gaurī, Śumbha and Niśumbha were killed. The narrative on Skanda is found in the Skanda Purāṇa.

## \|\| 11.30.30 \|\|

*vadhārthe tārakākhyasya daityendrasyendravidviṣaḥ \|*  
*brahmaṇābhyarthito devo mandarāntaḥpuraṃ gataḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The lord, requested by Brahmā for the destruction of the leading Daitya Tāraka the enemy of Indra, went to his harem on the Mandara mountain.

## \|\| 11.30.31-32 \|\|

*vihṛtya suciraṃ devyā vihārā 'tiprasaṅgataḥ \|*  
*rasāṃ rasātalaṃ nītāmiva kṛtvābhidhāṃ tataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*devīṃ ca vaṃcayaṃstasyāṃ svavīryamatidurvaham \|*  
*avisṛjya visṛjyāgnau haviḥ pūtamivāmṛtam \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. The lord indulged in sexual dalliance with the goddess for a long time. Due to the excessive sport the earth appeared to sink into the nether worlds. He deceived his own name and the goddess by withholding the discharge of semen in her. The unbearable semen was discharged into the fire like nectar or the sanctified Havis.

## \|\| 11.30.33-34 \|\|

*gaṃgādiṣvapi nikṣipya vahnidvārā tadaṃśataḥ \|*  
*tatsamāhṛtya śanakaistokaṃstokamitastataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*svāhayā kṛttikārūpātsvabhartrā ramamāṇayā \|*  
*suvarṇībhūtayā nyastaṃ merau śaravaṇe kvacit \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. The fire cast it off into Gaṅgā and other places. Svāhā who assumed the form of the Kṛttikās and sported with her husband gathered the parts and deposited them in the Śara plants somewhere on the Meru. Svāhā was turned into gold in the process.

## \|\| 11.30.35 \|\|

*saṃdīpayitvā kālena tasya bhāsā diśo daśa \|*  
*rañjayitvā girīnsarvānkāṃcanīkṛtya meruṇā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. After some time her lustre illuminated quarters and the mountains. Meru itself was turned into gold.

## \|\| 11.30.36 \|\|

*tataścireṇa kālena saṃjāte tatra tejasi \|*  
*kumāre sukumārāṃge kumārāṇāṃ nidarśane \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. After a long time the splendour grew into a boy of beautiful and tender limbs, a model for all boys.

## \|\| 11.30.37 \|\|

*tacchaiśavaṃ svarūpaṃ ca tasya dṛṣṭvā manoharam \|*  
*saha devasurairlokairvismite ca vimohite \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. On seeing him of charming features, the world of the gods, Asuras and mankind was surprised and fascinated.

## \|\| 11.30.38-40 \|\|

*devo 'pi svayamāyātaḥ putradarśanalālasaḥ \|*  
*saha devyāṃkamāropya tato 'sya smeramānanam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*pītāmṛtamiva snehavivaśenāntarātmanā \|*  
*deveṣvapi ca paśyatsu vītarāgaistapasvibhiḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*svasya vakṣaḥsthale svairaṃ nartayitvā kumārakam \|*  
*anubhūya ca tatkrīḍāṃ saṃbhāvya ca parasparam \|\| 40 \|\|*

38-40. The lord himself came there along with the goddess to sec his son. He took the boy on his lap. The gods and the sages though averse to worldly pleasures glanced at his smiling face. The lord made him play on his chest and enjoyed the fun. The lord and the goddess congratulated each other.

## \|\| 11.30.41-45 \|\|

*stanyamājñāpayandevyāḥ pāyayitvāmṛtopamam \|*  
*tavāvatāro jagatāṃ hitāyetyanuśāsya ca \|\| 41 \|\|*

*svayandevaśca devī ca na tṛptimupajagmatuḥ \|*  
*tataḥ śakreṇa saṃdhāya bibhyatā tārakāsurāt \|\| 42 \|\|*

*kārayitvābhiṣekaṃ ca senāpatye divaukasām \|*  
*putramantarataḥ kṛtvā devena tripuradviṣā \|\| 43 \|\|*

*svayamaṃtarhitenaiva skandamindrādirakṣitam \|*  
*tacchaktyā krauñcabhedinyā yudhi kālāgnikalpayā \|\| 44 \|\|*

*cheditaṃ tārakasyāpi śiraśśakrabhiyā saha \|*  
*stutiṃ cakrurviśeṣeṇa haridhātṛmukhāḥ surāḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

41-45 He asked the goddess to feed him on her breast-milk. He blessed him saying “your incarnation is for the welfare of the world.” The lord and the goddess were not satiated. Indra who was afraid of the demon Tāraka joined in alliance and performed the coronation of the infant as the commander-in-chief of the gods. The lord vanished himself keeping him in the protection of Indra and the gods. Tāraka’s head along with Indra’s fear was chopped off by his trident in battle, the trident that resembled the deadly fire and pierced the Asura Krauñca. Viṣṇu Brahmā and other gods particularly eulogised him.

## \|\| 11.30.46-47 \|\|

*tathā rakṣodhipaḥ sākṣādrāvaṇo balagarvitaḥ \|*  
*uddharansvabhujairdīrghaiḥ kailāsaṃ girimātmanaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*tadāgo 'sahamānasya devadevasya śūlinaḥ \|*  
*padāṃguṣṭhaparispandānmamajja mṛdito bhuvi \|\| 47 \|\|*

46-47 Rāvaṇa, king of Rākṣasas, arrogant of his prowess lifted up Kailāsa with his long arms. Śiva, the trident-bearing lord of the gods could not brook that sin. He pressed it with his big toe and the demon sank under the pressure.

## \|\| 11.30.48 \|\|

*baṭoḥ kenacidarthena svāśritasya gatāyuṣaḥ \|*  
*tvarayāgatya devena pādāṃtaṃ gamitontakaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. For a brahmin boy whose life came to an end and who sought refuge in him, the lord came there hurriedly and kicked Yama with his foot.

## \|\| 11.30.49 \|\|

*svavāhanamavijñāya vṛṣendraṃ vaḍavānalaḥ \|*  
*sagalagrahamānītastato 'styekodakaṃ jagat \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The submarine fire, not knowing the bull as the lord’s vehicle swallowed him. Thereafter the universe became a vast sheet of water.

## \|\| 11.30.50 \|\|

*alokaviditaistaistairvṛttairānandasundaraiḥ \|*  
*aṃgahārasvasenedamasakṛccālitaṃ jagat \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. By means of different activities blissfully beautiful and unknown to the people, the universe has been set to motion frequently.

## \|\| 11.30.51 \|\|

*śānta eva sadā sarvamanugṛhṇāti cecchivaḥ \|*  
*sarvāṇi pūrayedeva kathaṃ śaktena mocayet \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. If Śiva is calm and blesses all, he shall fulfil all desires. Being competent why docs he not liberate?

## \|\| 11.30.52 \|\|

*anādikarma vaicitryamapi nātra niyāmakam \|*  
*kāraṇaṃ khalu karmāpi bhavedīśvarakāritam \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. The variety of beginningless Karmans cannot be the restraining factor here. The Karman that is the cause is also effected by the lord.

## \|\| 11.30.53 \|\|

*kimatra bahunoktena nāstikyaṃ hetukārakam \|*  
*yathā hyāśu nivarteta tathā kathaya māruta \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Of what avail is much talk? O Māruta, please explain in detail so that the arguments of atheism may be refuted quickly.

## Chapter 31 - Instruction in perfect wisdom

## \|\| 11.31.1 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*sthane saṃśayitaṃ viprā bhavadbhirhetucoditaiḥ \|*  
*jijñāsā hi na nāstikyaṃ sādhayetsādhubuddhiṣu \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

1\. O brahmins, it is but proper that you have had your doubts prompted by sufficient reasons. Mere desire to know does not bring about atheism in those with good intellects.

## \|\| 11.31.2 \|\|

*pramaṇamatra vakṣyāmi satāmmohanivartakam \|*  
*asatāṃ tvanyathābhāvaḥ prasādena vinā prabhoḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. I shall mention authoritative testimonies in this context quelling your delusions. The wickedness of the wicked is due to the absence of the grace of the lord.

## \|\| 11.31.3 \|\|

*śivasya paripūrṇasya parānugrahamantarā \|*  
*na kiṃcidapi kartavyamiti sādhu viniścitam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. It is clear and certain that nothing can be done without the grace of Śiva, the perfect and supreme soul.

## \|\| 11.31.4 \|\|

*svabhāva eva paryāptaḥ parānugrahakarmaṇi \|*  
*anyathā nissvabhavena na kimapyanugṛhyate \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Innate good nature alone is the sufficient ground for the lord’s benediction; nothing can be blessed without innate good nature.

## \|\| 11.31.5 \|\|

*paraṃ sarvamanugrāhyaṃ paśupāśātmakaṃ jagat \|*  
*parasyānugrahārthaṃ tu patyurājñāsamanvayaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The universe in the form of Paśu and Pāśa, has to be blessed. The lord endowed with the authority blesses the universe.

## \|\| 11.31.6 \|\|

*patirājñāpakaḥ sarvamanugṛhṇāti sarvadā \|*  
*tadarthamarthasvīkāre parataṃtraḥ kathaṃ śivaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The lord, the commander blesses everything always. If a means is adopted for that, how does Śiva become dependant?

## \|\| 11.31.7 \|\|

*anugrāhyanapekṣo 'sti na hi kaścidanugrahaḥ \|*  
*ataḥ svātantryaśabdārthānanapekṣatvalakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. No blessing can be independent of one that is blessed. Hence the meaning of the word freedom is not characterised by ‘not depending on another’.

## \|\| 11.31.8 \|\|

*etatpunaranugrāhyaṃ parataṃtraṃ tadiṣyate \|*  
*anugrahādṛte tasya bhuktimuktyorananvayāt \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. That which is to be blessed is accepted as ‘depending on another’. Without blessing, the enjoyment of pleasures or liberation cannot take place.

## \|\| 11.31.9 \|\|

*mūrtātmano 'pyanugrāhyā śivājñānanivartanāt \|*  
*ajñānādhiṣṭhitaṃ śambhorna kiṃcidiha vidyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Embodied Ātmans too stand in the category of those who are to be blessed. Śiva’s blessing is construed in the form of driving out their ignorance. There is nothing in Śiva influenced by ignorance.

## \|\| 11.31.10 \|\|

*yenopalabhyate 'smābhissakalenāpi niṣkalaḥ \|*  
*sa mūrtyātmā śivaḥ śaivamūrtirityupacaryate \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Śiva in the form of the idol, whereby despite its beings Saguṇa the Niṣkala is realised, is called Śaivamūrti only in a figurative use.

## \|\| 11.31.11 \|\|

*na hyasau niṣkalaḥ sākṣācchivaḥ paramakāraṇam \|*  
*sākāreṇānubhāvena kenāpyanupalakṣitaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Actually in the Niṣkala form Śiva is not the cause of the universe. In the Sakala form too he has not been seen by any.

## \|\| 11.31.12 \|\|

*pramāṇagamyatāmātraṃ tatsvabhāvopapādakam \|*  
*na tāvatātropekṣādhīrupalakṣaṇamaṃtarā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The state of being understood through the testimonies alone indicates his nature. Merely on account of this it should not be treated with indifference without the implication.

## \|\| 11.31.13 \|\|

*ātmopamolvaṇaṃ sākṣānmūrtireva hi kācana \|*  
*śivasya mūrtirmūrtyātmā parastasyopalakṣaṇam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Some form, intense with the similarity of Ātman, is Śiva’s idol. The other, the great one, the Ātman of the Mūrti is its implication.

## \|\| 11.31.14 \|\|

*yathā kāṣṭheṣvanārūḍho na vahnirupalabhyate \|*  
*evaṃ śivo 'pi mūrtyātmanyanārūḍha iti sthitiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Just as fire cannot be obtained without its being, mounted in the twigs so also Śiva is not known or understood without its being superimposed in the idol.

## \|\| 11.31.15 \|\|

*yathāgnimānayetyukte jvalatkāṣṭhādṛte svayam \|*  
*nāgnirānīyate tadvatpūjyo mūrtyātmanā śivaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. If some one says “Bring fire,” only the burning twig is brought. The fire by itself is not brought. In the same way Śiva is to be worshipped in the form of the idol.

## \|\| 11.31.16 \|\|

*ata eva hi pūjādau mūrtyātmaparikalpanam \|*  
*mūrtyātmani kṛtaṃ sākṣācchiva eva kṛtaṃ yataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. That is why an idol is used in the worship of Śiva, for what is done unto the idol is what is done unto Śiva himself.

## \|\| 11.31.17 \|\|

*liṃgādāvapi tatkṛtyamarcāyāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*tattanmūrtyātmabhāvena śivo 'smābhirupāsyate \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. In the form of different idols, phallic etc. and particularly in Arcā (offerings of flowers etc.) Śiva is worshipped by us.

## \|\| 11.31.18 \|\|

*yathānugṛhyate so 'pi mūrtyātmā pārameṣṭhinā \|*  
*tathā mūrtyātmaniṣṭhena śivena paśavo vayam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Just as the Ātman of the idol is blessed by the great Ātman so also we, the paśus, are blessed by śiva stationed in the Mūrtyātman.

## \|\| 11.31.19 \|\|

*lokānugrahaṇāyaiva śivena parameṣṭhinā \|*  
*sadāśivādayassarve mūrtyātmano 'pyadhiṣṭhitāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The Mūrtyātmans, Sadāśiva and others are presided over by Śiva for blessing the worlds.

## \|\| 11.31.20 \|\|

*ātmanāmeva bhogāya mokṣāya ca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*tattvātattvasvarūpeṣu mūrtyātmasu śivānvayaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. It is for the enjoyment of pleasures and for salvation in particular, that Śiva’s connection with the Mūrtyātmans in the form of Tattva and Atattva is accepted.

## \|\| 11.31.21 \|\|

*bhogaḥ karmavipākātmā sukhaduḥkhātmako mataḥ \|*  
*na ca karma śivo 'stīti tasya bhogaḥ kimātmakaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Enjoyment of pleasures is in the nature of the ultimate transformation of the Karmans either by way of happiness or by way of misery. There is no Karman in Śiva and hence of what nature can his enjoyment be?

## \|\| 11.31.22 \|\|

*sarvaṃ śivo 'nugṛhṇāti na nigṛhṇāti kiṃcana \|*  
*nigṛhṇatāṃ tu ye doṣāśśive teṣāmasaṃbhavāt \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Śiva blessess every one. He does not curb any. It is impossible to attribute to Śiva those faults which are usually present in those who kill.

## \|\| 11.31.23 \|\|

*ye punarnigrahāḥ kecidbrahmādiṣu nidarśitāḥ \|*  
*te 'pi lokahitāyaiva kṛtāḥ śrīkaṇṭhamūrtinā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The instances of killing and curbing pointed out with regard to Brahma and others are those of the activities of Śrīkaṇṭhamūrti performed for the welfare of the worlds.

## \|\| 11.31.24 \|\|

*brahmāṇḍasyādhipatyaṃ hi śrīkaṇṭhasya na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*śrīkaṇṭhākhyāṃ śivo mūrtiṃ krīḍatīmadhitiṣṭhati \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Surely Śrīkaṇṭha has the overlordship of the universe. Śiva presides over the Mūrti Śrīkaṇṭha in the course of his divine sport.

## \|\| 11.31.25 \|\|

*sadoṣā eva devādyā nigṛhītā yathoditam \|*  
*tatastepi vipāpmānaḥ prajāścāpi gatajvarāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Only the gods and others who were faulty were restrained or slain by him as described above. Thereby the gods became sinners and the people free from ailments.

## \|\| 11.31.26 \|\|

*nigraho 'pi svarūpeṇa viduṣāṃ na jugupsitaḥ \|*  
*ata eva hi daṇḍyeṣu daṇḍo rājñāṃ praśasyate \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Restraining or killing as such is not declared despicable by the learned. That is why the punishment meted out by kings to those who deserve it, is commended.

## \|\| 11.31.27 \|\|

*yatsiddhirīśvaratvena kāryavargasya kṛtsnaśaḥ \|*  
*na sa cedīśatāṃ kuryājjagataḥ kathamīśvaraḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. If he does not have that which is achieved through the suzerainty of the whole class of effects how can he rule over the universe?

## \|\| 11.31.28 \|\|

*īśecchā ca vidhātṛtvaṃ vidherājñāpanaṃ param \|*  
*ājñāvaśyamidaṃ kuryānna kuryāditi śāsanam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The wish of the lord comprises the establishment of rules and conditions. Brahmā is the commandment. His order is the mode of direction such as, “This shall be done. This shall not be done.”

## \|\| 11.31.29 \|\|

*tacchāsanānuvartitvaṃ sādhubhāvasya lakṣaṇam \|*  
*viparītasamādhoḥ syānna sarvaṃ tattu dṛśyate \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The characteristic of a man of good nature is the strict adherence to his directives; the opposite thereof is that of the non-saintly one.

## \|\| 11.31.30 \|\|

*sādhu saṃrakṣaṇīyaṃ cedvinivartyamasādhu yat \|*  
*nivartate ca sāmāderaṃte daṇḍo hi sādhanam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. If good nature is to be preserved the evil one is to be eschewed. It is quelled by the expedients of Sāma etc. If other means fail punishment alone is the means.

## \|\| 11.31.31 \|\|

*hitārthalakṣaṇaṃ cedaṃ daṇḍāntamanuśāsanam \|*  
*ato yadviparītaṃ tadahitaṃ saṃpracakṣate \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. This is the characteristic of what is beneficent viz. chastisement ending with disciplinary measures. What is contrary to this is called maleficent.

## \|\| 11.31.32 \|\|

*hite sadā niṣaṇṇānāmīśvarasya nidarśanam \|*  
*sa kathaṃ duṣyate sadbhirasatāmeva nigrahāt \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The lord is the standard example of those who perpetually abide by what is beneficent. How can he be condemned by good men for curbing and killing the evil ones alone.

## \|\| 11.31.33 \|\|

*ayuktakāriṇo loke garhaṇīyāvivekitā \|*  
*yadudvejayate lokantadayuktaṃ pracakṣate \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Perpetrators of improper actions are to be decried and despised by a judicious person. Improper action is that which afflicts and harasses the world.

## \|\| 11.31.34 \|\|

*sarvo 'pi nigraho loke na ca vidveṣapūrvakaḥ \|*  
*na hi dveṣṭi pitā putraṃ yo nigṛhyāti śikṣayet \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Every act of curbing and restraining is not attended with hatred. A father who trains his son even by curbing and restraining ḥim does not hate him.

## \|\| 11.31.35 \|\|

*mādhyasthenāpi nigrāhyānyo nigṛhṇāti mārgataḥ \|*  
*tasyāpyavaśyaṃ yatkiṃcinnairghṛṇyamanuvartate \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. There is bound to be some ruthlessness in him who curbs or slays those worthy of it even by standing detached.

## \|\| 11.31.36 \|\|

*anyathā na hinastyeva sadoṣānapyasau parān \|*  
*hinasti cāyamapyajñānparaṃ mādhyasthyamācaran \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The lord does not injure others though guilty, otherwise. Of course, he injures the ignorant by adopting neutrality.

## \|\| 11.31.37 \|\|

*tasmādduḥkhātmikāṃ hiṃsāṃ kurvāṇo yaḥ sanirghṛṇaḥ \|*  
*iti nirbaṃdhayaṃtyeke niyamo neti cāpare \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Hence we shall say that he who inflicts injury ultimately painful is ruthless. Thus a few insist upon this condition. Others do not.

## \|\| 11.31.38 \|\|

*nidānajñasya bhiṣajo rugṇo hiṃsāṃ prayuṃjataḥ \|*  
*na kiṃcidapi nairghṛṇyaṃ ghṛṇaivātra prayojikā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Ruthlessness cannot be attributed to the surgeon who operates upon the patient. The inducing factor is kindness alone.

## \|\| 11.31.39 \|\|

*ghṛṇāpi na guṇāyaiva hiṃsreṣu pratiyogiṣu \|*  
*tādṛśeṣu ghṛṇī bhrāntyā ghṛṇāntaritanirghṛṇaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Even kindness to violent enemies is not conducive to ultimate good. He who is kind to such persons is ruthless though his ruthlessness is concealed by aft illusory kindness.

## \|\| 11.31.40 \|\|

*upekṣāpīha doṣāha rakṣyeṣu pratiyogiṣu \|*  
*śaktau satyāmupekṣāto rakṣyassadyo vipadyate \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Even neglect and indifference for the opponents who ought to be protected, results in default. He who ought to be protected perishes immediately if neglected despite the capacity of the protector.

## \|\| 11.31.41 \|\|

*sarpasyāsyagatampaśyanyastu rakṣyamupekṣate \|*  
*doṣābhāsānsamutprekṣya phalataḥ so 'pi nirghṛṇaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. He who neglects the man worthy of being protected on considering the apparent defaults though he observes his plight is in effect ruthless.

## \|\| 11.31.42 \|\|

*tasmādghṛṇā guṇāyaiva sarvatheti na saṃmatam \|*  
*saṃmataṃ prāptakāmitvaṃ sarvaṃ tvanyadasammatam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Hence it is not generally agreed that kindliness is conducive to good in every respect. What is admitted is the performance of what is befitting. Everything else is unapproved.

## \|\| 11.31.43-45 \|\|

*mūrtyātmasvapi rāgādyā doṣāḥ santyeva vastutaḥ \|*  
*tathāpi teṣāmevaite na śivasya tu sarvathā \|*  
*agnāvapi samāviṣṭaṃ tāmraṃ khalu sakālikam \|*  
*iti nāgnirasau duṣyettāmrasaṃsargakāraṇāt \|\| 43 \|\|*

*nāgneraśucisaṃsargādaśucitvamapekṣate \|*  
*aśucestvagnisaṃyogācchucitvamapi jāyate \|\| 44 \|\|*

*evaṃ śodhyātmasaṃsargānna hyaśuddhaḥ śivo bhavet \|*  
*śivasaṃsargatastveṣa śodhyātmaiva hi śudhyati \|\| 45 \|\|*

43-45. In reality there are the defects of passion, etc., in the Mūrtyātmans (Sadāśiva, Brahmā and others). Still the defects belong to them alone and not to Śiva. There may be flaw in the copper put in fire but due to its contact fire does not fade. If impure things are consigned to fire they do not make the fire impure. Some impure things become pure due to their contact with fire. Similarly Śiva does not become impure due to the contact with the Ātmans that are to be purified.

## \|\| 11.31.46 \|\|

*ayasyagnau samāviṣṭe dāho 'gnereva nāyasaḥ \|*  
*mūrtātmanyevamaiśvaryamīśvarasyaiva nātmanām \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The Ātman alone is purified through the contact with Śiva. If the iron-rod is put in fire and heated, the burning is that of the fire, not of the iron-rod.

## \|\| 11.31.47 \|\|

*na hi kāṣṭhaṃ jvalatyūrdhvamagnireva jvalatyasau \|*  
*kāṣṭhasyāṃgāratā nāgnerevamatrāpi yojyatām \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. The prosperity, glory etc. of the Mūrtyātmans is really that of lord Śiva and not of the Ātmans. It is the fire, not the fuel, that blazes upwards.

## \|\| 11.31.48-50 \|\|

*ata eva jagatyasminkāṣṭhapāṣāṇamṛtsvapi \|*  
*śivāveśavaśādeva śivatvamupacaryate \|\| 48 \|\|*

*maitryādayo guṇā gauṇāstasmātte bhinnavṛttayaḥ \|*  
*tairguṇairuparaktānāṃ doṣāya ca guṇāya ca \|\| 49 \|\|*

*yattu gauṇamagauṇaṃ ca tatsarvamanugṛhṇataḥ \|*  
*na guṇāya na doṣāya śivasya guṇavṛttayaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

48-50. The state of being the coal belongs to the wood and not to the fire. Similarly Śivatva is imposed on wood, stone and clay. But the attributes Maitrī, etc., are secondary and they act differently. They are conducive to both good and evil to those who are endowed with qualities. What is both secondary and non-secondary is not wholly conducive to good or evil.

## \|\| 11.31.51 \|\|

*na cānugrahaśabdārthaṃ gauṇamāhurvipaścitaḥ \|*  
*saṃsāramocanaṃ kiṃ tu śaivamājñāmayaṃ hitam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Learned men do not say that the meaning of Anugraha is secondary. But the liberation from worldly existence (saṃsāra) is in the form of Ājñā and is beneficent.

## \|\| 11.31.52 \|\|

*hitaṃ tadājñākaraṇaṃ yaddhitaṃ tadanugrahaḥ \|*  
*sarvaṃ hite niyuñjāvaḥ sarvānugrahakārakaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Carrying out his Ājñā is beneficent. What is beneficent is Blessing. He who employs everything in what is beneficent is the cause of blessing to all.

## \|\| 11.31.53 \|\|

*yastūpakāraśabdārthastamapyāhuranugraham \|*  
*tasyāpi hitarūpatvācchivaḥ sarvopakārakaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The sense of the word Upakāra (benevolence) is also Anughraha. Since that too is of beneficent nature Śiva is all-benevolent.

## \|\| 11.31.54-55 \|\|

*hite sadā niyuktaṃ tu sarvaṃ cidacidātmakam \|*  
*svabhāvapratibandhaṃ tatsamaṃ na labhate hitam \|\| 54 \|\|*

*yathā vikāsayatyeva raviḥ padmāni bhānubhiḥ \|*  
*samaṃ na vikasantyeva svasvabhāvānurodhataḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. Everything in the form of sentient and non-sentient is engaged in what is beneficent? But obstructed by their innate nature all do not get the benefit simultaneously. The sun spreads his rays on all the lotuses impartially. But all the flowers do not bloom simultaneously; they do so in accordance with their innate nature.

## \|\| 11.31.56-57 \|\|

*svabhāvo 'pi hi bhāvānāṃ bhāvino 'rthasya kāraṇam \|*  
*na hi svabhāvo naśyantamarthaṃ kartṛṣu sādhayet \|\| 56 \|\|*

*suvarṇameva nāṃgāraṃ drāvayatyagnisaṃgamaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ pakvamalāneva mocayenna śivaparān \|\| 57 \|\|*

56-57. Even the innate nature of the entities is the cause of what is destined to be. The innate nature does not transform that what perishes. The contact with fire melts only gold and not the coal. Śiva liberates those whose ignorance is ripe and not the others.

## \|\| 11.31.58 \|\|

*yadyathā bhavituṃ yogyaṃ tattathā na bhavetsvayam \|*  
*vinā bhāvanayā kartā svatantrassantato bhavet \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. What is capable of becoming does not become so by itself without conception. But the maker needs no such conception and is free perpetually.

## \|\| 11.31.59 \|\|

*svabhāvavimalo yadvatsarvānugrāhakaśśivaḥ \|*  
*svabhāvamalināstadvadātmano jīvasaṃjñitāḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Śiva the blesser is innately pure but the Ātmans (individual souls) are naturally impure.

## \|\| 11.31.60 \|\|

*anyathā saṃsarantyete niyamānna śivaḥ katham \|*  
*karmamāyānubandhosya saṃsāraḥ kathyate budhaiḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Otherwise how is it that they invariably undergo worldly existence and do not merge into Śiva? Being infested by Karman and Māyā is called worldly existence (saṃsāra) by the learned.

## \|\| 11.31.61 \|\|

*anubandho 'yamasyaiva na śivasyeti hetumān \|*  
*sa heturātmanāmeva nijo nāgantuko malaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. There is sufficient cause for this that this infestation is for individual souls and not for Śiva. That cause is the personal but not extraneous dirt.

## \|\| 11.31.62 \|\|

*āgantukatve kasyāpi bhāvyaṃ kenāpi hetunā \|*  
*yo 'yaṃ heturasāvekastvavicitrasvabhāvataḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Should it be extraneous it may happen to anyone through any cause. But this cause is single due to its nature not being variegated.

## \|\| 11.31.63-64 \|\|

*ātmatāyāḥ samatve 'pi baddhā muktāḥ pare yataḥ \|*  
*baddheṣveva punaḥ kecillayabhogādhikārataḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*jñānaiśvaryādivaiṣamyaṃ bhajante sottarādharāḥ \|*  
*kecinmūrtyātmatāṃ yānti kecidāsannagocarāḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

63-64. Though the Ātman-hood is common some are bound and some liberated. Among those in bondage some have differing degrees of knowledge and eminence due to their being inclined towards abstinence and enjoyment. Some attain the status of identicality with the lord. Some attain the state of nearness.

## \|\| 11.31.65 \|\|

*mūrtyātmasu śivāḥ kecidadhvanāṃ mūrdhasu sthitāḥ \|*  
*madhye maheśvarā rudrāstvarvācīnapade sthitāḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Among those who have attained identicality, some are Śivas. They are stationed on the top of the Adhvas (pathways). Maheśvaras are stationed in the middle; Rudras in the lower region.

## \|\| 11.31.66-67 \|\|

*āsanne 'pi ca māyāyāḥ parasmātkāraṇāttrayam \|*  
*tatrāpyātmā sthito 'dhastādantarātmā ca madhyataḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*parastātparamātmeti brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarāḥ \|*  
*vartante vasavaḥ kecitparamātmapadāśrayāḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

66-67. In the vicinity too the three are stationed beyond Māyā: the Ātman is stationed below; the Antarātman is stationed:n the middle and the Paramātman is stationed beyond. They are Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Maheśvara. Some Vasus too are stationed in the region of Paramātman.

## \|\| 11.31.68 \|\|

*antarātmapade kecitkecidātmapade tathā \|*  
*śāntyatītapade śaivāḥ śānte māheśvare tataḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Some are stationed in the region of Antarātman, some in the region of Ātman. In the region of Śāntyatīta Śaivas are stationed and in the Śānta region the Māheśvaras are stationed.

## \|\| 11.31.69 \|\|

*vidyāyāntu yathā raudrāḥ pratiṣṭhāyāṃ tu vaiṣṇavāḥ \|*  
*nivṛttau ca tathātmāno brahmā brahmāṃgayonayaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Just as Raudras are stationed in Vidyā and the Vaiṣṇavas in Pratiṣṭhā, so also the Ātmans. Brahmā and Brahmā-born are stationed in Nivṛtti.

## \|\| 11.31.70 \|\|

*devayonyaṣṭakaṃ mukhyaṃ mānuṣyamatha madhyamam \|*  
*pakṣyādayo 'dhamāḥ pañcayonayastāścaturdaśa \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. The eight groups of Deva-Beings are the chief ones. The human beings constitute the middling. The five Beings birdes \[birds?\] etc. constitute the lower ones. Thus there are fourteen Beings.

## \|\| 11.31.71-72 \|\|

*uttarādharabhāvo 'pi jñeyassaṃsāriṇo malaḥ \|*  
*yathāmabhāvo muktasya pūrvaṃ paścāttu pakvatā \|\| 71 \|\|*

*malo 'pyāmaśca pakvaśca bhavetsaṃsārakāraṇam \|*  
*āme tvadharatā puṃsāṃ pakve tūttaratā kramāt \|\| 72 \|\|*

71-72. The state of being chief or subsidiary shall be known as the dirt of the worldly being. Just as the food we take in has two states, the undigested and the digested, so the dirt too. When it is undigested the men go lower down; when it is digested they go up. Thus the dirt plays its part in the worldly existence (saṃsāra).

## \|\| 11.31.73 \|\|

*paśvātmānastridhābhinnā ekadvitrimalāḥ kramāt \|*  
*atrottarā ekamalā dvimalā madhyamā matāḥ \|*  
*trimalāstvadhamā jñeyā yathottaramadhiṣṭhitāḥ \|*  
*trimalānadhitiṣṭhaṃti dvimalaikamalāḥ kramāt \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. The individual souls are threefold: those with single dirt, with two dirts and with three dirts. Those with single dirt are the higher ones, those with two dirts the middlings and those with three dirts shall be known meanest. Thus they are stationed in order.

## \|\| 11.31.74 \|\|

*itthamaupādhiko bhedo viśvasya parikalpitaḥ \|*  
*ekadvitrimalānsarvāñchiva eko 'dhitiṣṭhati \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Those with three dirts are presided over by those with two dirts and those in turn are presided over by those with single dirt. Thus is the conditioned difference in the universe.

## \|\| 11.31.75 \|\|

*aśivātmakamapyetacchivenādhiṣṭhitaṃ yathā \|*  
*arudrātmakamityevaṃ rudrairjagadadhiṣṭhitam \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Śiva presides over all these, those with single, two and three dirts. Though they are of non-Śiva nature they are presided over by Śiva.

## \|\| 11.31.76 \|\|

*aṇḍāntā hi mahābhūmiśśatarudrādyadhiṣṭhitā \|*  
*māyāntamantarikṣaṃ tu hyamareśādibhiḥ kramāt \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Similarly the universe which is not in the nature of Rudra is presided over by Rudras. The Mahābhūmi, ending with the cosmic Egg, is presided over by Śatarudra etc.

## \|\| 11.31.77 \|\|

*aṃguṣṭhamātraparyantaissamaṃtātsaṃtataṃ tatam \|*  
*mahāmāyāvasānā dyaurvāyvādyairbhuvanādhipaiḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. The atmosphere ending with Māyā is pervaded in order by the lords of gods of the size of the thumb all round.

## \|\| 11.31.78 \|\|

*anāśritāntairadhvāntarvartibhissamadhiṣṭhitāḥ \|*  
*te hi sākṣāddiviṣadastvantarikṣasadastathā \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. The heaven ending with Mahāmāyā is presided over by the lords of worlds, Vāyu, etc., which are stationed within the Adhvas and whose ends are not resorted to. (?)

## \|\| 11.31.79 \|\|

*pṛthivīpada ityevaṃ devā devavrataiḥ stutā \|*  
*evantribhirmalairāmaiḥ pakvaireva pṛthakpṛthak \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. They are the squatters in heaven, atmosphere and earth. They are the gods observing the rites of the gods.

## \|\| 11.31.80 \|\|

*nidānabhūtaissaṃsārarogaḥ puṃsāṃ pravartate \|*  
*asya rogasya bhaiṣajyaṃ jñānameva na cāparam \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Thus functions the ailment of worldly existence (saṃsāra) with the three dirts and their pathological reasons separately, whether ripe or unripe.

## \|\| 11.31.81 \|\|

*bhiṣagājñāpakaḥ śambhuśśivaḥ paramakāraṇam \|*  
*aduḥkhenā 'pi śakto 'sau paśūnmocayituṃ śivaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. The medicine for this ailment is the perfect knowledge of Śiva and nothing else. The physician is the lord Śiva himself who heals the sufferer.

## \|\| 11.31.82 \|\|

*kathaṃ duḥkhaṃ karotīti nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|*  
*duḥkhameva hi sarvo 'pi saṃsāra iti niścitam \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. In this regard no doubt need be entertained—“Śiva can liberate the souls without subjecting them to misery. Why does he then subject them to misery?”

## \|\| 11.31.83 \|\|

*kathaṃ duḥkhamaduḥkhaṃ syātsvabhāvo hyaviparyayaḥ \|*  
*na hi rogī hyarogī syādbhiṣagbhaiṣajyakāraṇāt \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. It is certain that the entire worldly existence is misery itself. How can misery be non-misery? The innate nature cannot be otherwise.

## \|\| 11.31.84 \|\|

*rogārtaṃ tu bhiṣagrogādbhaiṣajaissukhamuddharet \|*  
*evaṃ svabhāvamalinānsvabhāvādduḥkhinaḥ paśūn \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. A patient does not become non-patient merely because the physician administers medicine. The physician redeems the patient from the sickness through the medicines.

## \|\| 11.31.85 \|\|

*svājñauṣadhavidhānena duḥkhānmocayate śivaḥ \|*  
*na bhiṣakkāraṇaṃ roge śivaḥ saṃsārakāraṇam \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Similarly, through the administration of the medicine in the form of his Ājñā, Śiva liberates the souls from misery—the souls innately dirty and innately miserable.

## \|\| 11.31.86 \|\|

*ityetadapi vaiṣamyaṃ na doṣāyāsya kalpate \|*  
*duḥkhe svabhāvasaṃsiddhe kathantatkāraṇaṃ śivaḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. This inequality like the physician is not the cause of the ailment. So Śiva is the cause of worldly existence need not be a symbol of defect.

## \|\| 11.31.87 \|\|

*svābhāviko malaḥ puṃsāṃ sa hi saṃsārayatyamūn \|*  
*saṃsārakāraṇaṃ yattu malaṃ māyādyacetanam \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. When misery is innately acquired how can Śiva be its cause? The dirt is inborn in men. It is that which makes them undergo the sufferings of worldly existence.

## \|\| 11.31.88 \|\|

*tatsvayaṃ na pravarteta śivasānnidhyamantarā \|*  
*yathā maṇirayaskāṃtassānnidhyādupakārakaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. The dirt which is the cause of worldly existence (saṃsāra), the insentient Māyā, etc., cannot function by itself without the proximity of Siva.

## \|\| 11.31.89 \|\|

*ayasaścalatastadvacchivo 'pyasyeti sūrayaḥ \|*  
*na nivartayituṃ śakyaṃ sānnidhyaṃ sadakāraṇam \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. The wise say just as the magnetic stone causes the movement of the iron filings by its mere proximity, so also Śiva causes the movement of the world.

## \|\| 11.31.90 \|\|

*adhiṣṭhātā tato nityamajñāto jagataśśivaḥ \|*  
*na śivena vinā kiṃcitpravṛttamiha vidyate \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. It is not possible to avoid the proximity of Sat without its cause. Moreover the presiding deity Śiva is even unknown to the universe.

## \|\| 11.31.91 \|\|

*tatpreritamidaṃ sarvaṃ tathāpi na sa muhyati \|*  
*śaktirājñātmikā tasya niyantrī viśvatomukhī \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. Nothing functions without Śiva. Everything is induced by him. Still he is not deluded.

## \|\| 11.31.92 \|\|

*tayā tatamidaṃ śaśvattathāpi sa na duṣyati \|*  
*anidaṃ prathamaṃ sarvamīśitavyaṃ sa īśvaraḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. His Śakti in the form of Ājñā is the all-round restraining factor. This universe is perpetually covered over by it. Still he is not defiled.

## \|\| 11.31.93 \|\|

*īśanācca tadīyājñā tathāpi sa na duṣyati \|*  
*yo 'nyathā manyate mohātsa vinaṣyati durmatiḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. This is ruled over even from the beginning. He is the lord. His ruling is his Ājñā. Still he is not defiled.

## \|\| 11.31.94 \|\|

*tacchaktivaibhavādeva tathāpi sa na duṣyati \|*  
*etasminnaṃtare vyomnaḥ śrutāḥ vāgarīriṇī \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. He who considers otherwise due to delusion is evil-minded. He perishes and that too due to the power of his Śakti. Still he is not defiled.

## \|\| 11.31.95 \|\|

*satyamomamṛtaṃ saumyamityāvirabhavatsphuṭam \|*  
*tato hṛṣṭatarāḥ sarve vinaṣṭāśeṣasaṃśayāḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. In the meantime an unembodied voice was heard from the sky. “Satyam (Truth), Amṛtam (nectar), Saumyam” (gentle), Om Amen. This sound came out clearly.

## \|\| 11.31.96 \|\|

*munayo vismayāviṣṭāḥ preṇemuḥ pavanaṃ prabhum \|*  
*tathā vigatasandehānkṛtvāpi pavano munīn \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. Then the sages were surprised and delighted; their doubts were quelled. They bowed to the lord, the wind-god.

## \|\| 11.31.97 \|\|

*naite pratiṣṭhitajñānā iti matvaivamabravīt \|*  
*vāyuruvācva \|*  
*parokṣamaparokṣaṃ ca dvividhaṃ jñānamiṣyate \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. Although he had cleared their doubts he thought that their knowledge was not firmly established. So he said:

## \|\| 11.31.98 \|\|

*parokṣamasthiraṃ prāhuraparokṣaṃ tu susthiram \|*  
*hetūpadeśagamyaṃ yattatparokṣaṃ pracakṣate \|\| 98 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

98\. Knowledge is of two types: indirect and direct. They say that the former is unsteady and the latter is stable.

## \|\| 11.31.99 \|\|

*aparokṣaṃ punaḥ śreṣṭhādanuṣṭhānādbhaviṣyati \|*  
*nāparokṣādṛte mokṣa iti kṛtvā viniścayam \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. What is acquired by reasoning and instructions is the indirect knowledge. The direct knowledge results from the practice of rites.

## \|\| 11.31.100 \|\|

*śreṣṭhānuṣṭhānasiddhyarthaṃ prayatadhvamatandritāḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. Coming to the conclusion that salvation is not possible without direct knowledge, strive assiduously for the acquisition of practice.

## Chapter 32 - The description of excellent practice

## \|\| 11.32.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kiṃ tacchreṣṭamanuṣṭhānaṃ mokṣo yenaparokṣitaḥ \|*  
*tattasya sādhanaṃ cādya vaktumarhasi māruta \|\| 1 \|\|*

The sages said:—

1\. What is that excellent practice of holy rites, whereby salvation is directly acquired? O Māruta, it behoves you to explain it as well as its means.

## \|\| 11.32.2 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*śaivo hi paramo dharmaḥ śreṣṭhānuṣṭhānaśabditaḥ \|*  
*yatrāparokṣo lakṣyeta sākṣānmokṣapradaḥ śivaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

2\. What is termed excellent practice is the great cult of Śiva wherein Śiva the bestower of salvation is directly perceived.

## \|\| 11.32.3 \|\|

*sa tu pañcavidho jñeyaḥ pañcabhiḥ parvabhiḥ kramāt \|*  
*kriyātapojapadhyānajñānātmabhiranuttaraiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. It is fivefold divided into five sections, holy rites, penance, japa, meditation and knowledge

## \|\| 11.32.4 \|\|

*taireva sottaraissiddho dharmastu paramo mataḥ \|*  
*parokṣamaparokṣaṃ ca jñānaṃ yatra ca mokṣadam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The five activities along with attendant virtuous rites constitute the greatest Dharma. Thereby one attains the direct and indirect knowledge that bestows salvation.

## \|\| 11.32.5 \|\|

*paramo 'paramaścobhau dharmau hi śruticoditau \|*  
*dharmaśabdābhidheyerthe pramāṇaṃ śrutireva naḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The two Dharmas the higher and secondary are mentioned in the Vedas. In the matter of Dharma the Vedas constitute the final authority for us.

## \|\| 11.32.6 \|\|

*paramo yogaparyanto dharmaḥ śrutiśirogataḥ \|*  
*dharmastvaparamastadvadadhaḥ śrutimukhotthitaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The higher dharma upto the practice of Yoga is mentioned in the Vedantic section of the Vedas. The secondary Dharma is mentioned in the Karmakāṇḍa section of the same.

## \|\| 11.32.7 \|\|

*apaśvātmādhikāratvādyo dharamaḥ paramo mataḥ \|*  
*sādhāraṇastato 'nyastu sarveṣāmadhikārataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The Ātmans freed from Pāśa are authorised in the higher Dharma and in the other one, every one is authorised.

## \|\| 11.32.8 \|\|

*sa cāyaṃ paramo dharmaḥ paradharmasya sādhanam \|*  
*dharmaśāstrādibhissamyaksāṃga evopabṛṃhitaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. This higher Dharma is the means for achieving the greatest virtue of Śiva. It shall be supplemented in all parts by Dhasmaśāstras and other holy treatises.

## \|\| 11.32.9 \|\|

*śaivo yaḥ paramo dharmaḥ śreṣṭhānuṣṭhānaśabditaḥ \|*  
*itihāsapurāṇābhyāṃ kathaṃcidupabṛṃhitaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The greatest Dharma of Śiva termed the excellent practice is explained in the Itihāsas and the Purāṇas.

## \|\| 11.32.10 \|\|

*śaivāgamaistu saṃpannaḥ sahāṃgopāṃvistaraḥ \|*  
*tatsaṃskārādhikāraiśca samyagevopabṛṃhitaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. In the Śaiva Āgamas a detailed explanation of every thing including the consecratory rites is given.

## \|\| 11.32.11 \|\|

*śaivāgamo hi dvividhaḥ śrauto 'śrautaśca saṃskṛtaḥ \|*  
*śrutisāramayaḥ śrautassvataṃtra itaro mataḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The Śaiva Āgama is of two varieties: Śrauta and Aśrauta. The Śrauta consists of condensed Vedic texts; the other one consists of independent texts but well consecrated.

## \|\| 11.32.12 \|\|

*svataṃtro daśadhā pūrvaṃ tathāṣṭādaśadhā punaḥ \|*  
*kāmikādisamākhyābhissiddhaḥ siddhāntasaṃjñitaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The independent texts were originally ten but supplemented subsequently by eight more so as to constitute eighteen texts. They are called Kāmika etc., and the entire literature is called “Śaiva Siddhānta”

## \|\| 11.32.13 \|\|

*śrutisāramayo yastu śatakoṭipravistaraḥ \|*  
*paraṃ pāśupataṃ yatra vrataṃ jñānaṃ ca kathyate \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The Śrauta literature consists of a billion verses. In it the Pāśupata Vrata and Jñāna are explained.

## \|\| 11.32.14 \|\|

*yugāvarteṣu śiṣyeta yogācāryasvarūpiṇā \|*  
*tatratatrāvatīrṇena śivenaiva pravartyate \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. In every circle of Yugas, Śiva incarnates as Yogācārya in different places and propagates yoga.

## \|\| 11.32.15 \|\|

*saṃkṣipyāsya pravaktāraścatvāraḥ paramarṣaya \|*  
*rururdadhīco 'gastyaśca upamanyurmahāyaśāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The four great sages Ruru, Dadhīca, Agastya and the renowned Upamanyu have condensed these principles and propagated them.

## \|\| 11.32.16 \|\|

*te ca pāśupatā jñeyāssaṃhitānāṃ pravartakāḥ \|*  
*tatsaṃtatīyā guravaḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. They are all Pāśupatas and exponents of the Saṃhitās. Hundreds and thousands of their descendants have been the preceptors of their principles.

## \|\| 11.32.17 \|\|

*tatroktaḥ paramo dharmaścaryādyātmā caturvidhaḥ \|*  
*teṣu pāśupato yogaḥ śivaṃ pratyakṣayeddṛḍham \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The great virtue of Śiva mentioned before is four-fold with regular performance and observance as the basic Atman for them. Among them the Pāśupata yoga facilitates the direct perception of Siva.

## \|\| 11.32.18 \|\|

*tasmācchreṣṭhamanuṣṭhānaṃ yogaḥ pāśupato mataḥ \|*  
*tatrāpyupāyako yukto brahmaṇā sa tu kathyate \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Hence the excellent practice is this Pāśupata Yoga. The mode of it as practised by Brahmā shall now be mentioned.

## \|\| 11.32.19 \|\|

*nāmāṣṭakamayo yogaśśivena parikalpitaḥ \|*  
*tena yogena sahasā śaivī prajñā prajāyate \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. This is Nāmāṣṭakayoga prescribed by Śiva himself. By means of this Yoga the discernment of Śiva is generated.

## \|\| 11.32.20 \|\|

*prajñayā paramaṃ jñānamacirāllabhate sthiram \|*  
*prasīdati śivastasya yasya jñānaṃ pratiṣṭhitam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Through this discernment the stable and perfect knowledge is attained ere long. Śiva is delighted with him whose knowledge is well-founded.

## \|\| 11.32.21 \|\|

*prasādātparamo yogo yaḥ śivaṃ cāparokṣayet \|*  
*śivāparokṣātsaṃsārakāraṇena viyujyate \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Thanks to his grace the great Yoga is attained which facilitates the direct perception of Śiva. By perceiving Śiva directly the cause of worldly existence (saṃsāra) is quelled.

## \|\| 11.32.22 \|\|

*tataḥ syānmuktasaṃsāro muktaḥ śivasamo bhavet \|*  
*brahmaprokta ityupāyaḥ sa eva pṛthagucyate \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Then the devotee is liberated from worldly existence and being liberated he becomes identical with Śiva. The means mentioned by Brahmā is now separately mentioned here.

## \|\| 11.32.23-24 \|\|

*śivo maheśvaraścaiva rudro viṣṇuḥ pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*saṃsāravaidyaḥ sarvajñaḥ paramātmeti mukhyataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*nāmāṣṭakamidaṃ mukhyaṃ śivasya pratipādakam \|*  
*ādyantu pañcakaṃ jñeyaṃ śāntyatītādyanukramāt \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. Śiva, Maheśvara, Rudra, Viṣṇu, Pitāmaha, Samsāravaidya, Sarvajña and Paramātman—these eight names mainly indicate Śiva. The first five are the names of the deities presiding over the Kalās, Śāntyatīta etc.

## \|\| 11.32.25-28 \|\|

*saṃjñā sadāśivādīnāṃ pañcopādhiparigrahāt \|*  
*upādhivinivṛttau tu yathāsvaṃ vinivartate \|\| 25 \|\|*

*padameva hi tannityamanityāḥ padinaḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*padānāṃ pratikṛttau tu mucyante padino yataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*parivṛttyantare bhūyastatpadaprāptirucyate \|*  
*ātmāntarābhidhānaṃ syādyadādyaṃ nāma pañcakam \|\| 27 \|\|*

*anyattu tritayaṃ nāmnāmupādānādiyogataḥ \|*  
*trividhopādhivacanācchiva evānuvartate \|\| 28 \|\|*

25-28. The five names of Sadāśiva originate from the conditioning factors. When the conditioning factors cease to exist they too recede. The region is eternal and the Ātmans who occupy them are non-eternal. When the Padas are changed the Padins are released. In another evolution they attain the same region. But the first five Ātmans undergo the change of names. The last three names are due to the adoption of the three conditioning factors. They indicate only Śiva.

## \|\| 11.32.29-30 \|\|

*anādimalasaṃśleṣaḥ prāgabhāvātsvabhāvataḥ \|*  
*atyaṃtaṃ pariśuddhātmetyato 'yaṃ śiva ucyate \|\| 29 \|\|*

*athavāśeṣakalyāṇaguṇaikadhana īśvaraḥ \|*  
*śiva ityucyate sadbhiśśivatattvārthavādibhiḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. He who is naturally pure is called Śiva. He has the antecedent non-existence of the contact of the primordial dirt. Or, he who is full of good attributes and is Īśvara is called Śiva by good men who propound the Śaivite principles.

## \|\| 11.32.31-35 \|\|

*trayoviṃśatitattvebhyaḥ prakṛtirhi parā matā \|*
