*prakṛtestu paraṃ prāhuḥ puruṣaṃ pañcaviṃśakam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*yaṃ vedādau svaraṃ prāhurvācyavācakabhāvataḥ \|*  
*vedaikavedyayāthātmyādvedānte ca pratiṣṭhitaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*tasya prakṛtilīnasya yaḥ parassa maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*tadadhīnapravṛttitvātprakṛteḥ puruṣasya ca \|\| 33 \|\|*

*athavā triguṇaṃ tattvamupeyamidamavyayam \|*  
*māyāntu prakṛtiṃ vidyānmāyinaṃ tu maheśvaram \|\| 34 \|\|*

*māyāvikṣobhako 'naṃto maheśvarasamanvayāt \|*  
*kālātmā paramātmādiḥ sthūlaḥ sūkṣmaḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

31-35. The name Maheśvara is explained thus: Prakṛti is greater than the twenty-three principles. Puruṣa the twenty fifth principle is greater than Prakṛti. Puruṣa is Praṇava the first Svara in the Vedas. Since his real nature is comprehensible only through the Vedas he is established in the Vedānta. He who is beyond this Puruṣa, who is associated with Prakṛti is Maheśvara because both the Prakṛti and Puruṣa function in subservience to him. Or, Maheśvara is the wielder of Māyā. Māyā is Prakṛti the principle with the three Guṇas. It is unchanging. He who makes this Māyā energetic is Maheśvara. He is glorified as Kālātman, Paramātman, the primordial, the gross and the subtle.

## \|\| 11.32.36 \|\|

*rudduḥkhaṃ duḥkhaheturvā tadrāvayati naḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*rudra ityucyate sadbhiḥ śivaḥ paramakāraṇam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The explanation of the word Rudra:—‘Rud’ means misery and ‘Drāvayati’ means ‘routs’. Since the lord quells our misery he is called Rudra. He is Śiva, the great cause.

## \|\| 11.32.37 \|\|

*tattvādibhūtaparyantaṃ śarīrādiṣvatandritaḥ \|*  
*vyāpyādhitiṣṭhati śivastato rudra itastataḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Śiva pervades all living beings, the principles and elements. He is wakefully present in the bodies and presides over them. Hence he is called Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 11.32.38 \|\|

*jagataḥ pitṛbhūtānāṃ śivo mūrtyātmanāmapi \|*  
*pitṛbhāvena sarveṣāṃ pitāmaha udīritaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Śiva is the progenitor of the souls that have attained the status of fathers. He is therefore called the grandfather.

## \|\| 11.32.39-40 \|\|

*nidānajño yathā vaidyo rogasya vinivartakaḥ \|*  
*upāyairbheṣajaistadvallayabhogādhikārataḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*saṃsārasyeśvaro nityaṃ samūlasya nivartakaḥ \|*  
*saṃsāravaidya ityuktaḥ sarvatattvārthavedibhiḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. Śiva is called the physician of the universe. Just as the physician who is conversant with the pathology diagnoses and cures the ailment with medicines so also the lord annihilates the worldly existence (saṃsāra) along with its roots. He is so called by all those who understand the nature of principles.

## \|\| 11.32.41-43 \|\|

*daśārthajñānasiddhyarthamindriyeṣveṣu satsvapi \|*  
*trikālabhāvino bhāvānsthūlānsūkṣmānaśeṣataḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*aṇavo naiva jānanti māyayaiva malāvṛtāḥ \|*  
*asatsvapi ca sarveṣu sarvārthajñānahetuṣu \|\| 42 \|\|*

*yadyathāvasthitaṃ vastu tattathaiva sadāśivaḥ \|*  
*ayatnenaiva jānāti tasmātsarvajña ucyate \|\| 43 \|\|*

41-43. Even when they have the sense-organs for comprehending the ten objects of sensual perception, the atoms do not know the beings gross and subtle, present in the three periods of time, in their entirety because they are hidden by the particles of dirt in the form of Māyā, whereas Sadāśiva has not these causes of perception. Even when they are not present, he knows without any strain every object as it is. Hence, he is Sarvajña (omniscient).

## \|\| 11.32.44 \|\|

*sarvātmā paramairebhirguṇairnityasamanvayāt \|*  
*svasmātparātmavirahātparamātmā śivaḥ svayam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Śiva is the Ātman of all. He perpetually possesses all these qualities. There is no greater Ātman than Śiva. Śiva is Paramātman.

## \|\| 11.32.45-47 \|\|

*nāmāṣṭakamidaṃ caiva labdhvācāryaprasādataḥ \|*  
*nivṛttyādikalāgranthiṃ śivādyaiḥ pañcanāmabhiḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*yathāsvaṃ kramaśaśchitvā śodhayitvā yathāguṇam \|*  
*guṇitaireva soddhātairaniruddhairathāpi vā \|\| 46 \|\|*

*hṛtkaṇṭhatālubhrūmadhyabrahmarandhrasamanvitām \|*  
*chittvā paryaṣṭakākāraṃ svātmānaṃ ca suṣumṇayā \|\| 47 \|\|*

45-47. By the grace of the preceptor the eight names shall be acquired. The knots of the Kalā, Nivṛtti and others shall be cut off with the five names of Śiva and purified by repetitions, strokes and non-restraints. By means of the Suṣumṇā, the Puryaṣṭaka alone with the chest, neck, palate, middle of the eyebrows and the hole on the top of the head, shall be cut off.

## \|\| 11.32.48-49 \|\|

*dvādaśāṃtaḥsthitasyendornītvopari śivaujasi \|*  
*saṃhṛtyaṃ vadanaṃ paścādyathāsaṃskaraṇaṃ layāt \|\| 48 \|\|*

*śāktenāmṛtavarṣeṇa saṃsiktāyāṃ tanau punaḥ \|*  
*avatārya svamātmānamamṛtātmākṛtiṃ hṛdi \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. The Ātman shall be taken above to the splendour of Śiva beyond the moon stationed in the twelve-petal led lotus of the heart. The mouth is shrunk in size. The body is drenched with the shower of the nectar of the Śakti and merged in their reasons. The Ātman is then let down into the heart.

## \|\| 11.32.50-52 \|\|

*dvādaśāṃtaḥsthitasyendoḥ parastācchvetapaṃkaje \|*  
*samāsīnaṃ mahādevaṃ śaṃkarambhaktavatsalam \|\| 50 \|\|*

*ardhanārīśvaraṃ devaṃ nirmalaṃ madhurākṛtim \|*  
*śuddhasphaṭikasaṃkāśaṃ prasannaṃ śītaladyutim \|\| 51 \|\|*

*dhyātvā hi mānase devaṃ svasthacitto 'tha mānavaḥ \|*  
*śivanāmāṣṭakenaiva bhāvapuṣpaissamarcayet \|\| 52 \|\|*

50-52. The devotee then meditates on the great god Śiva, favourably disposed to his devotees who is conceived as sitting in the white twelve-petalled lotus beyond the moon, who in the sweet crystal-pure, delighted, cool, lustrous form of Ardhanārīśvara, shall be meditated upon. The devotee shall have the mind in normal state. He shall then worship the lord with the eight names of Śiva and the sacred flowers.

## \|\| 11.32.53 \|\|

*abhyarcanānte tu punaḥ prāṇānāyamya mānavaḥ \|*  
*samyakcittaṃ samādhāya śārvaṃ nāmāṣṭakaṃ japet \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. At the end of the worship the devotee shall perform Prāṇāyāma and concentrate the mind well. He shall perform the japa of the eight names of Śiva.

## \|\| 11.32.54-56 \|\|

*nābhau cāṣṭāhutīrhutvā pūrṇāhutyā namastataḥ \|*  
*aṣṭapuṣpapradānena kṛtvābhyarcanamaṃtimam \|\| 54 \|\|*

*nivedayetsvamātmānaṃ culukodakavartmanā \|*  
*evaṃ kṛtvā cirādeva jñānaṃ pāśupataṃ śubham \|\| 55 \|\|*

*labhate tatpratiṣṭhāṃ ca vṛttaṃ cānuttamaṃ tathā \|*  
*yogaṃ ca paramaṃ labdhvā mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

54-56. He shall perform eight Āhutis in the navel and repeat “Namaḥ” alone with the Pūrṇāhūti, offering eight flowers and conclude worship. With a palmful of water he shall dedicate his Ātman. By doing this, ere long, the auspicious knowledge of Pāśupata cult is obtained. He acquires its magnificent status and the excellent conduct. Then securing the great Yoga he is liberated. There is no doubt in this.

## Chapter 33 - Rules governing Pāśupatavrata

## \|\| 11.33.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*bhagavañchrotumicchāmo vrataṃ pāśupataṃ param \|*  
*brahmādayo 'pi yatkṛtvā sarve pāśupatāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

The sages said:—

1\. O holy lord, we wish to hear of the great Pāśupatavrata on performing which Brahmā and others have become Pāśupatas.

## \|\| 11.33.2 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*rahasyaṃ vaḥ pravakṣyāmi sarvapāpanikṛntanam \|*  
*vrataṃ pāśupataṃ śrautamatharvaśirasi śrutam \|\| 2 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

2\. I shall tell you the great secret, Pāśupata-vrata that quells all sins. It is mentioned in the upaniṣad Atharvaśiras.

## \|\| 11.33.3 \|\|

*kālaścaitrī paurṇamāsī deśaḥ śivaparigrahaḥ \|*  
*kṣetrārāmādyaraṇyaṃ vā praśastaśśubhalakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3..The time is the month of Chaitra and the full-moon-day therein. The place is anywhere acceptable to Śiva having good characteristics. It shall be auspicious, say, the garden in a holy centre or a forest.

## \|\| 11.33.4-9 \|\|

*tatra pūrvaṃ trayodaśyāṃ susnātaḥ sukṛtāhnikaḥ \|*  
*anujñāpya svamācāryaṃ saṃpūjya praṇipatya ca \|\| 4 \|\|*

*pūjāṃ vaiśeṣikīṃ kṛtvā śuklāṃbaradharaḥ svayam \|*  
*śuklayajñopavītī ca śuklamālyānulepanaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*darbhāsane samāsīno darbhamuṣṭiṃ pragṛhya ca \|*  
*prāṇāyāmatrayaṃ kṛtvā prāṅmukho vāpyudaṅmukhaḥ \|*  
*dhyātvā devaṃ ca devīṃ ca tadvijñāpanavartmanā \|*  
*vratametatkaromīti bhavetsaṃkalpya dīkṣitaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*yāvaccharīrapātaṃ vā dvādaśābdamathāpi vā \|*  
*tadardhaṃ vā tadardhaṃ vā māsadvādaśakaṃ tu vā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tadardhaṃ vā tadardhaṃ vā māsamekamathāpi vā \|*  
*dinadvādaśakaṃ vā 'tha dinaṣaṭkamathāpi vā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tadardhaṃ dinamekaṃ vā vratasaṃkalpanāvadhi \|*  
*agnimādhāya vidhivadvirajāhomakāraṇāt \|\| 9 \|\|*

4-9. There, first of all, on the thirteenth day he shall perform the special worship after taking his bath and performing the daily rites. He shall take the formal permission of the preceptor after bowing to him and honouring him. He shall wear pure white cloths. The sacred thread shall be white. He shall wear a garland of white flowers. White unguent shall be measured over the body. He shall be seated on Darbha grass. He shall hold a handful of Darbha grass, sit facing east or the north. After performing the Prāṇāyāma three times he shall meditate on the lord and the goddess. By way of submitting to them he shall perform the Saṅkalpa saying, “I am performing this Vrata (of Pāśupata) The time limit for this Vrata is till death, or twelve years or six years, or three years or twelve months, or six months or three months or a month or twelve days or six days or three days or one day.

## \|\| 11.33.10-11 \|\|

*hutvājyena samidbhiśca caruṇā ca yathākramam \|*  
*pūrṇāmāpūrya tāṃ bhūyastattvānāṃ śuddhimuddiśan \|\| 10 \|\|*

*juhuyānmūlamantreṇa taireva samidādibhiḥ \|*  
*tattvānyetāni maddehe śuddhyaṃtām 1 tyanusmaran \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. He shall arrange the sacrificial fire duly as in the Virajāhoma. He shall make the offerings of ghee, sacrificial twigs and caru and perform homa. After the Pūrṇāhūti, deserving the purity of the Tattvas, he shall perform the homa with the five-syllabled mantra and the sacrificial twigs.

## \|\| 11.33.12-15 \|\|

*pañcabhūtāni tanmātrāḥ pañcakarmendriyāṇi ca \|*  
*jñānakarmavibhedena pañcakarmavibhāgaśaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tvagādidhātavassapta pañca prāṇādivāyavaḥ \|*  
*manobuddhirahaṃ khyātirguṇāḥ prakṛtipūruṣau \|\| 13 \|\|*

*rāgo vidyākale caiva niyatiḥ kāla eva ca \|*  
*māyā ca śuddhividyā ca maheśvarasadāśivau \|\| 14 \|\|*

*śaktiśca śivatattvaṃ ca tattvāni kramaśo viduḥ \|*  
*mantraistu virajairhutvā hotāsau virajā bhavet \|\| 15 \|\|*

12-15. In the course of the sacrifice -he shall think thus—“Let the Tattvas in my body be purified.” The Tattvas are:—The five elements, the five Tanmātras, the five sense-organs of knowledge, the five organs of activity, the seven Dhātus beginning with the skin, the five vital airs beginning with Prāṇa, mind, intellect, ego, the three Guṇas, Prakṛti, Puruṣa, Rāga (passion), Vidyā, Kalā, Niyati, Time, Mayā, pure Vidyā, Maheśvara, Sadāśiva, Śakti and Śiva Tattva.

## \|\| 11.33.16 \|\|

*śivānugrahamāsādya jñānavānsa hi jāyate \|*  
*atha gomayamādāya piṇḍīkṛtyābhimaṃtrya ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. After performing the Homa with the Viraja mantras he is freed from sin. Attaining Śiva’s blessing he is endowed with perfect knowledge.

## \|\| 11.33.17 \|\|

*vinyasyāgnau ca samprokṣya dine tasminhaviṣyabhuk \|*  
*prabhāte tu caturdaśyāṃ kṛtvā sarvaṃ puroditam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. He shall collect cowdung and roll it into balls and repeat the mantras over them. He shall place these into the fire and sprinkle with water. That day he shall take in only the cooked rice soaked in ghee.

## \|\| 11.33.18 \|\|

*dine tasminnirāhāraḥ kālaṃ śeṣaṃ samāpayet \|*  
*prātaḥ parvaṇi cāpyevaṃ kṛtvā homā vasānataḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. On the morning of the fourteenth day he shall perform everything as mentioned before. On that day he shall observe fast and thus spend the latter part of the day.

## \|\| 11.33.19 \|\|

*upasaṃhṛtya rudrāgniṃ gṛhṇīyādbhasma yatnataḥ \|*  
*tataśca jaṭilo muṇḍī śikhaikajaṭa eva vā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. On the full moon day also he shall perform similar rites. At the conclusion of the sacrifice the sacred fire shall be extinguished and the ashes gathered assiduously.

## \|\| 11.33.20 \|\|

*bhūtvā snātvā tato vītalajjaścetsyāddigambaraḥ \|*  
*api kāṣāyavasanaścarmacīrāmbaro 'tha vā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Thereafter he shall keep matted hair or shave off the hair completely or keep one matted tuft of hair. He shall take bath then. If he is not extremely bashful he shall remain naked thereafter.

## \|\| 11.33.21 \|\|

*ekāmbaro valkalī vā bhaveddaṇḍī ca mekhalī \|*  
*prakṣālya caraṇau paścāddvirācamyātmanastanum \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Or he can wear ochre robes, hide or barks of trees. Only a single cloth or a single bark garment shall be worn. He shall have the staff and the girdle.

## \|\| 11.33.22-23 \|\|

*saṃkulīkṛtya tadbhasma virajānalasaṃbhavam \|*  
*agnirityādibhirmaṃtraiḥ ṣaḍbhirātharvaṇaiḥ kramāt \|\| 22 \|\|*

*vibhṛjyāṃgāni mūrdhādicaraṇāṃtāni taisspṛśet \|*  
*tatastena krameṇaiva samuddhṛtya ca bhasmanā \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. He shall wash the feet and perform Ācamana twice. He shall apply the ashes taken out of the Viraja fire all over his body from head to foot repeating the six mantras beginning with “Agniriti” from the Ātharvaṇa texts.

## \|\| 11.33.24 \|\|

*sarvāṃgoddhūlanaṃ kuryātpraṇavena śivena vā \|*  
*tatastripuṇḍraṃ racayettriyāyuṣasamāhvayam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Then in the same way he shall dust the body entirely repeating the Praṇava Oṃ and ‘Śiva’.

## \|\| 11.33.25 \|\|

*śivabhāvaṃ samāgamya śivayogamathācaret \|*  
*kuryātstrisandhyamapyevametatpāśupataṃ vratam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Then repeating the mantra ‘Triyāyuṣam’ he shall wear Tripuṇḍra marks. He shall realise his own Śiva-hood and perform ‘Śivayoga’.

## \|\| 11.33.26 \|\|

*bhuktimuktipradaṃ caitatpaśutvaṃ vinivartayet \|*  
*tatpaśutvaṃ parityajya kṛtvā pāśupataṃ vratam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. He shall act thus during all the three Sandhyās. This Pāśupata Vrata yields worldly pleasures and salvation dispelling Paśu-hood.

## \|\| 11.33.7 \|\|

*yāvaccharīrapātaṃ vā dvādaśābdamathāpi vā \|*  
*tadardhaṃ vā tadardhaṃ vā māsadvādaśakaṃ tu vā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Freed from Paśu-hood, the devotee shall worship the phallic image of Śiva.

## \|\| 11.33.28-29 \|\|

*karṇikākeśaropetamāsanaṃ parikalpayet \|*  
*vibhave tadabhāve tu raktaṃ sitamathāpi vā \|\| 28 \|\|*

*padmaṃ tasyāpyabhāve tu kevalaṃ bhāvanāmayam \|*  
*tatpadmakarṇikāmadhye kṛtvā liṃgaṃ kanīyasam \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. If capacity permits, an eight-petalled Padma shall be made in gold embellished with the nine precious gems. The pericarp and the filaments shall be furnished. If the capacity does not permit, a red or a white lotus shall be used. If that is not available, an imaginary lotus shall be conceived.

## \|\| 11.33.30 \|\|

*sphīṭikaṃ pīṭhikopetaṃ pūjayedvidhivatkramāt \|*  
*pratiṣṭhāpya vidhānena talliṃgaṃ kṛtaśodhanam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. In the middle of the pericarp a small crystal phallic image along with its pedestal shall be kept and worshipped.

## \|\| 11.33.31 \|\|

*parikalpyāsanaṃ mūrtiṃ pañcavaktraprakārataḥ \|*  
*pañcagavyādibhiḥ pūrṇairyathāvibhavasaṃbhṛtaiḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. After installing the phallic image in accordance with the rules with due consecrations the pedestal shall be conceived along with the idol of five faces.

## \|\| 11.33.32 \|\|

*snāpayetkalaśaiḥ pūrṇairaṣṭāpadasamudbhavaiḥ \|*  
*gaṃdhadravyaissakarpūraiścandanādyaissakuṃkumaiḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The ablution shall be performed with golden vessels, filled with Pañcagavya collected in accordance with one’s capacity.

## \|\| 11.33.33-35 \|\|

*savedikaṃ samālipya liṃgaṃ bhūṣaṇabhūṣitam \|*  
*bilvapatraiśca padmaiśca raktaiḥ śvetaistathotpalaiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*nīlotpalaistathānyaiśca puṣpaistaistaissugaṃdhibhiḥ \|*  
*puṇyaiḥ praśastaiḥ patraiśca citrairdūrvākṣatādibhiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*samabhyarcya yathālābhaṃ mahāpūjāvidhānataḥ \|*  
*dhūpaṃ dīpaṃ tathā cāpi naivedyaṃ ca samādiśet \|\| 35 \|\|*

33-35. The vessels shall contain scents along with camphor, sandal and saffron and these shall be smeared over the phallic image bedecked in ornaments. He shall worship it with Bilva leaves, red, white and blue lotuses, other fragrant flowers, holy and auspicious leaves, Dūrvā grass of various types, in accordance with their availability and the rules of worship.

## \|\| 11.33.36 \|\|

*nivedayitvā vibhave kalyāṇaṃ ca samācaret \|*  
*iṣṭāni ca viśiṣṭāni nyāyenopārjitāni ca \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Showing of lights, incense and the food offerings shall be made to the deity. After offering it to the deity the devotee shall be engaged in auspicious activities.

## \|\| 11.33.37 \|\|

*sarvadravyāṇi deyāni vrate tasminviśeṣataḥ \|*  
*śrīpatrotpalapadmānāṃ saṃkhyā sāhasrikī matā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. In this Vrata exquisite and pleasing things acquired legitimately, whatever they may be, shall be offered to the deity.

## \|\| 11.33.38 \|\|

*pratyekamaparā saṃkhyā śatamaṣṭottaraṃ dvijāḥ \|*  
*tatrāpi ca viśeṣeṇa na tyajedbilvapatrakam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The number of lotuses to be offered is a thousand. O brahmins, with regard to the other flowers it shall be a hundred and eight for each.

## \|\| 11.33.39-40 \|\|

*haimamekaṃ paraṃ prāhuḥ padmaṃ padmasahasrakāt \|*  
*nīlotpalādiṣvapyetatsamānaṃ bilbapatrakaiḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*puṣpāntare na niyamo yathālābhaṃ nivedayet \|*  
*aṣṭāṅgamarghyamutkṛṣṭaṃ dhūpālepau viśeṣataḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. The leaf of the Bilva tree shall never be excluded. A gold lotus is greater than a thousand lotuses. The case of blue lotuses is also on a par with that of Bilva leaves. With regard to the other flowers there is no restriction. They shall be offered just as they are available.

## \|\| 11.33.41-43 \|\|

*candanaṃ vāmadevākhye haritālaṃ ca pauruṣe \|*  
*īśāne bhasitaṃ kecidālepanamitīdṛśām \|\| 41 \|\|*

*na dhūpamiti manyante dhūpāntaravidhānataḥ \|*  
*sitāgurumaghorākhye mukhe kṛṣṇāguruṃ punaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*pauruṣe guggulaṃ savye saumye saugaṃdhikaṃ mukhe \|*  
*īśāne 'pi hyuśīrādi deyāddhūpaṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

41-43 The Arghya with eight materials of worship as constituents is highly commended. So also the incense and the unguent. To the deity Vāmadeva sandal paste is recommended. To the Pauruṣa deity yellow orpiment shall be offered; to Īśāna the ashes. In regard to the incense the procedure is different. To Aghora white and black Aguru in the mouth. To Pauruṣa fragrant gum-resin in the left; to Saumya scents in the mouth. To Īśāna, Uśīra shall be offered as Dhūpa.

## \|\| 11.33.44 \|\|

*śarkarāmadhukarpūrakapilāghṛtasaṃyutam \|*  
*caṃdanāgurukāṣṭhādyaṃ sāmānyaṃ saṃpracakṣate \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Sandal, Aguru, etc., along with sugar candy, honey, camphor and the ghee of a tawny-coloured cow can be offered to all.

## \|\| 11.33.45 \|\|

*karpūravartirājyāḍhyā deyā dīpāvalistataḥ \|*  
*arghyamācamanaṃ deyaṃ prativaktramataḥ param \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Thereafter series of lights with camphor and wick soaked in ghee shall be offered. Arghya and Ācamana shall be offered to every face.

## \|\| 11.33.46 \|\|

*prathamāvaraṇe pūjyo kramāddherambaṣaṇmukhau \|*  
*brahmāṃgāni tataścaiva prathamāvaraṇercite \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. In the first (outer column of the mystic diagram) Gaṇeśa and Kārttikeya shall be worshipped. Brahmā’s body shall also be worshipped.

## \|\| 11.33.47 \|\|

*dvitīyāvaraṇe pūjyā vighneśāścakravartinaḥ \|*  
*tṛtīyāvaraṇe pūjyā bhavādyā aṣṭamūrtayaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. In the second Āvaraṇa shall be worshipped Vighneśas the Cakravartins. The eight deities Bhava and others shall be worshipped in the third Āvaraṇa.

## \|\| 11.33.48 \|\|

*mahādevādayastatra tathaikādaśamūrtayaḥ \|*  
*caturthāvaraṇe pūjyāḥ sarva eva gaṇeśvarāḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. There the eleven deities Mahādeva and others shall be worshipped. All the Gaṇeśvaras shall be worshipped in the fourth Āvaraṇa.

## \|\| 11.33.49-52 \|\|

*bahireva tu padmasya pañcamāvaraṇe kramāt \|*  
*daśadikpatayaḥ pūjyāḥ sāstrāḥ sānucarāstathā \|\| 49 \|\|*

*brahmaṇo mānasāḥ putrāḥ sarve 'pi jyotiṣāṃ gaṇāḥ \|*  
*sarvā devyaśca devāśca sarve sarve ca khecarāḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*pātālavāsinaścānye sarve munigaṇā api \|*  
*yogino hi sakhāssarve pataṃgā mātarastathā \|\| 51 \|\|*

*kṣetrapālāśca sagaṇāḥ sarvaṃ caitaccarācaram \|*  
*pūjanīyaṃ śivaprītyā mattvā śaṃbhuvibhūtimat \|\| 52 \|\|*

49-52. Outside the lotus the mystic diagram and in the fifth Āvaraṇa shall be worshipped the lords of the ten quarters along with their weapons and followers, the mental sons of Brahmā, the luminary bodies, the goddesses and gods, the heaven-walkers, the residents of the netherworlds, the other sages, Yogins, the sacrifices, the birds, the mothers, the Kṣetrapālas with their Gaṇas and the universe including the mobile and immobile beings. These shall be worshipped, as they are possessed of Śiva’s pre-eminence. They shall be worshipped for the pleasure of Siva.

## \|\| 11.33.53 \|\|

*athāvaraṇapūjāṃte saṃpūjya parameśvaram \|*  
*sājyaṃ savyaṃ janaṃ hṛdyaṃ havirbhaktyā nivedayet \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Then at the end of the worship of the Āvaraṇas, after worshipping the supreme lord, delicious Havis shall be offered as Naivedya along with ghee and side-dishes.

## \|\| 11.33.54-55 \|\|

*mukhavāsādikaṃ dattvā tāmbūlaṃ sopadaṃśakam \|*  
*alaṃkṛtya ca bhūyo 'pi nānāpuṣpavibhūṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*nīrājanāṃte vistīrya pūjāśeṣaṃ samāpayet \|*  
*caṣakaṃ sopakāraṃ ca śayanaṃ ca samarpayet \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. The betel with something to chew with to render the mouth fragrant shall be given. After bedecking once again with different flowers and ornaments the detailed worship shall be concluded with the waving of lights. The drinking bowl with the complements and bedding shall be offered.

## \|\| 11.33.56-57 \|\|

*candrasaṃkāśahāraṃ ca śayanīyaṃ samarpayet \|*  
*ādyaṃ nṛpocitaṃ hṛdyaṃ tatsarvamanurūpataḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*kṛtvā ca kārayitvā ca hitvā ca pratipūjanam \|*  
*stotraṃ vyapohanaṃ japtvā vidyāṃ pañcākṣarīṃ japet \|\| 57 \|\|*

56-57. A moon-like necklace shall be dedicated to the bedding. Everything done or caused to be done shall be royal in its quality, very pleasing and befitting. The contrary worship shall be avoided. After reciting the Vyapohana hymns the Japa of the fìve-syllabled Mantra shall be performed.

## \|\| 11.33.58 \|\|

*pradakṣiṇāṃ praṇāmaṃ ca kṛtvātmānaṃ samarpayet \|*  
*tataḥ purastāddevasya guruviprau ca pūjayet \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. After circumambulation and obeisance the devotee shall dedicate himself. Then in front of lord he shall worship two brahmin preceptors.

## \|\| 11.33.59-64 \|\|

*dattvārghyamaṣṭau puṣpāṇi devamudvāsya liṃgataḥ \|*  
*agneścāgniṃ susaṃyamya hyudvāsya ca tamapyuta \|\| 59 \|\|*

*pratyahaṃ ca janastvevaṃ kuryātsevāṃ puroditām \|*  
*tatastatsāmbujaṃ liṃgaṃ sarvopakaraṇānvitam \|\| 60 \|\|*

*samarpayetsvagurave sthāpayedvā śivālaye \|*  
*saṃpūjya ca gurūnviprānvratinaśca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

*bhaktāndvijāṃśca śaktaśceddīnānāthāṃśca toṣayet \|*  
*svayaṃ cānaśane śaktaḥ phalamūlāśane 'tha vā \|\| 62 \|\|*

*payovrato vā bhikṣāśī bhavedekāśanastathā \|*  
*naktaṃ yuktāśano nityaṃ bhūśayyānirataḥ śuciḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*bhasmaśāyī tṛṇeśāyī cīrājinadhṛto 'thavā \|*  
*brahmacaryavrato nityaṃ vratametatsamācaret \|\| 64 \|\|*

59-64. After offering Arghya and eight flowers the lord shall be ritualistically dismissed from the phallic idol. After restraining the fire from the fire and ritualistically removing that also, the devotee shall perform the service everyday. Then he shall hand over the phallic idol with the insignia and lotuses to the preceptor. Or he shall install it in the temple of Śiva After worshipping the elders, brahmins, Vrata-performers in particular, he shall propitiate brahmin devotees and if possible poor and helpless people also. If he is competent he shall observe fast or take to a diet of fruits and roots. Or he shall have milk for his diet, or live on alms or take single meal everyday only in the night. He shall be pure in body and mind and lie on the bare ground or ashes or grass. He shall wear deerskin or bark garment and observe celibacy. Thus he shall perform the holy rite.

## \|\| 11.33.65 \|\|

*arkavāre tathārdrāyāṃ pañcadaśyāṃ ca pakṣayoḥ \|*  
*aṣṭamyāṃ ca caturdaśyāṃ śaktastūpavasedapi \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. If he is strong enough he shall observe fast on Sundays on Ardrā star days, on full moon and new moon days and on the eighth and fourteenth days.

## \|\| 11.33.66 \|\|

*pākhaṇḍipatitodakyāssūtakāntyajapūrvakān \|*  
*varjayetsarvayatnena manasā karmaṇā girā \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Mentally, verbally and physically he shall avoid contact with heretics, fallen men, polluted women in their menses and Śūdras, by all means.

## \|\| 11.33.67 \|\|

*kṣamadānadayāsatyāhiṃsāśīlaḥ sadā bhavet \|*  
*saṃtuṣṭaśca praśāntaśca japadhyānaratastathā \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. He shall always practise forgiveness, charity, mercy non-violence to all living beings. He shall remain content, calm and engaged in meditation and Japa.

## \|\| 11.33.68 \|\|

*kuryāttriṣavaṇasnānaṃ bhasmasnānamathāpi vā \|*  
*pūjāṃ vaiśeṣikīṃ caiva manasā vacasā girā \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. He shall bathe thrice a day or he shall dust with the ashes instead. He shall perform special worship mentally, verbally and physically.

## \|\| 11.33.69-70 \|\|

*bahunātra kimuktena nācaredaśivaṃ vratī \|*  
*pramādāttu tathācāre nirūpya gurulāghave \|\| 69 \|\|*

*ucitāṃ niṣkṛtiṃ kuryātpūjāhomajapādibhiḥ \|*  
*āsamāptervratasyaivamācarenna pramādataḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

69-70. Of what avail is much talk? A performer of the rite shall not commit any misdeed. If inadvertently he docs commit, he shall consider its seriousness or otherwise and perform adequate expiatory rites in the form of worship, sacrifice, Japas etc. Till the conclusion of the Vrata he shall not repeat the mistake.

## \|\| 11.33.71 \|\|

*godānaṃ ca vṛṣotsargaṃ kuryātpūjāṃ ca saṃpadā \|*  
*bhaktaśca śivaprītyarthaṃ sarvakāmavivarjitaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. He shall make charitable gifts of cows and oxen, perform worship in accordance with her wealth and capacity devoutly and free from any specific desire, for the pleasure of Śiva.

## \|\| 11.33.72 \|\|

*sāmānyametatkathitaṃ vratasyāsya samāsataḥ \|*  
*pratimāsaṃ viśeṣaṃ ca pravadāmi yathāśrutam \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. The common features of this Vrata have been narrated briefly. I shall now explain the special features for every month in the manner I have heard.

## \|\| 11.33.73-76 \|\|

*vaiśākhe vajraliṃgaṃ tu jyeṣṭhe mārakataṃ śubham \|*  
*āṣāḍhe mauktikaṃ vidyācchrāvaṇe nīlanirmitam \|\| 73 \|\|*

*māse bhādrapade caiva padmarāgamayaṃ param \|*  
*āśvine māsi vidyādvai liṃgaṃ gomedakaṃ varam \|\| 74 \|\|*

*kārtikyāṃ vaidrumaṃ liṃgaṃ vaidūryaṃ mārgaśīrṣake \|*  
*puṣparāgamayaṃ pauṣe māghe dyumaṇijantathā \|\| 75 \|\|*

*phālguṇe candrakāntotthaṃ caitre tadvyatyayo 'thavā \|*  
*sarvamāseṣu ratnānāmalābhe haimameva vā \|\| 76 \|\|*

73-76. In Vaiśākha the phallic idol of adamant, in Jyeṣṭha that of an emerald, in Āṣāḍha that of pearl, in Śrāvaṇa that of Sapphire, in Bhādrapada that of ruby, in Āśvina that of onyx, in Kārttika that of a coral, in Mārgaśīrṣa that of lapis lazuli, in Pauṣa that of topaz in Māgha that of the sun-stone; in Phālguna that of the moon-stone and in Caitra that of sun-tone is auspicious. If gems are not available gold shall be substituted in every month.

## \|\| 11.33.77 \|\|

*haimābhāve rājataṃ vā tāmrajaṃ śailajantathā \|*  
*mṛnmayaṃ vā yathālābhaṃ jātuṣaṃ cānyadeva vā \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. If gold is not available silver, copper, rock or clay shall be used for making the phallic idol whichever is available. Even lac can be used.

## \|\| 11.33.78-82 \|\|

*sarvagaṃdhamayaṃ vātha liṃgaṃ kuryādyathāruci \|*  
*vratāvasānasamaye samācaritanityakaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

*kṛtvā vaiśeṣikīṃ pūjāṃ hutvā caiva yathā purā \|*  
*saṃpūjya ca tathācāryaṃ vratinaśca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

*deśikenāpyanujñātaḥ prāṅmukho vāpyudaṅmukhaḥ \|*  
*darbhāsano darbhapāṇiḥ prāṇāpānau niyamya ca \|\| 80 \|\|*

*japitvā śaktito mūlaṃ dhyātvā sāmbaṃ triyambakam \|*  
*anujñāpya yathāpūrvaṃ namaskṛtya kṛtāñjaliḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

*samutsṛjāmi bhagavanvratametattvadājñayā \|*  
*ityuktvā liṃgamūlasthāndarbhānuttaratastyajet \|\| 82 \|\|*

78-82. Or he can make the idol as he pleases having all types of flowers. At the conclusion of Vrata after performing the daily rites he shall perform the special worship and sacrifice as before. After worshipping the preceptor and the Vratins in particular he shall take the permission from his instructor. Sitting facing the east or the north on a Darbha seat holding Darbha grass in the hands he shall restrain Prāṇa and Apāna. He shall make the Japa of the Mūla mantra to the extent of his ability; he shall meditate on Śiva and Śivā. Taking permission and bowing as before he shall say with palms joined in reverence: “O lord, at your behest, I am concluding this Vrata.” After saying thus he shall cast off the Darbhas at the root of the idol towards the north.

## \|\| 11.33.83 \|\|

*tato daṇḍajaṭācīramekhalā api cotsṛjet \|*  
*punarācamya vidhivatpañcākṣaramudīrayet \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Then he shall eschew the staff, the matted hair, the bark garment and the girdle too. After performing Acamana he shall repeat the five-syllabled mantra.

## \|\| 11.33.84 \|\|

*yaḥ kṛtvātyaṃtikīṃ dīkṣāmādehāntamanākulaḥ \|*  
*vratametatprakurvīta sa tu vai naiṣṭhikaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. He who has resolved to perform this Vrata till death and takes the initiation accordingly and performs the Virata undistressedly is a Naiṣṭhika.

## \|\| 11.33.85 \|\|

*so 'tyāśramī ca vijñeyo mahāpāśupatastathā \|*  
*sa eva tapatāṃ śreṣṭha sa eva ca mahāvratī \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. He is an Atyāśramin, a Mahāpāśupata, the most excellent of all austere persons and a great Vratin.

## \|\| 11.33.86 \|\|

*na tena sadṛśaḥ kaścitkṛtakṛtyo mumukṣuṣu \|*  
*yo yatirnaiṣṭhiko jātastamāhurnaiṣṭhikottamam \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Among those desirous of salvation there is none like him who is so content. The Naiṣṭhika who becomes an ascetic is called the excellent Naiṣṭhika.

## \|\| 11.33.87 \|\|

*yo 'nvahaṃ dvādaśāhaṃ vā vratametatsamācaret \|*  
*so 'pi naiṣṭhikatulyaḥ syāttīvravratasamanvayāt \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. He who performs this rite for twelve days or every day is on a par with the Naiṣṭhika, his Vrata being too severe.

## \|\| 11.33.88 \|\|

*ghṛtākto yaścaredetadvrataṃ vrataparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*dvitraikadivasaṃ vāpi sa ca kaścana naiṣṭhikaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. A person who applies ghee over his body and performs the rite with devout feelings even for two or three clays is also a Naiṣṭhika.

## \|\| 11.33.89 \|\|

*kṛtyamityeva niṣkāmo yaścaredvratamuttamam \|*  
*śivārpitātmā satataṃ na tena sadṛśaḥ kvacit \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. He who performs the excellent Vrata without a desire for the fruit feeling that it is his duty, always dedicating his Arman to Śiva has no one equal to him.

## \|\| 11.33.90 \|\|

*bhasmacchanno dvijo vidvānmahāpātakasaṃbhavaiḥ \|*  
*pāpaissudāruṇaissadyo mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

90 A scholarly brahmin covered with ashes is immediately liberated from the terrible effects of even the great deadly sins.

## \|\| 11.33.91 \|\|

*rudrāgniryatparaṃ vīryantadbhasma parikīrtitam \|*  
*tasmātsarveṣu kāleṣu vīryavānbhasmasaṃyutaḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. The gícat virility of the Rudra fire is what is glorified as the ashes. Hence a person possessing the ashes is a virile and powerful person at all times.

## \|\| 11.33.92 \|\|

*bhasmaniṣṭhasya naśyanti deṣā bhasmāgnisaṃgamāt \|*  
*bhasmasnānaviśuddhātmā bhasmaniṣṭha iti smṛtaḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. A person who has bathed with the ashes is called Bhasmaniṣṭha. His faults perish due to the contact of Bhasma fire.

## \|\| 11.33.93 \|\|

*bhasmanā digdhasarvāṃgo bhasmadīptatripuṃḍrakaḥ \|*  
*bhasmasnāyī ca puruṣo bhasmaniṣṭha iti smṛtaḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. He who has smeared his body with the ashes, wears Tripuṇḍraka with Bhasma and has a Bhasma bath is Bhasmaniṣṭha.

## \|\| 11.33.94 \|\|

*bhūtapretapiśāsāśca rogāścātīva dussahāḥ \|*  
*bhasmaniṣṭhasya sānnidhyādvidravaṃti na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. Surely the evil spirits, ghosts and goblins and repugnant diseases flee at the very proximity of a Bhasmaniṣṭha.

## \|\| 11.33.95 \|\|

*bhāsanādbhāsitaṃ proktaṃ bhasma kalmaṣabhakṣaṇāt \|*  
*bhūtibhūtikarī caiva rakṣā rakṣākarī param \|\| 95 \|\|*

95 It is called Bhasita because it shines; Bhasma because it devours sins; Bhūti because it causes prosperity and Rakṣā because it protects.

## \|\| 11.33.96 \|\|

*kimanyadiha vaktavyaṃ bhasmamāhātmyakāraṇam \|*  
*vratī ca bhasmanā snātassvayaṃ devo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. What else need be cited to indicate the glory of Bhasma? The Vratin who has had the Bhasma-bath is lord Śiva himself.

## \|\| 11.33.97 \|\|

*paramāstraṃ ca śaivānāṃ bhasmaitatpārameśvaram \|*  
*dhaumyāgrajasya tapasi vyāpado yannivāritāḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. This Bhasma is a great weapon of the devotees of Śiva. It is a divine missile whereby the mishaps of the elder brother of Dhaumya in the course of his penance had been removed.

## \|\| 11.33.98 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena kṛtvā pāśupatavratam \|*  
*dhanavadbhasma saṃgṛhya bhasmasnānarato bhavet \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. Hence one should endeavour in all possible ways to collect Bhasma like wealth after performing the Pāśupata vrata and be engaged in Bhasma-bath.

## Chapter 34 - The penance of Upamanyu

## \|\| 11.34.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*dhaumyāgrajena śiśunā kṣīrārthaṃ hi tapaḥ kṛtam \|*  
*tasmātkṣīrārṇavo dattastasmai devena śūlinā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: For the similarity of expression and contents of this and the following chapter, see Liṅga-purāṇa. 1. 107. The Upamanyu, episode of the Liṅga-purāṇa is concise and condensed; that of Śiva-purāṇa is detailed and comprehensive. The former seems to be the abridged version of the latter.

The sages said:—

1\. It was for obtaining milk that penance was performed by the boy Upamanyu, the elder brother of Dhaumya. So an ocean of milk was granted to him by lord Śiva.

## \|\| 11.34.2 \|\|

*sa kathaṃ śiśuko lebhe śivaśāstrapravaktṛtām \|*  
*kathaṃ vā śivasadbhāvaṃ jñātvā tapasi niṣṭhitaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. How could that infant attain power to propound the sacred doctrine of Siva? How could he realise the existence of Śiva and perform the penance?

## \|\| 11.34.3 \|\|

*kathaṃ ca labdhavijñānastapaścaraṇaparvaṇi \|*  
*rudrāgneryatparaṃ vīryaṃ labhe bhasma svarakṣakam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. How could he attain the perfect knowledge in the course of his observance of penance? How did he secure the protective ashes the virile element of the Rudra fire.

## \|\| 11.34.4 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*na hyeṣa śiśukaḥ kaścitprākṛtaḥ kṛtavāṃstapaḥ \|*  
*munivaryasya tanayo vyāghrapādasya dhīmataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

4\. It was not an ignorant common infant who performed the penance. He was the son of a great, wise and the learned sage Vyāghrapāda.

## \|\| 11.34.5 \|\|

*janmāntareṇa saṃsiddhaḥ kenāpi khalu hetunā \|*  
*svapadapracyuto diṣṭyā prāpto munikumāratām \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. He was a great Siddha in his former birth who had fallen from his position for some reason. Fortunately he was born as the son of a sage.

## \|\| 11.34.6 \|\|

*mahādevaprasādasya bhāgyāpannasya bhāvinaḥ \|*  
*dugdhābhilāṣaprabhavadvāratāmagamattapaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. His penance for the sake of obtaining milk became the gateway to the future grace of lord Śiva obtained due to good luck.

## \|\| 11.34.7 \|\|

*ataḥ sarvagaṇeśatvaṃ kumāratvaṃ ca śāśvatam \|*  
*saha dugdhābdhinā tasmai pradadau śaṃkaraḥ svayam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Śiva granted him perpetual bachelorhood, lord-ship of all the Gaṇas along with an ocean of milk.

## \|\| 11.34.8 \|\|

*tasya jñānāgamopyasya prasādādeva śāṃkarāt \|*  
*kaumāraṃ hi paraṃ sākṣājjñānaṃ śaktimayaṃ viduḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The acquisition of Śiva’s knowledge is due to Śiva’s grace alone. He acquired the knowledge of Śakti even as a boy,

## \|\| 11.34.9 \|\|

*śivaśāstrapravaktṛtvamapi tasya hi tatkṛtam \|*  
*kumāro munito labdhajñānābdhiriva nandanaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. His ability to propound the Śivaśāstra was also derived from the lord. He rejoiced in attaining the ocean of knowledge from the sage.

## \|\| 11.34.10 \|\|

*dṛṣṭaṃ tu kāraṇaṃ tasya śivajñānasamanvaye \|*  
*svamātṛvacanaṃ sākṣācchokajaṃ kṣīrakāraṇāt \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. There was an apparent reason for his acquisition of Śiva-jñāna. These were his mother’s words full of sorrow for the milk.

## \|\| 11.34.11-12 \|\|

*kadācitkṣīramatyalpaṃ pītavānmātulāśrame \|*  
*īrṣayayā mātulasutaṃ saṃtṛptakṣīramuttamam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*pītvā sthitaṃ yathākāmaṃ dṛṣṭvā vai mātulātmajam \|*  
*upamanyurvyāghrapādiḥ prītyā provāca mātaram \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Once the boy had tasted some quantity of milk in the hermitage of his uncle. His uncle’s son had drunk ample milk to his satiety. The jealous Upamanyu affectionately told his mother thus.

## \|\| 11.34.13 \|\|

*upamanyuruvāca \|*  
*mātarmātarmahābhāge mama dehi tapasvini \|*  
*gavyaṃ kṣīramatisvādu nālpamuṣṇaṃ pibāmyaham \|\| 13 \|\|*

Upamanyu said:—

13\. O mother, my blessed mother, O saintly woman, please give me sweet cow’s milk. I shall drink it very hot.

## \|\| 11.34.14 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā putravacanaṃ tanmātā ca tapasvinī \|*  
*vyāghrapādasya mahiṣī duḥkhamāpattadā ca sā \|\| 14 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

14\. On hearing the words of her son, the saintly mother, the wife of Vyāghrapāda, was very much distressed.

## \|\| 11.34.15 \|\|

*upalālyātha suprītyā putramāliṃgya sādaram \|*  
*duḥkhitā vilalāpātha smṛtvā nairdhanyamātmanaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. With love and affection she embraced the son and fondled him. Considering her poverty she became dejected and lamented.

## \|\| 11.34.16 \|\|

*smṛtvāsmṛtvā punaḥ kṣīramupamanyussa bālakaḥ \|*  
*dehi dehīti tāmāha rudranbhūyo mahādyutiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The boy Upamanyu could not forget the milk he wanted. He the innocent child of great splendour cried frequently pressing his mother to give him milk.

## \|\| 11.34.17 \|\|

*taddhaṭhaṃ sā parijñāya dvijapatnī tapasvinī \|*  
*śāntaye taddhaṭhasyātha śubhopāyamarīracat \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Realising that the boy was tenacious the saintly brahmin lady thought of a plan to quieten his stubbornness.

## \|\| 11.34.18-19 \|\|

*uñchavṛttyārjitānbījānsvayaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca sā tadā \|*  
*bījapiṣṭamathāloḍya toyena kalabhāṣiṇī \|\| 18 \|\|*

*ehyehi mama putreti sāmapūrvaṃ tatassutam \|*  
*āliṃgyādāya duḥkhārtā pradadau kṛtrimaṃ payaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. She had gleaned a few grains which the sweet-voiced lady ground into a paste with water. “Come on, s?? dear,” she addressed her son and though she was distressed at heart she gave him the improvised milk.

## \|\| 11.34.20 \|\|

*pītvā ca kṛtrimaṃ kṣīraṃ mātrāṃ dattaṃ sa bālakaḥ \|*  
*naitatkṣīramiti prāha mātaraṃ cātivihvalaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. On drinking that watery stuff offered as milk, the excited boy shouted. ‘O mother, this is no milk.’

## \|\| 11.34.21 \|\|

*duḥkhitā sā tadā prāha saṃprekṣyāghrāya mūrdhani \|*  
*samārjya netra putrasya karābhyāṃ kamalāyate \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The distressed mother when she saw the boy thus in misery caught hold of him, kissed on his head, wiped his lotus-like eyes with her hand and said:—

## \|\| 11.34.22 \|\|

*jananyuvāca \|*  
*taṭinī ratnapūrṇāstāssvargapātālagocarāḥ \|*  
*bhāgyahīnā na paśyanti bhaktihīnāśca ye śive \|\| 22 \|\|*

The mother said:—

22\. Rivers full of gems whether in heaven or in the nether worlds are never seen by unlucky people and those devoid of devotion to Śiva.

## \|\| 11.34.23 \|\|

*rājyaṃ svargaṃ ca mokṣaṃ ca bhojanaṃ kṣīrasaṃbhavam \|*  
*na labhante priyāṇyeṣāṃ na tuṣyati yadā śivaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. If Śiva is not pleased with them, they do not get those pleasing things viz. kingdom, heaven, salvation or a milk diet.

## \|\| 11.34.24 \|\|

*bhavaprasādajaṃ sarvaṃ nānyaddevaprasādajam \|*  
*anyadeveṣu niratā duḥkhārtā vibhramanti ca \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Everything is the result of Śiva’s grace and not that of any other lord. Those who are devoted to other lords wander in distress.

## \|\| 11.34.25 \|\|

*kṣīraṃ tatra kuto 'smākaṃ vane nivasatāṃ sadā \|*  
*kva dugdhasādhanaṃ vatsa kva vayaṃ vanavāsinaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Whence can we have milk, we who stay in the forest for ever? O dear, where the sources of milk and where we the forest-dwellers?

## \|\| 11.34.26 \|\|

*kṛtsnābhāvena dāridryānmayā te bhāgyahīnayā \|*  
*mithyādugdhamidaṃ dattampiṣṭamāloḍya vāriṇā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Wanting everything and overwhelmed by poverty I, your unfortunate mother, have given you this improvised milk grinding the fried grains into paste with water.

## \|\| 11.34.27-28 \|\|

*tvaṃ mātulagṛhe svalpaṃ pītvā svādu payaḥ śṛtam \|*  
*jñātvā svādu tvayā pītaṃ tajjātīyamanusmaran \|\| 27 \|\|*

*dattaṃ na paya ityuktvā rudan duḥkhīkaroṣi mām \|*  
*prasādena vinā śaṃbho payastava na vidyate \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. You tasted the boiled milk at your uncle’s. So when you drank this ‘sour stuff you found out on comparison that what I gave you was not milk. When you cry out saying so you make me miserable. Without the grace of Lord Śiva you cannot have milk.

## \|\| 11.34.29 \|\|

*pādapaṃkajayostasya sāmbasya sagaṇasya ca \|*  
*bhaktyā samarpitaṃ yattatkāraṇaṃ sarvasampadām \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. What is dedicated with devotion at the lotus-like feet of the lord accompanied by Śivā and his Gaṇas is the cause of all riches.

## \|\| 11.34.30 \|\|

*adhunā vasudosmābhirmahādevo na pūjitaḥ \|*  
*sakāmānāṃ yathākāmaṃ yathoktaphaladāyakaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The great lord who is the bestower of wealth and befitting benefits to those who desire them, has not been worshipped by us now.

## \|\| 11.34.31 \|\|

*dhanānyuddiśya nāsmābhiritaḥ prāgarcitaḥ śivaḥ \|*  
*ato daridrāssaṃjātā vayaṃ tasmānna te payaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Aiming at riches we have not worshipped Śiva hitherto. So we are poor. Hence you do not get milk.

## \|\| 11.34.32 \|\|

*pūrvajanmani yaddattaṃ śivamuddiśya vai sutaḥ \|*  
*tadeva labhyate nānyadviṣṇumuddiśya vā prabhum \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. O son, nothing else is obtained by us except what has been given by us in respect of lord Śiva or Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 11.34.33 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*iti mātṛvacaḥ śrutvā tathyaṃ śokādisūcakam \|*  
*bālo 'pyanutapannaṃtaḥ pragalbhamidamabravīt \|\| 33 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

33\. On hearing the words of his mother, true but expressive of her grief, the boy, though distressed within spoke thus in a mature way.

## \|\| 11.34.34 \|\|

*upamanyuruvāca \|*  
*śokenālamito mātaḥ sāṃbo yadyasti śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*tyaja śokaṃ mahābhāge sarvaṃ bhadraṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 34 \|\|*

Upamanyu said:—

34\. O mother, do not feel unhappy; if there is Śiva and śivā every thing good will result. O blessed lady, eschew your grief.

## \|\| 11.34.35 \|\|

*śṛṇu mātarvaco medya mahādevo 'sti cetkvacit \|*  
*cirādvā hyacirādvāpi kṣīrodaṃ sādhayāmyaham \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. O mother, listen now to my words. If there is lord Śiva anywhere sooner or later I shall get an ocean of milk.

## \|\| 11.34.36 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā vacastasya bālakasya mahāmateḥ \|*  
*pratyuvāca tadā mātā suprasannā manasvinī \|\| 36 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

36\. On hearing the words of her highly intelligent son the delighted noble mother replied.

## \|\| 11.34.37 \|\|

*mātovāca \|*  
*śubhaṃ vicāritaṃ tāta tvayā matprītivardhanam \|*  
*vilaṃbaṃ mā kathāstvaṃ hi bhaja sāṃbaṃ sadāśivam \|\| 37 \|\|*

The mother said:—

37\. O dear, what you have thought of is auspicious. It increases my pleasure. Do not delay. Worship Sadāśiva and the goddess Śivā.

## \|\| 11.34.38 \|\|

*sarvasmādadhiko 'styeva śivaḥ paramakāraṇam \|*  
*tatkṛtaṃ hi jagatsarvaṃ brahmādyāstasya kiṃkarāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Definitely there is Śiva superior to all, the great cause. The entire universe in created by him. Brahmā and and others are his servants.

## \|\| 11.34.39 \|\|

*tatprasādakṛtaiśvaryā dāsāstasya vayaṃ prabhoḥ \|*  
*taṃ vinānyaṃ na jānīmaśśaṃkaraṃ lokaśaṃkaram \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. If we have any prosperity it is created by his grace. We are only the slaves of the lord. Except Śiva, the benefactor of the worlds we do not know anyone else.

## \|\| 11.34.40 \|\|

*anyāndevānparityajya karmaṇā manasā girā \|*  
*tameva sāṃbaṃ sagaṇaṃ bhaja bhāvapurassaram \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Eschewing other gods physically, mentally and verbally, worship him alone, with Śivā with due devotion.

## \|\| 11.34.41 \|\|

*tasya devādhidevasya śivasya varadāyinaḥ \|*  
*sākṣānnamaśśivāyeti maṃtro 'yaṃ vācakaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. “Namaḥ Śivāya”, this mantra is directly expressive of Śiva, the overlord of the gods, the bestower of boons.

## \|\| 11.34.42 \|\|

*saptakoṭimahāmaṃtrāḥ sarve sapraṇavāḥ pare \|*  
*tasminneva vilīyaṃte punastasmādvinirgatāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The seven crores of mantras including the Praṇava Om merge into this mantra and come out again.

## \|\| 11.34.43 \|\|

*saprasādāśca te maṃtrāḥ svādhikārādyapekṣayā \|*  
*sarvādhikārastveko 'yaṃ maṃtra eveśvarājñayā \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Those Mantras are also beneficent with regard to those who are authorized therein. At the behest of the lord every one is authorized in this Mantra.

## \|\| 11.34.44 \|\|

*yathā nikṛṣṭānutkṛṣṭānsarvānapyātmanaḥ śivaḥ \|*  
*kṣamate rakṣituṃ tadvanmaṃtro 'yamapi sarvadā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Just as Śiva, this mantra too is capable of protecting all Atmans base or excellent.

## \|\| 11.34.45 \|\|

*prabalaśca tathā hyeṣa maṃtro mantrāntarādapi \|*  
*sarvarakṣākṣamo 'pyeṣa nāparaḥ kaścidiṣyate \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. This mantra is stronger than any other mantra. Only this and no other mantra is capable of protecting all.

## \|\| 11.34.46 \|\|

*tasmānmantrāntarāṃstyaktvā pañcākṣaraparo bhava \|*  
*tasmiñjihvāṃtaragate na kiṃcidiha durlabham \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Hence eschew all the other Mantras and devote yourself to this five-syllabled mantra. When that is in the mouth nothing is inaccessible here.

## \|\| 11.34.47 \|\|

*aghorāstraṃ ca śaivānāṃ rakṣāheturanuttamam \|*  
*tacca tatprabhavaṃ matvā tatparo bhava nānyathā \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. The excellent Aghora missile affording protection to the devotees of Śiva originates from this mantra. Considering this, be devoted to it and not otherwise.

## \|\| 11.34.48 \|\|

*bhasmedantu mayā labdhaṃ pitureva tavottamam \|*  
*virajānalasaṃsiddhaṃ mahāvyāpannivāraṇam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. This Bhasma produced in the Viraja fire was obtained by me from your father. It is excellent and it averts great mishaps.

## \|\| 11.34.49 \|\|

*maṃtraṃ ca te mayā dattaṃ gṛhāṇa madanujñayā \|*  
*anenaivāśu japtena rakṣā tava bhaviṣyati \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Accept the Mantra bestowed on you by me. If the Japa of this mantra is performed your protection will be assured.

## \|\| 11.34.50-51 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*evaṃ mātrā samādiśya śivamastvityudīrya ca \|*  
*visṛṣṭastadvaco mūrdhni kurvanneva tadā muniḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*tāṃ praṇamyaivamuktvā ca tapaḥ kartuṃ pracakrame \|*  
*tamāha ca tadā mātā śubhaṃ kurvaṃtu te surāḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

50-51. The mother directed him thus saying, “May it be auspicious” and allowed him to go. The sage accepted her words with his bent head. Bowing to her he made preparations for performing penance. Then the mother said to him, “May the gods do everything auspicious for yo

## \|\| 11.34.52 \|\|

*anujñātastayā tatra tapastepe sa duścaram \|*  
*himavatparvataṃ prāpya vāyubhakṣaḥ samāhitaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Permitted by her he went to the mountain Himavat and performed penance with purity of minds. He took in only wind (no food).

## \|\| 11.34.53-54 \|\|

*aṣṭeṣṭakābhiḥ prasādaṃ kṛtvā liṃgaṃ ca mṛnmayam \|*  
*tatrāvāhya mahādevaṃ sāṃbaṃ sagaṇamavyayam \|\| 53 \|\|*

*bhaktyā pañcākṣareṇaiva putraiḥ puṣpairvanodbhavaiḥ \|*  
*samabhyarcya ciraṃ kālaṃ cacāra paramaṃ tapaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

53-54. With eight bricks he built an altar and installed Śiva’s phallic image of clay. He invoked the unchanging lord Śiva accompanied by the Gaṇas and Pārvatī. He worshipped him with the leaves and flowers available in the forest repeating the five-syllabled Mantra with devotion. He performed penance for a long time.

## \|\| 11.34.55-56 \|\|

*tatastapaścarattaṃ taṃ bālamekākinaṃ kṛśam \|*  
*upamanyuṃ dvijavaraṃ śivasaṃsaktamānasam \|\| 55 \|\|*

*purā marīcinā śaptāḥ kecinmunipiśācakāḥ \|*  
*saṃpīḍya rākṣasairbhāvaistapasovighnamācaran \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. Assuming the forms of Rākṣasa certain ghosts of sages cursed formerly by Marīci harassed the lonely, lean boy Upamanyu performing penance though he was an excellent brahmin devotee of Śiva. Thus they caused obstacles to his penance.

## \|\| 11.34.57 \|\|

*sa ca taiḥ pīḍyamāno 'pi tapaḥ kurvankathañcana \|*  
*sadā namaḥ śivāyeti krośati smārtanādavat \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Though harassed by them he somehow maintained his penance. He uttered “Namaḥ Śivāya” like one in great distress.

## \|\| 11.34.58 \|\|

*tannādaśravaṇādeva tapaso vighnakāriṇaḥ \|*  
*te taṃ bālaṃ samutsṛjya munayassamupācaran \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. At the very hearing of that sound the sages who hindered the penance left off that boy and began to serve him.

## \|\| 11.34.59 \|\|

*tapasā tasya viprasya copamanyormahātmanaḥ \|*  
*carācaraṃ ca munayaḥ pradīpitamabhūjjagat \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. O sages, the whole universe including the mobile and immobile beings became ignited due to the penance of that brahmin, the noble Upamanyu.

## Chapter 35 - The story of Upamanyu

## \|\| 11.35.1 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*atha sarve pradīptāṃgā vaikuṇṭhaṃ prayayurdrutam \|*  
*praṇamyāhuśca tatsarvaṃ haraye devasattamāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

1\. Then the excellent gods with their bodies illuminated hastened to Vaikuṇṭha. After bowing they mentioned everything to Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 11.35.2-3 \|\|

*śrutvā teṣāṃ tadā vākyaṃ bhagavānpuruṣottamaḥ \|*  
*kimidantviti saṃcintya jñātvā tatkāraṇaṃ ca saḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*jagāma mandaraṃ tūrṇaṃ maheśvaradidṛkṣayā \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā devaṃ praṇamyaivaṃ provāca sukṛtāṃjaliḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. On hearing them, lord Viṣṇu thought “What is this?” After understanding the reason he immediately went to the Mandara mountain with a desire to see lord Śiva. On seeing the lord and bowing to him with palms joined in reverence he said:—

Viṣṇu said

## \|\| 11.35.4 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*bhagavanbrāhmaṇaḥ kaścidupamanyuriti śrutaḥ \|*  
*kṣīrārthamadahatsarvaṃ tapasā tannivāraya \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O lord, a certain brahmin well known as Upamanyu has burnt everything by his penance for obtaining the milk.

## \|\| 11.35.5 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*iti śrutvā vaco viṣṇoḥ prāha devo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*śiśuṃ nivārayiṣyāmi tattvaṃ gaccha svamāśramam \|\| 5 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

5\. On hearing the words of Viṣṇu, lord Śiva said:—“I shall prevent the boy. You may please go back to your abodes”.

## \|\| 11.35.6 \|\|

*tacchrutvā śaṃbhuvacanaṃ sa viṣṇurdevavallabhaḥ \|*  
*jagāmāśvāsya tānsarvānsvalokamamarādikān \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. On hearing the words of lord Śiva, Visṇu the favourite of the gods went to his abode after consoling the gods and others.

## \|\| 11.35.7 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare devaḥ pinākī parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*śakrasya rūpamāsthāya gantuṃ cakre matiṃ tataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. In the meantime, the trident-bearing lord Śiva resolved to go there assuming the form of Indra.

## \|\| 11.35.8 \|\|

*atha jagāma munestu tapovanaṃ gajavareṇa sitena sadāśivaḥ \|*  
*saha surāsurasiddhamahoragairamararājatanuṃ svayamāsthitaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Taking up the physical form as the king of gods, accompanied by gods, Asuras, Siddhas and serpents, and seated on a white elephant Sadāśiva went to the hermitage of the sage.

## \|\| 11.35.9 \|\|

*sa vāraṇaścāru tadā vibhuṃ taṃ nivījya vālavyajanena divyam \|*  
*dadhāra śacyā sahitaṃ sureṃdraṃ kareṇa vāmena śitātapatram \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The elephant fanned the lord with the chowrie and held the white umbrella with the left hand while bearing the lord of gods accompanied by Śacī.

## \|\| 11.35.10 \|\|

*rarāja bhagavānsomaḥ śakrarūpī sadāśivaḥ \|*  
*tenātapatreṇa yathā candrabiṃbena mandaraḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Lord Sadāśiva accompanied by Umā and assuming the form of Indra, shone with that umbrella like the Mandara mountain with the disc of the moon.

## \|\| 11.35.11 \|\|

*āsthāyaivaṃ hi śakrasya svarūpaṃ parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*jagāmānugrahaṃ kartumupamanyostadāśramam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Assuming the form of Indra, lord Śiva went to the hermitage of Upamanyu in order to bless him.

## \|\| 11.35.12 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā parameśānaṃ śakrarūpadharaṃ śivam \|*  
*praṇamya śirasā prāha mahāmunivaraḥ svayam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. On seeing lord Śiva, in the form of Indra, the sage bowed his head and spoke.

## \|\| 11.35.13 \|\|

*upamanyuruvāca \|*  
*pāvitaścāśramasso 'yaṃ mama deveśvara svayam \|*  
*prāpto yattvaṃ jagannātha bhagavandevasattama \|\| 13 \|\|*

Upamanyu said:—

13\. O lord of gods, O lord of the universe, O excellent god, my hermitage is sanctified since you have come here.

## \|\| 11.35.14 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*evamuktvā sthitaṃ prekṣya kṛtāṃjalipuṭaṃ dvijam \|*  
*prāha gaṃbhīrayā vācā śakrarūpadharo haraḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

14\. Glancing at the brahmin who stood steady after saying thus, with palms joined in reverence, Śiva in the guise of Indra spoke majestically.

## \|\| 11.35.15 \|\|

*śakra uvāca \|*  
*tuṣṭo 'smi te varaṃ brūhi tapasānena suvrata \|*  
*dadāmi cepsitānsarvāndhaumyāgraja mahāmune \|\| 15 \|\|*

Indra said:—

15\. O sage of good rites, O elder brother of Dhaumya, I am delighted with your penance. Mention the boon you wish to have. I shall grant you whatever you desire.

## \|\| 11.35.16 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*evamuktastadā tena śakreṇa munipuṃgavaḥ \|*  
*vārayāmi śive bhaktimityuvāca kṛtāñjaliḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

16\. The leading sage when urged thus by Indra spoke with palms joined in reverence—‘I request you to grant me the boon of devotion to Śiva’.

## \|\| 11.35.17-19 \|\|

*tanniśamya hariḥ 1 prāha māṃ na jānāsi lekhapam \|*  
*trailokyādhipatiṃ śakraṃ sarvadevanamaskṛtam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*madbhakto bhava viprarṣe māmevārcaya sarvadā \|*  
*dadāmi sarvaṃ bhadraṃ te tyaja rudraṃ ca nirguṇam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*rudreṇa nirguṇenāpi kiṃ te kāryaṃ bhaviṣyati \|*  
*devapaṅktibahirbhūto yaḥ piśācatvamāgataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

17-19. On hearing that Indra said:—“you do not know me the lord of gods the overlord of the three worlds, Indra, saluted by the gods. O brahminical sage, be my devotee. Always worship only me. Welfare be to you. I shall give you everything. Abandon Rudra who is devoid of attributes. What purpose of yours can be served by Rudra who without attributes has become a ghost ostracised from the midst of the gods.”

## \|\| 11.35.20 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*tacchrutvā prāha sa munirjapanpañcākṣaraṃ manum \|*  
*manyamāno dharmavighnaṃ prāha taṃ kartumāgatam \|\| 20 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

20\. On hearing that, the sage began to repeat the five-syllabled Mantra. He thought that Indra had come there to put obstacles in his holy rites and so said.

## \|\| 11.35.21 \|\|

*upamanyuruvāca \|*  
*tvayaivaṃ kathitaṃ sarvaṃ bhavaniṃdāratena vai \|*  
*prasaṃgādeva devasya nirguṇatvaṃ mahātmanaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

Upamanyu said:—

21\. You have said all these things in your eagerness to disparage Śiva. In that context you have mentioned the Nirguṇatva of the great lord.

## \|\| 11.35.22 \|\|

*tvaṃ na jānāmi vai rudraṃ sarvadeveśvareśvaram \|*  
*brahmaviṣṇumaheśānāṃ janaka prakṛteḥ param \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. You do not know Rudra the lord of the chiefs of the gods, the progenitor of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva and who is greater than Prakṛti.

## \|\| 11.35.23 \|\|

*sadasadvyaktamavyaktaṃ yamāhurbrahmavādinaḥ \|*  
*nityamekamanekaṃ ca varaṃ tasmādvṛṇomyaham \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. I desire to get my boon granted by the lord who is separate from Sat and Asar, who is the unmanifest, as mentioned by the propounders of Brahman and who is eternal, single and multifarious

## \|\| 11.35.24 \|\|

*hetuvādavinirmuktaṃ sāṃkhyayogārthadamparam \|*  
*upāsate yaṃ tattvajñā varaṃ tasmādvṛṇomyaham \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. I desire to secure the boon from that lord whom the knowers of truth meditate upon, who bestows the goal of Sāṃkhya and Yoga, viz. release.

## \|\| 11.35.25 \|\|

*nāsti śaṃbhoḥ paraṃ tattvaṃ sarvakāraṇakāraṇāt \|*  
*brahmaviṣṇvādidevānāṃ sraṣṭurguṇaparādvibhoḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. There is no higher truth than Śiva who is the cause of all causes, the creator of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and other gods and who is the lord beyond attributes.

## \|\| 11.35.26 \|\|

*bahunātra kimuktena mayādyānumitaṃ mahat \|*  
*bhavāṃtare kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ śrutā nindā bhavasya cet \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Of what avail is such talk? I infer that in the previous birth I committed a great sin because a disparaging remark about Śiva was heard by me.

## \|\| 11.35.27 \|\|

*śrutvā niṃdāṃ bhavasyātha tatkṣaṇādeva santyajet \|*  
*svadehaṃ tannihatyāśu śivalokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. On hearing the censure of Śiva, one shall immediately abandon one’s life and slay that person too. He then attains Śiva’s region.

## \|\| 11.35.28 \|\|

*āstāṃ tāvanmameccheyaṃ kṣīraṃ prati surādhama \|*  
*nihatya tvāṃ śivāstreṇa tyajāmyetaṃ kalevaram \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. O base god, let my desire for milk wait. After killing you with Śiva’s missile I shall abandon this body of mine.

## \|\| 11.35.29 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*evamuktvopamanyustaṃ martuṃ vyavasitassvayam \|*  
*kṣīre vāñchāmapi tyaktvā nihantuṃ śakramudyataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

29\. After saying this, Upamanyu ready to die himself eschewed his desire for milk and got ready to kill Indra.

## \|\| 11.35.30-31 \|\|

*bhasmādāya tadā ghoramaghorāstrābhimaṃtritam \|*  
*visṛjya śakramuddiśya nanāda sa munistadā \|\| 30 \|\|*

*smṛtvā śaṃbhupadadvaṃdvaṃ svadehaṃ dugdhumudyataḥ \|*  
*āgneyīṃ dhāraṇāṃ bibhradupamanyuravasthitaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. He took the ash and reinvigorated it with the Aghorāstra mantra. Aiming it at Indra he cast it off and shouted loudly. Remembering the feet of Śiva he attempted to burn off his body. Upamanyu held the fiery missile ready for discharge.

## \|\| 11.35.32 \|\|

*evaṃ vyavasite vipre bhagavānbhaganetrahā \|*  
*vārayāmāsa saumyena dhāraṇāṃ tasya yoginaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. When the brahmin attempted this, lord Śiva disguised as Śiva who destroyed the eyes of Bhaga prevented the missile of the Yogin gently.

## \|\| 11.35.33 \|\|

*tadvisṛṣṭamaghorāstraṃ naṃdīśvaraniyogataḥ \|*  
*jagṛhe madhyataḥ kṣiptaṃ nandī śaṃkaravallabhaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. At the behest of the lord, Nandin the favourite of Śiva caught in the middle the Aghorāstra hurled by him.

## \|\| 11.35.34 \|\|

*svaṃ rūpameva bhagavānāsthāya parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*darśayāmāsa śiprāya bālendukṛtaśekharam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Assuming his own form with the crescent moon for his crest, Lord Śiva revealed himself to the brahmin.

## \|\| 11.35.35-36 \|\|

*kṣīrārṇavasahasraṃ ca pīyūṣārṇavameva vā \|*  
*dadhyāderarṇavāṃścaiva ghṛtodārṇavameva ca \|\| 35 \|\|*

*phalārṇavaṃ ca bālasya bhakṣya bhojyārṇavaṃ tathā \|*  
*apūpānāṃ giriṃ caiva darśayāmāsa sa prabhuḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. The Lord showed to him a thousand oceans of milk, nectar curds, ghee, fruits, foodstuffs and a mountain of sweet pies.

## \|\| 11.35.37 \|\|

*evaṃ sa dadṛśe devo devyā sārdhaṃ vṛṣopari \|*  
*gaṇeśvaraistriśūlādyairdivyāstrairapi saṃvṛtaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The lord appeared thus seated on the bull along with the goddess and surrounded by the lords of Gaṇas and holding the divine missiles, trident etc.

## \|\| 11.35.38 \|\|

*divi duṃdubhayo neduḥ puṣpavṛṣṭiḥ papāta ca \|*  
*viṣṇubrahmendrapramukhairdevaiśchannā diśo daśa \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The Dundubhi drums were sounded in the heaven. There was a shower of flowers; the ten quarters were filled with the gods, chiefs of whom were Viṣṇu, Brahmā and Indra.

## \|\| 11.35.39 \|\|

*athopamanyurānandasamudrormibhirāvṛtaḥ \|*  
*papāta daṇḍavadbhūmau bhaktinamreṇa cetasā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Then Upamanyu enveloped by the waves of bliss fell at his feet, his mind made humble with devotion.

## \|\| 11.35.40 \|\|

*etasminsamaye tatra sasmito bhagavānbhavaḥ \|*  
*ehyehīti tamāhūya mūrdhnyāghrāya dadau varān \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Then the smiling lord Śiva called him nearer, kissed him on the head and granted him boons.

## \|\| 11.35.41 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*bhakṣyabhojyānyathākāmaṃ bāndhavairbhukṣva sarvadā \|*  
*sukhī bhava sadā duḥkhānnirmuktā bhaktimānmama \|\| 41 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

41\. Partake of various foodstuffs as you please along with your kinsmen, for ever. Be happy always, free from misery. Be my devotee.

## \|\| 11.35.42 \|\|

*upamanyo mahābhāga tavāmbaiṣā hi pārvatī \|*  
*mayā putrīkṛto hyadya dattaḥ kṣīrodakārṇavaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. O fortunate Upamanyu, this goddess Pārvatī is your mother. You have been adopted as my son. The milk ocean is given to you.

## \|\| 11.35.43 \|\|

*madhunaścārṇavaścaiva dadhyannārṇava eva ca \|*  
*ājyaudanārṇavaścaiva phalādyarṇava eva ca \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. So also the ocean of honey, of rice with curds and ghee and of fruits etc.

## \|\| 11.35.44 \|\|

*apūpagirayaścaiva bhakṣyabhojyārṇavastathā \|*  
*ete dattā mayā te hi tvaṃ gṛhṇīṣva mahāmune \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. O sage, mountains of sweet pies, the ocean of food stuffs, these are given to you. Please take them.

## \|\| 11.35.45 \|\|

*pitā tava mahādevo mātā vai jagadambikā \|*  
*amaratvaṃ mayā dattaṃ gāṇapatyaṃ ca śāśvatam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Your father is lord Śiva. Your mother is Pārvatī, the mother of the universe. I give you the status of a god; the eternal chieftainship of the Gaṇas.

## \|\| 11.35.46 \|\|

*varānvaraya suprītyā mano 'bhilaṣitānparān \|*  
*prasanno 'haṃ pradāsyāmi nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Choose boons as you please. I am delighted. I shall grant you boons. You need not hesitate at all.

## \|\| 11.35.47 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*evamuktvā mahādevaḥ karābhyāmupagṛhyatam \|*  
*mūrdhnyāghrāya sutaste 'yamiti devyai nyavedayat \|\| 47 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

47\. Saying thus lord Śiva caught him with his hands, kissed him on the head and handed him over to the goddess saying, “This is your son.”

## \|\| 11.35.48 \|\|

*devī ca guhavatprītyā mūrdhni tasya karāmbujam \|*  
*vinyasya pradadau tasmai kumārapadamavyayam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The goddess received him with pleasure like Guha, placed her hand on his head, granted him the unchangings status of a Bachelor.

## \|\| 11.35.49 \|\|

*kṣīrābdhirapi sākāraḥ kṣīraṃ svādu kare dadhat \|*  
*upasthāya dadau piṇḍībhūtaṃ kṣīramanaśvaram \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The milk ocean came in an embodied form holding sweet milk in his hands. Approaching the saintly boy he gave him imperishable condensed milk.

## \|\| 11.35.50 \|\|

*yogaiśvaryaṃ sadā tuṣṭiṃ brahmavidyāmanaśvarām \|*  
*samṛddhiṃ paramāntasmai dadau saṃtuṣṭamānasaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The goddess, out of delight, gave him the Yogic prosperity, perpetual contentment, imperishable Brahma-Vidyā and the greatest affluence.

## \|\| 11.35.51 \|\|

*atha śaṃbhuḥ prasannātmā dṛṣṭvā tasya tapomahaḥ \|*  
*punardadau varaṃ divyaṃ munaye hyupamanyave \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The delighted Śiva saw the splendour of his penance, granted boons again to the sage Upamanyu.

## \|\| 11.35.52 \|\|

*vrataṃ pāśupataṃ jñānaṃ vratayogaṃ ca tattvataḥ \|*  
*dadau tasmai pravaktṛtvapāṭavaṃ suciraṃ param \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. He gave him the Pāśupata rite, the Pāśupata knowledge and the perpetual ability to propound and discourse.

## \|\| 11.35.53 \|\|

*so 'pi labdhvā varāndivyānkumāratvaṃ ca sarvadā \|*  
*tasmācchivācca tasyāśca śivāyā mudito 'bhavat \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Obtaining the divine boons and the perpetual bachelorhood from Śivā and Śiva he became joyous.

## \|\| 11.35.54 \|\|

*tataḥ prasannacetaskaḥ supraṇamya kṛtāṃjaliḥ \|*  
*yayāce sa varaṃ vipro devadevānmaheśvarāt \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Delighted in his mind he bowed with palms joined in reverence. The brahmin then requested lord Śiva for a boon and said.

## \|\| 11.35.55 \|\|

*upamanyuruvāca \|*  
*prasīda devadeveśa prasīda parameśvara \|*  
*svabhaktindehi paramāndivyāmavyabhicāriṇīm \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. “O lord of the chiefs of the gods, be pleased. Please grant me devotion to you, great, divine and unflinching.

## \|\| 11.35.56 \|\|

*śraddhāndehi mahādeva dvasambandhiṣu me sadā \|*  
*svadāsyaṃ paramaṃ snehaṃ sānnidhyaṃ caiva sarvadā \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. O great lord, grant me an abiding faith in persons devoted to you. Grant me the great slavery and the perpetual proximity to you.

## \|\| 11.35.57 \|\|

*evamuktvā prasannātmāharṣagadgadayā girā \|*  
*satuṣṭāva mahādevamupamanyurdvijottamaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. After saying this, Upamanyu the excellent brahmin eulogised the lord in the words choked with delight.

## \|\| 11.35.58 \|\|

*upamanyuruvāca \|*  
*devadeva mahādeva śaraṇāgatavatsala \|*  
*prasīda karuṇāsiṃdho sāmba śaṃkara sarvadā \|\| 58 \|\|*

58.“O great lord, O lord of gods, favourably disposed to those who seek refuge in you. O ocean of mercy, be pleased always, O Śiva, accompanied by Pārvatī.

## \|\| 11.35.59 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*evamukto mahādevaḥ sarveṣāṃ ca varapradaḥ \|*  
*pratyuvāca prasannātmopamanyuṃ munisattamam \|\| 59 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

59\. Thus requested lord Śiva, the granter of boons replied with delighted ṃind to Upamanyu the excellent sage.

## \|\| 11.35.60 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*vatsopamanyo tuṣṭo 'smi sarvaṃ dattaṃ mayā hi te \|*  
*dṛḍhabhakto 'si viprarṣe mayā vijñāsito hyasi \|\| 60 \|\|*

Śiva said:—

60\. O dear Upamanyu, I am delighted. Indeed everything has been granted by me to you. O brahminical sage, you are of steady devotion. I wanted to test you.

## \|\| 11.35.61 \|\|

*ajaraścāmaraścaiva bhava tvanduḥkhavarjitaḥ \|*  
*yaśasvī tejasā yukto divyajñānasamanvitaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Be free from old age, death and misery. Be glorious and endowed with splendour and divine knowledge.

## \|\| 11.35.62 \|\|

*akṣayā bāndhavāścaiva kulaṃ gotraṃ ca te sadā \|*  
*bhaviṣyati dvijaśreṣṭha mayi bhaktiśca śāśvatī \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Your kinsmen, your family and spiritual lineage shall be everlasting. O excellent brahmin, your devotion to me shall be permanent.

## \|\| 11.35.63 \|\|

*sānnidhyaṃ cāśrame nityaṃ kariṣyāmi dvijottama \|*  
*upakaṃṭhaṃ mama tvaṃ vai sānandaṃ vihariṣyasi \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. O excellent brahmin, I shall always be present in your hermitage. Near me you shall always blissfully sport about.

## \|\| 11.35.64 \|\|

*evamuktvā sa bhagavānsūryakoṭisamaprabhaḥ \|*  
*īśānassa varāndattvā tatraivāntardadhe haraḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Thus granting him the boons lord Śiva who had the lustre of a crore suns, vanished there itself.

## \|\| 11.35.65 \|\|

*upamanyuḥ prasannātmā prāpya tasmādvarādvarān \|*  
*jagāma jananīsthānaṃ sukhaṃ prāpādhikaṃ ca saḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Securing the boons from the lord, Upamanyu, delighted in his mind, went to his mother's abode and attained the supreme bliss.

## Section 12 - Vāyavīya-saṃhitā (2)

## Chapter 1 - Acquisition of sons by Śrīkṛṣṇa (Śrī Kṛṣṇa)

## \|\| 12.1.1 \|\|

*oṃ \|*  
*namassamastasaṃsāracakrabhramaṇahetave \|*  
*gaurīkucataṭadvandvakuṃkumāṃkitavakṣase \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Obeisance to the lord whose chest is marked by the saffron from the plump pair of breasts of Gaurī and who causes the entire world whirl like a wheel.

## \|\| 12.1.2-4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*uktvā bhagavato labdhaprasādādupamanyunā \|*  
*niyamādutthito vāyurmadhye prāpte divākare \|\| 2 \|\|*

*ṛṣayaścāpi te sarve naimiṣāraṇyavāsinaḥ \|*  
*athāyamarthaḥ praṣṭavya iti kṛtvā viniścayam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*kṛtvā yathā svakaṃ kṛtyaṃ pratyahaṃ te yathā purā \|*  
*bhagavaṃtamupāyāṃtaṃ samīkṣya samupāviśan \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sūta said:—

2-4. After narrating how Upamanyu attained favours from the lord. Vāyu got up for the routine observances when the sun reached the middle of the sky. All the sages, the residents of the Naimiṣa forest, resolved within themselves what topic should be asked. After performing their duties as usual, they saw that the lord Vāyu was coming and so sat waiting for him.

## \|\| 12.1.5 \|\|

*athāsau niyamasyāṃte bhagavānambarodbhavaḥ \|*  
*madhye munisabhāyāstu bheje kḷptaṃ varāsanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. At the end of the observance of the daily routine lord Vāyu occupied his assigned seat in the middle of the assembly of the sages.

## \|\| 12.1.6 \|\|

*sukhāsanopaviṣṭaśca vāyurlokanamaskṛtaḥ \|*  
*śrīmadvibhūtimīśasya hṛdi kṛtvedamabravīt \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Vāyu, saluted by all the worlds, comfortably seated himself in the seat. Keeping well in his mind the glorious prosperity of the lord, he spoke thus.

## \|\| 12.1.7 \|\|

*taṃ prapadye mahādevaṃ sarvajñamaparājitam \|*  
*vibhūtissakalaṃ yasya carācaramidaṃ jagat \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. “I resort to that great lord, the unvanquished and the omniscient whose prosperity and glory constitute the universe consisting of the mobile and immobile beings.

## \|\| 12.1.8 \|\|

*ityākarṇya śubhāṃ vāṇīmṛṣayaḥ kṣīṇakalmaṣāḥ \|*  
*vibhūtivistaraṃ śrotumūcuste paramaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. On hearing the auspicious statement the sages of quelled sins spoke these words in order to hear further the details of the lord’s glory.

## \|\| 12.1.9-11 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*uktaṃ bhagavatā vṛttamupamanyormahātmanaḥ \|*  
*kṣīrārthenāpi tapasā yatprāptaṃ parameśvarāt \|\| 9 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭo 'sau vāsudevena kṛṣṇenākliṣṭakarmaṇā \|*  
*dhaumyāgrajastatastena kṛtvā pāśupataṃ vratam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*prāptaṃ ca paramaṃ jñānamiti prāgeva śuśruma \|*  
*kathaṃ sa labdhavān kṛṣṇo jñānaṃ pāśupataṃ param \|\| 11 \|\|*

The sages said:—

9-11. O lord, you have already mentioned the details of Upamanyu of noble soul, how he attained various favours from the supreme lord by means of the penance performed for the sake of milk. Formerly, we had heard that this elder brother of Dhaumya was met by Śrīkṛṣṇa of unstrained activities, son of Vasudeva. Then Kṛṣṇa performed the Pāśupatavrata and attained perfect knowledge. How did lord Kṛṣṇa attain the perfect knowledge of Paśupati?

## \|\| 12.1.12 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*svecchayā hyavatīrṇopi vāsudevassanātanaḥ \|*  
*niṃdayanniva mānuṣyaṃ dehaśuddhiṃ cakāra saḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

12\. Vāsudeva, the eternal god, had taken his incarnation out of his own free will. Still he performed the purificatory rites for his body thereby indicating that the human body is worthy of censure.

## \|\| 12.1.13 \|\|

*putrārthaṃ hi tapastaptuṃ gatastasya mahāmuneḥ \|*  
*āśramaṃ munibhirdṛṣṭaṃ dṛṣṭavāṃstatra vai munim \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. He went to the great sage’s hermitage resorted to by other sages, in order to perform a penance for the sake of sons. There he saw the sage Upamanyu.

## \|\| 12.1.14-15 \|\|

*bhasmāvadātasarvāṃgaṃ tripuṃḍrāṃkitamastakam \|*  
*rudrākṣamālābharaṇaṃ jaṭāmaṃḍalamaṃḍitam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tacchiṣyabhūtairmunibhiśśāstrairvedamivāvṛtam \|*  
*śivadhyānarataṃ śāṃtamupamanyuṃ mahādyutim \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. The sage had great splendour all over his body being rendered white due to the Bhasma smeared over. His forehead was marked with Tripuṇḍras. He was bedecked in resories of stringed Rudrākṣa beads. The clustered malted hair embellished him. He was surrounded by sages who were his disciples, just as the Veda is surrounded by the scriptural texts. He was calm and engaged in meditation on Śiva.

## \|\| 12.1.16 \|\|

*namaścakāra taṃ dṛṣṭvā hṛṣṭasarvatanūruhaḥ \|*  
*bahumānena kṛṣṇo 'sau triḥ kṛtvā tu pradakṣiṇām \|*

*stutiṃ cakāra suprītyā nataskaṃdhaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ \|*  
*tasyāvalokanādeva muneḥ kṛṣṇasya dhīmataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. On seeing him hairs stood on their ends in the body of Kṛṣṇa due to delight. Respectfully he circumambulated him thrice and knelt before him. With shoulders drooping and palms joined in reverence he delightfully eulogised him.

## \|\| 12.1.17 \|\|

*naṣṭamāsīnmalaṃ sarvaṃ māyājaṃ kārmameva ca \|*  
*tapaḥkṣīṇamalaṃ kṛṣṇamupamanyuryathāvidhiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. At the mere vision of the sage, all dirt born of Māyā and Karman of Kṛṣṇa was quelled.

## \|\| 12.1.18-19 \|\|

*bhasmanoddhūlya taṃ mantrairagnirityādibhiḥ kramāt \|*  
*atha pāśupataṃ sākṣādvrataṃ dvādaśamāsikam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*kārayitvā munistasmai pradadau jñānamuttamam \|*  
*tadāprabhṛti taṃ kṛṣṇaṃ munayaśśaṃsitavratāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. When the dirt of Kṛṣṇa had been quelled, Upamanyu dusted him with Bhasma repeating the Mantras “Agniriti” etc. He was then made to perforin the Pāśupata Vrata lasting for twelve months. Then the sage imparted to him the excellent knowledge.

## \|\| 12.1.20 \|\|

*divyāḥ pāśupatāḥ sarve parivṛtyopatasthire \|*  
*tato guruniyogādvai kṛṣṇaḥ paramaśaktimān \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Since then the divine Pāśupata sages of duly completed rites surrounded him.

## \|\| 12.1.21 \|\|

*tapaścakāra putrārthaṃ sāṃbamuddiśya śaṃkaram \|*  
*tapaso tena varṣāṃte dṛṣṭo 'sau parameśvaraḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Then at the behest of his preceptor, Kṛṣṇa of great prowess performed penance for the attainment of a son with Śiva and Pārvatī as the deity aimed at.

## \|\| 12.1.22 \|\|

*śriyā paramayā yuktassāṃbaśca sagaṇaśśivaḥ \|*  
*varārthamāvirbhūtasya harasya subhagākṛteḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Due to that penance, at the end of a year, lord Śiva, equipped with great splendour and accompanied by his Gaṇas and Pārvatī appeared there.

## \|\| 12.1.23 \|\|

*stutiṃ cakāra natvāsau kṛṣṇaḥ samyakkṛtāṃjaliḥ \|*  
*sāṃbaṃ samagaṇavyagro labdhavānputramātmanaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. After bowing to Śiva of handsome features, who appeared before him for granting boons, Kṛṣṇa eulogised him with palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 12.1.24 \|\|

*tapasā tuṣṭacittena dattaṃ viṣṇośśivena vai \|*  
*yasmātsāṃbo mahādevaḥ pradadau putramātmanaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Kṛṣṇa of composed mind obtained his son Samba of good qualities bequeathed by Śiva who was delighted by his penance.

## \|\| 12.1.25 \|\|

*tasmājjāṃbavatīsūnuṃ sāṃbaṃ cakre sa nāmataḥ \|*  
*tadetatkathitaṃ sarvaṃ kṛṣṇasyāmitakarmaṇaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Since it was Śiva accompanied by Ambā, who blessed him with a son, he named Jāmbavatī’s son Sāmba.

## \|\| 12.1.26 \|\|

*maharṣerjñānalābhaśca putralābhaśca śaṃkarāt \|*  
*ya idaṃ kīrtayennityaṃ śṛṇuyācchrāvayettathā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Thus I have narrated to you how Kṛṣṇa of wide activities attained knowledge from the great sage and a son from Śiva.

## \|\| 12.1.27 \|\|

*sa viṣṇorjñānamāsādya tenaiva saha modate \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. He who recites this everyday, listens to it or narrates it to others attains Viṣṇu’s wisdom and rejoices with him.

## Chapter 2 - The glory of lord Śiva

## \|\| 12.2.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kiṃ tatpāśupataṃ jñānaṃ kathaṃ paśupatiśśivaḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ dhaumyāgrajaḥ pṛṣṭaḥ kṛṣṇenākliṣṭakarmaṇā \|\| 1 \|\|*

The sages said:—

1\. What is the Pāśupata knowledge? How is Śiva the lord of Paśus? Why was Dhaumya’s elder brother asked by Kṛṣṇa of unstrained activities.

## \|\| 12.2.2 \|\|

*etatsarvaṃ samācakṣva vāyo śaṃkaravigraha \|*  
*tatsamo na hi vaktāsti trailokyeṣvaparaḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O lord Vayu, of the form of Śiva, please explain all these things. In the whole of the three worlds there is no other person competent to explain it like you.

## \|\| 12.2.3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ityākarṇya vacasteṣāṃ maharṣīṇāṃ prabhaṃjanaḥ \|*  
*saṃsmṛtya śivamīśānaṃ pravaktumupacakrame \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sūta said:—

3\. On hearing the words of the sages, Vāyu thought upon Śiva, and began to explain.

## \|\| 12.2.4 \|\|

*vāyuruvāca \|*  
*purā sākṣānmaheśena śrīkaṃṭhākhyena mandare \|*  
*devyai devena kathitaṃ jñānaṃ pāśupataṃ param \|\| 4 \|\|*

Vāyu said:—

4\. This excellent and exalted Pāśupata knowledge was mentioned to the goddess by lord Śiva on the mountain Mandara.

## \|\| 12.2.5 \|\|

*tadeva pṛṣṭaṃ kṛṣṇena viṣṇunā viśvayoninā \|*  
*paśutvaṃ ca surādīnāṃ patitvaṃ ca śivasya ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The same question was asked by Kṛṣṇa, the cause of the universe about the animal nature of the gods and others and the overlordship of Śiva.

## \|\| 12.2.6 \|\|

*yathopadiṣṭaṃ kṛṣṇāya muninā hyupamanyunā \|*  
*tathā samāsato vakṣye tacchṛṇudhvamataṃdritāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. I shall explain it succinctly as imparted to Kṛṣṇa by Upamanyu. Please hear attentively.

## \|\| 12.2.7 \|\|

*puropamanyumāsīnaṃ viṣṇuḥkṛṣṇavapurdharaḥ \|*  
*praṇipatya yathānyāyamidaṃ vacanamabravīt \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Formerly Viṣṇu in the form of Kṛṣṇa bowed to Upamanyu sitting in his hermitage and spoke courteously.

## \|\| 12.2.8 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*bhagavañchrotumicchāmi devyai devena bhāṣitam \|*  
*divyaṃ pāśupataṃ jñānaṃ vibhūtiṃ vāsya kṛtsnaśaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

Lord Kṛṣṇa said:—

8\. O lord, I wish to hear about the divine Pāśupata knowledge as mentioned to the goddess by the lord. I wish to hear about his prosperity and glory entirely.

## \|\| 12.2.9 \|\|

*kathaṃ paśupatirdevaḥ paśavaḥ ke prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*kaiḥ pāśaiste nibadhyaṃte vimucyaṃte ca te katham \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. How is the lord known as Paśupati, lord of Paśus? Who are the Paśus? What are those Pāśas (strings) with which they are bound? How are they released?

## \|\| 12.2.10 \|\|

*iti saṃcoditaḥ śrīmānupamanyurmahātmanā \|*  
*praṇamya devaṃ devīṃ ca prāha puṣṭo yathā tathā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Thus implored by the noble Kṛṣṇa the glorious Upamanyu bowed to the lord and the goddess and spoke as follows.

## \|\| 12.2.11 \|\|

*upamanyuruvāca \|*  
*brahmādyāḥ sthāvarāṃtāśca devadevasya śūlinaḥ \|*  
*paśavaḥ parikīrtyaṃte saṃsāravaśavartinaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

Upamanyu said:—

11\. Every being beginning with Brahmā and ending with immobile beings is called Paśu in relation to the lord of gods. Every being is subject to worldly existence.

## \|\| 12.2.12 \|\|

*teṣāṃ patitvāddeveśaḥ śivaḥ paśupatiḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*malamāyādibhiḥ pāśaiḥ sa badhnāti paśūnpatiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Śiva, lord of the gods, is known as Paśupati in view of his being the lord of the Paśus. The Pati binds the Paśus through the Pāśas (strings) of dirt.

## \|\| 12.2.13-14 \|\|

*sa eva mocakasteṣāṃ bhaktyā samyagupāsitaḥ \|*  
*caturviṃśatitattvāni māyākarmaguṇā amī \|\| 13 \|\|*

*viṣayā iti kathyante pāśā jīvanibandhanāḥ \|*  
*brahmādistambaparyaṃtān paśūnbaddhvā maheśvaraḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. He alone releases when he is meditated upon and worshipped with devotion. The twenty-four principles, Māyā, Karman and the three Guṇas are called Viṣayas. These are the Pāśas that bind the Paśus. After binding the Paśus, from Brahmā to the grass, by means of these Pāśas, lord Śiva makes them do their respective duties.

## \|\| 12.2.15-20 \|\|

*pāśairetaiḥ patirdevaḥ kāryaṃ kārayati svakam \|*  
*tasyājñayā maheśasya prakṛtiḥ puruṣocitām \|\| 15 \|\|*

*buddhiṃ prasūte sā buddhirahaṃkāramahaṃkṛtiḥ \|*  
*indriyāṇi daśaikaṃ ca tanmātrāpañcakaṃ tathā \|\| 16 \|\|*

*śāsanāddevadevasya śivasya śivadāyinaḥ \|*  
*tanmātrāṇyapi tasyaiva śāsanena mahīyasā \|\| 17 \|\|*

*mahābhūtānyaśeṣāṇi bhāvayaṃtyanupūrvaśaḥ \|*  
*brahmādīnāṃ tṛṇāntānāṃ dehināṃ dehasaṃgatim \|\| 18 \|\|*

*mahābhūtānyaśeṣāṇi janayaṃti śivājñayā \|*  
*adhyavasyati vai buddhirahaṃkārobhimanyate \|\| 19 \|\|*

*cittaṃ cetayate cāpi manaḥ saṃkalpayatyapi \|*  
*śrotrādīni ca gṛhṇanti śabdādīnviṣayān pṛthak \|\| 20 \|\|*

15-20. At his behest Prakṛti generates Buddhi befitting the Puruṣa. Buddhi (cosmic intellect)‘generates Ahaṅkāra (Ego). The ego generates the eleven sense-organs and five Tanmātras. At his bidding the Tanmātras too, create the great Bhūtas entirely in their order; the great Bhūtas create the physical bodies of all beings from Brahmā to the grass.
