Intellect determines and resolves. Ego feels pride in and identifies with what is possessed. Consciousness observes and becomes conscious of things. Mind conceives and imagines. The organs of knowledge apprehend the objects separately.

## \|\| 12.2.21-22 \|\|

*svāneva nānyāndevasya divyenājñābalena vai \|*  
*vāgādīnyapi yānyāsaṃstāni karmendriyāṇi ca \|\| 21 \|\|*

*yathā svaṃ karma kurvanti nānyatkiṃcicchivājñayā \|*  
*śabdādayopi gṛhyaṃte kriyante vacanādayaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. The sense-organs grasp their objects and not others and this is due to the divine command of the lord. The organs of activity too do their own duties. Nothing else. It is due to Śiva’s order that sound, etc. are grasped, speech, etc. are made. Śiva’s weighty command is not to be transgressed by any.

## \|\| 12.2.23-26 \|\|

*avilaṃghyā hi sarveṣāmājñā śaṃbhorgarīyasī \|*  
*avakāśamaśeṣāṇāṃ bhūtānāṃ saṃprayacchati \|\| 23 \|\|*

*ākāśaḥ parameśasya śāsanādeva sarvagaḥ \|*  
*prāṇādyaiśca tathā nāmabhedairaṃtarbahirjagat \|\| 24 \|\|*

*bibharti sarvaṃ śarvasya śāsanena prabhañjanaḥ \|*  
*havyaṃ vahati devānāṃ kavyaṃ kavyāśināmapi \|\| 25 \|\|*

*pākādyaṃ ca karotyagniḥ parameśvaraśāsanāt \|*  
*saṃjīvanādyaṃ sarvasya kurvatyāpastadājñayā \|\| 26 \|\|*

23-26. It is only at the behest of the lord that ether pervades all, yields space to the elements. At the bidding of Śiva the wind sustains the entire universe, internal and external, under different names of Prāṇa, etc. At the bidding of the lord the firegod bears offerings to the gods and oblations to the Pitṛs. It facilitates cooking etc. At his behest the waters enliven all. At the bidding of the lord the earth holds up the universe for ever.

## \|\| 12.2.27-30 \|\|

*viśvambharā jagannityaṃ dhatte viśveśvarājñayā \|*  
*devānpātyasurān haṃti trilokamabhirakṣati \|\| 27 \|\|*

*ājñayā tasya devendraḥ sarvairdevairalaṃghyayā \|*  
*ādhipatyamapāṃ nityaṃ kurute varuṇassadā \|\| 28 \|\|*

*pāśairbadhnāti ca yathā daṃḍyāṃstasyaiva śāsanāt \|*  
*dadāti nityaṃ yakṣendro draviṇaṃ draviṇeśvaraḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*puṇyānurūpaṃ bhūtebhyaḥ puruṣasyānuśāsanāt \|*  
*karoti saṃpadaḥ śaśvajjñānaṃ cāpi sumedhasām \|\| 30 \|\|*

27-30. In respect of Śiva’s inviolable command lord Indra protects the gods, kills the Asuras and guards the worlds. By Śiva’s command lord Varuṇa rules over the waters and binds those who are to be punished, by means of his noose. At the behest of Śiva the lord of wealth, the lord of the Yakṣas, distributes wealth to the living beings in accordance with their merit. At the bidding of Śiva, Īśāna bestows knowledge on the intelligent ones and affords them riches, and curbs the evil-doers.

## \|\| 12.2.31-34 \|\|

*nigrahaṃ cāpyasādhūnāmīśānaśśivaśāsanāt \|*  
*dhatte tu dharaṇīṃ mūrdhnā śeṣaḥ śivaniyogataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*yāmāhustāmasīṃ raudrīṃ mūrtimaṃtakarīṃ hareḥ \|*  
*sṛjatyaśeṣamīśasya śāsanāccaturānanaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*anyābhirmūrtibhiḥ svābhiḥ pāti cāṃte nihanti ca \|*  
*viṣṇuḥ pālayate viśvaṃ kālakālasya śāsanāt \|\| 33 \|\|*

*sṛjate trasate cāpi svakābhistanubhistribhiḥ \|*  
*haratyaṃte jagatsarvaṃ harastasyaiva śāsanāt \|\| 34 \|\|*

31-34. It is at the direction of Śiva that the earth is supported by Śeṣa. The Raudrī and Tāmasī form of Viṣṇu that brings about destruction is created by the four-faced lord. At his behest, through other forms of his own, he protects the universe and annihilates it in the end. He protects, creates and devours the universe through his own three bodies. At his bidding alone Rudra annihilates the universe in the end.

## \|\| 12.2.35-37 \|\|

*sṛjatyapi ca viśvātmā tridhā bhinnastu rakṣati \|*  
*kālaḥ karoti sakalaṃ kālassaṃharati prajāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*kālaḥ pālayate viśvaṃ kālakālasya śāsanāt \|*  
*tribhiraṃśairjagadbibhrattejobhirvṛṣṭimādiśan \|\| 36 \|\|*

*divi varṣatyasau bhānurdevadevasya śāsanāt \|*  
*puṣṇātyoṣadhijātāni bhūtānyāhlādayatyapi \|\| 37 \|\|*

35-37. The Ātman of the universe thus assuming three different forms creates and protects too. Time creates, protects and destroys at his behest. At his bidding with the three parts of his splendour, the sun supports the universe, commands the shower and rains in the heaven. At the behest of the moon-crested lord, the moon nourishes the plants, delights the living beings and is imbibed by the gods.

## \|\| 12.2.38-43 \|\|

*devaiśca pīyate caṃdraścandrabhūṣaṇaśāsanāt \|*  
*ādityā vasavo rudrā aśvinau marutastathā \|\| 38 \|\|*

*khecarā ṛṣayassiddhā bhogino manujā mṛgāḥ \|*  
*paśavaḥ pakṣiṇaścaiva kīṭādyāḥ sthāvarāṇi ca \|\| 39 \|\|*

*nadyassamudrā girayaḥ kānanāni sarāṃsi ca \|*  
*vedāḥ sāṃgāśca śāstrāṇi maṃtrastomamakhādayaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*kālāgnyādiśivāṃtāni bhuvanāni sahādhipaiḥ \|*  
*brahmāṃḍānyapyasaṃkhyāni teṣāmāvaraṇāni ca \|\| 41 \|\|*

*vartamānānyatītāni bhaviṣyantyapi kṛtsnaśaḥ \|*  
*diśaśca vidiśaścaiva kālabhedāḥ kalādayaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*yacca kiṃcijjagatyasmin dṛśyate śrūyate 'pi vā \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ śaṃkarasyājñā balena samadhiṣṭhitam \|\| 43 \|\|*

38-43. Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras, Aśvins, Maruts, heaven-walkers, Sages, Siddhas, Serpents, human beings, beasts, animals, birds, worms, immobile beings, rivers, oceans, mountains, forests, lakes, Vedas with their ancillaries, the scriptures, the compendiums of mantras, sacrifices, etc., the worlds beginning with Kālāgni and ending with Śiva and their over-lords, the innumerable Brahmāṇḍas, their coverings, the past, present and future, the quarters, interstices, the different units of time, Kalā etc.—all these, whatever is seen or heard in the world, are presided over by the order of Śiva.

## \|\| 12.2.44 \|\|

*ājñābalāttasya dharā sthiteha dharādharā vāridharāḥ samudrāḥ \|*  
*jyotirgaṇāḥ śakramukhāśca devāḥ sthiraṃ ciraṃ vā cidacidyadasti \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. It is through the power of his order that the earth, the mountains, clouds, oceans, luminary bodies, Indra and other gods, the mobile and immobile beings sentient or non-sentient are sustained.

## \|\| 12.2.45 \|\|

*upamanyuruvāca \|*  
*atyāścaryamidaṃ kṛṣṇa śaṃbhoramitakarmaṇaḥ \|*  
*ājñākṛtaṃ śṛṇuṣvaitacchrutaṃ śrutimukhe mayā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. O Kṛṣṇa, listen to the wonderful feat performed by the order of Śiva of unmeasured activity and heard by me from the Upaniṣads.

## \|\| 12.2.46 \|\|

*purā kila surāḥ seṃdrā vivadaṃtaḥ parasparam \|*  
*asurānsamare jitvā jetāhamahamityuta \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. After conquering the Asuras in the war formerly, the gods including Indra began to argue with one another “I am the victor, I am the victor”.

## \|\| 12.2.47 \|\|

*tadā maheśvarasteṣāṃ madhyato varaveṣadhṛk \|*  
*svalakṣaṇairvihīnāṃgaḥ svayaṃ yakṣa ivābhavat \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Then lord Śiva assumed the guise of a Yakṣa and stood in their midst devoid of his characteristic features in the limbs.

## \|\| 12.2.48 \|\|

*sa tānāha surānekaṃ tṛṇamādāya bhūtale \|*  
*ya etadvikṛtaṃ kartuṃ kṣamate sa tu daityajit \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. He set a blade of grass on the ground and told the gods, “He who can deform this grass is the conqueror of the Daityas.”

## \|\| 12.2.49 \|\|

*yakṣasya vacanaṃ śrutvā vajrapāṇiḥ śacīpatiḥ \|*  
*kiṃcitkruddho vihasyainaṃ tṛṇamādātumudyataḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. On hearing the words of the Yakṣa, the thunderbolt-bearing consort of Śacī became infuriated. Smiling a little he attempted to take up the grass.

## \|\| 12.2.50 \|\|

*na tattṛṇamupadātuṃ manasāpi ca śakyate \|*  
*yathā tathāpi tacchettuṃ vajraṃ vajradharo 'sṛjat \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. When he could not lift it up he hurled his thunderbolt at it in order to cut it.

## \|\| 12.2.51 \|\|

*tadvajraṃ nijavajreṇa saṃsṛṣṭamiva sarvataḥ \|*  
*tṛṇenābhihataṃ tena tiryagagraṃ papāta ha \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The thunderbolt coming into contact with the grass appeared to clash with a steel and fell aside.

## \|\| 12.2.52 \|\|

*tataścānye susaṃrabdhā lokapālā mahābalāḥ \|*  
*sasṛjustṛṇamuddiśya svāyudhāni sahasraśaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Then the guardians of the quarters and the worlds, of great strength exerted themselves and hurled thousands of their weapons at the grass-blade.

## \|\| 12.2.53 \|\|

*prajajjvāla mahāvahniḥ pracaṃḍaḥ pavano vavau \|*  
*pravṛddho 'pāṃpatiryadvatpralaye samupasthite \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The great fire blazed, the fìerce wind blew and the lord of the waters swelled as if the hour of dissolution had arrived.

## \|\| 12.2.54 \|\|

*evaṃ devaissamārabdhaṃ tṛṇamuddiśya yatnataḥ \|*  
*vyarthamāsīdaho kṛṣṇa yakṣasyātmabalena vai \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Thus everything initiated by the gods strenuously against the grass was a flop. O Kṛṣṇa, it was due to the power of that Yakṣa alone.

## \|\| 12.2.55 \|\|

*tadāha yakṣaṃ deveṃdraḥ ko bhavānityamarṣitaḥ \|*  
*tatassa paśyatāmeva teṣāmaṃtaradhādatha \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Then the infuriated lord of go is asked the Yakṣa, “Who are you, sir?” Then even as they were watching, the Yakṣa vanished.

## \|\| 12.2.56 \|\|

*tadaṃtare haimavatī devī divyavibhūṣaṇā \|*  
*āvirāsīnnabhoraṃge śobhamānā śucismitā \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. In the meantime the goddess Haimavatī bedecked in divine ornaments, appeared in the sky smiling and shining brilliantly.

## \|\| 12.2.57 \|\|

*tāṃ dṛṣṭvā vismayāviṣṭā devāḥ śakrapurogamāḥ \|*  
*praṇamya yakṣaṃ papracchuḥ ko 'sau yakṣo vilakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. On seeing her the wonderstruck gods, Indra and others bowed to her humbly and asked, “Who is this uncommon Yakṣa?”

## \|\| 12.2.58 \|\|

*sā 'bravītsasmitaṃ devī sa yuṣmākamagocaraḥ \|*  
*tenedaṃ bhramyate cakraṃ saṃsārākhyaṃ carācaram \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. The goddess smiled and said—“He is invisible to you. He is the lord by whom this wheel of the world including the mobile and immobile beings, revolves.

## \|\| 12.2.59 \|\|

*tenādau kriyate viśvaṃ tena saṃhriyate punaḥ \|*  
*na tanniyantā kaścitsyāttena sarvaṃ niyamyate \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. In the beginning the universe is created by him, and it is annihilated again by him. There is none to control him. Everything is controlled by him”.

## \|\| 12.2.60 \|\|

*ityuktvā sā mahādevī tatraivāṃtaradhatta vai \|*  
*devāśca vismitāḥ sarve tāṃ praṇamya divaṃ yayuḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. After saying this the great goddess vanished there itself. The surprised gods bowed to her and went to heaven.

## Chapter 3 - Upamanyu’s advice to lord Kṛṣṇa

## \|\| 12.3.1 \|\|

*upamanyuruvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu kṛṣṇa maheśasya śivasya paramātmanaḥ \|*  
*mūrtyātmabhistataṃ kṛtsnaṃ jagadetaccarācaram \|\| 1 \|\|*

Upamanyu said:—

1\. O Kṛṣṇa, listen; this universe of the mobile and immobile beings is pervaded by the Mūrtyātmans of lord Śiva, the great Ātman.

## \|\| 12.3.2 \|\|

*sa śivassarvamevedaṃ svakīyābhiśca mūrtibhiḥ \|*  
*adhitiṣṭhatyameyātmā hyetatsarvamanusmṛtam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Śiva presides over all these by means of his own Mūrtis. His Ātman is incomprehensible. This is said by the sages.

## \|\| 12.3.3 \|\|

*brahmā viṣṇustathā rudro maheśānassadāśivaḥ \|*  
*mūrtayastasya vijñeyā yābhirviśvamidaṃ tatam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. These shall be known as his Mūrtis whereby this universe is pervaded viz:—Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Maheśāna and Sadāśiva.

## \|\| 12.3.4 \|\|

*athānyāścāpi tanavaḥ pañca brahmasamāhvayāḥ \|*  
*tanūbhistābhirāvyāptamiha kiṃcinna vidyate \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. There are other bodies as well, called Pañcabrahmans. There is nothing which is not pervaded by those bodies.

## \|\| 12.3.5 \|\|

*īśānaḥ puruṣo 'ghoro vāmaḥ sadyastathaiva ca \|*  
*brahmāṇyetāni devasya mūrtayaḥ pañca viśrutāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The famous Pañcabrahmans, the bodies of the lord are Īśāna, Puruṣa, Aghora, Vāmadeva and Sadyojāta.

## \|\| 12.3.6 \|\|

*īśānākhyā tu yā tasya mūrtirādyā garīyasī \|*  
*bhoktāraṃ prakṛteḥ sākṣātkṣetrajñamadhitiṣṭhati \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. His greatest first Mūrti, Īśāna, presides over the individual soul the enjoyer of Prakṛti.

## \|\| 12.3.7 \|\|

*sthāṇostatpuruṣākhyā yā mūrtirmūrtimataḥ prabhoḥ \|*  
*guṇāśrayātmakaṃ bhogyamavyaktamadhitiṣṭhati \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The Mūrti of Śiva the lord having embodied forms, named Tatpuruṣā, presides over the unmanifest which is worthy of being enjoyed and which is in the form of the support of the Guṇas.

## \|\| 12.3.8 \|\|

*dharmādyaṣṭāṃgasaṃyuktaṃ buddhitattvaṃ pinākinaḥ \|*  
*adhitiṣṭhatyaghorākhyā mūrtiratyaṃtapūjitā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The highly venerable Mūrti Aghora, of the trident-bearing lord, presides over the principle of cosmic intellect consisting of eight parts of Dharma etc.

## \|\| 12.3.9 \|\|

*vāmadevāhvayāṃ mūrtiṃ mahādevasya vedhasaḥ \|*  
*ahaṃkṛteradhiṣṭhātrīmāhurāgamavedinaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Persons who know the Āgamas call the Mūrti Vāmadeva as the presiding deity of Ego.

## \|\| 12.3.10 \|\|

*sadyo jātāhvayāṃ mūrtiṃ śambhoramitavarcasaḥ \|*  
*mānasaḥ samadhiṣṭhātrīṃ matimaṃtaḥ pracakṣate \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The intelligent men say that the Mūrti Sadyojāta of Śiva of unmeasured splendour is the presiding deity of the mind.

## \|\| 12.3.11 \|\|

*śrotrasya vācaḥ śabdasya vibhorvyomnastathaiva ca \|*  
*īśvarīmīśvarasyemāmīśākhyāṃ hi vidurbudhāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Scholars understand that the Mūrti Īśāna is the presiding deity of the ear speech, sound and the all-pervasive ether.

## \|\| 12.3.12 \|\|

*tvakpāṇisparśavāyūnāmīśvarīṃ mūrtimaiśvarīm \|*  
*puruṣākhyaṃ vidussarve purāṇārthaviśāradāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Experts of the Purāṇas understand that the Mūrti Tatpuruṣa is the presiding deity of the skin, hand, touch and Vayu.

## \|\| 12.3.13 \|\|

*cakṣuṣaścaraṇasyāpi rūpasyāgnestathaiva ca \|*  
*aghorākhyāmadhiṣṭhātrīṃ mūrtimāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The wise understand that the Mūrti Aghora is the presiding deity of the eye, leg, colour and fire.

## \|\| 12.3.14 \|\|

*rasanāyāśca pāyośca rasasyāpāṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*īśvarīṃ vāmadevākhyāṃ mūrtiṃ tanniratāṃ viduḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The devotees understand that the Mūrti Vāmadeva is the presiding deity of the tongue, anus, taste and the waters.

## \|\| 12.3.15 \|\|

*ghrāṇasya caivopasthasya gaṃdhasya ca bhuvastathā \|*  
*sadyo jātāhvayāṃ mūrtimīśvarīṃ saṃpracakṣate \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. They say that the Mūrti Sadyojāta is the presiding deity of the nose, sexual organ, smell and the earth.

## \|\| 12.3.16 \|\|

*mūrtayaḥ pañca devasya vaṃdanīyāḥ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*śreyorthibhirnarairnityaṃ śreyasāmekahetavaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The five Mūrtis of the lord, the sole causes of prosperity shall be assiduously saluted by men seeking Śreyas.

## \|\| 12.3.17 \|\|

*tasya devādidevasya mūrtyaṣṭakamayaṃ jagat \|*  
*tasminvyāpya sthitaṃ viśvaṃ sūtre maṇigaṇā iva \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The universe consists of eight Munis, of the primordial lord of the gods, wherein lies stretched the universe as the gems and beads in the string.

## \|\| 12.3.18 \|\|

*śarvo bhavastathā rudra ugro bhīmaḥ paśoḥ patiḥ \|*  
*īśānaśca mahādevo mūrtayaścāṣṭa viśrutāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. These famous eight Mūrtis are Śarva, Bhava, Rudra, Ugra, Bhīma, Paśupati, Īśāna, and Mahādeva.

## \|\| 12.3.19 \|\|

*bhūmyaṃbhognimarudvyomakṣetrajñārkaniśākarāḥ \|*  
*adhiṣṭhitā maheśasya śarvādyairaṣṭamūrtibhiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The earth, waters, fire, wind, ether, Kṣetrajña, the sun and the moon are presided over by the eight Mūrtis, Śarva, etc, of the lord.

## \|\| 12.3.20 \|\|

*carācarātmakaṃ viśvaṃ dhatte viśvaṃbharātmikā \|*  
*śārvīrśivāhvayā mūrtiriti śāstrasya niścayaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. This is the conclusion of the scripture that the Mūrti of Śarva, in the form of the earth upholds the universe consisting of the mobile and immobile beings.

## \|\| 12.3.21 \|\|

*saṃjīvanaṃ samastasya jagatassalilātmikā \|*  
*bhāvīti gīyate mūrtibhavasya paramātmanaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The Mūrti of Bhava the great Ātman, in the form of water enlivens the universe.

## \|\| 12.3.22 \|\|

*bahiraṃtargatā viśvaṃ vyāpya tejomayī śubhā \|*  
*raudrī rudrāvyayā mūrtirāsthitā ghorarūpiṇī \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The Mūrti of Rudra having terrible form, is stationed all over the universe internally and externally and it consists of fire.

## \|\| 12.3.23 \|\|

*spaṃdayatyanilātmadaṃ bibharti spaṃdate svayam \|*  
*augrīti kathyate sadbhirmūrtirugrasya vedhasaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The Mūrti of Ugra in the form of the wind throbs itself and sustains eyerything and makes everything throb.

## \|\| 12.3.24 \|\|

*sarvāvakāśadā sarvavyāpikā gaganātmikā \|*  
*mūrtirbhīmasya bhīmākhyā bhūtavṛṃdasya bhedikā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The Mūrti of Bhīma is in the form of the ether It splits the elements. It. is all-pervasive and gives space to everything.

## \|\| 12.3.25 \|\|

*sarvātmanāmadhiṣṭhātrī sarvakṣetranivāsinī \|*  
*mūrtiḥ paśupaterjñeyā paśupāśanikṛṃtanī \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The Mūrti of Paśupati is the presiding deity of the Ātmans, immanent in the souls and splitting the binding cords of the Paśus.

## \|\| 12.3.26 \|\|

*dīpayaṃtī jagatsarvaṃ divākarasamāhvayā \|*  
*īśānākhyamaheśasya mūrtirdivi visarpati \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The Mūrti of Maheśa named Īśāna, otherwise called the sun, illuminates the universe and moves about in the firmament.

## \|\| 12.3.27 \|\|

*āpyāyayati yo viśvamamṛtāṃśurniśākaraḥ \|*  
*mahādevasya sā mūrtirmahādevasamāhvayā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The Mūrti of Mahādeva is the cause of the moon who delights and nourishes the universe with his nectarine rays.

## \|\| 12.3.28 \|\|

*ātmā tasyāṣṭamī mūrtiḥ śivasya paramātmanaḥ \|*  
*vyāpiketaramūrtīnāṃ viśvaṃ tasmācchivātmakam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The eighth Mūrti of the supreme lord Śiva is the Ātman. It pervades all the Mūrtis. Hence the universe has Śiva as its Ātman.

## \|\| 12.3.29 \|\|

*vṛkṣasya mūlasekena śākhāḥ puṣyaṃti vai yathā \|*  
*śivasya pūjayā tadvatpuṣyatyasya vapurjagat \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Just as the branches are nourished by watering the roots of the tree, so also by the worship of Śiva his body, the universe, is nourished.

## \|\| 12.3.30 \|\|

*sarvābhayapradānaṃ ca sarvānugrahaṇaṃ tathā \|*  
*sarvopakārakaraṇaṃ śivasyārādhanaṃ viduḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The propitiation of Śiva bestows protection, blessing and renders help unto all.

## \|\| 12.3.31 \|\|

*yatheha putrapautrādeḥ prītyā prīto bhavetpitā \|*  
*tathā sarvasya saṃprītyā prīto bhavati śaṃkaraḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. As the father is delighted at the pleasure of his sons and grandsons so also Śiva is pleased at the pleasure of all.

## \|\| 12.3.32 \|\|

*dehino yasya kasyāpi kriyate yadi nigrahaḥ \|*  
*aniṣṭamaṣṭamūrtestatkṛtameva na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. There is no doubt if any embodied soul is curbed it is a displeasing injury committed on the eight-bodied lord.

## \|\| 12.3.33 \|\|

*aṣṭamūrtyātmanā viśvamadhiṣṭhāya sthitaṃ śivam \|*  
*bhajasva sarvabhāvena rudraḥ paramakāraṇam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. With pious emotions worship Śiva who presides over the universe in the form of Aṣṭamūrti Rudra, the great cause.

## Chapter 4 - The exalted magnificence of Gaurī and Śiva

## \|\| 12.4.1 \|\|

*kṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*bhagavanparameśasya śarvasyāmitatejasaḥ \|*  
*mūrtibhirviśvamevedaṃ yathā vyāptaṃ tathā śrutam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: For the similarity of expression and contents of this chapter see ŚRS. 3.

Kṛṣṇa said—

1\. O holy lord, it has been heard how this universe is pervaded by the Mūrtis of lord Śiva, of unmeasured brilliance.

## \|\| 12.4.2 \|\|

*athaitajjñātumicchāmi yāthātmyaṃ pameśayoḥ \|*  
*strīpuṃbhāvātmakaṃ cedaṃ tābhyāṃ kathamadhiṣṭhitam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Now I wish to know the innate nature of the great lord and the goddess. How is this universe having male and female traits presided over by them?

Upamanyu said’.—

## \|\| 12.4.3 \|\|

*upamanyuruvāca \|*  
*śrīmadvibhūtiṃ śivayoryāthātmyaṃ ca samāsataḥ \|*  
*vakṣye tadvistarādvaktuṃ bhavenāpi na śakyate \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. I shall explain succinctly the glorious magnificence and the innate nature of Śiva and Śivā. It cannot be adequately explained in detail even by Śiva.

## \|\| 12.4.4 \|\|

*śaktiḥ sākṣānmahādevī mahādevaśca śaktimān \|*  
*tayorvibhūtileśo vai sarvametaccarācaram \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Śakti is Mahādevī herself and Mahādeva is one possessing Śakti. The entire universe of mobile and immobile beings is a fragment of their exalted magnificence.

## \|\| 12.4.5 \|\|

*vastu kiṃcidacidrūpaṃ kiṃcidvastu cidātmakam \|*  
*dvayaṃ śuddhamaśuddhaṃ ca paraṃ cāparameva ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Some objects are in the form of Cit and some in the form of Acit. Each of them is again twofold Śuddha and Para; Aśuddha and Apara.

## \|\| 12.4.6 \|\|

*yatsaṃsarati ciccakramaciccakrasamanvitam \|*  
*tadevāśuddhamaparamitaraṃ tu paraṃ śubham \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The wheel of Cit that undergoes worldly existence along with the wheel of Acit is Aśuddha and Apara. The other one is Śuddha and Para.

## \|\| 12.4.7 \|\|

*aparaṃ ca paraṃ caiva dvayaṃ cidacidātmakam \|*  
*śivasya ca śivāyāśca svāmyaṃ caitatsvabhāvataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Both the Cit and Acit whether Para or Apara and the lordship of Śiva and Śivā are natural.

## \|\| 12.4.8 \|\|

*śivayorvai vaśe viśvaṃ na viśvasya vaśe śivau \|*  
*īśitavyamidaṃ yasmāttasmādviśveśvarau śivau \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The universe is subject to the control of Śiva and Śivā, but Śiva and Śivā are not subject to the control of the universe. Since the universe is to be ruled over, Śiva and Śivā are the sovereigns of the universe.

## \|\| 12.4.9 \|\|

*yathā śivastathā devī yathā devī tathā śivaḥ \|*  
*nānayoraṃtaraṃ vidyāccaṃdracandrikayoriva \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Just as Śiva so also the goddess. Just as the goddess so also Śiva. No difference shall be thought of between the two as between the moon and the moonlight.

## \|\| 12.4.10 \|\|

*caṃdro na khalu bhātyeṣa yathā caṃdrikayā vinā \|*  
*na bhāti vidyamāno 'pi tathā śaktyā vinā śivaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Just as the moon does not shine without the moonlight so also though existing Śiva does not shine without Śakti.

## \|\| 12.4.11-12 \|\|

*prabhayā hi vināyadvadbhānureṣa na vidyate \|*  
*prabhā ca bhānunā tena sutarāṃ tadupāśrayā \|\| 11 \|\|*

*evaṃ parasparāpekṣā śaktiśaktimatoḥ sthitā \|*  
*na śivena vinā śaktirna śaktyā ca vinā śivaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Just as the sun does not exist without its light nor docs the light thereof exist without the sun, so also there is mutual dependence between Śakti and Śaktimān. There is no Śakti without Śiva and no Śiva without Śakti.

## \|\| 12.4.13-14 \|\|

*śaktauyayā śivo nityaṃ bhaktau muktau ca dehinām \|*  
*ādyā saikā parā śaktiścinmayī śivasaṃśrayā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*yāmāhurakhileśasya taistairanuguṇairguṇaiḥ \|*  
*samānadharmiṇīmeva śivasya paramātmanaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. The Śakti is the primordial and solitary one, of the form of Cit and depending on Śiva, by means of which Śiva can bestow worldly pleasures and salvation and which is of the same characteristics as Śiva, the great Ātman through the diverse befitting attributes of the lord.

## \|\| 12.4.15 \|\|

*saikā parā ca cidrūpā śaktiḥ prasavadharmiṇī \|*  
*vibhajya bahudhā viśvaṃ vidadhāti śivecchayā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The solitary and great Śakti of the form of Cit, is of parturient trait. It creates the universe with its manifold ramifications at the will of Śiva.

## \|\| 12.4.16 \|\|

*sā mūlaprakṛtirmāyā triguṇā ca tridhā smṛtā \|*  
*śivayā ca viparyastaṃ yayā tatamidaṃ jagat \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. It is also called Mūlaprakṛti, Māyā and Triguṇā. It is threefold. The universe is hurled back by her and pervaded.

## \|\| 12.4.17 \|\|

*ekadhā ca dvidhā caiva tathā śatasahasradhā \|*  
*śaktayaḥ khalu bhidyaṃte bahudhā vyavahārataḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. As one unit, as twofold, in hundreds and thousands Śaktis ramify themselves in their function.

## \|\| 12.4.18 \|\|

*śivecchayā parāśaktiḥ śivatattvaikatāṃ gatā \|*  
*tataḥ parisphuratyādau sarge tailaṃ tilādiva \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. At the will of Śiva, the great Śakti united with Śivatattva manifests from it at the first creation, like the oil from the gingelly seed.

## \|\| 12.4.19 \|\|

*tataḥ kriyākhyayā śaktyā śaktau śaktimadutthayā \|*  
*tasyāṃ vikṣobhyamāṇāyāmādau nādaḥ samudbabhau \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Then the śakti being agitated by the Kriyā Śakti originating from the Śaktimān, the primordial sound originates at the outset of creation.

## \|\| 12.4.20 \|\|

*nādādviniḥsṛto biṃdurbiṃdodevassadāśivaḥ \|*  
*tasmānmaheśvaro jātaḥ śuddhavidyā maheśvarāt \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The Bindu comes out of the Nāda; from Bindu comes out Sadāśiva. From him is born Maheśvara and Suddhavidyā originates from Maheśvara.

## \|\| 12.4.21 \|\|

*sā vācāmīśvarī śaktirvāgīśākhyā hi śūlinaḥ \|*  
*yā sā varṇasvarūpeṇa mātṛkepi vijṛmbhate \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. That is the deity of speech, the Śakti of Śiva named Vāgīśā; the same in the form of letters becomes manifest as Mātṛkā.

## \|\| 12.4.22 \|\|

*athānaṃtasamāveśānmāyā kālamavāsṛjat \|*  
*niyatiñca kalāṃ vidyāṃ kalātorāgapūruṣau \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Then by the infusion of the infinite, Māyā creates Kāla, Niyati, Kalā and Vidyā and through Kalā, Rāga and Puruṣa.

## \|\| 12.4.23 \|\|

*māyātaḥ punarevābhūdavyaktaṃ triguṇātmakam \|*  
*triguṇācca tato vyaktādvibhaktāḥ syustrayo guṇāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. From Māyā again originates the manifest consisting of the three Guṇas. From this Avyakta the three Guṇas become separated.

## \|\| 12.4.24-25 \|\|

*sattvaṃ rajastamaśceti yairvyāptamakhilaṃ jagat \|*  
*guṇebhyaḥ kṣobhyamāṇebhyo guṇeśākhyāstrimūrtayaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*abhavanmahadādīni tattvāni ca yathākramam \|*  
*tebhyassyuraṇḍapiṇḍāni tvasaṃkhyāni śivājñayā \|*

*adhiṣṭhitānyanantādyairvidyeśaiścakravartibhiḥ \|*  
*śarīrāṃtarabhedena śakterbhedāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. The three Guṇas are Sattva, Rajas and Tamas whereby the entire universe is pervaded. From the Guṇas, on being agitated and stirred up, the three deities are born as well as Mahat and other Tattvas in due order. At the behest of Śiva innumerable seeds are born. They are presided over by the infinite and other Vidyeśas, the Emperors.

## \|\| 12.4.26 \|\|

*nānārūpāstu vijñeyāḥ sthūlasūkṣmavibhedataḥ \|*  
*rudrasya raudrī sā śaktirviṣṇaurvai vaiṣṇavī matā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. In accordance with the difference in bodies, Śaktis are said to be different. They shall be known as having diverse forms both gross and subtle.

## \|\| 12.4.27 \|\|

*brahmāṇī brahmaṇaḥ proktā cendrasyaiṃdrīti kathyate \|*  
*kimatra bahunoktena yadviśvamiti kīrtitam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The Śakti of Rudra is called Raudrī, that of Viṣṇu Vaiṣṇavī; that of Brahmā Brahmāṇī and that of Indra Aindrī.

## \|\| 12.4.28 \|\|

*śakyātmanaiva tadvyāptaṃ yathā dehe 'ṃtarātmanā \|*  
*tasmācchaktimayaṃ sarvaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṃgamam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Of what avail is much talk? What is glorified as universe is pervaded by Śakti just as the physical body is pervaded by the immanent soul.

## \|\| 12.4.29-30 \|\|

*kalā yā paramā śaktiḥ kathitā paramātmanaḥ \|*  
*evameṣā parā śaktirīśvarecchānuyāyinī \|\| 29 \|\|*

*sthiraṃ caraṃ ca yadviśvaṃ sṛjatīti viniścayaḥ \|*  
*jñānakriyā cikīrṣābhistisṛbhissvātmaśaktibhiḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. The entire universe of the mobile and immobile beings is full of Śakti. Kalā, the greatest Śakti of the great Ātman, is called Parā Śakti, and it follows the wish of the lord and creates the mobile and immobile universe.

## \|\| 12.4.31 \|\|

*śaktimānīśvaraḥ śaśvadviśvaṃ vyāpyādhitiṣṭhati \|*  
*idamitthamidaṃ netthaṃ bhavedityevamātmikā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Lord Śiva is Śaktimān possessing the three Śaktis of knowledge, activity and wish. He pervades the universe for ever and stays.

## \|\| 12.4.32 \|\|

*icchāśaktirmaheśasya nityā kāryaniyāmikā \|*  
*jñānaśaktistu tatkāryaṃ karaṇaṃ kāraṇaṃ tathā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. “This shall be this way.” “This shall not be this way.” It is in this form that the wish of the lord permanently restrains activities.

## \|\| 12.4.33 \|\|

*prayojanaṃ ca tattvena buddhirūpādhyavasyati \|*  
*yathepsitaṃ kriyāśaktiryathādhyavasitaṃ jagat \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Śakti of knowledge is in the form of Buddhi and it determines its effect, instrument, cause and purpose factually.

## \|\| 12.4.34 \|\|

*kalpayatyakhilaṃ kāryaṃ kṣaṇātsaṃkalparūpiṇī \|*  
*yathā śaktitrayotthānaṃ śaktiprasavadharmiṇī \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Śakti of activity in the form of conception formulates and evolves the effect—universe, in the manner wished for and in the manner determined.

## \|\| 12.4.35 \|\|

*śaktyā paramayā nunnā prasūte sakalaṃ jagat \|*  
*evaṃ śaktisamāyogācchaktimānucyate śivaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. When the threefold Śaktis are risen, the Śakti of parturient traits urged by the Paramā Śakti gives birth to the universe.

## \|\| 12.4.36 \|\|

*śaktiśaktimadutthaṃ tu śāktaṃ śaivamidaṃ jagat \|*  
*yathā na jāyate putraḥ pitaraṃ mātaraṃ vinā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Śiva is called Śaktimān since he is in association with it. This universe born of both Śakti and Śaktimān is termed Śākta and Śaiva.

## \|\| 12.4.37 \|\|

*tathā bhavaṃ bhavānīṃ ca vinā naitaccarācaram \|*  
*strīpuṃsaprabhavaṃ viśvaṃ strīpuṃsātmakameva ca \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Just as no boy is born without parents, so also the universe of mobile and immobile beings does not originate without Śiva and Śivā. The universe has both a male and a female source, hence it is in the nature of male and female.

## \|\| 12.4.38 \|\|

*strīpuṃsayorvibhūtiśca strīpuṃsābhyāmadhiṣṭhitam \|*  
*paramātmā śivaḥ proktaśśivā sā ca prakīrtitā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. It is the effect of the superhuman power of male and female. It is presided over by a male and a female. Śiva is the great Ātman and Śivā the great Śakti.

## \|\| 12.4.39 \|\|

*śivassadāśivaḥ proktaḥ śivā sā ca manonmanī \|*  
*śivo maheśvaro jñeyaḥ śivā māyeti kathyate \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Sadāśiva is Śiva and Manonmanī is Śivā, Maheśvara is known as Śiva and Śivā as Māyā.

## \|\| 12.4.40 \|\|

*puruṣaḥ parameśānaḥ prakṛtiḥ parameśvarī \|*  
*rudro maheśvarassākṣādrudrāṇī rudravallabhā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Puruṣa is the great god and Prakṛti the great goddess. Rudra is the great god himself and Rudrāṇī is his beloved.

## \|\| 12.4.41 \|\|

*viṣṇurviśveśvaro devo lakṣmīrviśveśvarapriyā \|*  
*brahmā śivo yadā sraṣṭā brahmāṇī brahmaṇaḥ priyā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Viṣṇu is lord Viśveśvara and Lakṣmī his beloved. When Brahmā the creator is Śiva, Brahmāṇī is the beloved of Brahman.

## \|\| 12.4.42 \|\|

*bhāskaro bhagavāñchaṃbhuḥ prabhā bhagavatī śivā \|*  
*maheṃdro manmathārātiḥ śacī śailendrakanyakā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The sun is lord Śiva and his light is Śivā, Mahendra is Śiva and Śacī is Pārvatī.

## \|\| 12.4.43 \|\|

*jātavedā mahādevaḥ svāhā śarvārdhadehinī \|*  
*yamastriyaṃbako devastatpriyā girikanyakā \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Firegod is Mahādeva and Svāhā Śivā. Yama is Śiva and Yamī is Śivā, the daughter of the mountain.

## \|\| 12.4.44 \|\|

*nirṛtirbhagavānīśo nairṛtī naganaṃdanī \|*  
*varuṇo bhagavānrudro vāruṇī bhūdharātmajā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Nirṛti is lord Īśa. Nairṛtī is Śivā. Varuṇa is lord Rudra. Vāruṇī is Śivā.

## \|\| 12.4.45 \|\|

*bāleṃduśekharo vāyuḥ śivā śivamanoharā \|*  
*yakṣo yajñaśirohartā ṛddhirhimagirīndrajā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Vāyu is the moon-crested lord Śiva and his wife is Śivā, the captivator of Śiva’s mind. Sacrifice is the destroyer of sacrifice (= Śiva) and Ṛddhi is Śivā.

## \|\| 12.4.46 \|\|

*caṃdrārdhaśekharaścaṃdro rohiṇī rudravallabhā \|*  
*īśānaḥ parameśānastadāryā parameśvarī \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The moon is Śiva. Rohiṇī is Rudra’s beloved, Īśāna is Śiva. His Āryā is the goddess Umā.

## \|\| 12.4.47 \|\|

*anaṃtavalayo 'naṃto hyanaṃtānaṃtavallabhā \|*  
*kālāgnirudraḥ kālāriḥ kālī kālāṃtakapriyā \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Ananta the Serpent king is Śiva. Ananta’s beloved is the goddess Śivā. Kālāgnirudra is Śiva. Kālī is Śiva’s beloved.

## \|\| 12.4.48 \|\|

*puruṣākhyo manuśśaṃbhuḥ śatarūpā śivapriyā \|*  
*dakṣassākṣānmahādevaḥ prasūtiḥ parameśvarī \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Puruṣa Manu is Śiva and Śatarūpā is Śiva’s beloved. Dakṣa is lord Śiva himself and Prasūti is Parameśvarī.

## \|\| 12.4.49 \|\|

*rucirbhavo bhavānī ca budhairākūtirucyate \|*  
*bhṛgurbhagākṣihā devaḥ khyātistrinayanapriyā \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Ruci is Śiva and Ākūti is Śivā. Bhṛgu is the lord, the destroyer of the eyes of Bhaga. Khyāti is the beloved of the three-eyed lord Śiva.

## \|\| 12.4.50 \|\|

*marīcibhagavānrudraḥ saṃbhūtiśśarvavallabhā \|*  
*gaṃgādharo 'ṃgirā jñeyaḥ smṛtiḥ sākṣādumā smṛtā \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Marīci is lord Rudra. Sambhūti is Śarva’s beloved. Aṅgiras is Śiva. Smṛti is Umā herself.

## \|\| 12.4.51 \|\|

*pulastyaḥ śaśabhṛnmauliḥ prītiḥ kāṃtā pinākinaḥ \|*  
*pulahastripuradhvaṃsī tatpriyā tu śivapriyā \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Pulastya is the moon-crested lord. Prīti is the wife of the trident-bearing lord. Pulaha is the destroyer of the Tripuras. His wife is the beloved of Śiva.

## \|\| 12.4.52 \|\|

*kratudhvaṃsī kratuḥ proktaḥ saṃnatirdayitā vibhoḥ \|*  
*trinetro 'trirumā sākṣādanasūyā smṛtā budhaiḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Kratu is Śiva the destroyer of sacrifice. Sannati is the beloved of the lord. Atri is the three-eyed lord. Anasūyā is Umā herself.

## \|\| 12.4.53 \|\|

*kaśyapaḥ kālahā devo devamātā maheśvarī \|*  
*vasiṣṭho manmathārātirdevī sākṣādaruṃdhatī \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Kaśyapa is Śiva. His beloved is Śivā herself. Vasiṣṭha is Śiva and Arundhatī is the goddess herself.

## \|\| 12.4.54 \|\|

*śaṃkaraḥ puruṣāssarve striyassarvā maheśvarī \|*  
*sarve strīpuruṣāstasmāttayoreva vibhūtayaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. All men are identical with Śiva. All women are identical with Maheśvarī. Hence all men and women are their exalted superhuman power.

## \|\| 12.4.55 \|\|

*viṣayī bhagavānīśo viṣayaḥ parameśvarī \|*  
*śrāvyaṃ sarvamumārūpaṃ śrotā śūlavarāyudhaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Lord is the subject and his beloved is the object. Everything heard is the form of Umā and the hearer is the trident-holder Śiva.

## \|\| 12.4.56 \|\|

*praṣṭavyaṃ vastujātaṃ tu dhatte śaṃkaravallabhā \|*  
*praṣṭā sa eva viśvātmā bālacandrāvataṃsakaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. All that is worthy of being enquired about is sustained by Śiva’s beloved. The enquirer is the universal soul Śiva himself with crescent moon for an ornament.

## \|\| 12.4.57 \|\|

*draṣṭavyaṃ vasturūpaṃ tu bibharti vaktavallabhā \|*  
*draṣṭā viśveśvaro devaḥ śaśikhaṃḍaśikhāmaṇiḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Śiva’s beloved holds all objects to be perceived and the perceiver is lord Viśveśvara himself with the crescent moon as the crest-jewel.

## \|\| 12.4.58 \|\|

*rasajātaṃ mahādevī devo rasayitā śivaḥ \|*  
*preyajātaṃ ca girijā preyāṃścaiva garāśanaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. All objects of taste are identical with the goddess and Śiva is the taster. All lovable objects are identical with Śivā and Śiva is the lover.

## \|\| 12.4.59 \|\|

*maṃtavyavastutāṃ dhatte sadā devī maheśvarī \|*  
*maṃtā sa eva viśvātmā mahādevo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Goddess Maheśvarī holds all objects of reflection. The reflector is the all-pervading Lord himself.

## \|\| 12.4.60 \|\|

*boddhavyavasturūpaṃ tu bibharti bhavavallabhā \|*  
*devassa eva bhagavānboddhā mugdhenduśekharaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Lord’s beloved holds all objects to be understood. The understander is the lord himself.

## \|\| 12.4.61 \|\|

*prāṇaḥ pinākī sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ bhagavānprabhuḥ \|*  
*prāṇasthitistu sarveṣāmaṃbikā cāṃburūpiṇī \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Lord Śivā is the vital breath of all living beings. Śivā in the form of water is the existence of Prāṇa in all beings.

## \|\| 12.4.62 \|\|

*bibharti kṣetratāṃ devī tripurāṃtakavallabhā \|*  
*kṣetrajñatvaṃ tadā dhatte bhagavānaṃtakāṃtakaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. The beloved of Śiva is the abode of individual souls. Lord Śiva is the individual soul himself.

## \|\| 12.4.63 \|\|

*ahaḥ śūlāyudho devaḥ śūlapāṇipriyā niśā \|*  
*ākāśaḥ śaṃkaro devaḥ pṛthivī śaṃkarapriyā \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. The day is the trident-bearing lord and Night is the beloved of Śiva himself. The ether is lord Śiva and the earth is Śiva’s beloved.

## \|\| 12.4.64 \|\|

*samudro bhagavānīśo velā śailendrakanyakā \|*  
*vṛkṣo vṛṣadhvajo devo latā viśveśvarapriyā \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. The ocean is lord Śiva. The shore is the daughter of the king of mountains. The tree is the bull-bannered lord. The creeper is Śiva’s beloved.

## \|\| 12.4.65 \|\|

*puṃlliṃgamakhilaṃ dhatte bhagavānpuraśāsanaḥ \|*  
*striliṃgaṃ cākhilaṃ dhatte devī devamanoramā \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. The lord holds all masculine beings. The goddess holds all feminine beings.

## \|\| 12.4.66 \|\|

*śabdajālamaśeṣaṃ tu dhatte sarvasya vallabhā \|*  
*arthasvarūpamakhilaṃ dhatte mugdhenduśekharaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. The beloved of Śiva holds all words. The moon-crested lord holds all their meanings.

## \|\| 12.4.67 \|\|

*yasya yasya padārthasya yā yā śaktirudāhṛtā \|*  
*sā sā viśveśvarī devī sa sa sarvo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Whatever power is held by whatever object is identical with the goddess Viśveśvarī and Maheśvara.

## \|\| 12.4.68 \|\|

*yatparaṃ yatpavitraṃ ca yatpuṇyaṃ yacca maṃgalam \|*  
*tattadāha mahābhāgāstayostejovijṛṃbhitam \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. O fortunate ones, whatever is great, holy, pure and auspicious is the expansion of their brilliance.

## \|\| 12.4.69 \|\|

*yathā dīpasya dīptasya śikhā dīpayate gṛham \|*  
*tathā tejastayoretadvyāpya dīpayate jagat \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. As the flame of the brilliant lamp illuminates the house so also their brilliance pervades the universe and illuminates it.

## \|\| 12.4.70 \|\|

*tṛṇādiśivamūrtyaṃtaṃ viśvakhyātiśayakramaḥ \|*  
*sannikarṣakramavaśāttayoriti parā śrutiḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. The great Śruti says that the excellence of the universe from the blade of grass to Śiva’s Mūrti is due to their contact.

## \|\| 12.4.71 \|\|

*sarvākārātmakāvetau sarvaśreyovidhāyinau \|*  
*pūjanīyau namaskāryau ciṃtanīyau ca sarvadā \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. The two who are in the form of all and confer welfare on all shall be worshipped, bowed to and meditated upon always.

## \|\| 12.4.72 \|\|

*yathāprajñamidaṃ kṛṣṇa yāthātmyaṃ parameśayoḥ \|*  
*kathitaṃ hi mayā te 'dya na tu tāvadiyattayā \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. O Kṛṣṇa, the innate nature of the lord and the goddess has been explained to you by me in accordance with my ability but I have not exhausted it.

## \|\| 12.4.73 \|\|

*tatkathaṃ śakyate vaktuṃ yāthātmyaṃ parameśayoḥ \|*  
*mahatāmapi sarveṣāṃ manaso 'pi bahirgatam \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. The innate nature of the lord and the goddess is beyond the minds of even great men. How can it be explained?

## \|\| 12.4.74 \|\|

*aṃtargatamananyānāmīśvarārpitacetasām \|*  
*anyeṣāṃ buddhyanārūḍhamārūḍhaṃ ca yathaiva tat \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Just as it is present in the intellect and the minds, of the devotees who have dedicated their minds to the lord and who do not turn to any one else, so also it is not present in the intellect of others.

## \|\| 12.4.75 \|\|

*yeyamuktā vibhūtirvai prākṛtī sā parā matā \|*  
*aprākṛtāṃ parāmanyāṃ guhyāṃ guhyavido viduḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. The excellence and superhuman power that has been explained now is based on Prakṛti and is great as well. Those who know esoteric secrets understand the secret of non-Prākṛtika excellence.

## \|\| 12.4.76 \|\|

*yato vāco nivartaṃte manasā cendriyaissaha \|*  
*aprākṛtī parā caiṣā vibhūtiḥ pārameśvarī \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. The superhuman excellence of the lord which is non-Prākṛtika is that from which words recede along with the mind and the sense-organs.

## \|\| 12.4.77 \|\|

*saiveha paramaṃ dhāma saiveha paramā gatiḥ \|*  
*saiveha paramā kāṣṭhā vibhūtiḥ parameṣṭhinaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. That superhuman power of Parameṣṭhin is the greatest splendour, the greatest goal and the acme of achievement.

## \|\| 12.4.78 \|\|

*tāṃ prāptuṃ prayataṃte 'tra jitaśvāsā jiteṃdriyāḥ \|*  
*garbhakārā gṛhadvāraṃ niśchidraṃ ghaṭituṃ yathā \|\| 78 \|\|*

78 Persons who have conquered their vital breath and the sense-organs endeavour to achieve it in order to seal up the door to the prison in the form of womb.

## \|\| 12.4.79 \|\|

*saṃsārāśīviṣālīḍhamṛtasaṃjīvanauṣadham \|*  
*vibhūtiṃ śivayorvidvānna bibheti kutaścana \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. A person who has understood the superhuman excellence of Śiva and Śivā which is the divine medicine to resuscitate the dead on being bitten by the serpent of worldly existence, is not afraid of anything.

## \|\| 12.4.80 \|\|

*yaḥ parāmaparāṃ caiva vibhūtiṃ vetti tattvataḥ \|*  
*so 'paro bhūtimullaṃghya parāṃ bhūtiṃ samaśnute \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. The individual soul who understands factually the Parā and the Aparā excellences goes beyond the Aparā Bhūti and enjoys the Parā Bhūti (the greatest excellence).

## \|\| 12.4.81 \|\|

*etatte kathitaṃ kṛṣṇa yāthātmyaṃ paramātmanoḥ \|*  
*rahasyamapi yogyo 'si bhargabhakto bhavāniti \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. O Kṛṣṇa, thus I have explained to you the innate nature of the great souls, Śiva and Śivā, though it is a secret because you are a qualified devotee of Śiva.

## \|\| 12.4.82 \|\|

*nāśiṣyebhyo 'pyaśaivebhyo nābhaktebhyaḥ kadācana \|*  
*vyāharedīśayorbhūtimiti vedānuśāsanam \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. It is the injunction of the Vedas that the Vibhūti of the lord and the goddess shall not be imparted to those who are not disciples or who are not devotees or who are not the followers of Śiva.

## \|\| 12.4.83 \|\|

*tasmāttvamatikalyāṇaparebhyaḥ kathayenna hi \|*  
*tvādṛśebhyo 'nurūpebhyaḥ kathayaitanna cānyathā \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. O Kṛṣṇa of great welfare, so you do not tell others about this. Mention it to people, like you, who are deserving.

## \|\| 12.4.84 \|\|

*vibhūtimetāṃ śivayoryogyebhyo yaḥ pradāpayet \|*  
*saṃsārasāgarānmuktaḥ śivasāyujyamāpnuyāt \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. He who imparts this Vibhūti of Śiva and Śivā to qualified and competent men is liberated from the ocean of worldly existence and attains Sāyujya of Śiva.

## \|\| 12.4.85 \|\|

*kīrtanādasya naśyaṃti mahāntyaḥ pāpakoṭayaḥ \|*  
*triścaturdhāsamabhyastairvinaśyaṃti tato 'dhikāḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. By reciting this, crores of sins perish. Repeated thrice or four times it quells even more.

## \|\| 12.4.86 \|\|

*naśyaṃtyaniṣṭaripavo vardhante suhṛdastathā \|*  
*vidyā ca vardhate śaivī matissatye pravartate \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. All displeasing enemies perish. Friends increase. Learning flourishes. Auspicious intellect functions in Truth.

## \|\| 12.4.87 \|\|

*bhaktiḥ parāḥ śive sāmbe sānuge saparicchide \|*  
*yadyadiṣṭatamaṃ cānyattattadāpnotyasaṃśayam \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. He acquires devotion to Śiva, Śivā, their followers and attendants. He acquires whatever is pleasing and all other things undoubtedly.

## \|\| 12.4.88 \|\|

*antaḥśuciḥ śive bhakto visrabdhaḥ kīrtayedyadi \|*  
*prabalaiḥ karmabhiḥ pūrvaiḥ phalaṃ cetpratibadhyate \|*

*punaḥ punaḥ samabhyasyettasya nāstīha durllabham \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. One should recite this with purity of mind, devotion to Śiva and full conviction. If due to powerful previous Karmans the fruition is prevented, he shall repeat it again. There is nothing inaccessible to him.

## Chapter 5 - Knowledge of paśupati principle

## \|\| 12.5.1 \|\|

*upamanyuruvāca \|*  
*vigrahaṃ devadevasya viśvametaccarācaram \|*  
*tadevaṃ na vijānaṃti paśavaḥ pāśagauravāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

Upamanyu said:—

1\. This universe of the mobile and immobile beings is the cosmic body of the lord of the gods. The Paśus do not know it at all due to the intricacy of the Pāśa.

## \|\| 12.5.2 \|\|

*tamekameva bahudhā vadaṃti yadunaṃdana \|*  
*ajānantaḥ paraṃ bhāvamavikalpaṃ maharṣayaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O scion of the family of Yadu, not knowing his great, nature, never subject to alteration or doubts, some sages call him many though he is one.

## \|\| 12.5.3 \|\|

*aparaṃ brahmarūpaṃ ca paraṃ brahmātmakaṃ tathā \|*  
*kecidāhurmahādevamanādinidhanaṃ param \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. About the great lord, without beginning or death, some say he is Aparabrahmarūpa, some say he is Parabrahmarūpa.

## \|\| 12.5.4 \|\|

*bhūteṃdriyāṃtaḥkaraṇapradhānaviṣayātmakam \|*  
*aparaṃ brahma nirdiṣṭaṃ paraṃ brahma cidātmakam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. According to them Aparabrahmarūpa is that aspect when the godhead is identified with the elements, Antaḥkaraṇa the Indriyas, the Pradhāna and the sensual objects. The Parabrahman is the great Brahman in the form of Cit.

## \|\| 12.5.5 \|\|

*bṛhattvādbṛhaṇatvādvā brahma cetyabhidhīyate \|*  
*ubhe te brahmaṇo rūpe brahmaṇo 'dhipateḥ prabhoḥ \|*

*vidyā 'vidyāsvarūpīti kaiścidīśo nigadyate \|*  
*vidyāṃ tu cetanāṃ prāhustathāvidyāmacetanām \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The godhead is called Brahman because it is immense and it expands. Some say that the Īśa is of the form of Vidyā and Avidyā. Thus there are two forms of lord Brahman, the lord of Brahmā.

## \|\| 12.5.6 \|\|

*vidyā 'vidyātmakaṃ caiva viśvaṃ viśvagurorvibhoḥ \|*  
*rūpameva na saṃdeho viśvaṃ tasya vaśe yataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. They say that Vidyā is Cetanā (consciousness) and Avidyā is Acetanā (insentience). The universe too is in the form of Vidyā and Avidyā as belonging to the lord, the preceptor of the universe.

## \|\| 12.5.7 \|\|

*bhrāṃtirvidyā parā ceti śārvaṃ rūpaṃ paraṃ viduḥ \|*  
*ayathābuddhirartheṣu bahudhā bhrāṃtirucyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. There is no doubt in this that the universe is his form because it is subservient to him. Others know the form of Śiva as delusion and Para Vidyā.

## \|\| 12.5.8 \|\|

*yathārthākārasaṃvittirvidyeti parikīrtyate \|*  
*vikalparahitaṃ tattvaṃ paramityabhidhīyate \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Delusion usually means Ayathābuddhi (not knowing as it is) in regard to the objects. Vidyā is opposite to it where the knowledge is in the true form.

## \|\| 12.5.9 \|\|

*vaiparītyādasacchabdaḥ kathyate vedavādibhiḥ \|*  
*tayoḥ patitvāttu śivaḥ sadasatpatirucyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The great principle is devoid of alteration or doubts. The opposite thing is connoted by the word Asat as explained by those who propound the Vedas.

## \|\| 12.5.10 \|\|

*kṣarākṣarātmakaṃ prāhuḥ kṣarākṣaraparaṃ pare \|*  
*kṣarassarvāṇi bhūtāni kūṭastho 'kṣara ucyate \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Since he is the lord of the two, Śiva is called the lord of the Sat and Asat. Some say that he is in the form of Kṣara and Akṣara. Others say that he is beyond Kṣara and Akṣara.

## \|\| 12.5.11 \|\|

*ubhe te parameśasya rūpe tasya vaśe yataḥ \|*  
*tayoḥ paraḥ śivaḥ śāṃtaḥ kṣarākṣarāparassmṛtaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The living beings are called Kṣara. The Kūṭastha is called Akṣara. Both these are the forms of the lord because they are under his control.

## \|\| 12.5.12-13 \|\|

*samaṣṭivyaṣṭhirūpaṃ ca samaṣṭivyaṣṭikāraṇam \|*  
*vadaṃti munayaḥ kecicchivaṃ paramakāraṇam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*samaṣṭimāhuravyaktaṃ vyaṣṭiṃ vyaktaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*te rūpe parameśasya tadicchāyāḥ pravartanāt \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. Beyond the two is Śiva the quiescent. Hence he is Kṣarākṣarapara. Some say that Śiva is the great cause, that he is in the form of the universal as well as the individual and the cause of both. The Samaṣṭi is unmanifest, they say and the Vyaṣṭi is manifest.

## \|\| 12.5.14 \|\|

*tayoḥ kāraṇabhāvena śivaṃ paramakāraṇam \|*  
*kāraṇārthavidaḥ prāhuḥ samaṣṭivyaṣṭikāraṇam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. They are the forms of the lord because they function at his will. Since he is their cause, those who know the meaning of the ‘cause’ say that Śiva the great cause is the cause of both the universal and the individual.

## \|\| 12.5.15-17 \|\|

*jātivyaktisvarūpīti kathyate kaiścidīśvaraḥ \|*  
*yā piṃḍepyanuvarteta sā jātiriti kathyate \|\| 15 \|\|*

*vyaktirvyāvṛttirūpaṃ taṃ piṇḍajāteḥ samāśrayam \|*  
*jātayo vyaktayaścaiva tadājñāparipālitāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*yatastato mahādevo jātivyaktivapuḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*pradhānapuruṣavyaktakālātmā kathyate śivaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-17. The lord is explained by some as the one who inheres in ihe form of Jāti and Vyakti. That which inheres whole bodies is called Jāti. Vyakti is in the form of the separate unit and is the support of Jāti. Both are protected by his Ājñā. So the lord is called Jātivyaktivapus.

## \|\| 12.5.18-21 \|\|

*pradhānaṃ prakṛtiṃ prāhuḥkṣetrajñaṃ puruṣaṃ tathā \|*  
*trayoviṃśatitattvāni vyaktamāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*kālaḥ kāryaprapañcasya pariṇāmaikakāraṇam \|*  
*eṣāmīśo 'dhipo dhātā pravartakanivartakaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*āvirbhāvatirobhāvaheturekaḥ svarāḍajaḥ \|*  
*tasmātpradhānapuruṣavyaktakālasvarūpavān \|\| 20 \|\|*

*heturnetādhipasteṣāṃ dhātā coktā maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*virāḍḍhiraṇyagarbhātmā kaiścidīśo nigadyate \|\| 21 \|\|*

18-21. By some Śiva is called Pradhāna-Puruṣa-Vyakta-Kālātman. Pradhāna is Prakṛti. Puruṣa is the individual soul. The twenty three principles constitute the Vyakta (manifest) Prakṛti. Kāla is the sole cause of the transformation of the effected creation. Śiva is the lord, creator, activisor, router, and the cause of evolution and dissolution of all these. He is one, the emperor, the unborn. Hence he is called ‘Pradhāna-Puruṣa-Vyakta-Kāla-Svarūpavān’. He is the cause, leader, overlord and the creator of all these.

## \|\| 12.5.22 \|\|

*hiraṇyagarbho lokānāṃ heturviśvātmako virāṭ \|*  
*aṃtaryāmī paraśceti kathyate kavibhiśśivaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. By some he is mentioned as the Ātman of Virāṭ and Hiraṇyagarbha. Hiraṇyagarbha is the cause of the worlds, Brahmā etc., Virāṭ is the cosmic form or being.

## \|\| 12.5.23 \|\|

*prājñastaijasaviśvātmetyapare saṃpracakṣate \|*  
*turīyamapare prāhuḥ saumyameva pare viduḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Śiva is called as the immanent and the great soul. Others say he is the Ātman of Prājña, Taijasa and Viśva.

## \|\| 12.5.24 \|\|

*mātā mānaṃ ca meyaṃ ca matiṃ cāhurathāpare \|*  
*kartā kriyā ca kāryaṃ ca karaṇaṃ kāraṇaṃ pare \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Others say he is the fourth being Saumya. Others say that he is the measurer, measure and the measured as well as the intellect.

## \|\| 12.5.25 \|\|

*jāgratsvapnasuṣuptyātmetyapare saṃpracakṣate \|*  
*turīyamapare prāhusturyātītamitītare \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Others declare that he is the maker, the action, the effect, the instrument and the cause. Others say that he is the Ātman of wakefulness, dream and slumber.

## \|\| 12.5.26 \|\|

*tamāhurviguṇaṃ kecidguṇavantaṃ pare viduḥ \|*  
*kecitsaṃsāriṇaṃ prāhustamasaṃsāriṇaṃ pare \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Some call him the fourth one or the being beyond the fourth one. Some call him devoid of Guṇas or possessing Guṇas.

## \|\| 12.5.27-33 \|\|

*svataṃtramapare prāhurasvataṃtraṃ pare viduḥ \|*  
*ghoramityapare prāhuḥ saumyameva pare viduḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*rāgavaṃtaṃ pare prāhurvītarāgaṃ tathā pare \|*  
*niṣkriyaṃ ca pare prāhuḥ sakriyaṃ cetare janāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*niriṃdriyaṃ pare prāhuḥ seṃdriyaṃ ca tathāpare \|*  
*dhruvamityapare prāhustamadhruvāmitīrate \|\| 29 \|\|*

*arūpaṃ kecidāhurvai rūpavaṃtaṃ pare viduḥ \|*  
*adṛśyamapare prāhurdṛśyamityapare viduḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*vācyamityapare prāhuravācyamiti cāpare \|*  
*śabdātmakaṃ pare prāhuśśabdātītamathāpare \|\| 31 \|\|*

*keciccintāmayaṃ prāhuścintayā rahitaṃ pare \|*  
*jñānātmakaṃ pare prāhurvijñānamiti cāpare \|\| 32 \|\|*

*kecicjñeyamiti prāhurajñeyamiti kecana \|*  
*parameke tamevāhuraparaṃ ca tathā pare \|\| 33 \|\|*

27-33. Some call him having worldly existence; Others having no worldly existence. Still others call him free, not free, terrible, gentle, passionate, passionless, inactive, active, possessed or devoid of sense-organs, stable, not stable, with colour or no colour, visible, invisible, expressible, inexpressible, in the form of word and sound or beyond that, possessed or devoid of thought and knowledge, comprehensible or incomprehensible, great and not great.

## \|\| 12.5.34 \|\|

*evaṃ vikalpyamānaṃ tu yāthātmyaṃ parameṣṭhinaḥ \|*  
*nādhyavasyaṃti munayo nānāpratyayakāraṇāt \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Thus his innate nature, the true form, is being doubted. The sages are unable to determine the true nature of the lord due to the presence of different ideas and beliefs.

## \|\| 12.5.35 \|\|

*ye punassarvabhāvena prapannāḥ parameśvaram \|*  
*te hi jānaṃtyayatnena śivaṃ paramakāraṇam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. On the other hand, only those who have resorted to the lord in all piety know Śiva, the great cause, without any strain.

## \|\| 12.5.36 \|\|

*yāvatpaśurnaiva paśyatyanīśaṃ 1 purāṇaṃ bhuvanasyeśitāram \|*  
*tāvadduḥkhe vartate baddhapāśaḥ saṃsāre 'smiñcakranemikrameṇa \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. As long as the individual does not achieve the realization of the primordial lord who has no lord above him and who is the ruler of the worlds, he remains in misery bound by the noose. He undergoes the sufferings of the worldly existence in succession like the rim of the wheel.

## \|\| 12.5.37 \|\|

*yadā 2 paśyaḥ paśyate rukmavarṇaṃ kartāramīśaṃ puruṣaṃ brahmayonim \|*  
*tadāvidvānpuṇyapāpe vidhūya niraṃjanaḥ paramamupaiti sāmyam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. When the seer sees the maker, the lord, golden in colour, the Puruṣa the origin of Brahmā, he shakes off both merits and sins and becomes unsullied. He attains the great equality or union with the lord.

## Chapter 6 - The Principle of Śiva (1)

## \|\| 12.6.1-2 \|\|

*upamanyuruvāca \|*  
*naśivasyāṇavo baṃdhaḥ kāryo māyeya eva vā \|*  
*prākṛto vātha boddhā vā hyahaṃkārātmakastathā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*naivāsya mānaso baṃdho na caitto neṃdriyātmakaḥ \|*  
*na ca tanmātrabaṃdho 'pi bhūtabaṃdho na kaścana \|\| 2 \|\|*

Upamanyu said:—

1-2. Śiva has no bondage due to the atoms, effects, Māyā, Prakṛti, cosmic intellect, ego, mind, sense-organs,

Tanmātras or the elements.

## \|\| 12.6.3 \|\|

*na ca kālaḥ kalā caiva na vidyā niyatistathā \|*  
*na rāgo na ca vidveṣaḥ śaṃbhoramitatejasaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. To Śiva of unmeasured brilliance there is no Kāla or Kalā; no Vidyā or Niyati; neither lust nor hatred.

## \|\| 12.6.4 \|\|

*na cāstyabhiniveśo 'sya kuśalā 'kuśalānyapi \|*  
*karmāṇi tadvipākaśca sukhaduḥkhe ca tatphale \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He has no keen desire. He has neither happiness nor unhappiness; neither Karmans nor their after-effects; neither# pleasure nor misery as a result of those Karmans.

## \|\| 12.6.5 \|\|

*āśayairnāpi saṃbandhaḥ saṃskāraiḥ karmaṇāmapi \|*  
*bhogaiśca bhogasaṃskāraiḥ kālatritayagocaraiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. He has no connection with the seats of feelings nor with the impressions of actions. He has no contact with enjoyments of pleasures nor with their impressions of the three units of lime—past, present, future

## \|\| 12.6.6 \|\|

*na tasya kāraṇaṃ kartā nādiraṃtastathāṃtaram \|*  
*na karma karaṇaṃ vāpi nākāryaṃ kāryameva ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He has no cause or maker; he has no beginning no end nor the intervening space. He has no activity or instrument. He has neither Akārya nor Kārya.

## \|\| 12.6.7 \|\|

*nāsya baṃdhurabaṃdhurvā niyaṃtā prerako 'pi vā \|*  
*na patirna gurustrātā nādhiko na samastathā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. He has neither kinsman nor non-kinsman; he has no one to check or to urge. He has no lord, preceptor or protector. He has no superior or equal.

## \|\| 12.6.8 \|\|

*na janmamaraṇe tasya na kāṃkṣitamakāṃkṣitam \|*  
*na vidhirna niṣedhaśca na muktirna ca bandhanam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He has neither birth nor death; neither expectation nor disinclination. He is not subject to injunctions or prohibitions; he has neither liberation nor bondage.

## \|\| 12.6.9 \|\|

*nāsti yadyadakalyāṇaṃ tattadasya kadācana \|*  
*kalyāṇaṃ sakalaṃ cāsti paramātmā śivo yataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. He never has anything not conducive to welfare or inauspicious. He has everything auspicious since Śiva is the great Ātman.

## \|\| 12.6.10 \|\|

*sa śivassarvamevedamadhiṣṭhāya svaśaktibhiḥ \|*  
*apracyutassvato bhāvaḥ sthitaḥ sthāṇurataḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Presiding over everything by means of his Śaktis, he is stationed without dropping his intrinsic nature. Hence he is known as Śiva.

## \|\| 12.6.11 \|\|

*śivenādhiṣṭhitaṃ yasmājjagatsthāvarajaṃgamam \|*  
*sarvarūpaḥ smṛtaśśarvastathā jñātvā na muhyati \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Since the universe consisting of the mobile and immobile beings is presided over by Śiva, he is known as omniformed. One who knows him as such, is never deluded.

## \|\| 12.6.12 \|\|

*śarvo rudro namastasmai puruṣaḥ satparo mahān \|*  
*hiraṇyabāhurbhagavānhiraṇyapatirīśvaraḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Śiva is Rudra. Obeisance to him. He is the great Puruṣa beyond the Sat. He has golden arms, he is the lord of gold.

## \|\| 12.6.13 \|\|

*aṃbikāpatirīśānaḥ pinākī vṛṣavāhanaḥ \|*  
*eko rudraḥ paraṃ brahma puruṣaḥ kṛṣṇapiṃgalaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Isāna is the consort of Śivā. He is the trident-bearing, and bull-vehicled lord. The sole Rudra is the great Brahman. He is the black and tawny Puruṣa.

## \|\| 12.6.14 \|\|

*bālāgramātro hṛnmadhye viciṃtyo daharāṃtare \|*  
*hiraṇyakeśaḥ padmākṣo hyaruṇastāmra eva ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. He shall be meditated upon in the cavity within the heart as minute as the tip of a hair, with golden hair, and lotus eyes. He is pink and copper-coloured.

## \|\| 12.6.15-16 \|\|

*yo 'vasarpatya sau devo nīlagrīvo hiraṇmayaḥ \|*  
*saumyo ghorastathā miśraścākṣāraścāmṛto 'vyayaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*sa puṃviśeṣaḥ paramo bhagavānantakāṃtakaḥ \|*  
*cetanacetanonmuktaḥ prapañcācca parātparaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. He moves about golden in colour, blue-necked, both gentle and terrible and a mixure of the both, imperishable, deathless and unchangeable. Such is the great lord, the slayer of the god of death. He is liberated from the sentient and non-sentient. He is greater than the great universe.

## \|\| 12.6.17 \|\|

*śivenātiśayatvena jñānaiśvarye vilokite \|*  
*lokeśātiśayatvena sthitaṃ prāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Since the knowledge and supremacy of Śiva excels those of others he excels all the lords of the worlds so say the intelligent persons.

## \|\| 12.6.18 \|\|

*pratisargaprasūtānāṃ brahmaṇāṃ śāstravistaram \|*  
*upadeṣṭā sa evādau kālāvacchedavartinām \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. In the beginning he was the instructor of the scriptural texts to the Brahmans born during the period of re-creation.

## \|\| 12.6.19 \|\|

*kālāvacchedayuktānāṃ gurūṇāmapyasau guruḥ \|*  
*sarveṣāmeva sarveśaḥ kālāvacchedavarjitaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. He is not conditioned by time. He is the lord of all. He is the preceptor of all the preceptors, subject to the influence of Time.

## \|\| 12.6.20 \|\|

*śuddhā svābhāvikī tasya śaktissarvātiśāyinī \|*  
*jñānamapratimaṃ nityaṃ vapuratyantanirmitam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. His Śakti is pure, natural and all-excelling. His knowledge is unparalleled. His physical body is eternal and built to defy death.

## \|\| 12.6.21 \|\|

*aiśvaryamapratidvaṃdvaṃ sukhamātyantikaṃ balam \|*  
*tejaḥprabhāvo vīryaṃ ca kṣamā kāruṇyameva ca \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. His lordship is unrivalled, so also his happiness, undying strength, power of brilliance, virility, forbearance and mercifulness.

## \|\| 12.6.22 \|\|

*paripūrṇasya sargādyairnātmano 'sti prayojanam \|*  
*parānugraha evāsya phalaṃ sarvasya karmaṇaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Since he is full and perfect he has no selfish end to be served by creation etc. The fruit of his activities is only the blessing of others.

## \|\| 12.6.23 \|\|

*praṇavo vācakastasya śivasya paramātmanaḥ \|*  
*śivarudrādiśabdānāṃ praṇavo hi parassmṛtaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Praṇava is the word expressive of lord Śiva. Praṇava is the greatest symbol of Śiva, Rudra and other words.

## \|\| 12.6.24 \|\|

*śaṃbho praṇavavācyasya bhavanāttajjapādapi \|*  
*yā siddhissā parā prāpyā bhavatyeva na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Undoubtedly the great Siddhi can be acquired by meditation on Praṇava that is expressive of Śiva and by the performance of its Japa.

## \|\| 12.6.25 \|\|

*tasmādekākṣaraṃ devamāhurāgamapāragāḥ \|*  
*vācyavācakayoraikyaṃ manyamānā manasvinaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Hence intelligent men well-versed in the Āgamas considering identity between the word and its meaning call the lord as single-syllabled.

## \|\| 12.6.26 \|\|

*asya mātrāḥ samākhyātāścatasro vedamūrdhani \|*  
*akāraścāpyukāraśca makāro nāda ityapi \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. In the Upaniṣads its Mātrās are four A, U, M and nāda.

## \|\| 12.6.27 \|\|

*akāraṃ bahvṛcaṃ prāhurukāro yajurucyate \|*  
*makāraḥ sāmanādosya śrutirātharvaṇī smṛtāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The letter “A” is the Ṛgveda; “U” is the Yajurveda; “M” is the Sāmaveda and the Nāda is the Atharvaveda.

## \|\| 12.6.28 \|\|

*akāraśca mahābījaṃ rajaḥ sraṣṭā caturmukhaḥ \|*  
*ukāraḥ prakṛtiryoniḥ sattvaṃ pālayitā hariḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The letter “A” is the great Bīja, Rajas and the creator, the four-faced lord. The letter “U” is Prakṛti, the womb, Sattva and the protector Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 12.6.29 \|\|

*makāraḥ puruṣo bījaṃ tamaḥ saṃhārako haraḥ \|*  
*nādaḥ paraḥ pumānīśo nirguṇo niṣkriyaḥ śivaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The letter “M” is Puruṣa, the seed, the Tamas and the annihilator Rudra. Nāda is the great Puruṣa, Īśa, Śiva, devoid of Guṇas and activities.

## \|\| 12.6.30 \|\|

*sarvaṃ tisṛbhirevedaṃ mātrābhirnikhilaṃ tridhā \|*  
*abhidhāya śivātmānaṃ bodhayatyardhamātrayā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Praṇava expresses everything through the three Mātrās in three ways and indicates Śivātman through half a Mātrā.

## \|\| 12.6.31 \|\|

*yasmātparaṃ nāparamasti kiṃcidyasmānnāṇīyo na jyāyo 'sti kiṃcit \|*  
*vṛkṣa iva stabdho divi tiṣṭhatyekastenedaṃ pūrṇaṃ puruṣeṇa sarvam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. All this is filled by that Puruṣa than whom there is nothing else greater; than whom there is nothing smaller nor bigger and who like a tree stands steady and stiff in the heaven.

## Chapter 7 - The principle of Śiva (2)

## \|\| 12.7.1 \|\|

*upamanyuruvāca \|*  
*śaktissvābhavikī tasya vidyā viśvavilakṣaṇā \|*  
*ekānekasya rūpeṇa bhāti bhānoriva prabhā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Upamanyu said:—

1\. His Śakti shall be known as natural and dissimilar to the universe in its characteristics. It is single but appears in many forms like the light of the sun.

## \|\| 12.7.2 \|\|

*anaṃtāḥ śaktayo yasyā icchājñānakriyādayaḥ \|*  
*māyādyāścābhavanvahnorvisphuliṃgā yathā tathā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Endless are the Śaktis, viz, wish, knowledge, activity and Māyā etc. just like the flames of fire.

## \|\| 12.7.3 \|\|

*sadāśiveśvarādyā hi vidyā 'vidyeśvarādayaḥ \|*  
*abhavanpuruṣāścāsyāḥ prakṛtiśca parātparā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The Puruṣas—Sadāśiva, Īśvara and others, Vidyeśvara Avidyeśvara and others and Prakṛti—greater than the greatest were born of this Śakti.

## \|\| 12.7.4 \|\|

*mahadādiviśeṣāṃtāstvajādyāścāpi mūrtayaḥ \|*  
*yaccānyadasti tatsarvaṃ tasyāḥ kāryaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. There is no doubt that the principles from Mahat to Viśeṣa, the deities Brahmā and others and whatever there is as effect are produced by it.

## \|\| 12.7.5 \|\|

*sā śaktissarvagā sūkṣmā prabodhānaṃdarūpiṇī \|*  
*śaktimānucyate devaśśivaśśītāṃśubhūṣaṇaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. That Śakti is all-pervasive and subtle. It has the form of enlightenment and bliss. The moon-bedecked lord is, called Śaktimān.

## \|\| 12.7.6 \|\|

*vedyaśśivaśśivā vidyā prajñā caiva śrutiḥ smṛtiḥ \|*  
*dhṛtireṣā sthitirniṣṭhā jñānecchākarmaśaktayaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Śiva is the one who shall be known. Sivā is intellect, the Vedas, the firmness, stability, fixity and the Śakti of knowledge, wish and activity.

## \|\| 12.7.7 \|\|

*ājñā caiva paraṃ brahma dve vidye ca parāpare \|*  
*śuddhavidyā śuddhakalā sarvaṃ śaktikṛtaṃ yataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Ājñā is the great Brahman. The two Vidyās are Parā and Aparā, Śuddhavidyā and Śuddhakalā since everything is created by Śakti.

## \|\| 12.7.8 \|\|

*māyā ca prakṛtirjīvo vikāro vikṛtistathā \|*  
*asacca sacca yatkiṃcittayā sarvamidaṃ tatam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Māyā is Prakṛti. Jīva is Vikṛti. Whatever there is Sat or Asat is pervaded by Śakti.

## \|\| 12.7.9 \|\|

*sā devī māyayā sarvaṃ brahmāṃḍaṃ sacarācaram \|*  
*mohayatyaprayatnena mocayatyapi līlayā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The goddess enchants and deludes the universe without any strain through Māyā. She releases the Jīvas sportively.

## \|\| 12.7.10 \|\|

*anayā saha sarveśaḥ saptaviṃśaprakārayā \|*  
*viśvaṃ vyāpya sthitastasmānmuktiratra pravartate \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. With her ramified into twenty-seven forms, the lord stands pervading the universe. Hence the process of liberation functions.

## \|\| 12.7.11-17 \|\|

*mumukṣavaḥ purā kecinmunayo brahmavādinaḥ \|*  
*saṃśayāviṣṭamanaso vismṛśaṃti yathātatham \|\| 11 \|\|*

*kiṃ kāraṇaṃ kuto jātā jīvāmaḥ kena vā vayam \|*  
*kutrāsmākaṃ saṃpratiṣṭhā kena vādhiṣṭhitā vayam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*kena vartāmahe śaśvatsukheṣvanyeṣu cāniśam \|*  
*avilaṃghyā ca viśvasya vyavasthā kena vā kṛtā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*kālasya bhāvo niyatiryadṛcchā nātra yujyate \|*  
*bhūtāni yoniḥ puruṣo yogī caiṣāṃ paro 'tha vā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*acetanatvātkālādeścetanatvepi cātmanaḥ \|*  
*sukhaduḥkhāni bhūtatvādanīśatvādvicāryate \|\| 15 \|\|*

*taddhyānayogānugatāṃ prapaśyañchaktimaiśvarīm \|*  
*pāśavicchedikāṃ sākṣānnigūḍhāṃ svaguṇairbhṛśam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*tayā vicchinnapāśāste sarvakāraṇakāraṇam \|*  
*śaktimaṃtaṃ mahādevamapaśyandivyacakṣuṣā \|\| 17 \|\|*

11-17. Formerly some sages desirous of salvation held a discourse on Brahman. Their minds were pestered by doubts. They began to reflect and ponder. “What is the ultimate reason? Whence are we born? Whereby do we live? Where is our final establishment? By whom are we presided Over? Whereby do we permanently abide by happiness or other things? By whom was the untransgressable arrangement of the universe made? It is not befitting to take time, nature, destiny, chance as the ultimate, reason. Nor can it be the Puruṣa or any of the living beings or a Yogin greater than these. Time etc. are insentient and cannot function as the ultimate reason. Though the Ātman is sentient and experiences happiness and misery yet it is incapable of ruling. After these reflections those who meditate can realise the Śakti of the lord, the splitter of the Pāśa but hidden by the Guṇas. Through this Śakti when their binding cords are cut they can see the Śaktimān, the cause of all causes, through their divine eyes.

## \|\| 12.7.18 \|\|

*yaḥ kāraṇānyaśeṣāṇi kālātmasahitāni ca \|*  
*aprameyo 'nayā śaktyā sakalaṃ yo 'dhitiṣṭhati \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He is incomprehensible and through this Śakti he presides over all causes, including the Time-soul.

## \|\| 12.7.19 \|\|

*tataḥ prasādayogena yogena parameṇa ca \|*  
*dṛṣṭena bhaktiyogena divyaḥ gatimavāpnuyuḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Then through his grace, the great Yoga and the path of devotion they can attain the supreme divine goal.

## \|\| 12.7.20 \|\|

*tasmātsaha tathā śaktyā hṛdi paśyaṃti ye śivam \|*  
*teṣāṃ śāśvatikī śāṃtirnaitareṣāmiti śrutiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The Vedas declare that only those have permanent peace who see Śiva in their hearts along with that Śakti and none of the others.

## \|\| 12.7.21 \|\|

*na hi śaktimataśśaktyā viprayogo 'sti jātucit \|*  
*tasmācchakteḥ śaktimatastādātmyānnirvṛtirdvayoḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Never is Śaktiman apart from the blissful Śakti due to the identity between Śakti and Śaktimān

## \|\| 12.7.22 \|\|

*kramo vivakṣito nūnaṃ vimuktau jñānakarmaṇoḥ \|*  
*prasāde sati sā mūrtiryasmātkaratale sthitā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. In regard to salvation the sequence of knowledge and activity is not intended because if there is divine grace salvation is accessible to everyone.

## \|\| 12.7.23 \|\|

*devo vā dānavo vāpi paśurvā vihago 'pi vā \|*  
*kīro vātha kṛmirvāpi mucyate tatprasādataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Whether one is a god or an asura, an animal or a bird, a worm on a germ, one is liberated due to his grace.

## \|\| 12.7.24-25 \|\|

*garbhastho jāyamāno vā bālo vā taruṇopi vā \|*  
*vṛddho vā mriyamāṇo vā svargastho vātha nārakī \|\| 24 \|\|*

*patito vāpi dharmātmā paṃḍito mūḍha eva vā \|*  
*prasāde tatkṣaṇādeva mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. There is no doubt that a child in the womb, a nascent child, a boy, a young, old or a dying man, a soul in heaven or hell, a fallen or a pious, or a wise man or a fool is immediately released if there is divine grace.

## \|\| 12.7.26 \|\|

*ayogyānāṃ ca kāruṇyādbhaktānāṃ parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*prasīdati na saṃdeho vigṛhya vividhānmalān \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The merciful lord quells different dirts of his devotees though they may be unqualified. He is pleased with their devotion.

## \|\| 12.7.27 \|\|

*prasadādeva sā bhaktiḥ prasādo bhaktisaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*avasthābhedamutprekṣya vidvāṃstatra na muhyati \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Their devotion is due to their grace and the grace is a result of devotion in view of the difference in states. A learned man is not deluded therein.

## \|\| 12.7.28 \|\|

*prasādapūrvikā yeyaṃ bhuktimuktividhāyinī \|*  
*naiva sā śakyate prāptuṃ narairekena janmanā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. This devotion with grace as its antecedent and causing worldly pleasures and salvation cannot be acquired in a single birth.

## \|\| 12.7.29 \|\|

*anekajanmasiddhānāṃ śrautasmārtānuvartinām \|*  
*viraktānāṃ prabuddhānāṃ prasīdati maheśvaraḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Maheśvara is delighted with enlightened people not attached to worldly pleasures who follow the rules prescribed in Śrutis and Smṛtis and who achieve Siddhis in the course of several births.

## \|\| 12.7.30-31 \|\|

*prasanne sati deveśa paśau tasminpravartate \|*  
*asti nātho mametyalpā bhaktirbuddhipurassarā \|\| 30 \|\|*

*tapasā vividhaiśśaivairdharmaissaṃyujyate naraḥ \|*  
*tatra yoge tadabhyāsastato bhaktiḥ parā bhavet \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. When the lord of gods is delighted a modicum of devotion is generated in the individual with the consciousness, “My lord exists”. Then he begins to be associated with penance and various Śaivitc holy rites. After their performance and their frequent practice the devotion becomes greater.

## \|\| 12.7.32 \|\|

*parayā ca tayā bhaktyā prasādo labhyate paraḥ \|*  
*prasādātsarvapāśebhyo muktirmuktasya nirvṛtiḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. As a result of that a greater grace is acquired. As a result of the grace liberation is attained. A liberated soul enjoys bliss.

## \|\| 12.7.33 \|\|

*alpabhāvo 'pi yo martyasso 'pi janmatrayātparam \|*  
*nayoniyaṃtrapīḍāyai bhavennaivātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. There is no doubt that even a man of limited piety

is spared the excruciating pain of being crushed in the machine of the vaginal passage after three births.

## \|\| 12.7.34 \|\|

*sāṃgā 'naṃgā ca yā sevā sā bhaktiriti kathyate \|*  
*sā punarbhidyate tredhā manovākkāyasādhanaiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Service with or without the ancillaries is called devotion. It is threefold due to the three means of mind speech and body.

## \|\| 12.7.35 \|\|

*śivarūpādiciṃtā yā sā sevā mānasī smṛtā \|*  
*japādirvācikī sevā karmapūjādi kāyikī \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The meditation on Śiva’s form is mental service. Repetition of mantras is verbal service. The rites of worship constitute the physical service.

## \|\| 12.7.36 \|\|

*seyaṃ trisādhanā sevā śivadharmaśca kathyate \|*  
*sa tu pañcavidhaḥ proktaḥ śivena paramātmanā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. This threefold service is called the holy rite of Śiva. It is of five kinds as explained by Śiva the great Ātman.

## \|\| 12.7.37-38 \|\|

*tapaḥ karma japo dhyānaṃ jñānaṃ ceti samāsataḥ \|*  
*karmaliṅgārcanādyaṃ ca tapaścāndrāyaṇādikam \|\| 37 \|\|*

*japastridhā śivābhyāsaścintā dhyānaṃ śivasya tu \|*  
*śivāgamoktaṃ yajjñānaṃ tadatra jñānamucyate \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. In brief they are penance, holy rites, repetition of mantras, meditation and knowledge. Penance is the rite of Cāndrāyaṇa, etc. What is termed holy rite is the worship of Śiva’s phallic image. Japa is the repetition of the names of Śiva in three ways. Meditation is pondering over Śiva. What is mentioned in the Śaivite Āgamas as perfect knowledge is meant by the word knowledge here.

## \|\| 12.7.39 \|\|

*śrīkaṃṭhena śivenoktaṃ śivāyai ca śivāgamaḥ \|*  
*śivāśritānāṃ kāruṇyācchreyasāmekasādhanam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The Śaivite Āgama was narrated to Śivā by Śiva out of mercy for those who have resorted to him. That is the sole means of ultimate welfare.

## \|\| 12.7.40 \|\|

*tasmādvivardhayedbhaktiṃ śive paramakāraṇe \|*  
*tyajecca viṣayāsaṃgaṃ śreyo 'rthī matimānnaraḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. An intelligent man seeking welfare shall avoid too much adherence to sensual objects and increase devotion towards Śiva, the great cause.

## Chapter 8 - The incarnations of Vyāsa

## \|\| 12.8.1-2 \|\|

*kṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*bhagavañchrotumicchāmi śivena paribhāṣitam \|*  
*vedasāre śivajñānaṃ svāśritānāṃ vimuktaye \|\| 1 \|\|*

*abhaktānāmabuddhīnāmayuktānāmagocaram \|*  
*arthairdaśardhaiḥ saṃyuktaṃ gūḍhamaprājñaniṃditam \|\| 2 \|\|*

Lord Kṛṣṇa said:—

1-2. O lord, I wish to hear about Śiva’s knowledge expounded by Śiva in the Vedasāra for the salvation of his devotees. It is incomprehensible to non-devotees, the unintelligent and those who do not practise Yoga. It consists of five topics. It is censured by the unwise stupid persons.

## \|\| 12.8.3 \|\|

*varṇāśramakṛtairdharmairviparītaṃ kvacitsamam \|*  
*vedātṣaḍaṃgāduddhṛtya sāṃkhyādyogācca kṛtsnaśaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. At places it is opposed to the rites prescribed for the different castes and men in different stages of life. At places it is the same. It has been adopted from the Vedas, their ancillary texts and from the systems of Sāṅkhya and Yoga.

## \|\| 12.8.4-5 \|\|

*śatakoṭipramāṇena vistīrṇaṃ graṃthasaṃkhyayā \|*  
*kathitaṃ parameśena tatra pūjā kathaṃ prabhoḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*kasyādhikāraḥ pūjādau jñānayogādayaḥ katham \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ vistarādeva vaktumarhasi suvrata \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. It extends to a hundred crores of verses as narrated by lord Śiva. How shall the worship be performed, O lord? Who is authorised in the worship? What are the practices of Jñānayoga etc.? O sage of good rites, it behoves you to narrate all these things in detail.

## \|\| 12.8.6-7 \|\|

*upamanyuruvāca \|*  
*śaivaṃ saṃkṣipya vedoktaṃ śivena paribhāṣitam \|*  
*stutiniṃdādirahitaṃ sadyaḥ pratyayakāraṇam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*guruprasādajaṃ divyamanāyāsena muktidam \|*  
*kathayiṣye samāsena tasya śakyo na vistaraḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

Upamanyu said:—

6-7. I shall succinctly narrate the lore of Śiva condensed from the Vedas as narrated by Śiva. I shall avoid its praises or condemnations. It is convincing and divine. It can be acquired only by the grace of the preceptor. It is conducive to salvation without any strain. A detailed explanation of the same is impossible.

## \|\| 12.8.8 \|\|

*sisṛkṣayā purāvyaktācchivaḥ sthāṇurmaheśvaraḥ \|*  
*satkāryakāraṇopetassvayamāvirabhūtprabhuḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Formerly, with the desire to create, lord Śiva, equipped with the causes of the effects already present, manifested himself from the unmanifest.

## \|\| 12.8.9 \|\|

*janayāmāsa ca tadā ṛṣirviśvādhikaḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*devānāṃ prathamaṃ devaṃ brahmāṇaṃ brahmaṇaspatim \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Then the lord, the sage, superior to all procreated the first of the gods Brahmā, the Brahmaṇaspati.

## \|\| 12.8.10 \|\|

*brahmāpi pitaraṃ devaṃ jāyamānaṃ nyavaikṣata \|*  
*taṃ jāyamānaṃ janako devaḥ prāpaśyadājñayā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. While being born, Brahmā saw the lord his father. The lord saw and commanded him.

## \|\| 12.8.11 \|\|

*dṛṣṭo rudreṇa devo 'sāvasṛjadviśvamīśvaraḥ \|*  
*varṇāśramavyavasthāṃ ca cakāra sa pṛthakpṛthak \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Brahmā viewed by Rudra created the universe. He prescribed the rules for different bastes and stages of life separately.

## \|\| 12.8.12 \|\|

*somaṃ sasarja yajñārthe somāddyaussamajāyata \|*  
*dharā ca vahniḥ sūryaśca yajño viṣṇuśśacīpatiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. For the sake of sacrifice he created Soma. From Soma was born the heaven, earth, fire, sun, sacrifice, Viṣṇu and Indra.

## \|\| 12.8.13 \|\|

*te cānye ca surā rudraṃ rudrādhyāyena tuṣṭuvuḥ \|*  
*prasannavadanastasthau devānāmagrataḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. They and the gods eulogised Rudra with the hymns dedicated to him. The lord stood before the gods with his face beaming with delight.

## \|\| 12.8.14 \|\|

*apahṛtya svalīlārthaṃ teṣāṃ jñānaṃ maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*tamapṛcchaṃstato devāḥ ko bhavāniti mohitāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The lord took away their knowledge, sportively. The deluded gods asked him, “Who are you Śir?”

## \|\| 12.8.15-18 \|\|

*so 'bravīdbhagavānrudro hyahamekaḥ purātanaḥ \|*  
*āsaṃ prathamamevāhaṃ vartāmi 1 ca surottamāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*bhaviṣyāmi ca mattonyo vyatirikto na kaścana \|*  
*ahameva jagatsarvaṃ tarpayāmi svatejasā \|\| 16 \|\|*

*matto 'dhikaḥ samo nāsti māṃ yo veda sa mucyate \|*  
*ityuktvā bhagavānrudrastatraivāṃtaradhatta sa \|*

*apaśyaṃtastamīśānaṃ stuvaṃtaścaiva sāmabhiḥ \|*  
*vrataṃ pāśupataṃ kṛtvā tvatharvaśirasi sthitam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*bhasmasaṃchannasarvāṃgā babhūvuramarāstadā \|*  
*atha teṣāṃ prasādārthaṃ paśūnāṃ patirīśvaraḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

15-18. Lord Rudra said:—“I had been the only primeval being, O gods, I am and I shall be. There is none except me or separate from me. I alone satisfy the universe through my splendour. There is none superior to or equal to me. He who knows me is liberated.” After saying, this the lord vanished there itself. Unable to see him the gods began to eulogise him with Sāmans. They performed the holy rites of Pāśupata as prescribed in the Atharvaśiras Upaniṣads. They smeared Bhasma all over their bodies.

## \|\| 12.8.19-25 \|\|

*no sanskrit verse \|\| 19 \|\|*

*sagaṇaścomayā sārdhaṃ sānnidhyamakarotprabhuḥ \|*  
*yaṃ vinidrā jitaśvāsā yogino dagdhakilbiṣāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*hṛdi paśyaṃti taṃ devaṃ dadṛśurdevapuṃgavāḥ \|*  
*yāmāhuḥ paramāṃ śaktimīśvarecchānuvartinīm \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tāmapaśyanmaheśasya vāmato vāmalocanām \|*  
*ye vinirdhūtasaṃsārāḥ prāptāḥ śaivaṃ paraṃ padam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*nityasiddhāśca ye vānyaṃ te ca dṛṣṭā gaṇeśvarāḥ \|*  
*atha taṃ tuṣṭuvurdevā devyā saha maheśvaram \|\| 23 \|\|*

*stotrairmāheśvarairdivyaiḥ śrotaiḥ paurāṇikairapi \|*  
*devo 'pi devānālokya ghṛṇayā vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*tuṣṭo 'smītyāha suprītassvabhāvamadhurāṃ giram \|*  
*atha suprītamanasaṃ praṇipatya vṛṣadhvajam \|*

*arthamahattamaṃ devāḥ papracchurimamādarāt \|*  
*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*bhagavankena mārgeṇa pūjanīyo 'si bhūtale \|\| 25 \|\|*

19-25. In order to please them the lord came there with the Gaṇas and Umā. The leading gods saw the lord whom the awakened sinless Yogins of restrained breath see within their hearts. To the left of lord Śiva they saw the beautiful goddess, the greatest Śakti who followed the wish of the lord. The chiefs of the gaṇas who had forsaken worldiness and acquired the region of Śiva and the Siddhas were also seen. Then the gods eulogised the lord and the goddess with the divine hymns from the Vedas and the Purāṇas. The delighted bull-bannered lord saw the gods with mercy and spoke sweetly, ‘I am delighted.’ Then, bowing to him the gods asked him about this important topic.

## \|\| 12.8.26 \|\|

*kasyādhikāraḥ pūjāyāṃ vaktumarhasi tattvataḥ \|*  
*tataḥ sasmitamālokya devīṃ devavaroharaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

The gods said:—

26\. O lord, how shall they worship you on the earth? What is the path? Who is authorised in the worship?

## \|\| 12.8.27 \|\|

*svarūpaṃ darśayāmāsa ghoraṃ sūryātmakaṃ param \|*  
*sarvaiśvaryaguṇopetaṃ sarvatejomayaṃ param \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Glancing smilingly at the goddess, Śiva the chief of the gods revealed his terrible form brilliant as the sun.

## \|\| 12.8.28 \|\|

*śaktibhirmūrtibhiścāṃgairgrahairdevaiśca saṃvṛtam \|*  
*aṣṭabāhuṃ caturvaktramardhanārīkamadbhutam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. It was equipped with the attributes of lordship. It comprised all splendours. It was surrounded by the Śaktis, images, planets and the gods.

## \|\| 12.8.29-31 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvaivamadbhutākāraṃ devā viṣṇupurogamāḥ \|*  
*buddhvā divākaraṃ devaṃ devīṃ caiva niśākaram \|\| 29 \|\|*

*pañcabhūtāni śeṣāṇi tanmayaṃ ca carācaram \|*  
*evamuktvā namaścakrustasmai cārghyaṃ pradāya vai \|\| 30 \|\|*

*no sanskrit verse \|\| 31 \|\|*

29-31. The lord had eight arms and four faces. Half of that form was female. On seeing this wondrous form, Viṣṇu and other gods understood the lord as the sun and the goddess as the moon and the remaining parts as elements. They realised the universe of the mobile and immobile beings identical with him. Then they worshipped the lord and made obeisance to him.

## \|\| 12.8.32-33 \|\|
