*tasya nāsti samo loke sa siddhaḥ siddhado bhavet \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. There is none equal to him in the world who, after the Puraścaraṇa is over, continues to perform the Japa everyday. He is Siddha himself and confers Siddhi on others too.

## \|\| 12.14.20-23 \|\|

*snānaṃ kṛtvā śucau deśe baddhvā ruciramānasam \|*  
*tvayā māṃ hṛdi saṃciṃtya saṃciṃtya svaguruṃ tataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*udaṅmukhaḥ prāṅmukho vā maunī caikāgramānasaḥ \|*  
*viśodhya pañcatattvāni dahanaplāvanādibhiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*mantranyāsādikaṃ kṛtvā saphalīkṛtavigrahaḥ \|*  
*āvayorvigrahau dhyāyanprāṇāpānau niyamya ca \|\| 22 \|\|*

*vidyāsthānaṃ svakaṃ rūpamṛṣiñchando 'dhidaivatam \|*  
*bījaṃ śaktiṃ tathā vākyaṃ smṛtvā pañcākṣarīṃ japet \|\| 23 \|\|*

20-23. He shall take bath, sit in a pleasing posture in a sacred spot. He shall meditate on me in his heart along with you and shall remember his preceptor. He shall sit facing the north or the east, observe silence and concentration of the mind, purify the five principles by means of Dahana and Plāvana rituals. He shall perform the Mantranyāsa, make his body worthy and pure, meditate on us restraining Prāṇa and Apāna. He shall remember the respective place, form, sage, metre, the presiding deity, Bīja, Śakti and the statement. Then he shall perform the Japa of the five-syllabled mantra.

## \|\| 12.14.24 \|\|

*uttamaṃ mānasaṃ jāpyamupāṃśuṃ caivamadhyamam \|*  
*adhamaṃ vācikaṃ prāhurāgamārthaviśāradāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Experts in the meanings of Āgama texts say that the mental Japa is excellent, the Upāṃśu Japa (in a low voice) is the middling. The verbal Japa is of the lowest quality.

## \|\| 12.14.25 \|\|

*uttamaṃ rudradaivatyaṃ madhyamaṃ viṣṇudaivatam \|*  
*adhamaṃ brahmadaivatyamityāhuranupūrvaśaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The Japa with Rudra as the presiding deity is the most excellent, that with Viṣṇu as the presiding deity is the middling and that with Brahmā as the presiding deity is of the lowest quality.

## \|\| 12.14.26 \|\|

*yaduccanīcasvaritaiḥspaṣṭāspaṣṭapadākṣaraiḥ \|*  
*maṃtramuccārayedvācā vāciko 'yaṃ japassmṛtaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The muttering of the mantra with high, low or middle accentuation, the words and the letters being clear or otherwise, is called the verbal japa.

## \|\| 12.14.27 \|\|

*jihvāmātraparispaṃdādīṣaduccārito 'pi vā \|*  
*aparairaśrutaḥ kiṃcicchruto vopāṃśurucyate \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Upāṃśu Japa is the one where the tongue throbs and there is slight utterance. It may not be heard by others or may be slightly heard.

## \|\| 12.14.28 \|\|

*dhiyā yadakṣaraśreṇyā varṇādvarṇaṃ padātpadam \|*  
*śabdārthaciṃtanaṃ bhūyaḥ kathyate mānaso japaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Mental Japa is that where the series of letters are thought well and the wrords and their meanings are pondered over.

## \|\| 12.14.29 \|\|

*vācikastveka eva syādupāṃśuḥ śatamucyate \|*  
*sāhasraṃ mānasaḥ proktaḥ sagarbhastu śatādhikaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. If the efficacy of the Vācikajapa is one, that of the Upāṃśu Japa is hundred; that of the Mānasajapa is a thousand; that of the Sagarbha Japa is hundred times more.

## \|\| 12.14.30 \|\|

*prāṇāyāmasamāyuktassagarbho japa ucyate \|*  
*ādyaṃtayoragarbho 'pi prāṇāyāmaḥ praśasyate \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The Japa performed with the prāṇāyāma is Sagarbha Japa. In the first and the last even Agarbha Prāṇāyāma is commended.

## \|\| 12.14.31 \|\|

*catvāriṃśatsamāvṛttīḥ prāṇānāyamya saṃsmaret \|*  
*maṃtraṃ maṃtrārthaviddhīmānaśaktaḥ śaktito japet \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. After performing the Prāṇāyāma forty times, the intelligent devotee, knowing the meaning of the mantra, shall remember the mantra. If he is unable to repeat so many times he shall repeat as many times as his physical strength permits him.

## \|\| 12.14.32 \|\|

*pañcakaṃ trikamekaṃ vā prāṇāyāmaṃ samācaret \|*  
*agarbhaṃ vā sagarbhaṃ vā sagarbhastatra śasyate \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. He shall perform five, three or one Prāṇāyāma whether Agarbha or Sagarbha. The Sagarbha Prāṇāyāma is better of the two.

## \|\| 12.14.33 \|\|

*sagarbhādapi sāhasraṃ sadhyāno japa ucyate \|*  
*eṣu pañcavidheṣvekaḥ kartavyaḥ śaktito japaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The Sadhyāna Japa is a thousand times better than the Sagarbha Japa. One of the five types of Japas shall be performed upto the extent of one’s ability.

## \|\| 12.14.34-36 \|\|

*aṅgulyā japasaṃkhyānamekamevamudāhṛtam \|*  
*rekhayāṣṭaguṇaṃ vidyātputrajīvairdaśādhikam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*śataṃ syācchaṃkhamaṇibhiḥ pravālaistu sahasrakam \|*  
*sphaṭikairdaśasāhasraṃ mauktikairlakṣamucyate \|\| 35 \|\|*

*padmākṣairdaśalakṣantu sauvarṇaiḥ koṭirucyate \|*  
*kuśagraṃthyā ca rudrākṣairanaṃtaguṇitaṃ bhavet \|\| 36 \|\|*

34-36. There are various ways of counting the number of times the mantra has been repeated. Counting with the fingers is one mode. Eight times that number can be calculated by lines, ten times by dolls, hundred times by shells or gems, thousand times by corals, ten thousand times by crystal pieces, hundred thousand times by pearls, million times by seeds of lotuses, a crore of times by gold pieces, infinite time by a bundle of Kuśa grass or Rudrākṣa beads.

## \|\| 12.14.37-38 \|\|

*triṃśadakṣaiḥ kṛtā mālā dhanadā japakarmaṇi \|*  
*saptaviṃśatisaṃkhyātairakṣaiḥ puṣṭipradā bhavet \|\| 37 \|\|*

*pañcaviṃśatisaṃkhyātaiḥ kṛtā muktiṃ prayacchati \|*  
*akṣaistu pañcadaśabhirabhicāraphalapradā \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. A rosary containing thirty beads of Rudrākṣa for Japa bestows wealth, containing twenty-seven beads yields nourishment, containing twenty-five beads bestows salvation, containing fifteen beads bestows the fruits of black magic.

## \|\| 12.14.39 \|\|

*aṃguṣṭhaṃ mokṣadaṃ vidyāttarjanīṃ śatrunāśinīm \|*  
*madhyamāṃ dhanadāṃ śāṃtiṃ karotyeṣā hyanāmikā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The thumb used in counting the number bestows salvation. The index finger destroys enemies. The middle finger bestows wealth. The ring finger brings about calmness and peace.

## \|\| 12.14.40-41 \|\|

*aṣṭottaraśataṃ mālā tatra syāduttamottamā \|*  
*śatasaṃkhyottamā mālā pañcāśadbhistu madhyamā \|\| 40 \|\|*

*catuḥ pañcāśadakṣaistu hṛcchreṣṭhā hi prakīrtitā \|*  
*ityevaṃ mālayā kuryājjapaṃ kasmai na darśayet \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. If there are hundred and eight beads that rosary is the most excellent. If it has hundred beads it is excellent. If it has fifty beads it is the middling. With fifty-four beads it is good. The Japa shall be performed with these different rosaries. They must not be exhibited to anyone.

## \|\| 12.14.42 \|\|

*kaniṣṭhā kṣariṇī proktā japakarmaṇi śobhanā \|*  
*aṃguṣṭhena japejjapyamanyairaṃgulibhissaha \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The use of little finger in the Japa shall be avoided. In the act ot Japa it is held to be auspicious. The Japa shall be performed by means of the thumb in contact with other fingers.

## \|\| 12.14.43 \|\|

*aṃguṣṭhena vinā japyaṃ kṛtaṃ tadaphalaṃ yataḥ \|*  
*gṛhe japaṃ samaṃ vidyādgoṣṭhe śataguṇaṃ viduḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. If Japa is performed without the thumb it is futile. If performed in the house it is ordinarily efficacious. If performed in the cowpen it is hundred times more.

## \|\| 12.14.44 \|\|

*puṇyāraṇye tathārāme sahasraguṇamucyate \|*  
*ayutaṃ parvate puṇye nadyāṃ lakṣamudāhṛtam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. In a holy forest or park it is thousand times more. On a holy mountain it is ten thousand times more. On the banks of a river it is hundred thousand times more.

## \|\| 12.14.45-46 \|\|

*koṭiṃ devālaye prāhuranantaṃ mama sannidhau \|*  
*sūryasyāgnerguroriṃdordīpasya ca jalasya ca \|\| 45 \|\|*

*viprāṇāṃ ca gavāṃ caiva sannidhau śasyate japaḥ \|*  
*tatpūrvābhimukhaṃ vaśyaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ cābhicārikam \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. They say that the Japa performed in a temple is a crore of times more efficacious. That performed in my presence is infinite number of times more efficacious. Japa in the presence of the sun, fire, preceptor, moon, lamp, water, brahmins and cows is commended. Sitting east of these is conducive to favourable control; south of these is of the same nature as black magic.

## \|\| 12.14.47-50 \|\|

*paścimaṃ dhanadaṃ vidyādauttaraṃ śātidaṃ bhavet \|*  
*sūryāgnivipradevānāṃ gurūṇāmapi sannidhau \|\| 47 \|\|*

*anyeṣāṃ ca prasaktānāṃ mantraṃ na vimukho japet \|*  
*uṣṇīṣī kuṃcukī namro muktakeśo galāvṛtaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*apavitrakaro 'śuddho vilapanna japetkvacit \|*  
*krodhaṃ madaṃ kṣutaṃ trīṇi niṣṭhīvanavijṛṃbhaṇe \|\| 49 \|\|*

*darśanaṃ ca śvanīcānāṃ varjayejjapakarmaṇi \|*  
*ācametsaṃbhave teṣāṃ smaredvā māṃ tvayā saha \|\| 50 \|\|*

47-50. West of these is conducive to riches and north of these is peace-bestowing. If Japa is performed in the presence of sun, fire, brahmins, gods, preceptors and others one should not turn the face away from them. One should never perform Japa with the turban on, or wearing an armour or a bodice, in the nude, or with the hair dishevelled, or the neck covered, or without the Pavitra in the hand or while impure or while lamenting. While performing Japa the following must be avoided—anger, intoxication sneezing, spitting, yawning and seeing a dog or a lowborn person. If they happen, Ācamana shall be performed or I shall be remembered along with you.

## \|\| 12.14.51-53 \|\|

*jyotīṃṣi ca prapaśyedvā kuryādvā prāṇasaṃyamam \|*  
*anāsanaḥ śayāne vā gacchannutthita eva vā \|\| 51 \|\|*

*rathyāyāmaśive sthāne na japettimirāntare \|*  
*prasārya na japetpādau kukkuṭāsana eva vā \|\| 52 \|\|*

*yānaśayyādhirūḍho vā ciṃtāvyākulito 'tha vā \|*  
*śaktaścetsarvamevaitadaśaktaḥ śaktito japet \|\| 53 \|\|*

51-53. Or he shall see the luminary bodies or he shall perform a Prāṇāyāma. One should not perform Japa without a seat to sit on nor shall it be performed lying down, or standing up and walking. One shall not perform Japa in the open street or in an inauspicious place or in darkness. Legs shall not be stretched while performing the Japa nor shall one be in the cocklike posture, or seated in a vehicle or in a couch. Japa shall not be performed when one is worried. If one is competent one shall perform many Japas. Weak persons shall perform Japa according to capacity.

## \|\| 12.14.54 \|\|

*kimatra bahunoktena samāsena vacaḥ śṛṇu \|*  
*sadācāro japañchuddhaṃ dhyāyanbhadraṃ samaśnute \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Of what avail is much talk? Hear these words in brief. A person of good conduct, performing Japa and meditating purely attains welfare.

## \|\| 12.14.55 \|\|

*ācāraḥ paramo dharma ācāraḥ paramaṃ dhanaṃ \|*  
*ācāraḥ paramā vidyā ācāraḥ paramā gatiḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Good conduct is the greatest virtue. It is the greatest wealth, the greatest knowledge and the greatest goal.

## \|\| 12.14.56 \|\|

*ācārahīnaḥ puruṣo loke bhavati niṃditaḥ \|*  
*paratra ca sukhī na syāttasmādācāravānbhavet \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. A person devoid of good conduct is censured in the world. He will not be happy in the other world. Hence one must possess good conduct.

## \|\| 12.14.57 \|\|

*yasya yadvihitaṃ karma vede śāstre ca vaidikaiḥ \|*  
*tasya tena samācāraḥ sadācāro na cetaraḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Doing the duties prescribed by the Vedas, Śāstras and the followers of the Vedas is meant by the word good conduct, nothing else.

## \|\| 12.14.58 \|\|

*sadbhirācaritatvācca sadācāraḥ sa ucyate \|*  
*sadācārasya tasyāhurāstikyaṃ mūlakāraṇam \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Good conduct is also the conduct of the good. Theism is the source of goodness.

## \|\| 12.14.59 \|\|

*āstikaścetpramādādyaiḥ sadācārādavicyutaḥ \|*  
*na duṣyati naro nityaṃ tasmādāstikatāṃ vrajet \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. If he is a believer he will not err from the path of good conduct or commit errors or get defiled. Hence one shall be a believer in God and the Vedas.

## \|\| 12.14.60 \|\|

*yathehāsti sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ sukṛtairduṣkṛtairapi \|*  
*tathā paratra cāstīti matirāstikyamucyate \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Faith is the conviction that happiness and misery are attained by means of good and evil deeds hereafter too just as in this world.

## \|\| 12.14.61 \|\|

*rahasyamanyadvakṣyāmi gopanīyamidaṃ priye \|*  
*na vācyaṃ yasya kasyāpi nāstikasyātha vā paśoḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. O beloved, I shall tell you another secret which shall be guarded well. It shall not be mentioned to any one and every one or to an atheist brute.

## \|\| 12.14.62 \|\|

*sadācāravihīnasya patitasyāntyajasya ca \|*  
*pañcākṣarātparaṃ nāsti paritrāṇaṃ kalau yuge \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. In the age of Kali there is no greater protective factor than the five-syllabled Mantra to a fallen or a low-born person devoid of good conduct.

## \|\| 12.14.63 \|\|

*gacchatastiṣṭhato vāpi svecchayā karma kurvataḥ \|*  
*aśucervā śucervāpi mantro 'yanna ca niṣphalaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. This mantra is not ineffective when repeated by a person whether walking or standing or doing any other work or whether he is pure or impure.

## \|\| 12.14.64 \|\|

*anācāravatāṃ puṃsāmaviśuddhaṣaḍadhvanām \|*  
*anādiṣṭo 'pi guruṇā mantro 'yaṃ na ca niṣphalaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. This mantra is not ineffective even if it is not properly imparted by the preceptor. It is not ineffective even in the case of persons not caring for good conduct and who have not purified the six paths.

## \|\| 12.14.65 \|\|

*antyajasyāpi mūrkhasya mūḍhasya patitasya ca \|*  
*nirmaryādasya nīcasya maṃtro 'yaṃ na ca niṣphalaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. This mantra is not ineffective in the case of a base-born, a fool, a deluded person, a fallen man and a lowly one transgressing the bounds of decency.

## \|\| 12.14.66 \|\|

*sarvāvasthāṃ gatasyāpi mayi bhaktimataḥ param \|*  
*sidhyatyeva na saṃdeho nāparasya tu kasyacit \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. There is no doubt in this that this mantra becomes efficacious in the case of a man endowed with devotion to me whatever be his condition. It is not so in the case of other mantras.

## \|\| 12.14.67 \|\|

*na lagnatithinakṣatravārayogādayaḥ priye \|*  
*asyātyaṃtamavekṣyāḥ syurnaiṣa saptassadoditaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. O beloved, in the case of this mantra, the auspicious hour, date, star, day of the week etc. need not be taken into consideration too much. It is ever wakeful, not slumbering.

## \|\| 12.14.68 \|\|

*na kadācinna kasyāpi ripureṣa mahāmanuḥ \|*  
*susiddho vāpi siddho vā sādhyo vāpi bhaviṣyati \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. This great mantra is never harmful to anyone. It may be either Susiddha, or Siddha or Sādhya.

## \|\| 12.14.69 \|\|

*siddhena guruṇādiṣṭassusiddha iti kathyate \|*  
*asiddhenāpi vā dattassiddhasādhyastu kevalaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. It is Susiddha if it is imparted by a preceptor who is a Siddha. If it is imparted by a preceptor who is not a Siddha it is Siddha. The mere mantra is Sādhya.

## \|\| 12.14.70 \|\|

*asādhitassādhito vā sidhyatvena na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*śraddhātiśayayuktasya mayi maṃtre tathā gurau \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. If one has faith in me, the mantra and the preceptor, the mantra will undoubtedly be achieved whether it is Asādhita or Sādhita.

## \|\| 12.14.71 \|\|

*tasmānmaṃtrāntarāṃstyaktvā sāpāyān 1 dhikārataḥ \|*  
*āśrametparamāṃ vidyāṃ sākṣātpañcākṣarīṃ budhaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Hence a scholarly devotee shall resort to the five-syllabled mantra eschewing other mantras attended with risks in the matter of authorisation.

## \|\| 12.14.72 \|\|

*maṃtrāntareṣu siddheṣu maṃtra eṣa na sidhyati \|*  
*siddhe tvasminmahāmaṃtre te ca siddhā bhavaṃtyuta \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. There is no guarantee that if the other mantras are achieved this mantra too will be achieved. But if this mantra is achieved all the other mantras will be achieved.

## \|\| 12.14.73 \|\|

*yathā deveṣvalabdho 'smi labdheṣvapi maheśvari \|*  
*mayi labdhe tu te labdhā maṃtreṣveṣu samo vidhiḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Just as, O goddess, I am not achieved even if the other gods are attained but if I am attained the other gods too are attained so also is the case with the Mantras.

## \|\| 12.14.74 \|\|

*ye doṣāssarvamaṃtrāṇāṃ na te 'sminsaṃbhavaṃtyapi \|*  
*asya maṃtrasya jātyādīnanapekṣya pravartanāt \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Since this mantra functions without reference to castes, the defects found in the other mantras are not found in this mantra.

## \|\| 12.14.75 \|\|

*tathāpi naiva kṣudreṣu phaleṣu prati yogiṣu \|*  
*sahasā viniyuṃjīta tasmādeṣa mahābalaḥ \|*  
*upamanyuruvāca \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Still this mantra shall not be used for the trivial benefits or against insignificant opponents. Then alone this is very efficacious.

Upamanyu mid:—

## \|\| 12.14.76 \|\|

*evaṃ sākṣānmahādevyai mahādevena śūlinā \|*  
*hitā ya jagatāmuktaḥ pañcākṣaravidhiryathā \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Thus the mode of repeating this mantra of five syllables was explained to the goddess by lord Śiva himself for the benefit of the worlds.

## \|\| 12.14.77 \|\|

*ya idaṃ kīrtayedbhaktyā śṛṇuyādvā samāhitaḥ \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ prayāti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. He who glorifies this with devotion or listens to it with a pious mind is liberated from all sins and attains the greatest goal.

## Chapter 15 - The greatness of the Preceptor (guru)

## \|\| 12.15.1-2 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*bhagavānmaṃtramāhātmyaṃ bhavatā kathitaṃ prabho \|*  
*tatprayogavidhānaṃ ca sākṣācchrutisamaṃ yathā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*idānīṃ śrotumicchāmi śivasaṃskāramuttamam \|*  
*maṃtrasaṃgrahaṇe kiṃcitsūcitanna tu vismṛtam \|\| 2 \|\|*

Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:—

1-2. O holy lord, the greatness of the mantra has been mentioned by you as well as the rules governing its practice as found in the Śruti itself. Now I wish to hear the details of Śivasaṃskāra. While explaining the mode of accepting the mantra it has been slightly indicated.

## \|\| 12.15.3 \|\|

*upamanyuruvāca \|*  
*hanta te kathayiṣyāmi sarvapāpaviśodhanam \|*  
*saṃskāraṃ paramaṃ puṇyaṃ śivena patibhāṣitam \|\| 3 \|\|*

Upamanyu said:—

3\. Well, I shall mention to you the holy and sin-destroying details of consecration as explained by Śiva.

## \|\| 12.15.4 \|\|

*samyakkṛtādhikāraḥ syātpūjādiṣu naro yataḥ \|*  
*saṃskāraḥ kathyate tena ṣaḍadhvapariśodhanam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The consecration is so called because thereby the devotee is authorised in a splendid manner. It is the mode of purifying the six paths.

## \|\| 12.15.5 \|\|

*dīyate yena vijñānaṃ kṣīyate pāśabaṃdhanam \|*  
*tasmātsaṃskāra evāyaṃ dīkṣetyapi ca kathyate \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The same Saṃskāra is called initiation because thereby the perfect knowledge is imparted and the bondage of Pāśa is quelled.

## \|\| 12.15.6 \|\|

*śāṃbhavī caiva śāktī ca māṃtrī caiva śivāgame \|*  
*dīkṣopadiśyate tredhā śivena paramātmanā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The initiation as ordained by Śiva the great Ātman in the Śivāgama is threefold—pertaining to Śiva, Śakti and mantra.

## \|\| 12.15.7-8 \|\|

*gurorālokamātreṇa sparśātsaṃbhāṣaṇādapi \|*  
*sadyassaṃjñā bhavejjaṃtoḥ pāśopakṣayakāriṇī \|\| 7 \|\|*

*sā dīkṣā śāṃbhavī proktā sā punarbhidyate dvidhā \|*  
*tīvrā tīvratarā ceti pāśo pakṣayabhedataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. The initiation of Śiva is that whereby at the mere sight, touch and talk of the preceptor (guru) the individual soul gains immediately the consciousness quelling the bondage. It is twofold in view of the difference in the destruction of bondage, viz. acute and more acute.

## \|\| 12.15.9 \|\|

*yayā syānnirvṛtiḥ sadyassaiva tīvratarā matā \|*  
*tīvrā tu jīvatotyaṃtaṃ puṃsaḥ pāpaviśodhikā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. That is Tivratara whereby the bliss is immediately attained. The acute one purifies the sin of the living man effectively.

## \|\| 12.15.10 \|\|

*śaktī jñānavatī dīkṣā śiṣyadehaṃ praviśya tu \|*  
*guruṇā yogamārgeṇa kriyate jñānacakṣuṣā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The Śaktī form of initiation coupled with knowledge is performed by the preceptor with knowledge for his vision, after entering the body of the disciple along the path of Yoga.

## \|\| 12.15.11 \|\|

*māṃtrī kriyāvatī dīkṣā kuṃḍamaṃḍalapūrvikā \|*  
*maṃdamaṃdataroddeśātkartavyā guruṇā bahiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The Mantra form of initiation is coupled with the rites performed in the sacrificial altar. This has to be performed by the preceptor (guru) externally with respect to the dull-witted disciple.

## \|\| 12.15.12 \|\|

*śaktipātānusāreṇa śiṣyo 'nugrahamarhati \|*  
*śaivadharmānusārasya tanmūlatvātsamāsataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The disciple receives blessing in respect of his Śakti, because the pursuit of Śaivite virtue has that as the condition in brief.

## \|\| 12.15.13 \|\|

*yatra śaktirna patitā tatra śuddhirna jāyate \|*  
*na vidyā na śivācāro na muktirna ca siddhayaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Where the Śakti is not grasped neither purity nor Vidyā nor right conduct nor salvation nor any achievement is secured.

## \|\| 12.15.14 \|\|

*tasmālliṃgāni saṃvīkṣya śaktipātasya bhūyasaḥ \|*  
*jñānena kriyayā vātha guruśśiṣyaṃ viśodhayet \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Hence, observing the symbols for securing Śakti, the preceptor shall purify and consecrate the disciple either by knowledge or by means of rites.

## \|\| 12.15.15 \|\|

*yo 'nyathā kurute mohātsa vinaśyati durmatiḥ \|*  
*tasmātsarvaprakāreṇa guruḥ śiṣyaṃ parīkṣayet \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. He who performs otherwise is the wicked person who perishes. Hence the preceptor shall test the disciple in every respect.

## \|\| 12.15.16 \|\|

*lakṣaṇaṃ śaktipātasya prabodhānaṃdasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*sā yasmātparamā śaktiḥ prabodhānaṃdarūpiṇī \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Since Śakti is enlightenment and bliss, the two are the signs of its manifestation.

## \|\| 12.15.17 \|\|

*ānaṃdabodhayorliṃgamaṃtaḥkaraṇavikriyāḥ \|*  
*yathā syātkaṃparomāṃcasvaranetrāṃgavikriyāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The symbol of bliss and enlightenment is constituted by the changes and alterations in the mind in the manner of shivering, horripilation and alterations in the voice, eyes and other parts of the body.

## \|\| 12.15.18 \|\|

*śiṣyopi lakṣaṇairebhiḥ kuryādguruparīkṣaṇam \|*  
*tatsaṃparkaiḥ śivārcādau saṃgatairvātha tadgataiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The disciple too shall carry out the test of the preceptor through these characteristic symbols and contacts with him during the worship of Śiva or through those associated with him or resorting to him.

## \|\| 12.15.19 \|\|

*śiṣyastu śikṣaṇīyatvādgurorgauravakāraṇāt \|*  
*tasmātsarvaprayatnena gurorgauravamācaret \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The test for the disciple has in view his worthiness of being taught and for the preceptor the gravity of his pursuit. Hence the disciple shall endeavour in every respect to honour the preceptor.

## \|\| 12.15.20 \|\|

*yo gurussa śivaḥ prokto yaḥ śivaḥ sa guruḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*gururvā śiva evātha vidyākāreṇa saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. He who is the preceptor is Śiva and he who is Śiva is the preceptor. Whether the preceptor or Śiva the same person is stationed in the form of knowledge.

## \|\| 12.15.21 \|\|

*yathā śivastathā vidyā yathā vidyā tathā guruḥ \|*  
*śivavidyā gurūṇāṃ ca pūjayā sadṛśaṃ phalam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. As is Śiva so the knowledge. As is the knowledge so is the preceptor. The benefit is similar in the worship of Śiva, knowledge or the preceptor.

## \|\| 12.15.22 \|\|

*sarvadevātmakaścāsau sarvamaṃtramayo guruḥ \|*  
*tasmātsarvaprayatnena yasyājñāṃ śirasā vahet \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The preceptor is in the form of gods and the mantras. Hence every endeavour shall be made to accept his behest with bent head.

## \|\| 12.15.23 \|\|

*śreyo 'rthī yadi gurvājñāṃ manasāpi na laṃghayet \|*  
*gurvājñāpālako yasmājjñānasaṃpattimaśnute \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The seeker of welfare shall never even think of transgressing the commands of the preceptor, because only he who carries out the behests of the preceptor attains the wealth of knowledge.

## \|\| 12.15.24 \|\|

*gacchaṃstiṣṭhansvapanbhuṃjannānyatkarma samācaret \|*  
*samakṣaṃ yadi kurvīta sarvaṃ cānujñayā guroḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. He shall not do any thing without the permission of the preceptor, nor even walk, stand, sleep or eat. Especially if the work is performed in the presence of the preceptor it must necessarily be with his permission.

## \|\| 12.15.25 \|\|

*gurorgṛhe samakṣaṃ vā na yatheṣṭāsano bhavet \|*  
*gururdevo yataḥ sākṣāttadgṛhaṃ devamandiram \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Since the preceptor is the lord himself and his house is the temple of the lord, the disciple shall not sit as he pleases in the house of the preceptor or in his presence.

## \|\| 12.15.26-28 \|\|

*pāpināṃ ca yathā saṃgāttatpāpātpatito bhavet \|*  
*yatheha vahnisaṃparkānmalaṃ tyajati kāṃcanam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tathaiva gurusaṃparkātpāpaṃ tyajati mānavaḥ \|*  
*yathā vahnisamīpastho ghṛtakumbho vilīyate \|\| 27 \|\|*

*tathā pāpaṃ vilīyeta hyācāryasya samīpataḥ \|*  
*yathā prajvalito vahniḥ śuṣkamārdraṃ ca nirdahet \|\| 28 \|\|*

26-28. He becomes a fallen man due to his sins as due to the contact with the sinners. As the price of gold sheds off its impurities when put in fire so also the disciple sheds off his sins due to the contact with the preceptor. As the ghee melts when kept near the fire, so also the sin melts in the presence of the preceptor. As the blazing fire burns the twig whether dry or damp, so also the delighted preceptor burns off his sins.

## \|\| 12.15.29-31 \|\|

*tathāyamapi saṃtuṣṭo guruḥ pāpaṃ kṣaṇāddahet \|*  
*manasā karmaṇā vācā guroḥ krodhaṃ na kārayet \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tasya krodhena dahyaṃte hyāyuḥśrījñānasatkriyāḥ \|*  
*tatkrodhakāriṇo ye syusteṣāṃ yajñāśca niṣphalāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*yamaśca niyamāścaiva nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|*  
*gurorviruddhaṃ yadvākyaṃ na vadejjātucinnaraḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

29-31. The disciple shall never incite the anger of the preceptor mentally, verbally or physically. Due to his anger the longevity, prosperity, knowledge and sacred rites all these are burnt. The sacrifices of those who incite his anger are futile as also their restraints and observances. No doubt need be entertained in this respect. No man shall ever make any statement against the preceptor. If out of delusion he were to make such statements he will fall into the Raurava hell.

## \|\| 12.15.32-37 \|\|

*vadedyadi mahāmohādrauravaṃ narakaṃ vrajet \|*  
*manasā karmaṇā vācā gurumuddiśya yatnataḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*śreyorthī cennaro dhīmānna mithyācāramācaret \|*  
*gurorhitaṃ priyaṃ kuryādādiṣṭo vā na vā sadā \|\| 33 \|\|*

*asamakṣaṃ samakṣaṃ vā tasya kāryaṃ samācaret \|*  
*itthamācāravānbhakto nityamudyuktamānasaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*gurupriyakaraḥ śiṣyaḥ śaivadharmāṃstato 'rhati \|*  
*guruścedguṇavānprājñaḥ paramānaṃdabhāsakaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*tattvavicchivasaṃsakto muktido na tu cāparaḥ \|*  
*saṃvitsaṃjananaṃ tattvaṃ paramānaṃdasaṃbhavam \|\| 36 \|\|*

*tattattvaṃ viditaṃ yena sa evānaṃdadarśakaḥ \|*  
*na punarnāmamātreṇa saṃvidārahitastu yaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

32-37. If the man is intelligent and seeks welfare he shall not act falsely to the preceptor mentally, verbally or physically. Whether expressly bidden or not, the disciple shall perform what is beneficent and pleasing to the preceptor. He shall carry out his task in his presence or otherwise. He who conducts himself like this, who is ever devoted, alert in mind and performs what is pleasing to the preceptor is entitled to the Śaivite rites. If the preceptor is intelligent, endowed with virtues, is capable of illumining the great bliss, knows reality and is attached to Śiva he is competent to bestow salvation. None else. The principle of producing knowledge is born of great bliss. Only he by whom that principle is known can point out bliss and not the one who is that only in name but is devoid of true knowledge.

## \|\| 12.15.38 \|\|

*anyonyaṃ tārayennaukā kiṃ śilā tārayecchilām \|*  
*etasyā nāmamātreṇa muktirvai nāmamātrikā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Two boats can carry each other across the river. A piece of rock cannot take another piece of rock across the river. If the preceptor is nominal, the liberation too is nominal.

## \|\| 12.15.39 \|\|

*yaiḥ punarviditaṃ tattvaṃ te muktā mocayantyapi \|*  
*tattvahīne kuto bodhaḥ kuto hyātmaparigrahaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Those by whom this principle is known are liberated and can liberate others. There can be no enlightenment, no realisation of the self in one who is devoid of principles.

## \|\| 12.15.40 \|\|

*parigrahavinirmuktaḥ paśurityabhidhīyate \|*  
*paśubhiḥ preritaścāpi paśutvaṃ nātivartate \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. He who is devoid of realisation is an animal. One urged by an animal cannot eschew his animal nature.

## \|\| 12.15.41 \|\|

*tasmāttattvavideveha mukto mocaka iṣyate \|*  
*sarvalakṣaṇasaṃyuktaḥ sarvaśāstravidapyayam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Hence, only a knower of principles is sought as the liberated and liberator. He is endowed with all characteristics and he is the knower of all Śāstras.

## \|\| 12.15.42-43 \|\|

*sarvopāyavidhijño 'pi tattvahīnastu niṣphalaḥ \|*  
*yasyānubhavaparyaṃtā buddhistattve pravartate \|\| 42 \|\|*

*tasyāvalokanādyaiśca parānando 'bhijāyate \|*  
*tasmādyasyaiva saṃparkātprabodhānaṃdasaṃbhavaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. One devoid of principles is inefficient though he may know all means and rules of procedure. The greatest bliss is generated by the sight of the preceptor whose intellect extending upto personal realisation functions in the principle. Hence an intelligent person shall choose one as his preceptor who can impart enlightenment and bliss.

## \|\| 12.15.44-46 \|\|

*guruṃ tameva vṛṇuyānnāparaṃ matimānnaraḥ \|*  
*sa śiṣyairvinayācāracaturairucito guruḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*yāvadvijñāyate tāvatsevanīyo mumukṣubhiḥ \|*  
*jñāte tasminsthirā bhaktiryāvattattvaṃ samāśrayet \|\| 45 \|\|*

*na tu tattvaṃ tyajejjātu nopekṣeta kathaṃcana \|*  
*yatrānaṃdaḥ prabodho vā nālpamapyupalabhyate \|\| 46 \|\|*

44-46. The right preceptor shall be served by the disciples who desire salvation and who are expert in humble conduct to that end. When realisation dawns upon him he shall abide in him with stable devotion. He shall never eschew the principles nor neglect them. If neither enlightenment nor bliss is obtained by the disciple even after a year, even slightly, the disciple shall resort to another preceptor.

## \|\| 12.15.47 \|\|

*vatsarādapi śiṣyeṇa so 'nyaṃ gurumupāśrayet \|*  
*gurumanyaṃ prapanne 'pi nāvamanyeta paurvikam \|*

*gurorbhrātḥṃstathā putrānbodhakānprerakānapi \|*  
*tatrādāvupasaṃgamya brāhmaṇaṃ vedapāragam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Even though he may resort to another preceptor he shall never dishononr his previous preceptor, his brothers, or sons or illuminers or urgers.

## \|\| 12.15.48-49 \|\|

*gurumārādhayetprājñaṃ śubhagaṃ priyadarśanam \|*  
*sarvābhayapradātāraṃ karuṇākrāṃtamānasam \|\| 48 \|\|*

*toṣayettaṃ prayatnena manasā karmaṇā girā \|*  
*tāvadārādhayecchiṣyaḥ prasannosau bhavedyathā \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. Having at the outset approached the brahmin preceptor who has mastered the Vedas, who is intelligent, handsome, of pleasant sight, the bestower of protection and merciful, he shall propitiate him and endeavour to delight him mentally, verbally and physically.

## \|\| 12.15.50 \|\|

*tasminprasanne śiṣyasya sadyaḥ pāpakṣayo bhavet \|*  
*tasmāddhanāni ratnāni kṣetrāṇi ca gṛhāṇi ca \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. He shall continue to propitiate him till he is pleased. If the preceptor is pleased the sins of the disciple are immediately quelled.

## \|\| 12.15.51-52 \|\|

*bhūṣaṇāni ca vāsāṃsi yānaśayyāsanāni ca \|*  
*etāni gurave dadyādbhaktyā vittānusārataḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*vittaśāṭhyaṃ na kurvīta yadīcchetparamāṃ gatim \|*  
*sa eva janako mātā bhartā bandhurdhanaṃ sukham \|\| 52 \|\|*

51-52. Hence he shall give the preceptor coins, gems fields, houses, ornaments, garments, vehicles, beds, seats etc. in accordance with his wealth and resources. If he wishes for the great goal hç shall not be stringent with regard to wealth.

## \|\| 12.15.53 \|\|

*sakhā mitraṃ ca yattasmātsarvaṃ tasmai nivedayet \|*  
*nivedya paścātsvātmānaṃ sānvayaṃ saparigraham \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Since he is his father, mother, master, kinsman, wealth, happiness, friend, comrade etc. he shall offer everything to him.

## \|\| 12.15.54 \|\|

*samarpya sodakaṃ tasmai nityaṃ tadvaśago bhavet \|*  
*yadā śivāya svātmānaṃ dattavān deśikātmane \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. After offering these, he shall dedicate to him, himself, his family and all his possessions along with water and remain subservient to him for ever.

## \|\| 12.15.55 \|\|

*tadā śaivo bhaveddehī na tato 'sti punarbhavaḥ \|*  
*guruśca svāśritaṃ śiṣyaṃ varṣamekaṃ parīkṣayet \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Since he has offered himself to Śiva as his devotee he shall ever remain so. He will have no rebirth thereafter.

## \|\| 12.15.56 \|\|

*brāhmaṇaṃ kṣatriyaṃ vaiśyaṃ dvivarṣaṃ ca trivarṣakam \|*  
*prāṇadravyapradānādyairādeśaiśca samāsamaiḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The teacher shall test the brahmin disciple for a year, the kṣatriya for two years and the vaiśya for three years.

## \|\| 12.15.57 \|\|

*uttamāṃścādhame kṛtvā nīcānuttamakarmaṇi \|*  
*ākruṣṭāstāḍitā vāpi ye viṣādaṃ na yāntyapi \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. He shall test the disciples, with commands to give up life and wealth or by engaging the superior devotees in mean tasks and the inferior ones in noble tasks.

## \|\| 12.15.58 \|\|

*te yogyāḥ saṃyatāḥ śuddhāḥ śivasaṃskārakarmaṇi \|*  
*ahiṃsakā dayāvaṃto nityamudyuktacetasaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Even when rebuked or beaten if they do not feel distressed they shall be considered self-controlled and pure and hence deserving consecration in Śaiva rituals.

## \|\| 12.15.59-61 \|\|

*amānino buddhimaṃtastyaktaspardhāḥ priyaṃvadāḥ \|*  
*ṛjavo mṛdavaḥ svacchā vinītāḥ sthiracetasaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*śaucācārasamāyuktāḥ śivabhaktā dvijātayaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ vṛttasamopetā vāṅmanaḥkāyakarmabhiḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

*śodhyā bodhyā yathānyāyamiti śāstreṣu niścayaḥ \|*  
*nādhikāraḥ svato nāryāḥ śivasaṃskārakarmaṇi \|\| 61 \|\|*

59-61. The decision of the sacred texts is this that brahmin devotees with the following qualifications shall be consecrated properly and enlightened. They shall be nonviolent, merciful, ever active and alert in mind, free from arrogance, intelligent, devoid of rivalry sweet- tongued, straightforward, soft-hearted, pure, humble, steady, endowed with purity of conduct, and well-behaved in every respect.

## \|\| 12.15.62 \|\|

*niyogādbharturastyeva bhaktiyuktā yadīśvare \|*  
*tathaiva bhartṛhīnāyā putrāderabhyanujñayā \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Women by themselves are not authorised in Śaivite consecration. If they are devoted to the lord they can be consecrated at the instance of their husbands.

## \|\| 12.15.63-64 \|\|

*adhikāro bhavatyeva kanyāyāḥ piturājñayā \|*  
*śūdrāṇāṃ martyajātīnāṃ patitānāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*tathā saṃkarajātīnāṃ nādhvaśuddhirvidhīyate \|*  
*taipyakṛtrimabhāvaścecchive paramakāraṇe \|\| 64 \|\|*

63-64. A widow can be consecrated with the permission of her sons; a virgin with the permission of her father. The purificatory rite for the pathways is not prescribed for Śudra men, particularly the fallen ones and the intercastes. If they have pious feelings for Śiva, the purification of sins shall be performed by administering holy washings of his feet.

## \|\| 12.15.65-67 \|\|

*pādodakapradānādyaiḥ kuryuḥ pāpaviśodhanam \|*  
*atrānulomajātā ye yuktā eva dvijātiṣu \|\| 65 \|\|*

*teṣāmadhvaviśuddhyādi kuryānmātṛkulocitam \|*  
*yā tu kanyā svapitrādyaiśśivadharme niyojitā \|\| 66 \|\|*

*sā bhaktāya pradātavyā nāparāya virodhine \|*  
*dattā cetpratikūlāya pramādādbodhayetpatim \|\| 67 \|\|*

65-67. The consccratory rite for people born of Anuloma marriage shall be performed in the manner customary to the family of the mother. The girl who is authorised in Śaivite rites by her father shall be given in marriage only to a devotee of Śiva and not to a non-devotee. If inadvertently she is given in marriage to a non-devotee she shall try to convince her husband about the Śaivite faith. If she is unable to do so she shall leave him off and perform holy rites mentally.

## \|\| 12.15.68-70 \|\|

*aśaktā taṃ parityajya manasā dharmamācaret \|*  
*yathā munivaraṃ tyaktvā patimatriṃ pativratā \|\| 68 \|\|*

*kṛtakṛtyā 'bhavatpūrvaṃ tapasārādhya śaṅkaram \|*  
*yathā nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ tapasārādhya pāṃḍavān \|\| 69 \|\|*

*patīṃllabdhavatī dharme gurubhirna niyojitā \|*  
*asvātantryakṛto doṣo nehāsti paramārthataḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

68-70. The chaste lady Anasūyā abandoned her husband Atri the excellent sage and propitiated Śiva by penance; Draupadī who was not engaged in holy rites of the elders propitiated Nārāyaṇa by penance and attained the Pāṇḍavas as her husbands. In view of the weightiness of Śiva’s behest, the woman engaged in Śaivite virtue does not incur sin as she has no choice of freedom.

## \|\| 12.15.71-72 \|\|

*śivadharme niyuktāyāśśivaśāsanagauravāt \|*  
*bahunātra kimuktena yo 'pi ko 'pi śivāśrayaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*saṃskāryo gurvadhīnaścetsaṃskriyā na prabhidyate \|*  
*gurorālokanādeva sparśātsaṃbhāṣaṇādapi \|\| 72 \|\|*

71-72. Of what avail is much talk? Whoever solely resorts to Śiva shall be purified if he is subservient to the preceptor. The rite of consecration does not differ. He who develops consciousness by the mere sight, touch or talk of the preceptor is not faced with failure.

## \|\| 12.15.73-74 \|\|

*yasya saṃjāyate prajñā tasya nāsti parājayaḥ \|*  
*manasā yastu saṃskāraḥ kriyate yogavartmanā \|\| 73 \|\|*

*sa neha kathito guhyo guruvaktraikagocaraḥ \|*  
*kriyāvānyastu saṃskāraḥ kuṃḍamaṃḍapapūrvakaḥ \|*

*sa vakṣyate samāsena tasya śakyo na vistaraḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

73-74. The mental consecratory rite which is performed along the path of Yoga is not mentioned here. It is a great secret and shall be known straight from the mouth of the preceptor. The consecratory rite with holy rites shall now be mentioned briefly. Its detailed explanation is not possible.

## Chapter 16 - The consecration of the disciple (śiṣya)

## \|\| 12.16.1 \|\|

*upamanyuruvāca \|*  
*puṇye 'hani śucau deśe bahudoṣavivarjite \|*  
*deśikaḥ prathamaṃ kuryātsaṃskāraṃ samayāhvayam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Upamanyu said:—

1\. On an auspicious day, in a pure spot devoid of major defects, the preceptor shall at the outset perform the consecration ‘Samaya’.

## \|\| 12.16.2 \|\|

*parīkṣya bhūmiṃ vidhivadgaṃdhavarṇarasādibhiḥ \|*  
*śilpiśāstroktamārgeṇa maṇḍapaṃ tatra kalpayet \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. After testing the ground duly by way of smell, colour, taste etc., he shall cause a platform to be constructed along the path mentioned in the science of architecture.

## \|\| 12.16.3-4 \|\|

*kṛtvā vediṃ ca tanmadhye kuṇḍāni parikalpayet \|*  
*aṣṭadikṣu tathā dikṣu tatraiśānyāṃ punaḥ kramāt \|\| 3 \|\|*

*pradhānakuṃḍaṃ kurvīta yadvā paścimabhāgataḥ \|*  
*pradhānamekamevātha kṛtvā śobhāṃ prakalpayet \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. After making the altar, he shall make eight pits in the eight quarters making the chief one in the north-east. It may also be in the west when only the important pit need be dug. It shall be beautified by smearing it with powder.

## \|\| 12.16.5 \|\|

*vitānadhvajamālābhirvividhābhiranekaśaḥ \|*  
*vedimadhye tataḥ kuryānmaṃḍalaṃ śubhalakṣaṇam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. It shall be decorated with garlands, festoons, banners and canopy. In the middle of the altar a mystic diagram shall be drawn. It shall have auspicious characteristics.

## \|\| 12.16.6 \|\|

*raktahemādibhiścūrṇairīśvarāvāhanocitam \|*  
*siṃdūraśālinīvāracūrṇairevātha nirdhanaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The powder used for the mystic diagram shall be gold dust mixed with saffron so as to befit for the invocation of the lord. If the devotee is poor he can use the powdered Nīvāra grain mixed with saffron.

## \|\| 12.16.7 \|\|

*ekahastaṃ dvihastaṃ vā sitaṃ vā raktameva vā \|*  
*ekahastasya padmasya karṇikāṣṭāṃgulā matā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The width of the mystic lotus diagram may be one hand or two hands. It may be white or red in colour. The pericarp of the lotus of a hand’s width shall be eight aṅgulas.

## \|\| 12.16.8 \|\|

*kesarāṇi tadardhāni śeṣaṃ cāṣṭadalādikam \|*  
*dvihastasya tu padmasya dviguṇaṃ karṇikādikam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The filaments shall be half that length. The remaining portion is occupied by the eight petals. If the width of the lotus is two hands, the measurements will be doubled.

## \|\| 12.16.9 \|\|

*kṛtvā śobhopaśobhāḍhyamaiśānyāṃ tasya kalpayet \|*  
*ekahastaṃ tadardhaṃ vā punarvedyaḥ tu maṃḍalam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Another diagram shall be made on the altar one hand in width or half of it, to the north-east of the previous one and decorated well.

## \|\| 12.16.10 \|\|

*vrīhitaṃdulasiddhārthatilapuṣpakuśāstṛte \|*  
*tatra lakṣaṇasaṃyuktaṃ śivakuṃbhaṃ prasādhayet \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Paddy or rice grains mixed with gingelly seeds and flowers shall be strewn on it and covered with Darbha grass. The water-jar with the necessary characteristics shall be placed thereon.

## \|\| 12.16.11-12 \|\|

*sauvarṇaṃ rājataṃ vāpi tāmrajaṃ mṛnmayaṃ tu vā \|*  
*gandhapuṣpākṣatākīrṇaṃ kuśadūrvāṃkurācitam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*sitasūtrāvṛtaṃ kaṃṭhe navavastrayugāvṛtam \|*  
*śuddhāmbupūrṇamutkūrcaṃ sadravyaṃ sapidhānakam \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. The water-jar shall be made of gold, silver or copper or it may be earthen. It shall contain scents, flowers, Akṣatas, Kuśa and Dūrvā grass. It shall be tied round with two cloths and a white thread round the neck. It shall be filled with pure water with bundle of Kuśa grass inserted in it. It shall contain the materials of worship and a covering lid.

## \|\| 12.16.13-14 \|\|

*bhṛṅgāraṃ vardhanīṃ cāpi śaṃkhaṃ ca cakrameva vā \|*  
*vinā sūtrādikaṃ sarvaṃ padmapatramathāpi vā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tasyāsanāraviṃdasya kalpayeduttare dale \|*  
*agrataścaṃdanāṃbhobhirastrarājasya vardhanīm \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. The vessels Bhṛṅgāra and Vardhanī as well as Śaṅkha and Cakra shall also be put. Except the thread the other thing may consist of lotus petals and leaves. On the northern petal of the lotus conceived as seat shall be placed the Vardhanī of the Astrarāja (?) with sandal paste and water.

## \|\| 12.16.15 \|\|

*maṇḍalasya tataḥ prācyāṃ maṃtrakuṃbhe ca pūrvavat \|*  
*kṛtvā vidhivadīśasya mahāpūjāṃ samācaret \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. To the east of the diagram the great worship of the lord shall start on the consecrated jar.

## \|\| 12.16.16-19 \|\|

*athārṇavasya tīre vā nadyāṃ goṣṭhe 'pi vā girau \|*  
*devāgare gṛhe vāpi deśe 'nyasminmanohare \|\| 16 \|\|*

*kṛtvā pūrvoditaṃ sarvaṃ vinā vā maṃḍapādikam \|*  
*maṃḍalaṃ pūrvavatkṛtvā sthaṃḍilaṃ ca vibhāvasoḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*praviśya pūjābhavanaṃ prahṛṣṭavadano guruḥ \|*  
*sarvamaṃgalasaṃyuktaḥ samācaritanaityakaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*mahāpūjāṃ maheśasya kṛtvā maṇḍalamadhyataḥ \|*  
*śivakuṃbhe tathā bhūyaḥ śivamāvāhya pūjayet \|\| 19 \|\|*

16-19. What has been mentioned before can be performed on the seashore, or river-bank, or in the cowpen or on a mountain, or in a temple or in the house or in any other charming place, except the platform. After making the diagram as before and the raised ground for fire the preceptor shall eater the worship chamber with a delighted face. He shall invoke all auspicious things about him. He shall have completed all the daily rites. He shall perform the great worship in the middle of the mystical diagram. He shall invoke Śiva again in the water-jar and worship.

## \|\| 12.16.20-21 \|\|

*paścimābhimukhaṃ dhyātvā yajñarakṣakamīśvaram \|*  
*arcayedastravardhanyāmastramīśasya dakṣiṇe \|\| 20 \|\|*

*mantrakumbhe ca vinyasya mantraṃ mantraviśāradaḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā mudrādikaṃ sarvaṃ mantrayāgaṃ samācaret \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. He shall meditate upon the lord the protector of sacrifice facing the west. In the vessel Astravardhanī he shall worship the weapon of the lord on “he south. He shall place the Mantra in the Mantra vessel. Expert in the mantras he shall exhibit the mystic gestures and begin the sacrifice with the mantra.

## \|\| 12.16.22 \|\|

*tataśśivānale homaṃ kuryāddeśikasattamaḥ \|*  
*pradhānakuṇḍe parito juhuyuścāpare dvijāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The excellent preceptor shall perform the sacrifice in the sacred fire in the main pit. The other brahmins shall perform the sacrifice all round in the other pits.

## \|\| 12.16.23 \|\|

*ācāryātpādamardhaṃ vā homasteṣāṃ vidhīyate \|*  
*pradhānakuṇḍa evātha juhuyāddeśikottamaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The excellent preceptor shall perform the sacrifice only in the main pit. The number of sacrifices made by the others is half or one fourth of those of the chief priest.

## \|\| 12.16.24 \|\|

*svādhyāyamapare kuryuḥ stotraṃ maṃgalavācanam \|*  
*japaṃ ca vidhivaccānye śivabhaktiparāyaṇāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Some shall recite the Vedic mantras or auspicious hymns. Some shall perform the Japa duly.

## \|\| 12.16.25-26 \|\|

*nṛtyaṃ gītaṃ ca vādyaṃ ca maṃgalānyaparāṇi ca \|*  
*pūjanaṃ ca sadasyānāṃ kṛtvā samyagvidhānataḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*puṇyāhaṃ kārayitvātha punaḥ saṃpūjya śaṃkaram \|*  
*prārthayeddeśiko devaṃ śiṣyānugrahakāmyayā \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. Dance, music, instrumental as well as vocal, and other auspicious conventional rites shall be performed. After propitiating the assembled brahmins he shall make them recite the Punyāha mantras. He shall then worship. He shall pray to the lord with a desire to bless the disciple (śiṣya).

## \|\| 12.16.27 \|\|

*prasīda devadeveśa dehamāviśya māmakam \|*  
*vimocayainaṃ viśveśa ghṛṇayā ca ghṛṇānidhe \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. ‘O lord of the chief of gods be pleased. O lord, ocean of mercy, please enter my body mercifully and release me from the bondage’.

## \|\| 12.16.28-30 \|\|

*atha caivaṃ karomīti labdhānujñastu deśikaḥ \|*  
*ānīyopoṣitaṃ śiṣyaṃ haviṣyāśinameva vā \|\| 28 \|\|*

*ekāśanaṃ vā virataṃ snātaṃ prātaḥkṛtakriyam \|*  
*japaṃtaṃ praṇavaṃ devaṃ dhyāyaṃtaṃ kṛtamaṃgalam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*dvārasya paścimasyāgramaṇḍale dakṣiṇasya vā \|*  
*darbhāsane samāsīnaṃ vidhāyodaṅmukhaṃ śiśum \|\| 30 \|\|*

28-30. The preceptor shall perform the Saṃkalpa. ‘I shall do thus’ and with the formal permission, he shall bring the disciple who had been observing fast taking only Haviṣya once and who had taken bath and performed daily rites. The disciple shall continue the Japa of Praṇava and meditate on the lord. Auspicious rites shall then be performed for him. In the Maṇḍala in front of the western or the southern door he shall be made to sit on the Darbha grass. The disciple shall sit facing the north.

## \|\| 12.16.31-32 \|\|

*svayaṃ prāgvadanastiṣṭhannūrdhvakāyaṃ kṛtāṃjalim \|*  
*saṃprokṣya prokṣaṇautoyairmūrdhanyastreṇa mudrayā \|\| 31 \|\|*

*puṣpakṣepeṇa saṃtāḍya badhnīyāllocanaṃ guruḥ \|*  
*dukūlārdhena vastreṇa maṃtritena navena ca \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. The preceptor shall stand facing the cast and sprinkle the water from the vessel Prokṣaṇī, on his head as the disciple sits straight with palms joined in reverence. He shall lightly touch with flowers the eyes of the disciple and bind them with a strip of new silk cloth repeating the mantras.

## \|\| 12.16.33 \|\|

*tataḥ praveśayecchiṣyaṃ gururdvāreṇa maṃḍalam \|*  
*so 'pi teneritaḥ śaṃbhorācarettriḥ pradakṣiṇam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Then he shall make the disciple enter the Maṇḍapa through the door and circumambulate thrice.

## \|\| 12.16.34 \|\|

*tatassuvarṇasaṃmiśraṃ dattvā puṣpāṃjaliṃ prabhoḥ \|*  
*prāṅmukhaścodaṅmukho vā praṇameddaṃḍavatkṣito \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Then after offering a handful of flowers with a piece of gold to the lord he shall prostrate on the ground facing the cast or the north.

## \|\| 12.16.35 \|\|

*tatassaṃprokṣya mūlena śirasyastreṇa pūrvavat \|*  
*saṃtāḍya deśikastasya mocayennetrabaṃdhanam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Then as before, the preceptor shall sprinkle the water on his head and strew flowers. The bandage around his eyes shall be removed.

## \|\| 12.16.36-37 \|\|

*sa dṛṣṭvā maṃḍalaṃ bhūyaḥ praṇametsāñjaliḥ prabhum \|*  
*athāsīnaṃ śivācāryo maṃḍalasya tu dakṣiṇe \|\| 36 \|\|*

*upaveśyātmanassavye śiṣyaṃ darbhāsane guruḥ \|*  
*ārādhya ca mahādevaṃ śivahastaṃ pravinyaset \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. After seeing the Maṇḍala, he shall bow to the lord again with palms joined in reverence. The preceptor shall make the disciple sit to the south of the Maṇḍala and to his left on a Darbha grass scat. After propitiating the lord, the preceptor shall place his auspicious hand over his head.

## \|\| 12.16.38 \|\|

*śivatejomayaṃ pāṇiṃ śivamaṃtramudīrayet \|*  
*śivābhimānasaṃpanno nyasecchiṣyasya mastake \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Uttering the mantra of Śiva, the preceptor, identical with Śiva, shall place his hand refulgent with Śaivite splendour, on the head of the disciple.

## \|\| 12.16.39 \|\|

*sarvāṃgālaṃbanaṃ caiva kuryāttenaiva deśikaḥ \|*  
*śiṣyo 'pi praṇamedbhūmau deśikākṛtamīśvaram \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. With the same hand the preceptor shall touch all the parts of his body. The disciple shall prostrate on the ground before the lord in the form of the preceptor.

## \|\| 12.16.40-41 \|\|

*tataśśivānale devaṃ samabhyarcya yathāvidhi \|*  
*hutāhutitrayaṃ śiṣyamupaveśya yathā purā \|\| 40 \|\|*

*darbhāgraiḥ saṃspṛśaṃstaṃ ca vidyayātmānamāviśet \|*  
*namaskṛtya mahādevaṃ nāḍīsaṃdhānamācaret \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. He shall worship the lord duly and perform three Āhutis. He shall sit as before. The preceptor shall touch the disciple with the tips of the Darbha grass. By means of his Vidyā he shall enter the Ātman. After bowing to the lord he shall perform the rite of Nāḍīsandhāna.

## \|\| 12.16.42-44 \|\|

*śivaśāstroktamārgeṇa kṛtvā prāṇasya nirgamam \|*  
*śiṣyadehapraveśaṃ ca smṛtvā maṃtrāṃstu tarpayet \|\| 42 \|\|*

*saṃtarpaṇāya mūlasya tenaivāhutayo daśa \|*  
*deyāstisrastathāṃgānāmaṃgaireva yathākramam \|\| 43 \|\|*

*tataḥ pūrṇāhutiṃ dattvā prāyaścittāya deśikaḥ \|*  
*punardaśāhutīnkuryānmūlamaṃtreṇa maṃtravit \|\| 44 \|\|*

42-44. He shall perform the rite of Prāṇanirgama as mentioned in Śiva Sāstras. Remembering the mystical entry into the body of the disciple he shall perform the Tarpaṇa rite with the mantras. For the Tarpaṇa he shall offer thrice the ten Āhutis with the ancillary mantras. After offering the Pūrṇāhuti, the expert preceptor shall offer again ten Āhutis repeating the Mūlamantra, by way of expiation.

## \|\| 12.16.45-46 \|\|

*punaḥ saṃpūjya deveśaṃ samyagācamya deśikaḥ \|*  
*hutvā caiva yathānyāyaṃ svajātyā vaiśyamuddharet \|\| 45 \|\|*

*tasyaivaṃ janayetkṣātramuddhāraṃ ca tataḥ punaḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā tathaiva vipratvaṃ janayedasya deśikaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. Worshipping the lord of the gods again and performing the Ācamana the preceptor shall perform Homa duly and uplift the disciple from his caste. If he is a vaiśya he is first lifted into a kṣatriya. Then performing these rites the preceptor shall lift Him into a brahmin.

## \|\| 12.16.47 \|\|

*rājanyaṃ caivamuddhṛtya kṛtvā vipraṃ punastayoḥ \|*  
*rudratvaṃ janayedvipre rudranāmaiva sādhayet \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. If the disciple is a kṣatriya he is first raised into a brahmin and then to the form of Rudra. If the disciple is a brahmin he is raised into the form of Rudra.

## \|\| 12.16.48-49 \|\|

*prokṣaṇaṃ tāḍanaṃ kṛtvā śiśossvātmānamātmani \|*  
*śivātmakamanusmṛtya sphuraṃtaṃ visphuliṃgavat \|\| 48 \|\|*

*nāḍyā yathoktayā vāyuṃ recayenmaṃtrato guruḥ \|*  
*nirgamya praviśennāḍyā śiṣyasya hṛdayaṃ tathā \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. After sprinkling and striking lightly the disciple and remembering the Ātman of the disciple in his own, the preceptor shall drain out the wind that throbs like a flame, through the veins as mentioned. He shall then enter the vein and the heart of the disciple.

## \|\| 12.16.50 \|\|

*praviśya tasya caitanyaṃ nīlabindunibhaṃ smaran \|*  
*svatejasāpāstamalaṃ jvalaṃtamanuciṃtayet \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. After entering his consciousness that appears to him like a blue spot he shall meditate on it as blazing with its brilliance free from dirt.

## \|\| 12.16.51-52 \|\|

*tamādāya tayā nāḍyā maṃtrī saṃhāramudrayā \|*  
*na pūrakeṇa niveśyainamekībhāvārthamātmanaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*kuṃbhakena tathā nāḍyā recakena yathā purā \|*  
*tasmādādāya śiṣyasya hṛdaye tanniveśayet \|\| 52 \|\|*

51-52. After breathing in the vein repeating the mantra and showing the Saṃhāra-mudrā (the gesture of annihilation) he shall refill it with Pūraka for uniting the Ātmans. Now taking it again with Kumbhaka as with Recaka before, he shall place it in the heart of the disciple.

## \|\| 12.16.53 \|\|

*tamālabhya śivāllabdhaṃ tasmai dattvopavītakam \|*  
*hutvāhutitrayaṃ paścāddadyātpūrṇāhutiṃ tataḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. After touching him and giving him the sacred thread secured from Śiva he shall offer three Āhutis and the Pūrṇāhuti thereafter.

## \|\| 12.16.54-56 \|\|

*devasya dakṣiṇe śiṣyamupaveśyavarāsane \|*  
*kuśapuṣpaparistīrṇe baddhāṃjalirudaṅmukham \|\| 54 \|\|*

*svastikāsanamārūḍhaṃ vidhāya prāṅmukhaḥ svayam \|*  
*varāsanasthito maṃtrairmahāmaṃgalaniḥsvanaiḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*samādāya ghaṭaṃ pūrṇaṃ pūrṇameva prasāditam \|*  
*dhyāyamānaḥ śivaṃ śiṣyamābhiṣiṃceta deśikaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

54-56. To the south of the lord, the disciple is made to sit on a splendid seat over which Kuśa, and flowers are strewn. He shall join his palms with reverence and face the north. He shall sit in the posture of Svastika. He shall face the east and sitting in a splendid seat shall repeat the mantras with the auspicious songs and music and take the water-jar. Meditating on the joyous Śiva he shall pour water over the disciple.

## \|\| 12.16.57 \|\|

*athāpanudya snānāṃbu paridhāya sitāṃbaram \|*  
*ācāntolaṃkṛtaśśiṣyaḥ prāṃjalirmaṃḍapaṃ vrajet \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Wiping off the water over his body and wearing a white cloth, he shall perform the Ācamana. Fully bedecked he shall go to the Maṇḍapa with palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 12.16.58 \|\|

*upaveśya yathāpūrvaṃ taṃ gururdarbhaviṣṭare \|*  
*saṃpūjya maṃḍalaṃ devaṃ karanyāsaṃ samācaret \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. He shall make him sit as before on the Kuśa seat and worship the lord in the Maṇḍala. He shall perform the Karanyāsa rite.

## \|\| 12.16.59 \|\|

*tatastu bhasmanā devaṃ dhyāyanmanasi deśikaḥ \|*  
*samālabheta pāṇibhyāṃ śiśuṃ śivamudīrayet \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Meditating on the lord he shall take Bhasma in both the hands and smear it over the body of the disciple repeating Śiva’s names.

## \|\| 12.16.60-61 \|\|

*atha tasya śivācāryo dahanaplāvanādikam \|*  
*sakalīkaraṇaṃ kṛtvā mātṛkānyāsavartmanā \|\| 60 \|\|*

*tataḥ śivāsanaṃ dhyātvā śiṣyamūrdhni deśikaḥ \|*  
*tatrāvāhya yathānyāyamarcayenmanasā śivam \|\| 61 \|\|*

60-61. He shall then perform the rites of Dahana and Plāvana and conclude with the rite of Mātṛkānyāsa. Meditating on Śiva’s seat and invoking him on the head of the disciple he shall mentally worship him in the prescribed manner.

## \|\| 12.16.62 \|\|

*prārthayetprāṃjalirdevaṃ nityamatra sthito bhava \|*  
*iti vijñāpya taṃ śaṃbhostejasā bhāsuraṃ smaret \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. With palms joined in reverence he shall pray to the lord. ‘Stay here permanently’. After submitting this he shall remember him shining with refulgent splendour.

## \|\| 12.16.63 \|\|

*saṃpūjyātha śivaṃ śaivīmājñāṃ prāpya śivātmikām \|*  
*karṇe śiṣyasya śanakaiśśivamantramudīrayet \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. After worshipping Śiva and securing his behest in the form of Śiva he shall slowly mutter Śiva’s Mantra into the ear of the disciple.

## \|\| 12.16.64 \|\|

*sa tu baddhāṃjaliḥ śrutvā mantraṃ tadgatamānasaḥ \|*  
*śanaistaṃ vyāharecchiṣyaśivācāryasya śāsanāt \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. At the behest of the preceptor he shall repeat the mantra with palms joined in reverence and mind concentrating on it.

## \|\| 12.16.65 \|\|

*tataḥ śāktaṃ ca saṃdiśya mantraṃ mantravicakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*uccārayitvā ca sukhaṃ tasmai maṃgalamādiśet \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Then after instructing him in the Śakti mantra,

the expert preceptor shall make him repeat it easily and bless him with auspiciousness.

## \|\| 12.16.66 \|\|

*tatassamāsānmantrārthaṃ vācyavācakayogataḥ \|*  
*samadiśyeśvaraṃ rūpaṃ yogamāsanamādiśet \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. After briefly explaining to him the syllabic meaning of the mantra, the preceptor shall advise him about the form of the lord and instruct him in different postures.

## \|\| 12.16.67 \|\|

*atha gurvājñayā śiṣyaḥ śivāgnigurusannidhau \|*  
*bhaktyaivamabhisaṃdhāya dīkṣāvākyamudīrayet \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Then at the behest of the preceptor, in the presence of Śaivite fire and the preceptor, the disciple shall think with devotion and repeat the statement of initiation.

## \|\| 12.16.68 \|\|

*varaṃ prāṇaparityāgaśchedanaṃ śiraso 'pi vā \|*  
*na tvanabhyarcya bhuṃjīya bhagavantaṃ trilocanam \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. ‘Better to abandon life, better to cut off the head than to take food without worshipping the three-eyed lord.’

## \|\| 12.16.69 \|\|

*sa eva dadyānniyato yāvanmohaviparyayaḥ \|*  
*tāvadārādhayeddevaṃ tanniṣṭhastatparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. The lord alone will invariably give till the delusion is removed. The disciple shall propitiate the lord with concentrated devotion till delusion is quelled.

## \|\| 12.16.70 \|\|

*tataḥ sa samayo nāma bhaviṣyati śivāśrame \|*  
*labdhādhikāro gurvājñāpālakastadvaśo bhavet \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Thereafter the disciple will be known as Samaya in the preceptor’s hermitage. He shall carry out the behests of the preceptor and remain subservient to him.

## \|\| 12.16.71 \|\|

*ataḥ paraṃ nyastakaro bhasmādāya svahastataḥ \|*  
*dadyācchiṣyāya mūlena rudrākṣaṃ cābhimaṃtritam \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Then after performing the rite of Karanyāsa the preceptor shall take the Bhasma with his own hand and hand it over to the disciple along with the Mūlamantra and the Rudrākṣa over which the mantra has been repeated.

## \|\| 12.16.72 \|\|

*pratimā vāpi devasya gūḍhadehamathāpi vā \|*  
*pūjāhomajapadhyānasādhanāni ca saṃbhave \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. If it is possible he shall give him the phallic or the embodied idol of the lord, the requisites of worship, sacrifice, Japa and meditation.

## \|\| 12.16.73 \|\|

*sopi śiṣyaḥ śivācāryāllabdhāni bahumānataḥ \|*  
*ādadītājñayā tasya deśikasya na cānyathā \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. The disciple (śiṣya) shall take these things from the Śaiva preceptor with great respect only at the behest of his family preceptor. Not otherwise.

## \|\| 12.16.74 \|\|

*ācāryādāptamakhilaṃ śirasyādhāya bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*rakṣayetpūjayecchaṃbhuṃ maṭhe vā gṛha evavā \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. He shall keep on his head everything obtained from the preceptor, with great devotion and preserve it carefully. He shall worship Śiva in the hermitage or in his own house.

## \|\| 12.16.75 \|\|

*ataḥ paraṃ śivācāramādiśedasya deśikaḥ \|*  
*bhaktiśraddhānusāreṇa prajñāyāścānusārataḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. The preceptor shall impart to him the Śaivite conduct of life in proportion to his devotion and faith as well as his grasping capacity.

## \|\| 12.16.76 \|\|

*yaduktaṃ yatsamājñātaṃ yaccaivānyatprakīrtitam \|*  
*śivācāryeṇa samaye tatsarvaṃ śirasā vahet \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Whatever is mentioned, or commanded, or even glorified by the preceptor to the Samaya, he shall retain in his intellect.

## \|\| 12.16.77 \|\|

*śivāgamasya grahaṇaṃ vācanaṃ śravaṇaṃ tathā \|*  
*deśikadeśataḥ kuryānna svecchāto na cānyataḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Understanding of Śaivite Āgama, reading it and listening to it shall be done at the behest of the preceptor. Not by himself at his will nor from anyone else.

## \|\| 12.16.78 \|\|

*iti saṃkṣepataḥ proktaḥ saṃskāraḥ samayāhvayaḥ \|*  
*sākṣācchivapuraprāptau nṛṇāṃ paramasādhanam \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Thus the consecration ‘Samaya’ has been briefly explained to you. It is the greatest means in attaining the city of Śiva himself.

## Chapter 17 - The rules governing Śaivite initiation

## \|\| 12.17.1 \|\|

*upamanyuruvāca \|*  
*ataḥ paraṃ samāvekṣya guruḥ śiṣyasya yogyatām \|*  
*ṣaḍadhvaśuddhiṃ kurvīta sarvabaṃdhavimuktaye \|\| 1 \|\|*

Upamanyu said:—

1\. Hereafter the preceptor shall perform the purification of the six pathways after understanding the disciple’s capacity, for the sake of liberation from bondage.

## \|\| 12.17.2 \|\|

*kalāṃ tattvaṃ ca bhuvanaṃ varṇaṃ padamataḥ param \|*  
*maṃtraśceti samāsena ṣaḍadhvā paripaṭhyate \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The six paths are Kalā, Tattva, Bhuvana, Varṇa, Pada and Mantra in brief.

## \|\| 12.17.3 \|\|

*nivṛttyādyāḥ kalāḥ pañca kalādhvā kathyate budhaiḥ \|*  
*vyāptāḥ kalābhiritare tvadhvānaḥ pañca pañcabhiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The five Kalās, Nivṛtti etc. are the pathway of Kalā. The five Kalās pervade the five paths.

## \|\| 12.17.4 \|\|

*śivatattvādibhūmyaṃtaṃ tattvādhvā samudāhṛtaḥ \|*  
*ṣaḍviṃśatsaṃkhyayopetaḥ śuddhāśuddhobhayātmakaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The principles from Śivatattva to the earth constitute the paths of principles. They are twenty-six, both pure and impure.

## \|\| 12.17.5 \|\|

*ādhārādyunmanāṃtaśca bhuvanādhvā prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*vinā bhedopabhedābhyāṃ ṣaṣṭisaṃkhyāsamanvitaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Those beginning with Ādhāra and ending with Unmana constitute the paths of worlds. They are sixty in number without difference and subsidiary divisions.

## \|\| 12.17.6 \|\|

*pañcāśadrudrarūpāstu varṇā varṇādhvasaṃjñitāḥ \|*  
*anekabhedasaṃpannaḥ padādhvā samudāhṛtaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The fifty letters in the form of Rudras constitute the path of letters. The path of words has many varieties.

## \|\| 12.17.7-8 \|\|

*sarvopamaṃtrairmaṃtrādhvā vyāptaḥ paramavidyayā \|*  
*yathā śivo na tattveṣu gaṇyate tattvanāyakaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*maṃtrādhvani na gaṇyeta tathāsau maṃtranāyakaḥ \|*  
*kalādhvano vyāpakatvaṃ vyāpyatvaṃ cetarādhvanām \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. The path of mantras consisting of subsidiary Mantras is pervaded by the excellent mantra. Just as Śiva, the leader of Tattvas, is not included among Tattvas so also the leader of Mantras is not included in the path of Mantra. The Kalādhvā pervades and the other Adhvās are pervaded.

## \|\| 12.17.9-10 \|\|

*na vetti tattvato yasya naivārhatyadhvaśodhanam \|*  
*ṣaḍvidhasyādhvano rūpaṃ na yena viditaṃ bhavet \|\| 9 \|\|*

*vyāpyavyāpakatā tena jñātumeva na śakyate \|*  
*tasmādadhvasvarūpaṃ ca vyāpyavyāpakatāṃ tathā \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. He who does not know that factually should not perform the rite of the six Adhvās. He who has not understood the form of the six paths cannot understand the order of pervasiveness and is incompetent to perform the rite.

## \|\| 12.17.11-14 \|\|

*yathāvadavagamyaiva kuryādadhvaviśodhanam \|*  
*kuṃḍamaṃḍalaparyaṃtaṃ tatra kṛtvā yathā purā \|\| 11 \|\|*

*dvihastamānaṃ kurvīta prācyāṃ kalaśamaṃḍalam \|*  
*tataḥ snātaśśivācāryaḥ saśiṣyaḥ kṛtanaityakaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*praviśya maṃḍalaṃ śaṃbhoḥ pūjāṃ pūrvavadācaret \|*  
*tatrāḍhakāvaraissiddhaṃ taṃdulaiḥ pāyasaṃ prabhoḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*ardhaṃ nivedya homārthaṃ śeṣaṃ samupakalpayet \|*  
*purataḥ kalpite vātha maṃḍale varṇimaṃḍite \|\| 14 \|\|*

11-14. After making the pits and the Maṇḍapa as before, to the east he shall make the mystic diagram measuring two hastas for keeping the water-jar on. The preceptor shall perform his routine rites and enter the Maṇḍapa with his disciples to begin the worship of Śiva as before. Milk pudding shall be made with rice measuring not less than one Āḍhaka. Half of that shall be offered to the lord as Naivedya and the remaining shall be kept reserved for Homa. In the Maṇḍala drawn in front with various colours, the preceptor shall place five water-pots, one in each of the four quarters and one in the middle.

## \|\| 12.17.15-17 \|\|

*sthāpayetpañcakalaśāndikṣu madhye ca deśikaḥ \|*  
*teṣu brahmāṇi mūlārṇairbindunādasamanvitaiḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*nama ādyairyakarāṃtaiḥ kalpayetkalpavittamaḥ \|*  
*īśānaṃ madhyame kuṃbhe puruṣaṃ purataḥ sthite \|\| 16 \|\|*

*aghoraṃ dakṣiṇe vāme vāmaṃ sadyaṃ ca paścime \|*  
*rakṣāṃ vidhāya mudrā ca baddhvā kuṃbhābhimaṃtraṇam \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-17. The preceptor, most expert in the procedural code, shall invoke the five Brahmans on them, repeating the Mūlāvaraṇas along with Bindu and Nāda, and the letters beginning with Namaḥ and ending with Ya. Īśāna is invoked in the middle jar, Puruṣa in the eastern, Aghora in the southern, Vāma in the northern and Sadyojāta in the western jar. After performing the rites of protection, mystic gestures and invocation of the jar he shall sacrifice in the Śiva fire as before.

## \|\| 12.17.18-20 \|\|

*kṛtvā śivānalairhomaṃ prārabhetyathā purā \|*  
*yadardhaṃ pāyasaṃ pūrvaṃ homārthaṃ parikalpitam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*hutvā śiṣyasya taccheṣaṃ bhoktuṃ samupakalpayet \|*  
*tarpaṇāṃtaṃ ca maṃtrāṇāṃ kṛtvā karma yathā purā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*hutvā pūrṇāhutiṃ teṣāṃ tataḥ kuryātpradīpanam \|*  
*oṃkārādanu huṃkāraṃ tato mūlaṃ phaḍaṃtakam \|\| 20 \|\|*

18-20. The milk pudding reserved for sacrifice shall be offered and what still remains shall be kept for the disciple to eat. The rites upto the Tarpaṇa shall be conducted in the manner mentioned before. After the Pūrṇāhuti the rite of illumination with the ancillaries shall be performed.

## \|\| 12.17.21-22 \|\|

*svāhāṃtaṃ dīpane prāhuraṃgāni ca yathākramam \|*  
*teṣāmāhutayastisro deyā dīpanakarmaṇi \|\| 21 \|\|*

*maṃtrairekaikaśastaistu vicintyā dīptamūrtayaḥ \|*  
*triguṇaṃ triguṇī kṛtya dvijakanyākṛtaṃ sitam \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. In this rite three Āhutis shall be given. With the specific mantras the refulgent deities shall be meditated upon. He shall then take the thrice-spun white threads made by brahmin girls, strung into three and with these bind the tip of the tuft of the disciple.

## \|\| 12.17.23-26 \|\|

*sūtraṃ sūtreṇa saṃmaṃtrya śikhāgre baṃdhayecchiśoḥ \|*  
*caraṇāṃguṣṭhaparyaṃtamūrdhvakāyasya tiṣṭhataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*laṃbayitvā tu tatsūtraṃ suṣumṇāṃ tatra yojayet \|*  
*śāṃtayā mudrayādāya mūlamaṃtreṇa maṃtravit \|\| 24 \|\|*

*hutvāhutitrayaṃ tasyāssānnidhyamupakalpayet \|*  
*hṛdi saṃtāḍya śiṣyasya puṣpakṣepeṇa pūrvavat \|\| 25 \|\|*

*caitanyaṃ samupādāya dvādaśāṃte nivedya ca \|*  
*sūtraṃ sūtreṇa saṃyojya saṃrakṣyāstreṇa varmaṇā \|\| 26 \|\|*

23-26. The thread shall be let loose till the tip of the toe of the disciple standing straight. The Suṣumnā (the nerve of the backbone) shall be joined with it. The consciousness shall be invoked with the basic mantra and he shall offer three Āhutis to create its presence. With the flowers he shall strike the chest of the disciple as before and invoke consciousness. It shall then be conceived as placed in the twelve-petalled lotus. The thread shall be joined with the other thread (?) with the Astra and Varma mantras. After veiling the body of the disciple the thread shall be meditated upon (?)

## \|\| 12.17.27-30 \|\|

*avaguṃṭhyātha tatsūtraṃ śiṣyadehaṃ viciṃtayet \|*  
*mūlatrayamayaṃ pāśaṃ bhogabhogyatvalakṣaṇam \|\| 27 \|\|*

*viṣayendriyadehādijanakaṃ tasya bhāvayet \|*  
*vyomādibhūtarūpiṇyaḥ śāṃtyatītādayaḥ kalāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*sūtre svanāmabhiryojyaḥ pūjyaścaiva namoyutaiḥ \|*  
*athavā bījabhūtaistatkṛtvā pūrvoditaṃ kramāt \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tato malādestattvādau vyāptiṃ samalokayet \|*  
*kalāvyāptiṃ malādau ca hutvā saṃdīpayetkalāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

27-30. It shall then be imagined that the three strings represent a bond with the objects and the state of enjoyment. The Kalās Śāntyatīta etc. in the forms of the elements ether etc. shall be joined to the thread (?) with their respective names and worshipped. With these as the base the foregoing rites shall be performed. Then he shall survey the pervasion of the dirt etc. in Tattvas. After offering as Āhuti, the pervasion of Kalā in the dirt etc. the Kalās shall be illuminated.

## \|\| 12.17.31 \|\|

*śiṣyaṃ śirasi saṃtāḍya sūtraṃ dehe yathākramam \|*  
*śāṃtyatītapade sūtraṃ lāñchayenmaṃtramuccaran \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. After striking the disciple on the head and the thread worne on the body he shall bedeck the sūtra in the Śāntyatīta Pada, repeating the mantra.

## \|\| 12.17.32 \|\|

*evaṃ kṛtvā nivṛttyantaṃ śāṃtyatītamanukramāt \|*  
*hutvāhutitrayaṃ paścānmaṇḍale ca śivaṃ yajet \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. In this manner after offering the Āhutis of Śāntyatīta upto the end of Nivṛtti he shall perform three Āhutis and worship Śiva in the Maṇḍala.

## \|\| 12.17.33 \|\|

*devasya dakṣiṇe śiṣyamupaveśyottarāmukham \|*  
*sadarbhe maṇḍale dadyāddhomaśiṣṭaṃ caruṃ guruḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The preceptor shall make the disciple sit to the south of the lord facing the north, on the Maṇḍala strewn with Darbha grass. He shall give him the rice soaked in ghee left after the Homa.

## \|\| 12.17.34 \|\|

*śiṣyastadguruṇā dattaṃ satkṛtya śivapūrvakam \|*  
*bhuktvā paścāddvirācamya śivamantramudīrayet \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The disciple shall take the Caru offered by the preceptor, and eat it repeating the name Śiva. After performing the Ācamana twice he shall repeat the mantra of Śiva.

## \|\| 12.17.35 \|\|

*apare maṇḍale dadyātpañcagavyaṃ tathā guruḥ \|*  
*so 'pi tacchaktitaḥ pītvā dvirācamya śivaṃ smaret \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The preceptor shall give him the Pañcagavya on the other Maṇḍala. The disciple shall drink it upto his capacity, perform the Ācamana twice and remember Śiva.

## \|\| 12.17.36 \|\|

*tṛtīye maṇḍale śiṣyamupaveśya yathā purā \|*  
*pradadyāddaṃtapavanaṃ yathāśāstroktalakṣaṇam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. He shall make the disciple sit on a third Maṇḍala as before, and hand over a tooth brush twig having the characteristics mentioned in the scriptures.

## \|\| 12.17.37 \|\|

*agreṇa tasya mṛdunā prāṅmukho vāpyudaṅmukhaḥ \|*  
*vācaṃ niyamya cāsīnaśśiṣyo daṃtānviśodhayet \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The disciple shall sit silently facing the east or the north and clean his teeth with its soft tip.

## \|\| 12.17.38 \|\|

*prakṣālya daṃtapavanaṃ tyaktvācamya śivaṃ smaret \|*  
*praviśeddeśikādiṣṭaḥ prāṃjaliḥ śivamaṇḍalam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. He shall cast off the tooth brush, wash his hands and mouth, perform Ācamana and remember Śiva. Then at the behest of the preceptor he shall enter Śiva Maṇḍapa with palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 12.17.39-40 \|\|

*tyaktaṃ taddantapavanaṃ dṛśyate guruṇā yadi \|*  
*prāgudakpaścime vāgre śivamanyacchivetaram \|\| 39 \|\|*

*aśastāśāmukhe tasmingurustaddoṣaśāṃtaye \|*  
*śatamardhaṃ tadardhaṃ vājuhuyānmūlamantrataḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. If the cast-off tooth brush is seen by the preceptor in the north-east or west or in front it is auspicious, otherwise it is inauspicious. If it is seen in an inauspicious quarter the preceptor shall perform a hundred, or a fifty or twenty-five Homas with the basic Mantra for the removal of the defect.

## \|\| 12.17.41 \|\|

*tataḥ śiṣyaṃ samālabhya japitvā karṇayoḥ śivam \|*  
*devasya dakṣiṇe bhāge taṃ śiṣyamadhivāsayet \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Then he shall strike the disciple and whisper the name of Śiva into his ears. He shall make him settle to the south of the lord.

## \|\| 12.17.42 \|\|

*ahatāstaraṇāstīrṇe sa darbhaśayane śuciḥ \|*  
*maṃtrite 'ntaḥ śivaṃ dhyāyañśayīta prākchirā niśi \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. During the night the disciple shall lie on a Darbha mattress covered with an unwashed bed-sheet and consecrated with mantra. While lying he shall meditate on Śiva and keep his head to the east.

## \|\| 12.17.43-44 \|\|

*śikhāyāṃ baddhasūtrasya śikhayā tacchikhāṃ guruḥ \|*  
*ābadhyāhatavastreṇa tamācchādya ca varmaṇā \|\| 43 \|\|*

*rekhātrayaṃ ca parito bhasmanā tilasarṣapaiḥ \|*  
*kṛtvāstrajaptaistadvāhye digīśānāṃ baliṃ haret \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. To his tuft the thread has already been tied. Along with that tuft the preceptor shall tie the unwashed bed-sheet. With Varma mantra he shall cover him up. All round him he shall make three lines with gingelly seeds and mustard fully consecrated by Astra mantra. Outside the lines he shall offer oblations to the guardians of the quarters.

## \|\| 12.17.45 \|\|

*śiṣyo 'pi parato 'naśnankṛtvaivamadhivāsanam \|*  
*prabudhyotthāya gurave svapnaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ nivedayet \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The disciple shall not take anything in after settling down like this. After getting up the next day he shall intimate to the preceptor if he had any dream.

## Chapter 18 - The purification of the six paths

## \|\| 12.18.1 \|\|

*upamanyuruvāca \|*  
*tataḥ snānādikaṃ sarvaṃ samāpyācāryacoditaḥ \|*  
*gacchedbaddhāṃjalirdhyāyañchivamaṇḍalapārśvataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Upamanyu said:—

1\. After completing ablution and other rites the disciple shall, at the bidding of the preceptor, go near the Maṇḍala of Śiva meditating on Śiva, with palms joined in reverence.

## \|\| 12.18.2 \|\|

*atha pūjāṃ vinā sarvaṃ kṛtvā pūrvadine yathā \|*  
*netrabaṃdhanaparyaṃtaṃ darśayenmaṇḍalaṃ guruḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. All rites upto the binding of the eyes shall be performed as on the previous day, except the worship. Then the preceptor shall show him the Maṇḍala.

## \|\| 12.18.3 \|\|

*baddhanetreṇa śiṣyeṇa puṣpāvakiraṇe kṛte \|*  
*yatrāpataṃti puṣṇāṇi tasya nāmā 'sya saṃdiśet \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. When flowers are strewn by the disciple whose eyes are tied, the preceptor shall tell him the places where the flowers fell.

## \|\| 12.18.4 \|\|

*taṃ copanīya nirmālyamaṇḍale 'sminyathā purā \|*  
*pūjayeddevamīśānaṃ juhuyācca śivānale \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The preceptor shall take him to the Maṇḍala where worship had already been performed. As before he shall worship lord Īśāna and perform homa in the fire.

## \|\| 12.18.5 \|\|

*śiṣyeṇa yadi duḥsvapno dṛṣṭastaddoṣaśāṃtaye \|*  
*śatamardhaṃ tadardhaṃ vā juhuyānmūlavidyayā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. If any bad dream had been seen by the disciple, the preceptor shall perform hundred, or fifty, or twenty five homas with the basic mantra for the removal of that defect.

## \|\| 12.18.6-8 \|\|

*tataḥ sūtraṃ śikhābaddhaṃ laṃbayitvā yathā purā \|*  
*ādhārapūjāprabhṛti yannivṛttikalāśrayam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*vāgīśvarīpūjanāṃtaṃ kuryāddhomapurassaram \|*  
*atha praṇamya vāgīśaṃ nivṛttervyāpikāṃ satīm \|\| 7 \|\|*

*maṇḍale devamabhyarcya hutvā caivāhutitrayam \|*  
*prāpayecca śiśoḥ prāptiṃ yugapatsarvayoniṣu \|\| 8 \|\|*

6-8. The thread tied to the tuft shall be loosened to hang down as before, He shall perform the worship of Ādhāra based on Nivṛttikalā and conclude with the worship of Vāgīśvarī with due homas. He shall bow to Vāgīśa and Satī who pervade Nivṛtti. He shall worship the lord in the Maṇḍala and make three Āhutis Then the mystical rite of making the simultaneous entry into all types of living beings, shall be performed.

## \|\| 12.18.9-10 \|\|

*sūtradehe 'tha śiṣyasya tāḍanaprokṣaṇādikam \|*  
*kṛtvātmānaṃ samādāya dvādaśāṃte nivedya ca \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tato 'pyādāya mūlena mudrayā śāstradṛṣṭayā \|*  
*yojayenmanasācāryo yugapatsarvayoniṣu \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. The rites of striking and sprinkling shall be performed in the gross body of the disciple and then the Ātman shall be taken and placed in the twelvc-petalled lotus. It shall be taken again from there through the repetition of the basic mantra and the gestures as prescribed in the scripture. The preceptor shall unite it mentally with all types of living beings simultaneously.

## \|\| 12.18.11 \|\|

*devānāṃ jātayaścāṣṭau tiraścāṃ pañca jātayaḥ \|*  
*jātyaikayā ca mānuṣyā yonayaśca caturdaśa \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The living beings are fourteen in number: the eight types of the gods, five types of the lower animals and birds, and human beings forming one type.

## \|\| 12.18.12 \|\|

*tāsu sarvāsu yugapatpraveśāya śiśordhiyā \|*  
*vāgīśānyāṃ yathānyāyaṃ śiṣyātmānaṃ niveśayet \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. In order to facilitate the simultaneous entry into all of them, he shall deposit the Ātman of the disciple along with his mind into Vāgīśānī duly.

## \|\| 12.18.13 \|\|

*garbhaniṣpattaye devaṃ saṃpūjya praṇipatya ca \|*  
*hutvā caiva yathānyāyaṃ niṣpannaṃ tadanusmaret \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. For the accomplishment of the spiritual knowledge he shall worship and bow to the lord. After performing the homa he shall remember it as developed.

## \|\| 12.18.14 \|\|

*niṣpannasyaivamutpattimanuvṛttiṃ ca karmaṇā \|*  
*ārjavaṃ bhoganiṣpattiḥ kuryātprītiṃ parāṃ tathā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. He shall duly perform the mystical rites of nativity, the pursuit of previous actions, straightforwardness and the great pleasure of enjoyment.

## \|\| 12.18.15 \|\|

*niṣkṛtyarthaṃ ca jātyāyurbhogasaṃskārasiddhaye \|*  
*hutvāhutitrayaṃ devaṃ prārthayeddeśikottamaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. For the sake of redemption and the achievement of birth, longevity, enjoyment and purificatory impressions, the preceptor shall perform three Āhutis and pray to the lord.

## \|\| 12.18.16 \|\|

*bhoktṛtvaviṣayāsaṃgamalaṃ tatkāyaśodhanam \|*  
*kṛtvaivameva śiṣyasya chiṃdyātpāśatrayaṃ tataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Thus he shall purify his body that contains the dirt of enjoyment of pleasures and contact with sensual objects. He shall cut off the three bondages of the disciple.

## \|\| 12.18.17 \|\|

*nikṛtyā pari baddhasya pāśasyātyaṃtabhedataḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā śiṣyasya caitanyaṃ svacchaṃ manyeta kevalam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. By the complete splitting of the bondage he shall make the disciple dean.

## \|\| 12.18.18 \|\|

*hutvā pūrṇāhutiṃ vahnau brahmāṇaṃ pūjayettataḥ \|*  
*hutvāhutitrayaṃ tasmai śivājñāmanusaṃdiśet \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. After making the Pūrṇāhuti in the fire he shall worship Brahmā. After performing three Āhutis for him he shall submit to him the behest of Śiva.

## \|\| 12.18.19 \|\|

*pitāmaha tvayā nāsya yātuḥ śaivaṃ paraṃ padam \|*  
*pratibandho vidhātavyaḥ śaivājñaiṣā garīyasī \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. ‘O Pitāmaha, no hindrance shall be placed for this disciple who is going to the great region of Śiva. This is the behest of Śiva’.

## \|\| 12.18.20 \|\|

*ityādiśya tamabhyarcya visṛja ca vidhānataḥ \|*  
*samabhyarcya mahādevaṃ juhuyādāhutitrayam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Thus imploring him, he shall worship and ritualistically dismiss him. He shall worship Mahādeva and perform three Āhutis.

## \|\| 12.18.21 \|\|

*nivṛttyā śuddhamuddhṛtya śiṣyātmānaṃ yathā purā \|*  
*niveśyātmani sūtre ca vāgīśaṃ pūjayettataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Uplifting the Ātman of the disciple, as before, when it has been purified by Nivṛttikalā he shall deposit it in his own Ātman. He shall then worship Vāgīśa.

## \|\| 12.18.22 \|\|

*hutvāhutitrayaṃ tasmai praṇamya ca visṛjya tām \|*  
*kuryānnivṛttaḥ saṃdhānaṃ pratiṣṭhāṃ kalayā saha \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. He shall perform three Āhutis now and ritualistically dismiss him. Returning he shall make it united with Pratiṣṭhākalā.

## \|\| 12.18.23 \|\|

*saṃdhāne yugapatpūjāṃ kṛtvā hutvāhutitrayam \|*  
*śiṣyātmanaḥ pratiṣṭhāyāṃ praveśaṃ tvatha bhāvayet \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Performing the worship and the three Āhutis simultaneously he shall imagine the entry of the Ātman of the disciple into the Pratiṣṭhā Kalā.

## \|\| 12.18.24 \|\|

*tataḥ pratiṣṭhāmāvāhya kṛtvāśeṣaṃ puroditam \|*  
*tadvyāptiṃ vyāpikāṃ tasya vāgīśānīṃ ca bhāvayet \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Then after invoking Pratiṣṭhā and performing everything as previously mentioned he shall conceive its pervasion and the pervading Vāgīśānī.

## \|\| 12.18.25 \|\|

*pūrṇedumaṃḍalaprakhyāṃ kṛtvā śeṣaṃ ca pūrvavat \|*  
*viṣṇave saṃviśedājñāṃ śivasya paramātmanaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. He shall imagine Vāgīśānī as lustrous as the disc of the full moon. After doing everything as before he shall submit to Viṣṇu the behest of Śiva the great Ātman.

## \|\| 12.18.26-28 \|\|

*viṣṇorvisarjanādyaṃ ca kṛtvā śeṣaṃ ca vidyayā \|*  
*pratiṣṭhāmanusaṃdhāya tasyāṃ cāpi yathā purā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*kṛtvānucintya tadvyāptiṃ vāgīśāṃ ca yathākramam \|*  
*dīptāgnau pūrṇahomāntaṃ kṛtvā śeṣaṃ ca pūrvavat \|\| 27 \|\|*

*nīlarudramupasthāpya tasmai pūjādikaṃ tathā \|*  
*kṛtvā karma śivājñāṃ ca dadyātpūrvoktavartmanā \|\| 28 \|\|*

26-28. Performing everything like the ritualistic dismissal of Viṣṇu by means of Vidyā he shall think of Pratiṣṭhā and its pervasion and Vāgīśā too in order. He shall then perform everything concluding with the Pūrṇāhuti in the blazing fire as before. Nīlarudra shall be invoked and its worship performed. As mentioned before, the behest of the lord shall be carried out.

## \|\| 12.18.29 \|\|

*tapastamapi codvāsya kṛtvā tasyātha śāṃtaye \|*  
*vidyākalāṃ samādhāya tadvyāptiṃ cāvalokayet \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Then the lord shall be ritualistically dismissed. For the purpose of quietening him, Vidyākalā shall be conceived and its pervasion surveyed.

## \|\| 12.18.30 \|\|

*svātmano vyāpikāṃ tadvadvāgīśīṃ ca yathā purā \|*
