*pramādena tu bhuṃkte cettadudgīrya prayatnataḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*snātvā dviguṇamabhyarcya devaṃ devīmupoṣya ca \|*  
*śivasyāyutamabhyasyedbrahmacaryapurassaram \|\| 71 \|\|*

*paredyuśśaktito dattvā suvarṇādyaṃ śivāya ca \|*  
*śivabhaktāya vā kṛtvā mahāpūjāṃ śucirbhavet \|\| 72 \|\|*

70-72. If a sinner takes meals freely there is no atonement for him. If he takes in anything inadvertently he shall vomit it off, take bath and worship the lord and the goddess twice. He shall observe fast thereafter and repeat the names of Śiva ten thousand times. He shall observe celibacy also. The next day he shall make a charitable gift of gold to a devotee of Śiva. Then he shall perform great worship and sanctify himself.

## Chapter 25 - The Worship of Śiva

## \|\| 12.25.1 \|\|

*upamanyuruvāca \|*  
*anuktaṃ cātra pūjāyāḥ kamalopabhayādiva \|*  
*yattadanyatpravakṣyāmi samāsānna tu vistarāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

Upamanyu said:—

1\. What has not been mentioned because I was afraid of losing the sequence of worship, I shall now mention briefly,

## \|\| 12.25.2 \|\|

*havirnivedanātpūrvaṃ dīpadānādanantaram \|*  
*kuryādāvaraṇābhyarcāṃ prāpte nīrājane 'tha vā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. After offering the light but before offering the Havis, the devotee shall perform the worship of the Āvaraṇa; or just when the time of Nīrājana has arrived.

## \|\| 12.25.3-5 \|\|

*tatreśānādisadyāṃtaṃ rudrādyastrāṃtameva ca \|*  
*śivasya vā śivāyāśca prathamāvaraṇe japet \|\| 3 \|\|*

*aiśānyāṃ pūrvabhāge ca dakṣiṇe cottare tathā \|*  
*paścime ca tathāgneyyāmaiśānyāṃ nairṛte tathā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*vāyavyāṃ punaraiśānyāṃ caturdikṣu tataḥ param \|*  
*garbhāvaraṇamākhyātaṃ mantrasaṃghātameva vā \|\| 5 \|\|*

3-5. In the first Āvaraṇa of Śiva and Śivā, the mantra of Rudra etc. upto the Astra shall be used for Japa. The five Brahmans from Īśāna to Śadyojāta shall be meditated upon in the north-east, east, south and north or in the west, south-east, north-east and south-west or in the north-west north-east and in the four quarters. Beyond that he shall perform the Garbhāvaraṇa and repeat the mantras.

## \|\| 12.25.6-8 \|\|

*hṛdayādyastraparyaṃtamathavāpi samarcayet \|*  
*tadbahiḥ pūrvataḥ śakraṃ yamaṃ dakṣiṇato yajet \|\| 6 \|\|*

*varuṇaṃ vāruṇe bhāge dhanadaṃ cottare budhaḥ \|*  
*īśamaiśe 'nalaṃ svīye nairṛte nirṛtiṃ yajet \|\| 7 \|\|*

*mārute mārutaṃ viṣṇuṃ nairṛte vidhimaiśvare \|*  
*bahiḥpadmasya vajrādyānyabjāṃtānyāyudhānyapi \|\| 8 \|\|*

6-8. Or he shall worship everything from the heart to the Astra. Outside he shall worship Indra in the east, Yama in the south, Varuṇa in the west, Kūbera in the north, Īśa in the north-east, fire in the south-east, Nirṛti in the south-west, Vāyu in the north-west, Viṣṇu in the south-west, Brahmā in the north-east and the weapons from thunderbolt to the lotus outside the lotus.

## \|\| 12.25.9-11 \|\|

*prasiddharūpāṇyāśāsu lokeśānāṃ kramādyajet \|*  
*devaṃ devīṃ ca saṃprekṣya sarvāvaraṇadevatāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*baddhāṃjalipuṭā dhyeyāḥ samāsīnā yathāsukham \|*  
*sarvāvaraṇadevānāṃ svābhidhānairnamoyutaiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*puṣpaiḥ saṃpūjanaṃ kuryānnatvā sarvānyathākramam \|*  
*garbhāvaraṇamevāpi yajetsvāvaraṇena vā \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. He shall worship the famous forms of the lord in the quarters in order. The deities of the Āvaraṇa shall be meditated upon as looking at the lord and the goddess with palms joined and seated comfortably. He shall worship the Āvaraṇa deities with their names with the word ‘Namaḥ’ with flowers and bow to them in order. He shall worship the Garbhāvaraṇa with its Āvaraṇa.

## \|\| 12.25.12-13 \|\|

*yoge dhyāne jape home vāhye vābhyaṃtare 'pi vā \|*  
*haviśca ṣaḍvidhaṃ deyaṃ śuddhaṃ mudgānnameva ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

*pāyasaṃ dadhisaṃmiśraṃ gauḍaṃ ca madhunāplutam \|*  
*eteṣvekamanekaṃ vā nānāvyaṃjanasaṃyutam \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. In the Yoga, meditation, Japa and homa whether external or internal, the Haviṣ of six types shall be given as pure rice or rice mixed with green gram. The milk-pudding mixed with curd or honey-soaked jaggery shall be offered with side-dishes.

## \|\| 12.25.14 \|\|

*guḍakhaṃḍanvitaṃ dadyānmathitaṃ dadhi cottamam \|*  
*bhakṣyāṇyapūpamukhyāni svādumaṃti phalāni ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Churned curd shall be given with jaggery and sugar-candy. Tasteful foodstuffs especially sweet pie and fruits shall be given.

## \|\| 12.25.15-16 \|\|

*raktacandanapuṣpāḍhyaṃ pānīyaṃ cātiśītalam \|*  
*mṛdu elārasāktaṃ ca khaṇḍaṃ pūgaphalasya ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

*dalāni nāgavallyāśca yuktāni khadirādibhiḥ \|*  
*gaurāṇi svarṇavarṇāni vihitāni śivāni ca \|*

*śailameva sitaṃ cūrṇaṃ nātirūkṣaṃ na dūṣitam \|*  
*karpūraṃ cātha kaṃkolaṃ jātyādi ca navaṃ śubham \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. Cold water with red sandal and flowers thrown in shall be given. A piece of Areca nut soaked in Cardamom juice shall be given. Betel leaves with Khadira etc. shall be given. White and yellow are auspicious. The white lime powder shall be rocky but neither very hard nor defective.

## \|\| 12.25.17-18 \|\|

*ālepanaṃ candanaṃ syānmūlakāṣṭhaṃrajomayam \|*  
*kastūrikā kuṃkumaṃ ca raso mṛgamadātmakaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*puṣpāṇi surabhīṇyeva pavitrāṇi śubhāni ca \|*  
*nirgaṃdhānyugragaṃdhāni dūṣitānyuṣitāni ca \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. The camphor, Kaṅkola and Jāti, if fresh, are auspicious. As an unguent the sandal shall be in powdered form. The lower stem is better. The musk and saffron shall be pasted. Only fragrant flowers are holy and auspicious.

## \|\| 12.25.19 \|\|

*svayameva viśīrṇāni na deyāni śivārcane \|*  
*vāsāṃsi ca mṛdūnyeva tapanīyamayāni ca \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Flowers devoid of smell, of obnoxious smell, defiled, stale and broken at fall shall not be used for the worship of lord Śiva.

## \|\| 12.25.20-21 \|\|

*vidyudvalayakalpāni bhūṣaṇāni viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*sarvāṇyetāni karpūraniryāsāgurucandanaiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*ādhūpitāni puṣpaughairvāsitāni samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*candanāgurukarpūrakāṣṭhaguggulucūrṇikaiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. Soft fine cloths and golden ornaments shall be given along with camphor, gum-resin and sandal, well fumigated and rendered fragrant with flowers.

## \|\| 12.25.22 \|\|

*ghṛtena madhunā caiva siddho dhūpaḥ praśasyate \|*  
*kapilāsambhavenaiva ghṛtenātisugandhinā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Incense mixed with sandal, gum-resin, camphor, ghee and honey is excellent.

## \|\| 12.25.23 \|\|

*nityaṃ pradīpitā dīpāḥ śastāḥ karpūrasaṃyutāḥ \|*  
*pañcagavyaṃ ca madhuraṃ payo dadhi ghṛtaṃ tathā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Lamps lighted with fragrant ghee from the milk of tawny cows, accompanied by camphor are excellent.

## \|\| 12.25.24 \|\|

*kapilāsambhavaṃ śambhoriṣṭaṃ snāne ca pānake \|*  
*āsanāni ca bhadrāṇi gajadaṃtamayāni ca \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Pañcagavya consisting of sweet milk, curd and ghee all taken from tawny cows is favourite of Śiva for bath and drink.

## \|\| 12.25.25 \|\|

*suvarṇaratnayuktāni citrāṇyāstaraṇāni ca \|*  
*mṛdūpadhānayuktāni sūkṣmatūlamayāni ca \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Seats of ivory framed in gold and set with gems and the covering cloths of various colours shall be used.

## \|\| 12.25.26 \|\|

*uccāvacāni ramyāṇi śayanāni sukhāni ca \|*  
*nadyassamudragāminyā naṭādvāmbhaḥ samāhṛtam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Beds shall be comfortable, charming, high and low with soft pillows. They shall be filled with fine cotton.

## \|\| 12.25.27 \|\|

*śītañca vastrapūtaṃ tadviśiṣṭaṃ snānapānayoḥ \|*  
*chatraṃ śaśinibhaṃ cāru muktādāmavirājitam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Water taken from an east-flowing or west-flowing river is excellent for bath and drink. It shall be cool and filtered with a cloth.

## \|\| 12.25.28 \|\|

*navaratnacitaṃ divyaṃ hemadaṇḍamanoharam \|*  
*cāmare ca site sūkṣme cāmīkarapariṣkṛte \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The umbrella shall resemble the moon. It shall be embellished with pearls and nine varieties of gems. It shall be divine and charming with a golden handle.

## \|\| 12.25.29 \|\|

*rājahaṃsadvayākāre ratnadaṃḍopaśobhite \|*  
*darpaṇaṃ cāpi susnigdhaṃ divyagandhānulepanam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The chowries shall be white and fine. They shall be embellished with gold. The handle shall be studded with gems. They shall shine like two royal swans.

## \|\| 12.25.30 \|\|

*samaṃtādratnasañchannaṃ sragvairaiścāpi bhūṣitam \|*  
*gambhīraninadaḥ śaṃkho haṃsakuṃdendusannibhaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The mirror shall be smooth and polished. Divine sweet smelling unguents shall be smeared over it. It shall be studded with gems all round. It shall be decorated with excellent garlands.

## \|\| 12.25.31 \|\|

*āsvapṛṣṭhādideśeṣu ratnacāmīkarācitaḥ \|*  
*kāhalāni ca ramyāṇi nānānādakarāṇi ca \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The conch shall be white like the swan, Kunda flower or the moon. It shall have a majestic resonant sound. At the mouth, back and other places it shall be studded with gems and framed in gold.

## \|\| 12.25.32 \|\|

*suvarṇanirmitānyeva mauktikālaṃkṛtāni ca \|*  
*bherīmṛdaṃgamurajatimicchapaṭahādayaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The bugles shall be charmingly made of gold and decorated with pearls. They shall be capable of producing different notes.

## \|\| 12.25.33 \|\|

*samudrakalpasannādāḥ kalpanīyāḥ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*bhāṃḍānyapi ca ramyāṇi patrāṇyapi ca kṛtsnaśaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Different kinds of drums like Bheri, Mṛdaṅga, Muraja, Timiccha, Paṭaha shall be used, capable of sounding like'the roaring sea.

## \|\| 12.25.34 \|\|

*tadādhārāṇi 1 sarvāṇi sauvarṇānyeva sādhayet \|*  
*ālayaṃ ca maheśasya śivasya paramātmanaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. All pots and vessels shall be beautiful. Their supporting stands shall be made of gold.

## \|\| 12.25.35 \|\|

*rājāvasathavatkalpyaṃ śilpaśāstroktalakṣaṇam \|*  
*uccaprākārasaṃbhinnaṃ bhūdharākāragopuram \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The temple of Śiva shall be made like a royal palace with all the characteristics mentioned in the science of architecture.

## \|\| 12.25.36 \|\|

*anekaratnasaṃcchannaṃ hemadvārakapāṭakam \|*  
*taptajāṃbūnadamayaṃ ratnastambhaśatāvṛtam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. It shall be encircled by high walls with the ornamental gateway as lofty as a mountain. It shall be studded with gems. The doors shall be made of gold.

## \|\| 12.25.37 \|\|

*muktādāmavitānāḍhyaṃ vidrumadvāratoraṇam \|*  
*cāmīkaramayairdivyairmukuṭaiḥ kumbhalakṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. It must have a hundred columns of molten gold studded with gems. The canopy shall be embellished with pearls and the festoons at the gateway shall be brightened with corals.

## \|\| 12.25.38 \|\|

*alaṃkṛtaśirobhāgamastra 2 ājena cihnitam \|*  
*rājanyārhanivāsaiśca rājavīthyādiśobhitaiḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Its top shall be decorated with golden domes resembling divine crowns and marked with the lordly missile.

## \|\| 12.25.39-40 \|\|

*procchritaprāṃśuśikharaiḥ prāsādaiśca samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*āsthānasthānavaryaiśca sthitairdikṣu vidikṣu ca \|\| 39 \|\|*

*atyantālaṃkṛtaprāṃtamaṃtarāvaraṇairiva \|*  
*uttamastrīsahasraiśca nṛtyageyaviśāradaiḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. It shall be richly decorated in the border all round by palatial buildings with tall minarets, great mansions for the residence of kings, royal highways and excellent halls of assembly situated in the different quarters appearing like an inner rampart.

## \|\| 12.25.41 \|\|

*veṇuvīṇāvidagdhaiśca puruṣairbahubhiryutam \|*  
*rakṣitaṃ rakṣibhirvīrairgajavājirathānvitaiḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. It shall contain thousands of courtezans in dance and music and those adepts in playing on flutes and lutes.

## \|\| 12.25.42-44 \|\|

*anekapuṣpavāṭībhiranekaiśca sarovaraiḥ \|*  
*dīrghikābhiranekābhirdigvidikṣu virājitam \|\| 42 \|\|*

*vedavedāṃtatattvajñaiśśivaśāstraparāyaṇaiḥ \|*  
*śivāśramaratairbhaktaiḥ śivaśāstroktalakṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*śāṃtaiḥ smitamukhaiḥ sphītaiḥ sadācāraparāyaṇaiḥ \|*  
*śaivairmāheśvaraiścaiva śrīmadbhissevitadvijaiḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

42-44. It shall be guarded by heroic guards and watch men equipped with elephants, horses and chariots. It shall contain many flower gardens, lakes, and tanks in the different quarters. It shall be inhabited by the brahmin devotees of Śiva, who must know the truth of the Vedas and Vedānta, who are devoted to Śaivite scriptures who are engaged in Śaivite way of life, who must have the characteristics prescribed in Śaivite scriptures, who must be quiet, prosperous and devoted to good conduct, who have smiling faces and who follow lord Śiva.

## \|\| 12.25.45-48 \|\|

*evamaṃtarbahirvāthayathāśaktivinirmitaiḥ \|*  
*sthāne śilāmaye dāṃte dārave ceṣṭakāmaye \|\| 45 \|\|*

*kevalaṃ mṛnmaye vāpi puṇyāraṇye 'tha vā girau \|*  
*nadyāṃ devālaye 'nyatra deśe vātha gṛhe śubhe \|\| 46 \|\|*

*āḍhyo vātha daridro vā svakāṃ śaktimavaṃcayan \|*  
*dravyairnyāyārjitaireva bhaktyā devaṃ samarcayet \|\| 47 \|\|*

*athānyāyārjitaiścāpi bhaktyā cecchivamarcayet \|*  
*na tasya pratyavāyo 'sti bhāvavaśyo yataḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

45-48. All people whether rich or poor shall worship the lord with devotion through the wealth legitimately earned by them. They shall worship in a place built by the people according to their capacity. The temple shall be built in stone, or ivory, or wood or brick or even day. It may be in a holy forest or on a mountain or on the banks of a river. The worship may be performed in any other holy spot or in the house. Even if the wealth is illegitimately acquired he does not incur sin or hindrance if he worships Śiva with devotion since the lord is subservient to piety.

## \|\| 12.25.49 \|\|

*nyāyārjitairapi dravyairabhaktyā pūjayedyadi \|*  
*na tatphalamavāpnoti bhaktirevātra kāraṇam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. If one worships without devotion even with legitimately earned wealth he does not derive the benefit thereof. Devotion alone is the main concern.

## \|\| 12.25.50 \|\|

*bhaktyā vittānusāreṇa śivamuddiśya yatkṛtam \|*  
*alpe mahati vā tulyaṃ phalamāḍhyadaridrayoḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The benefit of even a little or a great service rendered by a poor or a rich man, according to the affluence, to Śiva with devotion is the same.

## \|\| 12.25.51 \|\|

*bhaktyā pracoditaḥ kuryādalpavittopi mānavaḥ \|*  
*mahāvibhavasāropi na kuryādbhaktivarjitaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Even a poor man urged by devotion, may do what a rich man devoid of devotion will not do.

## \|\| 12.25.52 \|\|

*sarvasvamapi yo dadyācchive bhaktivivarjitaḥ \|*  
*na tena phalabhāksa syādbhaktirevātra kāraṇam \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. If a man devoid of devotion were to dedicate his entire possession to Śiva he will not derive the benefit thereof. Devotion is the sole criterion.

## \|\| 12.25.53 \|\|

*na tattapobhiratyugrairna ca sarvairmahāmakhaiḥ \|*  
*gacchecchivapuraṃ divyaṃ muktvā bhaktiṃ śivātmakam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Without this none can go to the divine city of Śiva through any sort of penances.

## \|\| 12.25.54 \|\|

*guhyādguhyataraṃ kṛṣṇa sarvatra parameśvare \|*  
*śive bhaktirna saṃdehastayā bhakto vimucyate \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. O Kṛṣṇa, this is the secret of secrets in regard to the lord. There is no doubt that a devotee becomes liberated through devotion.

## \|\| 12.25.55 \|\|

*śivamaṃtrajapo dhyānaṃ homo yajñastapaḥśrutam \|*  
*dānamadhyayanaṃ sarve bhāvārthaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. The Japa of Śiva’s Mantra meditation, Horn a, Yajña, penance, learning, charitable gift, study of Vedas—all these are conducive to piety. There is no doubt about this.

## \|\| 12.25.56 \|\|

*bhāvahīno narassarvaṃ kṛtvāpi na vimucyate \|*  
*bhāvayuktaḥ punassarvamakṛtvāpi vimucyate \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. A person devoid of piety and devotion is not liberated even after doing everything but one with devotion is liberated even without doing anything.

## \|\| 12.25.57 \|\|

*cāṃdrāyaṇasahasraiśca prājāpatyaśataistathā \|*  
*māsopavāsaiścānyaiśca śivabhaktasya kiṃ punaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. To a devotee of Śiva, of what avail are thousands of Cāndrāyaṇas,\[3\] hundreds of Prājāpatyas, and other monthly fasts.

## \|\| 12.25.58 \|\|

*abhaktā mānavāścāsmiṃlloke giriguhāsu ca \|*  
*tapaṃti cālpabhogārthaṃ bhakto bhāvena mucyate \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. In this world, even non-devotees perform penances in mountain caves for the enjoyment of insignificant pleasures. But only a devotee is liberated through pious feelings.

## \|\| 12.25.59 \|\|

*sāttvikaṃ muktidaṃ karma sattve vai yoginaḥ sthitāḥ \|*  
*rājasaṃ siddhidaṃ kuryuḥ karmiṇo rajasāvṛtāḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. The Sāttvic activity yields salvation. Yogins abide by the Sattvaguṇa. The ritualists perform Rājasic rites bestowing Siddhis because they are enveloped by Rajas Guṇa.

## \|\| 12.25.60 \|\|

*asurā rākṣasāścaiva tamoguṇasamanvitāḥ \|*  
*aihikārthaṃ yajantīśaṃ narāścānye 'pi tādṛśāḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Asuras and Rākṣasas possessing Tamas Guṇa and men of that ilk worship the lord for securing worldly pleasures.

## \|\| 12.25.61 \|\|

*tāmasaṃ rājasaṃ vāpi sāttvikaṃ bhāvameva ca \|*  
*āśritya bhaktyā pūjādyaṃ kurvanbhadraṃ samaśnute \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Whether the attitude is Sāttvic, Rājasic or Tāmasic one performing worship etc. with devotion attains welfare.

## \|\| 12.25.62 \|\|

*yataḥ pāpārṇavāttrātuṃ bhaktirnauriva nirmitā \|*  
*tasmādbhaktyupapannasya rajasā tamasā ca kim \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Since devotion is a boat that saves one from the ocean of sins, of what avail are Rajas and Tamas to one who is endowed with devotion?

## \|\| 12.25.63 \|\|

*antyajo vādhamo vāpi mūrkho vā patito 'pi vā \|*  
*śivaṃ prapannaścetkṛṣṇa pūjyassarvasurāsuraiḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. O Kṛṣṇa, a low born, a base or a fool, or a fallen man, if he resorts to Śiva is worthy of being worshipped by the gods and Asuras.

## \|\| 12.25.64 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena bhaktyaiva śivamarcayet \|*  
*abhuktānāṃ kvacidapi phalaṃ nāsti yatastataḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Hence, by all means, one shall worship Śiva with devotion alone, since non-devotees secure no benefit from anywhere.

## \|\| 12.25.65 \|\|

*vakṣyāmyatirahasyaṃ te śṛṇu kṛṣṇa vaco mama \|*  
*vedaiśśāstrairvedavidbhirvicārya suviniścitam \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. O Kṛṣṇa, I shall tell you a great secret. Listen to my words. This is what has been decided conclusively by the Vedas, scriptures and those who know them, after careful consideration.

## Chapter 26 - The worship of Śiva with the ancillary rites

## \|\| 12.26.1-2 \|\|

*upamanyuruvāca \|*  
*brahmaghno vā surāpo vā steyīvā gurutalpagaḥ \|*  
*mātṛhā pitṛhā vāpi vīrahā bhrūṇahāpi vā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*saṃpūjyāmantrakaṃ bhaktyā śivaṃ paramakāraṇam \|*  
*taistaiḥ pāpaiḥ pramucyeta varṣairdvādaśabhiḥ kramāt \|\| 2 \|\|*

Upamanyu said:—

1-2. Even a slayer of brahmin, a wine-addict, a thief, a defiler of the preceptor’s bed, one guilty of matricide or patricide, a murderer of a hero and one guilty of destroying a child in the womb becomes absolved of those sins within twelve years by worshipping Śiva with devotion even without mantras.

## \|\| 12.26.3 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena patito 'pi yajecchivam \|*  
*bhaktaścennāparaḥ kaścidbhikṣāhāro jiteṃdriyaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Hence by all means let even a fallen man worship Śiva sustaining himself on alms and conquering the sense-organs. This he shall do if he is a devotee and none else.

## \|\| 12.26.4 \|\|

*kṛtvāpi sumahatpāpaṃ bhaktyā pañcākṣareṇa tu \|*  
*pūjayedyadi deveśaṃ tasmātpāpātpramucyate \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Even if one commits a great sin he is liberated from that if he worships the lord of the gods with devotion, repeating the five-syllabled mantra.

## \|\| 12.26.5 \|\|

*abbhakṣā vāyubhakṣāśca ye cānye vratakarśitāḥ \|*  
*teṣāmetairvratairnāsti śivalokasamāgamaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. There are many persons who live solely on water or air and who emaciate their bodies by means of holy rites. They cannot attain Śivaloka through these rites.

## \|\| 12.26.6 \|\|

*bhaktyā pañcākṣareṇaiva yaḥ śivaṃ sakṛdarcayet \|*  
*sopi gacchecchivasthānaṃ śivamantrasya gauravāt \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He who worships Śiva even once with devotion repeating the five-syllabled mantra goes to the abode of Śiva due to the efficacy of the mantra of Śiva.

## \|\| 12.26.7 \|\|

*tasmāttapāṃsi yajñāṃśca sarve sarvasvadakṣiṇāḥ \|*  
*śivamūrtyarcanasyaite koṭyaṃśenāpi no samāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Hence the penances and the sacrifices wherein the entire possession may be given as Dakṣiṇā, are not equal to even a croreth part of the worship of Śiva.

## \|\| 12.26.8 \|\|

*baddho vāpyatha mukto vā paścātpañcākṣareṇa cet \|*  
*pūjayanmucyate bhakto nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Whether bound or free, if the devotee worships with the five-syllabled mantra he is liberated. No doubt need be entertained in this respect.

## \|\| 12.26.9 \|\|

*arudro vā sarudro vā sūktena śivamarcayet \|*  
*yaḥ sakṛtpatito vāpimūḍho vā mucyate naraḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Whether a man is a follower of Rudra or not, whether he is fallen or deluded if he worships but once with Rudra Sūkta he is liberated.

## \|\| 12.26.10 \|\|

*ṣaḍakṣareṇa vā devaṃ sūktamantreṇa pūjayet \|*  
*śivabhakto jitakrodho hyalabdho labdha eva ca \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. A devotee of Śiva who has conquered anger, whether he has or has not secured grace shall worship the lord with the Sūktamantra or the six-syllabled mantra.

## \|\| 12.26.11 \|\|

*alabdhāllabdha evātra viśiṣṭo nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*sa brahmāṃgena vā tena sahaṃsena vimucyate \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Surely the former is better than the latter. He becomes liberated and absorbed into Brahman.

## \|\| 12.26.12 \|\|

*tasmānnityaṃ śivaṃ bhaktyā sūktamantreṇa pūjayet \|*  
*ekakālaṃ dvikālaṃ vā trikālaṃ nityameva vā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Hence one shall always worship Śiva with devotion repeating the mantras, once, twice or thrice or always.

## \|\| 12.26.13-15 \|\|

*ye 'rcayaṃti mahādevaṃ vijñeyāste maheśvarāḥ \|*  
*jñānenātmasahāyena nārcito bhagavāñchivaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*sa ciraṃ saṃsaratyasminsaṃsāre duḥkhasāgare \|*  
*durllabhaṃ prāpya mānuṣyaṃ mūḍho nārcayate śivam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*niṣphalaṃ tasya tajjanma mokṣāya na bhavedyataḥ \|*  
*durllabhaṃ prāpya mānuṣyaṃ ye 'rcayanti pinākinam \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. Those who worship the lord shall be known as Maheśvaras themselves. If one does not worship him through knowledge assisted by the prompting of the soul he suffers for long in the world which is an ocean of misery. Even after attaining the rare human body, if a deluded individual does not worship Śiva, his life becomes futile since it does not lead to salvation. After attaining the rare human birth those who worship the lord are excellent and blessed. Their life alone is fruitful.

## \|\| 12.26.16-19 \|\|

*teṣāṃ hi saphalaṃ janma kṛtārthāste narottamāḥ \|*  
*bhavabhaktiparā ye ca bhavapraṇatacetasaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*bhavasaṃsmaraṇodyuktā na te duḥkhasya bhāginaḥ \|*  
*bhavanāni manojñāni vibhramābharaṇāḥ striyaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*dhanaṃ cātṛptiparyantaṃ śivapūjāvidheḥ phalam \|*  
*ye vāñchanti mahābhogānrājyaṃ ca tridaśālaye \|\| 18 \|\|*

*te vāñchanti sadākālaṃ harasya caraṇāmbujam \|*  
*saubhāgyaṃ kāntimadrūpaṃ sattvaṃ tyāgārdrabhāvatā \|\| 19 \|\|*

16-19. Those who are devoted to the lord, whose minds are inclined to him and who endeavour to remember the lord are never subjected to misery. The fruit of the worship of Śiva is the sufficient wealth, charming houses and women folk seductively bedecked in ornaments. Those who desire great pleasures and kingdom in heaven shall love his lotus feet for ever. Good fortune, handsome and brilliant features, good strength, compassionate and renouncing temperament, heroism, fame in the world—all these are secured by one who worships the lord.

## \|\| 12.26.20-22 \|\|

*śauryaṃ vai jagati khyātiśśivamarcayato bhavet \|*  
*tasmātsarvaṃ parityajya śivaikāhitamānasaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*śivapūjāvidhiṃ kuryādyadīcchecchivamātmanaḥ \|*  
*tvaritaṃ jīvitaṃ yāti tvaritaṃ yāti yauvanam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tvaritaṃ vyādhirabhyeti tasmātpūjyaḥ pinākadhṛk \|*  
*yāvannāyāti maraṇaṃ yāvannākramate jarā \|\| 22 \|\|*

20-22. So desiring welfare, one shall invariably worship Śiva. forsaking everything else and dedicating the mind solely to him. The life passes off quickly. Youth goes off rapidly. Sickness approaches all too suddenly. Hence the lord shall be worshipped. Worship Śiva before death overtakes you, before old age attacks you, before the sense-organs become atrophied and inefficient.

## \|\| 12.26.23-28 \|\|

*yāvannendriyavaikalyaṃ tāvatpūjaya śaṃkaram \|*  
*na śivārcanatulyo 'sti dharmo 'nyo bhuvanatraye \|\| 23 \|\|*

*iti vijñāya yatnena pūjanīyassadāśivaḥ \|*  
*dvārayāgaṃ javanikāṃ parivārabalikriyām \|\| 24 \|\|*

*nityotsavaṃ ca kurvīta prasāde yadi pūjayet \|*  
*havirnivedanādūrdhvaṃ svayaṃ cānucaro 'pi vā \|\| 25 \|\|*

*prasādaparivārebhyo baliṃ dadyādyathākramam \|*  
*nirgamya saha vāditraistadāśābhimukhaḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*puṣpaṃ dhūpaṃ ca dīpañca dadyādannaṃ jalaiḥ saha \|*  
*tato dadyānmahāpīṭhe tiṣṭhanbalimudaṅmukhaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*tato niveditaṃ deve yattadannādikaṃ purā \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ sāvaśeṣaṃ vā caṇḍāya vinivedayet \|\| 28 \|\|*

23-28. Realising that there is no holy rite in the three worlds, on a par with the worship of Śiva, Sadāśiva shall be worshipped assiduously. If the worship is conducted in a palace the following rites too shall be performed—sacrifice at the gateway, worship within the screen, offering oblation to Śiva’s attendants and perpetual festivities. After offering libation the devotee or his servant shall offer oblation to the attendants in the palace. The devotee shall come out to the accompaniment of instrumental music and facing the northern direction he shall offer flowers, incense, lamp and cooked rice with water. Then he shall stand on the Mahāpīṭha facing the north and offer oblations. Thereafter, whatever had been offered to the lord before, as Naivedya, cooked rice shall be offered to Caṇḍa as Naivedya. The remnants also shall be offered thus.

## \|\| 12.26.29-30 \|\|

*hutvā ca vidhivatpaścātpūjāśeṣaṃ samāpayet \|*  
*kṛtvā prayogaṃ vidhivadyāvanmantraṃ japaṃ tataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*nityotsavaṃ prakurvīta yathoktaṃ śivaśāsane \|*  
*vipule taijase pātre raktapadmopaśobhite \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. Performing Homa, the latter part of worship shall be concluded. After conducting the regular rites he shall perform the perpetual festivities, Japa etc. in accordance with the injunction in Śaivite scriptures. In a large metallic vessel shining splendidly with a red lotus the divine Pāśupata missile shall be invoked and worshipped.

## \|\| 12.26.31-35 \|\|

*astraṃ pāśupataṃ divyaṃ tatrāvāhya samarcayet \|*  
*śivasyāropyaḥ tatpātraṃ dvijasyālaṃkṛtasya ca \|\| 31 \|\|*

*nyastāstravapuṣā tena dīptayaṣṭidharasya ca \|*  
*prāsādaparivārebhyo bahirmaṃgalaniḥsvanaiḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*nṛtyageyādibhiścaiva saha dīpadhvajādibhiḥ \|*  
*pradakṣiṇatrayaṃ kṛtvā na drutaṃ cāvilambitam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*mahāpīṭhaṃ samāvṛtya triḥpradakṣiṇayogataḥ \|*  
*punaḥ praviṣṭo dvārastho yajamānaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ \|*

*ādāyābhyaṃtaraṃ nītvā hyastramudvāsayettataḥ \|*  
*pradakṣiṇādikaṃ kṛtvā yathāpūrvoditaṃ kramāt \|\| 34 \|\|*

*ādāya cāṣṭapuṣpāṇi pūjāmatha samāpayet \|\| 35 \|\|*

31-35. The vessel shall be carried on the head by a Śaivite brahmin well-bedecked. He shall hold a lighted torch. With dances and songs to the accompaniment of auspicious instrumental music the party shall make three circumambulations round the palace of the lord The movement shall be neither quick nor slow. Thereafter the devotee shall stand a the door with palms joined in reverence shall take it in and ritualistically dismiss the Astra. After one more circumambulation he shall offer eight flowers and conclude the worship.

## Chapter 27 - The rite of sacrifice

## \|\| 12.27.1-2 \|\|

*upamanyuruvāca \|*  
*athāgnikāryaṃ vakṣyāmi kuṇḍe vā sthaṃḍile 'pi vā \|*  
*vedyāṃ vā hyāyase pātre mṛnmaye vā nave śubhe \|\| 1 \|\|*

*ādhāyāgniṃ vidhānena saṃskṛtya ca tataḥ param \|*  
*tatrārādhya mahādevaṃ homakarma samācaret \|\| 2 \|\|*

Upamanyu said:—

1-2. I shall mention the sacrificial rites in the fire to be performed in sacred pits, or raised ground or in altar Fire shall be taken in an iron vessel or a fresh mud pot in accordance with the injunctions and transferred to the actual place of sacrifice. After due consecration he shall propitiate the lord and commence sacrifice.

## \|\| 12.27.3 \|\|

*kuṇḍaṃ dvihastamānaṃ vā hastamātramathāpi vā \|*  
*vṛttaṃ vā caturasraṃ vā kuryādvediṃ ca maṇḍalam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The pit may be one or two Hastas wide. The altar shall be made in the form of a circle or a square.

## \|\| 12.27.4 \|\|

*kuṇḍaṃ vistāravannimnaṃ tanmadhye 'ṣṭadalāmbujam \|*  
*caturaṃgulamutsedhaṃ tasya dvyaṃgulameva vā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. In the altar he shall make the eight-petalled lotus. It shall be two or four Aṅgulas high above the altar.

## \|\| 12.27.5-6 \|\|

*vitastidviguṇonnatyā nābhimantaḥ pracakṣate \|*  
*madhyaṃ ca madhyamāṃgulyā madhyamottamaparvaṇoḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*aṃgulaiḥ kathyate sadbhiścaturviṃśatibhiḥ karaḥ \|*  
*mekhalānāṃ trayaṃ vāpi dvayamekamathāpi vā \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. The navel within the altar shall be two Vitastis high One Aṅgula is the distance between the middle and the first knot in the middle finger. Twenty-four such Aṅgulas constitute a Hasta. Three, two or only one Mekhalā (circular girdle) shall also be made.

## \|\| 12.27.7-8 \|\|

*yathāśobhaṃ prakurvīta ślakṣṇamiṣṭaṃ mṛdā sthiram \|*  
*aśvatthapatravadyoniṃ gajādhāravadeva vā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*mekhalāmadhyataḥ kuryātpaścime dakṣiṇe 'pi vā \|*  
*śobhanāmagnitaḥ kiṃcinnimnāmunmīlikāṃ śanaiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. The altar shall be made with smooth clay. In the middle of the Mekhalā to the west or south the passage shall be made like the leaf of the Aśvattha tree or like the lower lip of an elephant. It shall be beautifully made slightly lower than the fire. It shall close in gradually.

## \|\| 12.27.9-10 \|\|

*agreṇa kuṇḍābhimukhīṃ kiṃcidutsṛjya mekhalām \|*  
*notsedhaniyamo vedyāḥ sā mārdī vātha saikatī \|\| 9 \|\|*

*maṃḍalaṃ gośakṛttoyairmānaṃ pātrasya noditam \|*  
*kuṇḍaṃ ca mṛnmayaṃ vedimālipedgomayāṃbunā \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. The Mekhalā shall be left out a little where it faces the pit. There is no stipulated height for the altar. It shall be made of clay or sand. The circular ground shall be smeared with cowdung and water. The measurement of the basin is not stipulated. The Kuṇḍa shall be made of clay. The altar shall be smeared with cowdung and water.

## \|\| 12.27.11 \|\|

*prakṣālya tāpayetpātraṃ prokṣayedanyadaṃbhasā \|*  
*svasūtroktaprakāreṇa kuṇḍādau villikhettataḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The vessel shall be washed and warmed in fire The sacrificial material shall be sprinkled with water. The devotee shall draw lines on the pit etc. in the manner prescribed in his own branch of learning.

## \|\| 12.27.12 \|\|

*saṃprokṣya kalpayeddarbhaiḥ puṣpairvā vahniviṣṭaram \|*  
*arcanārthaṃ ca homārthaṃ sarvadravyāṇi sādhayet \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The seat of fire shall be made after due sprinkling, with Darbhas or flowers. He shall gather the material for the purpose of worship and sacrifice.

## \|\| 12.27.13-15 \|\|

*prakṣālyakṣālanīyāni prokṣaṇyā prokṣya śodhayet \|*  
*maṇijaṃ kāṣṭhajaṃ vātha śrotriyāgārasambhavam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*anyaṃ vābhyarhitaṃ vahniṃ tataḥ sādhāramānayet \|*  
*triḥ pradakṣiṇamāvṛtya kuṇḍāderupari kramāt \|\| 14 \|\|*

*vahnibījaṃ samuccārya tvādadhītāgnimāsane \|*  
*yonimārgeṇa vā tadvadātmanaḥ saṃmukhena vā \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. Things to be washed shall be washed and to be sprinkled shall be sprinkled and purified. Then he shall fetch fire in a supporting vessel. The fire may be one produced from crystals, lens etc. or from wood. It shall be brought from the house of a Vedic scholar. It shall be whirled round the sacrificial pit thrice repeating the Bīja mantra of the fire. The fire shall be placed in its seat through the passage or straight in front.

## \|\| 12.27.16-18 \|\|

*niyogaḥ pradeśa sarvaṃ kuṃḍaṃ kuryādvicakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*svanābhyaṃtaḥsthitaṃ vahniṃ tadraṃdhrādvisphuliṃgavad \|\| 16 \|\|*

*nirgamya pāvake bāhye līnaṃ biṃbākṛti smaret \|*  
*ājyasaṃskāraparyaṃtamanvādhānapurassaram \|\| 17 \|\|*

*svasūtroktakramātkuryānmūlamantreṇa mantravit \|*  
*śivamūrtiṃ samabhyarcya tato dakṣiṇapārśvataḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

16-18. Seated near the passage the devotee shall survey the fire and think that the internal fire stationed in his umbilicus has risen in the form of flames and has merged in the external fire in the form of a disc. The expert devotee shall repeat the basic mantra in the manner prescribed in his Sūtra and shall perform the rites of Anvādhāna and Ājyasaṃskāra. To its south he shall worship the idol of Śiva, perform the rite of Mantranyāsa with the butter and show the Mudrā of cow.

## \|\| 12.27.19-20 \|\|

*nyasya mantraṃ ghṛte mudrāṃ darśayeddhenusaṃjñitām \|*  
*sruksruvau taijasau grāhyau na kāṃsyāyasasaisakau \|\| 19 \|\|*

*yajñadārumayau vāpi smārtau vā śilpasammatau \|*  
*parṇe vā brahmavṛkṣāderacchidre madhya utthite \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. The sacrificial spoons shall be metallic but not of bell metal, iron or lead. These shall be made of sacrificial wood as mentioned in Smṛtis and approved by artisans. The leaves of the Brahmā tree shall be holeless. They shall be raised in the middle.

## \|\| 12.27.21-22 \|\|

*saṃsṛjya darbhaistau vahnau saṃtāpya prokṣayetpunaḥ \|*  
*pārārṣarcyasvasūtroktakrameṇa śivapūrvakaiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*juhuyādaṣṭabhirbījairagnisaṃskārasiddhaye \|*  
*bhruṃstuṃbruśruṃ krameṇaiva puṃḍraṃdramityataḥ param \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. The leaves shall be scrubbed with Darbhas, warmed in the fire, then sprinkled with water in the manner prescribed in his Sūtra, repeating the name of Śiva. He shall then make offering to the fire with the eight Bīja mantras. The seven Bījas for the seven flames are respectively Bhrum, Stum, Brum, Śrum, Pum, Ḍrum and Drum.

## \|\| 12.27.23-24 \|\|

*bījāni sapta saptānāṃ jihvānāmanupūrvaśaḥ \|*  
*triśikhā madhyamā jihvā bahurūpasamāhvayā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*raktāgneyī nairṛtī ca kṛṣṇānyā suprabhā matā \|*  
*atiriktā marujjihvā svanāmānuguṇaprabhā \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. The middle tongue has three flames. The flame in the east is yellow. The flame in the south-east is red; that in the south-west is black and the other one is refulgent. As its name implies it is brilliant. It is the flame in the northwest.

## \|\| 12.27.25-26 \|\|

*svabījānantaraṃ vācyā svāhāṃtañca yathākramam \|*  
*jihvāmaṃtraistu tairhutvājyaṃ jihvāstvekaikaśa kramāt \|\| 25 \|\|*

*raṃ vahnayeti svāheti madhye hutvāhutitrayam \|*  
*sarpiṣā vā samidbhirvā pariṣecanamācaret \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. After repeating their Bīja mantras the tongues shall be mentioned and the rite concluding with Svāhā performed in due order. The Ājya shall be used for Āhuti with the mantras of the tongues one by one. In the middle he shall perform three Āhutis repeating ‘Ram Vahnyeti Svāhā’ either with ghee or with sacrificial twigs. Then the rite of Pariṣecana shall be performed.

## \|\| 12.27.27 \|\|

*evaṃ kṛte śivāgniḥ syātsmarettatra śivāsanam \|*  
*tatrāvāhya yajeddevamardhanārīśvaraṃ śivam \|*

*dīpāntaṃ pariṣicyātha samiddhomaṃ samācaret \|*  
*tāḥ pālāśyaḥ parā vāpi yājñiyā dvādaśāṃgulāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. When this is performed it becomes fire of Śiva. The devotee shall conceive it as the seat of Śiva. The lord shall be invoked there and worshipped, in the half-male and half-female form. After sprinkling everything ending with the light he shall perform the sacrifice with the sacrificial twigs.

## \|\| 12.27.28-29 \|\|

*avakrā na svayaṃ śuṣkāssatvaco nirvraṇāḥ samāḥ \|*  
*daśāṃgulā vā vihitāḥ kaniṣṭhāṃgulisaṃmitāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*prādeśamātrā vālābhe hotavyāḥ sakalā api \|*  
*dūrvāpatrasamākārāṃ caturaṃgulamāyatām \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. The sacrificial twigs shall consist of Palāśa or other trees worthy of sacrifice. They shall be twelve Aṅgulas in length. They shall not be crooked. They shall not be dry by themselves. The bark shall be intact, even and without cuts. Or they shall be ten Aṅgulas in length, as thick as the small finger or they may be of the length of Prādeśa. If they are not available any kind of twig shall be offered in the fire.

## \|\| 12.27.30 \|\|

*dadyādājyāhutiṃ paścādannamakṣapramāṇataḥ \|*  
*lājāṃstathā sarṣapāṃśca yavāṃścaiva tilāṃstathā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The Ājya Āhuti shall be made with the leaf four Aṅgulas wide, shaped in the form of a Dūrvāpatra. Afterwards, cooked rice of the size of an Akṣa shall be offered.

## \|\| 12.27.31 \|\|

*sarpiṣāktāni bhakṣyāṇi lehyacoṣyāṇi sambhave \|*  
*daśaivāhutayastatra pañca vā tritayaṃ ca vā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Fried grains, mustard seeds, barleys, gingelly seeds, foodstuffs soaked in ghee etc. shall be offered if possible.

## \|\| 12.27.32 \|\|

*hotavyāḥ śaktito dadyādekamevātha vāhutim \|*  
*śruveṇājyaṃ samityādyāsrucāśeṣātkareṇa vā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The number of Āhutis shall be ten, five or three according to capacity. It is enough even if one Āhuti is made.

## \|\| 12.27.33 \|\|

*tatra divyena hotavyaṃ tīrthenārṣeṇa vā tathā \|*  
*dravyeṇaikena vā 'lābhe juhuyācchraddhayā punaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The butter shall be offered with the wooden spoon and the articles with the wooden ladle or with hand. The Homa shall be performed at the divine or saintly spot.

## \|\| 12.27.34 \|\|

*prāyaścittāya juhuyānmaṃtrayitvāhutitrayam \|*  
*tato homaviśiṣṭena ghṛtenāpūrya vai srucam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. If full articles are not available only one material shall be offered with devotion. As an expiation he shall perform three Āhutis repeating the mantra.

## \|\| 12.27.35-36 \|\|

*nidhāya puṣpaṃ tasyāgre śruveṇādhomukhena tām \|*  
*sadarbhena samācchādya mūlenāṃjalinotthitaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*vauṣaḍaṃtena juhuyāddhārāṃ tu yavasaṃmitām \|*  
*itthaṃ pūrṇāhutiṃ kṛtvā pariṣiṃcecca pūrvavat \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. He shall fill the Sruk with the ghee that has been left after Homa and put a flower on it. The Sruva shall be placed above it upside down along with the Darbha. Through the root of the Darbha the ghee shall fall in drops of the size of a barley grain repeating the mantra ending with Vauṣaṭ.

## \|\| 12.27.37 \|\|

*tata udvāsya deveśaṃ gopayettu hutāśanam \|*  
*tamapyudvāsya vā nābhau yajetsaṃdhāya nityaśaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Performing the Pūrṇāhuti he shall perform the rite of sprinkling water. He shall ritualistically dismiss the lord and preserve the fire.

## \|\| 12.27.38-42 \|\|

*athavā vahnimānīya śivaśāstroktavartmanā \|*  
*vāgīśīgarbhasaṃbhūtaṃ saṃskṛtya vidhivadyajet \|\| 38 \|\|*

*anvādhānaṃ punaḥ kṛtvā paridhīn paridhāya ca \|*  
*pātrāṇi dvandvarūpeṇa nikṣipyeṣṭvā śivaṃ tataḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*saṃśodhya prokṣaṇīpātraṃ prokṣyatāni tadaṃbhasā \|*  
*praṇītāpātramaiśānyāṃ vinyasyā pūritaṃ jalaiḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*ājyasaṃskāraparyaṃtaṃ kṛtvā saṃśodhya sraksruvau \|*  
*garbhādhānaṃ puṃsavanaṃ sīmantonnayanaṃ tataḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*kṛtvā pṛthakpṛthagghutvā jātamagniṃ vicintayet \|*  
*tripādaṃ saptahastaṃ ca catuḥśṛṃgaṃ dviśīrṣakam \|\| 42 \|\|*

38-42. Or it can also be discharged and placed in the umbilicus of the altar and worshipped everyday. Or, bringing the fire along the path prescribed in Śaivite scriptures it shall be conceived as torn of the womb of the goddess of speech, consecrated duly and worshipped. Sacrificial fuels shall be put on the fire again and the sacred sticks laid round the fire covered with a cloth. The vessels shall be placed in pairs. Śiva shall be worshipped then. After purifying the Prokṣaṇī vessel the vessels shall be sprinkled with the water. The Praṇītā vessel shall be filled with the water and placed in the north-east. Then come the rites concluding with the consecration of ghee. After the Sruk and Sruva are purified, the rites of Garbhādhāna Puṃsavana and Sīmantonnayana shall be performed with the rites of Homa in each case. Then he shall think of the fire as born.

## \|\| 12.27.43-45 \|\|

*madhupiṃgaṃ trinayanaṃ sakapardenduśekharam \|*  
*raktaṃ raktāmbarālepaṃ mālyabhūṣaṇabhūṣitam \|\| 43 \|\|*

*sarvalakṣaṇasaṃpannaṃ sopavītaṃ trimekhalam \|*  
*śaktimantaṃ sruksruvau ca dadhānaṃ dakṣiṇe kare \|\| 44 \|\|*

*tomaraṃ tālavṛṃtaṃ ca ghṛtapātraṃ tathetaraiḥ \|*  
*jātaṃ dhyātvaivamākāraṃ jātakarma samācaret \|\| 45 \|\|*

43-45. Agni shall be conceived in the form of having three feet, seven hands, four horns, two heads and three eyes, as tawny as honey, having the matted hair, with the moon for his crest, of red colour, red garments and red unguents, bedecked in garlands and ornaments, richly equipped with all characteristics, having the sacred thread and three girdles, holding the Sruk and Sruva in the right hand, iron club, fan and the vessel of ghee in the other.

## \|\| 12.27.46-50 \|\|

*nālāpanayanaṃ kṛtvā tataḥ saṃśodhya sūtakam \|*  
*śivāgnirucināmāsya kṛtvāhutipurassaram \|\| 46 \|\|*

*pitrorvisarjanaṃ kṛtvā caulopanayanādikam \|*  
*aptoryāmāvasānāntaṃ kṛtvā saṃskāramasya tu \|\| 47 \|\|*

*ājyadhārādihomaṃ ca kṛtvā sviṣṭakṛtaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*ramityanena bījena pariṣiṃcettataḥ param \|\| 48 \|\|*

*brahmaviṣṇuśiveśānāṃ lokeśānāṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*tadastrāṇāṃ ca paritaḥ kṛtvā pūjāṃ yathākramam \|\| 49 \|\|*

*dhūpadīpādisiddhyarthaṃ vahnimuddhṛtya kṛtyavit \|*  
*sādhayitvājyapūrvāṇi dravyāṇi punareva ca \|\| 50 \|\|*

46-50. After meditating on the fire thus with these features he shall perform post-natal rites. The umbilical cord shall be removed and the purificatory rite for the post-natal pollution shall be performed. The rite of naming shall be performed by giving him the title of Śivāgni with due Āhuti. The rite of ritualistic dismissal of the parents as well as of tonsure, sacred thread shall be performed till the end of Āptoryāma. As a consecratory rite the Homa of ghce-pouring shall be performed. Agni shall be conceived as Sviṣṭakṛt. With the Bīja mantra “Raṃ” the water shall be sprinkled all round. The worship of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, Īśa and of their miraculous missiles shall be performed in due order. Then for the sake of incense and lamp, fire shall be taken out by the expert devotee.

## \|\| 12.27.51-52 \|\|

*kalpayitvāsanaṃ vahnau tatrāvāhya yathāpurā \|*  
*saṃpūjya devaṃ devīṃ ca tataḥ pūrṇāṃtamācaret \|\| 51 \|\|*

*atha vā svāśramoktaṃ tu vahnikarma śivārpaṇam \|*  
*buddhvā śivāśramī kuryānna ca tatrāparo vidhiḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

51-52. The devotee shall collect the materials of worship, ghee etc., think of the seat of the lord and the goddess, invoke them in the fire and perform the rites until the Pūrṇāhuti. Or the devotee following the Śaivite conduct of life shall perform the rites in fire as prescribed in his scriptural code dedicating the same to Śiva. There is no other injunction there.

## \|\| 12.27.53-54 \|\|

*śivāgnerbhasmasaṃgrāhyamagnihotrodbhavaṃ tu vā \|*  
*vaivāhognibhavaṃ vāpi pakvaṃ śuci sugaṃdhi ca \|\| 53 \|\|*

*kapilāyāḥ śakṛcchastaṃ gṛhītaṃ gagane patat \|*  
*na klinnaṃ nātikaṭhinaṃ na durgandhaṃ na śoṣitam \|\| 54 \|\|*

53-54. The ashes from Śivāgni shall be collected and preserved. Similarly the ashes of Agnihotra rite or from the fire connected with the celebration of marriage. The fire shall be ripe, pure and sweet-smelling. The dung shall be of the cow, tawny in colour. It is commendable if collected as it falls from the cow before it reaches the ground.

## \|\| 12.27.55 \|\|

*uparyadhaḥ parityajya gṛhṇīyātpatitaṃ yadi \|*  
*piṃḍīkṛtya śivāgnyādau tatkṣipenmūlamaṃtrataḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. If he collects the dung that has already fallen or the ground the upper and the lower portions shall be eschewed. The dung shall not be too watery nor too solidified nor dried up It shall not emit foul smell.

## \|\| 12.27.56-58 \|\|

*apakvamatipākvaṃ ca saṃtyajya bhasitaṃ sitam \|*  
*ādāya vā samāloḍya bhasmādhāre vinikṣipet \|\| 56 \|\|*

*taijasaṃ dāravaṃ vāpi mṛnmayaṃ śailameva ca \|*  
*anyadvā śobhanaṃ śuddhaṃ bhasmādhāraṃ prakalpayet \|\| 57 \|\|*

*same deśe śubhe śuddhe dhanavadbhasma nikṣipet \|*  
*na cāyuktakare dadyānnaivāśucitale kṣipet \|\| 58 \|\|*

56-58. It shall be made into balls and the balls shall be consigned to Śivāgni or other types of fires repeating the basic mantra. The portions over-burnt or under-burnt shall be eschewed and the white ashes shall be gathered and ground into powder. It shall be preserved in receptacles made of metals, wood, clay or stone or any other material. The receptacle of water shall be pare. It shall be kepi in a pure auspicious, even place and guarded like valuable wealth.

## \|\| 12.27.59 \|\|

*na saṃspṛśecca nīcāṃgairnopekṣeta na laṃghayet \|*  
*tasmādbhasitamādāya viniyuṃjīta mantrataḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. It shall not be handed to any undeserving person. It shall not be kept or thrown in any unholy place. If the hands or limbs are dirty it shall not be touched. It shall not be neglected nor shall one jump over it.

## \|\| 12.27.60 \|\|

*kāleṣūkteṣu nānyatra nāyogyebhyaḥ pradāpayet \|*  
*bhasmasaṃgrahaṇaṃ kuryāddeve 'nudvāsite sati \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Hence after taking the ashes it shall be utilised with the mantras on occasions previously mentioned and not otherwise. It shall not be given to others.

## \|\| 12.27.61 \|\|

*udvāsane kṛte yasmāccaṇḍabhasma prajāpate \|*  
*agnikārye kṛte paścācchivaśāstroktamārgataḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. The ashes shall be collected before the ritualistic dismissal of the lord. After the rite of the ritualistic dismissal it becomes Caṇḍabhasma.

## \|\| 12.27.62 \|\|

*svasūtroktaprakārādvā balikarma samācaret \|*  
*atha vidyāsanaṃ nyasya supralipte tu maṇḍale \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. After the rites in the fire have been concluded he shall perform the oblation rite according to the injunctions in the Śaivite scriptures or as mentioned in his own Sūtra.

## \|\| 12.27.63 \|\|

*vidyākośaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yajetpuṣpādibhiḥ kramāt \|*  
*vidyāyāḥ purataḥ kṛtvā gurorapi ca maṇḍalam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Then after conceiving the seat of Vidyā on the well-smeared Maṇḍala he shall install the sheath of Vidyā and worship the same with flowers etc. in due order.

## \|\| 12.27.64 \|\|

*tatrāsanavaraṃ kṛtvā puṣpādyai gurumarcayet \|*  
*tatonupūjayetpūjyān bhojayecca bubhukṣitān \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. In front of the seat of Vidyā, the seat of the preceptor too shall be conceived. After assigning the seat there, he shall worship the preceptor with flowers etc.

## \|\| 12.27.65 \|\|

*tatassvayaṃ ca bhuṃjīta śuddhamannaṃ yathāsukham \|*  
*niveditaṃ ca vā deve taccheṣaṃ cātmaśuddhaye \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Thereafter the venerable persons shall be worshipped and the hungry shall be fed. The devotee shall take the wholesome food at leisure, comfortably.

## \|\| 12.27.66-67 \|\|

*śraddadhāno na lobhena na caṇḍāya samarpitam \|*  
*gandhamālyādi yaccānyattatrāpyeṣa samo vidhiḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*na tu tatra śivosmīti buddhiṃ kuryādvicakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*bhuktvācamya śivaṃ dhyātvā hṛdaye mūlamuccaret \|\| 67 \|\|*

66-67. What has been offered as Naivedya or what is left over he shall partake of, with full faith and not out of covetousness. It shall be for the purity of the Ātman. Out of covetousness he shall not partake of what is offered to Caṇḍa. The injunctions about scents, garlands etc. are the same. But the expert devotee shall not have the conception “I am Śiva”.

## \|\| 12.27.68 \|\|

*kālaśeṣaṃ nayedyogyaiḥ śivaśāstrakathādibhiḥ \|*  
*rātrau vyatīte pūrvāṃśe kṛtvā pūjāṃ manoharām \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. After taking meals he shall perform Ācamana and meditate upon Śiva in the heart repeating the basic mantra. He shall spend the leisure thereafter in discussing Śaivite philosophy and legends.

## \|\| 12.27.69 \|\|

*śivayoḥ śayanaṃ tvekaṃ kalpayedatiśobhanam \|*  
*bhakṣyabhojyāṃbarālepapuṣpamālādikaṃ tathā \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. At night he shall perform worship and then make out bed for Śiva and Śivā.

## \|\| 12.27.70 \|\|

*manasā karmaṇā vāpi kṛtvā sarvaṃ manoharam \|*  
*tato devasya devyāśca pādamūle śucissvapet \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. He shall offer mentally or physically various foodstuffs, garments, unguents flower-garlands, etc. all performed in a charming way.

## \|\| 12.27.71 \|\|

*gṛhastho bhāryayā sārdhaṃ tadanye 'pi tu kevalāḥ \|*  
*pratyūṣasamayaṃ buddhvā mātrāmādyāmudīrayet \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. The devotee shall go to bed at the feet of the lord and the goddess. The householder shall sleep there with his wife. Others shall sleep alone.

## \|\| 12.27.72-73 \|\|

*praṇamya manasāṃ devaṃ sāṃbaṃ sagaṇamavyayam \|*  
*deśakālocitaṃ kṛtvā śaucādyamapi śaktitaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

*śaṃkhādininadairdivyairdevaṃ devīṃ ca bodhayet \|*  
*tatastatsamayonnidraiḥ puṣpairatisugaṃdhibhiḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

72-73. He shall wake up before dawn and utter the first Mātrā. After bowing mentally to the lord accompanied by Ambā and his Gaṇas he shall attend to his morning duties. After washing himself he shall awaken the lord and the goddess by the divine sounds of conch and other instruments.

## \|\| 12.27.74 \|\|

*nirvartya śivayoḥ pūjāṃ prārabheta puroditam \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. He shall perform the worship of Śiva and Śivā by means of fresh blown fragrant flowers and begin the rites as mentioned before.

## Chapter 28 - The compulsory and optional rites

## \|\| 12.28.1 \|\|

*upamanyuruvāca \|*  
*ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi śivāśramaniṣeviṇām \|*  
*śivaśāstroktamārgeṇa naimittikavidhikramam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Upamanyu said:—

1\. Now I shall explain the procedure of rites under certain conditions to be performed by those who follow the Śaivite conduct of life in the manner prescribed in the Śaivite scriptures.

## \|\| 12.28.2-3 \|\|

*sarveṣvapi ca māseṣu pakṣayorubhayorapi \|*  
*aṣṭābhyāṃ ca caturdaśyāṃ tathā parvāṇi ca kramāt \|\| 2 \|\|*

*ayane viṣuve caiva grahaṇeṣu viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*kartavyā mahatī pūjā hyadhikā vāpi śaktitaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. The great worship shall be performed every month in both the fortnights on the eighth and fourteenth days and on the Full-moon and the New-moon days. It must be performed particularly at the tropical and equinoctial transit of the sun and during the eclipses, according to his capacity.

## \|\| 12.28.4 \|\|

*māsimāsi yathānyāyaṃ brahmakūrcaṃ prasādhya tu \|*  
*snāpayitvā śivaṃ tena pibeccheṣamupoṣitaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Every month he shall observe fast for a day and prepare Brahmakūrca. He shall perform the ablution of Śiva thereby and drink the residue.

## \|\| 12.28.5 \|\|

*brahmahatyādidoṣāṇāmatīva mahatāmapi \|*  
*niṣkṛtirbrahmakūrcasya pānānnānyā viśiṣyate \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The atonement for the murder of a brahmin and other great sins is the drinking of Brahmakūrca. There is no better remedy.

## \|\| 12.28.6 \|\|

*pauṣe puṣyanakṣatre kuryānnīrājanaṃ vibhoḥ \|*  
*māghe maghākhye nakṣatre pradadyādghṛtakaṃbalam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. In the month of Dec-Jan. when the moon is in the asterism Puṣya he shall perform the rite of Nīrājana to the lord. In the month of Jan-February in the Maghā star he shall make the charitable gifts of ghee and woollen blanket.

## \|\| 12.28.7 \|\|

*phālgune cottarānte vai prārabheta mahotsavam \|*  
*caitre citrāpaurṇamāsyāṃ dolāṃ kuryādyathāvidhi \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. In the month of Feb-March in the star Uttarā-Phālgunī he shall start the great festival. In the month of March-April on the full-moon day and Citrā star, he shall perform the Swing-festival duly.

## \|\| 12.28.8 \|\|

*vaiśākhyāṃ tu viśākhāyāṃ kuryātpuṣpamahālayam \|*  
*jyeṣṭhe mūlākhyanakṣatre śītakumbhaṃ pradāpayet \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. In the month of April-May on the full-moon day with the star Viśākhā he shall make the great temple of flowers. In the month of May June on the star Mūlā he shall offer a pot of cold water.

## \|\| 12.28.9-10 \|\|

*āṣāḍhe cottarāṣāḍhe pavitrāropaṇaṃ tathā \|*  
*śrāvaṇe prākṛtānyāpi maṇḍalāni prakalpayet \|\| 9 \|\|*

*śraviṣṭhākhye tu nakṣatre prauṣṭhapadyāṃ tataḥ param \|*  
*prokṣayecca jalakrīḍāṃ pūrvāṣāḍhāśraye dine \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. In the month of June-July on the star Uttarāṣādhā the rite of investiture with sacred thread shall be performed. In the month of July-August the mystic diagrams shall be arranged. In the month of Aug-September in the star Pūrvāṣāḍhā the swimming festival of the lord shall be performed.

## \|\| 12.28.11 \|\|

*āśvayujyāṃ tato dadyātpāyasaṃ ca navodanam \|*  
*agnikāryaṃ ca tenaiva kuryācchatabhiṣagdine \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. In the month of Sep-October on the full moon day he shall make charitable gifts of milk pudding and cooked rice with grains recently harvested. On the star Śatabhiṣak he shall perform the rites of fire too with the same.

## \|\| 12.28.12 \|\|

*kārtikyāṃ kṛtikāyoge dadyāddīpasahasrakam \|*  
*mārgaśīrṣe tathārdrāyāṃ ghṛtena snāpayecchivam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. In the month of Octo-November when the moon is in conjunction with the star Kṛttikā he shall light a thousand lamps. In the month of Nov-December on the Ārdrā star he shall perform the ablution of Śiva with ghee.

## \|\| 12.28.13 \|\|

*aśaktasteṣu kāleṣu kuryādutsavameva vā \|*  
*āsthānaṃ vā mahāpūjāmadhikaṃ vā samarcanam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Those who are unable to perform the rites on the respective occasions shall perform the festival in the big hall of the temple or perform worship or more.

## \|\| 12.28.14-16 \|\|

*āvṛtte 'pi ca kalyāṇe praśasteṣvapi karmasu \|*  
*daurmanasye durācāre duḥsvapne duṣṭadarśane \|\| 14 \|\|*

*utpāte vāśubhenyasminroge vā prabale 'tha vā \|*  
*snānapūjājapadhyānahomadānādikāḥ kriyaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*nirmitānuguṇāḥ kāryāḥ puraścaraṇapūrvikāḥ \|*  
*śivānale ca vihate punassandhānamācaret \|\| 16 \|\|*

14-16. On occasions when commendable rites shall be performed, when the mind is afflicted and dejected, when the conduct of life has become defiled, when bad dreams occur, when wicked men are seen, when inauspicious portents occur or when afflicted by great ailments, the devotee shall perform ceremonial ablutions, worships, Japas, meditations, sacrifices and other rites and offer charitable gifts suitably along with Puraścaraṇa. When the scries of Śiva-fire is broken it shall be revived.

## \|\| 12.28.17 \|\|

*ya evaṃ śarvadharmiṣṭho vartate nityamudyataḥ \|*  
*tasyaikajanmanā muktiṃ prayacchati maheśvaraḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Śiva bestows salvation on the person who performs his rites thus, perpetually and assiduously, even in a single birth.

## \|\| 12.28.18 \|\|

*etadyathottaraṃ kuryānnityanaimittikeṣu yaḥ \|*  
*divyaṃ śrīkaṃṭhanāthasya sthānamādyaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He who performs in succession the compulsory and optional rites attains the divine and primordial region of lord Siva.

## \|\| 12.28.19-21 \|\|

*tatra bhuktvā mahābhogānkalpakoṭiśatannaraḥ \|*  
*kālāṃtarecyutastasmādaumaṃ kaumārameva ca \|\| 19 \|\|*

*saṃprāpya vaiṣṇavaṃ brāhmaṃ rudralokaṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*tatroṣitvā ciraṃ kālaṃ bhuktvā bhogānyathoditān \|\| 20 \|\|*

*punaścordhvaṃ gatastasmādatītya sthānapañcakam \|*  
*śrīkaṇṭhājjñānamāsādya tasmācchaivapuraṃ vrajet \|\| 21 \|\|*

19-21. The man enjoys great pleasures there for millions and millions of Kalpas. After some time, falling from there he occupies the regions of Umā, Kurnāra, Viṣṇu, Brahmā, Rudra and enjoys the pleasures there as mentioned. Again he goes up and transcends the five regions. Securing knowledge of Śiva he attains Śiva’s city.

## \|\| 12.28.22 \|\|

*ardhacaryārataścāpi dvirāvṛttyaivameva tu \|*  
*paścājjñānaṃ samāsādya śivasāyujyamāpnuyāt \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. A devotee who performs half the number of holy rites has this upward and downward journey twice and thereafter secures knowledge and attains Śiva’s Sāyujya.

## \|\| 12.28.23-26 \|\|

*ardhārdhacarito yastu dehī dehakṣayātparam \|*  
*aṃḍāṃtaṃ vordhvamavyaktamatītya bhuvanadvayam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*saṃprāpya pauruṣaṃ raudrasthānamadrīndrajāpateḥ \|*  
*anekayugasāhasraṃ bhuktvā bhogānanekadhā \|\| 24 \|\|*

*puṇyakṣaye kṣitiṃ prāpya kule mahati jāyate \|*  
*tatrāpi pūrvasaṃskāravaśena sa mahādyutiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*paśudharmānparityajya śivadharmarato bhavet \|*  
*taddharmagauravādeva dhyātvā śivapuraṃ vrajet \|\| 26 \|\|*

23-26. A devotee who performs one-fourth of the number of holy rites goes beyond the two worlds, to the end of the universe and the unmanifest above, and reaches the Pauruṣa and Raudra regions of Śiva. After enjoying the pleasures there in diverse ways for thousands of Yugas when the merit is exhausted he reaches the earth and is born in a great and noble family. There also due to the previous impressions, he will eschew brutish activities and be engaged in Śaivite holy rites. Meditating well due to the holy rites he will attain Śiva’s city.

## \|\| 12.28.27-28 \|\|

*bhogāṃśca vividhānbhuktvā vidyeśvarapadaṃ vrajet \|*  
*tatra vidyeśvaraissārdhaṃ bhuktvā bhogānbahūnkramāt \|\| 27 \|\|*

*aṇḍasyāṃtarbahirvātha sakṛdāvartate punaḥ \|*  
*tato labdhvā śivajñānaṃ parāṃ bhaktimavāpya ca \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. After enjoying extensive pleasures he will attain the region of Vidyeśvaras. After enjoying the vast pleasures along with Vidyeśvaras he will return for once either within or outside the universe. Thereafter he will secure the perfect knowledge of Śiva and the great devotion. After attaining identity with Śiva he does not return again.

## \|\| 12.28.29-30 \|\|

*śivasādharmyamāsādya na bhūyo vinivartate \|*  
*yaścātīva śive bhakto viṣayāsaktacittavat \|\| 29 \|\|*

*śivadarmānaso kurvannakurvanvāpi mucyate \|*  
*ekāvṛtto dvirāvṛttastrirāvṛtto nivartakaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. A person who is devoted to Śiva even as the others are devoted to sensual objects shall be liberated whether he performs or does not perform the Śaivite holy rites. He returns once, twice, or thrice but ultimately does not return.

## \|\| 12.28.31-32 \|\|

*na punaścakravartī syācchivadharmādhikāravān \|*  
*tasmāccchivāśrito bhūtvā yena kenāpi hetunā \|\| 31 \|\|*

*śivadharme matiṃ kuryācchreyase cetkṛtodyamaḥ \|*  
*nātra nirbaṃdhayiṣyāmo vayaṃ kecana kenacit \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. He becomes an emperor and is invested with the right in the Śaivite ritual. If one desires welfare one shall seek refuge in Śiva and resort to his holy rites. But we do not compel anyone through any means.

## \|\| 12.28.33-35 \|\|

*nirbandhebhyo 'tivādebhyaḥ prakṛtyaitanna rocate \|*  
*rocate vā parebhyastu puṇyasaṃskāragauravāt \|\| 33 \|\|*

*saṃsārakāraṇaṃ yeṣāṃ na praroḍhumalaṃ bhavet \|*  
*prakṛtyanuguṇaṃ tasmādvimṛśyaitadaśeṣataḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*śivadharme 'dhikurvīta yadīcchecchivamātmanaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

33-35. Neither importunities nor over-discussions are appealing. The Śaivite rites appeal to some others by virtue of the merits they bestow and the previous impressions they invoke if the cause of worldliness in their case is not competent to help. Hence, if one longs for the welfare of the Ātman, one shall ponder over all these things in accordance with his nature and engage himself in the Śaivite holy rites.

## Chapter 29 - Description of Kāmya rites

## \|\| 12.29.1 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*bhagavaṃstvanmukhādeva śrutaṃ śrutisamaṃ mayā \|*  
*svāśritānāṃ śivaproktaṃ nityanaimittikaṃ tathā \|\| 1 \|\|*

Lord Kṛṣṇa said:—

1\. O holy lord, the compulsory and optional rites of those who depend on him, as mentioned by Śiva, have been heard by me from your mouth itself which is to be as much respected as the Vedas.

## \|\| 12.29.2 \|\|

*idānīṃ śrotumicchāmi śivadharmādhikāriṇām \|*  
*kāmyamapyasti cetkarma vaktumarhasi sāmpratam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Now I wish to hear if there is any Kāmya rite for those who are authorized in Śaivite rites. It behoves you to mention it.

## \|\| 12.29.3-5 \|\|

*upamanyuruvāca \|*  
*astyaihikaphalaṃ kiñcidāmuṣmikaphalaṃ tathā \|*  
*aihikāmuṣmikañcāpi tacca pañcavidhaṃ punaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*kiṃcitkriyāmayaṃ karma kiṃcitkarma tapo mayam \|*  
*japadhyānamayaṃ kiṃcitkiṃcitsarvamayaṃ tathā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*kriyāmayaṃ tathā bhinnaṃ homadānārcanakramāt \|*  
*sarvaśaktimatāmeva nānyeṣāṃ saphalaṃ bhavet \|\| 5 \|\|*

Upamanyu said:—

3-5. Some rites yield benefit here itself. Some yield benefit hereafter. Both of them are of five types. Some rites are in the form of activities, some in the form of penance, some in the form of Japas, some in the form of meditation, some in the form of all these. Those in the form of activities are the rites of Homa and worship.

## \|\| 12.29.6 \|\|

*śaktiścājñā madeśasya śivasya paramātmanaḥ \|*  
*tasmātkāmyāni karmāṇi kuryādājñādharodvijaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The rites can be fruitful only for those who have all Śaktis. Śakti is the behest of Śiva the great Ātman.

## \|\| 12.29.7 \|\|

*atha vakṣyāmi kāmyaṃ hi cehāmutra phalapradam \|*  
*śaivairmāheśvaraiścaiva kāryamaṃtarbahiḥ kramāt \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Hence only the brahmin who upholds the behest shall perform the Kāmya rites. Now I shall mention the Kāmya rites yielding benefit.here and hereafter.

## \|\| 12.29.8-10 \|\|

*śivo maheśvaraśceti nātyaṃtamiha bhidyate \|*  
*yathā tathā na bhidyaṃte śaivā māheśvarā api \|\| 8 \|\|*

*śivāśritā hi te śaivā jñānayajñaratā narāḥ \|*  
*māheśvarāssamākhyātā karmayajñaratā bhuvi \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tasmādābhyantare kuryuḥ śaivā māheśvarā vahiḥ \|*  
*na tu prayogo bhidyeta vakṣyamāṇasya karmaṇaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

8-10. The internal rites shall be performed by the followers of Śiva and the external by the followers of Maheśvara. In fact the followers of Śiva and of Maheśvara are not different even as Śiva and Maheśvara are not different. Men engaged in the sacrifice of knowledge are the followers of Śiva and seek refuge in him. Those who are engaged in the sacrifice of activities are the followers of Maheśvara. Śaivas shall perform internal and the Māheśvaras external rites.

## \|\| 12.29.11-13 \|\|

*parīkṣya bhūmiṃ vidhivadgaṃdhavarṇarasādibhiḥ \|*  
*manobhilaṣite tatra vitānavitatāṃbare \|\| 11 \|\|*

*supralipte mahīpṛṣṭhe darpaṇodarasaṃnibhe \|*  
*prācīmutpādayetpūrvaṃ śāstradṛṣṭena vartmanā \|\| 12 \|\|*

*ekahastaṃ dvihastaṃ vā maṇḍalaṃ parikalpayet \|*  
*ālikhedvimalaṃ padmamaṣṭapatraṃ sakarṇikam \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. In the rite which is going to be mentioned the procedure is not different. The ground shall be tested through smell, colour and taste. It shall be desirable. A canopy shall be spread above. The ground shall be well-scrubbed and smeared to appear like the surface of a mirror. Along the path, as seen in the sacred scriptures he shall consecrate the eastern sector at first. The Maṇḍala shall be one Hasta or two Hastas in width.

## \|\| 12.29.14 \|\|

*ratnahemādibhiścūrṇairyathāsaṃbhavasaṃbhṛtaiḥ \|*  
*pañcāvaraṇasaṃyuktaṃ bahuśobhāsamanvitam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. An eight-petalled pure lotus along with its pericarp shall be drawn by means of gold dust, gem dust etc. gathered according to availability.

## \|\| 12.29.15-18 \|\|

*daleṣu siddhayaḥ kalpyāḥ kesareṣu saśaktikāḥ \|*  
*rudrā vāmādayastvaṣṭau pūrvādidalataḥ kramāt \|\| 15 \|\|*

*karṇikāyāṃ ca vairāgyaṃ bījeṣu nava śaktayaḥ \|*  
*skande śivātmako dharmo nāle jñānaṃ śivāśrayam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*karṇikopari cāgneyaṃ maṃḍalaṃ sauramaindavam \|*  
*śivavidyātmatattvākhyaṃ tattvatrayamataḥ param \|\| 17 \|\|*

*sarvāsanopari sukhaṃ vicitrakusumānvitam \|*  
*pañcāvaraṇasaṃyuktaṃ pūjayedaṃbayā saha \|\| 18 \|\|*

15-18. It shall have five Āvaraṇas and shall be very splendid. The Siddhis shall be conceived in the petals. The Rudras along with Śaktis shall be conceived in the filaments. The eight deities Vāma etc. shall be conceived in the petals beginning with the eastern one; Vairāgya in the pericarp, the nine Śaktis in the seeds, Śaivite holy rite in the bulbous root, knowledge of Śiva in the stalk. Above the pericarp the discs of the fire, the sun and the moon shall be conceived. Beyond that shall be conceived the trio: Śiva, Vidyā and Ātmā. Above all seats Śiva shall be conceived equipped with the flowers of various colours.

## \|\| 12.29.19-22 \|\|

*śuddhasphaṭikasaṃkāśaṃ prasannaṃ śītaladyutim \|*  
*vidyudvalayasaṃkāśajaṭāmukuṭabhūṣitam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*śārdūlacarmavasanaṃ kiñcitsmitamukhāṃbujam \|*  
*raktapadmadalaprakhyapādapāṇitalādharam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*sarvalakṣaṇasaṃpannaṃ sarvābharaṇabhūṣitam \|*  
*divyāyudhavarairyuktaṃ divyagaṃdhānulepanam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*pañcavaktraṃ daśabhujaṃ candrakhaṇḍaśikhāmaṇim \|*  
*asya pūrvamukhaṃ saumyaṃ bālārkasadṛśaprabham \|\| 22 \|\|*

19-22. He shall worship Śiva with the five Āvaraṇas accompanied by Ambā. Śiva shall be conceived as pure as the pure crystal, delighted and having cool lustre. He is bedecked with the coronet of matted hair resembling a circle of lightning. He wears the hide of the tiger. His lotus face is slightly smiling. His soles, palms and lips resemble the petals of the red lotus. He is richly endowed with all characteristics. He is bedecked in all ornaments, and equipped with excellent weapons. He has divine scents and unguents. He has five faces and ten arms. The sector of the moon is his crest.

## \|\| 12.29.23 \|\|

*trilocanāraviṃdāḍhyaṃ kṛtabāleṃduśekharam \|*  
*dakṣiṇaṃ nīlajīmūtasamānaruciraprabham \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. His eastern face is gentle, having the lustre of the rising sun. It has three lotus eyes and the rising moon for its crest.

## \|\| 12.29.24-27 \|\|

*bhrukuṭīkuṭilaṃ ghoraṃ raktavṛttekṣaṇatrayam \|*  
*daṃṣṭrākarālaṃ durdharṣaṃ sphuritādharapallavam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*uttaraṃ vidrumaprakhyaṃ nīlālakavibhūṣitam \|*  
*savilāsaṃ trinayanaṃ candrābharaṇaśekharam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*paścimaṃ pūrṇacandrābhaṃ locanatritayojjvalam \|*  
*candrarekhādharaṃ saumyaṃ maṃdasmitamanoharam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*pañcamaṃ sphaṭikaprakhyamiṃdurekhāsamujjvalam \|*  
*atīva saumyamutphullalocanatritayojjvalam \|\| 27 \|\|*

24-27. The southern face has the charming lustre of the blue cloud. The brows are crooked and the face is terrible with three red and circular eyes. It is terrible with the curved fangs. None dare offend it. His lips throb. The northern face is like a coral, bedecked with blue forelocks. It has charming movements. It has three eyes and the moon bedecks its crest. The western face has three brilliant eyes and the lustre of the full moon. It also wears the digit of the moon. It is gentle and charming with smiles. The fifth face is crystal-like with the shining digit of the moon. It is very gentle and looks splendid with the three shining eyes.

## \|\| 12.29.28-30 \|\|

*dakṣiṇe śūlaparaśuvajrakhaḍgānalojjvalam \|*  
*savye ca nāganārācaghaṇṭāpāśāṃkuśojjvalam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*nivṛttyājānusaṃbaddhamānābheśca pratiṣṭhayā \|*  
*ākaṃṭhaṃ vidyayā tadvadālalāṭaṃ tu śāṃtayā \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tadūrdhvaṃ śāṃtyatītākhyakalayā parayā tathā \|*  
*pañcādhvavyāpinaṃ sākṣātkalāpañcakavigraham \|\| 30 \|\|*

28-30. In his right side he shines with the trident, axe, thunderbolt, sword and fire. In his left side he shines brilliantly with the serpent, arrow, bell, noose and goad. The nivṛttikalā envelops him upto the knee, the pratiṣṭhākalā to the navel, the Vidyākalā to the neck and the Śāntākalā to the forehead. Above that he is enveloped by the great Śāntyatītakalā. Thus pervading the five pathways he has the five Kalās constituting his body.

## \|\| 12.29.31-37 \|\|

*īśānamukuṭaṃ devaṃ puruṣākhyaṃ purātanam \|*  
*aghorahṛdayaṃ tadvadvāmaguhyaṃ maheśvaram \|\| 31 \|\|*

*sadyapādaṃ ca tanmūrtimaṣṭatriṃśatkalāmayam \|*  
*mātṛkāmayamīśānaṃ pañcabrahmamayaṃ tathā \|\| 32 \|\|*

*oṃkārākhyamayaṃ caiva haṃsaśaktyā samanvitam \|*  
*tathecchātmikayā śaktyā samārūḍhāṃkamaṃḍalam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*jñānākhyayā dakṣiṇato vāmataśca kriyākhyayā \|*  
*tattvatrayamayaṃ sākṣādvidyāmūrtiṃ sadāśivam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*mūrtimūlena saṃkalpya sakalīkṛtya ca kramāt \|*  
*saṃpūjya ca yathānyāyamarghāntaṃ mūlavidyayā \|\| 35 \|\|*

*mūrtimantaṃ śivaṃ sākṣācchaktyā paramayā saha \|*  
*tatrāvāhya mahādevaṃ sadasadvyaktivarjitam \|\| 36 \|\|*

*pañcopakaraṇaṃ kṛtvā pūjayetparameśvaram \|*  
*brahmabhiśca ṣaḍaṅgaiśca tato mātṛkayā saha \|\| 37 \|\|*

31-37. The lord has Īśāna as his coronet. He is the eternal one named Puruṣa. Aghora constitutes his heart, Vāmadeva his private parts and Sadyojāta his legs. His form consists of thirty-eight Kalās. The lord consists of the Varṇas, letters. He is identical with the five Brahmans. He is of the Oṃkāra form. He is endowed with the Śakti of Haṃsa Ātman. His lap is enveloped by the Icchāśakti. His right side is flanked by Jñāna Śakti and the left by Kriyāśakti. Sadāśiva in the form Vidyā shall be conceived as identical with the trio of Tattvas. The Mūrti shall be conceived with the basic mantra and everything shall be combined into one unit. Until the Arghya he shall be worshipped duly with the basic mantra. Śiva shall be invoked along with the great Śakti, in the embodied form. The lord devoid of Sat and Asat shall be invoked and worshipped with the five articles of worship.

## \|\| 12.29.38-40 \|\|

*praṇavena śivenaiva śaktiyuktena ca kramāt \|*  
*śāṃtena vā tathānyaiśca vedamantraiśca kṛtsnaśaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*pūjayetparamaṃ devaṃ kevalena śivena vā \|*  
*pādyādimukhavāsāṃtaṃ kṛtvā prasthāpanaṃ vinā \|\| 39 \|\|*

*pañcāvaraṇapūjāṃ tu hyārabheta yathākramam \|\| 40 \|\|*

38-40. He shall be worshipped with the five brahmans and six ancillaries. With Mātṛkās repeating the Praṇava, he shall worship Śiva in the company of Śakti, in the quiet form repeating the mantras. Or he shall worship the lord only with the Śiva mantra. Then he shall begin the Pañcāvaraṇa Pūjā after offering Pādya etc. upto Mukhavāsa. But the rite of Prasthāpana (bidding the deity farewell) shall not be performed.

## Chapter 30 - The Kāmya rites of the followers of Śiva

## \|\| 12.30.1 \|\|

*tatrādau śivayoḥ pārśve dakṣiṇe vāmataḥ kramāt \|*  
*gaṃdhādyairarcayetpūrvaṃ devau heraṃbaṣaṇmukhau \|\| 1 \|\|*

Upamanyu said:—

1\. There at the outset he shall worship lords Heramba and Ṣaṇmukha on either side, the right and the left in order, of Śiva and Śivā.

## \|\| 12.30.2 \|\|

*tato brahmāṇi parita īśānādi yathākramam \|*  
*saśaktikāni sadyāṃtaṃ prathamāvaraṇe yajet \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Then in the first Āvaraṇa he shall worship the five Brahmans beginning with Īśāna and ending with Sadyojāta along with their Śaktis all round.

## \|\| 12.30.3 \|\|

*ṣaḍaṃgānyapi tatraiva hṛdayādīnyanukramāt \|*  
*śivasya ca śivāyāśca vāhneyādi samarcayet \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The six limbs—the heart etc. of Śiva and Śivā shall be worshipped from the south-east.

## \|\| 12.30.4 \|\|

*tatra vāmādikānrudrānaṣṭau vāmādiśaktibhiḥ \|*  
*arcayedvā na vā paścātpūrvādiparitaḥ kramāt \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Afterwards he may or may not worship the eight Rudras-Vāma etc. along with their Śaktis all round in order, from the east onwards.

## \|\| 12.30.5 \|\|

*prathamāvaraṇaṃ proktaṃ mayā te yadunaṃdana \|*  
*dvitīyāvaraṇaṃ prītyā procyate śraddhayā śṛṇu \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Thus, O Kṛṣṇa, the first Āvaraṇa has been mentioned to you. Now listen to the second Āvaraṇa with faith.

## \|\| 12.30.6 \|\|

*anaṃtaṃ pūrvādikpatre tacchaktiṃ tasya vāmataḥ \|*  
*sūkṣmaṃ dakṣiṇadikpatre saha śaktyā samarcayet \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He shall worship Ananta in the eastern petal and his Śakti to his left. In the southern petal he shall worship Sūkṣma and his Śakti.

## \|\| 12.30.7 \|\|

*tataḥ paścimadikpatre saha śaktyā śivottamam \|*  
*tathaivottaradikpatre caikanetraṃ samarcayet \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Then in the western petal he shall worship lord Śiva along with his Śakti. Similarly in the northern petal he shall worship Ekanetra and his Śakti.

## \|\| 12.30.8 \|\|

*ekarudraṃ ca tacchaktiṃ paścādīśadale 'rcayet \|*  
*trimūrtiṃ tasya śaktiṃ ca pūjayedagnidigdale \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Afterwards he shall worship Ekarudra and his Śakti in the north-eastern petal. He shall worship Trimūrti and his Śakti in the South-eastern petal.

## \|\| 12.30.9 \|\|

*śrīkaṇṭhaṃ nairṛte patre tacchaktiṃ tasya vāmataḥ \|*  
*tathaiva mārute patre śikhaṃḍīśaṃ samarcayet \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. He shall worship Śrīkaṇṭha and his Śakti towards his left in the south-western petal. Similarly he shall worship Śikhaṇḍīśa and his Śakti in the north-western petal.

## \|\| 12.30.10 \|\|

*dvitīyāvaraṇe cejyāssarvartaścakravartinaḥ \|*  
*tṛtīyāvaraṇe pūjyāḥ śaktibhiścāṣṭamūrtayaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. In the second Āvaraṇa the Cakravartins, in the third Āvaraṇa the Aṣṭamūrtis shall be worshipped along with their Śaktis.

## \|\| 12.30.11-12 \|\|

*aṣṭasu kramaśo dikṣu pūrvādiparitaḥ kramāt \|*  
*bhavaḥ śarvastatheśāno rudraḥ paśupatistataḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*ugro bhīmo mahādeva ityaṣṭau mūrtayaḥ kramāt \|*  
*anaṃtaraṃ tataścaiva mahādevādayaḥ kramāt \|*

*śaktibhissaha saṃpūjyāstatraikādaśamūrtayaḥ \|*  
*mahādevaḥ śivo rudraḥ śaṃkaro nīlalohitaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. They shall be worshipped in the eight quarters from the east onwards in order. The eight Mūrtis in order are Bhava, Śarva, Īśāna Rudra, Paśupati, Ugra, Bhīma and Mahādeva. Afterwards the eleven Mūrtis, Mahādeva etc. shall be worshipped along with their Śaktis.

## \|\| 12.30.13-15 \|\|

*īśāno vijayo bhīmo devadevo bhavodbhavaḥ \|*  
*kapardīśaśca kathyaṃte tathaikādaśaśaktayaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tatrāṣṭau prathamaṃ pūjyāḥ vāhneyādi yathākramam \|*  
*devadevaḥ pūrvapatre īśānaṃ cāgnigocare \|\| 14 \|\|*

*bhavodbhavastayormadhye kapālīśastataḥ param \|*  
*tasminnāvaraṇe bhūyo vṛṣendraṃ purato yajet \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. The eleven Mūrtis are: Mahādeva, Śiva, Rudra, Śaṅkara, Nīlalohita, Īśāna, Vijaya, Bhīma, Devadeva, Bhavodbhava and Kapardīśa. The first eight shall be worshipped in the south-eastern quarter onwards. Devadeva shall be worshipped in the eastern petel. Bhavodbhava shall be worshipped either in the north-east or in the south-east. Kapālīśa shall be worshipped in their middle.

## \|\| 12.30.16-18 \|\|

*naṃdinaṃ dakṣiṇe tasya mahākālaṃ tathottare \|*  
*śāstāraṃ vahnidikpatre mātḥrdakṣiṇadigdale \|\| 16 \|\|*

*gajāsyaṃ nairṛte patre ṣaṇmukhaṃ vāruṇe punaḥ \|*  
*jyeṣṭhāṃ vāyudale gaurīmuttare caṃḍamaiśvare \|\| 17 \|\|*

*śāstṛnandīśayormadhye munīndraṃ vṛṣabhaṃ yajet \|*  
*mahākālasyottarataḥ piṃgalaṃ tu samarcayet \|\| 18 \|\|*

16-18. In the same Āvaraṇa he shall worship the lordly bull in the east, Nandin in the south, Mahākāla in the north, Śāstṛ in the south-eastern petal or in the petal to the south of the goddess. He shall worship Gaṇeśa in the south-western petal and Ṣaṇmukha in the western petal. He shall worship Jyeṣṭhā in the north-western petal, Gaurī in the north and Caṇḍa in the north-cast. He shall worship Munīndra between Śāstṛ and Nandīśa.

## \|\| 12.30.19 \|\|

*śāstṛmātṛsamūhasya madhye bhṛṃgīśvaraṃ tataḥ \|*  
*mātṛvighneśamadhye tu vīrabhadraṃ samarcayet \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. He shall worship Piṅgala to the north of Mahākāla. Then he shall worship Bhrṅgīśvara in the middle of Śāstra and Mātṛ group.

## \|\| 12.30.20 \|\|

*skandavighneśayormadhye yajeddevīṃ sarasvatīm \|*  
*jyeṣṭhākumārayormadhye śriyaṃ śivapadārcitām \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. He shall worship Vīrabhadra in between the Mātṛs and Vighneśa. He shall worship goddess Sarasvatī in between Skanda and Vighneśa.

## \|\| 12.30.21 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhāgaṇāmbayormadhye mahāmoṭīṃ samarcayet \|*  
*gaṇāmbācaṇḍayormadhye devīṃ durgāṃ prapūjayet \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Śrī is to be worshipped at the feet of Śiva in between Jyeṣṭhā and Kumāra. He shall worship Mahāmoṭī in between Jyeṣṭhā and Gaṇāmbā.

## \|\| 12.30.22 \|\|

*atraivāvaraṇe bhūyaḥ śivānucarasaṃhatim \|*  
*rudraprathamabhūtākhyāṃ vividhāṃ ca saśaktikām \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. He shall worship goddess Durgā in between Gaṇāmbā and Caṇḍa. In the same Āvaraṇa he shall worship the host of Śiva’s attendants.

## \|\| 12.30.23 \|\|

*śivāyāśca sakhīvargaṃ japeddhyātvā samāhitaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ tṛtīyāvaraṇe vitate pūjite sati \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. He shall perform the Japa after due meditation with mental purity, of the female friends of Śivā along with the Śaktis of Rudra, Pramatha and Bhūta.

## \|\| 12.30.24 \|\|

*caturthāvaraṇaṃ dhyātvā bahistasya samarcayet \|*  
*bhānuḥ pūrvadale pūjyo dakṣiṇe caturānanaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. When the third Āvaraṇa has been worshipped thus he shall worship the fourth Āvaraṇa outside it after meditation.

## \|\| 12.30.25 \|\|

*rudro varuṇadikpatre viṣṇuruttaradigdale \|*  
*caturṇāmapi devānāṃ pṛthagāvaraṇānyatha \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The sun shall be worshipped in the eastern, Brahmā in the southern, Rudra in the western and Viṣṇu in the northern petal.

## \|\| 12.30.26 \|\|

*tasyāṃgāni ṣaḍevādau dīptādyābhiśca śaktibhiḥ \|*  
*dīptā sūkṣmā jayā bhadrā vibhūtirvimalā kramāt \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. There are separate Āvaraṇas to all the four lords. His six limbs shall be worshipped at the outset along with the Śaktis, Dīptā etc.

## \|\| 12.30.27 \|\|

*amoghā vidyutā caiva pūrvādi paritaḥ sthitāḥ \|*  
*dvitīyāvaraṇe pūjyāścatasro mūrtayaḥ kramāt \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. They are Dīptā, Sūkṣmā, Jayā, Bhadrā, Vibhūti, Vimalā, Amoghā and Vidyutā. These shall be worshipped all round form the east onwards.

## \|\| 12.30.28 \|\|

*pūrvādyuttaraparyaṃtāḥ śaktayaśca tataḥ param \|*  
*ādityo bhāskaro bhānū raviścetyanupūrvaśaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The four shall be worshipped in the second Āvaraṇa in order from the east to the north and their Śaktis afterwards.

## \|\| 12.30.29-30 \|\|

*arko brahmā tathā rudro viṣṇuścaite vivasvataḥ \|*  
*vistārā pūrvadigbhāge sutarāṃ dakṣiṇe sthitāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*bodhanī paścime bhāge āpyāyinyuttare punaḥ \|*  
*uṣāṃ prabhāṃ tathā prājñāṃ sandhyāmapi tataḥ param \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. Āditya, Bhāskara, Bhānu, Ravi, Arka, Brahmā, Rudra and Viṣṇu these are the extensions of Vivasvat in the cast and stationed more so in the south. Bodhinī is in the west and Āpyāyinī in the north.

## \|\| 12.30.31 \|\|

*aiśānādiṣu vinyasya dvitīyāvaraṇe yajet \|*  
*somamaṃgārakaṃ caiva budhaṃ buddhimatāṃ varam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. He shall worship in the second Āvaraṇa, Uṣā, Prabhā, Prājñā and Sandhyā after fixing them in Īśāna etc.

## \|\| 12.30.32-33 \|\|

*bṛhaspatiṃ bṛhadbuddhiṃ bhārgavaṃ tejasāṃ nidhim \|*  
*śanaiścaraṃ tathā rāhuṃ ketuṃ dhūmraṃ bhayaṃkaram \|\| 32 \|\|*

*samaṃtato yajedetāṃstṛtīyāvaraṇe kramāt \|*  
*athavā dvādaśādityā dvitīyāvaraṇe yajet \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. In the third Āvaraṇa he shall worship Soma (moon) Aṅgāraka (Mars), Budha (Mercury) most excellent among the intelligent, Bṛhaspati (Jupiter) of extensive intellect, Bhārgava (Venus), the storehouse of splendour, Śanaiścara (Saturn), Rāhu and Ketu the smoke-coloured and terrible.

## \|\| 12.30.34 \|\|

*tṛtīyāvaraṇe caiva rāśīndvādaśa pūjayet \|*  
*saptasapta gaṇāṃścaiva bahistasya samaṃtataḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Or he shall worship the twelve Ādityas in the second Āvaraṇa and the twelve Rāśis (signs of Zodiac) in the third Āvaraṇa.

## \|\| 12.30.35-36 \|\|

*ṛṣīndevāṃśca gaṃdharvānpannagānapsarogaṇān \|*  
*grāmaṇyaśca tathā yakṣānyātudhānāṃstathā hayān \|\| 35 \|\|*

*saptacchaṃdomayāṃścaiva vālakhilyāṃśca pūjayet \|*  
*evaṃ tṛtīyāvaraṇe samabhyarcya divākaram \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. Externally he shall worship the groups of seven, sages, gods, Gandharvas, serpents, Apsaras, Grāmaṇīs (leaders), Yakṣas, Yātudhānas, horses, and the seven Vālakhilyas in the form of Chandas.

## \|\| 12.30.37 \|\|

*brahmāṇamarcayetpaścāttribhirāvaraṇaiḥ sahaḥ \|*  
*hiraṇyagarbhaṃ pūrvasyāṃ virājaṃ dakṣiṇe tataḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. After worshipping the sun in the third Āvaraṇa he shall worship Brahmā along with the three Āvaraṇas.

## \|\| 12.30.38 \|\|

*kālaṃ paścimadigbhāge puruṣaṃ cottare yajet \|*  
*hiraṇyagarbhaḥ prathamo brahmā kamalasannibhaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. He shall worship Hiraṇyagarbha in the east, Virāṭ in the south, Kāla in the west and Puruṣa in the north.

## \|\| 12.30.39-40 \|\|

*kālo jātyaṃjanaprakhyaḥ puruṣaḥ sphaṭikopamaḥ \|*  
*triguṇo rājasaścaiva tāmasaḥ sāttvikastathā \|\| 39 \|\|*

*catvāra ete kramaśaḥ prathamāvaraṇe sthitāḥ \|*  
*dvitīyāvaraṇe pūjyāḥ pūrvādiparitaḥ kramāt \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. Hiraṇyagarbha is the first Brahmā resembling the lotus, Kāla has the lustre of Jāti and collyrium. Puruṣa resembles the crystal. He has three Guṇas: sattva, rajas and tamas. The four are stationed in order in the first Āvaraṇa.

## \|\| 12.30.41 \|\|

*sanatkumāraḥ sanakaḥ sanaṃdaśca sanātanaḥ \|*  
*tṛtīyāvaraṇe paścādarcayecca prajāpatīn \|\| 41 \|\|*
